pages.html:
Harry James Potter (born 31 July 1980) is a half-blood wizard of Gryffindor House, the Boy Who Lived. He survived Lord Voldemort's Killing Curse as a baby, then grew up in the cupboard under the stairs at Number Four, Privet Drive, the home of his Muggle aunt and uncle. By the summer of 1994 he had faced Voldemort twice. He had killed the Basilisk of the Chamber of Secrets with Andúril, the sword that came to him out of the Sorting Hat, and cast a Patronus that destroys Dementors. He had come to believe in Christ, and he had admitted to himself that he was in love with Dracina Malfoy, the Slytherin girl he once asked, quite seriously, whether she was a princess. He does not know that he descends from Aragorn and Arwen through his mother, or from King Arthur Pendragon through his father. Nor does he know that a fragment of Voldemort's soul has lived in him since the night he was marked.

Early life

Harry was born on 31 July 1980. His father, James Potter, was a pure-blood wizard of an ancient family. His mother, Lily Potter (née Evans), was a Muggle-born witch and a devout Anglican, the daughter of Susan Pevensie. The family went into hiding from Lord Voldemort under the Fidelius Charm. On the advice of Sirius Black, Harry's godfather, they made Peter Pettigrew their Secret-Keeper.

On 31 October 1981 Pettigrew's betrayal brought Voldemort to Godric's Hollow. James told Lily to take Harry and go. Lily begged to die in her son's place, and when Voldemort turned his wand on the child, the curse broke against her sacrifice. It left Harry with a lightning-shaped scar, and the memory of a flash of green light.

Hagrid carried him away on Sirius Black's flying motorbike. Albus Dumbledore, to his lasting shame, left him on the doorstep of Lily's sister, Petunia Dursley, because Lily's protection would hold only while Harry could call her house home. For ten years the Dursleys kept him in the cupboard under the stairs. They told him his parents had died drunk in a car crash.

He was hit with a frying pan, a rolling pin and Vernon's hand. He was hunted by Dudley's gang, never fed until he was full, and given presents chosen to hurt. On his sixth birthday his present was a parcel of Uncle Vernon's old socks, unwrapped while all three Dursleys watched his face fall. From them he took an inner voice. It told him that he was a freak, that kindness was the first half of a trick, and that hope was the worst mistake of all.

At St Grogory's Primary School he learnt the Lord's Prayer in assembly, with Dudley kicking his chair. He went inside a church only once, one Christmas when he was seven, and saw a face in a window that he would see again. Raised on the Muggle side, he could not have named a single Quidditch team before he was eleven. At the zoo in 1991 he spoke to a boa constrictor without knowing that it was Parseltongue. That summer Rubeus Hagrid came to the hut on the rock and told him he was a wizard.

Book One: first year, 1991 to 1992

In Madam Malkin's, wearing Dudley's old jeans rolled up four times at the ankle, Harry met a girl with waist-length silver-blonde hair, who held out her hand to be kissed. Not knowing the custom, he asked her quite seriously whether she was a princess. Then he stood up for Hagrid against her, and left without giving his name. On the Hogwarts Express he made friends with Ron Weasley, and refused Dracina Malfoy's hand a second time, saying he could work out the wrong sort for himself. The Sorting Hat saw courage, talent and great pain for one so young. It told him he could be great in Slytherin, but at his pleading it put him in Gryffindor.

Chasing Dracina on his first flight ever, to get back Neville Longbottom's Remembrall, he caught it at the end of a fifty-foot dive. It made him Seeker, the youngest house player in about a century. On Hallowe'en a troll trapped Hermione Granger and Dracina in the girls' toilets. Harry fought it off with Ron, and afterwards Hermione became his friend. In his first match his jinxed broom left him hanging on by one hand, before he caught the Snitch in his mouth.

At Christmas he was given the first real presents of his life, his father's Invisibility Cloak among them. He found the Mirror of Erised, and in it he saw his parents with both sets of grandparents. A little brother and sister stood with them.

On detention in the Forbidden Forest, Dracina clung to his hand and called him Harry for the first time. Then a hooded figure killed a unicorn and drank its blood. She fled, and the centaur Firenze carried Harry to safety.

On the night he went through the trapdoor, he first accepted her apology, as she lay stiff under Hermione's Body-Bind. The twinkle in her silver eyes stayed with him for years. Below, he found Quirrell at the Mirror. The Mirror put the Philosopher's Stone in his pocket, and Voldemort's face looked out from the back of Quirrell's head. When Quirrell's skin blistered at his touch, Harry held on, drawing on hatred for the first time, until he blacked out. Afterwards Dumbledore told him that his mother's love had left a protection in his skin, and that she might have come of a very powerful line of magic. Harry cried.

Book Two: second year, 1992 to 1993

The Dursleys forgot his twelfth birthday. The house-elf Dobby warned him not to go back to Hogwarts, then wrecked Uncle Vernon's dinner party. After that Vernon put bars on Harry's window and fed him through a cat-flap. Ron, Fred and George pulled the bars out with a flying Ford Anglia. At the Burrow Harry found he could not lie to Molly Weasley. He told her about the frying pan and the cupboard, then sobbed while she held him.

That autumn he heard a cold voice in the walls that nobody else could hear. On Hallowe'en he followed it to the message announcing that the Chamber of Secrets had been opened, and he came to suspect Dracina of being the Heir. In the Slytherin match a rogue Bludger broke his arm, after Dracina had thrown her broom across its path to shield him. At the Duelling Club he called off her conjured snake in Parseltongue, and the school decided he was the Heir.

At Christmas, disguised as Goyle, he heard a sick, frantic Dracina speak of Tom, the voice in her diary, and of the bars on his window. He realised that she had sent Dobby to warn him. He took the diary. It answered him, and showed him Riddle's memory of 13 June 1943. Without noticing, he began to call it 'precious'.

When Ginny Weasley was taken into the Chamber, he opened it in Parseltongue and went on alone. He found Dracina collapsing at the feet of Slytherin's statue, wearing his stolen scarf. He refused Riddle's offer of revenge on the Dursleys, though he wanted it, and called him a half-blood fraud. The Basilisk's fang pierced his arm. As he lay dying a warmth held him, and a fatherly voice said 'Your work is not yet done, my child.'

Fawkes brought the Sorting Hat, and Harry drew a sword from it. He met the Basilisk's eyes behind a golden heat that turned the stare aside. Standing astride Dracina, he cut off its head, then drove the blade through the diary. As the venom returned he saw a bearded man with long brown hair, in a plain white robe, watching him with pride.

He woke with his head in Dracina's lap, and left her out of his account to the teachers. Dumbledore told him that his Parseltongue came from Voldemort, passed into him on the night of the scar, and that a person is defined by his choices. Harry tricked Lucius Malfoy into freeing Dobby. In the hospital wing he laughed with Dracina for the first time, and they agreed to be friends.

He was told that he must go back to Privet Drive, because Lily's protection, the magic of Elves and of Númenor, lived in his aunt's blood. He wept in front of the school. At King's Cross he made the sign of the Cross for the first time in his life.

Book Three: third year, 1993 to 1994

After a visit from Dumbledore, the Dursleys stopped hitting him. Because Dumbledore had spoken of Elves and Númenor, Harry read The Lord of the Rings. Four times he walked to the lych-gate of St Michael's Church without going in. On the fourth, an old man on the bench told him the door was open, and vanished. Dracina's birthday letter came tied with a green ribbon, a lady's token of favour, and the ribbon became his bookmark.

When Aunt Marge called his parents drunks, his rage inflated her. He left Privet Drive hating Muggles. At the Leaky Cauldron he decided that there were two of him: an angry boy from the cupboard, and a boy from the Chamber who wanted to stand in front of good things.

A Dementor on the Hogwarts Express made him collapse to the sound of screaming. Dracina gave him chocolate violets with a card that read 'Not from Ginny'. He caught her when Buckbeak slashed her arm. A painted man at a smouldering altar, who resented his brother's accepted offering, told Harry that he could smell his anger, and that he should mind the door-sill. In the hurricane match more than a hundred Dementors flooded the pitch. Harry heard his mother plead for his life, and fell fifty feet. In the hospital wing he dreamt of revenge on the Dursleys while the painted man watched, until a beam of light burnt the watcher away.

He overheard that Sirius Black had been his father's best man, his own godfather and the Potters' betrayer. When a Ministry letter named Lucius Malfoy's complaint about Buckbeak, he concluded that Dracina had lied about dropping it. In fact Pansy Parkinson had posted it. Four times he came to the edge of asking her, and four times a conversation about faith, proof or forgiveness stopped him.

Lupin taught him the Patronus Charm. At the Ravenclaw match in March 1994 Harry gave the team its orders in flight for the first time. He cast a solid silver Patronus at three hooded figures, and Gryffindor won 230 to 70. The figures were Dracina, Crabbe, Goyle and Marcus Flint. Harry turned his back on her, until Snape's remark that she had wept left him with a doubt. When she begged him on the castle steps, he remembered Lupin's teaching of forgiveness seventy times seven. He put his arms round her, and believed her. He won the Quidditch Cup, and realised afterwards that she had let him.

On the night of Buckbeak's execution, in the Shrieking Shack, Harry flew at Sirius Black but could not kill him. Lupin, a Garou, and Black proved that Ron's rat was Peter Pettigrew. Harry, citing his own misjudgement of Dracina, blocked the door against Snape. Then he saved Pettigrew's life to clear Sirius. Under the full moon Lupin's war form sniffed Harry, found two smells on him and growled 'Wyrm'. By the lake Harry's faith collapsed, and his Patronus failed.

Sent back three hours by Hermione's Time-Turner, he found that Dracina had rescued Buckbeak herself. When the werewolf came for her, he knelt in a stream between them. His Shield Charm turned white and restored Lupin to his own shape. He carried Dracina out, forgave her and asked that they be friends openly. At the lake he understood that the rescuer he had seen was himself. He conjured a stag that destroyed Dementors, while an arrow of white light fell from the stars.

With Hermione and Dracina he linked to Myst Island. They brought Sirius back. As Sirius flew away on Buckbeak, with Dracina holding his clenched fist, Harry resolved that the wizarding world must be made to change, and that he would gain the power to do it. A white star shone out low in the west. Lupin gave him his wooden cross. Dumbledore told him the anger never completely goes away, and Harry resolved to use it 'for the greater good'.

Back home, he went into St Michael's for Evensong, and found that the vicar was the old man from the bench. He murmured to the figure of Christ in the window, 'You planned this, didn't you.'

Book Four: the summer of 1994

In August 1994 Harry dreamt that he walked down a Privet Drive sunk in a valley. Number Four had become an orphanage, where his mother had died giving birth to him. He went on to a shack with a dead boa constrictor nailed to the door. Inside he spoke in hisses with a filthy Uncle Vernon, then took Vernon's wand and a gold ring with a black stone. In the house on the hill James, dining with Fleamont and Euphemia, claimed that Lily had tricked him. Harry tortured all three, then killed them, and felt wonderful. Dracina, in a scaled blue dress, embraced him and slipped away into a rainy circus as a snake, while he screamed that he loved her. He woke with his scar burning.

That morning he admitted to himself that he loved her. He had known it since the hospital wing at the end of his second year. He had gone to Evensong every Sunday since July. He had studied harder than ever, expecting the new Defence teacher to try to kill him.

Then Mrs Weasley's invitation to the Quidditch World Cup arrived, with pond mud up the plughole and the postscript 'Actions have consequences'. Afterwards he watched the news with Dudley: the Augment War, Superman before the Security Council, protests against superhumans. He saw the wizarding world as a garden shed beside a motorway, and felt ashamed of his plans to rearrange it.

Appearance and personality

Harry is small and thin for his age. He has untidy black hair that sticks up at the back, round glasses mended with Spellotape, a thin lightning scar and startlingly green eyes. The eyes came down his mother's line, through generations of quiet people who never knew what they carried. By June 1994 he had grown taller than Dracina. He carries the Basilisk's wound in his right arm. Above his left elbow are four pale claw lines from Lupin's war form, which would not heal by magic.

He is brave to the point of recklessness, kind by reflex and blind to romantic signals. He is also far funnier, angrier and more foul-mouthed than he lets most people see; Fred Weasley thought him the funniest bloke in the school. Beneath it the Dursleys' voice still speaks. He hides his feelings behind a blank face, and cries without a sound, because at Privet Drive noise brought feet. He hunches at heavy footsteps. He is afraid of letting people close, in case they turn and hurt him.

Anger is his besetting danger. It inflated Aunt Marge. It sent him towards the staffroom with his wand drawn against Snape, and it gave him dreams of hurting the Dursleys. By 1994 he had come to believe in two kinds of anger. One lashes out like a cornered animal; the other is quieter, and means to put the world right. He likened the second to Narsil reforged.

He reveres Dumbledore, and will not listen to the small question at the back of his mind about the summers he was sent back. The phrase he chose, 'for the greater good', is one that Dumbledore once heard from Greta Grindelwald.

Abilities

Harry is a natural flier. He caught the Snitch in his mouth in his first match, and in about five minutes in his second. In 1994 he won the Quidditch Cup on the Firebolt. Oliver Wood told him he would be captain one day, because others followed him without knowing it.

Hopeless at Potions without help, he became good at Defence Against the Dark Arts under Lupin, and took full marks in his third-year exam. He learnt Expelliarmus by watching Snape. The Shield Charm that Hermione drilled into him held off a Garou.

His Patronus is unique in its power. He cast his first corporeal Patronus at thirteen, one-handed from a broom. At the lake his stag destroyed Dementors, which none of the teachers' Patronuses could do. The Fat Friar told him it had killed them because he had touched God and stopped doubting, like Peter walking on the water.

He is a Parselmouth. He survived the Basilisk's stare and venom. He wielded the sword from the Sorting Hat with a strength poured into him from outside himself. His wand, of holly and phoenix feather, went up a troll's left nostril on his first Hallowe'en. His rage spills over into accidental magic: flames lean away from him, and mugs crack. He can mimic voices, Hermione's flattery of Lockhart among them. He once turned that flattery on the Minister for Magic, and was frightened by how well it worked. He knows the Muggle world better than any pure-blood.

Relationships

Dracina Malfoy is the central relationship of his life. In 1991 he refused her hand twice, because she reminded him of Dudley. He laughed off her mother's invitation to Malfoy Manor as a prank, and missed her while he called her his arch-enemy. He saved her life once a year for three years running: from a troll, a Basilisk and a werewolf. He forgave her on the castle steps against every instinct, and later counted that as the reason he could believe Sirius. He keeps her green ribbons in his copy of The Lord of the Rings, and her note in his inside pocket.

Hermione Granger has been his best friend since the troll. She wrote his History of Magic essays, drilled spells into him and defended him in Trelawney's tower. She is jealous of Dracina, and possessive of him. On the Myst dock Harry understood that both girls had feelings for him. He wished he could tell Hermione, gently, that he did not feel about her as she hoped.

Ron Weasley is his best mate. Ron flew the car to his barred window, and has put extra sausages on his plate at every meal since. He caught Harry with the diary, and broke his leg under the Whomping Willow. It was Ron's letting go of a quarrel that first taught Harry to let go of a grievance.

His family has mostly been found rather than born. The Dursleys abused him for twelve years. Dudley, though, on a diet and devoted to the Green Ranger, made room for him on the sofa in 1994. Molly Weasley held him while he told her the truth. She set her children to watch over him, and condemned Dumbledore for leaving him there. Sirius Black offered him a home that the blood ward would not let him take. Remus Lupin taught him the Patronus and gave him his cross. Hagrid gave him an album of his parents' photographs. Dumbledore he regards as his saviour.

Faith

Harry was raised by a family who thought religion was for old people and Americans. The turning point was the Chamber: the fatherly voice, the golden heat, and the man in white by the fallen pillar, whose face Harry had seen in a church window at seven. Dracina saw him too. For months Harry called the vision concussion, and that doubt broke his first Patronus.

Lupin told him that the Patronus runs on light that comes from God meeting a good soul, and that Lily had believed in Christ with all her heart. Sirius quoted 'Be ye angry, and sin not', a verse Lily had kept on her wall.

His faith failed him once, at the lake. The second time he dared to have faith, and something in his blood answered. Since July 1994 he has gone to Evensong at St Michael's every Sunday. The congregation is elderly and never speaks to him, but the vicar, Ambrose Greyhame, comes to the back pew each week to ask after his soul. He also gave Harry a little black Bible. Harry wears Lupin's wooden cross under his shirt. More than once he has found that something caught him when he fell.

Secrets and ancestry

Through his mother Harry descends from Aragorn and Arwen Undómiel. Aragorn was King of Gondor and Arnor. All four Pevensie children, Peter, Susan, Edmund and Lucy, were of that line. Susan, who was once crowned in Narnia, was not aboard the train that killed her brothers and sister. In her grief, moved by the courage of Aslan, she came back to Christ. In time she became Lily's mother. Dumbledore's phrase for Lily's protection, the magic of Elves and of Númenor, names both halves of the descent. Only two people living know of it: Albus Dumbledore and Lord Voldemort.

Through his father Harry is a direct descendant of King Arthur Pendragon. The Pendragons descend from the Peverell brother who received the Invisibility Cloak, so the Cloak that James left with Dumbledore came down the line intact. Arthur's descendants took the name Potter to escape dark wizards who sided with Morgana. The descent is documented, and obscure only because almost nobody looks. Lucius Malfoy has looked. In 1993 he told Harry that Potters had been kings before they were Potters. Harry knows of neither descent.

The sword he drew from the Sorting Hat is Narsil reforged as Andúril, the Flame of the West, the sword of Elendil and of Aragorn. Ambrose Greyhame had brought it to Dumbledore wrapped in oilcloth. Harry worked this out while reading of its forging at Rivendell, and told nobody.

On 31 October 1981 the rebounding curse tore loose a fragment of Voldemort's broken soul. It lodged in the only living thing in the room. Harry is a Horcrux that Voldemort never meant to make. The fragment is the root of his Parseltongue, and of the pain in his scar when Voldemort is near or stirring. It explains his kinship with the diary's Riddle, and the Slytherin the Hat saw in his mind. When Lupin's Garou breathed him in, it found two smells, and named one of them Wyrm. The diary was a Horcrux of the same craft, a crude descendant of the One Ring, the first Horcrux. Greyhame recognised it at once.

The dream of the house on the hill was Voldemort's memory of the summer of 1943. That summer he walked down into Little Hangleton. From the shack with the dead snake nailed to its door he took his uncle Morfin Gaunt's wand, with the Gaunt ring. Then he murdered his Muggle father and grandparents in the Riddle House. The dream recast it all with the faces of Harry's own life. Number Four became the orphanage where Merope Gaunt died. James spoke the elder Tom Riddle's excuse for abandoning her, and Mrs Figg, knitting by the bus shelter, told Harry he had the wrong face on. The closing images, a scaled dress, a circus and an open iron cage, recall Nagini, the Maledictus who was shown in a travelling circus before she became Voldemort's serpent. Harry has told nobody about the dream.

Lore and legacy

Ambrose Greyhame, who is Gandalf, saw in Harry's jaw and stance a man in a dark corner of a rain-soaked inn: Aragorn at the Prancing Pony. He spoke of Harry to Dumbledore as 'the heir'. He warned that Tom Riddle was only a leaf on a far older tree, planted by an ancient enemy. Dumbledore told Harry that things older and far worse than Voldemort had begun to take an interest in him.

One of them was Cain, the first murderer and the father of vampires. He spoke to Harry from the fourth-floor painting, and watched his revenge dream until a beam of light burnt him out of it. Harry cannot account for the white star in the west at the hour of his resolve, or for the arrow from the stars that felt to him somehow like family. Eärendil, whose star shines in the west, is the forefather of both Aragorn and Arwen.

Harry is the hinge between the wizarding world and the Muggle one. He grew up watching Muggle television through the 1980s. In 1993 he held up the Power Rangers, new on the Muggle news, to Lucius Malfoy as proof that some Muggles help. Dobby, once freed, swore to serve him by choice, and calls him a champion of the light.

In the years to come half the wizarding world would learn to do as Harry told them, and be the happier for it, in a struggle against an enemy far older than Voldemort. That struggle ended in a golden age.

pages.html:
Dracina Malfoy (born 5 June 1980) is a pure-blood witch of Slytherin House, the only child of Lucius and Narcissa Malfoy of Malfoy Manor in Wiltshire. She has been Slytherin's Seeker since 1992. Proud, sharp-tongued and jealous, she is fiercely loyal to the few people she chooses. She has loved Harry Potter since the day he asked her, in Madam Malkin's, whether she was a princess. Because her father forbade the friendship, she spent two years making herself his enemy instead. In her second year she was possessed by Tom Riddle's diary, and Harry saved her in the Chamber of Secrets. In her third she saved the hippogriff Buckbeak from the executioner's axe, and Harry from a Garou. By the summer of 1994 she was Harry's friend, as well as Hermione Granger's friend and rival. She was also the girl Harry had at last admitted to himself that he loved.

Early life

Dracina was born on 5 June 1980, the only child of Lucius Malfoy and Narcissa Malfoy, born Narcissa Black. The Malfoys are a pure-blood family of Dark wizards who came over with the Norman Conquest. She grew up at Malfoy Manor, which she later called the biggest, most beautiful cage in Wiltshire. It has forty bedrooms, with a wing of her own, an orangery, her mother's roses, peacocks on the lawn and a music room. There is a great woven hanging of Saint George in the east drawing room, and a family tree covers the whole of one drawing-room wall. The house also holds her father's collection of dark objects, and there is an armoury in the cellar.

She had a pony, and a governess who spent six years drilling her into the small, neat, spiky hand she writes to this day. A dancing master came by Floo from Paris to teach her ballet. When she was eight she was afraid of the peacocks, so her father had them moved. He had the lake frozen, too, so that she could skim stones on it.

It was a lonely childhood. Lucius never raised a hand to her, and bought her whatever she screamed for. But he chose every friend she had, Pansy Parkinson, Daphne Greengrass, Vincent Crabbe and Gregory Goyle among them. When she made friends with the gardener's little girl at six, the girl was gone by the end of the week. By nine she had worked out that Crabbe and Goyle reported everything to her father, so she fed them insults to report.

All she wanted was for her father to look at her and be pleased. Instead, for thirteen years, he told her that she was very nearly what a Malfoy should be. Her mother read her stories of knights and princesses. Because Dracina kept falling off her pony, her mother also taught her a healing charm. From the family gamekeeper she learnt a stable boy's whistle, which her mother knew about and her father did not.

Book One: first year, 1991 to 1992

Dracina met Harry in Madam Malkin's in the summer of 1991. She offered him her hand palm down, to be kissed, as was due to a witch of good family. When he asked her, quite seriously, whether she was a princess, two spots of pink came into her cheeks. Wizards had no princesses, she told him, though she could see why he had made the mistake. She called Hagrid a drunken servant, and asked whether Harry's dead parents had been 'our sort'. After he had gone she went on gazing at the door long after the bell had stopped ringing.

On the train he refused her hand, and her guidance about the wrong sort. Her eyes stayed on him as she left, like someone who has seen a thing in a shop window and already decided to have it. The Sorting Hat called Slytherin before it had touched her hair, and she looked disappointed when Harry went to Gryffindor.

Her first year ran on a contradiction. She called Hermione a Mudblood in their first week. When Harry turned down her offer of an alliance she coined 'Pottyhead' for him, and she flew Neville's Remembrall up into an oak. Yet when Harry, raging on the Quidditch pitch, shouted out what the Dursleys had done to him, she began to cry. She stammered an apology that only Oliver Wood heard, and she never once used the crueller insults he had handed her.

On Hallowe'en she was the troll's first target in the girls' toilets. She never took her eyes off Harry while he fought it. Afterwards she lied to Professor McGonagall to protect him and Ron. At his first match she went white, with her hands over her mouth, when his broom was jinxed, and she cheered when Slytherin lost. She delivered her mother's invitation to spend Christmas at Malfoy Manor, and stood alone under the mistletoe. In Potions she corrected his stirring. At the Hufflepuff match she clawed Ron's face, then bit his ear, screaming about Harry and the company he kept.

In the Forbidden Forest she was left with Harry and the only lamp. She claimed the favour he owed her, took his hand and called him Harry for the first time. She was radiant: her knight was protecting his princess. A unicorn came to her, and let her touch its neck. Quirrell had brought the detention there because unicorns will come to the pure of heart, and not to a man like him. When a hooded figure killed it she ran with the lamp. Three times on the way back she began a sentence with 'I', and could not finish it.

On the night of the trapdoor she was kind to Neville to get the Gryffindor password, and came to apologise. Hermione put a Full Body-Bind on her, but Harry accepted the apology. A twinkle came into her silver eyes, meant for him alone. Dumbledore took a hundred points from Slytherin for her trespass, which cost them the House Cup. She wept at the table. At King's Cross she warned Harry, almost worriedly, to watch out next year.

Book Two: second year, 1992 to 1993

In the summer of 1992 she ordered the family house-elf, Dobby, to warn Harry of danger at Hogwarts. Dobby misread the order and tried to stop him instead. From Dobby she learnt about the cupboard, the bread and the bars on Harry's window. She lay awake over it.

In Borgin and Burkes her father warned her that it was imprudent to seem obsessed with the Potter boy. He shamed her, too, because a girl of no wizard family beat her in every exam. At Flourish and Blotts she bullied Ginny Weasley until Ginny threw books at her head. Ordered to pick them up, she swept up the whole heap, a small black book among them, and kept it. In late August she found Tom Riddle's diary in her bag. She began writing in it every night, because it was the only thing that had ever listened to her.

She became Slytherin Seeker on the strength of her father's gift to the team of seven Nimbus Two Thousand and Ones. She blushed when she thought Harry had called her pretty. She had a hair-pulling fight with Hermione on the Quidditch pitch. All through the autumn the diary drained her. She grew grey and sleepless, talking to an empty bench she called Tom. She lost hours at a time; once she woke in the out-of-order bathroom with wet shoes and red marks on her hands.

Riddle walked her about the castle while she believed she was asleep. He opened the Chamber with her mouth, set the Basilisk on Muggle-borns with her voice and wrote on the walls with her hands. On Hallowe'en a red stain ran down her pointing finger as she told Hermione that she would be next. The last word Harry heard from her was 'Mine'. In the Slytherin match she threw her broom across the path of a rogue Bludger to shield Harry. While he slept in the hospital wing she cried at his bedside, and left him sugared violets tied with a ribbon from her Quidditch plaits.

At the Duelling Club, grey and feverish, she conjured the snake that Harry turned in Parseltongue. Her face lit up as if she were in church: it was him, she whispered, and it always had been. Snape, looking only at her, went grey with recognition and muttered 'Foolish girl'. Ambrose Greyhame was watching unseen. He felt a cold, whispering thing fastened over her heart, a piece of someone poured into a vessel to make its bearer love it and need it.

At Christmas she told two boys she took for Crabbe and Goyle about her lost time. They were Harry and Ron. When Harry took the diary she turned out every trunk in the Slytherin dormitories. On Boxing Day she came barefoot to the Great Hall in her nightdress, raving that a thief had taken her 'precious'. She beat Harry with her fists until Dumbledore laid a hand on her head. He announced that she had Morrigan's Fever.

She took the diary back on the eve of the Hufflepuff match, together with Harry's match scarf. From then on Riddle possessed her completely, so that she seemed radiant and well. Possessed, she struck Ginny down with the diary and dragged her into the Chamber. Riddle would have drained Dracina's life to rebuild himself if Ginny had not followed.

Harry found her collapsing at the feet of Slytherin's statue in his stolen scarf: 'You came... He said you'd come.' She woke to see him behead the Basilisk while he stood over her, and she saw him as Saint George. She cradled him as he lay dying, saying his name over and over. She healed Ginny's cut with her mother's charm. In McGonagall's office she confessed until Harry's hand on her shoulder silenced her, and Dumbledore cleared her. Her part was never made public.

In the hospital wing she and Harry laughed together for the first time. They agreed to be friends, on condition that he admitted she was the superior witch. She told him that she too had seen the man in the white robe by the pillar. Molly Weasley thanked her, then sweetly promised to kill her slowly if she ever broke Harry's heart.

Book Three: third year, 1993 to 1994

For Harry's thirteenth birthday she wrote to him from the Manor on cream parchment embossed with a serpent-pierced M. The letter came with a green ribbon, a lady's token of favour, which her mother insisted on. She wrote that her father had forbidden the letter, and that she did not miss him. She would like, she wrote, to see three items from the cellar used slowly on a fat man who fed a boy through a hole. She ended with 'Burn this'. At home she told the Chamber story eleven times, and each time the Basilisk grew, until it reached eighty feet.

On the train she insulted Ron for her escorts' benefit while signalling to Harry to play along. During the dementor attack she burst into the Weasley twins' compartment, demanding that someone fetch him. At the carriages she gave him a dozen chocolate violets she had spent four days decorating, one of them with a tiny H.

She was jealous of Hermione, and mimicked her with an antisemitic slur. When Buckbeak bowed to Harry, she wanted the hippogriff for her own. She insulted Buckbeak, and he slashed her down her right arm. Overnight she wrote, left-handed, a four-page letter meant to have Hagrid gone by Christmas and Buckbeak dead by Easter. Then she decided not to send it. She told Harry so in Potions, after Snape had warned them that friendships end over a single word. Pansy Parkinson had already posted it.

Her boggart was her father, saying that she was always second and not a real Malfoy. She wept, then turned him into a drunken tramp begging for 20p. For weeks she was publicly kind to everyone Harry cared for. She wore her silk sling for two months as a prop. On Hallowe'en night she wriggled across the Great Hall in her sleeping bag to lie beside him, and told him that nobody had ever been awake for him.

At the hurricane match she was halfway over the rail when Harry fell, until Pansy caught her cloak. Afterwards she declared that nobody was permitted to kill him. She moved from stand to stand to watch Gryffindor practise. She gave him her mother's dragon-hide gloves, skimmed stones with him on the frozen lake and lent him her spare Nimbus.

Marcus Flint and Montague said she had gone soft on Potter. They threatened to write to her father. So, not knowing that Harry already believed she had lied about the letter, she let them bully her into posing as a dementor at the Ravenclaw match. She insisted on riding on top, on Goyle's shoulders, so that she could see. She had practised Arresto Momentum every night for a week, so that she could catch Harry if he fell. When he turned his back on her, her guilt was there for anyone to see.

Days later her father's letter, sealed in green wax, thanked her for her four pages. She begged him to drop the case. For a week she hunted Harry with notes, which he burnt unread. After he pelted her with mud she would not let Snape clean her hair, saying that she deserved it. Snape told her that she still had a chance to do something instead of just saying something.

On the castle steps she fought Hermione, whom she suspected of posting the letter. She begged Harry to believe her, swearing on her mother. When he embraced her she wept with happiness, and resolved that doing kind things mattered more than saying them. In secret she studied the stake and chain that held Buckbeak, then the slope down to the Forest. She borrowed the hippogriff books, practised bowing to a suit of armour and left a dead ferret on Hagrid's doorstep.

She made Harry his first Easter egg. In the Quidditch final she took a Bludger meant for him, and let him win. She whispered corrections to him in the Potions exam. At sunset on the day of the execution she threw Buckbeak a dead ferret, and swung on to his back as Macnair's axe fell. She flew him into the Forest, waving to the castle.

When the werewolf found Harry in the Forest she dived on Buckbeak to his rescue, and was thrown into a stream. Behind his shield she whispered that she loved him, but he did not hear. She sobbed out her apologies for everything she had ever said. He carried her out of the water and forgave her. She covered Lupin with her cloak, and learnt that her mother's cousin Sirius Black was innocent. Then she flew Harry and Hermione round the back of the castle. For the flight she put Harry's hands on her waist, calling it an old custom.

On the dock of Myst Island she broke down, and told them about the cage at the Manor. Hermione held her, and offered her friendship. Dracina accepted it, the first thing she had ever chosen for herself. The two of them agreed to be friends and rivals for Harry, each certain that she would win.

Back at the castle she whistled Buckbeak up to Flitwick's window. She held Harry's clenched fist as he resolved to change the wizarding world, and told him he would make them all pay. She made him promise that her father would never know. Dumbledore told her that he had always known she had it in her.

When Pansy confessed to posting the letter, Dracina flew at her, until Ron talked her into forgiveness. She wrote Molly Weasley nine pages about the Dursleys in green ink. At the feast she raised her goblet very slightly to Harry. On the train she slipped him a note telling him to write through her owl, Juniper, because her father never read Juniper's post.

Book Four: the summer of 1994

Her letter for Harry's fourteenth birthday came by Juniper. It told him to answer 'How are you?' properly. It reported that the cellar held four things she would like to see used on Vernon Dursley, and one for Petunia. It announced that she and Hermione had come to an understanding, with the help of one other person. Her father had asked after Harry at Sunday dinner. Her mother had calmly claimed that Severus said the boy was very well, and asked whether he still had his father's hair. Dracina promised him a present, chosen the year before, to be given in person at a proper moment. She ended 'P.S. Burn this. P.P.S. Don't forget me.' The last line made Harry's scar sear.

In his dream that August she appeared barefoot, in a long, scaled, dark blue circus dress. She clapped as he killed, embraced him and turned into a midnight-blue snake with slitted silver eyes.

Appearance and personality

Dracina has a pale, pointed, fine-boned face and silver eyes the colour of a new Sickle. Her hair is straight and silver-blonde. It reached her waist at eleven, and she often wears it plaited into a crown. At eleven and twelve she was taller than Harry. At thirteen she was very nearly as tall, and she indignantly denies that he has outgrown her. Her sly, lopsided grin is her father's. She huffs, tosses her hair and puts her nose in the air. She snaps her fingers for Crabbe and Goyle. She carries the scent of cold flowers.

She is proud, imperious and spoilt. She is quick to scream, and capable of real cruelty. From their first year she called Hermione a Mudblood almost every week, sneering at her 'people' and their 'kabalistic sorcery'. She bullied Neville and Ginny. She offered, quite seriously, to see dark objects used on the Dursleys. She is jealous and possessive. Her word is 'mine'. The morning after Cho Chang flirted with Harry, Cho's bag split on the marble staircase.

Yet she keeps Harry's secrets. She prizes accuracy ('I'm not being kind, I'm being accurate'). She exaggerates the stories she loves, and giggles helplessly at his jokes. Once she has seen what is right, she will plan for weeks to do it. Under it all lie self-loathing and a hunger for her father's approval. From her mother's stories she sees herself as a princess, and Harry as her knight. She has thought of him as 'my Harry' since she was eleven.

Abilities

Dracina is a strong flier. She claims once to have outflown a Muggle helicopter, though Madam Hooch told her that she had been holding her broom wrong for years. As Seeker she caught the Snitch against Ravenclaw in January 1994 with four inches to spare. She flew Buckbeak beautifully, steering with her knees and her voice.

She is Snape's favourite, and a natural at practical Potions. She uses techniques learnt at home that are not in the book, such as putting the daisy roots in before the fig. Hermione beats her in examinations all the same. She duels fiercely, with Everte Statum, Tarantallegra, Densaugeo and Serpensortia. She took full marks in Lupin's obstacle-course exam. She knows a healing charm, and in the dark tunnel to the Chamber she saw better than the others.

She dances and rides. She decorates chocolates with a brush. She writes in a small, neat, spiky hand, pressed so hard into the parchment that the words come through on the back.

Relationships

Harry is the centre of her life. Forbidden to be his friend, she made herself his enemy, and hated every minute of it. He was the only person who had ever properly looked at her. She counts three times that he has saved her life: from a troll, from a basilisk, and from a werewolf in a stream. She watches him closely enough to notice when he comes back thinner. She found their secret friendship romantic, like something out of one of her mother's books. She believed that she knew what he wanted better than he did.

For years Hermione was 'the thing standing in his light'. Their war ran from hair-pulling on the Quidditch pitch, and three scratches down Hermione's cheek, to a punch on the castle steps. Hermione admitted to tampering with Dracina's heirloom brooch, and with her hair ribbons. On Myst they became friends, though never allies where Harry is concerned. They spent the summer of 1994 writing to each other.

She bit Ron's ear in their first year, leaving a crescent scar, and she calls him the Weasel. But she conceded that he had a fair point about the Basilisk. It was Ron who talked her down from her fury at Pansy. She bullied Ginny, struck her down under the diary and then healed her. She watched the Weasleys round Ginny's bed the way Harry had once looked into the Mirror of Erised.

Her father forbade the friendship with Harry. She remarked that he had never forbidden her anything she did not then go and do. Her mother helps her in secret. From her grandmother Black she has a silver serpent brooch with emerald eyes, which she wears in her hair. Pansy Parkinson is her closest friend. Pansy posted the Buckbeak letter, believing it was what Dracina wanted. Crabbe and Goyle are her escorts. They are also her father's informants. Snape favours her. He rebuked her for disrespecting McGonagall, and in 1994 he saw her weep over a person for the first time.

Faith

Dracina was raised in a wizarding world that despises Christianity. Yet she believes that Saint George was a wizard who rode out and killed the dragon. She remembers that the Saint George on her mother's hanging in the east drawing room has black hair. She saw Harry behead the Basilisk as Saint George.

She also saw the man by the fallen pillar. He was fair-skinned, long-haired and bearded, in a plain white robe with no badge or house. She described him before Harry had said a word. She was the first person Harry told that he believed it had been Jesus.

At the lake she watched the white stag, and the arrow out of the sky, with her lips pressed together. She was thinking of the Chamber, and she said nothing at all.

Secrets and ancestry

Her parents' feelings about Harry are not what she believes. At Hogwarts Narcissa Black fought her sister Bellatrix over James Potter for years, with hexes and with flowers, until Lily Evans won him. Narcissa now secretly encourages her daughter's romance. She is delighted by the idea of a Potter marrying a Malfoy at last, and charmed by Harry's chivalry. It was she who sent Ganymede with the birthday letter, and she who insisted on the green ribbon.

Lucius forbids the friendship because of the Dark Mark on his left forearm. He knows that it will compel him to fight Harry for his master, and so hurt his daughter. He has told her none of this. He has come to like Harry, and but for the Mark he would be glad to see them marry. Dracina, whose boggart is his disappointment, knows nothing of it.

Ambrose Greyhame, who is Gandalf, saw in her eyes the clear, bright silver of starlight on still water, of mist on a river at dawn in a very old wood. He remembered a prince of the forest folk, a lightfoot archer with an infuriating habit of keeping score: Legolas of Mirkwood. The Malfoys, for their part, claim to have been in Britain before there was a Britain. Dumbledore judged her fair, fierce and clever. She was so much in love with Harry, he thought, that she would burn the whole world down to keep him in it.

The diary marked her. She spoke of it as Gollum spoke of the Ring, as 'my precious'. The thing Greyhame sensed on her heart had been made in the same way as the One Ring. On the first day of her third year Lupin narrowed his eyes at her like a man catching a scent he knew. In the Forest the Garou turned towards her as if it smelt something on her. Harry took it for the residue of the diary, which had written itself into her head.

Loose ends

Dracina is one of only five people at Hogwarts who know what happened on the night that Sirius Black, Buckbeak and Peter Pettigrew vanished. Her alibi, a wrist sprained on the dungeon steps, was Pansy's arrangement. At the Manor, her father said, the portraits left their frames whenever she came in to tell the Chamber story yet again.

In her second year Harry once saw her in the library with an old picture book, open at a knight in silver armour who knelt to offer his sword to a pale-haired girl in a tower. She slammed it shut so that he would not see. The picture found its echo in the Chamber, when he stood over her with a sword. She has promised Harry a present, chosen in 1993, that cannot be sent by owl. It has not yet been given.

In their own words

You are supposed to kiss it. It's how one greets a witch of good family. Everybody knows that.Dracina Malfoy · B1 Ch1
Fine then, pottyhead!Dracina Malfoy · B1 Ch4
You will escort me, Potter. It's your duty as a wizard to escort a young witch.Dracina Malfoy · B1 Ch11
Stupid Potter, did you get yourself a girlfriend?Dracina Malfoy · B2 Ch5

pages.html:
Rubeus Hagrid is the gamekeeper of Hogwarts and, since 1993, its teacher of Care of Magical Creatures. He is a huge, bearded half-giant who lives in a hut at the edge of the Forbidden Forest, and he loves every creature all the more for being dangerous. He was the first friend Harry Potter ever had. In 1981 he carried Harry out of the ruins of his parents' house, and ten years later he was the one who brought him back into the wizarding world.

Early life and expulsion

Rubeus Hagrid was born on 6 December 1928, the son of a wizard and the giantess Fridwulfa. His mother left when he was about three, so it was his father who brought him up. His father died while Hagrid was in his second year at Hogwarts, and the funeral is among the worst memories of his life. He had been sorted into Gryffindor. A traveller gave him an egg from a distant land, and he raised the spider that hatched from it, Aragog, in a cupboard in the castle on scraps from the table.

In June 1943 the prefect Tom Riddle caught him trying to smuggle a creature out of the castle in a wooden box. Hagrid insisted that it had never killed anybody. He was blamed for opening the Chamber of Secrets, and for the death of a girl. He was expelled in his third year, and his wand was snapped. Albus Dumbledore believed in him, and saw to it that he was kept on as gamekeeper. Aragog escaped into the Forest. Hagrid found him a wife there, Mosag, and visits him still.

Gamekeeper

Hagrid lives in a one-roomed wooden hut on the edge of the Forest, with a crossbow by the door and his boarhound, Fang. In the 1960s, when he was a shaggy gamekeeper in his thirties, he gave a bullied Muggle-born Slytherin called John Constantine tea, tooth-breaking rock cakes and somewhere to hide. The two of them are friends still. Lucius Malfoy describes him as practically wild, the sort of man who sets his own bed alight when he has been drinking.

On the night the Potters died in 1981, Hagrid carried the infant Harry out of the ruins of the house. A white and shaking Sirius Black begged to take the baby. Hagrid had his orders from Dumbledore, so he refused, and comforted Black instead. Black gave him his flying motorbike to carry Harry to the Dursleys.

Personality and appearance

Hagrid is twice the height of an ordinary man, with a great tangled beard and black eyes like beetles. In winter he wears a moleskin overcoat, rabbit-fur gloves and beaverskin boots. His tea is as good as his baking is bad. He knits. He once spent a whole afternoon coaxing a bird with a broken wing to eat scrambled egg, and in December 1991 he nursed the storm-battered owls by his fire.

He cannot keep a secret, and he trusts too easily. He is fiercely loyal to Dumbledore and to Harry. He refuses to blame a creature for its nature: 'Can' be cross with a grub fer bein' a grub.'

In the saga: 1991 to 1992

Hagrid found Harry in a hut on a rock in the sea and gave him his first birthday cake. He took him to Diagon Alley, where the Gringotts carts turned Hagrid green. He met the first-years at the station with a lantern, and he asked Harry to tea in his first week. He watched Harry's first match through enormous binoculars, and lent Dean Thomas a Gryffindor scarf to wear over his West Ham one. He had bought the three-headed dog Fluffy from a man in a pub whom he took for a Greek, though the man was really a Traveller with a caravan. Hagrid lent the dog to Dumbledore to guard the Philosopher's Stone. He also let slip that the guarded object had something to do with Nicolas Flamel.

Hagrid had always wanted a dragon. In the spring of 1992 he won a Norwegian Ridgeback egg at cards from a hooded stranger in the Hog's Head. The stranger bought him drinks, and learnt from him that Fluffy falls asleep to music. Hagrid hatched Norbert in his fire and called himself the dragon's mummy. He sobbed as he sent him off to Romania in a crate packed with rats, brandy and a teddy bear. When he understood that the stranger had been working for Voldemort, he blamed himself for the danger to the Stone and swore never to drink again. For Christmas he gave Harry a hand-carved flute that sounded like an owl. At the end of the year he gave him a leather album of photographs of James and Lily, collected by owling their old school friends.

In the saga: 1992 to 1993

In August 1992 he found Harry lost in Knockturn Alley, where Hagrid himself had gone for Flesh-Eating Slug Repellent. In Flourish and Blotts he pulled Arthur Weasley and Lucius Malfoy apart. Then he declared the whole Malfoy family rotten to the core. He told Gilderoy Lockhart that he had never read his books. He grew vast pumpkins with an Engorgement Charm, cast with his old wand from inside his flowery pink umbrella. When his roosters began to die, he burst into Dumbledore's office to swear that Harry was innocent. There was not a dark bone in Harry's parents, he said, nor one in Harry.

In the spring Cornelius Fudge took him to Azkaban as a precaution, because of his record. As he went, he accused Lucius of blackmailing the governors. For the benefit of Harry and Ron, who were hiding in the hut, he said that anyone wanting to find something out need only follow the spiders. Somebody, he added, would have to feed Fang. He was freed on the night the Chamber was destroyed. He came back at half past three in the morning with Fawkes on his shoulder and the sea still on his coat. Then he clouted Harry and Ron face first into their trifle.

In the saga: 1993 to 1994

When Professor Kettleburn retired, Dumbledore went straight down to Hagrid's hut to offer him the post. The appointment was announced at the start-of-term feast, and Hagrid wiped his eyes on the tablecloth. He had already sent Harry The Monster Book of Monsters for his birthday. At his first lesson he brought a dozen hippogriffs to a paddock. When Buckbeak slashed Dracina Malfoy's arm, Hagrid restrained the hippogriff, told Harry to put his wand away and carried her up to the castle himself. That night he sat drinking from a tankard the size of a bucket, sure that he would be sacked. He put his head in the water butt, then marched the trio back up to the castle, telling Harry that nobody was worth risking himself for, least of all Hagrid. He was sorry even for Dracina: 'yeh don' get ter pick which ones yeh're sorry for.' After that he lost his nerve and taught flobberworms for weeks, until he killed them all with lettuce.

The Ministry cleared Hagrid of blame but upheld Lucius's complaint. Buckbeak was summoned to a hearing before the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures. At Christmas Hagrid had the hippogriff in his cabin with him. He told the trio that in Azkaban his worst days had queued up to sit with him: his expulsion, his father's funeral, the parting with Norbert. He would not go back there, whatever it cost. When the hearing was brought forward, he bought a hairy brown suit for it, with a yellow and orange tie. He became tongue-tied, dropped his notes and lost.

On the day of the execution he threw Walden Macnair into his own pumpkin patch for insulting his giant mother. When Buckbeak broke free and flew into the Forest with a small hooded rider, Hagrid danced among the pumpkins shouting, 'Go on, yeh beauty!' The next morning, red-eyed from celebrating all night, he blessed whoever had snatched the hippogriff. He almost certainly knew who it was. That summer he sent Harry a sack of rock cakes and a birthday cake.

In their own words

There wasn' a dark bone in either of 'em, an' there's not one in you.Rubeus Hagrid · B2 Ch14
If anyone was wantin' ter find somethin' out... all they'd have ter do is follow the spiders.Rubeus Hagrid · B2 Ch16
Put it away. He on'y did what he is.Rubeus Hagrid · B3 Ch6
Can' be cross with a grub fer bein' a grub.Rubeus Hagrid · B3 Ch6

Madam Malkin is a plump, cheerful witch who runs Madam Malkin's Robes for All Occasions in Diagon Alley, where most Hogwarts pupils are fitted for their school robes. It was in her shop, in the summer of 1991, that Harry Potter first met Dracina Malfoy.

The shop

The shop smells of new cloth and warm irons. Its bell tinkles when the door opens. Madam Malkin hurries out to meet each customer with a mouthful of pins, then stands them on a footstool at the back while she works.

She is known for her kindness. She does not remark on the clothes her customers arrive in, however shabby.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter One, Harry came into the shop in Dudley's old jeans and a grey jumper with a hole in the elbow. If Madam Malkin thought anything of the jumper, she kept it to herself. She stood him on a stool next to a girl, whose hem a second witch was pinning up. The girl was Dracina Malfoy.

She fitted the two of them side by side. Just as Dracina asked Harry's surname, Madam Malkin interrupted. ‘That's you finished, my dear,’ she said, and Harry jumped down so quickly that he trod on his own hem.

In Book Two, Chapter One, Harry looked back on that first meeting. He had refused Dracina's hand in Madam Malkin's, and again on the train. Looking at her, he had seen Dudley in a long blonde wig. In Chapter Eight he remembered asking her in the shop whether she was a princess, and the pink she had gone.

In Chapter Nineteen Dracina admitted to herself that she had known since Madam Malkin's, since the first time she looked at him, that Harry was her knight.

In Book Three, Chapter Four, in August 1993, Harry went back for new robes. Madam Malkin stood him on the very same footstool as in 1991 and told him he had grown three inches since the spring. She tutted at his old robes. ‘Somebody's been feeding you at last.’

In Chapter Twenty-One Dracina told Harry that he was the only person who had ever looked at her properly. ‘You were standing on a footstool in Madam Malkin's with pins in your hem. You looked at me, and you asked if I was a princess.’

The second witch at Madam Malkin's is one of Madam Malkin's assistants at her robe shop in Diagon Alley. In the summer of 1991 she pinned up the hem of Dracina Malfoy's long black robes. Her name is not recorded.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter One, Harry Potter came into the shop to be fitted for his first Hogwarts robes. At the back of the shop a girl stood on a footstool while a second witch pinned up her hem. Madam Malkin stood Harry on the stool beside her. The girl was Dracina Malfoy, and that was how the two of them met.

pages.html:
Lucius Malfoy is a pure-blood wizard, the master of Malfoy Manor in Wiltshire, the husband of Narcissa Malfoy and the father of Dracina Malfoy. He is a former governor of Hogwarts with a seat on several Ministry committees. He bears Lord Voldemort's Dark Mark, and in 1992 it was his hand that put Tom Riddle's diary into the world. Against every one of his intentions, he has come to like Harry Potter.

Family and background

The Malfoys came to England from Normandy with William the Conqueror. William himself granted Armand Malfoy the family's land in Wiltshire. Tom Riddle once called the line older even than the Potters'. Lucius keeps the family tree in the drawing room at Malfoy Manor, where it covers an entire wall.

He is tall and pale, with long fair hair. He has the same pointed face and silver eyes as his daughter, though his are as cold as a coin. He wears black gloves and a black travelling cloak, with a silver-topped cane in his hand.

Hogwarts and John Constantine

Lucius started at Hogwarts in 1964, a thin, pale, white-blond boy with a stammer, smaller than the Muggle-born John Constantine. He introduced himself as being 'of the n-noble and ancient house of M-Malfoy'. He was terrified, because a cousin had told him that first-years had to fight a troll to be sorted. Constantine made him laugh, a startled, unpractised laugh, as though he seldom did. Lucius was sorted into Slytherin straight after John, and hurried over to sit beside him.

For four years the two boys sat together in every lesson. When John was poisoned, Lucius read aloud to him in the hospital wing. In public Lucius still repeated his father's views on blood. In private he told John that he was different, an exception. At fifteen Lucius grew tall and handsome, but the girls passed him over for John. He drifted into a set with old names and cold eyes. Later they would have a master, and a mark burnt into their arms. By the sixth year he had mostly lost his stammer. He watched John with open jealousy.

In March of their seventh year Lucius ambushed Constantine over a Ravenclaw girl. He called him a Mudblood for the first time, and fought him until the caretaker, Pringle, pulled them apart. Lucius swore: 'On my b-blood, Constantine. You'll p-pay for this. Every drop.' Constantine has detested him ever since, as everything that is wrong with pure-bloods.

The first war

After leaving Hogwarts in 1971 Lucius joined Lord Voldemort and took the Dark Mark on his left forearm, the same Mark that Severus Snape carries. Arthur Weasley believes he stood in the inner circle. He married Narcissa Black, six or seven years his junior, after she left school in 1978. Their only child, Dracina, was born in 1980.

When Voldemort fell in 1981, the Malfoys were among the first families to come back to the wizarding side, claiming that they had been bewitched. Lucius escaped Azkaban on that claim, helped along by generous gifts of gold to the right causes. Arthur Weasley never believed a word of it. Lucius keeps a large collection of Dark artefacts, part of it in a hidden room beneath the drawing-room floor at the Manor and part in the cellar. Some of the pieces have not been used in anger for a century.

Influence

Lucius sat on the Board of Governors of Hogwarts until June 1993, and he still sits on several Ministry committees. Cornelius Fudge calls him a very generous man to all sorts of good causes. Even after his removal from the Board, half the governors still go pale when his owl arrives. The office of the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures is frightened of him. The executioner, Walden Macnair, is an old friend.

As a father

Lucius has never raised a hand to Dracina, and he spoils her. When she was eight and frightened of the peacocks, he had them moved. That same year he had the lake frozen so that she could skate. He buys her things when she screams. He has also chosen every one of her friends for the use of their fathers. When she made friends at six with the gardener's little girl, he sent the child away.

Dracina believes that she has never once been looked at as something to be proud of. He tells her she is very nearly what a Malfoy should be. Her boggart takes his shape. It sighs over her that she is always second, not a real Malfoy, the first Malfoy in eleven hundred years to come second.

Secrets

Lucius forbids any attachment between Dracina and Harry because of the Dark Mark. He knows that when his master returns, the Mark will compel him to fight Harry on Voldemort's behalf, and that it will break his daughter's heart. He has told her none of this.

In truth Harry has won him over. If it were not for the Mark, he would be content to see Harry marry Dracina. He will never admit it.

When he told Harry that Potters had been kings before they were Potters, he knew exactly what he meant. The Potters descend from King Arthur Pendragon, by a documented line that Lucius, unlike almost everybody else, has taken the trouble to look up. Of Lily Potter's ancestry he knows nothing at all beyond her birth to Muggles.

In the saga: 1991 to 1993

During Dracina's first year Lucius was mostly a voice in her conversation, full of opinions about house teams, Hagrid and Weasleys. Professor Quirrell later revealed that it was Lucius who had arranged the Ministry owl that took Dumbledore to London on the night Quirrell went after the Philosopher's Stone.

In August 1992, fearing raids by the Ministry, he sold poisons and other objects from the Manor to Mr Borgin of Borgin and Burkes. Harry, hidden in a cabinet, overheard him warn Dracina that it was imprudent for a young witch to seem obsessed with a young wizard. Lucius muttered that 'Cissy' had been putting fanciful ideas about the cursed Potter boy into her head. He laid a gentle hand on Dracina's shoulder and said he hoped she would amount to more than a thief. Then he rebuked her for letting a Muggle-born beat her in every exam.

At Flourish and Blotts he sneered at the Weasleys and the Grangers until Arthur Weasley threw the first punch. He took an Encyclopaedia of Toadstools in the eye before Hagrid separated them. In the confusion, on Voldemort's instruction, he slipped Tom Riddle's diary into Ginny Weasley's old Transfiguration book. But Dracina swept up the spilled books, and the diary went home with her. When Dracina became Seeker he bought the whole Slytherin Quidditch team Nimbus Two Thousand and Ones. He had Arthur fined fifty Galleons over the flying car, and demanded his resignation in the Daily Prophet.

Lucius would not tell Dracina about the last opening of the Chamber of Secrets. He hinted that a Muggle-born had died. He told her to keep out of danger and let the Heir get on with it, though she thought his heart was not in it. Then he forced Dumbledore's suspension with the signatures of all twelve governors. Several of them said that he had threatened to curse their families.

At the end of the school year, in Professor McGonagall's office, Lucius learnt that his own daughter had carried the diary and been possessed by it. He went white. Had anybody but Dracina held it, he would have let the attacks go on. Harry handed him the ruined diary wrapped in a sock. Lucius threw the sock away; his house-elf, Dobby, caught it, and was free. Lucius nearly drew on Harry. Then he laughed: 'Fair play, Potter. Fair play. That was well done.'

In private he told Harry that he had been instructed, and that 'One does not decline'. Voldemort, he said, knew magic that was old when the castle was a hill, and was barely a man any more. Harry's mockery of his master made him laugh. He told Harry he would have done well in Slytherin. Almost to himself, he added that he began to see what Dracina saw in him. He visited Dracina's hospital bed to tell her, in his Ministry voice, that she was not to befriend Harry. Being close to him, he said, was a very dangerous place to stand. At the end of the year he was dismissed from the Board of Governors.

In the saga: 1993 to 1994

Through the summer of 1993 Lucius forbade Dracina to write to Harry. He was in a peculiar mood, saying 'fair play' at breakfast and looking annoyed with himself. He later admitted that forbidding her had been approximately as effective as forbidding the tide.

In August 1993 he met Harry near Knockturn Alley and walked him back down Diagon Alley. He complained that he had heard the story of the Chamber from Dracina eleven times, with the Basilisk growing to eighty feet; Harry told him it was fifty. He knew about Aunt Marge from the Ministry, and he was coldly furious. Lily Potter had been a Mudblood he never cared for, but she was a witch. Had that woman said such a thing in his house, she would have left in a smaller box, chosen by his wife. 'And this woman is still breathing.' He told Harry that 'Potters have been kings before they were Potters', and that blood was a fact like the colour of one's eyes, not a prejudice. Harry should stop living, he said, as though he were a Muggle. He had never heard of Khan Noonien Singh, Superman or Spider-Man, and he dismissed the Muggle wars as their own business.

When Harry answered that Muggle heroes save people, just as he had gone down the pipe for Dracina, Lucius flared with white anger. All through the conversation his free hand had gone, quite unconsciously, to his own left forearm. Walking away, he muttered that the boy was exceedingly hard to dislike, and that Cissy was not helping. He looked back at Harry with naked fear before his face broke into his daughter's sly, lopsided grin.

After Buckbeak injured Dracina in September 1993, Lucius took his complaint to the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures, and it was upheld. Pansy Parkinson had taken Dracina's angry four-page letter to the Owlery, although Dracina had never meant to send it. Lucius put it before the Committee. He had the hearing brought forward from 20 April to a Friday in March 1994, and wrote to thank his daughter in a letter sealed with green wax. He ignored her plea to drop the case. At the hearing the Committee did as he said. He writes to Dracina every week, and he reads Crabbe's post, though never that of her owl, Juniper.

In the summer of 1994 he asked Dracina at dinner how Harry was, and whether Dumbledore had sent him back to his Muggles, which he called a scandal. Then he told her once again to have nothing to do with him.

In their own words

We're dignified purebloods. Unlike some wizards.Lucius Malfoy · B2 Ch5
I was instructed, Potter. Do you understand what that means, from him? One does not decline.Lucius Malfoy · B2 Ch19
And I think that I begin to see what she sees in you.Lucius Malfoy · B2 Ch19
Fair play, Potter. Fair play. That was well done.Lucius Malfoy · B2 Ch19

pages.html:
Narcissa Malfoy, born Narcissa Black, is the wife of Lucius Malfoy and the mother of Dracina Malfoy. She keeps every old pure-blood custom there is. She is also, quietly and against her husband's express wishes, the chief ally of her daughter's attachment to Harry Potter, who is the son of the boy she lost to Lily Evans.

Early life

Narcissa was born into the House of Black, one of the oldest and proudest of the pure-blood families. Her parents were Cygnus Black and Druella Rosier. Her sister Bellatrix was born within the same twelve months. The two girls started at Hogwarts together in 1971, in the same year as James Potter, Lily Evans and the sisters' cousin Sirius Black. A third sister, Andromeda, was later disowned by the family for marrying the Muggle-born Ted Tonks. Bellatrix was black-haired; Narcissa was fair.

At school both sisters decided that James Potter was theirs. Professor Flitwick remembers them feuding across his Charms classroom for years, with hexes and with flowers. Remus Lupin remembers Bellatrix trying to hex her sister's eyebrows off. Once the two of them fought in the entrance hall while James stood between them, looking bewildered. The rivalry caused James great distress, and the other Marauders teased him about it without mercy. It ended only when Lily Evans came along and won him. Flitwick says that neither sister ever quite forgave anybody afterwards.

Marriage and family

After she left Hogwarts in 1978, Narcissa married Lucius Malfoy. Their daughter Dracina was born on 5 June 1980. Lucius calls his wife Cissy, as her cousin Sirius does. In the east drawing room at Malfoy Manor she keeps a woven hanging of Saint George, and she grows roses in the Manor gardens.

When Dracina was a little girl, Narcissa read her stories of knights protecting princesses. She arranged years of lessons for her at the Manor with a man from Paris. Because Dracina kept falling off her pony, her mother taught her a healing charm. Narcissa describes a boggart as something that wears your fear like a coat, a definition Lupin called sensible. She knows, as Lucius does not, that Dracina learnt to whistle from the gamekeeper.

She is a stickler for the old customs. Gifts of consequence, she says, are not sent by post. It is unlucky, too, to throw away a favour ribbon.

Her reasons

Narcissa encourages her daughter's romance with Harry Potter in secret. She lost James to Lily, so she loves the idea of a Potter marrying a Malfoy at last: her daughter need not lose the son. She finds Harry's chivalry genuinely romantic. At Madam Malkin's, Harry asked Dracina quite seriously whether she was a princess, and Dracina has seen herself as one ever since. Narcissa thinks that charming. She thinks it just as charming that Dracina sees Harry as the knight from the stories her mother used to read her.

She does not know why Lucius forbids it. His reason is the Dark Mark on his arm, of which he has told neither his wife nor his daughter.

In the saga: Narcissa and Harry Potter

In December 1991, during Dracina's first year, Narcissa asked her daughter to invite Harry Potter to Malfoy Manor for Christmas. Dracina told Harry that her mother must have taken leave of her senses. Harry laughed the invitation off as a prank. By the summer of 1992 Lucius was muttering that Cissy had been putting fanciful ideas about the Potter boy into Dracina's head.

In July 1993, with Lucius forbidding all contact, Narcissa helped Dracina write to Harry for his thirteenth birthday. She found out when the birthday was. She sent her own eagle owl, Ganymede, across three counties to Surrey. She insisted that the letter be tied with a green ribbon, the old token of a lady's favour. Harry kept the ribbon, and uses it as his bookmark. Lucius complained that his wife had been 'of no assistance whatever'. That winter she sent a pair of dragon-hide gloves, which Dracina passed on to Harry. She could also have had a Nimbus sent up from London on loan.

In the summer of 1994 Lucius asked after Harry at dinner. Narcissa turned him aside with 'Severus tells me the boy is very well indeed', and was careful not to look at her daughter afterwards. Out of nowhere, she asked Dracina whether Harry still had his father's hair.

Sirius Black, on hearing how matters stood, thought that Cissy would be delighted that James's son had won over a Malfoy.

In the saga: in the background

Narcissa has never appeared in Harry's company. In 1991 she was up the street seeing about Dracina's wand, while Harry and Dracina were being fitted for robes. In 1992 Dumbledore told Lucius to tell her himself about Dracina's ordeal in the Chamber of Secrets, adding that he would send his own letter anyway. Shortly before the June 1994 examinations Ganymede brought Dracina a long, soft parcel from home. She hid it on her lap, then carried it out of the Great Hall.

In their own words

Severus tells me the boy is very well indeed.Narcissa Malfoy · B4 Ch2

pages.html:
Petunia Dursley, born Petunia Evans, is the elder sister of Lily Potter, and the aunt with whom Harry Potter was left in 1981. She refused her mother's faith as well as her sister's magic, and she has resented both all her life. Yet her blood carries the same ancient protection that Lily laid on Harry, and her house is the one place where Lord Voldemort cannot touch him.

Family

Petunia is the daughter of Susan Pevensie, once a crowned Queen of Narnia, who survived the railway accident that killed her brothers and sister. Afterwards Susan came back to Christ. She raised her daughters to be godly. Through her, both girls descend from Aragorn and Arwen.

Lily took her mother's faith seriously from childhood, and she turned out to be a witch. Her magic reconciled Susan to her, because in Lily, Susan at last had somebody who could not dismiss Narnia. Petunia refused both halves. She has neither faith nor magic, and her resentment of Lily is the resentment of a sister shut out of two countries at once. As a girl she wrote to Albus Dumbledore asking to be admitted to Hogwarts, and was refused.

She married Vernon Dursley, and their only son, Dudley, was born in June 1980. She is thin, bony and horse-faced, with a long neck that she uses to look over the garden hedge at the neighbours, because she is very nosy. She hates animals. She buys magazines with horoscopes in them and prefers posh wine. She watches every documentary about serial killers that Channel 4 shows, mouth open, tea going cold. On the rare occasions when she has to say the word 'magic', she wrinkles her nose. The only thing about her that is like Lily is her eyes.

When Lily went to Hogwarts, Susan began to tell her daughters about Narnia. Petunia met it with scorn and derision. It drew Lily closer to their mother, and it left Petunia more resentful than ever.

Harry's childhood

Petunia doted on Dudley. Harry she starved, worked and beat. When he overcooked the eggs, she hit him round the head with a frying pan. She hit him with a rolling pin too, and used it to shoo him away from the television. When he was six and down with flu, the most she did was lay a cold flannel on his forehead, telling him not to be sick on the sheets. The same year she watched from the kitchen window while he weeded the flower beds in the heat.

On his sixth birthday she came to the cupboard door and told him, quite kindly, that there was a parcel for him on the kitchen table. It was a pair of Uncle Vernon's old socks wrapped in newspaper. All three Dursleys watched his face while he opened it. When a dinner lady at St Grogory's slipped Harry an extra bread roll every day for a fortnight, Petunia came in to complain about his jumper, and the dinner lady never looked at him again. Nobody ever said 'there, there' to Harry. Petunia said 'There, there, Diddykins' to Dudley through every thunderstorm.

She once warned the two boys about Uncle Vernon's boss, a man with a big nose and curly hair. Years later Harry recognised the same prejudice when Dracina Malfoy mocked Hermione's looks. The family went to church only twice. The first time was one Christmas when Harry was seven, because the Polkisses had started going and Petunia would not be outdone. The second time was to meet a churchwarden who might buy drills.

In the saga: 1992

On Harry's twelfth birthday, 31 July 1992, Dudley claimed that Harry was doing magic. Petunia knew perfectly well that he was not, but she came out of the back door swinging a soapy frying pan at him all the same. Then she made him clean, mow, weed and paint until evening. For the Masons' dinner she wore a salmon-pink cocktail dress. Her pudding of whipped cream and sugared violets ended up on Mrs Mason's head, dropped there by Dobby. While Harry was locked in his room she pushed food through the cat-flap, a bowl of cold tinned soup among it. On one day the family forgot him altogether.

The protection

When Lily died for Harry in 1981 she laid an old protection on him, the magic of the Elves and of Númenor. It lives in his blood, and it lives in Petunia's too. While Harry can call her house his home, and his mother's blood lives under its roof, Voldemort cannot touch him there. That is why Dumbledore insists that Harry go back to Privet Drive every summer.

At the end of Harry's second year, Dumbledore sat on Petunia's sofa. He told her and Vernon that he would know the moment they harmed the boy: 'Not a hand, not a word.' Petunia stopped locking the fridge. On the third night of the summer of 1993 she twitched, fetched a fourth plate and banged it down in front of the empty chair. Then she told Harry to sit. When Vernon raged, she reminded him what the old man had said: 'He said a word. Not a hand, not a word. He didn't say whose.'

In the saga: 1993 to 1994

During Marge Dursley's visit in 1993, Petunia agreed with Marge's complaints about immigrants. She did not agree when Marge urged extreme force on Harry. When Marge began to inflate, Petunia watched Harry rather than Marge, as if a warning she had long expected had come true. When Harry raised his wand, she whispered to Vernon not to move.

In November 1993 she wrote to Harry for the first time in her life: six lines, to say that the school had contacted them and that he was not to come home for Christmas.

On Thursday 18 August 1994 she found the refrigerator full of bleeding rats. She cleaned it out alone, in yellow rubber gloves, crying, 'In my fridge. In my nice, clean fridge...' Afterwards she opened the new one every morning with her eyes shut. That summer she put the whole family on Dudley's diet, making sure that Dudley got more than Harry. On 20 August pond mud came up out of the kitchen plughole and covered her from head to foot. Her hair, which she had put in rollers the night before, was plastered flat to her skull. It was Mrs Weasley's doing.

Sirius Black, who watched the house in the summer of 1993, saw her clipping a hedge that did not need it, peering up and down the road. He remembered that Lily used to talk about her.

In the saga: in Harry's dreams

In Harry's revenge dream of November 1993, Petunia stood at the sink and looked at him with his mother's eyes. In the dream of August 1994 she was the matron of an orphanage at number four. She was dressed in black, with keys at her belt, and she wrote in a ledger without ever looking up. Lily had died in her care, after giving birth on the last night of the year.

In their own words

He said a word. Not a hand, not a word. He didn't say whose.Petunia Dursley · B3 Ch2
In my fridge. In my nice, clean fridge...Petunia Dursley · B4 Ch2
