pages.html:
Vernon Dursley is a Muggle, the director of a drill-making firm called Grunnings, and the husband of Lily Potter's sister Petunia. For ten years he and his wife kept their orphaned nephew, Harry Potter, in the cupboard under the stairs at Number Four, Privet Drive. He struck the boy until the summer of 1993, when Albus Dumbledore came to sit in his front room.

Background

Vernon is a large man with hardly any neck, small sharp eyes and an enormous moustache, which Petunia makes him groom every morning. He was educated at Smeltings, the school Dudley now attends. He runs Grunnings, which makes drills, and in 1993 he had a new company car. He married Petunia Evans, and their son Dudley was born in June 1980.

On 1 November 1981 the infant Harry Potter was left on the Dursleys' doorstep after the murder of his parents. Vernon took him in, but only, as he later told Molly Weasley, as family 'in a manner of speaking'.

Opinions

Vernon holds firm views on almost everything, and he is wrong about most of them. He shouts at the Irish on the television and goes red with rage at reports of IRA attacks. He is in favour of hanging. By the summer of 1993 he had loathed John Major for about a year, ever since the trouble over the pound and the ERM.

He sneers 'Bloody God-botherers' at vicars on the television. He has been to church perhaps twice: once to keep up with the Polkisses, and once to sell drills to a churchwarden. A picture in his study shows a vast bald man in a white suit between two bodyguards, whom Vernon calls, with deep respect, a very successful American businessman. In July 1993 a British National Party membership card fell out of his wallet. He believes that karate teaches a boy 'dominance'. All through the summer of 1994 he complained about the price of petrol.

Above all he forbids any mention of magic in his house. He calls it Harry's abnormality. 'This is a respectable house!'

Harry's childhood

Harry spent about ten years in the cupboard under the stairs, with the spiders and a bolt on the outside. Before he could read he had learnt to keep very still in the dark until Uncle Vernon had gone past. The sound of heavy footsteps in a corridor still makes his shoulders creep up round his ears.

Vernon struck him across the back of the head, for burning the bacon among other things. He kept an old slipper with mould on the heel behind the kitchen door, for beating him. For birthdays he gave Harry a coat-hanger, or a pair of his own old socks. The socks came on his sixth birthday, wrapped in newspaper, with all three Dursleys watching his face.

When the Hogwarts letters began to arrive in 1991, Vernon nailed planks across the letter box with his mouth full of nails. He swore when they came down the chimney instead.

In the saga: 1992

In the summer of 1992 Vernon padlocked Harry's school things in the cupboard and Hedwig in her cage. On 31 July he forgot Harry's birthday altogether. Instead he rehearsed the family for a dinner at which he hoped to sell an enormous order of drills to a rich builder, Mr Mason, and then buy a villa in Majorca. Dobby's falling pudding ruined it, along with the Ministry owl that landed on Mrs Mason, who was terrified of birds. Vernon asked Mr Mason whether 'their people' were always nervous of birds, and Mr Mason stormed out.

When he learnt that Harry was not allowed to use magic outside school, Vernon locked him in his bedroom. He paid a man to put bars on the window, whistling as it was done. He fitted a cat-flap in the door himself, to push food through, and swore that Harry would never go back to Hogwarts. He claimed the lock was the kind they fit in prisons. Fred and George Weasley picked it with a piece of wire in under a minute. As Harry climbed out of the window into the Weasleys' flying car, Vernon seized his ankle and left a ring of bruises.

In the saga: 1993

At the end of Harry's second year Albus Dumbledore called on Vernon and Petunia. He sat on their sofa and promised them that he would know the moment they used a hand or a word against Harry. Vernon never laid a finger on him again. Whenever he moved to strike, he twitched and froze. He let Hedwig out at night and gave Harry a plate at every dinner, though he still goes purple when Harry comes into a room. He told Petunia that he would not have 'that man' in his house again, whatever it took. When Ron Weasley telephoned that summer, Vernon answered in his sales voice, then bellowed that there was no Harry Potter there.

On 31 July 1993 he announced that his sister Marge was coming for a week. Harry was to pretend that he attended St Brutus's Secure Centre for Incurably Criminal Boys. Harry blackmailed him with the BNP card into promising to sign his Hogsmeade form. Vernon gagged on his rage. He muttered 'torture', 'psychological damage' and 'said he'd know', then gave in: 'I'll sign the bloody form, you cursed child, just do what I say about Marge!'

All that week he told Marge that James Potter had been unemployed, and poured her more brandy while she abused Harry. On the last evening he looked at Harry pleadingly, begging him with his eyes to go upstairs. When Marge inflated, her dog Ripper bit Vernon's leg. Harry held him off at wandpoint while he backed away with his hands raised. He did not sign the form.

In the saga: 1994

At King's Cross in June 1994 Vernon stood well back from the Weasleys. He quailed under Molly Weasley's look, trod on a pigeon and told Harry that he had no godfather.

In August he found the refrigerator full of bleeding rats. He reached for Harry's collar, stopped short and looked out at the garden, as though for a man with a wand. Then he went grey, and left for work an hour early.

Two days later, on 20 August, pond mud erupted from the kitchen plughole, coating Vernon and the kitchen alike. He shouted at the sink. Then he thrust Molly Weasley's heavily stamped invitation to the Quidditch World Cup at Harry, told him to say that he was being looked after, and said that he could go.

In the saga: Harry's dream

In August 1994 Harry dreamt of Vernon as a filthy wretch in a string vest, living in a shack in a wood that was really the cupboard under the stairs, with a dead boa constrictor nailed to the door. This Vernon hissed at Harry. He wore a gold ring with a black stone and had a wand stuck through the rope at his waist. Harry put him to sleep and took both. The dream was a memory of Lord Voldemort's, with Harry's family put in the places of the people in it.

In their own words

I'll sign the bloody form, you cursed child, just do what I say about Marge!Vernon Dursley · B3 Ch2
This is a respectable house! I will not have it, do you hear me? I WILL NOT HAVE IT!Vernon Dursley · B4 Ch3

pages.html:
Dudley Dursley is Harry Potter's cousin, the only son of Vernon and Petunia Dursley. He was spoilt to the bone, and for most of their childhood he was Harry's chief tormentor. Since 1993 he has begun, slowly and to his own surprise, to want to be something better. What he wants to be is a Power Ranger.

Childhood

Dudley is blond, pink and very large; by 1992 his bottom drooped over both sides of the kitchen chair. His parents spoilt him completely. Every year he was given nine or ten Easter eggs while Harry got none, and he had Knickerbocker Glories while Harry got the cheapest lemon ice lolly. He kept a second bedroom full of broken things. Christmas at Privet Drive was Dudley's day. He has been able to cry whenever he likes since he was three, usually to get a second pudding. He ran to his parents' room in thunderstorms until he was well past ten.

At St Grogory's Primary School he scribbled on the princesses in the picture books, and kicked the back of Harry's chair in assembly. He made sure that nobody picked Harry for games, or was his friend. Every summer he and his gang, his best friend Piers Polkiss among them, played Harry Hunting behind the shops. Once they hung Harry off the school roof by his ankles while Dudley's friends kicked at his head. Dudley broke Harry's glasses with his fist in the playground, and the teacher let him off because boys would be boys. He liked to tease Harry by holding out sweets at arm's length, then snatching them back. Harry wore his cast-offs.

He owned an Amiga, which he smashed in a Boxing Day tantrum (the pieces are in a box in Harry's wardrobe), and later a Megadrive. He sulked furiously whenever his father refused him a new game. When the family put up a Sky satellite dish he discovered WWF wrestling, and stopped reading altogether. As a small boy he collected superhero annuals. He has never forgiven Spider-Man for retiring. After Superman's death in November 1992 he got a commemorative Superman mug free with something. On Saturday afternoons he watches old Doctor Who episodes on video.

At the zoo in 1991 Harry, who did not yet know that he was a wizard, accidentally set a boa constrictor on him.

Smeltings

Dudley followed his father to Smeltings. The uniform is a maroon tailcoat, orange knickerbockers and a flat straw hat called a boater. Every boy also carries a knobbly stick, for hitting other boys when the masters are not looking, which is supposed to be good training for later life. Harry has mocked Dudley for needing remedial work there.

In July 1992 Dudley rehearsed greeting the Masons. He planned to tell Mr Mason that he had written a school essay about him as his hero. On Harry's twelfth birthday he taunted him for having no cards and no friends. He fled screaming when Harry pretended to be turning the hedge into an Ent.

In the saga: the Power Rangers (1993)

By the summer of 1993 Dudley was thirteen. He had a new television in the kitchen, and he had not hit Harry once all summer. On 31 July he watched, with shining eyes, as the Power Rangers fought a giant creature in Birmingham. Harry saw then, for the first time, that his cousin wanted to be something. Dudley was enthralled by the reports of Khan Noonien Singh as well. During her visit that August, Aunt Marge gave him a twenty-pound note and a video recorder.

Marge had once given him a one-volume The Lord of the Rings for Christmas, which he used to prop up a wobbly table until Harry took it. Harry read it all through his third year at Hogwarts, with Narcissa Malfoy's green ribbon for a bookmark. He finished it in the summer of 1994.

In the saga: 1994

Dudley's Smeltings report for 1994 carried a note from the school nurse: he had grown to the dimensions of a young killer whale. He was put on a strict diet. In August he smashed his Megadrive by throwing it out of the window, after being caught smuggling doughnuts. He is devoted to the Green Ranger, and worries that he is unwell. He has taken up karate at the leisure centre on Tuesday and Thursday evenings. He seems to understand that 'there is no first attack in karate', even if his father does not.

By August 1994 he had not thumped Harry for a long time. On 20 August he made room for Harry on the sofa, and they watched the news together. The bulletin covered the Augment War and crowds protesting against superhumans. Superman was on it too, asking the United Nations to let the Justice League and the Avengers step in. Dudley asked the television: 'Why would anyone be against people saving people's lives?'

In their own words

Why would anyone be against people saving people's lives?Dudley Dursley · B4 Ch3

pages.html:
Ronald Bilius Weasley (born 1 March 1980) is a pure-blood wizard of Gryffindor House, the youngest son of Arthur and Molly Weasley. He has been Harry Potter's best friend since 1991. In 1992 he flew his father's car to rescue Harry from a barred window, not long after playing the best game of chess Hogwarts had seen in years. In June 1994 he stood on a broken leg between Harry and Sirius Black. He watches the long war between Hermione Granger and Dracina Malfoy over Harry with a weary, knowing sigh.

Early life

Ron is the sixth of seven children and the youngest of six sons. He was raised at the Burrow, determined to live up to five older brothers. Almost everything he owned came to him second-hand: Bill's old robes, Charlie's chipped wand with its unicorn hair nearly coming out, and Percy's old rat Scabbers, handed down because the family could not afford an owl.

He has red hair and freckles. He collects Chocolate Frog cards, about five hundred of them, and supports the Chudley Cannons. His bedroom, at the top of the house under the ghoul's attic, is painted a violent orange and covered in Cannons posters, with a plaque on the door that reads Ronald's Room.

His older brothers shaped him. When he was three, Fred turned his teddy bear into a spider for breaking Fred's toy broomstick, and Ron has been terrified of spiders ever since. At seven, Fred gave him an Acid Pop, calling it a Sugar Quill, and it burnt right through his tongue. He plays wizard chess with his grandfather's battered set, whose pieces obey him completely. His uncle Bilius saw a Grim and died the next day.

First year (1991 to 1992)

Ron met Harry on the Hogwarts Express on 1 September 1991. When Dracina Malfoy insulted both their families, he squared up to her. Sorted into Gryffindor, pale green with nerves, he rebuked Dracina for calling Hermione a Mudblood. Yet on Hallowe'en he called Hermione a nightmare within her hearing. That night he levitated the troll's own club and dropped it on its head. The blow saved Harry, Hermione and Dracina. He alone noticed the jealous looks between the two girls afterwards, which puzzled him for years. In the Mirror of Erised he saw himself standing alone, older, Head Boy, Quidditch captain, holding the House Cup and the Quidditch Cup. He warned Harry not to go back to it.

At the Hufflepuff match, provoked by Dracina, he threw himself at her and came off badly. She bit his ear, leaving a small crescent scar, scratched four lines down his cheek and tore out a patch of hair above one temple. He gave her a black eye, which he said she had run into. Norbert bit his hand, which swelled up green. When the school turned on Harry over the lost points, Ron alone walked beside him down every corridor.

Under the trapdoor he directed the black pieces in the giant chess game, and he let the white queen strike him down so that Harry could go on. It won Gryffindor fifty points, for the best-played game of chess the school had seen in many years.

Second year (1992 to 1993)

Ron wrote to Harry about twelve times in the summer of 1992. When none of the letters was answered, he flew his father's enchanted Ford Anglia to Privet Drive with Fred and George. He hauled the bars off Harry's window and pulled him free of Vernon Dursley's grip. Shaken, he told his mother that the Dursleys had been starving Harry. From then on he quietly put extra sausages on Harry's plate at every meal. When the barrier at King's Cross sealed itself, he flew the car north to Hogwarts and crashed it into the Whomping Willow. The crash snapped his wand, but he knocked Harry clear of a falling branch.

His Spellotaped wand misfired all year. It raised a green boil between Flitwick's eyes, and when he tried to curse Dracina it set him belching slugs. It blew purple bubbles, and it whistled like a kettle. In detention he polished the trophy room's silver and was sick over a Special Award for Services to the School, which later let him recognise Tom Riddle's name. Disguised as Crabbe, he nearly gave himself away by correcting Dracina about Percy's name, and he filed away her mention of a hidden room at Malfoy Manor. He followed the spiders into the Forest, where one of them carried him off, and found his father's car living wild.

When Ginny was taken into the Chamber, Lockhart seized Ron's broken wand to cast a Memory Charm. Its backfire brought the tunnel roof down. Ron kicked the unconscious Lockhart, for Ginny and for his wand. Then he cleared a gap in the rubble for Harry's return. He won a Special Award for Services to the School and two hundred points. He glared at Dumbledore for sending Harry back to the Dursleys.

Third year (1993 to 1994)

In the summer of 1993 Ron telephoned Privet Drive, shouting, because he thought telephones had to be yelled into. Then he spent a month in Egypt with Bill, and appeared in the Daily Prophet with Scabbers. His new wand from Ollivander's is willow and unicorn tail-hair, fourteen inches. At school he kept filling Harry's plate, saying 'Eat'. His boggart was a six-foot spider, which he defeated by taking away its legs.

On Hallowe'en night, sleeping in the Great Hall, he lay crossways above Harry and the two girls. He vowed before Merlin and God to look after Harry himself, because the womenfolk were not to be trusted. He threw a crocodile heart into Dracina's face after her dementor imitation. It cost Gryffindor fifty points, and ten more when he said it was worth it. He was outraged that the twins gave the Marauder's Map to Harry: 'I'm their brother.'

He stayed at Hogwarts for Christmas, claiming he wanted to avoid Percy. He told Harry that the Weasleys were his family: too many redheads, but his if he wanted it. When Scabbers vanished, leaving blood on his sheet and ginger hairs on the floor, he blamed Crookshanks. He grieved more than anyone expected. After the Ravenclaw match he woke to find Sirius Black slashing his bed curtains with a knife, and he punched him in the face. The knife grew longer every time he told the story. On the day Buckbeak lost his case, he chose to forgive Hermione first and took over the appeal research. During the exams he carried her bag and made her cocoa, gazing at her with a puzzled frown.

On 6 June 1994 he chased Scabbers across the lawn and was dragged under the Whomping Willow by a black dog, his leg snapping on a root. In the Shrieking Shack he stood in front of Harry and told Black he would knock his head off first. He learnt that the rat his family had kept for twelve years was Peter Pettigrew, and took it as a personal insult. He joined in the Disarming Charm that knocked out Snape. Going pink, he asked Hermione to remind him never to forget her birthday. He chained himself to Pettigrew on the side nearest Harry. Pettigrew struck him down with Lupin's wand, and he lay unconscious through Sirius's rescue. Afterwards he admitted that he had been wondering about God since seeing Harry's Patronus.

On the castle steps at the end of term, Dracina flew at Pansy Parkinson. Ron handed Harry his bag, marched up with his mother's set to his shoulders and told Dracina quietly that no friendship was worth destroying with that kind of anger. He did not notice Pansy gazing at him afterwards. He adopted the tiny owl Sirius sent, after checking with Crookshanks that it was definitely an owl.

Summer 1994

In August 1994 Ron wrote that his father had got tickets for the Quidditch World Cup final, Ireland against Bulgaria. The Weasleys would come for Harry at five o'clock on Sunday, he wrote, whatever the Dursleys said. He passed on the news that Percy had started work at the Ministry, and that Hermione was arriving that afternoon. He had sent Harry a birthday cake, and he now claimed to know how to use a 'fellytone'.

Personality

Ron is loyal, funny, quick-tempered and practical. He is the friend who notices when Harry has not eaten, and who makes tea, because that is what his mother does when anyone is upset. He reads people better than Harry does. He saw Dracina's feelings for Harry long before Harry did, and he suspected Hermione of taking Dracina's brooch. He repeats his father's line, 'Women...', with a two-handed shrug he cannot explain. He holds that a gentleman wizard never hits a girl, a rule his mother taught him and he has learnt the hard way.

He shares some of his family's blind spots. His remarks about 'Dean's people' and foreign footballers have strained his friendship with Dean Thomas. He resents Dumbledore, whom his mother condemned for leaving Harry with the Dursleys for eleven years. When Harry praises the headmaster, though, he keeps quiet, letting Harry keep his faith.

Relationships

Harry became his best mate in their first autumn. Ron treats him as a brother, guarding him against the Dursleys, against Sirius Black and, when necessary, against the girls who love him. Hermione is his friend and his sparring partner. By June 1994 she was also something more puzzling.

Dracina bit him, mocked his family's poverty and called him the Weasel. Yet he sometimes looks sorry for her. Since halfway through their first year he has heaved a particular long-suffering sigh about her and Harry. He and Pansy Parkinson once caught each other sighing in exactly the same way at Dracina's behaviour.

In their own words

My dad always used to say, 'Women...'Ron Weasley · B1 Ch6
She bit me. She's mental, Harry. Properly mental.Ron Weasley · B1 Ch9
I always said he was as mental as a soup sandwich.Ron Weasley · B1 Ch13
Oh, Harry. I missed you, mate.Ron Weasley · B2 Ch3

pages.html:
Molly Weasley, née Prewett (born 30 October 1949), is a witch, the wife of Arthur Weasley and the mother of seven children. She is a short, warm, formidable woman. In the summer of 1992 she learnt how the Dursleys were treating Harry Potter, and she has treated him as one of her own ever since. She has made her anger about it felt by the Dursleys, by Albus Dumbledore and by anyone else in range.

Family and home

Molly was born a Prewett. Her brothers, Fabian and Gideon, were killed fighting Death Eaters in the first war against Voldemort. She married Arthur Weasley in 1969, so that by 1994 they had been married twenty-five years.

They have seven children. Bill is the eldest, then Charlie, then Percy, then the twins, Fred and George. Ron comes next, and Ginny is the youngest. With five of them still at home in 1991 she had little time to spare, which is why Ron's sandwiches were always corned beef, though he cannot stand it. A second cousin is an accountant, whom the family never mentions. She tells her children that the Weasleys are an old and proper family.

She wears a flowered apron with her wand in the pocket, and she is an excellent cook. The clock on her kitchen wall has one hand and no numbers. It tells the family when it is time to make tea or to feed the chickens. Every Christmas she knits each of her children a jumper. She keeps Gilderoy Lockhart's Guide to Household Pests on the kitchen mantelpiece, because she fancies him. When the family ghoul gets noisy she quietens it by going up with a poker.

As a girl she gave a boy three drops of love potion in his pumpkin juice every morning for a fortnight, over the Easter holidays. Looking at Arthur, she implied that he had chosen to stay without it. She has views on Minerva McGonagall. She calls her a sweetheart, then adds that she knows where McGonagall has been and who she knows.

Harry Potter

Molly sent Harry an emerald-green jumper with a box of home-made fudge for Christmas 1991, though Ron had told her Harry was not expecting anything. At King's Cross in 1992 she sensed more in his thanks than he meant to show. She watched Vernon Dursley's rudeness with thin lips.

That summer her sons brought Harry to the Burrow in the flying car. She confronted them in the yard like a mother bear, but she told Harry that she was not angry with him in the least. She noticed the bruise Vernon had left round his ankle, and gently drew out the truth. She held him while he wept. She told him to stay for as long as he wanted, a promise she repeated all summer. She refused his money for school things, but let him buy her a box of Chocolate Frogs, which nearly made her cry. When Ron wondered how they would explain a lost Harry to the Dursleys, she burst out that Harry was not going back there.

She wrote to Dumbledore stating where Harry would live from now on. She told him, too, what she thought of a headmaster who had let the abuse go on for eleven years. Dumbledore said he had never been shouted at like it. On the night Ginny came back from the Chamber of Secrets, Molly called Harry and Ron the two bravest boys in all the world.

Then she weighed up Dracina Malfoy, as a mother weighs up a son's future wife. She thanked her for healing Ginny. After that she told her sweetly that if she broke Harry's heart, she would kill her slowly. She shouted at Dumbledore for sending Harry back to Surrey. After Ron's telephone call in 1993 she wrote to Dumbledore again, and the owl came back with scorch marks.

On 31 August 1993 she dropped her shopping to hug Harry, then kept filling his plate. She argued that he should not be told Sirius Black was after him, because he was happy not knowing. She packed him the thickest sandwiches for the train, with a card that read 'For the train. Eat ALL of it. M.W.' She wrote to her five children at Hogwarts that Harry had nobody at home to notice if he did something stupid, so they must keep him alive between them.

In June 1994 Hermione and Dracina sent her twenty pages about the Dursleys by one owl. She read them without a word. Then she looked east, towards Surrey, and smiled a smile that sent Arthur straight back out to his shed. At King's Cross she gave Vernon a long, measuring look that made him step back on to a pigeon.

Summer 1994

When the Dursleys' household diet left Harry hungry, Molly fed him by owl. She sent fruitcake, meat pies, home-made biscuits and a plate of Sunday roast with Yorkshire pudding. One parcel held a steak and ale pie, charmed to stay hot. With them came a note saying that he was one of the family, and that he was being looked after in all matters.

She wrote to the Dursleys asking for Harry to come to the Quidditch World Cup, then stay for the rest of the summer. She underlined 'I will be waiting' three times, adding 'P.S. Actions have consequences.' Harry deduced that she was behind the pond mud that erupted from the Dursleys' kitchen plughole on 20 August 1994. She had been sending letters all summer, and would not tell Ron to whom. She spoke of other plans if the Dursleys refused, at which Arthur left the room.

Personality

Molly is loving, practical and fierce. Her children know the face she had on the morning she came back from the Prewetts', the time Bill told them about. It is the face that means somebody's house is getting taken apart. She taught her sons never to hit a girl, and never to go into a girls' bathroom. She forbade the twins to tell Ron the Angelus stories. In Egypt she would not let Ginny see the mummies. She nearly cried when Percy said he wanted to be Minister for Magic so that he could help poor families.

In their own words

You're to stay here, Harry. For as long as you want.Molly Weasley · B2 Ch4
He's not going back there, Ronald!Molly Weasley · B2 Ch5
If you break Harry's heart, I'll kill you slowly.Molly Weasley · B2 Ch19
P.S. Actions have consequences.Molly Weasley · B4 Ch3

pages.html:
Ginevra Molly Weasley, known as Ginny (born 11 August 1981), is a witch of Gryffindor House. She is the youngest of the seven Weasley children, Arthur and Molly's only daughter. Red-haired and brown-eyed, she began Hogwarts in 1992 with a hopeless crush on Harry Potter. She spent her first year shadowing Dracina Malfoy and the diary of Tom Riddle. In the end she was dragged into the Chamber of Secrets, where Riddle began to drain her life.

Early life

Ginny is the seventh Weasley child, and the first girl born into the family for generations. Since she was six she has been creeping into the broom shed to borrow her brothers' broomsticks, and none of them has ever found out.

In September 1991 she ran along Platform Nine and Three-Quarters after the Hogwarts Express until it gathered speed. The following summer, at King's Cross, she squealed, pointed at Harry Potter, and was told that it was rude to point.

She talked about Harry all summer. When he came to stay at the Burrow in 1992 she was so shy that she squeaked and fled. She knocked things over. Once she put both elbows in the butter dish. Ron said that normally she never stopped talking. Many of her school things were second-hand, so Harry gave her the set of Lockhart books he had been given free.

First year (1992 to 1993)

At Flourish and Blotts Ginny stood slightly in front of Harry and told Dracina Malfoy to leave him alone. It was the first thing she had ever said in his presence. When Dracina mocked her second-hand books, Ginny threw Dracina's new books at her head and screamed names at her. Lucius Malfoy had meant to slip Tom Riddle's diary into Ginny's cauldron, but in the struggle it went to Dracina instead. Dracina called her Little Weasel, made her cry and hissed at her like a snake.

Ginny was sorted into Gryffindor on 1 September 1992. On the way to King's Cross that morning the car had to turn back, because she had left her own diary on her bed: a pink one with a lock, from her mother.

She went red whenever Harry was near. She drank Percy's Pepperup Potion in one gulp to impress him, with steam pouring out of her hair. She wished him luck in a rush before the Slytherin match, and at Christmas she gave him a painted card of himself catching the Snitch. On Valentine's Day a dwarf sang him her Valentine, about his raven hair and frog-green eyes. Dracina mocked it until Ginny ran away in tears.

She became friends with Colin Creevey over their shared admiration of Harry. After the attack on Mrs Norris she cried every night, being a great lover of cats. She told Harry and Ron that Dracina had pointed at Hermione on Hallowe'en, then smiled at Ginny as if she were writing her name down somewhere. When Dracina stopped her by the Charms classroom and asked whether she loved him, Ginny ran. When she looked back, Dracina was writing in a little black book.

From then on Ginny watched. She grew pale and thin. Her fingers were stained with ink, and her nightmares woke her dormitory. For weeks she stalked Dracina, hiding behind pillars. Twice she tried to tell Harry what she had seen, the second time three days before the exams, rocking in her seat. Each time Percy interrupted.

Soon afterwards she followed Dracina and the diary into the Chamber of Secrets. There the possessed Dracina struck her with the diary, drawing blood from her temple to write the second message on the wall. Riddle began to take her life force to restore himself.

She woke after the Basilisk's death. Dracina healed the cut on her temple, and Ginny thanked her. When her mother asked what had happened, Ginny shielded Dracina, saying that nasty Tom Riddle had hit her with the diary. By the end of term she was perfectly happy again. On the train home she let slip that she had walked in on Percy kissing Penelope Clearwater, and she asked the others not to tease him.

Second year (1993 to 1994)

In the summer of 1993 Ginny went to Egypt with the family. Her mother would not let her in to see the mummies, and by Ron's count she asked about Harry nine times a day. She was embarrassed whenever she saw him, since he had saved her life. When the dementor boarded the Hogwarts Express on 1 September 1993 she shook badly. Afterwards she sobbed.

She wears an HP badge as a member of Colin Creevey's Harry Potter fan club. She and Colin have been best friends since the Basilisk. After Harry's fall in the Hufflepuff match she brought him a lumpy, home-made singing card with a lion on it, then fled. In early 1994 she sat where she could see him, and she went silent whenever Sirius Black was mentioned.

When Scabbers vanished she quietly pushed the toast rack towards Ron. At the victory party after the Ravenclaw match she held the Firebolt, said she would tell Charlie, and admitted that she had watched the whole match through her fingers.

Relationships

Ginny's feelings for Harry are unresolved. Harry thinks of her as his best friend's little sister and nothing more. She was quietly saddened to hear him shout that she was not his girlfriend.

Her dealings with Dracina Malfoy began with books thrown in Flourish and Blotts and passed through fear, but after the Chamber she chose to protect Dracina. She is close to Colin Creevey. She is fond of her brothers, despite their teasing, and she keeps Percy's secrets.

In their own words

I'm going to kill you.Ginny Weasley · B2 Ch9
It's not funny. It's not funny, Ron.Ginny Weasley · B2 Ch10
It was that nasty Tom Riddle. He hit me, Mum! With the diary.Ginny Weasley · B2 Ch19
I watched the whole thing through my fingers.Ginny Weasley · B3 Ch13

pages.html:
Fred Weasley (born 1 April 1978), George's twin, is the fourth son of Arthur and Molly Weasley. He is a wizard of Gryffindor House, where he plays Beater for the house team, and with his brother he is the school's leading practical joker. In 1992 he drove the flying car that rescued Harry Potter from Privet Drive, and in 1993 he gave Harry the Marauder's Map.

Family and character

The twins are tall and broad-shouldered. Their mother knits them Weasley jumpers lettered F and G. As George once pointed out, this is hardly necessary, since they know perfectly well that they are called Gred and Forge.

Some of Fred's mischief has been unkind. When Ron was three, Fred turned his teddy bear into a great spider because Ron had broken his toy broomstick, and Ron has been afraid of spiders ever since. When Ron was seven, Fred gave him an Acid Pop and told him it was a Sugar Quill. It burnt straight through Ron's tongue, and their mother went after Fred with her broom. He also told Ron that the Sorting meant wrestling a troll. His great friend outside the family is Lee Jordan.

Fred is curious about Muggles. He thinks Muggle tricks such as lock-picking are well worth learning, and from the window of the flying car in 1992 he asked Harry who Superman was. He told Harry that the Malfoys had been Dark wizards since the Norman Conquest, and that his father believed Lucius had been in Voldemort's inner circle.

Pranks

In their first week at Hogwarts the twins found a secret passage behind Gregory the Smarmy. Before their first year was out they had taken the Marauder's Map from a drawer in Filch's office marked Confiscated and Highly Dangerous. Filch now keeps a drawer of punishment records for the two of them alone.

In December 1991 they bewitched snowballs to bounce off the back of Quirrell's turban. They made Christmas baubles that burst into live slugs. They pinched Percy's prefect badge, which they later bewitched to read Pinhead, then Bighead Boy.

Fred once fed a Filibuster firework to a Salamander in the common room. He supplied the fireworks for Harry's diversion in Potions. With George he enchanted about twenty suits of armour in the Entrance Hall to dance the can-can, a routine that took twenty-six hours to time. When the school suspected Harry of being the Heir of Slytherin, Fred paraded ahead of him through the corridors crying, 'Heir of Slytherin coming through! Thoroughly evil!'

Quidditch

Fred has been a Beater for Gryffindor since before Harry joined the team. In Harry's first match he drove off a Bludger aimed at Harry and belted it at Marcus Flint. In November 1992 he guarded Harry from the rogue Bludger, then wrestled it back into its box.

He once fell asleep on Alicia Spinnet's shoulder during one of Oliver Wood's tactics talks. At another team meeting Wood whacked him across the knees with a Beater's bat. In the 1994 final he hit Flint on the back of the head with his club after Flint barged Angelina Johnson.

Fred and Harry

In the summer of 1992 Fred drove the Ford Anglia to Privet Drive, though he was still working out how the Muggle machine handled; the twins had already flown it five or six times without being seen. In December 1993 he and George gave Harry the Marauder's Map. They offered to go with him whenever he went after Sirius Black, on condition that he told them first.

Ron once reported Fred's opinion of Harry: 'Fred reckons you're the funniest bloke in this school and nobody's noticed because they're all too busy looking at your forehead.'

Fred is wary of Dracina Malfoy. He checked his toast for poison after she praised his home-made fireworks. He saw her pass a full salt shaker with her supposedly injured arm, and he suspected her of bribing the house-elves with something dead.

After the Ravenclaw match in 1994 he fetched crates of butterbeer, pumpkin fizz and Honeydukes sweets for the party. He gave all the credit to Messrs Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot and Prongs. He taught Ron the swear word that Sirius Black most admired. In June 1994 he scraped through his O.W.L.s with a few passes and celebrated as if he had won the World Cup. He was sixteen that August.

In their own words

Stand aside, stand aside! Heir of Slytherin coming through! Thoroughly evil! Mind your ankles!Fred Weasley · B2 Ch14
Nerve damage. Invisible. I'm moved.Fred Weasley · B3 Ch10
Corrupted by a broomstick. Mum'll be heartbroken.Fred Weasley · B3 Ch13

pages.html:
George Weasley (born 1 April 1978), Fred's twin, is the fifth son of Arthur and Molly Weasley. He is a wizard of Gryffindor House, a Beater for the house team and his brother's partner in every joke. In 1992 he picked the lock on Harry Potter's door at Privet Drive, and in 1993 he set the Marauder's Map working for him.

Character

George shares his twin's looks, his sense of humour and a Weasley jumper lettered with his own initial, a G. With Fred he answers to Gred and Forge.

He has a gentler side. On Christmas Day 1991 he insisted that Percy sit with the family rather than the prefects, because Christmas is a time for family. He congratulated Harry quietly on becoming Seeker. He joked that he could not stand the shame of another Head Boy in the family, and he holds that prefects take all the fun out of life.

Pranks

With Fred, George enchanted the suits of armour in the Entrance Hall to dance the can-can. He said it was worth every hour of the twenty-six it had taken to time. He once leapt out at Ginny from behind the statue of Boris the Bewildered, covered in shaggy orange fur. It was George, too, who gave Ron the dud rhyme for turning Scabbers yellow.

When the school took Harry for the Heir of Slytherin, George jumped back from him in the Great Hall, holding up a huge clove of garlic. Harry, he explained to everybody, was only popping down to the Chamber for a cup of tea and a biscuit with his giant fanged pet. He helped to turn Percy's badge into one that read Bighead Boy.

Quidditch

George has been a Gryffindor Beater since before Harry arrived. In Harry's first match he and Fred tried to pull him off his jinxed broom, then circled beneath him to catch him if he fell.

He fell off his broom in shock on hearing that Snape would referee the Hufflepuff match of 1992. During the match he hit a Bludger at Snape, which gave Hufflepuff a penalty. In November 1992 he guarded Harry from the rogue Bludger. Afterwards he blamed Wood's 'catch the Snitch or die trying' talk for Harry's recklessness. In the 1994 final he elbowed the Slytherin Beater Bole across the nose after Bole clubbed Alicia Spinnet.

George and Harry

During the rescue from Privet Drive in the summer of 1992, the bent wire that opened Harry's prison-grade lock came out of George's pocket. He passed back a hairpin to free Hedwig from her padlock, then found the way home by the car's dashboard compass. He had heard his father call Lucius Malfoy a big supporter of You-Know-Who.

In December 1993 George tapped the Marauder's Map with his wand and spoke the words 'I solemnly swear that I am up to no good' to show Harry how it worked.

During the dementors' search of the Hogwarts Express on 1 September 1993, Dracina Malfoy gripped George's arm hard enough to leave marks. One night he saw her coming up from the kitchens alone, carrying a parcel. After Ginny was rescued from the Chamber of Secrets he visited her in the hospital wing in his pyjamas. In June 1994 he scraped through his O.W.L.s. He was sixteen that August.

In their own words

We know perfectly well we're called Gred and Forge.George Weasley · B1 Ch8
He's popping down to the Chamber of Secrets for a nice cup of tea and a biscuit with his giant fanged pet.George Weasley · B2 Ch14
That sling had a longer run than Lockhart.George Weasley · B3 Ch10

pages.html:
Lee Jordan is a Gryffindor wizard in the year of Fred and George Weasley. He is their closest friend and their partner in mischief. He is also the school's Quidditch commentator, and he makes no secret of whose side he is on.

Life

Lee wears his hair in dreadlocks. In September 1991 he brought a tarantula the size of a dinner plate on to the Hogwarts Express. That same month he claimed to have found a new secret passage out of the school. In Diagon Alley in 1992 the twins greeted him by chanting his name, and the three of them stocked up on Filibuster fireworks at Gambol and Japes. After the exams of 1992 he tickled the giant squid with the twins.

Commentator

Lee commentates on Quidditch matches under Professor McGonagall's watchful eye. His commentary has been biased towards Gryffindor ever since Harry's first match in November 1991. In 1992 McGonagall rebuked him for open partisanship against Slytherin. She also seized his magical megaphone to stop Dean Thomas's chant. In 1993 he conducted the Gryffindor stand with his wand during the Hufflepuff match. In 1994 he advertised the Firebolt during the Ravenclaw match, then did it again in the final, where he gave up all pretence of impartiality. Afterwards he repeated his commentary three times from a table at the party.

In the saga

Lee hailed Harry and Ron's crash into the Whomping Willow as an inspired entrance. During the attacks of 1993 he pointed out that every Slytherin had escaped, and he urged that they all be expelled. Later he stood on a table proposing that fifty Gryffindors should storm the Slytherin dungeons. On the night in 1992 when Harry went down the trapdoor, Lee was the last Gryffindor to go to bed. Percy Weasley confiscated his Exploding Snap cards during exam revision in 1994.

In their own words

Harry, mate, you've been spending too much time with Ron. Pack it in.Lee Jordan · B1 Ch7
Hasn't one teacher noticed that every single Slytherin is fine?Lee Jordan · B2 Ch16

pages.html:
William Arthur Weasley, always known as Bill (born 29 November 1970), is the eldest child of Arthur and Molly Weasley. He was Head Boy at Hogwarts and left with twelve O.W.L.s. He now works for Gringotts Wizarding Bank as a curse-breaker, in the tombs of the pharaohs in Egypt.

Life and career

Bill was sorted into Gryffindor. He was made a prefect, then Head Boy, and he left Hogwarts in 1989 with twelve O.W.L.s, a record only his brother Percy has matched. His old school robes went to Ron.

Gringotts took him on as a curse-breaker and sent him to Egypt, where he breaks the enchantments laid on the tombs of the pharaohs. His mother does not approve of his long hair, or of the fang he wears in one ear. His parents spent Christmas 1992 with him. In the summer of 1993, after Arthur won the Daily Prophet Grand Prize Galleon Draw, the whole family came out to stay with him for a month.

In the saga

Ron thought that Bill might once have told him a story about a secret chamber at Hogwarts. Bill also told the twins about the morning their mother came back from the Prewetts' with a face that meant somebody's house was getting taken apart. They still quote it.

In Egypt in 1993 Bill let the family look through a door at the mummies. The tombs were safe, he told them, provided they touched nothing, though his mother would not let Ginny go in. When the twins pushed Percy into a tomb, its guardian questioned him. Bill explained that it does that to everyone who comes in uninvited. He told Ron that Pocket Sneakoscopes were rubbish sold to tourists. Percy becoming Head Boy, he said, was the worst thing that could have happened.

Bill was still in Egypt in 1994. Harry supposed that a good many of Molly's letters that summer were going to Bill and Charlie.

Charles Weasley, always known as Charlie (born 12 December 1972), is the second son of Arthur and Molly Weasley. He was a celebrated Seeker for Gryffindor, and captain of the house team. He now works with dragons in Romania. In 1992 he took the Norwegian Ridgeback Norbert off Hagrid's hands.

Hogwarts

Charlie was the outdoor sort, according to Percy, and took Care of Magical Creatures. According to Ron he learnt a Shield Charm in his first year. He was Gryffindor's Seeker when the house won the Quidditch Cup in 1987, and he went on to captain the team. Oliver Wood once said he could have played for England if he had not gone off chasing dragons. In the common room he is still spoken of like a minor saint. Professor McGonagall said that not even Charlie could have matched Harry Potter's first dive.

A Welsh Green once had a go at him. Madam Pomfrey grew him a new ear afterwards, and the new one is slightly bigger than the old. His chipped old wand went to Ron when he left, together with his Shooting Star broom.

Romania

After Hogwarts Charlie went to Romania to study dragons, and to keep them. His arms are covered in burns from the wild ones there. His parents spent Christmas 1991 with him. That year he sent Percy an idol from Romania, which their mother confiscated for having too many tentacles.

In the spring of 1992 Ron wrote to ask whether he would take Norbert, and Charlie agreed. He sent friends of his to collect the dragon from the top of the tallest tower at Hogwarts, at midnight on a Saturday.

In the Daily Prophet's photograph of the family in Egypt in 1993, Charlie was the only Weasley missing. In 1994 Ron joked about going off to keep dragons with him, and quoted him as saying that hippogriffs can fly for days. Ginny promised to tell him all about Harry's Firebolt.

pages.html:
Percy Ignatius Weasley (born 22 August 1976) is a wizard, the third son of Arthur and Molly Weasley. He was a Gryffindor prefect from 1991 and Head Boy in 1993 to 1994. Pompous, ambitious and devoted to rules, he has meant to become Minister for Magic since he was about six years old. By August 1994 he had joined the Ministry, in the Department of International Magical Cooperation.

Early life and character

Percy wears glasses and polishes his badges constantly. At school he was always the least popular of six brothers. When he was made a prefect in 1991 his parents bought him a screech owl, Hermes, which he refused to lend to Ron. His old rat, Scabbers, was passed down to Ron at the same time. In 1991 Charlie sent him an idol from Romania, which his mother took off him because it had too many tentacles for her liking. All the following summer he behaved very oddly, shutting himself in his room and sending a great many letters. Like Bill, he gained twelve O.W.L.s, and he hardly gloated about it at all.

His ambition is detailed, and it is written down. In his trunk he keeps a list of plans for when he is Minister. Some of them are kindly meant: help for poor families with books and robes; an end to old families buying their way into Ministry jobs. Others are a good deal less comfortable: identity papers, a register of everyone's blood, curfews and a department of censorship. Taken together, he calls the result a fair and orderly society. His mother nearly cried when he told her he wanted to help poor families. He reads books such as Prefects Who Gained Power.

Prefect (1991 to 1993)

Percy met Harry and Ron at their Sorting in 1991. He told Harry that Dumbledore was brilliant but a little mad, and that Snape wanted Quirrell's job. Then he led the first-years up to Gryffindor Tower with the password Caput Draconis. During the troll alarm he was in his element, leading the whole house to safety. At Christmas 1991 the twins forced him into a jumper with a P on it and pinched his badge. Later they bewitched the badge to read Pinhead, and he never noticed. He docked Ron five points for being outside Moaning Myrtle's bathroom, threatening to write to their mother. He also rebuked the twins furiously for frightening Ginny.

Over Christmas 1992 he stayed at school, saying that it was his duty as a prefect, and was seen coming out of a little side room in the dungeons with his ears pink. Dracina Malfoy humiliated him over his family's poverty and called him Peter. On Valentine's Day 1993 he plucked Tom Riddle's diary out of her hands on a staircase and gave it back to Harry, with no idea of what it was. When she made Ginny cry, he threatened to march her to her lesson by the ear.

Twice he interrupted Ginny just as she was trying to tell Harry what she had seen. When his secret girlfriend, Penelope Clearwater, was Petrified, he was stunned into silence. When Ginny was taken into the Chamber he owled his parents, then shut himself in his dormitory. Afterwards he kept touching her hair, as if to make sure she was still there.

Head Boy (1993 to 1994)

Percy was made Head Boy in 1993. The letter came on the day the family left for Egypt. There the twins pushed him into a tomb, where its bandaged guardian sat up on its slab and asked whether he was ready to have his heart weighed. Percy answered it for about ten minutes, with examples, until it lay back down. At the Leaky Cauldron the twins relettered his badge to read Bighead Boy. On the night the Fat Lady was slashed he sent for Dumbledore, then ran the Great Hall like a junior Fudge.

Mrs Weasley wrote to her five children at Hogwarts, asking them to keep Harry safe. Percy took it to heart. He shadowed Harry round the castle at a distance of four paces, and he drew up a timetable of Harry's unaccounted hours. He bet Penelope ten Galleons, which he did not have, on the Ravenclaw match, and won. On the night of Sirius Black's break-in he put his badge on over his pyjamas and told the house that Ron had had a nightmare.

Before his N.E.W.T.s he enforced silence in the common room after seven o'clock. He gave a second-year a week's detention for laughing. He also confiscated three of Seamus Finnigan's Chocolate Frogs, one of which he ate.

He left Hogwarts in 1994 with the highest N.E.W.T. grades there are. At breakfast after Sirius Black's escape he held forth about it to the only person who would listen, Penelope. If he managed to get into the Ministry, he told her, he would have a lot of proposals to make about Magical Law Enforcement. She nodded patiently and went on eating her toast. By August 1994 he had started work in the Department of International Magical Cooperation. Ron warned Harry not to mention anything about Abroad at the Burrow, unless he wanted the pants bored off him.

In their own words

I am a Prefect. It's my job to roam.Percy Weasley · B2 Ch14
He told you to give it back, Ms Malfoy.Percy Weasley · B2 Ch15
I happen to be patrolling. Head Boy duties. The route is confidential.Percy Weasley · B3 Ch9
It feels like twice.Percy Weasley · B3 Ch12

pages.html:
Arthur Weasley (born 6 February 1950) runs the Misuse of Muggle Artefacts Office at the Ministry of Magic. He is Molly Weasley's husband and the father of seven children. Thin, balding, red-haired and bespectacled, he is fascinated by Muggles, above all by their machines. He enchanted the Ford Anglia in which his sons rescued Harry Potter in 1992. He is also the old enemy of Lucius Malfoy.

Family

Arthur is the son of Septimus Weasley and Cedrella Black. He married Molly Prewett in 1969, so that by 1994 they had been married for twenty-five years. Their children are Bill, Charlie, Percy, Fred, George, Ron and Ginny. He bought Percy an owl for being made a prefect. He and Molly spent Christmas 1991 in Romania with Charlie, then Christmas 1992 in Egypt with Bill. In the summer of 1993, at forty-three, he won the Daily Prophet Grand Prize Galleon Draw of seven hundred Galleons, and took the whole family to Egypt for a month.

Ministry career

Arthur works in the Misuse of Muggle Artefacts Office, a job the rest of the Ministry laughs at. He has one colleague, an old warlock called Perkins. Cornelius Fudge is his superior, and Arthur says 'the Minister' the way other people say 'the drains'. His raids turn up shrinking door keys and biting kettles. After one night of nine raids he reported that Mundungus Fletcher had tried to hex him. He deals with cursed and bewitched books as well. One sang lullabies until the reader never woke; another ate a man's fingers. The worst, he says, are the ones you like. He wrote the Muggle Protection Act. He once visited Azkaban on Ministry business, and came home grey in the face, unable to eat.

In September 1992 Ron and Harry were seen flying his car to Hogwarts. Arthur faced an inquiry at work, was fined fifty Galleons and had to listen to Lucius Malfoy demanding that he step down. In 1993 he and his colleagues were taken off their usual work to hunt for Sirius Black. He learnt that Fudge had heard Black say 'He's at Hogwarts' in his sleep. For the final of the 1994 Quidditch World Cup he got prime tickets through friends in the Department of Magical Games and Sports.

Muggles and the flying car

Arthur fills his shed with Muggle objects, which he takes apart, enchants and puts back together. He keeps a picture of a jump jet out there, and he is mad on Muggle football. He questioned Harry eagerly about plugs, the post, telephones and escalators. In the summer of 1992 Harry taught him how to use a telephone. He has been pestering McGonagall about hers for fifteen years. Molly sighs whenever he starts on electricity.

His Ford Anglia was enchanted to fly. It had cushioned seats, puncture-proof tyres, an engine that ran on vegetable oil and a charm to hide all this from Muggles. It also had a stretched boot and a faulty Invisibility Booster. It was legal because Arthur had written a loophole into the law himself: a car may be enchanted, provided its owner never intends to fly it. After it crashed into the Whomping Willow it went to live wild in the Forbidden Forest.

Harry Potter

In 1992 Arthur told Harry that Dumbledore knew where he was, and that since hearing from Molly, Dumbledore 'really knew now'. At Flourish and Blotts, when Lucius Malfoy sneered at his family and at the Grangers, Arthur threw the first punch. He came away with a cut lip. He would have chinned Lucius, he said, if Hagrid had not pulled them apart. He mended Harry's glasses with a tap of his wand, then took the Grangers for a drink. After the Chamber of Secrets he warned the children never to trust anything that can think for itself if you cannot see where it keeps its brain.

On 31 August 1993 he looked Harry over in the light, as though he were inspecting a plug. Then he asked him privately whether the Dursleys or Marge had laid a finger on him. He argued that Harry had a right to know Black was after him. He arranged Ministry cars to take them to King's Cross, putting Harry on the list under 'Weasley'. He also made Harry promise not to go looking for Black. In June 1994, seeing the smile on Molly's face over the letters from Hermione and Dracina, he fled back to his shed with a toaster under his arm.

Sayings

Ron quotes his father often. Arthur's only remark on the subject of women is 'Women...', with a shrug of both hands. He holds that night adds about forty per cent to any trouble. By midnight, he says, a man who wants to kill somebody has worked out how. Having suffered Mundungus Fletcher's tricks in his youth, he believes that you should never sneak up on a sleeping man. He thinks Squibs come from the same five families marrying one another for three hundred years. He never believed the Malfoys' claim that Voldemort had bewitched them, and he is practically certain that Lucius served him. Being in the same grounds as dementors, he once said, was like living downwind of something.

In their own words

Yeah, and I would've chinned him if Hagrid didn't stop us.Arthur Weasley · B2 Ch5
Never trust anything that can think for itself if you can't see where it keeps its brain.Arthur Weasley · B2 Ch19

pages.title: Molly Weasley's second cousin
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Apparently none: a Squib, or a Muggle
pages.html:
Molly Weasley's second cousin is an accountant, and the one relation the Weasley family never mentions. As far as Ron Weasley knew, he was the only person in the family who was not a witch or wizard.

A family silence

Ron did not say so outright, but the way he spoke suggested that the cousin had no magic. He is either a Squib, one of the rare people born into a wizarding family without any magic of their own, or a Muggle. Squibs are often a source of embarrassment in the old wizarding families, which may be why nobody mentions him.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Two, on the Hogwarts Express on 1 September 1991, Harry Potter asked Ron whether everyone in his family was a wizard. 'Er, yeah, I think so,' said Ron. 'Mum's got a second cousin who's an accountant, but nobody mentions him.'

Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Scabbers was the Weasley family's fat grey rat, passed down from Percy Weasley to Ron as the last word in hand-me-downs. In June 1994 he was unmasked as the Animagus form of Peter Pettigrew, who had hidden in the family for twelve years after betraying Harry Potter's parents.

As a pet

Scabbers was a small, fat, grey, second-hand rat who almost never woke up. He had a tattered left ear and a toe missing from one front paw. He belonged to Percy until 1991, when Percy became a prefect and was given an owl. Then he went to Ron, because the family could not afford a second owl.

On the Hogwarts Express in 1991 he bit Goyle's knuckle when Goyle grabbed at the Chocolate Frogs, leaving a scar. He was flung against the window and went straight back to sleep. On his first night at school he tried to eat Ron's sheets. Later he chewed through the sheet that became the Potter for President banner. He was fond of Fudge Flies. In the summer of 1993 he appeared on Ron's shoulder in the Daily Prophet photograph of the Weasleys in Egypt.

Decline and disappearance

After Egypt Scabbers grew thin and droopy. The witch at the Magical Menagerie told Ron that an ordinary rat lives about three years, and sold him a rat tonic. Crookshanks attacked him in the shop. By Christmas 1993 he was gaunt, breathing fast and losing his fur. He had been losing weight ever since Sirius Black's escape.

In early March 1994 he vanished, leaving blood on Ron's sheet and ginger hairs on the floor. Ron grieved for him more than anybody expected, and he blamed Crookshanks.

Unmasking

On 6 June 1994 Hermione found Scabbers hiding in a milk jug in Hagrid's cabin, thin and patchy with bald spots. He fought frantically to get out of Ron's pocket. He bit Ron, and fled from Crookshanks across the lawn. In the Shrieking Shack Remus Lupin and Sirius Black forced him back into human form as Peter Pettigrew. He had been with the Weasley family for twelve years. Ron took it as a personal insult.

When Lupin transformed under the full moon, Pettigrew escaped again as a rat. Sirius later gave Ron a tiny owl, since it was his fault that Ron no longer had a rat.

pages.title: The trolley witch

Sweets, Pumpkin Pasties, Cauldron Cakes, ice-cold pumpkin juice
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
The trolley witch is the plump, smiling witch who pushes the food trolley along the Hogwarts Express. The train is usually kept for students. Until September 1993 she was the only grown-up Harry Potter and his friends had ever seen aboard it.

The trolley

Her trolley carries Bertie Bott's Every-Flavour Beans, Drooble's Best Blowing Gum, Chocolate Frogs, Pumpkin Pasties, Cauldron Cakes and Liquorice Wands, along with a great many other things. There are no Mars Bars on it. She also sells ice-cold pumpkin juice. She comes clanking along the corridor at lunchtime, pulling back each compartment door in turn.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Two, at about half past twelve on 1 September 1991, something came clanking along the corridor, and she pulled back the door of the compartment Harry Potter was sharing with Ron Weasley. "Fancy anything from the trolley, my loves?" The Dursleys had never given Harry money for sweets. He had meant to buy every Mars Bar on the trolley, but there were none, so he bought some of each instead, for eleven silver Sickles and seven bronze Knuts.

In Book Two, Chapter Six, on 1 September 1992, Harry and Ron were flying north in Mr Weasley's car with nothing to drink. Harry thought longingly of the train somewhere far below them, where ice-cold pumpkin juice could be had from a plump, smiling witch with a trolley.

In Book Three, Chapter Five, on 1 September 1993, she reached their compartment at one o'clock and handed Harry a large stack of Cauldron Cakes. Professor Lupin was asleep by the window. "Don't worry, dear," she said. "If he's hungry when he wakes, I'll be up front with the driver."

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty-Two, on the journey home in June 1994, Harry bought an enormous lunch from her trolley. He did not buy anything with chocolate in it.

pages.html:
Albus Dumbledore is the Headmaster of Hogwarts. He is the wizard who defeated Greta Grindelwald in 1945, and his powers are said to rival Lord Voldemort's at their height. Well past a hundred years old, he has been Harry Potter's protector at a distance ever since the night in 1981 when he left him on the Dursleys' doorstep, a thing he has never forgiven himself for. He is one of only two people living who know the truth of Harry's descent.

Early life

Albus Percival Wulfric Brian Dumbledore was born in 1881, the eldest child of Percival and Kendra Dumbledore. He had a younger brother, Aberforth, and a younger sister, Ariana. The family lived in the West Country. When he was eleven he was sent out of the house for setting fire to the curtains. Down by the river at the bottom of the lane he met a very old man in grey, who went by the name of Ambrose Greyhame in those days and is better known as Gandalf. Ambrose spent six summers, from 1892 to 1899, teaching him the old magic of the staff. Dumbledore believes there are not five wizards living who can do what Ambrose taught him, 'maybe old Mad-Eye', and that even the Unspeakables have forgotten the art.

He was sorted into Gryffindor. He was one of the most brilliant pupils the school had ever known, a prefect and then Head Boy. His friendship with Ambrose outlasted his schooling. The old man still visits him, and calls the Headmaster's study simply 'the office'.

Greta Grindelwald

In the last of those summers, in 1899, a girl with golden hair learnt staff magic alongside him. She was Greta Grindelwald, and Dumbledore loved her. He still remembers a summer afternoon by the river, and a girl who turned it all to light. There are whispers in the pubs that she was once a great deal more to him than an enemy. Their friendship ended at Godric's Hollow, in a three-cornered duel with his brother Aberforth in which Ariana was killed. Nobody has ever known whose spell it was. In Greta's eyes that summer Dumbledore saw a burning, righteous anger that he would not see again in anyone for nearly a hundred years.

Greta became the most dangerous Dark witch of her age. The words she used to justify all of it were 'the greater good'. In 1945 Dumbledore defeated her and took her wand. His Chocolate Frog card names that victory first among his achievements. He still thinks of her most days. He wonders whether things might have gone differently if he had been braver, or cleverer, or less in love.

Teacher and Headmaster

Dumbledore taught Transfiguration at Hogwarts under Armando Dippet. He taught Tom Riddle among the rest, and is one of very few people who know that Lord Voldemort was ever called by that name. In 1943, with long auburn hair and an auburn beard, he warned the young Riddle not to wander the corridors. When Rubeus Hagrid was expelled that year for opening the Chamber of Secrets, Dumbledore saw to it that the boy was kept on as gamekeeper. Among his pupils were Minerva McGonagall and, years afterwards, the Muggle-born Slytherin John Constantine. His Chocolate Frog card also credits him with the twelve uses of dragon's blood, and with his work on alchemy alongside his partner, Nicolas Flamel.

He was Headmaster by 1971. One of the first things he did in the post was to admit Remus Lupin, a bitten Garou boy whom no other headmaster would have taken. He had the Whomping Willow planted, and the Shrieking Shack built with its tunnel, so that Lupin could be taken out of the castle at each full moon. Then he encouraged the rumour that the Shack was haunted. Later, when a trick of Sirius Black's nearly killed Severus Snape, Dumbledore forbade Snape to tell anyone what he had seen.

The first war

Through the first war against Lord Voldemort he led the Order of the Phoenix, the witches and wizards who fought back. Suspecting a traitor close to James and Lily Potter, he told them to hide. He suggested the Fidelius Charm, and offered to be their Secret-Keeper himself. After their deaths he gave evidence that Sirius Black had been the Secret-Keeper.

He had once said that nothing Severus Snape could ever do would make up for what Snape had done. He made him Potions master all the same. On the night of 1 November 1981 he left the infant Harry on the doorstep of number four, Privet Drive. Professor McGonagall had watched the Dursleys all day, and he overruled her.

Personality and appearance

Dumbledore is tall and thin. His silver hair and beard are several feet long. He wears half-moon spectacles on a long, crooked nose, and his eyes are a very bright blue. He gives an impression of tremendous energy, and he is a good deal stronger than an old man has any right to be. He likes chamber music, tenpin bowling and sweets. His office passwords have included Sherbet lemon and Acid Pop.

Under the whimsy he carries a great weight of guilt: for the doorstep, for the partial truths he has told Harry, for Greta. He keeps a grudge a long time. On the rare occasions when he is angry, rooms fall silent.

Secrets

Dumbledore and Lord Voldemort are the only two people living who know of the lost ages before the Flood. They are also the only two who know of Harry's descent through his mother, which runs back to Aragorn and Arwen.

Between the bookcases of his office hangs a Muggle portrait of a bald, blue-skinned man in golden armour. It is inscribed 'For Albus. From your friend who keeps watch. May the Power protect you.' The man is Zordon of Eltar. The maker of the Myst book, a very old acquaintance who is far older than Dumbledore, has exchanged letters with him on the Art. He is Atrus of the D'ni.

He is the only man living who knows the whole truth about Atlantis: that the island of the old story was Númenor, and that neither of the kingdoms under the sea that claim its name has the right to it.

He also suspects that the Ancients, who built the Stargates, were somehow related to Númenor. He cannot work out exactly how, or, if he is right, how they left Earth to build an empire among the stars and make the gates.

In the saga: 1991 to 1992

Dumbledore began the feast in September 1991 with 'Flapdoodle! Gumboot! Nincompoop! Sprout!' He warned the school that the right-hand corridor on the third floor was out of bounds to all who did not wish to die a most painful death. He wept with pleasure at the school song. Hagrid's three-headed dog was guarding the Philosopher's Stone for him. Its last defence he set himself: the Mirror of Erised, enchanted so that only someone who wanted to find the Stone, but not to use it, could take it out. At Christmas he found Harry in front of the Mirror. He told him that people like the two of them go on living, burdened by destiny, and claimed that when he looked into it he saw himself holding a pair of thick woollen socks. Harry suspected that this was not entirely true.

On the last day of the exams an urgent owl from the Ministry called him to London. He realised as soon as he landed that he was needed at Hogwarts, and he came back in time to pull Quirrell off Harry. In the hospital wing he promised never to lie to Harry, and told him to call Voldemort by his name. He said that Lily Potter was descended from 'a very powerful line of magic indeed'. He would not say which, because he might be wrong, and because the knowledge would put Harry's friends in danger. He was deeply ashamed of himself as he said it. At the feast at the end of the year he gave Ron fifty points, Hermione fifty and Harry sixty. Then he took a hundred from Slytherin for Dracina Malfoy's trespass, and Gryffindor won the House Cup.

In the saga: 1992 to 1993

In September 1992 Dumbledore spared Harry and Ron expulsion over the flying car. At Hallowe'en he found that Mrs Norris had been Petrified, not killed. When Snape suggested taking Harry off the Quidditch team, he answered, 'Innocent until proven guilty, Severus.' After the attack on Colin Creevey he declared that the Chamber of Secrets had been opened once more.

In December, while he was away at the Ministry because Cornelius Fudge was in a flap, Ambrose Greyhame came up through the snow and waited for him in his office. The next morning Dumbledore confessed that he hated himself for leaving Harry with the Dursleys. His anger stopped the instruments, turned the fire blue and opened the eyes of the portraits. Ambrose insisted that the protection must hold. Dumbledore said that Tom would never be finished with Harry, and that he would have to send Harry out to meet it every year. Ambrose gave him a long package holding something Godric had once used, and Dumbledore hid it inside the Sorting Hat. It was the sword Andúril. When Dracina broke down in the Great Hall on Boxing Day, he quietened her with a hand on her head, then told the school she had Morrigan's Fever.

In the spring the governors suspended him. He told Fudge that Hagrid had his complete trust, and that he would not truly be gone while one soul at Hogwarts kept faith with him. He came back when the other eleven governors, some of whom Lucius Malfoy had threatened, wrote to him. He shielded Dracina by asking how Voldemort could possibly have enchanted her from the forests of Albania. He punished neither girl. At the sight of Harry and Dracina together he wept without a sound.

He told Harry that it is our choices, far more than our abilities, that show what we truly are. The sword, he said, had come from an ancient and noble bloodline. Lily's protection, 'the magic of Elves, Harry. And of Númenor', lived in his blood and his aunt's. While he called her house home, it kept Voldemort from him, and older, worse things besides. Before Harry went home that summer, Dumbledore had sat on the Dursleys' sofa and told them he would know the moment they harmed Harry: 'Not a hand, not a word.' After that, Vernon Dursley stopped hitting Harry.

In the saga: 1993 to 1994

In the summer of 1993, eight years after John Constantine stole his Deluminator, Dumbledore had him burgle a D'ni linking book to Myst Island from Ephraim Shacklewell of New Mexico. When Constantine arrived Dumbledore lost his temper. He began to say that he would send men to their deaths 'for the greater...', then stopped, horrified to hear Greta's words in his own mouth. He said that anger becomes as comfortable as an old armchair, and that he did not know whether he was a coward. There was a certain thing, he said, that he would have to do one day, before the end. After Harry blew up Aunt Marge, Dumbledore went back to Privet Drive with Fudge and had what Fudge called 'another word' with the Dursleys.

He agreed, reluctantly, to dementors at the gates. He gave the Defence post to Lupin rather than Snape, and Care of Magical Creatures to Hagrid. At the Hufflepuff match he was the first onto the pitch. He slowed Harry's fifty-foot fall and drove off more than a hundred dementors with a silver Patronus 'like a charge of cavalry', angrier than anyone had ever seen him. At Christmas he lied lightly that Lupin was unwell. When Slytherins in hooded robes frightened Harry off the Snitch, all he said was, 'Dear me. And on such a fine afternoon.'

On the night of Buckbeak's execution he believed Harry and Hermione, but he could not overrule the Minister. What they needed, he told them, was more time. He named the thirteenth window from the right of the West Tower, and said that three turns should do it. He had left a linking book open on Flitwick's desk for Sirius. He gave Harry a small one too, and warned him to read the book in the office first. When the children came back with Dracina he smiled at her in delighted triumph: 'Well done, Miss Malfoy. I always knew you had it in you.' At the end of term Harry asked him whether the anger ever stops. Dumbledore saw Greta's anger looking out of Harry's eyes, and for once he told the whole truth: not completely.

In their own words

Strange, how short-sighted being invisible can make you.Albus Dumbledore · B1 Ch8
People like you and me, Harry, we go on living, burdened by destiny.Albus Dumbledore · B1 Ch8
Call him Voldemort, Harry. Always use the proper name for a thing.Albus Dumbledore · B1 Ch13
The question isn't who, Minerva. The question is how.Albus Dumbledore · B2 Ch11
