pages.title: Greta Grindelwald
infobox:
Albus Dumbledore defeated by, loved by him, rumoured former lover
Gandalf teacher
Fascism: a world empire ruled by wizards
The sign of the Deathly Hallows
Captain America and the Invaders; the Justice Society
Imprisoned in her own fortress, Nurmengard, in the mountains of Austria
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Greta Grindelwald is the Dark witch whom Albus Dumbledore overcame in 1945, the most dangerous witch or wizard of the age before Lord Voldemort. She was a convinced fascist who admired Benito Mussolini and talked Fascism with him many times. She meant to build a world empire ruled by wizards. In the Second World War she fought Captain America, the Invaders and the Justice Society. Long before she and Dumbledore were enemies, she was the girl with golden hair with whom he spent the summer of 1899 in Godric's Hollow. They loved each other then. Neither of them has ever stopped, not through her war, her defeat or her long imprisonment.

Youth

Greta was born in 1883, a brilliant, fierce and beautiful witch. At sixteen she was expelled from Durmstrang for twisted experiments. In the summer of 1899 she came to Godric's Hollow to stay with her great-aunt, the historian Bathilda Bagshot, and there she met the young Albus Dumbledore.

He has never been so happy before or since. She laughed at everything, and she took to everything faster than he did. She had a way of looking at a thing and understanding it all at once, while he was still reading the instructions.

The summer of 1899

Ambrose Greyhame had spent six summers, from 1892 to 1899, teaching Albus the old magic of the staff. In the last of them he taught Greta too, and she took to it faster than Albus. One morning she turned a whole river to light, just to see if she could, and Albus thought it the most beautiful thing he had ever seen.

Nearly a hundred years later he still remembers her fierce young face beneath its mass of golden hair, and the anger in it. It was a burning, righteous, terrible anger, which knew precisely what was wrong with the world and meant to put it right.

They fell in love. They swore a blood pact never to fight each other, sealed in a small crystal phial in which their blood ran together. They dreamed of wizards ruling openly over Muggles for the greater good. They dreamed, too, of uniting the three Deathly Hallows of the Peverell legend to become masters of death.

The summer ended in a three-cornered duel with Albus's brother Aberforth, in which their sister Ariana was killed. Greta fled. Nobody has ever known whose spell killed Ariana.

Fascism and Mussolini

Not long afterwards Greta stole the Elder Wand from the workshop of the wandmaker Gregorovitch, and escaped from his window laughing. She took the triangular sign of the Hallows for her own.

She found her politics in the Fascism of Benito Mussolini. From the early 1920s she sought him out. She talked with him many times, at length, about the State, the single will of a people and the right of the strong to rule the weak. She admired him as she admired almost nobody.

She was no opportunist. She believed in Fascism completely. Where Mussolini dreamed of a new Roman empire of Italians, Greta dreamed of a fascist empire of the whole world. Wizards would be its ruling people, with Muggles beneath them. The International Statute of Secrecy would be torn up, and every will would be bent to one purpose, which she called the greater good.

She gathered followers across continental Europe under that watchword. In the mountains of Austria she built a black fortress, Nurmengard, to hold her enemies, with For the Greater Good carved over its gate.

New York, Paris and the Confederation

In 1926 Greta was in New York, disguised as Percival Graves, Director of Magical Security at MACUSA, hunting an Obscurus. The British magizoologist Newt Scamander exposed her, and MACUSA imprisoned her. In 1927 she escaped while she was being moved to Europe.

In Paris that year, at a rally in the Lestrange mausoleum, she showed her followers a vision of the war to come and of the bomb that would end it. Only wizards, she told them, could stop the Muggles from destroying the world. Some of the best of the wizarding world went over to her that night. Among them were Queenie Goldstein of New York, an old Ilvermorny pupil, and the Obscurial Credence Barebone, who was Aurelius Dumbledore.

In 1932 she tried to make herself leader of the International Confederation of Wizards by trickery, and failed in front of the whole wizarding world. In the same struggle the blood pact she had sworn with Albus in 1899 was broken. Nothing now prevented them from fighting each other.

The Second World War

Her war and the Muggles' war ran side by side. She meant to come out of the second as master of the first. In that war she fought the costumed heroes of the Allies, who took her for one more sorceress of the Axis.

More than once the Invaders fought her followers in occupied Europe, and they came close to taking her. Captain America led them, with Bucky, the Human Torch, Toro and Namor. The Justice Society fought her too. The Spear of Destiny kept those of its heroes who were touched by magic out of the Axis lands, so its battles with her were fought where her war spilt over those borders.

When Mussolini fell in 1943 and was shot by partisans in April 1945, she lost the one man in the Muggle world she had ever counted her equal.

Defeat

For years Albus Dumbledore put off facing her, afraid to learn which of them had killed Ariana. In 1945 he faced her at last, in the most famous duel of the age. He overcame her, and the Elder Wand passed to him.

Ambrose Greyhame, who had been there at the very beginning, was there at the end too, in the ruins with the smoke going up. His own regrets about her are not small.

She has been imprisoned ever since in the topmost cell of her own fortress, Nurmengard. In 1994 she is still alive there, past a hundred and ten.

Albus

Greta loved Albus Dumbledore from that summer in Godric's Hollow, and she has never stopped. The blood pact they swore in 1899 was broken in 1932, but nothing she felt for him was. Her love for him has outlasted everything else she believed in: her empire, her war, his victory over her and nearly fifty years in Nurmengard.

He has never stopped loving her either.

In the saga

Dumbledore still thinks of her most days. He wonders whether it might have gone differently had he been braver, or cleverer, or less in love, or had he seen sooner where she was going.

When Ambrose spoke to him of Dracina Malfoy in December 1992, Dumbledore described her himself: 'Fair, and fierce, and very clever'. She was so much in love, he said, that she would burn the whole world down to keep Harry in it. He had seen that before, and he knew how it ended.

In the summer of 1993, losing his temper with John Constantine, Dumbledore began to echo Greta's words about the greater good, then stopped in horror. Constantine had seen the words over the gate of Nurmengard. He had heard pub whispers that she had once been a great deal more than an enemy to the young Dumbledore, and he had never believed them until then.

In June 1994 Dumbledore, who had been looking for Greta in Dracina's face, found her instead in Harry Potter's: the very same anger that had been in her eyes on that summer evening in Godric's Hollow. He told Harry that such anger never goes away completely, and Harry resolved to use it for the greater good.

Among schoolboys her name is a byword for overreaching ambition. Ron Weasley says that his brother Percy has ideas that would make Grindelwald tell him to steady on. Once he said it to Percy's face, and Percy did not speak to him for a week.

The only known maker of the Philosopher's Stone
pages.html:
Nicolas Flamel is a celebrated alchemist, the only known maker of the Philosopher's Stone and Albus Dumbledore's partner in alchemical work. He was born in the fourteenth century, and the Elixir of Life that the Stone yields has kept him alive for more than six hundred years. He lives quietly in Devon with his wife, Perenelle, and he is a great lover of opera. In 1992, after Lord Voldemort had very nearly stolen the Stone from Hogwarts, Flamel agreed with Dumbledore that it should be destroyed.

The Philosopher's Stone

The Stone turns any metal into pure gold and yields the Elixir of Life, which makes the drinker immortal. Many claims to it have been made down the centuries, but Flamel's was the only Stone known to exist. His partnership in alchemy with Dumbledore is famous enough to be printed on Dumbledore's Chocolate Frog card.

In 1991 Flamel knew that somebody was after the Stone, and he asked Dumbledore to look after it for him. It was moved out of Gringotts to Hogwarts, where Fluffy, Hagrid's three-headed dog, guarded it with the teachers' enchantments. In June 1992 Quirinus Quirrell, who carried Lord Voldemort on the back of his head, got through every defence but the last before Harry Potter stopped him.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Two, the first Chocolate Frog card Harry Potter ever opened, on the Hogwarts Express, was Dumbledore's. It named Flamel as Dumbledore's partner in alchemy.

In Chapter Seven Hagrid let the name slip while warning Harry, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger off the dog he had lent Dumbledore: 'You forget that dog, an' you forget what it's guardin'. That's between Professor Dumbledore an' Nicolas Flamel...'

In Chapter Nine Harry found the name again on another Dumbledore card, which Neville Longbottom had given him, and Hermione ran upstairs for an enormous old library book. 'Nicolas Flamel,' she whispered, with great drama, 'is the only known maker of the Philosopher's Stone!' The book called him a celebrated alchemist and lover of opera. It said he had marked his six hundred and sixty-fifth birthday the year before. He lived quietly in Devon with his wife. Hermione worked out that Fluffy was guarding his Stone, and that Flamel must have asked Dumbledore to look after it.

In Chapter Thirteen Dumbledore told Harry that the Stone had been destroyed, with Flamel's agreement. 'They have enough Elixir put by to set their affairs in order. And then, yes, they will die.' To Nicolas and Perenelle, he said, it would be rather like going to bed after a very, very long day: 'To the well-organised mind, Harry, death is only the next great adventure.'

pages.title: Agrippa
infobox: Famous Witches and Wizards card, Chocolate Frog card
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
pages.html:
Cornelius Agrippa was a German wizard of the early sixteenth century and one of the great scholars of magic. Muggles imprisoned him for his writings, which they believed to be evil. His Chocolate Frog card is one of the hardest to find, and Ron Weasley has never managed to get it.

Life

He was born at Cologne in 1486. In the course of a restless life he was a soldier, a physician, a lawyer and a lecturer in theology. His great work, the Three Books of Occult Philosophy, was written when he was a young man, though it was not printed until the early 1530s. It set out the whole of magic as the learned of his day understood it: the magic of nature, of the heavens and of the spirit.

Muggle scholars read him for centuries. Muggle authorities locked him up for what he wrote. He died at Grenoble in 1535.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Two, on the Hogwarts Express on 1 September 1991, Ron asked Harry Potter which card he had found in his Chocolate Frog. 'I need Agrippa.' Harry knew nothing about the cards, so Ron explained. 'There's a card in every one, Famous Witches and Wizards, for collecting. I've got five hundred or so, but I can't get Agrippa or Ptolemy.' Then he asked for one of Harry's frogs, in case.

pages.title: Ptolemy
infobox: Famous Witches and Wizards card, Chocolate Frog card
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
pages.html:
Ptolemy was a famous wizard of Alexandria in the second century: astronomer, astrologer and geographer. His Chocolate Frog card is one of the two that Ron Weasley has never managed to get.

Life

Claudius Ptolemy lived and worked in Alexandria, in Roman Egypt. His great book on astronomy, the Almagest, put the Earth at the centre of everything, with the Sun, the Moon and the planets wheeling round it. For fourteen hundred years, until Copernicus, hardly anybody thought otherwise. He also wrote a book on astrology and drew maps of the whole known world.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Two, on the Hogwarts Express on 1 September 1991, Ron explained the Chocolate Frog cards to Harry Potter. 'There's a card in every one, Famous Witches and Wizards, for collecting. I've got five hundred or so, but I can't get Agrippa or Ptolemy.'

pages.title: Morgana
infobox: Famous Witches and Wizards card, Arthurian legend, Dark witch, Chocolate Frog card
Geoffrey of Monmouth, Vita Merlini (c. 1150), as Morgen
Arthur and his descendants, the Potters
pages.html:
Morgana, or Morgan le Fay, was the dark sorceress of King Arthur's day, his half-sister and his enemy. Dark wizards aligned with her persecuted Arthur's descendants until they changed their name to Potter. Today she is one of the commonest of all Chocolate Frog cards, and Ron Weasley owns six of her.

In Arthur's day

Morgana was a daughter of Igraine of Cornwall, which made her Arthur's half-sister. She was learned in healing as well as in the Dark Arts, and some said she had learnt her healing from Merlin himself.

For years she plotted against Arthur and Queen Guinevere. She stole the scabbard of Excalibur, which kept its bearer from bleeding, and threw it into a lake. She sent enchantments to Camelot to expose the queen.

All the same, legend says that when Arthur lay dying after Camlann, she was one of the queens who carried him away to Avalon, and that she was mistress of the isle. Avalon was in truth the Grey Havens of the Elves, and no mortal sorceress was ever mistress there. Wizarding tradition remembers her as a dark sorceress, and as an Animagus who could take the shape of a bird.

Her faction and the Potters

Her followers outlived her. Dark wizards aligned with Morgana went on persecuting Arthur's descendants, the Pendragons, until the family changed its name to Potter to escape them.

The name is camouflage. It worked so well that the wizarding world forgot what it was hiding. Harry Potter is Arthur's direct descendant through his father.

Chocolate Frog card

Morgana appears on one of the commonest of the Famous Witches and Wizards cards. On the Hogwarts Express on 1 September 1991, swapping cards with Harry, Ron Weasley turned her up yet again: 'Oh no, Morgana again, I've got six of her.'

So the witch whose faction hunted Harry's ancestors into changing their name is now traded by eleven-year-olds in a train corridor, mostly by those trying to get rid of her.

pages.html:
Neville Longbottom (born 30 July 1980) is a pure-blood wizard of Gryffindor House in Harry Potter's year. He is round-faced, forgetful and clumsy. He is also braver than he believes: he once fought Crabbe and Goyle single-handed. Starved of kindness, he was twice talked by Dracina Malfoy into letting her into Gryffindor Tower. In 1994 his lost list of passwords let Sirius Black in.

Early life

Neville is the only child of Frank and Alice Longbottom, who were both Aurors. In 1981 Bellatrix Lestrange and other Death Eaters tortured them into madness. They have lived in St Mungo's Hospital for Magical Maladies and Injuries ever since. Neville was brought up by his formidable grandmother, Augusta.

His family feared that he had no magic at all. Then, when he was eight, his Great-uncle Algie accidentally dropped him from an upstairs window, and he bounced all the way down the garden into the road. Great-uncle Algie was so pleased when Neville's Hogwarts letter came that he bought him a toad, Trevor. His relatives include a Great-auntie Enid. His grandmother often told him that he was practically a Squib. She never let him on a broomstick. He came to Hogwarts with his father's wand.

First year (1991 to 1992)

Neville spent the journey to Hogwarts losing his toad. At the Sorting he fell over on his way to the stool. Once the Hat had put him in Gryffindor, he ran off still wearing it. In his first fortnight he melted Seamus Finnigan's cauldron and came out in boils. He fell down two staircases, then set fire to his sleeve in Herbology. At the first flying lesson he rose twenty feet before the whistle, fell off and broke his wrist. His grandmother sent him a Remembrall, which Dracina Malfoy stole twice. Locked out of the tower one night for forgetting the password, he tagged along with Harry, Ron and Hermione on their midnight escape. That was how he came to see the three-headed dog.

Dracina put the Leg-Locker Curse on him outside the library. He bunny-hopped all the way to Gryffindor Tower, but he refused to report her. At the Hufflepuff match he told her he was worth twelve of her, repeating Harry's words. He pulled Ron off her, then fought Crabbe and Goyle single-handed. He doubled Goyle up before they knocked him out. The pair have avoided him ever since.

He went out at night to warn Harry that Dracina meant to catch him with a dragon. He lost fifty points for it, cried himself to sleep and served his detention in the Forbidden Forest. Before the end of term he gave Dracina the Gryffindor password, because she sat beside him and was kind to him. Nobody ever asked him for things like that. He confessed it to Harry, afraid that she had meant him harm. When he learnt that Hermione had put the Body-Bind on her, his first question was whether Dracina was all right.

Second and third years (1992 to 1994)

Neville spent a quarter of an hour hanging from a chandelier by his ears in Lockhart's pixie lesson. In Potions Dracina told him he was a disgrace to his blood. Frightened by the attacks, he bought a green onion, a purple crystal and a rotting newt's tail for protection. He feared that he was close enough to a Squib to be a target. Harry told him he was as brave as anyone in Gryffindor.

Tom Riddle later revealed that Dracina had worked on Neville until he let her into Gryffindor Tower a second time. Neville was easy, Riddle said, because nobody was ever kind to him. When she thanked him for being such a help, he dropped all his books.

In 1993 Professor Trelawney told him not to count on his grandmother's health, adding that he would soon lose something precious. His boggart was Professor Snape. Neville dressed it in his grandmother's vulture hat, green dress and red handbag, which earned him ten points from Lupin. Dracina partnered him in the sunlight-charm practical, and helped him to a feeble yellow glow.

He wrote down Sir Cadogan's passwords for the week, then lost the list. Crookshanks took it from his bedside table for Sirius Black, who used it to get into the tower. It was the third such incident. Neville was banned from Hogsmeade for the rest of his schooling, and from being told the password, though Harry told him anyway. His grandmother sent him a Howler. In the June 1994 Herbology exam a Fanged Geranium bit him only twice, which he regarded with pride.

Character and interests

Neville is gentle, honest and anxious. He has a real gift for Herbology, which saved his exams in 1992. He knows a good deal about the Malkavian vampires, which he studied, he said, for a family matter. When Lupin described Malkavians who know things they cannot possibly know, Neville observed that Professor Trelawney said the same of herself.

After a butterbeer and a half he does a very good impression of Marcus Flint. Professor McGonagall sometimes gives him a quiet, proud smile when he finally gets a spell right. On the Knight Bus in 1993 Harry gave Neville's name as his own.

In their own words

I'm worth twelve of you, Malfoy.Neville Longbottom · B1 Ch9
Professor Snape.Neville Longbottom · B3 Ch7
Can a person actually burst?Neville Longbottom · B3 Ch16

pages.title: Trevor the toad
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
pages.html:
Trevor is Neville Longbottom's toad, and he would rather be almost anywhere else. Neville's Great-uncle Algie gave him to Neville as a reward for getting into Hogwarts, which nobody in the family had been entirely sure he would.

Escapes

Trevor escapes whenever he gets the chance. He was lost on the Hogwarts Express on Neville's very first journey to school. Hermione Granger went up and down the train asking whether anybody had seen him. He turned up at the end of the night in one of the boats at the underground harbour beneath the castle, where Hagrid found him.

At the end of Neville's first year, in the summer of 1992, he was found lurking in a corner of the boys' toilets. Nobody ever found out how long he had been there.

The Shrinking Solution

In the autumn of 1993 Neville's Shrinking Solution came out bright orange in Professor Snape's Potions class. Snape announced that he would feed a few drops of it to Trevor at the end of the lesson to see what happened. Hermione whispered instructions to Neville for the rest of the class, which saved Trevor's life.

The potion worked. Trevor shrank to a tadpole and wriggled in the palm of Snape's hand until Snape gave him the antidote, which turned him back into a toad. Snape took five points from Gryffindor for Hermione's help all the same.

pages.title: Neville Longbottom's grandmother
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Neville Longbottom, whom she brought up
A tall hat with a stuffed vulture, a long green dress, a fox-fur scarf and a big red handbag
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Neville Longbottom's grandmother, Augusta Longbottom, is the pure-blood witch who brought him up. She is very formidable. She cried with joy when he first showed magic, and she tells him all the time that he is practically a Squib.

Neville's gran

She has brought Neville up herself since 1981, when his parents were tortured into madness. She keeps an eye on him at school by post. She sends on the things he forgets, along with a Howler when she thinks he has earned one.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, Neville told the Welcome Feast of 1991 that his gran had brought him up, and that she cried when he bounced. In Book One, Chapter Five, she sent him a Remembrall, because she knew he forgot things. It turned scarlet at once.

In Book Two, Chapter Seven, Neville said she was sending on a few things he had forgotten. She had sent him a Howler once, he told Ron, and he had ignored it, which had been horrible. In Book Two, Chapter Twelve, he told Harry that he was practically a Squib, because Gran said so all the time. Harry told him he did not care what his gran said.

In Book Three, Chapter One, in the summer of 1993, Harry, with nobody likely to sign his own Hogsmeade form, reflected that even Neville's gran would sign one. In Book Three, Chapter Four, he saw her in Diagon Alley in August 1993, telling Neville off for mislaying his booklist, and hoped she never found out that he had pretended to be Neville on the Knight Bus. In Book Three, Chapter Six, Trelawney asked Neville how his grandmother was, then told him gently not to count on her being fine. In Book Three, Chapter Seven, Lupin told Neville to picture her clothes when he faced the boggart: the tall hat with the stuffed vulture, the long green dress and the big red handbag. The boggart Snape duly appeared in them.

In Book Three, Chapter Eight, she sent Neville's Hogsmeade form straight to Professor McGonagall, having thought that wiser than trusting him with it. In Book Three, Chapter Fourteen, in March 1994, two days after Sirius Black's second break-in, she sent Neville a Howler. It told him, and everybody else within half a mile, that he had disgraced the entire family.

pages.title: Great-uncle Algie
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Pushing Neville off Blackpool pier; dangling him from an upstairs window
pages.html:
Great-uncle Algie is Neville Longbottom's great-uncle. For years the family thought Neville might have no magic in him, so Algie made it his business to startle some out of him. When Neville's Hogwarts letter came, Algie was so pleased that he bought him a toad, Trevor.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, at the Welcome Feast of 1991, Neville told his new friends about it. Algie had once pushed him off the end of Blackpool pier, and he had nearly drowned. Nothing happened until Neville was eight. Then Algie came to tea and was dangling him out of an upstairs window by his ankles when Great-auntie Enid offered him a meringue. He let go by accident, and Neville bounced. When the letter came, Neville said, Great-uncle Algie was that happy he bought him his toad.

pages.title: Great-auntie Enid
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Offering a meringue at the right moment
pages.html:
Great-auntie Enid is one of Neville Longbottom's relations. For years the family feared that Neville had no magic at all. Enid did more than anyone to prove them wrong, though she did it entirely by accident, with a meringue.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, at the Welcome Feast of 1991, Neville told the story. When he was eight, Great-uncle Algie came to tea and dangled him out of an upstairs window by the ankles, trying to startle some magic out of him. Just then Great-auntie Enid offered Algie a meringue. He let go by accident. Neville bounced all the way down the garden into the road. The whole family was delighted, and his gran cried.

pages.html:
Hermione Jean Granger (born 19 September 1979) is a Muggle-born witch who was sorted into Gryffindor in 1991. With Ron Weasley, she is one of Harry Potter's two closest friends. The best student of her year, she spent her third year in three places at once with the help of a Time-Turner. Her fierce, possessive attachment to Harry began with the Hallowe'en troll of 1991. It set her against Dracina Malfoy for three years, until the two girls forgave each other on Myst Island in June 1994.

Early life

Hermione is the only child of Mr and Mrs Granger, Muggle dentists who run their own surgery. The Grangers are respectable, mild and thoroughly middle class. They are also atheists, and Hermione was brought up to believe that people simply stop when they die. She is a Virgo. She has read a good deal about astrology and the moon's effect on magic.

Before Hogwarts she had no friends. The girls at her primary school hid her books. They called her Bossy Boots, Swot and Teacher's Pet. She ate her lunch in the library, because the librarian was pleased to see her. She came to believe that if she learnt everything, people would need her; and people do not leave you if they need you. Before her first term she learnt all her set books by heart. She also tried several easy spells, all of which worked.

First year, 1991 to 1992

Hermione met Harry and Ron on the Hogwarts Express on 1 September 1991, while she was helping Neville Longbottom look for his toad. She had bushy brown hair, slightly large front teeth and a brisk, commanding voice. She was sorted into Gryffindor, the house she had hoped for, and was soon the best in the year at nearly everything. When Dracina Malfoy called her a Mudblood she went red and silent. She explained quietly what it meant, then went to the library.

On Hallowe'en she overheard Ron calling her a nightmare, and hid in the girls' toilets to cry. There, by Hermione's later account, Dracina mocked her and said that Harry was hers. Hermione answered that Dracina's father did not love her. Then the troll trapped both girls, until Harry and Ron came for them. Afterwards Hermione threw herself into Harry's arms. Over his shoulder she gave Dracina a small, triumphant look, which only Ron saw. She lied to McGonagall to protect the boys, and from that night she was their friend.

The friendship soon became a kind of guardianship. She wrote whole essays for Harry, and she always knew where he was. At his first Quidditch match she knocked Quirrell over and set Snape's robes alight with her portable blue flames. She found Nicolas Flamel in a book she had borrowed for a bit of light reading.

After the Norbert affair she told McGonagall that Dracina was evil and bullied Harry every day. On the night they went through the trapdoor, Dracina came to the Gryffindor common room to apologise, and Hermione, sure she was Snape's spy, put a Body-Bind on her. Under the trapdoor Hermione burned back the Devil's Snare and solved Snape's logic puzzle of seven bottles. She won fifty points for Gryffindor. She came top of the year, with a hundred and twelve per cent in Charms. On the train home she let her hand rest on Harry's.

Second year, 1992 to 1993

Hermione was thrilled by Gilderoy Lockhart, and scored full marks on his quiz about himself. Through his Voyages with Vampires she became fascinated by vampires. She kept three brooding pictures of Angelus folded inside her copy of Gadding with Ghouls.

Her jealousy of Dracina sharpened. The two girls fought on the Quidditch pitch, pulling each other's hair. Hermione proposed brewing Polyjuice Potion to question Dracina: partly, she let slip, to show Harry how dreadful Dracina was. Her faith in Lockhart broke when she caught him claiming to have fought the Master, who had been sealed beneath a Californian town since 1937. Even so, she played a nervous admirer well enough to get his signature for Moste Potente Potions. She muttered in her sleep that she was first.

At Christmas 1992 Hermione put a hair from Millicent Bulstrode's robes into her Polyjuice Potion. It had come from Millicent's cat. The potion gave her black fur, yellow eyes with slit pupils, pointed ears and a tail. She stayed in the hospital wing until February, in the bed next to Dracina's, and the two of them argued through the curtains for two days. As she recovered, she admitted that she had made it personal and bullied the boys into it. She resolved to be 'less a lot'.

That spring she worked out that the monster was a Basilisk, and wrote 'Pipes' beneath a page torn from a library book. Then she was Petrified beside Penelope Clearwater. Tom Riddle had chosen her on purpose, as a favour to Dracina. Revived on the night of the Chamber, she ran the length of the Great Hall to hug Harry, and heard him call Malfoy 'Dracina'. She resolved to be his best friend for as long as it took. She would deal with Dracina when the time came.

Third year, 1993 to 1994

After a summer in Brittany, Hermione bought Crookshanks with early birthday money, because nobody else had wanted him. On 1 September 1993 Professor McGonagall gave her a Time-Turner so that she could take five new subjects at once. The strain showed. By early 1994 she was about a stone lighter, and her bag was held together with string.

Her rivalry with Dracina became a quiet campaign. She took Dracina's grandmother's brooch and left it where Peeves would find it. She turned Dracina's ribbons scarlet and gold. She made Dracina think she was going mad, and later admitted that she had enjoyed every bit of it. Twice at breakfast she drew the Time-Turner from her collar while staring at Dracina. Once she murmured that it would be so easy, and nobody would ever know. When Dracina began a slur implying that she was Jewish, Hermione threw the first punch on the castle steps.

She quarrelled with both boys as well. She reported Harry's anonymous Firebolt as probably sent by Sirius Black, and she denied that Crookshanks had eaten Scabbers. She guessed from Snape's essay that Lupin was a Garou, and kept his secret. She wrote out Buckbeak's defence by hand. She walked out of Divination after Professor Trelawney called her mind hopelessly mundane.

On the night of 6 June 1994, in the tunnel under the Whomping Willow, she whispered in a flat, frightening voice that she would kill whoever hurt Harry. In the Shrieking Shack she clawed at Black's face. She joined in the Disarming Charm that knocked Snape out, and told Peter Pettigrew she knew at least four spells that would kill a man slowly. She could not produce a Patronus, and at the lake she fainted.

Going back three hours with Harry, she confessed to the brooch and the ribbons. Under her breath she said that she had been 'keeping' Harry. She cast Stunners at the transformed Lupin until the creature threw her into a tree.

Then she recognised the book on Flitwick's desk as a D'ni linking book. She linked to Myst Island with Harry and Dracina. On the dock Dracina broke down over her life at Malfoy Manor. Hermione held her, forgave her for the toilets and everything since, then asked forgiveness in turn. The two of them agreed to be friends and rivals. Hermione also worked out that Dumbledore had planned the escape.

At the end of term she passed Muggle Studies with three hundred and twenty per cent, then handed back the Time-Turner. She also sent Molly Weasley an eleven-page letter about the Dursleys, with underlined headings and a summary.

The summer of 1994

Her father bought a computer, and gave up on the game that came with it, Myst, after one evening. Hermione finished all four of its endings. She filled two exercise books with notes, and recognised its island as the one they had visited. She has since been back to it, on the screen, eleven times.

On a Muggle newsgroup about adventure games she found six Muggles, in different countries, who described a calling towards a desert they had never seen. A few of them were talking of going to New Mexico, and one had got as far as a fence in the middle of nowhere, with men behind it who told him to go home. Hermione wondered whether descendants of Anna might carry a little D'ni blood without knowing it.

Her birthday card to Harry read 'Still searching. We're all looking after you!' She was due at the Burrow on 20 August 1994.

Personality

Hermione is brilliant, tireless and fiercely logical. She is an empiricist, and once dismissed the theory that Muggle-born magic comes from recessive ancestry as pseudoscience with no data. Beneath the competence she is lonely, and her loyalty to Harry runs to possession. Ambrose Greyhame, the vicar of Little Whinging, said that she watched over Harry like a hawk over its nest, perhaps a little too like a hawk, but that she would walk into fire for him. A part of her that she has privately named, and does not like, sits up pleased whenever she is proved right about Dracina.

She is most frightening when she is calm. She once silenced a Hufflepuff eleven inches taller than herself with one flat look, and by early 1994 Harry had begun to be afraid of her. She follows real vampires the way other girls follow Take That. Harry felt that she studied them the way one studies something one has privately decided to kill.

Abilities

Lupin called her the cleverest witch of her age. Small, portable, waterproof fires are a speciality of hers. She froze Cornish pixies with a Freezing Charm, and moved a Christmas tree with Mobiliarbus to hide Harry from Fudge. She brewed Polyjuice Potion at twelve. Before the 1994 Quidditch final she drilled Harry in the Shield Charm.

She cannot yet produce a Patronus, and flying does not suit her. Chess is the only thing she ever loses at.

Relationships

Harry is the centre of her world, and she still dreams about the troll. In June 1994 he told her that he could not manage without her, and she took it as a declaration.

Ron is her friend, as well as her opponent in a running quarrel over rules, homework and pets. In the 1994 exams he carried her bag, and took her quill away from her at two in the morning.

Dracina was her enemy for three years; now she is her friend and rival. Hermione had known of Dracina's feelings for Harry since Narcissa Malfoy invited him to the Manor for Christmas in their first year.

She trusts Professor McGonagall, her Head of House. She helped Hagrid write to the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures about Buckbeak.

In their own words

You're my friend now, Harry, and I owe you, after the troll.Hermione Granger · B1 Ch7
We might have been killed. Or worse, expelled.Hermione Granger · B1 Ch5
She's evil, Harry. Don't trust her.Hermione Granger · B1 Ch12
She's VERY dangerous, Harry.Hermione Granger · B2 Ch5

Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Vincent Crabbe is a Slytherin in Harry Potter's year. With Gregory Goyle, he is one of Dracina Malfoy's two heavy bodyguards. He writes to his father every week, and what he writes finds its way to Lucius Malfoy.

Background

Crabbe is a broad, heavy boy with knuckles the size of conkers. Harry thought that he and Goyle looked as though they had been bred for war. His father served Lord Voldemort alongside Lucius Malfoy in the first war, and Crabbe was chosen as Dracina's companion because his father was useful. He has reported to Lucius since the age of six. Lucius reads his post.

The first two years

Crabbe travelled with Dracina on the Hogwarts Express in September 1991. He was sorted into Slytherin, where Dracina told him off sharply for looking gormless. She picked him as her second for the midnight duel that never happened, looking him and Goyle over as though she were choosing a pudding.

At the Hufflepuff match of 1992 Neville Longbottom fought Crabbe and Goyle at once. He won. Crabbe has kept downwind of Neville ever since, and once flattened himself against the hospital-wing wall to hide as Neville went by. He laughs on cue. In a real fight he is of no use to Dracina at all.

At the Duelling Club in December 1992 a Furnunculus Curse of Harry's, meant for Dracina, covered Crabbe's face in boils. On Christmas Day he ate a cake laced with Sleeping Draught. He was shut in a broom cupboard, which took some doing, since he weighed about as much as a small rhinoceros. There Ron Weasley pulled out a few of his hairs to take his shape, and took his shoes as well. He turned up at breakfast on Boxing Day with no shoes and no idea where he had been. In February 1993 he tugged at Dracina's sleeve to lead her away from Ginny Weasley, and was shoved aside by a Valentine dwarf for his trouble.

The third year

In 1993 to 1994 Crabbe imitated a dementor at Harry after the Hallowe'en feast, and again in Potions. When Professor Lupin's boggart became a werewolf, he screamed and hid behind Goyle. He was one of the four fake dementors at the Ravenclaw match in March 1994. At the Shrieking Shack he was covered in green slime, and trod on the Invisibility Cloak, exposing Harry's head.

Because Crabbe writes home every week, Dracina performs her hostility to Harry in front of him. At the final he sat behind Professor Snape, watching Dracina rather than the match. On the train home he laughed at her jokes a second after Goyle, once he had worked out that something was funny.

pages.title: Gregory Goyle
infobox:
Dracina Malfoy leader, follower, housemate

Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Gregory Goyle is a Slytherin in Harry Potter's year who follows Dracina Malfoy about the castle with Vincent Crabbe, the pair of them planted on either side of her like gateposts. He is nearly as stupid as he is nasty, and he reports to his father every week.

Background

Goyle is a broad, heavy boy, with long arms, small dull eyes under a heavy brow, a drooping jaw and hair that grows almost to his eyebrows. Rather unexpectedly, he has perfect eyesight.

His father, like Crabbe's, served Lord Voldemort beside Lucius Malfoy. Goyle was chosen as Dracina's friend because his father was useful. Both boys report to Lucius, as their fathers do.

First year

On the Hogwarts Express in September 1991 Goyle grabbed at Ron Weasley's Chocolate Frogs and was bitten on the knuckle by Scabbers. He still carries the scar on his finger.

At the Hufflepuff match of 1992 he tried to come to Dracina's aid, and Neville Longbottom hit him in the stomach so hard that he doubled up. Goyle has watched Neville warily ever since. He passed his first-year examinations.

Second year

In September 1992 he flanked Dracina in the courtyard. When she was in a temper at breakfast she shouted at him, poked him and hit him on the arms. He took it without a word.

In Potions his Swelling Solution exploded when Harry threw a firework into it, swelling his eyes to the size of dinner plates. The uproar covered Hermione's raid on Snape's stores.

At Christmas tea Dracina screamed at him for reaching towards her diary. That evening he ate a drugged cake. Harry plucked his bristles for Polyjuice Potion and spent the evening as Goyle. On Boxing Day the real Goyle came down to breakfast with no shoes on and no memory of most of the night. Harry once claimed to have seen him try to open a door by reading the sign on it.

Third year

In his third year Goyle insisted that Dracina had not worn her serpent brooch all through Potions; he had watched the back of her head for the whole lesson. One Monday in March 1994, when Dracina knocked her goblet over at breakfast, the pumpkin juice dripped off the table on to his knees, and he looked down at them in mild surprise.

At the Ravenclaw match that March he was one of the fake dementors, with Dracina on his shoulders, and he got his head stuck in the robes. He watched Dracina from behind Snape at the final. On the train home he guffawed at her taunts.

pages.html:
Lord Voldemort, born Tom Marvolo Riddle, is the Dark wizard who terrorised wizarding Britain in the 1970s. On 31 October 1981 he murdered James and Lily Potter, then failed to kill their infant son. Broken by Lily's protection, he has survived ever since as something less than a man, anchored to the world by pieces of his own soul. He is not the root of the evil he serves, only one leaf on a very old tree.

Origins

Tom Riddle's mother, Merope Gaunt, was a witch of the decayed Gaunt family, the last descendants of Salazar Slytherin. She bewitched a handsome Muggle called Tom Riddle, the son of the family in the big house on the hill above Little Hangleton. When the enchantment wore off he left her, though she was expecting his child. She died in a Muggle orphanage in London on the last night of 1926. She lived just long enough to name her son Tom, after his father, and Marvolo, after her own.

Tom grew up in the orphanage, and hated it. The woman who ran it locked the little ones in the coal cellar. She first locked him there when he was five. Albus Dumbledore came to tell him that he was a wizard. One summer, having found out what he could do, he went back and made them sorry.

Hogwarts

Riddle was at Hogwarts from 1938 to 1945, in Slytherin. At sixteen he was a tall, handsome prefect with black hair like Harry Potter's, admired by his teachers, though he spent every holiday in the orphanage he loathed. He was a Parselmouth, and he discovered that he was Slytherin's heir. In his fifth year he opened the Chamber of Secrets and set the Basilisk on the school. A Muggle-born girl was killed in a bathroom. On 13 June 1943, when Headmaster Dippet refused to let him stay at the castle for the summer, he framed the young Rubeus Hagrid for the attacks. He blasted open the box in which Hagrid was keeping a young spider. Dippet hushed the death up and gave Riddle a Special Award for Services to the School. He also received a Medal for Magical Merit, and became Head Boy.

He bought a cheap diary from a newsagent's on Vauxhall Road, London, and at sixteen made it the vessel for a piece of himself. That summer he went to Little Hangleton. He found his uncle, Morfin Gaunt, in the family shack, with a dead snake nailed to the door. He put Morfin to sleep and took his wand, along with a gold ring set with a black stone. With Morfin's wand he murdered his Muggle father and grandparents in the house on the hill.

Rise

After leaving school Riddle vanished. He travelled, and sank deep into the Dark Arts. He remade his name: TOM MARVOLO RIDDLE, rearranged, is I AM LORD VOLDEMORT. He gathered followers from the old pure-blood families, the Death Eaters, and branded them with the Dark Mark on the left forearm. Lucius Malfoy, Severus Snape and Peter Pettigrew are among those who served him. Lucius says that his master knew magic that was old when the castle was a hill, things forgotten before the Romans came, and that one did not decline him: 'One is not consulted.'

Through the 1970s his war made the wizarding world a place where people would not speak his name. Most of them still say You-Know-Who. Dobby remembers that when the Dark Lord was strong, house-elves were kicked like dogs. Dumbledore is said to have been the only wizard he ever feared.

Horcruxes

Voldemort tore himself to pieces looking for a way never to die. A Horcrux is a piece of a soul poured into a made thing, there to wait, to whisper and to be carried. Its maker cannot be ended while the thing endures. The first was the One Ring, into which Sauron put the greater part of himself. It needed elven craftsmanship. When the Elves passed out of the world, the technique went with them, and every Horcrux since has been an imitation. The method a modern wizard can actually perform was pieced together after the Flood by a surviving Stygian, whom history misremembers as Herpo the Foul of Greece. It costs what it costs because it is guesswork: the soul torn on purpose.

Voldemort's Horcruxes are therefore the work of a man reconstructing a lost art from a damaged manual. He believes that he stands at the summit of the discipline. He is standing in its ruins. Tom Riddle's diary was one of them. When Ambrose Greyhame sensed it fastened over Dracina Malfoy's heart in 1992, he knew it had been made in the same way as a gold ring he had once known. Dumbledore told Harry in 1992 that Voldemort could not be killed because he was not properly alive: the things anchoring him to the mortal plane would not let him die.

Godric's Hollow

In the last days of October 1981 he went to the house of Lily's mother, Susan Evans, to find out where the Potters were hiding. She did not know, and she fought him; he killed her without ever learning that she had once been a queen of Narnia.

Acting on Peter Pettigrew's betrayal, Voldemort came to the Potters' house at Godric's Hollow on 31 October 1981. He killed James first, in the hall; James fought him well. Upstairs he ordered Lily to stand aside. When she would not, he laughed as he killed her. Then the Killing Curse he aimed at the year-old Harry rebounded. Lily's sacrifice was fuelled by love, as well as by the magic of Elves and of Númenor in her blood. Combined with the very evil that anchored Voldemort to life, it laid a protection on her son. Voldemort was reduced to a shadow and fled, leaving Harry with a lightning scar. That night, without meaning to, he passed some of his own powers into the boy. Harry's Parseltongue comes from him.

The older enemy

Ambrose Greyhame told Dumbledore in 1992 that Tom Riddle is not the root of the evil but a symptom of an older and growing sickness. He is one leaf on a very old tree, planted by an ancient enemy. Tom has a true master. That master is the enemy from whom all dark magic descends. In the elder days he was called Morgoth. Scripture calls him Satan, or Lucifer, and the Garou call him the Wyrm. Remus Lupin can smell him: on Peter Pettigrew, the reek of the Wyrm and the reek of Pettigrew's master are one scent. John Constantine, who has met worse, thinks Voldemort a scally with a flick knife compared with the Devil. One day Voldemort will be a footnote in a much longer story, with a far older enemy.

Only two people living know of the lost ages of the world, or that Harry descends through his mother from Aragorn and Arwen. Those two are Albus Dumbledore and Lord Voldemort.

Voldemort and Harry

Riddle and Harry are alike in ways that trouble Harry. Both are orphans, both were raised among Muggles who mistreated them, and both are Parselmouths with untidy black hair. Riddle looked through the diary into Harry's memories: the cupboard, Dudley's gang, the barred window. Then he offered Harry revenge: 'Don't you want to hurt them back?' Harry still hears the question. Dumbledore has warned Harry that Voldemort always knows where he is. He told Ambrose that Tom would never be finished with Harry while either of them lived. Harry himself counts having faced Voldemort twice, at eleven and at twelve.

In the saga: the Philosopher's Stone

For years he was rumoured to be half dead and in hiding. Dumbledore's sources place him in the forests of Albania. In 1991 he took possession of Quirinus Quirrell, the Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher. Through the school year he lived as a chalk-white face with red eyes and slit nostrils on the back of Quirrell's head, under his turban. He had Quirrell drink unicorn blood in the Forbidden Forest to keep him alive. He sought the Philosopher's Stone to make himself a body.

In June 1992, in the chamber of the Mirror of Erised, he showed the eleven-year-old Harry his face: 'See what I've become? Mere shadow. Mere vapour.' Then he taunted Harry about his parents' deaths, falsely claiming that they had begged for mercy. Quirrell's skin blistered wherever he touched Harry. When Harry clung on, Voldemort was for a moment terrified for his own life. He abandoned Quirrell to die.

In the saga: the diary and the Chamber

In 1992, on Voldemort's instruction, Lucius Malfoy slipped the diary into Ginny Weasley's school books. Dracina Malfoy picked it up by mistake. The sixteen-year-old memory inside it, calling itself Tom, became her understanding friend. It possessed her through her own writing, until it could walk her about the castle while she thought she slept. With her mouth it opened the Chamber of Secrets; with her voice it set the Basilisk on Muggle-borns; with her hands it wrote on the walls. In its own words, 'One pure-blood girl is very much like another, from where I was sitting.' It Petrified Hermione Granger as a favour to Dracina, calling her an obstacle to the union of strong magical blood. It wished to see what Harry and Dracina would make together. It told Harry that 'People don't write forty pages about something they hate.'

In the Chamber, at the end of Harry's second year, the memory took solid form and revealed itself as Lord Voldemort. He offered to teach Harry the old, deep magic, and to help him hurt the Dursleys back. Harry refused, and called him a fraud like Gilderoy Lockhart. Riddle set the Basilisk on him and sneered at his 'borrowed sword from a long forgotten ancestor'. He insisted that the diary could not be destroyed. By the end he was afraid of Harry. When the sword pierced the diary he dissolved, screaming. His last thought was a fear that Voldemort would be no more than a footnote in Harry Potter's history.

In the saga: 1994

At the end of Harry's Divination examination in June 1994, Professor Trelawney went into a trance. She foretold that the Dark Lord lay alone and friendless. His servant, she said, would break free that night and set out to rejoin him. That night Peter Pettigrew escaped.

In August 1994 Harry woke at Privet Drive with his scar burning worse than at any time since he had last been in a room with Voldemort. He had dreamt of walking down to a shack, where he took a wand and a gold ring with a black stone from a filthy man who hissed. Then he had murdered his father and grandparents in a house on the hill. It was Voldemort's own memory of the summer of 1943, with Harry's family put in the places of his.

In their own words

See what I've become? Mere shadow. Mere vapour.Lord Voldemort · B1 Ch13
People don't write forty pages about something they hate. They write forty pages about something they cannot stop thinking about.Lord Voldemort · B2 Ch15
One pure-blood girl is very much like another, from where I was sitting.Lord Voldemort · B2 Ch18
Don't you want to hurt them back?Lord Voldemort · B2 Ch18

pages.html:
Lily Potter, born Lily Evans, was a Muggle-born witch, the wife of James Potter and the mother of Harry Potter. Lord Voldemort murdered her at Godric's Hollow in 1981 as she stood between him and her son. In dying she left Harry a protection older than she knew: the magic of Elves and of Númenor, which had come down to her through her mother, Susan Pevensie.

Family and ancestry

Lily was the younger daughter of Susan Pevensie, who had once been a crowned Queen of Narnia. Susan had reigned in Narnia for a whole grown-up life, then come back to England a girl. For the rest of her days nobody believed her about it. She was not aboard the train that killed her brothers, Peter and Edmund. Her sister, Lucy, died with them. Afterwards, broken by grief and moved above all by the courage of Aslan, who was Christ, Susan came back to her faith. She was an Anglican. Lily was born into the household she made, and took its faith seriously from childhood.

Lily's magic brought mother and daughter together. In Lily, Susan at last had somebody who could not dismiss Narnia, and the two of them were close because of it. Lily's elder sister, Petunia, would have neither the faith nor the magic. She never forgave Lily for either.

All four Pevensies were descended from Aragorn and Arwen. Through Susan, so was Lily. Aragorn's line gave her Númenor, and Arwen's gave her the Elves. By the reckoning of the wizarding world Lily was simply Muggle-born. Albus Dumbledore believes that such magic may be the recessive power of some magical ancestor, and that Lily came of 'a very powerful line of magic indeed'. Tom Riddle said that her line ran back further than anybody had ever written down, further than memory. Only Dumbledore and Lord Voldemort know the whole of it. Lucius Malfoy, who has the Potters' pedigree at his fingertips, knows nothing of hers.

When Lily went to Hogwarts in 1971, Susan began to tell her about Narnia, knowing that Lily would believe her. Lily did, and it drew them closer than ever.

Hogwarts

Lily was at Hogwarts from 1971 to 1978, in Gryffindor. Her year included James Potter, Sirius Black, Remus Lupin and Peter Pettigrew. It also included the Black sisters, Bellatrix and Narcissa. She had been friends with Severus Snape since they were children. The friendship ended when he called her 'that word' by the lake; Sirius remembers that James had a face like thunder that day.

She was devout, and open about it, in a wizarding world that found faith quaint or embarrassing. Witches and wizards tutted at her. Some of them sniggered. She did not stop. All through her school years she was the only believer among her friends. When she was about thirteen, the Fat Friar, the ghost of Hufflepuff, helped her with her faith.

For years Bellatrix and Narcissa Black feuded over James Potter across Professor Flitwick's Charms classroom. Then Lily came, and won him. Flitwick says that neither sister ever quite forgave anybody afterwards. Of the three girls in James's school life, two each decided that he was theirs. The third, Lily, decided that he was nobody's.

Marriage and faith

Lily married James Potter with Sirius Black as best man, and Remus Lupin among the guests. Their wedding photograph is in Harry's album. After the wedding she brought Lupin to faith first, and then James. Peter Pettigrew followed in form only, and played the part well enough to satisfy everyone, Lily included. Sirius alone refused, and Lily never moved him while she lived. Yet something she once said to him about God kept him going through twelve years in Azkaban, where he came to faith at last.

In the flat where the Potters once lived, which Sirius calls 'that awful flat', she wrote a verse on the wall: 'Be ye angry, and sin not'. Lupin used to read it aloud to Sirius whenever he was in a temper. She used to say the evening collect, 'Lighten our darkness'. Lupin's Patronus memory is of Somebody a good deal older than Dumbledore: 'Your mother introduced us, as it happens.' She and James joined the Order of the Phoenix against Voldemort. With Harry, who was born on 31 July 1980, they went into hiding.

Death

Days before Voldemort came to Godric's Hollow, he went to Susan's house to find out where Lily was. Susan did not know, and would not have told him. She fought him, and he killed her.

The Potters hid under the Fidelius Charm. At the last moment, on Sirius's suggestion, they made Peter Pettigrew their Secret-Keeper, and Pettigrew betrayed them. On 31 October 1981 Voldemort came to their house at Godric's Hollow. He killed James first, in the hall, as James was telling Lily to take Harry and run. Upstairs, he ordered Lily to stand aside. She pleaded with him to take her instead of her son, 'Not Harry. Please', and screamed Harry's name. Then he killed her. She was twenty-one. Voldemort said afterwards that she need not have died.

Her death did something Dumbledore has never seen any other mother's death do. The power in her, fuelled by love, combined with her dying act and with the very evil that anchors Voldemort to life. Together they laid on Harry a protection that lives in his skin and in his blood. The Killing Curse rebounded, and Voldemort was broken. In 1992 the same protection blistered Quirrell's hands wherever he touched Harry. Because it lives in her sister's blood too, it holds at Number Four, Privet Drive while Harry calls that house his home. Sirius Black found her body upstairs in the ruined house.

James and Lily left their son a small fortune in a vault at Gringotts.

Memory

Harry first saw his mother in the Mirror of Erised at Christmas 1991: dark red hair, and eyes exactly like his own. Hagrid's album shows her laughing in a garden with James's arm round her. In another picture she is holding a black-haired baby who keeps grabbing at her nose. Harry's startlingly green eyes came down to him from her. Whenever the dementors come near, he hears her last minute again.

Lucius Malfoy says that he never cared for her, and calls her a Mudblood. All the same, he insists that she was a witch, and that no Muggle had the standing to insult her. Marge Dursley called her a bad egg. Sirius says that Harry has Lily's eyes and Lily's temper; his rage is hers. She would have liked Hermione Granger, Sirius says, and she would want Harry to sort things out with Christ.

In the saga: Harry's dream

In Harry's dream of August 1994 Lily appeared as Petunia's sister. She chased the man from the house on the hill, was abandoned by him while she was expecting, and died in the orphanage at the bottom of the road after giving birth on the last night of the year. The dream came from Lord Voldemort's memory. The story it gave Lily was his own mother's, with Harry's family put in the places of his.

pages.html:
James Potter was a wizard of the ancient house of Potter, the husband of Lily Evans and the father of Harry Potter. He was the ringleader of the Marauders, a fine Quidditch player and an unregistered Animagus whose form was a stag; his friends called him Prongs. Lord Voldemort murdered him at Godric's Hollow in 1981, while he was holding Voldemort off so that his wife and son could run.

The Potter line

The Potters are a very old wizarding family. They descend directly from King Arthur Pendragon, and the Pendragons in their turn from the Peverell brother who received the Invisibility Cloak. Arthur's descendants took the name Potter to escape persecution by dark wizards aligned with Morgana. The disguise worked so well that the wizarding world forgot what it was hiding. The descent is no secret. It is documented, and anybody who cares to look can trace it in the right archive; almost nobody does. Lucius Malfoy has looked. In 1993 he told James's son that 'Potters have been kings before they were Potters.'

James was the only child of Fleamont and Euphemia Potter, who had him late in life. He grew up well loved and a little spoilt. His hair stood up at the back in every photograph ever taken of him, just as his son's does.

Hogwarts

James started at Hogwarts in 1971 and was sorted into Gryffindor. He and Sirius Black were inseparable. They were the ringleaders of their gang, and by common consent the cleverest students in the school; Professor McGonagall says they were never topped for mischief. They were regulars at the Three Broomsticks. James was a fine Quidditch player, and the old school paper reported his matches. McGonagall, then newly a teacher, gave him the same advice she later gave his son: that one is only punished for what one is caught doing. In their fourth year he knocked Sirius off his broom with a tackle that Sirius rated the worst he ever suffered until Harry's in the Shrieking Shack.

With Sirius, Remus Lupin and Peter Pettigrew he made up the Marauders, who wrote the Marauder's Map. It was James who worked out that Lupin was a Garou. In their fifth year he, Sirius and Peter became illegal Animagi so that they could keep Lupin company at the full moon. James's form was a stag, which is why his friends called him Prongs. Under his Invisibility Cloak, which he mostly used for sneaking down to the kitchens, the Marauders slipped out of the castle every month.

He loathed Severus Snape. When Sirius tricked Snape into following Lupin past the Whomping Willow, James pulled Snape back from the tunnel and saved his life. Snape maintains that James only backed out of a deadly joke at the last moment. He remembers James as arrogant and contemptuous of rules. Quirrell, a few years below him, recalled that James liked to meddle in the business of Quirrell's circle.

For years Bellatrix and Narcissa Black, who were in his own year, fought over him. They fought with hexes and flowers across Flitwick's classroom. Once they fought it out in the entrance hall while James stood between them, looking bewildered. It caused him great distress, and the other Marauders teased him about it without mercy. Lupin has promised Harry the story of James and the Black sisters. Sirius has promised him an account of James's trouble with girls. It all ended when Lily Evans came. At school James did not believe in God, and said so.

Marriage, faith and the war

James married Lily Evans after they left school. Sirius was his best man, and Lupin was at the wedding. In the photograph James is waving, with his hair standing up like Harry's. After the marriage Lily brought Lupin to faith, and then James, who believed sincerely, if more lightly than she did herself. Their son Harry was born on 31 July 1980.

James and Lily fought Voldemort in the Order of the Phoenix. When they learnt that he was hunting them, they went into hiding under the Fidelius Charm. Dumbledore offered to be their Secret-Keeper, but James insisted on Sirius. At the last moment Sirius persuaded them to change to Peter Pettigrew, and Pettigrew betrayed them. Before he died James left his Invisibility Cloak in Dumbledore's keeping.

Death

On 31 October 1981 Voldemort came to the house at Godric's Hollow. James told Lily to take Harry and run while he held Voldemort off. Voldemort killed him first, in the hall. He later admitted to Harry that James had fought him well. Sirius Black found his body there that night.

Legacy

Harry looks very like his father, who appeared in the Mirror of Erised as a taller, older Harry with the same untidy black hair. Harry's eyes, though, are Lily's. At Christmas 1991 the Cloak came back to Harry with an unsigned note: 'Your father left this in my keeping before he died. It's time it came back to you. Use it well.' Hagrid's album shows James in a garden with his arm round Lily. Hagrid says there was not a dark bone in either of them. Whenever the dementors come near, Harry hears his father's last words.

In June 1994, by the lake, Harry cast a Patronus in the shape of a stag, and he called it Prongs. Lupin says James would have been highly disappointed if his son had never found the secret passages out of the castle. Dumbledore, who knew him well, is sure that James would have spared Pettigrew too. He told Harry that his father lives in him. Sirius told Harry that James was looking down on him, and was proud.

Vernon Dursley told his sister that James had been unemployed. Marge called him a wastrel and a scrounger who died drunk in a car crash. Harry told her that he was not. When she went on, Harry's rage blew her up like a balloon.

In the saga: Harry's dream

In Harry's dream of August 1994 James, a handsome man, sat at dinner with his parents in the house on the hill. He claimed that Lily had tricked him with something in his drink, and that when it wore off he had come home, leaving her pregnant. Harry tortured him until he apologised, then killed him. The figure was not James at all. The dream was Lord Voldemort's memory of murdering his own Muggle father and grandparents, with Harry's family put in their places.

pages.html:
Hedwig is Harry Potter's owl, a snowy owl with great amber eyes. Rubeus Hagrid bought her for him in July 1991, as a present for his eleventh birthday. She is proud, loyal and quick to take offence. She has never yet failed to deliver a letter, even one with no address on it.

A birthday present

Hagrid bought Hedwig at Eeylops Owl Emporium in Diagon Alley on 31 July 1991, Harry's eleventh birthday. Harry took her name from A History of Magic. She is particular about her water, which she likes changed.

At Hogwarts she sleeps in the Owlery with the school owls. Every so often she comes down at breakfast to nibble Harry's ear and help herself to his toast. The first letter she ever brought him was a note from Hagrid, on the Friday of his first week. In 1992 she brought him another, which said only 'It's hatching'. She was also the owl who came back with Charlie Weasley's reply about Norbert.

At Privet Drive

In the summer of 1992 Hedwig hooted mournfully at not being let out. Vernon Dursley padlocked her into her cage so that she could carry no messages. She turned her beak up at the soggy vegetables from cold tinned soup that Harry tipped through the bars, which nobody could really blame her for.

She kept silent through most of the Weasleys' rescue, until a final screech woke Vernon. George's hairpin freed her, and she flew alongside the car. For days afterwards she was furious with Harry about the flying car. She forgave him at Christmas, when she brought him the Dursleys' toothpick and nibbled his ear.

In the summer of 1993 the Dursleys let her out to hunt at night. In late July she flew, without being asked, to Hermione's hotel balcony in Brittany, where she ate a good deal of Hermione's croissant. She came back at midnight on Harry's birthday with Hermione's present. Harry sent her off to Egypt with Errol for the length of Aunt Marge's visit. All the same, she was waiting on top of the wardrobe in his room at the Leaky Cauldron about five minutes after he arrived.

Later years

In 1994 she bit Harry's wrist to get his attention when she brought Hagrid's invitation to tea. She finished off Neville's abandoned cornflakes. Later she brought Hagrid's note with the date of Buckbeak's appeal.

On the train home that summer she screeched when a pack of Exploding Snap went off. She clicked her beak in disapproval at the tiny owl Sirius had sent. At four minutes past midnight on 31 July 1994 she arrived with Hermione's card and a book. She let Sirius's gaudy tropical birds drink from her water dish with the worst possible grace.

On 20 August 1994 she glared at Pigwidgeon, nipped Harry's finger fondly and set off with his letter to Sirius.

pages.html:
Minerva McGonagall is the Deputy Headmistress of Hogwarts, the Head of Gryffindor House and the school's Transfiguration teacher. She is a tall, stern Scottish witch who runs her house with an iron hand and a dry tongue. Behind the square spectacles lies a career she may not speak of. Before she came to teach, and on sabbaticals afterwards, she was an Unspeakable of the Department of Mysteries. She has fought Garou, vampires, Nephilim and worse on several continents.

Early life

Minerva McGonagall was born on 4 October 1935 in Caithness, in the far north of Scotland. Her father, Robert McGonagall, was a Presbyterian minister. Her mother, Isobel Ross, was a witch, which her husband did not discover until after they were married. The family kept her magic quiet in the village for the rest of Minerva's childhood.

At Hogwarts the Sorting Hat took a long time to choose between Ravenclaw and Gryffindor for her. In the end it chose Gryffindor. She was taught by Albus Dumbledore. She played on the Gryffindor house team.

The Unspeakable

After school she joined the Ministry of Magic and became an Unspeakable. From 1960 to 1962 she had a romance with James Bond, the Muggle intelligence officer. She ended it when she discovered how much he had lied to her. All contact between them ceased late in 1962, when he was imprisoned without trial on Alcatraz under the name John Mason. She has not forgotten the lies. Years later, faced with Gilderoy Lockhart, she thought of what she had once done to a charming MI6 agent who lied to her face for the last time.

In the winter of 1966 she went into a village of dark wizards in Siberia, forty miles past the last road, with one other operative: a young man of about her own age. The village's nine men had been harming the people of the valley below for thirty years. The Ministry would not acknowledge that the place existed. The pair waited four days in the snow, until the men grew bored and came out to them. Her partner was the soldier known as Big Boss.

She carries a scar on the back of her hand from that winter. She also carries his three rules: do not announce yourself; most people are beaten by weather and appetite before anybody fights them; the most dangerous moment is just after you believe you have won. He put it rather better himself, she says: 'The hard part is not learning to carry a weapon. The hard part is learning to put it down.'

Her work took her a long way. She once turned a vault's worth of gold into beetles for a Scottish Muggle gentleman, who had a seldom-used desk at a dull-sounding office near the river. She spent what she calls a holiday in Kosovo, transfiguring rather larger targets. She spent a long night outside Kandahar, warding a camp against creatures taught in the third year. She has heard lies from feral mujahideen. She knows of a parasite of the vocal cords that spread by language, through Russian soldiers in Afghanistan and through conscripts in Africa.

She learnt her soundless approach from an old friend she met in a place called Zanzibar Land. Big Boss, the man with one eye and a cigar, taught her a very long time ago to step sideways into shadow. She has faced Garou, walked where Wraiths walk, and tangled with William the Bloody in a cellar in Whitechapel. When she was still learning, placing wards as she learnt them, she watched Nephilim snatch and eat her friends around her. Her old friend Julius, 'dear Julius' as she calls him, is Julius Belmont. He spent some years in Transylvania, and always carried a whip.

Somewhere far from Britain she once tried to separate a creature from the man it had possessed. No Transfiguration would do it. In the end it took a knife, a steady hand and a good deal of help from a man considerably better with the knife than she was. That man, too, was Big Boss. The host died. So did the creature, a Goa'uld symbiote, which she had stuffed. She keeps it in a lit glass case over the fire in her office, as a reminder. The Ministry's file on that campaign against the parasite creatures and the Nephilim makes Cornelius Fudge shudder.

At Hogwarts

She began teaching about 1970. She was still very new to it when James Potter and Sirius Black were getting up to no good. She never left the Department entirely. Through the 1980s she took sabbaticals for Unspeakable work, which is where her many Muggle friends come from, and she remains a semi-retired Unspeakable to this day.

On one sabbatical she mentored Jack O'Neill, an officer of the United States Air Force, who never knew that she was a witch. They still write to each other, across two large silences. She keeps in touch with David, the soldier called Solid Snake. From the striking resemblance she knows him to be Big Boss's son. With Big Boss himself she is estranged, because he sent another man out into the world to be him, with his face and his memories. She owns a telephone, about which Arthur Weasley has pestered her for fifteen years.

She is a registered Animagus, and her cat is a tabby with the marks of her spectacles round its eyes. On 1 November 1981 she sat on a garden wall in Surrey as that cat for most of a day, watching the Dursleys. At midnight she told Dumbledore what she thought of them, and she was overruled. She has followed Harry's file ever since, and has noted the bars on his window.

Teaching

Her lessons are exact and unforgiving. Before her first lesson with Harry's year began, she turned her desk into a pig and back again. She set the first-years to turn matches into needles, and she teaches that Transfiguration depends on intent.

In 1993 she taught its limits. Some creatures go in through the back of the neck and wrap themselves round the spine. They speak through the host's mouth with shining eyes and a doubled voice. No Transfiguration can part them from the host.

Outside the syllabus she has told Harry a good many things. No charm, she told him, turns a werewolf back into a man. One must be Stunned from a distance, by at least three casters from different directions; silver kills. The Garou serve Gaia against the Wyrm, stand nine feet tall in the Crinos and cloud the memory of anyone who sees them. Of one kind of Garou she gave a particular warning. 'If it has black fur, and it's dancing, run faster.' She has murmured, too, that Tzimisce has three syllables, not four. Nor, she says, is a vampire of the fourth generation killed with a wand. Struck down, a Tzimisce does not fall: it comes apart and walks off in several directions.

Personality and appearance

McGonagall is tall and extremely stern. She wears square spectacles, with her black hair in a tight bun by day and in a plait at night. At bedtime she adds a tartan dressing gown and a hairnet. She can arrive without a sound.

She cannot abide being lied to. That trait ended her friendships with Bond and with Big Boss. It also made Lockhart her natural enemy. She is fiercely partisan about Quidditch. After Slytherin flattened Gryffindor in one final, she could not look Snape in the eye for weeks.

Her past comes to the surface only in rare, dry asides, and in a particular knowing look. Harry has come to feel that underneath she is somebody else entirely. Hermione Granger's boggart takes her shape, to tell Hermione that she has failed everything.

In the saga: 1991 to 1992

She received the first-years from Hagrid and conducted the Sorting. After seeing Harry's dive for Neville's Remembrall she made him Gryffindor's Seeker. She sent him a Nimbus Two Thousand and told him his father had been a fine player, though she never delivered the reports of James's matches that she had promised.

When Charlie Weasley's letter told her the dragon was real, she covered for Harry. She called Dracina Malfoy's account a lie in public, while taking fifty points each from Harry, Hermione and Neville. She advised him that one is only punished for what one is caught doing. In the exams she let slip Kosovo and Kandahar. Her giant chessmen guarded the Philosopher's Stone.

In the saga: 1992 to 1993

She gave Harry and Ron detentions for the flying car, then conjured them sandwiches. She exposed Lockhart's lies about the vocal-cord parasite, and about Julius, whom he called Julius Carrow. She warned him that if he brought another creature into a classroom without her written permission, he would leave by the window the pixies had used. She opposed Snape's attempt to take Harry off the team, noting that the cat had not been hit with a broomstick.

At Christmas she tilted Dracina's chin to the light, and asked when she had last slept through the night. When Hermione was attacked, she told Harry and Ron gently. When Ginny was taken, she warned Harry that even with her training she would not go into the Chamber alone, citing the Garou and William the Bloody. She and the other staff manoeuvred Lockhart into facing the monster by himself. Snape treats her with wary respect. He once ordered Dracina to speak of her respectfully.

In the saga: 1993 to 1994

Now Deputy Headmistress, she obtained a Time-Turner from the Ministry for Hermione's impossible timetable. She swore Hermione to secrecy, and lectured her on the dangers of time. She turned into a tabby cat for her lesson on Animagi. She told Harry that Trelawney predicted a pupil's death every year, and that none had obliged. After Black's break-in she told Harry plainly that he was Black's object. She forbade him to go about alone after dark, and she set Madam Hooch over Gryffindor's practices.

At Christmas she told the table about Siberia. When Pomona Sprout asked where her young man was now, she said she had not had word of him in some years. He was the better of the two of them, she said, and the people who use men like that use them up. 'Eat your pudding, Pomona, it's going cold.'

She confiscated Harry's anonymous Firebolt to have it stripped for jinxes. She returned it in late February, smiling, and said he had a very good friend somewhere. When he hugged her, she stood a long while on the landing. Watching five boys escort him down the stairs, she remarked over her toast that they were more protective than 'those absolute glaikits in Afghanistan'.

She called the fake dementors an unworthy trick, and took fifty points from Slytherin. She banned Neville from Hogsmeade for losing the passwords. At the final she lost her hat. When Gryffindor won the Cup, she wept into a Gryffindor flag. Snape said that she kept a silver dagger ready in case Lupin proved dangerous.

In their own words

I've had more convincing lies out of feral mujahideen who were... oh, bother.Minerva McGonagall · B1 Ch11
I learned the hard way, Potter, that one is only ever punished for what one is caught doing.Minerva McGonagall · B1 Ch11
I suppose you think you're hard men, the pair of you, who can defy authority!Minerva McGonagall · B1 Ch12
You're learning, Potter. Very good.Minerva McGonagall · B2 Ch6
