pages.title: The Fat Friar
infobox:
Helga Hufflepuff teacher in his youth
Harry Potter confidant, counsel
Hermione Granger acquaintance
Lily Potter helped
Ghost, Hufflepuff, ghost, Hogwarts ghost, Hogwarts, Benedictine, Christian
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Hogwarts, in its first years, under Helga Hufflepuff
About two centuries before the first friars reached England
His priory on the Wash, until its dissolution
The window at the end of the kitchen corridor
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
The Fat Friar is the ghost of Hufflepuff house, a plump, round, bald and cheerful Benedictine monk. He was a boy at Hogwarts when the school was new, and Helga Hufflepuff taught him herself. For centuries he haunted his own priory on the Wash; when King Henry pulled it down, he came home to the castle. In Harry Potter's third year, 1993 to 1994, the Friar became his counsellor in matters of faith. He turned Harry back from vengeance, and told him plainly that he had touched God.

Life

The Friar was a pupil at Hogwarts in its earliest years, when the hall on the crag had half a roof and no gate. Many of the villagers who came up to stare gave it ten years. Helga Hufflepuff boxed his ears in his first week for turning the porridge into frogspawn, and often caught him in the honey crock. He remembers her as a great woman and a terrible cook.

One winter a very tall old man in a grey hat walked up out of the valley in the snow. He sat half the night by the kitchen fire with the first-years, telling them that magic was a gift, given long ago by Somebody who had never given up on men. It was not theirs, he said, to do as they liked with. The Friar never asked his name. It was Gandalf, who had gathered the four founders in the first place.

In those days, the Friar says, half the boys who left the school went into the Church, while the witches went home to be the wise women of their villages. He became a Benedictine monk himself, at a priory that was in effect a school of magic, believing that God had given magic on purpose, to be used in His service. He is a monk, not a friar. The friars reached England a couple of hundred years after he died, but the name stuck to him like porridge, and he gave up correcting people at about the time of the Armada.

Death and haunting

After his death he haunted his own priory on the Wash for a few hundred years. Then King Henry VIII pulled it down to sell the lead off the roof, and the Friar came home to Hogwarts.

The old rule of the Church, already old when he was a novice, held that belief in witches who rode out at night was a delusion. From beyond the grave the Friar watched that view harden. The writings of the Dominican Johannes Nider, and then the Malleus Maleficarum of 1486, made witchcraft an organised heresy. England, Wales and Scotland went their own way: when they came to make laws about it, they made it a felony rather than a heresy. He watched friends burn.

He now haunts a tall window at the far end of the ground-floor corridor that leads down to the kitchens, which nobody uses but the house-elves. He says he has not been anywhere else for a great many centuries.

Personality

The Friar is generous, humorous and unhurried. He is a portly ghost with a rope girdle, a broad transparent face and the look of being endlessly pleased about something. In 1991 he argued that Peeves deserved one more chance, and he waves to each new Hufflepuff at the Sorting.

He believes it is God's own joke that wizards keep Christmas without knowing whose feast it is. A man who cannot make a joke about his faith, he says, has generally not looked at it very hard. He helped Lily Potter with her faith when she was about thirteen.

In the saga

In November 1993, as Harry was on his way to confront Snape for humiliating Hermione, the Friar came down through the ceiling. He told Harry the story of David, the shepherd king, who was turned back from killing the household of the fool Nabal when Nabal's wife Abigail knelt in the road with bread, wine and two hundred fig cakes. Wrath, he warned, pays its wages in the morning, and always pays in full. He told Harry he would have made a decent Hufflepuff.

In the spring of 1994 Harry found him at his window and asked why the wizarding world hated Christianity. The Friar gave him the history. When Harry confessed that in church he felt like a burglar, the Friar told him that he had not broken into anybody's house: 'The door was open. It always has been.' Then, without laughing, he heard Harry's account of seeing Jesus by a fallen pillar in the Chamber of Secrets. He said that he believed him, that Christ had been there all along, and that He was proud of him.

After the night of Sirius Black's escape the Friar told Harry that the Patronus had been taught when he was a boy, but that he had never heard of one doing what Harry's had done. It was the doubt going out of Harry that had made it kill. He had touched God, and like Peter walking on the water he had not looked down. The Friar told him to ask the Headmaster about his blood. He also asked him, as a favour, to go into the church near his home just once. A week after he reached Privet Drive that summer, Harry went to Evensong at St Michael's.

In their own words

Wrath pays its wages in the morning, young Potter, and it always pays in full.The Fat Friar · B3 Ch9
A man who can't make a joke about his faith generally hasn't looked at it very hard.The Fat Friar · B3 Ch15
The door was open. It always has been. Nobody's going to ask you for a ticket.The Fat Friar · B3 Ch15
He was proud of you, Harry Potter. You saw it yourself.The Fat Friar · B3 Ch15

pages.title: Nearly Headless Nick
infobox: Nick; Sir Nicholas; Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington

Sir Patrick Delaney-Podmore rival
Harry Potter friend
Ghost, Gryffindor, ghost, Hogwarts ghost, Hogwarts, Gryffindor ghost, Basilisk victim
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington, known to everyone but himself as Nearly Headless Nick, is the resident ghost of Gryffindor Tower. He was beheaded so badly on 31 October 1492 that an inch of skin and sinew still holds his head on. A sociable, sensitive ghost in a ruff and tights, he befriended Harry Potter. In December 1992 the Basilisk Petrified him, the only ghost it ever struck.

Life and death

Sir Nicholas was a wizard who served as a courtier at the court of King Henry VII. One afternoon, out walking, he met the Lady Grieve and offered to straighten her teeth by magic. The spell went wrong, leaving her with a tusk. He was condemned for it.

On 31 October 1492 he was struck forty-five times on the neck with a blunt axe. It left an inch of skin and sinew holding his head to his body, so that the head now swings off his neck as if on a hinge. He has to be careful whenever he moves it. He chose to stay behind as a ghost, and he is older than the Reformation.

Because of that inch, he has been refused membership of the Headless Hunt. The Hunt is led by Sir Patrick Delaney-Podmore. Its members play Head Polo and Horseback Head-Juggling, for which a head has to come properly off. Nick has not eaten in almost five hundred years. He still misses it, and he watches the living eat with a wistful look.

Personality

Nick is courteous, a little pompous and easily put out. He would much prefer to be called Sir Nicholas. He is delighted whenever anyone is impressed by his trick with his head. He told Harry that ghosts are dreadful gossips who moan endlessly about how they died, and he was grateful when Harry agreed.

He takes the House Cup to heart. In 1991 he told the new Gryffindors that the house had never gone so long without it, adding that the Bloody Baron was becoming insufferable.

In the saga

Nick sat opposite Harry at his first feast in 1991. He patted Harry's arm, which felt like plunging it into icy water, and showed the first-years how nearly headless he was.

In October 1992 the Headless Hunt refused him again. Dracina Malfoy offered him mocking condolences, having heard the story, he believed, from the Bloody Baron. Still smarting, he caught Harry being marched to Filch's office. He persuaded Peeves to drop a cabinet overhead, so that Harry could escape punishment. In gratitude Harry, Ron and Hermione went to his five hundredth Deathday Party on Hallowe'en 1992, which kept them from the feast. Harry later thought it the nearest thing to religion he had seen at Hogwarts. When Sir Patrick arrived to mock him, Harry defended Nick in front of everyone, then told Sir Patrick to leave. Nick looked at him as though he had waited five hundred years for somebody to take his side.

In December 1992 Nick was found beside Justin Finch-Fletchley. He had turned black and smoky. He floated flat and motionless six inches above the floor, with the same shocked look on his face as Justin. He had taken the full blast of the Basilisk's stare. Since he could not die again he was Petrified, while Justin, who saw the creature only through him, survived. The attack on a ghost frightened the school more than any other. He was revived with the Mandrake draught in 1993.

At the Hallowe'en feast of 1993 he re-enacted his own bungled beheading. In 1994 he told Ron he had heard that a very rough crowd lived in the Shrieking Shack. He also kept sending Harry to places where the Fat Friar had just been.

pages.title: Peeves
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
A battered hat and an orange bow tie
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Peeves is the poltergeist of Hogwarts: a solid-looking little man with wicked dark eyes and a wide mouth, who lives to cause chaos. Only the Bloody Baron can control him. In 1992, however, he met one other visitor he did not dare to cross.

Habits

Peeves is not a ghost, and he has never been alive. He has haunted the castle for as long as anybody can remember, usually in a battered hat with an orange bow tie, and he can make himself invisible whenever it suits him. He likes to float about cross-legged in the air, or to hang upside down while he thinks of something worse to do.

His favourite victims are the new pupils, whom he pelts with walking sticks, chalk and ink pellets, or sends the wrong way to their lessons. He tips wastepaper baskets over people's heads from the gallery above the Entrance Hall. He loosens the carpets on the stairs, and he sings rude songs about whoever happens to be nearest; one of them was about Harry Potter's hair.

The caretaker, Argus Filch, is his oldest enemy. Peeves once made Filch say please before telling him nothing at all. The only person he gives way to is the Bloody Baron. In June 1992 Harry, invisible under his cloak, did an impression of the Baron, and Peeves grovelled greasily to the empty air: 'So sorry, your bloodiness, Mr Baron, sir.'

In the saga

In 1991 Peeves greeted the new first-years with 'Ickle firsties!' He betrayed Harry and his friends to Filch by bellowing 'Students out of bed!' On the night Norbert left, he was playing tennis against the wall of the Entrance Hall.

In October 1992, at Nearly Headless Nick's request, he crashed a valuable vanishing cabinet down over Filch's office. At Nick's Deathday Party he wore an orange party hat with a spinning bow tie and offered round mouldy peanuts. He repeated Hermione's remarks to Moaning Myrtle, then chased Myrtle off, shouting 'Spotty'. That Hallowe'en he upset her so badly that she tried to kill herself, quite forgetting that she was already dead.

It was Peeves who found Harry standing over the Petrified Justin and Nick. He screamed the alarm, 'ANOTHER ONE'S BEEN GOT!', and doors flew open all down the corridor. When he burst into a song about it, 'Oh Potter, the plotter', Professor McGonagall ordered him out. Later he conducted the enchanted armour's can-can from a chandelier with a stick of celery. For months he kept singing 'Oh Potter, the plotter' in crowded corridors, now with a high-kicking dance to go with it, until in the spring of 1993 he grew bored of it at last.

When Ambrose Greyhame came up to the castle in December 1992, Peeves was lying in wait with a handful of ink pellets. He raised his arm to throw them and took one look at the old man. Then he hid the pellets behind his back and shot away through a wall without a word.

In September 1993 he found Dracina Malfoy's silver serpent brooch, set with emeralds, lying by the dungeon steps. Hermione had taken it from Dracina's hair and left it there for him to find. He pinned it to his orange bow tie and was showing it off, upside down outside a broom cupboard with its keyhole full of chewing gum, when Professor Lupin's class came by. He sang at Lupin, 'Shabby Lupin, shabby Lupin, patches on his patches!', and blew a raspberry in his face. Lupin's Waddiwasi shot the gum straight up his left nostril. Peeves fled howling, tore the brooch off his bow tie as he went and flung it into a fire bucket.

On Hallowe'en he told Dumbledore that Sirius Black had slashed the Fat Lady: 'Shocking temper on him.' He woke Harry at half past four on the morning of the Hufflepuff match by blowing in his ear. On the night of the escape in June 1994 he turned somersaults along a portrait corridor, cheering the silver Patronuses and blowing raspberries at the dementors: 'Dementies in a tizzy! Ministry in a flap! Oh, it's better than Christmas, it is!'

In their own words

Oooooh! Ickle firsties! What a treat!Peeves · B1 Ch3
So sorry, your bloodiness, Mr Baron, sir.Peeves · B1 Ch12
ANOTHER ONE'S BEEN GOT! THE LIVING AND THE DEAD, THERE'S NOBODY SAFE!Peeves · B2 Ch12
Shabby Lupin, shabby Lupin, patches on his patches!Peeves · B3 Ch7

pages.title: Sorting Hat
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Tenth century, by the four founders of Hogwarts
On a shelf behind the Headmaster's desk
Sorting first-years into the four houses
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
The Sorting Hat is the patched, frayed old wizard's hat that sorts each year's new pupils at Hogwarts into Gryffindor, Hufflepuff, Ravenclaw or Slytherin by reading their minds. It knew the four founders personally, and it sings a new song every year. From December 1992 it held, hidden in its brim, the sword that Harry Potter drew from it in the Chamber of Secrets.

Description and history

The Hat is a pointed wizard's hat, patched, frayed and filthy, of the sort Aunt Petunia would have carried to the dustbin with the fire tongs. A tear near the brim opens like a mouth when it sings. It once belonged to Godric Gryffindor. The four founders enchanted it with something of their own minds, so that it could go on choosing their students after they were gone. It knew all four of them as people. It still speaks of them by their first names, Godric, Helga and Salazar.

Between Sortings it sits on a shelf behind the Headmaster's desk. Dumbledore says it gets lonely there, since it so rarely has anyone to talk to. It is said never to have been wrong, and it never changes its mind.

The Sorting

On the first night of each school year Professor McGonagall sets the Hat on a stool in the Great Hall and calls each first-year forward to put it on. After its song it sorts each child by looking into the head beneath it. Sometimes it decides in an instant, and sometimes only after long thought. When it takes more than five minutes, the case is called a hatstall. Its song of 1991 sent to Gryffindor 'the bold, the daring and the true'. Hufflepuff was to have 'the fair of heart who see a hard task through', Ravenclaw 'the quick of wit' and Slytherin 'the cunning', 'who leave no means behind'.

It sent John Constantine to Slytherin in 1964 for his cunning, almost before it had touched his hair. Minutes later it sorted Lucius Malfoy into the same house. In 1991 it placed Dracina Malfoy in Slytherin almost the moment it touched her. It took nearly a minute over Seamus Finnigan. It took a long time over Neville Longbottom, who ran off still wearing it. On 1 September 1992 it sorted Ginny Weasley into Gryffindor.

Harry Potter

Harry was one of the hardest pupils the Hat ever had to place. It found in him a good deal of courage, a sound mind, talent and a healthy wish to prove himself. It also found 'so much pain, too, for one so young'. It told him that he could be great in Slytherin, and that Slytherin would set him well on the road to greatness. When he begged it, 'Not Slytherin', it respected his wish and sent him to Gryffindor.

In December 1992, alone in Dumbledore's office, Harry put the Hat on again to ask whether it had got him wrong. It told him that it did not change its mind. His sadness, his pain, his need to prove himself, his drive and his resolve were all traits that Slytherin had prized. Of all the minds it had ever sat on, it said, his reminded it most of Slytherin's.

It defended Salazar Slytherin sharply. He was never evil, it said, only difficult, proud and suspicious, with good reason. He had quarrelled with Godric over a great many things, and at the end over one thing too many. He would never have stood for evil in his house, and his going broke Helga's heart. Godric, it added, would have been very proud of Harry too.

It warned him that every house's virtue can be turned to evil, even Hufflepuff's kindness, in the hands of somebody convinced she is working for the greater good. Many of the darkest wizards it had sat on, it said, began with the best of intentions, before the master of all that darkness drew them away. When Harry asked who that master was, it made a horrible choking noise and went dead in his hands.

The sword in the brim

On the night of the Duelling Club in December 1992, Ambrose Greyhame brought Dumbledore a long, narrow package wrapped in oilcloth. The next morning Dumbledore laid it inside the Hat's brim. The Hat swallowed it, quite impossibly, with a muffled sigh: the sound of something recognising an old friend. When Harry wore the Hat shortly afterwards, it was much heavier than he remembered. Something inside the brim shifted with a sound like a bell struck a long way off.

In 1993, as Harry lay wounded before the Basilisk in the Chamber of Secrets, Fawkes brought him the Hat. Harry pushed his hand down into it, past where the bottom ought to have been, and drew out a long sword, much longer than the Hat was deep. The sword is Andúril, the sword of Elendil reforged for Aragorn, which Gandalf had carried back to Hogwarts. Harry worked that out over the winter of his third year, and he has told nobody. He carried the Hat back up the pipe tucked into his belt.

In the saga

Harry and Hermione missed the Sorting of 1993. Professor McGonagall had kept them in her office after the dementor boarded the train. They came into the Great Hall just as Professor Flitwick was carrying the Hat and its stool away. Harry has never told Ron or Hermione how seriously the Hat considered putting him in Slytherin.

Quotations

And so much pain, too, for one so young... now, that is interesting.The Sorting Hat · B1 Ch3
Salazar Slytherin was never evil, boy. Never.Sorting Hat · B2 Ch14

pages.title: Hannah Abbott
infobox: Ernie Macmillan, Justin Finch-Fletchley, Susan Bones
pages.html:
Hannah Abbott is a half-blood witch of Hufflepuff House in Harry Potter's year, a pink-faced girl with fair pigtails. In 1991 she was the very first of the new students to be sorted.

Life

Hannah comes of one of the old wizarding families; the Abbotts were counted among the pure-bloods in the 1930s, although Hannah herself is a half-blood. She was the first of the first-years called up to the Sorting Hat on 1 September 1991. She went pinker than ever as she stumbled forward. The Hat dropped straight down over her eyes, and after a pause it sent her to Hufflepuff. The Hufflepuff table cheered her all the way across the Hall, the Fat Friar gave her a jolly wave, and Susan Bones, who was sorted next, hurried over to sit beside her.

Her closest friends are Ernie Macmillan, Justin Finch-Fletchley and Susan. She takes Herbology with the Gryffindors of her year. She is a kind, nervous girl, easily frightened by rumour and just as easily reassured. She sets great store by what her gran says.

In the saga

After the attack on Mrs Norris in October 1992, Justin once hurried away from Harry without a backward glance. His friends did look back. Hannah gazed at Harry over her shoulder with frightened eyes. Harry heard her repeating what her gran said.

That winter the Hufflepuffs gathered at the back of the library to discuss whether Harry was the Heir of Slytherin. Ernie was sure of it. Hannah was not. 'But he's always seemed so nice,' she said uncertainly. 'And he's the one who got rid of You-Know-Who. He can't be all bad. Can he?' Harry chose that moment to step out from behind the bookshelves, spread his arms and introduce himself as the Dark Lord Potter, to show them how silly they sounded. Hannah let out a small squeak.

In the spring of 1993, once Ernie had apologised to Harry, Hannah came with him to work beside Harry and Ron in Herbology, pruning Abyssinian Shrivelfigs. Ernie wondered aloud whether Dracina Malfoy might be the Heir. Harry said only 'Maybe', so flatly that both Hufflepuffs stared at him. A moment later they watched curiously as a line of spiders hurried across the vegetable patch and away over the lawn.

pages.title: Susan Bones
infobox: Edgar Bones (killed in the first war)
pages.html:
Susan Bones is a witch of Hufflepuff House in Harry Potter's year, the second pupil to be sorted in 1991. Her family suffered heavily in the first war against Voldemort.

Family

Susan has red hair, which she wears in a long plait. She is the niece of Amelia Bones, a senior official in the Department of Magical Law Enforcement at the Ministry of Magic, who is known for being strict but fair. Several of her relatives were killed by Voldemort's followers in the first war. Among them was Amelia's brother, Susan's uncle Edgar Bones, who died with his family. So Susan, like Harry, has grown up with the gaps that a war leaves in a family.

In the saga

Susan was sorted into Hufflepuff on 1 September 1991, straight after Hannah Abbott. She hurried away to sit by Hannah at the Hufflepuff table. As a Hufflepuff in Harry's year she shares Herbology with the Gryffindors in the greenhouses, along with Hannah, Ernie Macmillan and Justin Finch-Fletchley.

pages.title: Terry Boot
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
pages.html:
Terry Boot is a Ravenclaw wizard in Harry Potter's year at Hogwarts. At the Sorting of 1 September 1991 he was the first new Ravenclaw of the night.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, Terry came third to the stool, after Hannah Abbott and Susan Bones had both gone to Hufflepuff. The Sorting Hat shouted 'RAVENCLAW!' This time the applause came from the second table on the left. Several Ravenclaws stood up to shake Terry's hand.

pages.title: Mandy Brocklehurst
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
pages.html:
Mandy Brocklehurst is a Ravenclaw witch in Harry Potter's year at Hogwarts. She was sorted into Ravenclaw on 1 September 1991.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, Mandy followed Terry Boot to the Ravenclaw table, the second new Ravenclaw of the night. Lavender Brown, who came next, became the first Gryffindor, and the table at the far left erupted.

pages.title: Lavender Brown
infobox:
Parvati Patil friend, best friend
Binky pet rabbit
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Lavender Brown is a Gryffindor witch in Harry Potter's year, and the best friend of Parvati Patil. She is a great spreader of rumours and a devoted follower of Professor Trelawney. In October 1993 a fox killed her rabbit, Binky, and she took it as proof of a prophecy.

Background

Lavender was the first new Gryffindor to be sorted in 1991. She comes from a village with a Muggle school. In 1993 she was afraid that she would have to go there if the Ministry sent the students home. With Parvati she follows Take That, and the two of them visit Professor Trelawney's tower at lunchtimes.

In the saga

On Hallowe'en 1991 Lavender heard from Parvati that Hermione was crying in the girls' toilets. In 1992 she started the rumour that fifty centaurs had attacked Quirrell, though she had not been there, as Dean pointed out. She told Ron that Ginny cried every night after the attack on Mrs Norris. She sighed over Lockhart until even she grew tired of his stories. When Snape disarmed Lockhart at the Duelling Club, it was Lavender who handed him back his wand. After the double attack of 1993 she cried in the common room. Her mother had written, she said, that the Ministry was drawing up letters to send the students home.

In her first Divination lesson in 1993 Trelawney told her that the thing she was dreading would happen on 16 October. She shrieked at Dracina Malfoy's joke about a dementor. When Harry volunteered for Buckbeak she swooned, which earned her glares from Hermione and Dracina alike. On 16 October she learnt that a fox had killed her rabbit, Binky. Hermione picked apart her belief that Trelawney had foreseen it, then lent her a clean handkerchief. Later, when Lavender called Crookshanks a murderer, Hermione silenced her by reminding her of that handkerchief. Lavender privately wondered when Hermione would turn up on the Muggle news. She also noticed that Lupin's boggart, a werewolf, seemed to know him.

In their own words

It's the sixteenth of October!Lavender Brown · B3 Ch8

pages.title: Millicent Bulstrode
infobox: The Bulstrodes, an old pure-blood family
pages.html:
Millicent Bulstrode is a broad, square-shouldered Slytherin girl in Harry Potter's year. She is best remembered for the headlock she put on Hermione Granger at the Duelling Club, and for the cat whose hair ended up in Hermione's Polyjuice Potion.

Description

Millicent is a big, broad, square-shouldered girl with a heavy jaw. To Harry she looked as though she would be more at home wrestling trolls than duelling. She would certainly rather settle a quarrel with her arms than with her wand. She keeps a cat.

The Bulstrodes are one of the old pure-blood families of Britain, among the twenty-eight named in the Pure-Blood Directory of the 1930s.

At Hogwarts

Millicent was the first of Harry's year to be sorted into Slytherin, in September 1991. Harry studied the table that received her and thought they looked an unpleasant crowd, with a well-fed, pleased-with-themselves air. They reminded him, every one, of Dudley.

At the Duelling Club in December 1992 she was paired with Hermione Granger, and soon had her in a headlock. Afterwards Hermione found a hair on her own robes and kept it. She was brewing Polyjuice Potion so as to question Dracina Malfoy in disguise. She meant to take Millicent's shape, since Millicent would be at home for Christmas.

The hair was not Millicent's at all. It had come off her cat. On Christmas Day the potion turned Hermione into a cat-girl, and she spent weeks in the hospital wing. Ron Weasley maintained that it was all Millicent's fault for having a cat.

pages.title: Justin Finch-Fletchley
infobox: Hufflepuff, Hogwarts student, Muggle-born, Basilisk victim
pages.html:
Justin Finch-Fletchley is a curly-haired, well-spoken Muggle-born wizard in Hufflepuff, in Harry Potter's year. His name was down for Eton before his Hogwarts letter came. In December 1992, soon after accusing Harry of setting a snake on him, he was Petrified by the Basilisk of the Chamber of Secrets.

Background

Justin was sorted into Hufflepuff in 1991. His name had been down for Eton, and his mother was a little disappointed when he went to Hogwarts instead. He admired Gilderoy Lockhart so much that he made her read Lockhart's books. His favourite was the tale of the werewolf in the telephone box. Ron thought him an idiot for going on about how great Lockhart was.

In the saga

On 2 September 1992 Justin shared a Mandrake tray with Harry, Ron and Hermione in Herbology. He told Harry about Eton. After the attack on Mrs Norris he turned and fled when he saw Harry coming along a corridor. At the Duelling Club Lockhart paired him with Neville Longbottom. When Dracina Malfoy's conjured snake menaced him, Harry spoke to it in Parseltongue. The terrified Justin accused Harry of setting it on him and ran from the Hall.

Ernie Macmillan told him to stay hidden in the dormitory. All the same, Justin was found during a cancelled Herbology lesson, in a dark corridor by a loose window, Petrified beside Nearly Headless Nick. He had seen the Basilisk's eyes through the ghost. Professors Flitwick and Sinistra carried him up to the hospital wing. He was revived with Mandrake juice in June 1993. At the feast he hurried over to Harry and apologised about fifteen times.

pages.title: Seamus Finnigan
infobox: A witch mother and a Muggle father
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Seamus Finnigan is a half-blood Irish wizard in Harry Potter's year, and he shares Harry's dormitory in Gryffindor Tower. He is sandy-haired, cheerful and inclined to set things on fire. He can be relied on for the latest school gossip, and he is a loud supporter at Quidditch matches.

Background

Seamus is half and half. His father is a Muggle, whose witch wife did not tell him what she was until after they were married. Seamus claimed to have spent his childhood flying over the Irish countryside, chased by leprechauns whose gold he had stolen. At the Sorting in 1991 he sat under the Hat for nearly a minute before it chose Gryffindor. At the feast that followed he sang the school song like a football chant.

In the saga

Seamus asked Professor Quirrell whether he had fought a vampire in Romania. In their first Potions lesson Neville melted Seamus's cauldron. Partnered with Harry in Charms, he lost patience with their feather and set it alight. In 1992 he set fire to his own eyebrows, and a Potions explosion swelled his ear up like a cushion. It was Seamus who warned Harry that the Seeker always gets nobbled. He helped to make the Potter for President banner, and he lent Harry his chess set, whose pieces did not trust Harry an inch. Professor Binns called him O'Halloran. He spread the story that fifty centaurs had attacked Quirrell, which he had from Lavender Brown.

In 1993 Seamus ogled the Firebolt in Diagon Alley. He sniggered that Harry was getting messages in Divination, and said he would only believe in a Grim if he could grab a fistful of its fur, even if he died of it. He laughed when Harry asked him about signs. His boggart was a banshee, which he silenced. He called Sir Cadogan a nutter, and he reported that a Muggle dog-walker had sighted Sirius Black. He told Harry about Cho Chang's bag splitting on the marble staircase.

In a Charms lesson in the spring of 1994 he cheered Dean with a Cheering Charm so hard that Dean had to be sent out to calm down. At the Quidditch final he bawled abuse at the Slytherins. In the weeks before the N.E.W.T.s, Percy Weasley confiscated three of Seamus's Chocolate Frogs and ate one.

In their own words

I'd be dead and sure. That's more than most people get.Seamus Finnigan · B3 Ch6

pages.title: Seamus Finnigan's father
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
pages.html:
Seamus Finnigan's father is a Muggle. His wife, Seamus's mother, is a witch, and she did not tell him so until after they were married. It gave him a fright.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, at the feast after the Sorting on 1 September 1991, the talk turned to families over the puddings. 'I'm half and half,' said Seamus. 'Me da's a Muggle. Mam never told him she was a witch till they were married. Gave him a fair old fright.'

The others laughed, and so did Harry Potter. Then he remembered some of the things Uncle Vernon liked to shout at the television about the Irish. He looked at Seamus, cheerfully passing Neville the custard, and decided that his uncle had been wrong about that, as he was about most things.

pages.title: Seamus Finnigan's mother
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
pages.html:
Seamus Finnigan's mother is an Irish witch who married a Muggle and did not tell him what she was until after the wedding. According to Seamus, it gave his father a fair old fright.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, at the start-of-term feast in September 1991, Seamus explained himself to the new Gryffindors. 'I'm half and half,' he said. 'Me da's a Muggle. Mam never told him she was a witch till they were married. Gave him a fair old fright.'

The others laughed, and Harry Potter laughed with them. Then he remembered some of the things Uncle Vernon liked to shout at the television about the Irish. He looked at Seamus, who was cheerfully passing Neville the custard, and decided that Uncle Vernon had been wrong about that, as he was about most things.

pages.title: Morag MacDougal
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
pages.html:
Morag MacDougal is a witch in Harry Potter's year at Hogwarts. She was sorted on 1 September 1991, straight after Neville Longbottom, who ran off with the Sorting Hat still on his head.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, Neville fell over on his way to the stool. The Sorting Hat considered him for a long time. When it finally shouted "GRYFFINDOR!" he ran off with it still on his head, then had to trot back through howls of laughter to hand it to Morag, who was next. Dracina Malfoy was called after her.

pages.title: Moon
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
pages.html:
Moon is a student in Harry Potter's year at Hogwarts, known only by surname. Moon was sorted on 1 September 1991, one of the last of that year's first-years.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, by the time the Sorting Hat had sent Dracina Malfoy to Slytherin, there were not many first-years left in the line. Moon came next, followed by Nott and Parkinson. Then came a pair of twin girls called Patil, then Sally-Anne Perks. After them, at last, Harry Potter was called.

pages.title: Theodore Nott
infobox: Mr Nott, a Death Eater of the first war
pages.html:
Theodore Nott is a Slytherin in Harry Potter's year: a thin, solitary boy who keeps his own counsel and stands apart from Dracina Malfoy's circle.

Family

Nott is the son of an elderly widower who served Lord Voldemort as a Death Eater in the first war. Like Lucius Malfoy, his father kept out of Azkaban after his master's fall. Theodore's mother is dead, and he lives with his father.

At Hogwarts

Nott was sorted in September 1991, between Dracina Malfoy and Harry Potter in the alphabet: he was called up just after Moon, with Parkinson next. The Hat put him in Slytherin.

He is a clever, rather weedy boy, and very much a loner. He has never been one of Dracina's circle. The bullying of Gryffindors he leaves to Crabbe, Goyle and Pansy Parkinson. So far he has made little mark on Harry's years at the school.

In the saga

In December 1992 Dracina was overheard at dinner talking to an invisible 'Tom'. Ron Weasley pointed out to Harry that nobody in Slytherin answered to the name: 'There isn't a Tom in Slytherin. Not in our year. There's Theodore Nott, but nobody calls him Tom.'

pages.title: Pansy Parkinson
infobox:
Dracina Malfoy friend, housemate, friend and follower
Daphne Greengrass housemate, friend
Ron Weasley crush
Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Pansy Parkinson is a Slytherin witch in Harry Potter's year: Dracina Malfoy's closest friend, and the most loyal. In the autumn of 1993 it was Pansy, meaning only to be helpful, who posted the letter that condemned the hippogriff Buckbeak. She carried the secret for six months.

Description

Pansy is a hard-faced girl with a flat, snub-nosed face like a disappointed pug, and a laugh like a horse that could strip paint. She reads Witch Weekly. Until 1994 she had no interest at all in Quidditch, and used to take a novel to Slytherin matches.

She was one of the friends Lucius Malfoy chose for his daughter. Of them all, though, she is the one whose devotion is entirely her own. She has followed Dracina for nearly three years 'like a shadow with a bad temper', and puts up with her without complaint.

1991 to 1993

Pansy was sorted into Slytherin in September 1991, and was soon shrieking with laughter at Dracina's side. Neville Longbottom's fall from his broom set her off, as did every taunt Dracina aimed at Harry and his friends. She turned on Parvati Patil for sticking up for Neville. At the end-of-year feast in 1992, when Dracina wept over the House Cup, Pansy was the only person who comforted her, holding her with both arms.

Through the autumn of 1992 she watched Dracina withdraw into a small black book. She jumped when Dracina slammed it shut. When Dracina spoke to the empty air at dinner, Pansy asked her whom she was talking to. On Christmas night she mocked Harry as a broom handle with glasses whom the Muggles must starve. When Dracina screamed and broke down, Pansy held her, apologising.

On Boxing Day she followed her into the Great Hall, begging her to come back. She walked beside her stretcher holding her limp hand, crying. She sat with Dracina through the spring. At the end of term she led her away from the carriages, still weeping, saying that Dracina was not well yet.

The Buckbeak letter

Pansy wrote to Dracina every day of the summer of 1993, about nothing in particular. When Buckbeak slashed Dracina's arm in September, she sobbed that Hagrid should be sacked. She blamed Harry, and brought flowers to the hospital wing. Dracina wrote her father a furious letter four pages long, then left it on the table beside her bed in the hospital wing. Pansy believed it was what a friend would want. She took it to the Owlery herself, and said nothing.

In a Potions lesson soon afterwards she heard Dracina tell Harry that she had decided not to send it. Pansy went the colour of the dungeon wall. The guilt sat on her chest like a cat. In November, when the Slytherins called on Harry in the hospital wing, she stared in fright at the bare table by Dracina's old bed, where the letter had lain. She went pale again when Lucius's green-wax letter of thanks arrived in March. She went pale a third time when Dracina accused Hermione of stealing the letter. Dracina never suspected her. After the mud fight at the Shrieking Shack, Pansy waited outside Snape's office with a towel and Sleekeazy's Hair Potion, which Dracina refused.

On the night of Buckbeak's execution Dracina told Pansy everything she meant to do. Pansy covered for her until breakfast, telling Slytherin House that Dracina was in the hospital wing with a sprained wrist. Then she waited up for her.

The next day, on the castle steps, she confessed in tears that she had sent the letter: 'I thought you wanted the letter sent. I thought you left it and I was being helpful.' Dracina flew at her. Ron Weasley calmly talked Dracina out of her rage. Pansy stopped sobbing to stare at him. She thanked him in a small voice, twisting her hair round her finger. She knows a piece of what really happened that night, and has told nobody.

Ron Weasley

On the train home in June 1994 Pansy lingered in the compartment doorway to say 'Bye, Weasley', giggling nervously until Daphne Greengrass pulled her away by the elbow. That summer she took up the Chudley Cannons. She hung an orange poster over her bed, then wrote to Dracina four times in a fortnight about their Keeper. She added that she appreciated that they were all English. Ron has not noticed a thing.

Personality

Pansy can be cruel. She taunted Harry that something cold was coming for him. She taunted him too about his unsigned Hogsmeade form ('Did your Muggles forget to sign your little form? Or can't they write?'), until Dracina stopped her.

But she is loyal to the bone. At the storm match of November 1993 she held a dead umbrella over Dracina. When Dracina tried to climb over the rail as Harry fell, Pansy caught her cloak. Through the December practices she held a green umbrella over her. She sighs at Dracina's behaviour towards Harry with exactly the long-suffering nasal droop of Ron Weasley.

In their own words

He's like a broom handle with glasses on. A strong wind would have him over.Pansy Parkinson · B2 Ch14
Did your Muggles forget to sign your little form? Or can't they write?Pansy Parkinson · B3 Ch8
I thought you wanted the letter sent. I thought you left it and I was being helpful.Pansy Parkinson · B3 Ch22
Bye, Weasley.Pansy Parkinson · B3 Ch22

pages.title: Parvati Patil
infobox:
Parvati Patil's twin sister twin sister
Lavender Brown friend, best friend
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Parvati Patil is a Gryffindor witch in Harry Potter's year. She is the twin sister of Padma Patil of Ravenclaw, and the best friend of Lavender Brown. She is devoted to Divination and to Professor Trelawney.

Background

Parvati and Padma were sorted in 1991, shortly before Harry. Padma went to Ravenclaw, Parvati to Gryffindor, where she shares a dormitory with Lavender and Hermione Granger. The twins feel very passionately about India, though they have never been there. Since Khan Noonien Singh took New Delhi in the summer of 1993, a great deal of the country has been under his rule.

With Lavender, Parvati follows the band Take That. The two of them spend their lunchtimes in Trelawney's tower.

In the saga

At the first flying lesson in 1991 Parvati told Dracina Malfoy to shut up when she mocked Neville. She tried to tell Professor McGonagall that Harry's flight was not his fault. On Hallowe'en she told Lavender that Hermione was crying in the girls' toilets. Hermione hugged her when Harry caught the Snitch against Hufflepuff. In 1992 she suggested to Professor Binns that opening the Chamber of Secrets would need Dark Magic. He called her Miss Pettigrew. In the spring of 1993, when Lavender wept in the common room, Parvati comforted her.

In her first Divination lesson in 1993 Trelawney warned her to beware a man with red hair. Parvati moved her chair away from Ron. She swooned when Harry volunteered to approach Buckbeak. Her boggart was a mummy, which tripped on its own bandage. She asked Lupin whether vampires were on their side. She asked, too, whether they had families like Houses. When Lavender's rabbit died, Parvati comforted her. During revision in 1994 she sat next to Harry in the library, so Hermione moved her to another table. In her Divination exam Trelawney told her she had the makings of a true Seer.

pages.title: Parvati Patil's twin sister
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
pages.html:
Parvati Patil's twin sister started at Hogwarts with her in September 1991. At the Sorting she was simply the other half of a pair of twin girls called Patil. She is Padma Patil, who went to Ravenclaw while her sister went to Gryffindor.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, on 1 September 1991, the twins were among the last few first-years left in line after Dracina Malfoy had been sorted. They came after Moon, Nott and Parkinson. Only Sally-Anne Perks stood between them and Harry Potter.

pages.title: Sally-Anne Perks
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
pages.html:
Sally-Anne Perks is a witch in Harry Potter's year at Hogwarts. At the Sorting on 1 September 1991 she was called immediately before Harry.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, after Dracina Malfoy had gone to Slytherin, there were not many left in the line: Moon, Nott, Parkinson, the Patil twins and Sally-Anne. Then, at last, the call came: "Potter, Harry!" Whispers sprang up all over the Hall like small hissing fires.

pages.title: Lisa Turpin
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
pages.html:
Lisa Turpin is a Ravenclaw witch in Harry Potter's year at Hogwarts. She was among the last first-years to be sorted in September 1991, going to Ravenclaw just before Ron Weasley went to Gryffindor.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, on 1 September 1991, only three first-years were left on the floor of the Great Hall when Lisa's name was called. The Sorting Hat put her in Ravenclaw. Ron Weasley, who had gone pale green with waiting, came next, and Blaise Zabini went last of all, to Slytherin.

pages.title: Blaise Zabini
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
A much-married witch, famous for her beauty
pages.html:
Blaise Zabini is a Slytherin in Harry Potter's year. He was the last of the first-years to be sorted in September 1991.

Appearance and family

Blaise is a tall black boy with high cheekbones and long, slanting eyes. His mother is a witch famous for her beauty. She has been married several times, and each of her husbands has died mysteriously, leaving her richer than before.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, at the Sorting on 1 September 1991, only three students were left when Lisa Turpin went to Ravenclaw. Then the hat put Ron Weasley in Gryffindor. While Percy Weasley was congratulating his brother grandly across Harry, Blaise was sent to Slytherin. Professor McGonagall rolled up her parchment and carried the hat away.

pages.title: Quirinus Quirrell
aliases: the man with Voldemort on the back of his head
the teacher with Voldemort on the back of his head
infobox: Hogwarts staff, Servant of Voldemort, former Hogwarts staff, Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher, Death Eater
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher; formerly Muggle Studies teacher
Book One, Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Quirinus Quirrell was the stammering, turbaned Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher at Hogwarts in 1991 to 1992, and a servant of Lord Voldemort. Under the turban, his master's face grew out of the back of his head. He spent the year trying to steal the Philosopher's Stone, and he died in June 1992, after laying hands on Harry Potter.

Early life

Quirrell was at Hogwarts a few years below James Potter, who, he complained, liked to stick his nose into 'our business'. He was sorted into Ravenclaw. Later he taught Muggle Studies at the school, before taking time away to travel. On his travels, still a foolish young man, he met Lord Voldemort in the forests of Albania. Voldemort taught him that there is no such thing as good or evil, only power, and those too weak to reach for it.

In the summer of 1991 he tried to steal the Philosopher's Stone from vault seven hundred and thirteen at Gringotts, on the very day that Rubeus Hagrid had emptied it. That same day, in the Leaky Cauldron, he shook Harry's hand without quite meeting his eye. Voldemort punished the failure by deciding to keep a much closer watch on him, and took up residence in Quirrell's own body.

Defence teacher

Quirrell taught in a classroom that reeked of garlic, wearing a large purple turban, and he stammered through everything. The garlic, everybody said, was to keep off a vampire he had fought in Romania. When Seamus Finnigan asked him whether that was true, he went white and knocked over his inkwell. Fred and George Weasley bewitched snowballs to bounce off his turban. Snape's sinister looks made perfect cover for him. All year Harry believed that Snape was the danger, and Quirrell the victim.

On Hallowe'en 1991 Quirrell let a troll into the castle; he claimed a special understanding with trolls. Then he ran into the Great Hall to announce it, and fainted. At Harry's first match he jinxed Harry's broom. The jinx held until Hermione Granger, on her way to set fire to Snape's robes, knocked Quirrell head first into the row in front and broke his eye contact. All the while, Snape had been muttering a counter-curse. Snape confronted him in the Forest afterwards and told him to decide where his loyalties lay. Hooded, in the Hog's Head, he bought Hagrid drinks and let him win a dragon's egg at cards. In return he learnt that Fluffy falls asleep to music.

In the spring of 1992 he took Harry, Hermione, Neville Longbottom and Dracina Malfoy into the Forbidden Forest, on a pretended hunt for spotted fire mushrooms. The silver trail that he called mushroom secretion was the blood of a unicorn he had wounded that day. He abandoned the four of them as bait, since unicorns will not come near men like him. His stammer fell away whenever he was irritated. He drank the unicorn's blood for his master. At dawn he was found at the edge of the trees, covered in cuts, howling in tongues. The school blamed the centaurs.

Unmasking and death

In June 1992 he got past Fluffy, knocked out the troll guarding the Stone and reached the Mirror of Erised. Without his stammer he was calm and cold. He told Harry that 'dear Severus does like to sit on the fence', bound him with chains conjured by a snap of his fingers, and unwound his turban to show him Voldemort's face on the back of his head.

When he seized Harry, his hands and face blistered wherever they touched the boy's skin, burned by the protection that Lily Potter's death had left in her son. Dumbledore pulled him off, and Voldemort left him to die.

Harry counts him the first of the Defence teachers who tried to kill him. The hiring of a man with Voldemort on the back of his head is also among the failures that made Harry doubt the adults in charge. Dumbledore described Quirrell and his dark passenger in a letter to Ambrose Greyhame.

In their own words

I'll tell you when I'm damn well ready!Professor Quirrell · B1 Ch11
Whilst dear Severus does like to sit on the fence, he does look the part, doesn't he?Professor Quirrell · B1 Ch13
There's no good and evil, Potter. There's power, and there are those too weak to reach for it.Professor Quirrell · B1 Ch13

Harry Potter least favourite pupil, pupil he dislikes, pupil
Dracina Malfoy favourite pupil, student in his house, favoured pupil
Gilderoy Lockhart colleague
Minerva McGonagall respects

Lord Voldemort marked by
Hogwarts staff, Slytherin, Potions master, Potions, Head of Slytherin, Potions teacher, Death Eater
Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Potions (taught Defence Against the Dark Arts as a substitute in 1993)
Tobias Snape, a Muggle, and Eileen Prince, a witch
Death Eaters; bears the Dark Mark on his left forearm
James Potter, Sirius Black, Remus Lupin, Peter Pettigrew, Lily Evans
Book One, Book Two, Book Three
pages.html:
Severus Snape is the Potions master at Hogwarts and the Head of Slytherin House. He is sallow, black-eyed, sarcastic and widely feared. He is Dracina Malfoy's favourite teacher and Harry Potter's least favourite. A former Death Eater who still bears the Dark Mark, he protects the son of the man he hated, brews the potion that keeps Remus Lupin from killing him, and keeps more secrets than anybody else on the staff.

Early life

Severus Snape was born on 9 January 1960, the son of Tobias Snape, a Muggle, and Eileen Prince, a witch. He grew up at Spinner's End, in the mill town of Cokeworth. As a boy he made friends with a Muggle-born girl from the same town, Lily Evans. Later he called himself the Half-Blood Prince, after his mother's family.

He started at Hogwarts in 1971, in the same year as Remus Lupin, James Potter, Sirius Black and Peter Pettigrew. The Hat put him in Slytherin, while Lily went to Gryffindor. He and James detested each other, partly because Snape was jealous of James's Quidditch. When they were sixteen, Sirius tricked him into prodding the knot of the Whomping Willow and following Lupin down the tunnel. James pulled him back, but not before he had glimpsed the transformed Lupin. Dumbledore forbade him ever to tell.

Snape maintains that James only stopped the joke because he got cold feet. He owes James a life debt, and he cannot forgive him for it. One day by the lake he called Lily 'that word', and their friendship was over.

Death Eater

After leaving school Snape joined Lord Voldemort's Death Eaters and took the Dark Mark on his left forearm. As a young follower he overheard part of a prophecy about the one who would defeat the Dark Lord. He carried it to his master, who came to believe that it meant the Potters' son.

Later Snape turned to Albus Dumbledore. Dumbledore once said that nothing Severus could ever do would make up for what he had done, then winced as though he had said too much. All the same, he gave Snape the Potions post in 1981, and he has stood by him ever since. Snape has applied for the Defence Against the Dark Arts post every year, without success.

Teaching

Snape teaches in a cold dungeon lined with pickled things in jars. He favours Slytherin openly and docks points from Gryffindor for almost anything; once it was five points for breathing in a sarcastic way. He holds that nearly all the really old spells are dark, and Lupin concedes that he is right about most of them. His protection for the Philosopher's Stone was a logic puzzle of seven bottles between purple and black fire.

When he covered Lupin's Defence class in November 1993, he set the syllabus aside and lectured on the Garou. There is no such creature as the werewolf of the textbook, he told them. The Garou are born, or else a man is bitten. They have five shapes, from the man through the nine-foot war form to an ordinary wolf, and they wear whichever they choose, moon or no moon. The moon is their birth sign, and it sets each one's calling. They carry a rage that sits in them like fire in a lamp. They keep to thirteen tribes; a fourteenth went over whole to the enemy.

The sight of their full shape, he said, clouds the memory of everybody but the mad, the dying and 'those with a certain... grounding'. He invited the class to draw their own conclusions about which of those applied to the man presently teaching them. He set two rolls of parchment on recognising and killing them in each shape, which Lupin cancelled.

Personality and appearance

Snape is thin and sallow. He has greasy black hair to his shoulders, a hooked nose and eyes that make Harry think of deep water in the dark. He is bitter, exact and cruel to Gryffindors. Yet his cruelty has limits. He rebukes his own house over McGonagall, and he offers Dracina silence rather than comfort, which is the kindest thing he has. When Lockhart filled the castle with Valentine's decorations, Snape looked at them as though somebody had just made him drink Skele-Gro.

Snape and Lupin

To Lupin, Snape's Dark Mark reeks of the Wyrm. Every instinct of the Garou tells him to take his war form and tear Snape apart. The Wolfsbane Potion that Snape brews for him only just holds the war form down, and it is the only reason Lupin can bear to be in a room with him. Snape, in other words, brews the potion that keeps Lupin from killing him.

Each knows the other's secret. Each needles the other about it, even in front of Harry, and each keeps it. Once, looking at Snape's left arm, Lupin remarked that he knew when something reeked of Dark Magic. Snape covered his sleeve.

In the saga: 1991 to 1992

At Harry's first lesson Snape sneered at him for being famous, and took points for his ignorance. He praised Dracina's work in front of the class. He did dock her five points when she claimed to have gone after the troll, saying that he expected more cunning from her.

He suspected Quirrell from the start. At Hallowe'en he went to the third floor to head him off, and Fluffy savaged him for it. At Harry's first match he muttered a counter-curse to keep Harry on his jinxed broom. He refereed the Hufflepuff match to stop a second attempt. He confronted Quirrell in the Forest, telling him, 'You don't want me for an enemy, Quirrell.' Quirrell used Snape's sinister looks as cover all year, and Harry believed the worst of Snape until the end.

In the saga: 1992 to 1993

He pressed for the expulsion of Harry and Ron over the flying car. He signed the note that let the Slytherin team train their new Seeker, Dracina. At the Duelling Club he blasted Lockhart off the stage with the Disarming Charm. Watching Dracina duel Harry, his face went grey with a terrible recognition. He muttered, for Harry alone, 'Foolish girl. Foolish, foolish girl. They never look back.'

In the spring he noticed Dracina's decline when nobody else did. When she went missing, he reported only that one of his Slytherins had not been seen since breakfast, and he searched the dungeons for her. That same term he quietly ordered her to speak of Professor McGonagall with respect. It was the first time Harry had ever seen him rebuke a Slytherin. He clapped three times when Lockhart's departure was announced.

In the saga: 1993 to 1994

Passed over for Defence once again, he stared at Lupin with loathing. He sneered at Neville before the boggart lesson, and he expressed his concerns about the appointment to Dumbledore. All the while Lupin's smoking potion, which smells of burnt grass, simmered in a cauldron in his office. When the cauldrons of Harry and Dracina boiled over, he warned them that friendships in that school had ended over a single word said once in temper. He looked, as he said it, like a man who had been shown a picture he had once owned and lost. He took fifty points from Gryffindor for Ron's crocodile heart, and ten more for 'Worth it'.

In March 1994 Dracina came to his office and confessed the truth about the hooded robes. When she described Harry's fall, he gripped his own left forearm. He conjured her a handkerchief, and told her that people who are sure they deserve what is thrown at them only become easier to hit. On her face he saw a look he had seen on another face many years before. She still had a chance, he told her, to do something instead of just saying something. Afterwards he told Harry that she had wept, and that 'I do not share her opinion.'

When he found the Marauder's Map, it insulted him in the names of Messrs Moony, Prongs, Padfoot and Wormtail. He summoned Lupin by Floo, remarking on the map's 'rather hairy manufacturers'. On the night of the escape he found the map in Lupin's office and followed under Harry's Cloak. In the Shrieking Shack he bound Lupin, then held his wand between Black's eyes, telling him he had failed 'her'. Harry, Ron and Hermione disarmed him all at once, slamming him into the wall.

When he came round, he told Fudge that the children had been Confunded, and he was promised an Order of Merlin. Then he covered for Dumbledore with a statement in which every word was true and the whole was a lie. When Fudge withdrew the award, Snape swore at length, partly in Latin. The next morning he let slip to the Slytherins that Lupin was a werewolf, and Lupin resigned. He had guessed a good deal of what happened that night. He told nobody.

In their own words

Ah. Harry Potter. How very... famous.Severus Snape · B1 Ch4
You don't want me for an enemy, Quirrell.Severus Snape · B1 Ch9
Excuse me, but I believe I am the Potions master at this school.Severus Snape · B2 Ch10
Foolish girl. Foolish, foolish girl. They never look back. They never once...Severus Snape · B2 Ch12
