Blonde, fair-skinned women of strength and beauty
1898, by the Kalderash clan, in the Carpathians
pages.html:
Angelus, called the Scourge of Europe, is the most notorious vampire of the modern age. He is a Ventrue of the sixth generation, of the Aurelian line, sired in Galway in 1753. For a hundred and forty-five years his cruelty was unmatched by anyone of his kind. In 1898 a Romani clan cursed him with a new soul, and he vanished from the world's sight as Angel. In 2001, by a direct act of God, he became the father of a living son.

Liam of Galway

He was born Liam, in Galway, in 1727, the son of a linen merchant. He grew up handsome, idle and nearly always in drink, a constant disappointment to his father, who despaired of him.

On the night in 1753 when his father finally turned him out of the house, a pale lady from the colonies beckoned him into an alley. He was never alive again. She was Darla, of the fifth generation, the favourite childe of the vampire called the Master.

The night he came home

His first act as a vampire was to go home. He killed the whole household, servants included. His father he saved for last, so that he would have seen all the rest.

It was his little sister who let him in. She saw her dead brother standing in the moonlight at the window, believed he had come back as an angel and opened the door. From that came his name. He left no one alive to bury them.

As a vampire he had no soul. The curse that descends from Cain destroys the soul of everyone it takes, and what lives in its place is the Beast. In Liam the Beast found a man with a gift for cruelty, patience and imagination. Between them they became something that even other vampires spoke of with care.

The blood of the sixth generation

Darla gave him the blood of the sixth generation, six steps from Cain. It is an elder's blood. It grows stronger with the centuries, mends wounds that would end a younger vampire and puts the mind of every vampire of a later generation within its reach. Drusilla, William the Bloody and the rest of the Aurelian young could never bend his will, though he could bend theirs. Only Darla and the Master were beyond him.

Of the gifts of his clan he made Presence his instrument. He could fill a room with dread or with charm, as he chose. His victims found that they wanted, against all sense, to be near him. He used Dominate sparingly, because he preferred his victims to know what was happening to them.

The soul he was given in 1898 changed none of this. Angel still carries the blood of the sixth generation, with all its strength.

One kind of blood

Like every Ventrue, Angelus can feed from only one kind of mortal, and he would starve sooner than drink from anybody else. His kind is fair-skinned women with blonde hair, women of strength and beauty.

It is a very close description of his sire, Darla. It is just as close a description of Buffy Summers, in her looks and in her character alike.

Through his years as the Scourge of Europe he killed whoever he pleased, but he fed only on women of that kind. After 1898 he would not feed on people at all. He lived on the blood of animals instead. In 1999 Buffy gave him her own blood, freely, to save his life.

The Master's court

In 1760 Darla brought him to London to be presented to the Master. The Master kept his court in a lair beneath the city, among the vampire priests of the Order of Aurelius.

Angelus laughed at a lord of the night who lived in the sewers and called it piety. He walked out, and Darla went with him. The Master never forgave either of them.

The Scourge of Europe

For decades Angelus and Darla roamed Europe together. The accounts of their path stop being lists of victims and become lists of places. He cut a cross into the cheeks of the people he killed. It was his own joke, an angel leaving crosses, and it was in all the broadsheets of the day.

Slaughter alone did not interest him. He preferred to destroy a person slowly, through everyone they loved, and he thought a quick death wasted work.

Like the Master and Darla, he was unaligned. He openly ignored the Masquerade, the law under which the Kindred have hidden from mankind since 1435. Because he endangered every vampire in Europe, the Camarilla often secretly supported or manipulated the hunters who pursued him. Among them were the Society of Leopold and its hunters, such as Daniel Holtz. None of the men hunting Angelus knew whose money they were spending.

In York in 1764 the pair of them killed Holtz's wife and infant son, then turned his daughter. Holtz pursued them across Europe for nine years and never caught them.

Drusilla

About 1860, in London, Angelus found a devout and gentle young witch with a little of the Sight. Her name was Drusilla. He decided that killing her would be a waste.

Instead he killed her family one by one, slowly, in order, and let her find them. At last she fled to a convent. On the day she took her holy orders he came through the chapel. When nothing was left of her mind but pieces, he turned her, so that she would be mad for ever.

In 1880 Drusilla sired William the Bloody in London. For some years after that the four of them travelled together: Darla, Angelus, Drusilla and William. They were the most feared company of vampires in Europe.

His childer

Angelus sired few vampires, and he chose each one with care.

In the eighteenth century he sired Penn, a strict young Puritan. Penn's first act was to kill his own family, as Angelus had done before him. He took up his sire's signature of the cross cut into the cheek, and he kept it for two hundred years.

About 1860 he sired Drusilla. In 1943 he sired a dying American sailor, Sam Lawson, to save a submarine. He never gave Lawson a reason to go on. All three were of the seventh generation.

The curse of 1898

In 1898, in Romania, Angelus killed a girl of the Kalderash, an old and learned Romani clan travelling the Carpathians. She was the clan's favourite daughter. After a century and a half of horrors, she was one girl too many.

The elders did not hunt him or stake him. They sat down around a fire and cursed him, with a binding the Ministry of Magic has never reconstructed.

The curse gave him a soul. It was not his old one, which vampirism had destroyed. It was a new soul. The magic that gave it grew from the same root as the working by which the monks who guarded the Key later made it into a living girl, Dawn Summers. The Beast remained in him.

The clan meant the soul as a punishment, to make him feel every one of his crimes. The curse also carried a condition. Should he ever know one moment of true happiness, the soul would leave him, and Angelus would return.

He was never seen again in the old way. A hundred and forty-five years of horrors, from 1753 to 1898, ended overnight. There was no body. There was no grave.

It is not generally known that he was ensouled. Most of those who know his name know only that he disappeared, not why. Some of the Kindred who have heard the rumours take him for one who has found Golconda, the fabled peace between a vampire and his Beast. He has not. The Beast is still in him, held down by a soul that is not his own, waiting for one moment of happiness to have him back.

Darla, and Beijing

When Darla learned what he had become, she cast him out. She went to the Kalderash camp to demand that the curse be taken back. It was not. Drusilla and William killed everyone they found there.

In 1900 Angel followed her to Beijing, during the Boxer Rising, and asked to come back to her. She tested him with a baby taken from a missionary family. He could not kill it. He fled with it through a window, and Darla knew that Angelus was gone.

The long exile

For most of the twentieth century Angel lived alone, out of sight. He could not forgive himself, and he would not feed on people. He lived on rats and on the blood of animals. The Ventrue curse binds a vampire to one kind of mortal. It does not forbid the blood of beasts, which keeps a vampire alive but gives him little strength.

In 1943 the United States Navy pressed him into service aboard a submarine that had taken German prisoners. Among them were vampires the Germans had captured for experiments, William the Bloody one of them. To bring the boat home, Angel sired a dying sailor, Sam Lawson.

In 1952 he was living at the Hyperion Hotel in Los Angeles when a demon that fed on paranoia set the guests against each other. He let them hang him. Then he walked away.

In 1996 a demon named Whistler found him starving in the streets of New York. Whistler showed him the newly called Slayer, Buffy Summers, in Los Angeles, and from that night Angel had a purpose.

Sunnydale

In 1997 he went to Sunnydale to help her. He fought beside her against the Master's followers, and against his own former companions. He staked Darla, his sire, in the Slayer's own house.

In January 1998, on Buffy's seventeenth birthday, he knew a moment of true happiness with her. The curse broke, and Angelus returned. He killed Jenny Calendar of the Kalderash, who had been sent to watch him. In May 1998 he tried to wake the demon Acathla, to swallow the world into hell.

The witch Willow Rosenberg restored his soul at the last moment. Buffy had no other way to close the vortex, so she ran him through and sent him into it. He came back out of hell that autumn, after what had been centuries by the reckoning of that place.

Los Angeles

In 1999 he moved to Los Angeles and set up as a private detective, helping those who came to him in trouble. In 2000 Wolfram and Hart raised Darla as a mortal woman to torment him. Drusilla sired her again.

Early in 2001, on a night of despair, not of happiness, Angel and Darla lay together. By every law of the blood nothing could come of it. Vampires of blood as strong as theirs cannot have children, and even the thin-blooded, who can, bear only dhampirs. Something did come of it, because God intervened directly. Darla conceived. In November 2001 she gave her life so that their son could be born, a living human boy with a soul of his own. Angel named him Connor.

God's purpose for the boy was not allowed to run. Jasmine had once been among the powers that watched over the world, and now she meant to rule it. She set out to undo what God intended. In February 2002 the hunter Daniel Holtz, kept asleep since 1773 and woken at last to serve her ends, leapt with the baby into the hell dimension Quor-toth. Connor came back that spring, a young man raised to hate his father. In May 2002, believing that Angel had murdered Holtz, he sank him in the sea in a steel box. Angel was freed three months later.

Through Connor, Jasmine brought herself into the world. The boy fathered her on Cordelia Chase, whose body she had taken. She was born in 2003. She held Los Angeles in thrall until Angel broke her hold, and Connor killed her.

Angel then made a bargain with Wolfram and Hart. He took charge of the firm's Los Angeles office. In return his son was given a new life, with new memories, in an ordinary family that knew nothing of vampires.

In 2004 he turned the firm against its masters. He struck down the Circle of the Black Thorn, the secret council of its servants. Then, with William the Bloody and the last of his friends, he stood in an alley against the army sent to punish him.

In the saga

On the first morning of the autumn term of 1992 Hermione Granger, reading Voyages with Vampires, told Harry Potter about a Ventrue called Angelus, of the Aurelian bloodline. He had gone right across Europe in the seventeen hundreds, she said, and done terrible things in Romania, then in London, including at a convent. Later that autumn Gilderoy Lockhart claimed that the Master was Angelus's grandsire, which for once was true. Harry knew that Hermione kept three pictures of Angelus folded inside the cover of Gadding with Ghouls. One was an engraving, two had been cut from a book on vampire history, and in all three he was brooding. She looked at them under the table in Charms.

In the second week of October 1993, as Remus Lupin began his lesson on vampires, Hermione asked whether one of them could ever be good. Her eyes were on the folded picture on her desk. Lupin answered with something like a wince: 'I've never met one I'd turn my back on. Never. Vampirism destroys the soul.' What lives in its place, he told them, is the Beast. He had never met Angel.

Soon afterwards Ron Weasley, whose mother had never let the twins tell him the Angelus stories, asked Hermione for them. She read them from Blood Nobility: The Great Kindred Lineages, which Madam Pince kept behind the desk. It was all there: the Galway alley, the household, the sister at the window, the crosses, the London girl, the convent and the Romani curse, after which he was never seen again. The book says, in a footnote, that no one of his kind in all their history was ever crueller. Hermione does not know that he has a soul. Nobody at Hogwarts knows it.

In December 1993 Hermione still kept the engraving folded in her bag. She had read everything on the Scourge of Europe, down to the footnotes. In early 1994 Harry reflected that she had told them about him with shining eyes, always wanting to know exactly what he had done, in what order, to whom.

pages.title: William the Bloody
infobox: Fighters: only someone who is fighting him when he bites
pages.html:
William the Bloody, better known as Spike, is a vampire of the Aurelian line, a Ventrue of the eighth generation, sired in London in 1880 by Drusilla. He earned the name William the Bloody with his poetry, and the name Spike with his habit of torturing people with railway spikes. His blood is the thinnest of his line. He is also one of the very few vampires ever to have killed a Slayer, which he has done twice. Professor McGonagall once tangled with him in a cellar in Whitechapel.

The poet

William was a young London gentleman of the 1870s. He lived with his mother and wrote sentimental verse, so bad that his acquaintances called him William the Bloody: his poetry, they said, was bloody awful. In 1880 the woman he loved scorned him at a party. He fled into the street. There he met Drusilla, who saw what was in him and sired him. He kept his nickname, and he gave it a new meaning.

His first thought as a vampire was for his mother, who was dying of consumption. He sired her that same night, so that she would never be ill again. She rose of the ninth generation, cruel and mocking, with nothing left in her of the woman who had loved him. He destroyed her himself.

The blood of the eighth generation

Spike stands eight steps from Cain, the furthest removed of the old Aurelians, and his blood is the thinnest of the line. He cannot bend the mind of any of his elders. The gifts of the clan come to him more slowly than they come to older blood. Even so, eighth-generation blood is old and strong by the standards of the present day, when most new vampires are sired of the twelfth generation or the thirteenth.

He has made a fighter's blood of it. Of the Ventrue gifts, the one he trusts is Fortitude. He has been burned, staked at, beaten, and crushed under the falling organ of a burning church. Each time he walked away. He has the clan's Presence when he wants it, and he seldom troubles with Dominate. Angelus liked his cruelty slow and elaborate; Spike would always rather have a fight.

Like every Ventrue, Spike can feed from only one kind of mortal, and he would starve sooner than drink from anybody else. His kind is fighters. He can drink only from someone who is fighting him when he bites, so a victim who cowers is no use to him at all. That suits him very well. It is part of the reason he went looking for Slayers, since nobody alive fights harder than a Slayer.

Spike

He fell in with Drusilla's sire Angelus, and with Darla. For some years the four of them travelled together. It was in those years that William took the name Spike, from his practice of torturing people with railway spikes. He and Angelus were rivals from the start. Spike never let him forget that Angelus had made a career out of frightening the helpless.

Then he went looking for the Slayer, the one girl in each generation who is chosen to fight his kind. In 1900, in Beijing during the Boxer Rising, he killed his first, Xin Rong, and came away with the scar through his eyebrow. In 1977, on a New York subway train, he killed his second, Nikki Wood. He took her long black leather coat, which he has worn ever since.

In 1943 he was one of the vampires the German navy had taken prisoner for experiments. The submarine that held them was captured by the United States Navy, and aboard it he met Angel, whom the Americans had pressed into service to bring the boat home.

Sunnydale

He remained Drusilla's devoted consort for more than a century. In 1997, after a mob in Prague had left her weak, he brought her to Sunnydale in California, where the Slayer of the day, Buffy Summers, was living. There he destroyed the Anointed One, the child vampire who led the Master's followers. Not long afterwards the organ of a burning church fell on him, and it crippled him for months.

In May 1998 Angelus set out to end the world, which would have taken Drusilla with it. Rather than watch that happen, Spike made a bargain with the Slayer. He helped her stop Angelus, and she let him leave town with Drusilla. That autumn, in Brazil, Drusilla left him for a chaos demon.

Later years

In 1999 a secret military project in Sunnydale put a device in his head that stopped him from harming people. With no fights left to him he had nothing to drink but pig's blood from the butcher's, and for years he lived on it. The Ventrue curse binds a vampire to one kind of mortal, but it does not forbid the blood of beasts. Such blood keeps a vampire alive, though it gives him very little strength.

In 2002 he went to Africa, passed a demon's trials and won a soul. It cannot have been his own, since vampirism had destroyed that in 1880; like Angel's, it was a new one. In 2003 he died to save the world when Sunnydale was destroyed. He did not stay dead. Late in 2003 he came back in Los Angeles, first as a ghost and then in the flesh. In 2004 he fought beside Angel.

In the saga

In September 1992 Hermione Granger told Harry Potter about a vampire called William the Bloody, who had been sired in London and was called that because of the poetry. In 1993, warning Harry not to go after whatever lay in the Chamber of Secrets, Professor McGonagall told him something of what she had been through. She had faced Garou and walked through places where Wraiths walk. Once, in a cellar in Whitechapel, she had tangled with William the Bloody himself. She had come out of that one with her life and very little else. In December 1993 Harry noticed that Hermione could be made to talk about William the Bloody until the fire went out.

pages.html:
Dracula, born Mathias Cronqvist, is the most famous vampire in the world. He is a Tzimisce of the fourth generation, and since 1094 he has risen from destruction roughly once a century. The Belmont family has hunted him all that time with the whip called the Vampire Killer, and his own son, the dhampir Alucard, has fought him at their side. In the summer of 1994 he lies between returns, last destroyed in 1944. His final destruction came in the Demon Castle War of 1999.

Mathias Cronqvist

Mathias Cronqvist was a mortal nobleman of the late eleventh century, a knight celebrated as a strategist in the Church's wars, and a close friend of Leon Belmont. In 1093, while he was away on campaign, his wife Elisabetha fell ill and died. Mathias took her death as a betrayal by God. He withdrew from the Church's service on the plea of illness, and resolved to live for ever so that he could curse Heaven for all eternity.

To that end he obtained the Crimson Stone, an alchemical stone that turns the soul of a vampire into power for whoever holds it. In 1094 he set his friend against the vampire Walter Bernhard, lord of a castle in a forest of eternal night, by telling Leon where Walter had taken his betrothed, Sara Trantoul. Leon destroyed Walter with the newly made Vampire Killer. As Walter fell, the demon Death carried his soul to Mathias, who was waiting with the Stone. Through the Stone Mathias took Walter's blood and soul into himself. He rose as a vampire.

Becoming Dracula

What Mathias did to Walter Bernhard was diablerie, the drinking of another vampire's blood and soul, but the Crimson Stone broke the ordinary rules of that act. By those rules a mortal cannot commit diablerie at all, and a vampire who does gains a single step in generation at most. Walter was not of the third generation, yet Mathias rose at the fourth, the same distance from Cain as the childer of the Antediluvians. No one has explained how the Stone did it. Because Mathias had been mortal, he had no clan of his own. He took Walter's, and so became Tzimisce.

He offered Leon a place at his side. Leon refused. The demon Death, which has served Mathias ever since, fought Leon while Mathias withdrew, and Leon swore that his descendants would hunt the night for ever. So began the long war between the vampire and the Belmont family.

In the centuries that followed, the vampire took the name Dracula. In Wallachia he was known as Vlad Tepes, the Impaler, and the Wallachian prince's reported death at the end of 1476 fell in the same year that Trevor Belmont destroyed him. He married again. His second wife, Lisa, was a witch who healed the sick. She bore him a son, Adrian, the dhampir known as Alucard. Wallachian villagers who feared her as a witch later put her to death, and her death hardened Dracula's hatred of mankind.

That son should not have been possible. By the laws of the blood only the thin-blooded, of the fifteenth generation or later, can father a child, and Dracula is of the fourth. His blood came to him through the Crimson Stone, however, and nothing about that blood has ever obeyed the rules.

Among the Kindred he is nominally allied with the Sabbat. Between his deaths, his absences, his resurrections and his own designs, the alliance means very little. He has never answered to the Camarilla and has never kept the Masquerade with any care. He keeps his own court of Devil Forgemasters, servants and monsters. His castle comes back whenever he does.

Returns and defeats

Dracula does not stay destroyed. Every hundred years or so, and sometimes sooner, he rises again, by his own will or through followers who work to bring him back. His castle rises with him in the mountains. In 1450 Sonia Belmont faced him, the first of her family to fight him under the name Dracula, with Alucard's help. In 1476 he loosed armies of the dead on Wallachia. The Church called back the Belmonts, whom the people had driven out for fear of their powers. Trevor Belmont destroyed him, with Sypha Belnades, Grant DaNasty and Alucard beside him. His curse lingered over the land. In 1479 Death and the Devil Forgemaster Isaac tried to raise him through a borrowed body. Hector, who had once been a Forgemaster himself, destroyed what they raised, and the curse was broken.

Christopher Belmont destroyed him in 1576. Dracula survived as mist, however. In 1591 he seized and possessed Christopher's son, Soleiyu. Christopher had to defeat him all over again. In 1691 Simon Belmont fought his way through the castle and destroyed him, but took a curse from him in the battle. In 1698 Simon gathered the scattered remains of Dracula's body and burned them in the ruins of the castle. When Dracula rose from the fire, Simon destroyed him again and was free of the curse. In 1748 Juste Belmont fought a revenant raised from his relics.

In 1792 the dark priest Shaft revived him. Richter Belmont destroyed him and rescued the captives taken to his castle. Shaft revived him again in 1797, having made the missing Richter his puppet. This time Alucard woke from his long sleep, set Richter free and destroyed his father himself. In 1830 his servant Camilla raised him, and Nathan Graves destroyed him. In the nineteenth century the Order of Ecclesia tried to master his power. Shanoa, of that Order, destroyed him while the Belmonts were missing. Cornell fought his forces in 1844. In 1852 Reinhardt Schneider and Carrie Fernandez destroyed him in the body of a boy, Malus, in whom he had been reborn.

In 1897 Quincy Morris, a Texan of distant Belmont blood, destroyed him and died of his wounds. In 1917 Dracula's niece, Elizabeth Bartley, tried to raise him through the slaughter of the Great War. Quincy's son, John Morris, destroyed him with Eric Lecarde. In 1944, in the middle of the Second World War, the vampire painter Brauner seized the castle, and Death worked to restore its master. Jonathan Morris and Charlotte Aulin destroyed Dracula once more.

The Demon Castle War

His last return came in 1999. In the Demon Castle War, Julius Belmont, with Alucard beside him, destroyed Dracula for good, and the castle was sealed inside a solar eclipse. The struggle cost Julius his memory. In 1994 the war is still five years off, though it is already brewing.

Dracula's power did not vanish with him. In 2035, at the first solar eclipse of that century, his reincarnation, a young man named Soma Cruz, was drawn into the sealed castle. Soma refused the inheritance. In 2036 a cult tried to wake the Dark Lord in him, and he refused it a second time.

Powers and weaknesses

Like every vampire, Dracula carries the curse that descends from Cain: immortality, the burning of the sun and the loss of the soul, with the Beast in its place. As a Tzimisce he commands Vicissitude, the shaping of flesh and bone. He has the clan's other Disciplines, Animalism and Auspex, as well. Like all his clan, he must rest in the earth of his homeland. He has been seen to take the shapes of bats, wolves and mist. He can throw hellfire and command the dead. The castle itself is his creature, and its halls change from one return to the next.

Wands do little against him, as Professor McGonagall told Harry Potter in 1992. The weapon that has destroyed him most often is the Vampire Killer, made in 1094 for exactly that work. The Belmonts have carried it, and for a time their Morris kin. Faith also wounds him, since the curse he carries was pronounced by God.

In the saga

On the first morning of the autumn term of 1992, Hermione Granger was reading Gilderoy Lockhart's Voyages with Vampires at the Gryffindor table. Dracula, she told Harry Potter, was real; he was in chapter nine. A family called the Belmonts had been hunting him for about four hundred years with a whip. Every hundred years or so he came back, and one of them had to go up the mountain. Her figure was short. The family has hunted him since 1094, and under the name Dracula for more than five hundred years.

On the night of Halloween 1992, standing over the Petrified Mrs Norris, Lockhart claimed to have foiled a cult of Dracula worshippers in Transylvania, three hundred of them, all in red, who kept a cat like her on their altar, led by a fourth-generation Tzimisce Methuselah. Professor McGonagall asked whether he knew her old friend Julius, who had been in Transylvania for some years and always carried a whip. Then she told Harry quietly that no one kills a vampire of the fourth generation with a wand. Very few Tzimisce of that generation exist, and Dracula is one of them.

In December 1993 Hermione told Harry and Ron Weasley about Dracula's son Alucard, a dhampir who had hunted his own father. She had read the Belmont chronicles too, she said.

pages.title: The Bandon Banshee
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
A witch with a hairy chin
pages.html:
The Bandon Banshee was a banshee of Bandon, in County Cork, who was seen off by a witch with a hairy chin. Gilderoy Lockhart claimed the deed for himself, as he claimed so many others, after he had wiped the witch's memory.

Banshees

A banshee is a wailing spirit in the shape of a woman, with black hair down to the floor and a face like a skull. Her scream is a warning of death, and it makes every hair on a listener's head stand up.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Seven, at his first lesson with Harry Potter's class, Lockhart boasted: 'I didn't get rid of the Bandon Banshee by smiling at her!' He waited for the laugh. A few people smiled, weakly.

In Chapter Eight Hagrid made it plain that he did not believe a word of it. Lockhart had been giving him advice on getting kelpies out of a well, and going on about some banshee he had banished: 'If one word of it was true, I'll eat my kettle.'

In Chapter Eighteen Harry told Professor McGonagall, with heavy sarcasm, that Lockhart had done a werewolf, a vampire and the Bandon Banshee in class. Later that day Lockhart, packing his trunks to run, admitted the truth to Harry and Ron Weasley. The witch who really saw off the Bandon Banshee had a hairy chin.

pages.title: Joseph Campbell
infobox: The Hero with a Thousand Faces (1949); the Hero's Journey
pages.html:
Joseph Campbell was an American Muggle scholar of myth. In The Hero with a Thousand Faces he set out the pattern he found beneath the hero stories of every age, which has come to be called the Hero's Journey. Gilderoy Lockhart is an admirer.

Life

Campbell taught literature at a women's college in New York for nearly forty years. He spent his life reading the myths of the whole world. In them he found the same story told everywhere: the hero is called away from ordinary life into a world of wonders, meets a guide, passes through trials, wins a great victory and comes home changed. He died in Honolulu in 1987.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Five, at Flourish and Blotts in August 1992, Lockhart hauled Harry Potter in front of the photographers and gave him a free copy of his autobiography, Magical Me. He did it, he said, in the hope that it would help Harry's Hero's Journey. 'That's Joseph Campbell, by the way. A Muggle, but a very smart man. A true warrior-scholar such as myself never turns my nose up at knowledge.'

pages.title: Henry the Eighth
infobox: Six wives; the break with Rome; the Dissolution of the Monasteries
pages.html:
Henry the Eighth was King of England from 1509 to 1547. He broke with Rome, made himself Supreme Head of the Church in England and closed every monastery in his kingdom. Two ghosts in particular have reason to remember him: Brother Aldric of Glastonbury, whom his men put to death, and the Fat Friar, whose priory he pulled down.

The King

Henry came to the throne at seventeen, handsome, clever and devout. He married six times. When the Pope would not release him from his first marriage, to Catherine of Aragon, he broke with Rome, and in 1534 he made himself head of the Church in England.

From 1536 to 1541 his commissioners closed every abbey, priory and friary in the land. The Crown took their lands and treasure. The King's men stripped the lead off their roofs to sell. Abbots who resisted were tried for treason. At Glastonbury in 1539 the aged abbot was hanged, drawn and quartered on the Tor, with two of his monks.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Nine, at Nearly Headless Nick's Deathday Party on 31 October 1992, Hermione Granger met Brother Aldric, the Glastonbury monk whom Henry the Eighth's men had hanged, drawn and quartered. He confirmed that he had hidden the abbey's books from the King's commissioners in a cave on the Tor, where they were never found.

In Book Three, Chapter Fifteen, the Fat Friar told Harry Potter where he had spent the centuries before he came home to Hogwarts. 'I spent a few hundred years haunting my own priory, on the Wash, until King Henry pulled it down to sell the lead off the roof.'

pages.title: Little Whinging
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Privet Drive; Magnolia Crescent; Wisteria Walk
St Michael's, at the end of Magnolia Crescent
The Dursleys; Harry Potter, in the holidays
Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Little Whinging is a neat, quiet town in Surrey, where the Dursleys live at Number Four, Privet Drive. It is as flat as an ironing board from the railway station to the dual carriageway. Most of the town thinks about God not at all, except to feel rather superior to anybody who does.

The town

Privet Drive, Wisteria Walk and Magnolia Crescent are among its streets of square houses with square gardens. Round the corner from the end of Privet Drive, Magnolia Crescent runs down to St Michael's, the small Anglican church with a lych-gate and yew trees. Its vicar is Ambrose Greyhame.

Harry Potter grew up in the town, in the Dursleys' cupboard under the stairs, and he must go back to Number Four every summer. In the summer of 1992 Ron Weasley flew his father's Ford Anglia there, with Fred and George, to rescue him.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter One, in the summer of 1992, the Dursleys were preparing for the Masons' dinner. If the deal went through, Uncle Vernon said, they would be looking at villas in Majorca the next day. Harry did not suppose they would like him any better in Majorca than they did in Little Whinging. In Book Three, Chapter One, in the summer of 1993, Harry reflected that the Dursleys thought about God exactly as much as most of the town did, which was not at all.

In Book Four, Chapter One, in the summer of 1994, Harry dreamt of Little Whinging. The town had never been at the bottom of a valley before, but in the dream it lay in a deep green bowl, with dark hills rising on every side. Privet Drive ran down into it in a long, curving line of orange streetlamps, every one of them humming.

pages.title: Smeltings
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Maroon tailcoat, orange knickerbockers, a straw boater, a knobbly stick
Book Two, Book Three, Book Four
pages.html:
Smeltings is the expensive private school for boys that Vernon Dursley went to, and that his son Dudley has attended since 1991. Its boys wear maroon tailcoats, orange knickerbockers and flat straw hats called boaters. Every boy is issued a knobbly Smeltings stick, and the school holds that hitting one another with it behind the masters' backs is good training for later life.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter One, on 31 July 1992, Dudley announced that he knew what day it was. Harry Potter congratulated him on being able to count to seven. 'That remedial work at Smeltings is paying off.'

In Book Three, Chapter One, in the summer of 1993, Harry made his countdown chart on Dudley's Smeltings letter paper. In Book Four, Chapter Three, in the summer of 1994, the Smeltings outfitters no longer made knickerbockers in Dudley's size.

pages.title: Majorca
infobox: A villa, by Vernon Dursley, in 1992
pages.html:
Majorca is the largest of the Balearic Islands, off the eastern coast of Spain, and a favourite holiday island of the British. In the summer of 1992 Vernon Dursley hoped to celebrate his deal with the Masons by looking at villas there.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter One, Uncle Vernon went over his plans for the Masons' dinner. He would steer the conversation round to drills and, with any luck, have the deal signed before the News at Ten. He told Aunt Petunia: 'This time tomorrow we'll be looking at villas in Majorca.' Harry could not get very excited about that. He did not suppose the Dursleys would like him any better in Majorca than they did in Little Whinging. The dinner was ruined.

pages.title: The Burrow
infobox: Weasley family, Ottery St Catchpole, Devon
Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (July 1998)
The Weasley family, and a ghoul in the attic
Held up by magic; a one-handed kitchen clock; a garden full of gnomes
pages.html:
The Burrow is the home of the Weasley family: a crooked house outside the village of Ottery St Catchpole in Devon. Harry Potter first stayed there in August 1992. Molly Weasley has told him ever since that it can be his home for as long as he wants it.

The house

The Burrow looks as though it was once a large stone pigsty, with extra rooms added here and there until it stood four or five storeys high. It is so crooked that it is plainly held up by magic. It has a red roof, half a dozen chimneys and a lopsided sign stuck in the ground near the entrance. Hens wander about the yard. There is a tumbledown garage, and beyond it a small paddock ringed with trees, where the Weasleys can play Quidditch without being seen from the village. Arthur Weasley's shed stands nearby, full of the Muggle objects he likes to take apart and enchant.

The garden is large and wild. It has gnarled trees, unclipped borders and a green pond full of frogs. It is also overrun with gnomes, which the Weasley children are sent out now and then to throw over the hedge. They always come back.

Inside

Inside, the floors are lopsided and washing is piled on every chair. The kitchen has cookery books on the mantelpiece, a mirror above it that passes remarks on people's appearance, a wireless and plates that wash themselves. Its clock has a single hand and no numbers. Round its edge are written such things as 'Time to make tea', 'Time to feed the chickens' and 'You're late'.

A ghoul lives in the attic. Molly quietens it by going up with a poker, and she has threatened to set it on reporters. Ron's room is at the very top of the house, directly beneath the ghoul. It is painted a violent orange and covered in Chudley Cannons posters. In it are a stack of Martin Miggs, the Mad Muggle comics and a tank of frogspawn. The plaque on the door reads Ronald's Room.

In the saga

Fred, George and Ron brought Harry to the Burrow in the flying Ford Anglia in August 1992. He lived there until 1 September. In its kitchen Molly drew the truth about the Dursleys out of him. She held him while he wept, then told him he could stay for as long as he wanted.

Harry expected to spend the summer of 1993 there, until Dumbledore sent him back to Privet Drive instead. Molly wrote her letters about Harry from the Burrow, and in the summer of 1994 she sent him food from its kitchen by owl. The Weasleys planned to fetch Harry there for the Quidditch World Cup. Hermione was due on 20 August 1994.

pages.title: Ottery St Catchpole
infobox: The Burrow, home of the Weasleys
pages.html:
Ottery St Catchpole is a Muggle village in Devon. The Weasleys live a little way outside it, across the fields at the Burrow, and give it as their address.

The village

A few other wizarding families live round about, the Diggorys among them. The villagers have no idea who their neighbours are, since the wizards of the district take care to do their magic out of sight, behind hedges or on the far side of a hill. Mr Weasley, who is mad about everything to do with Muggles, keeps his shed full of their things. He takes them apart, puts spells on them and puts them back together again.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Three, Harry Potter first came there at dawn in the summer of 1992, in the Weasleys' flying car. 'We're a little way outside the village,' said George. 'Ottery St Catchpole...'

In Book Three, Chapter One, in the summer of 1993, the Daily Prophet reported that a Ministry of Magic employee from Ottery St Catchpole had won its annual Grand Prize Galleon Draw. It was Arthur Weasley, who spent the seven hundred Galleons on a month in Egypt for the family. In Chapter Twenty-Two, at the end of that school year, Hermione Granger and Dracina Malfoy sent Mrs Weasley their two thick letters together, by a single school owl. The address, in Hermione's neat handwriting, with Dracina watching to make sure she spelt it properly, read: Mrs M. Weasley, The Burrow, Ottery St Catchpole, Devon.

pages.title: The Weasley paddock
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
On a hill near the Burrow
pages.html:
The Weasley paddock is a small field the family owns on a hill near the Burrow, ringed with trees that hide it from the village below. The Weasleys can practise Quidditch there, so long as nobody flies too high.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Five, in the summer of 1992, Harry, Ron, Fred and George went up the hill to play there. They could not use real Quidditch balls, which would have taken some explaining if one had got away over the village, so they threw apples for each other to catch. Harry had not been near his broom since June. In Chapter Six, all summer long, Ron was forever at his elbow with a second helping, a spare jumper or a suggestion that they go up to the paddock.

pages.title: Knockturn Alley
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Shrunken heads, giant spiders, poisonous candles, Hands of Glory
pages.html:
Knockturn Alley is a dingy little street off Diagon Alley, given over to shops that deal in the Dark Arts. Its best-known shop is Borgin and Burkes. Respectable wizarding parents do not let their children go there, and the Weasley children have never been allowed in.

The shops

One window is full of shrunken heads. Two doors down a cage holds huge black spiders, while another shop sells poisonous candles. Hands of Glory can be had here too, for anybody with the stomach for them; the cheap sort has a candle stuck in the palm. Wizards think them a curiosity. They give light only to the person holding them, which makes them handy for burglars, and that is all.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Five, in August 1992, Harry Potter came out of the wrong grate on his first journey by Floo powder and found himself in Knockturn Alley. Hagrid rescued him. In Chapter Sixteen Harry remembered that Hagrid had been there to buy Flesh-Eating Slug Repellent.

In Book Three, Chapter Four, in August 1993, Lucius Malfoy steered Harry away from the bend into Knockturn Alley.

In the Book Three Interlude, John Constantine reflected that the wizarding world knew all about Hands of Glory: you could buy one in Knockturn Alley, if you had the stomach for it.

pages.title: Borgin and Burkes
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
pages.html:
Borgin and Burkes is the largest shop in Knockturn Alley, the dingy street off Diagon Alley that is given over to the Dark Arts. It deals in Dark objects. In 1992 Lucius Malfoy sold it some of the most dangerous things in his house, one step ahead of the Ministry's raids.

The shop

It is a dim place with a grimy window. In the summer of 1992 a glass case held a withered hand on a cushion, a bloodstained pack of cards and a glass eye that stared. Masks leered down from the walls. Human bones lay across the counter, with rusty, spiked things hanging from the ceiling on chains. A big black cabinet, a hundred years deep in dust, stood against one wall.

A necklace of opals lay on black velvet in another case. The card beside it read: Caution: Do Not Touch. Cursed. Has Claimed the Lives of Nineteen Muggle Owners to Date.

Mr Borgin, the proprietor, has a voice as oily as his hair. He bows very low to his richer customers. The oil drops off him the moment the door shuts behind them.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Five, in August 1992, Harry Potter came out of the wrong fireplace while travelling by Floo powder and found himself in the shop. When Dracina Malfoy came in with her father, Harry hid in the black cabinet. Through the crack in its doors he caught Lucius muttering something about Cissy and fanciful ideas about the cursed Potter boy. Then Lucius handed Mr Borgin a list of things he wanted moved before the Ministry called. Dracina pointed at the withered hand and asked what the disgusting thing was. Borgin told her it was a Hand of Glory, the best friend of thieves and plunderers. Her father said he hoped she would amount to more than a thief or a plunderer. She was delighted with the opal necklace until she read its card. Then she walked straight up to the cabinet and put out her hand for the handle. Her father called her away just in time. Borgin was to collect the goods from the manor the next day. The moment the door had shut behind them, he muttered that, if the stories were true, Mr Malfoy had not sold him half of what was hidden in that manor.

In Chapter Fifteen Harry remembered that he had heard Lucius muttering in Borgin and Burkes about the cursed Potter boy.

pages.title: Flourish and Blotts
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Lockhart's signing of August 1992; the cage of Monster Books, 1993
pages.html:
Flourish and Blotts is the bookshop in Diagon Alley where Hogwarts students buy their set books. Its shelves reach the ceiling, packed with books as big as paving stones and books as small as postage stamps. It was there, in August 1992, that Tom Riddle's diary passed into Dracina Malfoy's bag.

The shop

Besides the set books it sells books of every other kind, a good many of them with wounded maidens on their covers. When a new set book turns out to bite, the staff have to cope with it as best they can.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Five, in August 1992, Harry Potter came to Flourish and Blotts with the Weasleys and the Grangers to buy his books. Gilderoy Lockhart was signing copies of Magical Me there that day. He hauled Harry to the front for the photographer, announced to the crowd that he would be teaching at Hogwarts and presented Harry with his entire works. Then Lucius Malfoy sneered at Ginny Weasley's second-hand books. Arthur Weasley threw himself at him, and the two fathers came to blows on the floor among the collapsing shelves. While they fought, Dracina mocked Ginny's spilt books as low-class, second-hand rubbish, until Ginny threw books at her head. When Hagrid pulled the fathers apart, Arthur had a cut lip. Lucius had been caught in the eye by an Encyclopaedia of Toadstools.

In Chapter Eighteen the truth came out. Lucius had slipped the diary inside Ginny's battered old Transfiguration book. He had told Dracina to pick up the Weasley girl's book, and Ginny had screamed at her. In a temper Dracina swept up every book in sight, the diary among them. 'One pure-blood girl is very much like another, from where I was sitting,' said Riddle. In Chapter Nineteen Harry told Lucius to his face that he had slipped the diary into Ginny's book.

In Book Three, Chapter Four, in August 1993, the shop's window held an iron cage of about a hundred copies of The Monster Book of Monsters, fighting one another. The manager had been bitten five times that morning and swore he would never stock them again. Inside, Harry saw Death Omens: What to Do When You Know the Worst Is Coming, with a black dog as large as a bear on its cover. In Chapter Nine Dracina, her arm in a sling, turned herself into every wounded maiden on every book cover in Flourish and Blotts as she passed Harry on the path. In Chapter Sixteen Harry remembered Lucius in the shop the summer before last, sneering at Ginny's books.

pages.title: Quality Quidditch Supplies
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
pages.html:
Quality Quidditch Supplies is the Quidditch shop in Diagon Alley, and Harry Potter's favourite shop in the world. It sells broomsticks, team robes, balls and everything else a player could want.

The Firebolt

In August 1993, a week after Harry came to stay at the Leaky Cauldron, the shop put the new Firebolt on show on a newly erected podium. It was a state-of-the-art racing broom with a handle of ash, able to accelerate to 150 miles an hour in ten seconds, and its price was given only on request. The proprietor told the crowd that the Irish International Side had just put in an order for seven. Harry never asked how much it cost. He went back almost every day all the same, just to look at it. Seamus Finnigan and Dean Thomas came in to ogle it too.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Five, in the summer of 1992, Ron Weasley stood for a long time in front of a full set of Chudley Cannons robes in the window. In Book Three, Chapter Four, in August 1993, the shop was showing the Firebolt.

In Chapter Twelve, after a Firebolt had come for Harry with no card, Oliver Wood argued that it could not possibly have been sent by Sirius Black. Black was on the run, said Wood. He could hardly have walked into Quality Quidditch Supplies to buy one.

pages.title: Gambol and Japes
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
pages.html:
Gambol and Japes is a wizarding joke shop in Diagon Alley. It is a favourite with Fred and George Weasley.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Five, in August 1992, Harry Potter, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger found the twins in Gambol and Japes with their friend Lee Jordan. They were stocking up on Dr Filibuster's Fabulous Wet-Start, No-Heat Fireworks.

Filibuster fireworks turned up all through the year that followed. In Chapter Six the twins set some off in the Burrow's kitchen on the last evening of the holidays, filling it with red and blue stars. In Chapter Nine they fed one to a Salamander in the Gryffindor common room to see what would happen. In Chapter Twelve Harry lobbed one of Fred's fireworks into Goyle's cauldron in Potions as a diversion. In Chapter Nineteen the very last of them went off on the Hogwarts Express on the way home.

pages.title: The Diagon Alley junk shop
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Broken wands; wonky brass scales; potion-stained cloaks
pages.html:
The Diagon Alley junk shop is a tiny shop full of other people's cast-offs: broken wands, wonky brass scales and potion-stained cloaks. Nobody goes in for anything new.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Five, in the summer of 1992, while the Weasleys were doing their school shopping in Diagon Alley, Percy Weasley was found in the junk shop. He was deep in a small and very dull book called Prefects Who Gained Power.

pages.title: The second-hand robe shop
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
pages.html:
The second-hand robe shop in Diagon Alley sells wizarding robes that somebody else has worn first, for a good deal less than new ones cost. It does steady trade with families who have more children than Galleons.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Five, in August 1992, the Weasleys split up on the steps after their visit to Gringotts. Mrs Weasley took Ginny to the second-hand robe shop, to fit her out for her first year at Hogwarts. Ginny was the youngest of seven, and the Weasleys' vault had turned out to hold only a very small pile of Sickles, with one gold Galleon.

pages.title: The marble staircase
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Hogwarts, rising from the Entrance Hall
The first floor and the floors above
pages.html:
The marble staircase is the splendid staircase that sweeps up from the Entrance Hall at Hogwarts to the floors above. Anybody going upstairs from the Great Hall goes by it.

In the saga

In Book One, Chapter Three, after the start-of-term feast in 1991, Percy Weasley led the new Gryffindor first-years out of the Great Hall and up the marble staircase on the long climb to their tower. Harry was too full of treacle tart by then to be surprised by anything.

In Book Two, Chapter Nine, on Hallowe'en 1992, Harry glanced back from the top of the dungeon stairs and saw a flicker of silver-blonde hair on the marble staircase. Dracina Malfoy was going up it alone, away from the feast, at a quick light run, with one hand pressed flat to the front of her robes as though she were holding something against her. Then the stairs turned and she was gone.

Soon afterwards Harry tore up the same staircase himself, following a voice nobody else could hear, with Ron and Hermione clattering after him.

pages.title: The Hogwarts lake
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Below Hogwarts, at the foot of its cliff
pages.html:
The Hogwarts lake is the great lake below the castle, which stands on a cliff above it. It is better known as the Black Lake.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Six, on the night of 1 September 1992, Ron Weasley flew his father's Ford Anglia out over the lake towards the castle, with Harry Potter beside him. The water lay a mile below them, smooth and black as glass. Over the lake the engine gave a loud clunk, spluttered and died. The nose dropped. The car fell towards the castle wall, swung away from it by inches, and came down into the Whomping Willow. In Chapter Nine, that October, the rain came down for days and the lake rose.

pages.title: The London Underground
pages.html:
The London Underground, which Londoners call the Tube, is the Muggle railway that runs through tunnels beneath London. Its first line opened in 1863, and it is the oldest underground railway in the world. Hagrid took Harry Potter on it to Diagon Alley in the summer of 1991.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Five, in the summer of 1992, Harry told Mr Weasley that he had gone on the Underground with Hagrid, who had barely fitted through the barriers. Mr Weasley lit up at once. He wanted to know whether there had been 'escapators', and exactly how they worked. A few minutes later Fred vanished into green fire by Floo powder, making it look, Harry thought, as easy as feeding a ticket into the barrier on the Tube.

pages.title: Snape's office
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
The dungeons of Hogwarts, along a cold passage
pages.html:
Snape's office lies along a cold passage in the dungeons of Hogwarts. It belongs to Severus Snape, the Potions master, and it is about as welcoming as he is. Its walls are lined with shelves of jars, each with something slimy floating in it, glistening in the firelight.

The office

In March 1994 a small cauldron was simmering over a low blue flame in one corner, sending up a thin thread of grey smoke that smelt faintly bitter, like burnt grass. The fireplace is connected to the Floo Network, so Snape can summon other members of staff through it, and he keeps a jar of Floo powder on the mantelpiece.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Six, on the night of 1 September 1992, Snape took Harry Potter and Ron Weasley there after they flew the Weasleys' car into the Whomping Willow. The fireplace was black and empty. Snape unrolled that evening's Prophet and read them the reports of the Muggles who had seen them, Mr Angus Fleet of Peebles among them.

In Book Three, Chapter Fourteen, in March 1994, Dracina Malfoy came to the office with mud caked across her expensive cloak. 'Potter is in Hogsmeade,' she told Snape. He fetched Harry down to the dungeons. Harry had been inside only once before, in his second year, and Snape seemed to have collected a good many more slimy things in jars since then. There were little smears of dried mud on the flagstones in front of the desk.

When the Marauder's Map insulted him, Snape flung a handful of Floo powder into the fire. 'Lupin!' he called into the flames. 'I want a word!' A few seconds later Professor Lupin climbed out of the grate, beating ash from his shabby robes.

pages.title: Greenhouse Three
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
The Hogwarts greenhouses, behind the castle
Mandrakes; a Venomous Tentacula; hanging flowers the size of umbrellas
pages.html:
Greenhouse Three is the Hogwarts greenhouse where Professor Sprout keeps the more interesting and more dangerous plants. Students first work in it in their second year.

The greenhouse

Inside it smells of damp earth and fertiliser, with the heavy scent of the enormous flowers, each the size of an umbrella, that hang from the roof. Its plants include the Mandrakes, whose cry is fatal when they are fully grown. There is also a Venomous Tentacula, which was teething in September 1992.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Seven, on 2 September 1992, Harry Potter's year had their first lesson there, repotting Mandrakes. Until then they had only ever worked in Greenhouse One. Professor Sprout warned them to be careful of the Venomous Tentacula, because it was teething. Justin Finch-Fletchley introduced himself to Harry over the dragon-dung compost. In Chapter Sixteen, in March 1993, several of the Mandrakes threw a loud, wild party in the greenhouse that kept half of Hufflepuff awake and made Professor Sprout very happy indeed.

In Book Three, Chapter Fourteen, in March 1994, a Puffapod went off in Ron Weasley's face during Herbology. Dracina Malfoy was waiting for Harry outside Greenhouse Three when the lesson ended, standing quite alone on the gravel path.

pages.title: Lockhart's office
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Framed photographs of Lockhart, several of them signed
pages.html:
Lockhart's office was where Gilderoy Lockhart worked while he taught Defence Against the Dark Arts at Hogwarts, in the school year of 1992 to 1993. It was on the second floor, lit by a great many candles. Its walls were covered with countless framed photographs of Lockhart himself, several of which he had signed.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Eight, on a Saturday evening in the autumn of 1992, Harry Potter dragged his feet along the second-floor corridor to serve a detention in Lockhart's office. It was there that he first heard the cold, murderous voice that nobody else could hear.

In Book Two, Chapter Ten, at Hallowe'en 1992, Mrs Norris was found Petrified. Lockhart offered his office, which was the nearest, just upstairs from the corridor. Dumbledore laid the cat on the desk there. The photographs of Lockhart all round the walls ducked out of sight, some of them in hair curlers.

pages.title: Filch's office
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Punishment records; polished chains and manacles; confiscated goods
pages.html:
Filch's office is the room at Hogwarts from which Argus Filch, the caretaker, carries on his long war with the students. Most of them go to a good deal of trouble never to see the inside of it.

The office

It is a dingy room with no window. A single oil lamp hangs from the low ceiling over the desk, and a smell of fried fish has soaked into the walls. Wooden filing cabinets line the room, holding the particulars of every pupil Filch has ever punished. Fred and George Weasley have a drawer to themselves.

On the wall behind the desk hangs a collection of chains and manacles, very lovingly polished. Everybody knows that Filch is forever begging Dumbledore to let him hang students up by their ankles. One drawer of a filing cabinet is labelled Confiscated and Highly Dangerous.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Nine, in October 1992, Filch caught Harry Potter dripping mud from Quidditch practice and marched him down to the office. Harry had never been inside before. Filch was halfway through writing out his crime when something crashed on the ceiling overhead, and he ran off to catch Peeves. Left alone, Harry found a purple envelope from Kwikspell, a correspondence course in beginners' magic, lying on the desk. When Filch came back, he saw that it had moved. He went the colour of brick, flung it into a drawer and sent Harry away without a punishment. The crash had been Nearly Headless Nick's doing: he had persuaded Peeves to drop a cabinet over the office.

In Book Three, Chapter Ten, Fred and George told Harry how they had been dragged into the office in their first year for letting off a Dungbomb in a corridor. While Filch was going on at them, they noticed the drawer marked Confiscated and Highly Dangerous. George dropped another Dungbomb as a diversion. Fred had the drawer open in a second, and out came the Marauder's Map, which they were now handing on to Harry.

pages.title: The girls' toilet on the first floor
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Hogwarts, off the corridor of the Hallowe'en attack
The entrance to the Chamber of Secrets
pages.html:
The girls' toilet on the first floor, as Hermione Granger called it, is the out-of-order girls' toilet at Hogwarts that Moaning Myrtle haunts. Myrtle keeps having tantrums and flooding it, so nobody goes in if they can help it, which made it the perfect place to brew Polyjuice Potion. Under one of its sinks lies the entrance to the Chamber of Secrets.

The toilet

It opens off the corridor on the second floor where Mrs Norris was found Petrified on Hallowe'en 1992. It is the most dismal, depressing bathroom Harry Potter has ever set foot in. Under a big, cracked, speckled mirror stands a row of chipped stone basins. The floor is always damp. The wooden doors of the cubicles are scratched and flaking. One hangs off its hinges. Myrtle sits in the end cubicle, on top of the cistern or down in the U-bend.

One of the copper taps has a tiny snake scratched on its side. When the tap is spoken to in Parseltongue, the whole basin sinks out of sight, leaving a pipe wide enough for a man to slide into. It leads down to the Chamber of Secrets. Myrtle died in the end cubicle in 1943, the last time the Chamber was opened. She had been hiding there, crying, because Olive Hornby had teased her about her glasses. When she unlocked the door to tell a boy talking in a strange language to go and use his own toilet, she saw a pair of great yellow eyes by the sink in front of her cubicle.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Nine, at Nearly Headless Nick's Deathday Party on Hallowe'en 1992, Hermione steered Harry Potter and Ron Weasley away from Myrtle. 'She haunts the girls' toilet on the first floor,' she said. It had been out of order all year, she explained, because Myrtle kept having tantrums and flooding it. She herself never went in there if she could help it.

In Chapter Ten the three of them went in, ignoring the large OUT OF ORDER sign, to ask Myrtle whether she had seen anything on Hallowe'en night. Later that term they brewed their Polyjuice Potion in one of its cubicles, since nobody else ever came in. In Chapter Fifteen, in the new year, Myrtle told Harry about a posh girl with long, straight, shiny hair who had come crashing in one night to search the place on her hands and knees. The girl had whispered at the sinks, thrown her bag at Myrtle, then run away crying. In Chapter Eighteen Myrtle told Harry how she had died. Harry found the little snake scratched on the tap and opened the Chamber of Secrets.

pages.title: The second-floor corridor
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
The Heir of Slytherin's message, Hallowe'en 1992
pages.html:
The second-floor corridor at Hogwarts is a long, dim passage of tall windows, near Moaning Myrtle's bathroom. On Hallowe'en 1992 the Heir of Slytherin announced there that the Chamber of Secrets had been opened.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Nine, Harry followed a voice nobody else could hear up from the Entrance Hall to a corridor awash with water, with Ron and Hermione behind him. Between two of the tall windows, in letters a foot high, something had been daubed across the stone in red: THE CHAMBER OF SECRETS HAS BEEN OPENED. ENEMIES OF THE HEIR, BEWARE. Beneath it Mrs Norris hung by her tail from a torch bracket, as stiff as a board.

In Chapter Eighteen, on 29 May 1993, Professor McGonagall told the staff that the Heir had left a second message, directly under the first: Her skeleton will lie in the Chamber for ever. The student taken was Ginny Weasley.

pages.title: The Deathday Party dungeon
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Nearly Headless Nick's five hundredth deathday, Hallowe'en 1992
pages.html:
The Deathday Party dungeon is the roomy dungeon at Hogwarts where Nearly Headless Nick held the party for his five hundredth deathday on Hallowe'en 1992. For that one night it was given over entirely to ghosts.

The dungeon

It is reached by a passage that was lit, for the party, with long, thin black candles burning a cold, bright blue, and its doorway was hung with black velvet. Inside, a chandelier blazed midnight blue over hundreds of pearly-white ghosts, most of them waltzing. An orchestra of thirty musical saws played on a platform draped in black. Walking into it was like walking into a cold store.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Nine, Harry Potter, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger went to the party at Nick's invitation instead of to the Hallowe'en feast. Peeves called Moaning Myrtle over to them, and she fled the dungeon in tears. Later that night the three of them were found beside Filch's Petrified cat. They had to explain to the teachers why they had missed the feast.

pages.title: Dungeon five
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Frog brains on the ceiling, October 1992
pages.html:
Dungeon five is one of the dungeon rooms beneath Hogwarts Castle. In October 1992 some third-years splattered frog brains all over its ceiling. Argus Filch, the caretaker, spent a whole morning cleaning them off.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Nine, Nearly Headless Nick warned Harry Potter to make a brave retreat, because Filch was in a foul temper. He had a cold, and he had been cleaning dungeon five all morning. Harry, dripping mud from Quidditch practice, did not get away in time. Filch marched him off to his office, muttering about dung, frog brains and rat innards.

pages.title: Chamber of Secrets
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
Deep beneath Hogwarts, under the lake
A sink in the second-floor girls' bathroom
pages.html:
The Chamber of Secrets is the hidden hall Salazar Slytherin built deep beneath Hogwarts before he left the school. He sealed it so that only his heir could open it, and loose the Basilisk inside. For centuries it was dismissed as a legend. Tom Riddle opened it in 1943, when a Muggle-born girl died. It was opened again in 1992 to 1993, through Riddle's diary and the possessed Dracina Malfoy, until Harry Potter killed the Basilisk down there with the sword from the Sorting Hat.

Legend

According to the legend, Salazar Slytherin built a chamber inside the castle without the knowledge of the other three founders. Before he left he sealed it, so that nobody could open it until his own true heir came to the school. The heir alone would be able to break the seal. He would release the horror waiting inside, and with it purge the school of everyone unworthy to study magic.

Many times over the centuries the most learned witches and wizards have searched the castle for it. So has a long line of headmasters and headmistresses. In 1992 Professor Binns told his class that the whole thing was perfect nonsense, a story to frighten the credulous. There was not one scrap of evidence, he said, that Slytherin had ever built so much as a secret broom cupboard.

In truth Slytherin had kept the Basilisk to defend Hogwarts from Muggles. It was his use of it for that, not any wish to purge the school, that parted him from Godric Gryffindor.

The way in

The entrance is a sink in the out-of-order girls' bathroom on the second floor, which is haunted by Moaning Myrtle. It is marked by a tiny snake scratched on the side of one copper tap. When it is spoken to in Parseltongue, the sink sinks out of sight. Beneath it is a pipe wide enough for a man to slide down.

The pipe drops far below the dungeons into a slimy stone tunnel, which seems to run under the lake. Its floor is littered with the small bones of animals. The tunnel ends at a solid wall carved with two entwined serpents, with emeralds for eyes. It parts when commanded in Parseltongue.

The Chamber

Beyond the wall lies a long, dimly lit hall. Towering stone pillars, carved with more entwining serpents, rise into the darkness through a greenish gloom. At the far end stands a colossal statue of Salazar Slytherin, ancient and monkeyish, with a long, thin stone beard that reaches almost to the hem of his robes. The Basilisk lived inside the statue, and came out through its mouth.

The opening of 1943

Tom Riddle, Slytherin's last living descendant, found the Chamber in his fifth year and opened it. In June 1943 a Muggle-born Ravenclaw girl called Myrtle was killed in the bathroom above it, after which the school was to be closed. Riddle framed the third-year Rubeus Hagrid for the attacks, along with his pet Acromantula, Aragog, and Hagrid was expelled. Riddle kept the memory of that year in a diary. He meant it to lead somebody else, one day, to finish Slytherin's work.

The opening of 1992 to 1993

In the summer of 1992 a pile of books was spilt across the floor of Flourish and Blotts. Dracina Malfoy kept a small black book from among them, and began to write in it. It was Riddle's diary. It had been set loose as part of a plot of Lucius Malfoy's, who later admitted that he had been 'instructed'. The memory inside the diary fed on her confidences, and little by little it took control of her.

On Hallowe'en 1992 a message appeared on a wall of the second floor, daubed a foot high in glimmering red: 'The Chamber of Secrets has been opened. Enemies of the heir, beware'. Beneath it hung Filch's cat, Mrs Norris, Petrified. Colin Creevey was Petrified in November. In December it was Justin Finch-Fletchley, together with Nearly Headless Nick. In the spring it was Hermione Granger, with the Ravenclaw prefect Penelope Clearwater. The two girls were saved from death by a mirror, Justin because he saw the creature through Nick, Colin because he saw it through his camera.

Dracina lost hours at a time. She woke in corridors with red on her hands, and she fell ill when the diary was taken from her. The rest of the school, having heard Harry speak Parseltongue at the Duelling Club, decided that he was the heir.

In the summer term of 1993, with Dumbledore suspended and Hagrid in Azkaban, Dracina was drawn down into the Chamber wearing Harry's stolen Quidditch scarf. Ginny Weasley had followed her, and was taken too. From a page clutched in Hermione's fist Harry worked out that the monster was a Basilisk, moving about the castle through the pipes. He opened the entrance with Parseltongue. Ron and Gilderoy Lockhart went down with him. Lockhart's Memory Charm backfired through Ron's broken wand and brought the roof of the tunnel down. Harry went on alone.

Harry in the Chamber

Harry found Dracina collapsing, Ginny bleeding and the memory of Tom Riddle taking solid shape beside the open diary. Riddle explained how he had possessed Dracina, and how Lucius Malfoy's plot had worked. He spoke of a union between the Potter bloodline and the Malfoy one. He spoke, too, of Lily Potter's ancient lineage. Then he revealed that he was Lord Voldemort. Harry refused his offer of revenge on the Dursleys, and called him a fraud.

Riddle set the Basilisk on him. One of its fangs caught Harry's arm, but a warm presence and a fatherly voice held him up. Fawkes brought him the Sorting Hat, and out of it Harry drew a sword. It was Andúril, though it was not until the following winter that Harry worked that out. When the Basilisk's stare struck him, it met a golden heat like an opened furnace, and went no further. Its thrashing brought down several of the pillars. Harry stood astride Dracina on the cold stone, with a strength that was not his own pouring into his arms. He cut off the Basilisk's head with a single stroke. Then he drove the sword through the diary, and Riddle was destroyed.

As the venom came back into him Harry collapsed in Dracina's arms. A man in a white robe was standing by a fallen pillar, watching him with pride. Harry and Dracina both saw him. Harry, looking up from the floor, saw the kind, grave face of Christ from the window of St Michael's Church in Little Whinging. The Fat Friar told him afterwards that Christ had been there all along.

Harry woke unharmed, with his head in Dracina's lap. She healed Ginny's cut, then Fawkes carried them all back up the pipe. The doors of the Chamber were shut again, with the Basilisk's carcass still inside.

pages.title: Surrey
infobox: The Dursleys, of number four, Privet Drive
pages.html:
Surrey is the English county south-west of London where the Dursleys live, at number four, Privet Drive, in the town of Little Whinging. Harry Potter grew up there, in the cupboard under their stairs.

The county

It is a county of tidy commuter towns, where nothing in the least unusual is supposed to happen. Mrs Arabella Figg lives in Little Whinging too, a couple of streets from the Dursleys, and Ambrose Greyhame is the vicar of St Michael's Church there.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Four, at the Burrow in the summer of 1992, Molly Weasley held Harry in a long hug. Over the top of his head she turned a look towards the window, the south and Surrey that would have frightened Uncle Vernon very badly indeed. In Chapter Six she turned the same look on the window, in the general direction of Surrey, more than once that summer, after Harry had gone out to the paddock.

pages.title: London
infobox: Diagon Alley; Knockturn Alley; platform nine and three-quarters at King's Cross
The Master's court; Drusilla (about 1860); William the Bloody (1880)
pages.html:
London is the capital of Britain, Muggle and wizarding alike. Diagon Alley is there, together with the Ministry of Magic, and the Hogwarts Express leaves from King's Cross.

History

In the tenth century the last Hellenic sorcerers worked out of London, fighting a wizarding war against the Norse völvas of Jorvik until the Saxons took that city in 954.

The city has a long, dark history among vampires. In 1760 Darla brought Angelus there to be presented to the Master, who kept his court in a lair beneath the streets. About 1860 Angelus found the devout young witch Drusilla in London. He killed her family one by one and drove her into a convent. On the day she took her holy orders he came through its chapel and sired her. In 1880 she sired William the Bloody there.

Long afterwards Professor McGonagall tangled with William the Bloody himself in a cellar in Whitechapel, in the East End. She came out of it with her life and very little else.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Six, on 1 September 1992, two Muggles in London became convinced that they had seen an old car flying over the Post Office tower. They were right: Ron Weasley and Harry Potter were in it.

In Book Two, Chapter Seven, in September 1992, Hermione Granger told Harry of the atrocities Angelus had committed in London. She told him too that William the Bloody had been sired there.

pages.title: The Post Office tower
infobox: The Post Office's microwave telephone links
pages.html:
The Post Office tower is the tall, round tower in central London that was built to carry the Post Office's telephone and television links by microwave. It opened in 1965, and was the tallest building in London until 1980.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Six, on 1 September 1992, Professor Snape took Harry and Ron down to his office. There he unrolled that evening's Prophet and read it aloud. Two Muggles in London were convinced they had seen an old car flying over the Post Office tower. It was Mr Weasley's Ford Anglia, in which Harry and Ron had flown north after the barrier at King's Cross refused to let them through. Six or seven Muggles had seen it in all, among them Mrs Hetty Bayliss of Norfolk, who had been hanging out her washing at the time.

pages.title: Norfolk
pages.html:
Norfolk is a flat county of wide skies on the east coast of England. At noon on 1 September 1992 Mrs Hetty Bayliss saw a flying car there while she was hanging out her washing.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Six, Severus Snape held up that evening's Prophet under the headline FLYING FORD ANGLIA MYSTIFIES MUGGLES. He read it aloud to Harry Potter and Ron Weasley. Six or seven Muggles had seen the car. Among them were Mrs Bayliss in Norfolk, two people in London who had seen it over the Post Office tower and Mr Angus Fleet of Peebles, who had reported it to the police.

pages.title: Peebles
infobox: Mr Angus Fleet, who saw a flying car
pages.html:
Peebles is a small Scottish town in the Borders, on the River Tweed, south of Edinburgh. On 1 September 1992 one of its Muggles, Mr Angus Fleet, reported to the police that he had seen a flying car.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Six, the car was Arthur Weasley's Ford Anglia, which Ron Weasley and Harry Potter flew north to Hogwarts after the barrier at King's Cross sealed itself against them. Six or seven Muggles in all saw it on the way. That evening Severus Snape unrolled the Prophet in his office, under the headline FLYING FORD ANGLIA MYSTIFIES MUGGLES, and read the reports aloud to the two boys. Mr Angus Fleet, of Peebles, was among them.

pages.title: Kent
pages.html:
Kent is the county in the south-east corner of England, often called the Garden of England. It is the home county of the Wailing Widow, a ghost who drowned herself in a well in 1392, believing that her husband would never come back from the Crusades. He came home a week later.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Nine, at Nearly Headless Nick's five hundredth deathday party at Hallowe'en 1992, Hermione Granger told Harry Potter the Widow's story. Nick himself was proud to tell Harry that she had come all the way up from Kent.

pages.title: Glastonbury
pages.html:
Glastonbury is a small town in Somerset, below the Tor, a steep green hill with a lonely church tower on its top. Its abbey was once one of the richest in England. When the King's commissioners came for it, a monk named Brother Aldric hid the abbey's books in a cave on the Tor, where they never found them.

The abbey

The monks of Glastonbury claimed in 1191 to have found the grave of King Arthur in their grounds. They also claimed that Glastonbury was Avalon. It was not; Avalon was the Grey Havens of the Elves, a long way from Somerset. In 1539 Henry the Eighth's men closed the abbey and took its riches. Brother Aldric was hanged, drawn and quartered. His ghost comes in four pieces, which do not always agree on where to go, and he holds his left arm on with his right.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Nine, in the Gryffindor common room, Hermione Granger told Harry Potter and Ron Weasley about the ghosts who would be at Nearly Headless Nick's deathday party. Among them was a monk from Glastonbury who had been hanged, drawn and quartered by Henry the Eighth's men.

At the party itself, on 31 October 1992, she found Brother Aldric among the guests, a tall, mournful monk who was not quite assembled. She asked him whether it was true about the books. Nobody had asked him about anything but his quartering for about four hundred and fifty years. 'Young lady,' he said, in a voice like a cellar door, 'it is entirely true. Would you care to know where?' He told her, and she wrote it all down.

pages.title: Wolverhampton
pages.html:
Wolverhampton is a large industrial town in the West Midlands of England, on the edge of the Black Country. It was made a city in 2000.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Nine, in the autumn of 1992, Harry was left waiting in Filch's office and picked up a glossy purple envelope from the desk. It held a leaflet for Kwikspell, a correspondence course in beginners' magic, with a testimonial from Mrs P. Hoskins of Wolverhampton: 'For years I couldn't so much as warm a teapot without setting light to the cosy. Since Kwikspell, my Scouring Charms are the talk of the street!'

pages.title: Kendal
infobox: Mr L. Ashby, a Kwikspell customer
pages.html:
Kendal is a market town in Cumbria, on the edge of the Lake District, famous among Muggles for its mint cake. It is the home of Mr L. Ashby, whose testimonial appears in the advertising for Kwikspell, a correspondence course in beginners' magic.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Nine, in the autumn of 1992, Harry Potter found a Kwikspell envelope on Argus Filch's desk.
