The Headmaster, Professor Dippet, could not bear the shame of it, so the girl's death was put about as an accident.

Riddle was given a special award for services to the school, and told to keep quiet. He kept the memory of that year in a diary instead, meaning it to lead somebody else, one day, to finish Slytherin's work.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Fifteen, in February 1993, Riddle's diary told Harry Potter that in Riddle's fifth year the Chamber had been opened, that its monster had killed a girl, and that the one who opened it had been expelled. It drew Harry into its memory of 13 June 1943, in which Riddle caught Hagrid with a creature in a box. For a while Harry believed that Hagrid had done it.

In Book Two, Chapter Eighteen, in the Chamber itself, the memory of Riddle wrote its name in the air and rearranged the letters: I AM LORD VOLDEMORT. Riddle had been the heir of Slytherin all along. He had walked away unpunished.

pages.title: The opening of the Chamber of Secrets (1992 to 1993)
infobox: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets (2 July 1998)
The memory of Tom Riddle, through his diary
Dracina Malfoy, possessed by the diary
Mrs Norris, Colin Creevey, Justin Finch-Fletchley, Nearly Headless Nick, Hermione Granger, Penelope Clearwater
pages.html:
The opening of the Chamber of Secrets in 1992 to 1993 was the second opening of Slytherin's Chamber at Hogwarts. The memory of Tom Riddle kept in his diary, working through the possessed Dracina Malfoy, opened it again. The Basilisk Petrified six victims before Ginny Weasley was taken into the Chamber. It ended on 29 May 1993, when Harry Potter killed the Basilisk and destroyed the diary.

The diary

Lucius Malfoy meant the diary for Ginny Weasley, but in Flourish and Blotts in August 1992 his daughter swept it up by mistake with an armful of other books. Dracina began to write in it. The voice that answered, which she called Tom, became her understanding friend. That autumn she grew pale and sleepless. She lost hours, and woke in places she could not remember with red on her hands. Through her the memory opened the Chamber, set the Basilisk loose and wrote on the walls. On Christmas night Harry, disguised as Goyle, took the diary from her. She worked on Neville Longbottom until he let her have it back, and after that there was nothing left of her to resist with.

The attacks

On Hallowe'en 1992 the first message appeared on a wall of the second floor, daubed a foot high: 'The Chamber of Secrets has been opened. Enemies of the heir, beware.' Beneath it hung Filch's cat, Mrs Norris, Petrified. Colin Creevey was Petrified in November. In December it was Justin Finch-Fletchley, together with Nearly Headless Nick. In the spring it was Hermione Granger, with the Ravenclaw prefect Penelope Clearwater. Riddle afterwards claimed that he had removed Hermione as a favour to Dracina.

None of them died, because none of them met the Basilisk's eyes directly. Colin saw it through his camera, Justin through Nick, and the two girls in a mirror. Nick, who could not die again, took the full force of it.

Then Ginny Weasley was taken. She had followed Dracina and the diary into the Chamber, where Riddle had the possessed Dracina strike her down. Ginny's blood wrote the second message on the wall, and Riddle began to drain her life to restore himself.

In the saga

In Book Two, Chapter Eighteen, Harry opened the Chamber in Parseltongue and went on alone. He found Dracina collapsing at the feet of Slytherin's statue. The memory of Riddle, grown almost solid, told him that the heir's acts of that year had been his own, carried out through Dracina, and set the Basilisk on him. Its fang caught his arm. As he lay dying, a warmth held him, and he was healed. Then Fawkes dropped the Sorting Hat into his hands, and out of it came the sword with which he killed the Basilisk.

Then he drove the sword through the diary. Black ink gushed out of it like blood, and Riddle dissolved, screaming. It was 29 May 1993. By the end of that night the Petrified had been revived with the Mandrake draught, and Hagrid was home from Azkaban.

pages.title: Ripper
infobox: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (8 July 1999)
Chasing Harry Potter up a tree
pages.html:
Ripper is Aunt Marge Dursley's favourite bulldog, an old dog with an evil temper. He pines if he is away from her, which is why she brought him with her to Privet Drive in 1993 and left the rest of her dogs at home. The year before Harry Potter started at Hogwarts, Ripper chased him up a tree.

The tree

It happened on Marge's last visit before 1993, when Harry accidentally trod on Ripper's tail. Ripper chased him out into the garden and up a tree. Marge refused to call him off until past midnight. The memory still brings tears of laughter to Dudley's eyes.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Two, Marge came to stay at Privet Drive for a week in the summer of 1993, with Ripper tucked under her arm. Colonel Fubster was minding the rest of her dogs, but she could not leave poor old Ripper. 'Ripper can have some tea out of my saucer,' she said. He lapped it noisily in the corner. Aunt Petunia winced as specks of tea and drool flecked her clean floor. He growled when Harry sat down.

On the last evening of Marge's stay, Harry's temper blew her up like a balloon. Ripper came skidding into the room, barking madly. When Uncle Vernon seized one of Marge's feet to pull her down, Ripper sank his teeth into Vernon's leg. Vernon's trouser leg was left in bloody tatters.

In Chapter Nineteen, in June 1994, Remus Lupin in his Garou shape circled Harry in the dark, low to the ground, with his head down. Harry had seen something move like that once before. Aunt Marge's bulldog had circled him exactly the same way in the back garden at Privet Drive, just before it chased him up a tree.

In Book Four, Chapter One, Ripper was under the dinner table in Harry's dream of the house on the hill, gnawing at something with a horrible wet crunching noise. Aunt Marge, in a maid's black dress, went on pouring gravy until it covered the tablecloth. It dripped off the edges of the table on to the carpet, where Ripper lapped it up.

pages.title: Colonel Fubster
infobox: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (8 July 1999)
pages.html:
Colonel Fubster is a retired army officer and a friend of Marjorie Dursley, Harry Potter's Aunt Marge. He minds her dogs when she goes away, and he has drowned at least one of them for her.

Aunt Marge's dogs

Aunt Marge breeds bulldogs at her house in the country, and she has twelve of them. When she came to stay at Privet Drive in the summer of 1993 she left them in the Colonel's charge, all except Ripper, who pines if he is away from her. As she put it: 'He's retired now, good for him to have something to do.'

The year before, the Colonel had drowned a pup for her, a ratty little runt she thought weak and underbred. Not long before her visit a glass had broken in her hand at his house. A wineglass did the same at the Dursleys' table, though that time it was not her grip that did it.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Two, one evening at dinner, Aunt Marge told the table that Harry had a mean, runty look about him, the sort you get with dogs: 'I had Colonel Fubster drown one last year.' Harry tried very hard not to think about what he wanted to say back, which included the question of whether Colonel Fubster had ever been asked to drown anything of her weight.

pages.title: John Constantine
aliases: the dodgy bloke on the Knight Bus
the man on the Knight Bus
infobox: Constantine; John; Johnny; Johnny Constantine; J. Lennon, MACUSA

Lucius Malfoy former best friend, then enemy, detests
Albus Dumbledore creditor of an old grudge, owes a debt to
Rubeus Hagrid friend
John Constantine's father father
Lucifer adversary
His sister Cheryl Masters and her daughter Gemma; a twin brother who died in the womb
Rubeus Hagrid; Chas Chandler; the Swamp Thing; Zatanna
Lucius Malfoy; the First of the Fallen; the demon Nergal
pages.html:
John Constantine is a Muggle-born wizard and occultist from Liverpool, one of the very few Muggle-borns ever sorted into Slytherin. After seven miserable years at Hogwarts he turned his back on the wizarding world. He made his name instead in the older arts of chalk, candles and blood. He guided the Swamp Thing against the darkness of 1985 to 1986, has spent years among the costumed heroes, and is owed a favour by Superman. He was forty by the calendar in 1993, but younger in body after his time in Hell. He has bargained with the Devil and lived. In August 1993 he burgled the Linking Book to Myst Island from a collector in New Mexico for Albus Dumbledore, and carried it north on the Knight Bus, across the aisle from Harry Potter.

Early life

John Constantine was born in Liverpool in 1953. He grew up in the Dingle, at number seventeen, a two-up, two-down terraced house with an outside lavatory. His mother died giving birth to him. His father, a drunken docker, blamed the boy for her death every day of his life, and beat him for years. John learnt early to stay out of his father's way and to talk his way out of trouble. He stopped crying when he was six.

He was a twin. His brother died in the womb, strangled by John's own cord, and John has wondered all his life which of them was meant to be born. His only family worth the name is his older sister, Cheryl, who married and settled down as Cheryl Masters. Her daughter, Gemma, grew up thinking her Uncle John the most exciting man alive, which he has spent years trying to correct.

Hogwarts

He started at Hogwarts in 1964, eleven years old, small for his age and quite sure that he would be a Ravenclaw. While the first-years waited to be sorted, he befriended a frightened, stammering boy who had been told he would have to fight a troll. John promised to go first and sell the troll a snide watch. The boy was Lucius Malfoy. The Sorting Hat put John in Slytherin, for his cunning, almost before it touched his hair, and Lucius followed him to the table.

At the first feast the house learnt that his father was a docker, and that his dead mother had been no witch either. The laughter stopped all the way down the table. For seven years Slytherin persecuted him. His bed was charmed to tip him out every hour, his robes were shrunk, and his father's letter was read aloud at breakfast. He was locked in a broom cupboard over Hallowe'en, dangled from a tower over the lake, and had MUDBLOOD painted on his trunk. In his fifth year his pumpkin juice was poisoned. He spent nine days in the hospital wing turning green, with Lucius reading aloud at his bedside.

John always paid them back, with itching powder in Rookwood's underpants and a sixth-year's love letter pinned up on Valentine's Day. He cheated in every examination without once being caught. When it all got too much he went down to the young gamekeeper, Rubeus Hagrid, who gave him tea with rock cakes and never asked what was wrong.

At fifteen he shot up, grew handsome and became the Slytherin rebel. He smoked behind the greenhouses and played the Stones on a charmed Dansette in an empty third-floor classroom. Girls came to him from every house. Lucius, who had always told him privately that he was an exception, drifted off to a colder set, one that would later have a master and a mark on their arms. In March of their seventh year Lucius called him a Mudblood over a Ravenclaw girl. Their duel ended in a brawl on the flagstones. Each swore vengeance on his own blood.

The girl ended things a month after they left school, and John decided that real love was something put in songs to sell records. On his last morning he bellowed at the castle that he was never coming back. He kept his word for twenty-two years.

After school

Since 1971 John has had as little to do with the wizarding world as he could manage, and he has not set foot in the Leaky Cauldron in all that time. The war against Voldemort began while he was still at school. He kept as far from it as he could. In 1977 an unsigned parcel brought him a curse that would have taken off his hands; he sent it back.

In London in the later 1970s he fronted a punk band, Mucous Membrane, and took up the occult in earnest among Muggles. In 1978, in Newcastle, an exorcism he led went wrong. A child, Astra Logue, was dragged down to Hell by the demon he had raised to save her, and afterwards he spent time in Ravenscar psychiatric hospital. It was the first of many deaths he blames himself for. In 1981, when the wizarding papers were full of the baby who had defeated Voldemort, John was busy with something in Hell and missed the story.

The Swamp Thing and the darkness

John first came to wider notice in 1985, in America, as the guide and tempter of the Swamp Thing, the plant elemental of the Louisiana bayous. He took it across America on a journey he called American Gothic. He showed it vampires, werewolves and haunted houses, so that it would learn what it was. All the while he was readying it for something larger. A South American cult of sorcerers, the Brujería, had begun to wake a darkness older than the world.

The Crisis of 1985 to 1986 came in the middle of it all, when the skies turned red. John was in it, as everybody was. Like everybody, he does not agree with anybody else about what he saw.

In 1986, as the darkness rose, the Swamp Thing went down to meet it. John called a séance to watch over the Swamp Thing on its way and to guide it. He brought together the strongest magicians of the age for it, with a number of spirits besides. Among them were the Spectre, Doctor Fate, Deadman, the Phantom Stranger, the demon Etrigan, the stage magician Zatara with his daughter Zatanna, and the sorcerer Sargon. The darkness rose to the very edge of Heaven, met the Presence, and was gone. What passed between them nobody living can say. Sargon and Zatara died at the séance. Zatanna, once John's lover, has never entirely forgiven him. He has never forgiven himself.

Earlier, in 1985, he had faced a very old demon that fed on light. To beat it he gatecrashed a Ministry dinner and stole Dumbledore's Deluminator from his pocket. He returned it a week later, scorched, with the demon put away for a thousand years. He tried to apologise in the Hog's Head, but Dumbledore shouted him down and put the grudge away in his desk drawer, like a good cheque.

Among the heroes

John has spent years in the company of people who fly about with their underpants over their tights. He likes very few of them. They work in daylight and in public; he does not. Most of them think him a cheat and a liar. Most of them are right. They call him in all the same when the trouble is the kind no costume can punch.

He has shaken hands with Superman, and Superman made the very dangerous mistake of owing him a favour. Neither of them has ever said what it was for. The likeliest account puts it in the Crisis of 1985 to 1986, which nobody remembers properly, and that suits John very well. As far as anybody knows, he has not yet called it in. He is saving it.

In 1990 he was one of four men in trench coats who took a bespectacled London boy named Tim Hunter on a tour of magic past, present and to come. The others were the Phantom Stranger, Doctor Occult and Mister E. They meant to show the boy the power he might one day have, and to let him choose for himself whether to take it.

On his fortieth birthday, in May 1993, his old friends threw him a party. The guests included the Swamp Thing, Zatanna, Chas and a good many people John had assumed were dead or wanted him to be. He spent most of it wondering which of them he would bury next.

Demon blood and the Dreaming

In 1988 he lost his old friend Gary Lester to a hunger demon, Mnemoth, which John had sent Gary to carry. He fell into a war with the demon Nergal and the Damnation Army, a crusade of fanatics that Nergal was steering towards the end of the world. Dying, John was saved by a transfusion of Nergal's own blood. Since 1988 some of the blood in his veins has been a demon's, which is one reason he can tell the Mark of the Beast at a glance.

In 1989 Dream of the Endless, newly free after seventy-two years in a glass prison, came looking for a pouch of sand that had been stolen from him. It had passed through John's hands. John helped him get it back, and he has stayed on civil terms with the family ever since, with Death above all.

Hell and the Devil

John has sat across a table from the Devil himself, who has worn many names since he first sang out of tune. No man alive has come closer to getting the better of him. In 1990, in his guise as Lucifer, the Devil made a show of giving up his throne and emptying Hell. It was one more of his masks. By 1991 he was back on the throne as the First of the Fallen.

In 1991, dying of lung cancer, John arranged matters so that three of the lords of Hell each believed his soul belonged to them alone. Because each knew about the other two, he was cured rather than collected, and he is still alive. He thinks God a bastard on the whole, and the Devil a great deal worse. Beside the Devil, Voldemort is to him a scally with a flick knife.

He has died more than once and come back. He knows Death herself: a lovely girl, he says, who has always been kind to him, though she has shocking taste in admirers. Among them is a mad purple alien who has courted her with bad poetry for longer than John has been alive. John has sailed the Styx, been carried down to Hell in a lift made of screaming, driven a hearse over the Pennines with the corpse giving directions, and taken the shirt off a Duke of Hell at cards in Soho.

Time in Hell, in other dimensions and in death has muddied his age. Forty by the calendar in 1993, he looks about thirty, and he is vain enough not to want to know the truth.

Kit

After he cheated the lords of Hell in 1991, John fell properly in love for the first time since Hogwarts. She was Kit Ryan, a Belfast woman with a sharp tongue and no patience whatever with his world. She lived with him in London through 1991 and 1992. When that world came through her door, as it always does, she left him and went home to Ireland. It was the second time he had decided that real love was something put in songs to sell records.

Methods

John owns a wand. He keeps it in an inside pocket, between a pawn ticket and a packet of chewing gum. He hardly ever uses it. He prefers wandless magic and ritual: the occult arts, which wizards despise because Muggles can use them too. He travels by the old roads, stepping from one midnight crossroads to another round the world with salt on his shoes. He carries chalk, salt, a black candle, churchyard earth and a Hand of Glory from Prague. He swore never to use the Hand, and has used it at least four times.

He believes that only three men alive can join wizardry to the old occultism well enough to make one do what the other cannot: Victor von Doom, Stephen Strange and himself. Doctor Fate he discounts while his helmet sleeps. He distrusts black dogs, which he knows as Black Shuck, the Barghest, the Grim and the Gytrash.

The Myst book

In the summer of 1993 an owl landed in John's pint, in a Soho pub nobody knew about, carrying a letter in green ink. Dumbledore asked him, as a small favour, to bring him a book from Ephraim Shacklewell of New Mexico before the middle of August, unopened. ‘I think of my Deluminator, too,’ the letter said. John obeyed, as he always did in the end with Dumbledore.

He buried his wand in the desert so that the wards would see only a man. He set out salt and a black candle. He tasted Whitechapel churchyard earth, drew the seal of Andromalius in chalk and his own blood, then walked into the house backwards, reciting the Lord's Prayer backwards. The thumb of his Hand of Glory would not light, which meant that someone was awake. The book fell open in his hands and its picture pulled at him. He slammed it shut and left a Jackie Collins in its place. Caught by Shacklewell, he passed himself off as a MACUSA officer, with a glamoured, expired Liverpool library card and a Kojak accent. He signed the receipt ‘J. Lennon, MACUSA’.

He came home by the old roads. Then he rode the Knight Bus from Liverpool to Hogsmeade with his hand flat on the Tesco bag, and Stan Shunpike stopped him smoking three times. He saw through the boy who called himself Neville Longbottom: in the way the lad sat he recognised his own childhood of beatings, and he refused to get involved. He will treasure for life the boy's telling the Minister for Magic that he was Barry Trotter.

At Hogwarts Hagrid lifted him clean off the ground. In the Headmaster's office Dumbledore, angered, began to speak Greta Grindelwald's words, then stopped in horror and apologised. Taking the book from a man who had never owned it, he told John, was not burglary but a kindness. ‘You've got some front, Albus,’ said John. He took a sherbet lemon and put his feet up on the desk.

Appearance and character

John has rough blond hair, usually two days' stubble, and the look of a man who has slept in his clothes, which he generally has. He wears a grey suit, a long tan raincoat, a loosened tie and a once-white shirt. He smokes Silk Cut whenever he can. His voice goes back to the Dingle when he is angry.

He is cynical, funny, brave when he must be and untrustworthy when it suits him. His promises are like paper aeroplanes thrown into a full bath. He carries a churchyard of dead friends in his head. In Dumbledore he sees something too much like himself.

Later years

John aged as other men do, more or less, and went on doing what he did. In the years after 1994 he outlived more friends, lovers and enemies than he could count. He went back to Hell more than once, well into the new century. In 2010, to the astonishment of everybody who knew him, he married Epiphany Greaves, a young alchemist and the daughter of a London gangster. In 2013 he turned sixty.

In the saga

On the night Harry Potter ran away from Privet Drive in August 1993, an unnamed man of perhaps thirty-five, in a slept-in suit and a raincoat, rode the Knight Bus with his hand on a carrier bag that flickered green. He swore in what Harry thought was a Liverpool accent, looked up sharply at the name Voldemort, and rode on past Aberdeen. Harry took him for a Muggle-born, and thought him a dodgy bloke. It was the same journey on which John, across the aisle, saw through the boy who called himself Neville Longbottom.

In June 1994, staring at the Myst book on a desk, Harry remembered that he had seen somebody hold a book like that before: the man in the raincoat on the bed across the aisle, with one hand flat on his carrier bag.

In their own words

I'm never comin' back to this dump, d'you hear me? Never!John Constantine · B3 Interlude
Of the noble and ancient house of number seventeen, me. Two up, two down, and a lav in the yard.John Constantine · B3 Interlude
You've got some front, Albus.John Constantine · B3 Interlude

pages.title: Ganymede
pages.html:
Ganymede is Narcissa Malfoy's eagle owl, a huge, haughty bird who carries the Malfoys' parcels to Hogwarts. In July 1993 he carried Dracina Malfoy's first letter to Harry Potter, and he made it plain that he thought very little of where he had been sent.

Description

Ganymede is a very large eagle owl, dark and barred, with ear tufts like horns. His eyes are the colour of marmalade. He is Narcissa's own bird, although the whole family uses him. For nearly three years he has brought Dracina parcels of sweets from home every week. She unwraps them at the Slytherin table as though the whole Hall ought to be watching. That is how Harry came to know the bird by sight after two years of breakfasts.

He has a low opinion of most things. He flies as though every window were slightly beneath him, and he does not wait for replies.

Errands

At midnight on Harry's thirteenth birthday, 31 July 1993, Ganymede came in last of all through the bedroom window at Number Four, Privet Drive. He carried a scented letter from Dracina, tied to his leg with a thin green ribbon. Narcissa had sent him across three counties, saying that he knew the way to Surrey; Dracina did not ask her how. He settled on the one clear corner of the bedside table and looked round Harry's small, untidy bedroom with the deepest disdain. When Harry laughed out loud at the letter, the owl opened one eye and looked at him as though laughter were common.

He left without waiting for a reply. Dracina's postscript explained that it was not done to ask for one, and that if Harry wrote anyway, Ganymede knew the way home.

One Monday morning in March 1994 he dropped a thick envelope sealed in green wax in front of Dracina at breakfast, then swept out again without waiting for so much as a bacon rind. It was a letter from her father. Lucius wrote to thank her for her four pages about the hippogriff Buckbeak, which she had written but never sent, and which he had laid before the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures. On the strength of them, the hearing had been brought forward to that Friday. Dracina went white, then red, crushed the letter in her fist and walked out of the Great Hall. Her goblet went over, and the pumpkin juice dripped on to Goyle's knees.

On a Thursday in June 1994, shortly before the examinations, Ganymede brought Dracina a long, soft parcel wrapped in brown paper. She whisked it under the table on to her lap before anybody could see, and carried it out of the Great Hall.

pages.title: The tawny Hogwarts owl
infobox: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (8 July 1999)
Harry Potter's Hogwarts letter and Hagrid's parcel, 31 July 1993
pages.html:
The tawny Hogwarts owl is the sleek school owl that brought Harry Potter his Hogwarts letter, together with Hagrid's birthday parcel, at midnight on 31 July 1993.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter One, the tawny was one of four owls that came through Harry's window that night, after Hedwig and Errol. It was a sleek brown bird with a serious face. It landed neatly on the back of his chair and held out its leg, like a school owl working to a timetable. It carried a thick envelope with the Hogwarts crest on the back. It also carried a parcel done up in brown paper, tied with knots that nobody but Hagrid tied.

The book inside the parcel bit Harry, then fled under the bed. The tawny closed its eyes, as if it had seen all this before. It had gone by the time he looked round.

pages.title: Crookshanks
infobox:
Hermione Granger owner
Sirius Black companion, ally
cat, pet, Hermione's pet, Granger family, part-Kneazle
Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (July 1999)
pages.html:
Crookshanks is Hermione Granger's cat, a huge, bow-legged ginger animal with a squashed face and a tail like a bottlebrush. He is part Kneazle, and uncannily clever. He knew Ron Weasley's rat Scabbers for Peter Pettigrew the moment he saw him. He spent the school year of 1993 to 1994 helping Sirius Black try to catch him.

Description

Crookshanks has the Kneazle's gift for knowing who cannot be trusted. He had been in the Magical Menagerie for ages, because nobody wanted him, which Hermione took personally. She bought him on 31 August 1993 with ten Galleons of early birthday money. A few moments earlier he had landed on Ron's head and gone for Scabbers, who fled under a bin outside Quality Quidditch Supplies.

In the saga

On the Hogwarts Express Crookshanks stared warily at the sleeping Remus Lupin with his fur on end, and kept an eye on him all afternoon. At school he brought a dead spider into the common room. He attacked Ron's bag when Ron said Scabbers was inside it, waited at the foot of the boys' staircase on the morning of a match and spat at Ron's Pocket Sneakoscope. On Christmas morning he leapt at Ron's chest with tinsel round his neck. When Scabbers vanished in March 1994, leaving ginger hairs on the floor, Ron blamed Crookshanks. The quarrel kept Ron and Hermione apart for weeks.

Crookshanks had seen at once that the rat was Peter Pettigrew. He had seen, too, that the enormous black dog in the grounds was no dog at all, and he was seen walking beside it at night. He tried to bring Pettigrew to Sirius Black. For Sirius he stole the list of Gryffindor passwords from Neville Longbottom's bedside table, and he took Sirius's order for Harry's Firebolt to the Owl Office.

On 6 June 1994 he pressed the knot that froze the Whomping Willow. He led Harry and Hermione down the tunnel to the Shrieking Shack. There he clawed Harry's arm, then lay across Black's chest as though guarding him. Pettigrew's spell flung him into the air, but he survived, and limped along after Snape's stretchers. At the end of term he sniffed at Sirius's tiny owl and purred, which Ron took as a sign of approval.

pages.title: Mr Crabbe
infobox: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (8 July 2000)
Lord Voldemort, in the first war
pages.html:
Mr Crabbe is the father of Vincent Crabbe. He reports to Lucius Malfoy, and his son has been reporting to Lucius in his turn since the age of six.

Background

Mr Crabbe followed the Dark Lord in the first war, as Lucius Malfoy did. Like Lucius, he kept out of Azkaban when it was over, and he has stayed close to the Malfoys ever since.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Five, on the Hogwarts Express in September 1993, Dracina Malfoy thought about what Vincent Crabbe and Gregory Goyle were for. They always reported to her father. They had been doing it since they were six, because their fathers reported to him as well. It had taken Dracina until she was about nine to work it out.

pages.html:
Mr Goyle is the father of Gregory Goyle. He reports to Lucius Malfoy, as Mr Crabbe does, and his son reports to Lucius too.

Background

Like Lucius Malfoy and Mr Crabbe, Mr Goyle was one of the Dark Lord's followers in the first war. All three of them stayed out of Azkaban when it ended.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Five, on the Hogwarts Express in September 1993, Dracina Malfoy reflected that Crabbe and Goyle had been reporting to her father since they were six. They did it because their fathers reported to him. She had been about nine before she understood that this was what the two boys were for.

pages.html:
Sirius Black is a pure-blood wizard of the House of Black, the best friend of James Potter and the godfather of Harry Potter. He was wrongly imprisoned in Azkaban for twelve years for betraying the Potters and murdering Peter Pettigrew. He became the first prisoner ever to escape from it, and he has been a fugitive since July 1993. In his cell he came to faith at last, and it is one of the two things that kept the dementors from hollowing him out.

Early life

Sirius was born into the House of Black, one of the proudest of the old pure-blood families. Ron Weasley says the Blacks and the Lestranges would rather marry their own sisters than a Muggle-born. He was the elder son of Orion and Walburga Black. His younger brother, Regulus, followed the family into Voldemort's service.

Sirius broke with all of it. In 1971 the Hat sorted him into Gryffindor, the first Black in generations to go anywhere but Slytherin. At sixteen he ran away from home to live with James Potter's parents, Fleamont and Euphemia, who treated him as a second son.

His cousins Bellatrix and Narcissa were in his own year at Hogwarts. Bella and Cissy, as he calls them, spent those years feuding over James. Sirius speaks of Bella now the way people at funerals speak of the dead. She went, he says, completely round the twist.

Hogwarts and the Marauders

Sirius and James Potter were inseparable. They were the ringleaders of their gang, and both of them were exceptionally bright. McGonagall says nobody ever topped them for mischief. With Remus Lupin and Peter Pettigrew they were the Marauders. Sirius, known as Padfoot, helped to write the Marauder's Map. When James found out that Lupin was a Garou, Sirius became an illegal Animagus with him in their fifth year, taking the form of a huge black dog. At thirteen he spent nearly two months telling the Gryffindor common room that Lupin's monthly absences were on account of a girl called Rita.

He and Severus Snape loathed each other. Sirius still calls him Snivellus. At sixteen Sirius tricked Snape into trying to follow Lupin past the Whomping Willow on the night of a full moon. Only James's intervention saved Snape's life. Snape says Sirius tried to kill him.

Among his friends, Sirius was the one honest unbeliever. Lily Evans, the only believer among them at school, talked to him about God. He refused her then, and he went on refusing her afterwards. She never moved him.

The betrayal

Sirius was best man at James and Lily's wedding. He became godfather to their son, Harry, and the Potters named him Harry's guardian. When the Potters went into hiding under the Fidelius Charm, James insisted on Sirius as their Secret-Keeper, over Dumbledore's own offer. But Sirius had come to suspect that Lupin was the spy in their circle. At the last moment, without telling Lupin, he persuaded the Potters to make Peter Pettigrew their Secret-Keeper instead, reasoning that nobody would ever think of Peter. Their circle had one unbeliever who was honest about it and one false believer who was not. The Order trusted the wrong one.

On the night of 31 October 1981 Sirius went to check on Pettigrew and found his hiding place empty. He went straight to Godric's Hollow, where he found James dead in the hall and Lily upstairs. Hagrid had already come for the baby. Sirius begged Hagrid to give Harry to him, and argued with him. In the end he gave Hagrid his flying motorbike, saying he would not need it any more.

The next day he cornered Pettigrew in a street full of Muggles. Pettigrew shouted, for everyone to hear, that Sirius had betrayed Lily and James. Then he blew the street apart with a wand held behind his back, killing twelve Muggles. He cut off his own finger and fled into the sewers as a rat. Sirius stood laughing in the crater. When twenty members of the Magical Law Enforcement Squad came for him, he went quietly. He was sent to Azkaban without a trial.

Azkaban

For twelve years dementors guarded Sirius's cell day and night. He survived because he knew he was innocent. That was not a happy thought, so the dementors could not feed on it. He could also become a dog, whose simpler feelings the blind dementors could not easily reach. Every dementor that passed made the night of the Potters' deaths fresh again, and he never properly mourned them. Bellatrix had the next cell. Through the walls he heard Voldemort's imprisoned followers screaming in their sleep that the double-crosser had double-crossed them.

In Azkaban he came to faith at last. It came to him through the Bible passages printed in The Quibbler, above all the verse 'I'd rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than dwell in the tents of wickedness.' He made a cross of two splinters of his bed frame bound with thread from his blanket, and he wore it smooth with his thumb. Once he believed, he said, the dementors stopped coming to him. Nobody knew: not Lupin, not Dumbledore, nobody living. It is why Cornelius Fudge found him so strangely normal on his inspections. He seemed bored. He asked whether Fudge had finished with his newspaper, because he missed the crossword.

On an inspection in the summer of 1993 Fudge gave him his Daily Prophet. In a photograph of the Weasley family in Egypt, Sirius recognised Ron's rat, a toe missing from its paw, as Pettigrew. He began to talk in his sleep, 'He's at Hogwarts', and he was found wrapped in issues of his magazine. Shortly afterwards he prayed. Then he slipped past the guards as a dog when they brought food, squeezed through the bars and swam to the mainland. It was the first escape in the history of Azkaban.

In the saga: fugitive (1993 to 1994)

On 31 July 1993 his gaunt face and elbow-length matted hair appeared on Muggle television. The Muggles were told that he was armed with a gun, and Fudge briefed the Muggle Prime Minister himself. A few days later Sirius, as a dog, watched Harry leave Privet Drive from a gap between a garage and a fence in Magnolia Crescent. Harry lit the gap with his wand, saw an enormous black dog with pale eyes and fell backwards into the gutter.

He lived in the Forbidden Forest through the school year and watched Harry play Quidditch. He made an ally of Hermione's cat, Crookshanks, who saw through Scabbers and helped him hunt the rat. At Hallowe'en 1993 he slashed the Fat Lady's portrait when she would not let him into Gryffindor Tower. At Christmas he sent Harry a Firebolt, ordered in Harry's name but paid for with his own Gringotts gold. Early in 1994 the Ministry authorised the dementors to give him the Kiss on sight.

On the night of the Ravenclaw match in March 1994 he got into the tower with Neville Longbottom's lost list of the week's passwords. He slashed the curtains of Ron's bed with a long knife. Ron punched him in the face, and he bled all the way to Hogsmeade.

In the saga: the Shrieking Shack

On the night of Buckbeak's execution in June 1994 Sirius, as the dog, dragged Ron down under the Whomping Willow, breaking Ron's leg on a root. Harry and Hermione followed them to the Shrieking Shack. Harry attacked him with his bare hands, screaming about the cupboard under the stairs and about his parents. Sirius, wearing his wooden cross, never once struck back. He muttered 'my fault' over and over. Afterwards he laughed that the rescue was James but the rage was Lily.

Lupin arrived and embraced him. Then the two men forced Scabbers back into the shape of Peter Pettigrew. When Lupin's war form threatened to break through at the reek of the rat, Sirius steadied him with the verse Lily had written on the wall of their old flat: 'Be ye angry, and sin not.' Harry stopped them killing Pettigrew, so that he could be handed over as proof.

In the tunnel Sirius asked Harry to come and live with him. Harry joyfully agreed, before he remembered the blood ward that binds him to his aunt's house. Sirius accepted Dumbledore's ruling. On the lawn he and Lupin said the evening collect together, 'Lighten our darkness', as Lily used to. Then the full moon came out. Lupin, who had missed his Wolfsbane Potion, changed. Thrown twenty feet, Sirius rose to his knees praying the twenty-third Psalm: 'Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil'. Then he turned into the dog and fought the Garou to save Harry. Pettigrew escaped in the confusion.

Sirius was found at the lake's edge without his cross, moaning that he had let Peter go again, as a hundred dementors closed in. Harry's stag Patronus drove them off. Snape bound and gagged him. He was locked in Professor Flitwick's office on the seventh floor to await the Kiss.

In the saga: Myst Island

Dumbledore left a D'ni linking book marked MYST on Flitwick's desk. Sirius touched it and linked to Myst Island. He left grey fingermarks on the cover, and a neatly coiled rope behind him. Harry, Hermione Granger and Dracina Malfoy followed him. They found him on the floor of the ruined library, gaunt and shaking. He had been keeping company with a woman who talked in riddles. She was dreadfully sad, had a lovely laugh and reminded him of Bella before she went round the twist. He never learnt her name. She was Yeesha, the daughter of Atrus, and she vanished when Harry arrived.

There in the library he told Harry that he had lost his cross down by the lake, and shrugged: 'Never mind. I don't suppose He needs it to find me.' Then he looked at the two girls, each of them guarding Harry as jealously as the other. 'Bella and Cissy,' he murmured, to nobody in particular. 'Bella and Cissy, all over again. God help the boy.' Then, quite seriously, he made the sign of the cross over Harry's head.

Back in Flitwick's office, Dracina whistled Buckbeak up to the window. Sirius thanked all three of them for believing him when nobody else did. He told Harry that James was looking down on him, and was proud. Privately he thought that Cissy would be delighted that James's son had won over a Malfoy. Lily, he told Harry, would want him to sort things out with Christ. He should go to church, and he should see the Fat Friar, who had helped Lily when she was Harry's age. Then Sirius flew away on Buckbeak, a little before midnight.

In the saga: since June 1994

A tiny owl reached the Hogwarts Express with his letter. He and Buckbeak were in hiding. He meant to let Muggles glimpse him far from Hogwarts, so that the castle's security could be lifted. The Firebolt had been thirteen birthdays' worth of presents from him. He enclosed signed permission for Harry to visit Hogsmeade. He gave the owl to Ron, since it was his fault that Ron no longer had a rat.

Over the summer he sent Harry two cheerful letters by large, gaudy tropical birds, never saying where he was. He also sent a birthday cake. Harry suspects him of the dead and bleeding rats in the Dursleys' fridge, which have Marauder written all over them.

In their own words

He asked if I'd finished with my newspaper, if you please, as cool as anything, said he missed the crossword.Cornelius Fudge · B3 Ch10
I'd rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than dwell in the tents of wickedness.Sirius Black · B3 Ch18
Believe me, Harry. I never betrayed James and Lily. I would have died before I betrayed them.Sirius Black · B3 Ch18
Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for thou art with me.Sirius Black · B3 Ch19

pages.title: Khan Noonien Singh
infobox: The Augment programme, from Weapon III data
From the Bay of Bengal to the Persian Gulf
pages.html:
Khan Noonien Singh is a genetically engineered warlord, the foremost of the Augments. He took New Delhi in July 1993, at the age of twenty. By August 1994 he ruled from the Bay of Bengal to the Persian Gulf, over roughly a quarter of the world's population. The Muggle news calls his conquest the Augment War. The wizarding world has never heard of him.

Origin

Khan was created in 1973. The data behind him came from Weapon III, Les Enfants Terribles, the cloning of Big Boss in 1972, which had produced Solid Snake and Liquid Snake. Within a year its findings had been spun off, stolen or transferred. A separate operation used them to make Khan and the other Augments. It was never part of the Weapon programme, and it has never been officially acknowledged.

He was made to be better than human. He is several times as strong as an ordinary man, faster, harder to injure and quicker to heal. His mind is the equal of his body. Western intelligence describes him as 'exceptionally intelligent, physically formidable, and entirely without scruple'. Superior ability breeds superior ambition, and Khan has never been given a reason to doubt that he was born to rule.

Rise

In 1993 genetically engineered rulers seized power in more than forty countries at once. Khan, the ablest of them, made his bid in India. His forces laid siege to New Delhi for eleven weeks and took it in July 1993. The Indian government withdrew to Bangalore. By the end of that month he held the land from the Afghan border to the Bay of Bengal, and he had declared what he called a 'new order' for the subcontinent. The British Foreign Office advised all British nationals to leave.

The Avengers and the Justice League declined to intervene. Their United Nations accord, they said, prohibited unilateral action in a war between sovereign states, so they would act only at the Security Council's request. Delhi greeted the statement with anger.

Empire

In the year after Delhi fell, most of the other engineered rulers were overthrown by their own people. The rest swore allegiance to Khan or were destroyed by him. A United Nations coalition crossed his front south of Delhi in March 1994. It was withdrawn in June, eleven miles further on. By August 1994 his territory ran from the Bay of Bengal across Pakistan and Iran to the shores of the Persian Gulf.

His commanders appear to know coalition battle plans before they are issued. His soldiers fight at night without lights. No Augment has ever been taken alive. In July 1994 his commander Joaquin opened a second front in the former Yugoslavia, and on 20 August his forces were reported within forty miles of Belgrade. Nobody will say in public what has become of India's nuclear weapons.

Appearance and manner

Harry saw him on television in the summer of 1993, standing on a balcony somewhere above a crowd, with his chin up and his eyes half closed, as if the whole of India were a dog that had finally learnt to sit. He had the look, Harry thought, of somebody who had decided long ago that he was better than everybody else, and who had never once been given a reason to think otherwise. A conqueror of twenty is a more frightening thing than a conqueror of fifty.

In the saga

Book Three, Chapter Two: on 31 July 1993 the Dursleys' breakfast news reported the fall of New Delhi and the superhumans' refusal to intervene. Harry thought that Khan and Voldemort would have got on for about ten minutes, until one of them had to kill the other. Dudley was enthralled by him.

Book Three, Chapter Four: in Diagon Alley Harry asked Lucius Malfoy what the Ministry thought about the Augment War. Mr Malfoy had never heard of Khan. Harry understood then that the wizarding world did not know, rather than did not care, that any of it was happening.

Book Four, Chapter Three: on 20 August 1994 the news led with Khan's forces near Belgrade. Outside the United Nations a grieving mother screamed that Khan was 'just the same as them', the superhumans whom the crowd wanted punished. Uncle Vernon had been complaining all summer about the price of petrol. Looking at the red round the Gulf on the map, Harry thought he knew why.

In their own words

exceptionally intelligent, physically formidable, and entirely without scrupleWestern intelligence sources · B3 Ch2

pages.html:
The Augment War is the conflict that Khan Noonien Singh and the genetically engineered Augments have waged since 1993. No Muggle army has been able to stop it. It began with the seizure of power in more than forty countries at once, followed by the fall of New Delhi. By August 1994 Khan ruled about a quarter of the world's population, and his forces were nearing Belgrade. It is also known as the Eugenics Wars. The wizarding world has not noticed it at all.

Outbreak, 1993

In 1993 genetically engineered rulers seized power in more than forty countries at once. In India, Khan's forces laid siege to New Delhi for eleven weeks and took it in July 1993. The Indian government withdrew to Bangalore. The British Foreign Office advised all British nationals to leave the region. By the end of July Khan held the land from the Afghan border to the Bay of Bengal, and he had proclaimed a 'new order' for the subcontinent.

Pressure fell at once on the world's two largest superhuman organisations. In a joint statement from New York, the Avengers and the Justice League said that the United Nations accord under which they operate expressly prohibits unilateral action in any conflict between sovereign states. They would act, they said, only at the request of the Security Council and under its authority. The statement was greeted with anger in Delhi. The Security Council, fearing the precedent, kept the League out of India.

Khan's empire

Over the following year most of the other engineered rulers were overthrown by their own people. The rest swore allegiance to Khan or were destroyed by him. His territory spread west across Pakistan and Iran to the shores of the Persian Gulf. By August 1994 it stretched from Bengal to the Gulf, with the Gulf oil coast among it, and held roughly a quarter of the world's population. In Britain the price of petrol climbed all through the summer of 1994.

The coalition offensive, 1994

In March 1994, under a United Nations mandate, the largest multinational force assembled since the Gulf War crossed the front line south of Delhi. American, Russian, British and French troops fought side by side for the first time since 1945. They were expected to reach Delhi within a month. They were withdrawn in June, having advanced eleven miles. The Pentagon is still paying for the campaign.

The reasons for the failure are not secret, only unexplained. Khan's commanders appear to know coalition battle plans before they are issued. His soldiers fight at night without lights. Western officials have no reliable estimate of how many Augments there are; there may be as few as a hundred. Nobody has ever taken one alive. A French television crew filmed one tearing the hatch off a tank in April 1994, and two of the crew were killed later that day. Nobody in Whitehall will say in public what has become of India's nuclear weapons.

The Balkan front

In July 1994 Augment forces appeared in the former Yugoslavia, and nobody is sure how they got there. Under a commander known only as Joaquin they took more ground in five weeks than any army in Europe since the Second World War. Kosovo fell, with the Montenegrin coast and most of eastern Bosnia. The Bosnian Serb headquarters at Pale fell in a single morning. The Bosnian Serb leadership, which had rejected the international peace plan less than three weeks before, fled across the Drina into Serbia.

By 20 August 1994 the army of the rump Yugoslav state had collapsed. United Nations peacekeepers had been withdrawn from the safe area of Goražde, and Augment forces were within forty miles of Belgrade. Some three hundred thousand people were on the move. Hungary closed its southern border. Italy appealed for help with the boats crossing the Adriatic. American peacekeepers in Macedonia found themselves looking across the border at Augment positions, and Greece put its army on alert. Nato's ambassadors met in emergency session in Brussels, under an acting Secretary-General who had taken over only after the death of Manfred Wörner. In London the Prime Minister came back early from his holiday, and two more battalions were placed on standby.

Superhumans and the United Nations

On 19 August 1994 Superman appeared before the Security Council, with the Justice League and the Avengers behind him. 'People are dying while we wait to be asked,' he said. He offered to put the League under written orders: 'The Justice League is ready. The Watchtower is ready. We can be in Belgrade within the hour.' The Council adjourned without a vote. Belgrade had not asked for help. Russia said it would veto any resolution sending superhumans into Serbia without Belgrade's consent. China said it would oppose any resolution allowing superhumans to act on a nation's soil without its government's consent. Washington was 'studying the request'.

The Council's mood had changed in a year. A good many of its members no longer trusted the League at all. In July the United Nations had suspended the charter under which the League had worked since 1987, and the League now operated from the Watchtower, a half-built station on the Moon.

The appeal brought more than twenty thousand people into the street outside the United Nations that night, chanting 'No more capes!' There were smaller protests in Los Angeles, Chicago and what remains of Metropolis. In Washington the Senate Armed Services Committee prepared to hear evidence on reviving the Sentinel programme, so that giant robots could be sent against Khan's forces without risking American lives.

In the saga

Book Three, Chapter Two: the Dursleys' breakfast news on 31 July 1993 reported the fall of New Delhi, the government's flight to Bangalore and the superhumans' refusal to intervene. Harry watched the map go red.

Book Three, Chapter Four: Harry told Lucius Malfoy that half a continent was going red on the map, and that Muggle armies could not stop Khan. He asked what the Ministry thought. Mr Malfoy had never heard of any of it. The wizarding world, Harry understood, had a wall round it that went both ways.

Book Four, Chapter Three: on 20 August 1994 the Augment War led the news, with the defence report, the Balkan front, Superman at the Security Council and the protest in New York. Harry thought the strangest part was that it was all happening somewhere else. Little Whinging knew all about it, and was going to the shops anyway.

pages.title: The Avengers
infobox: Thor, Iron Man (Tony Stark), the Hulk (Bruce Banner), Ant-Man (Henry Pym) and the Wasp (Janet van Dyne)

Avengers Mansion, Fifth Avenue, Manhattan (1963 to 1986, and again after its rebuilding); Hydrobase, off the New York coast (1987 to 1989); the West Coast compound at Palos Verdes, California (1984 to 1993)
Active under a United Nations accord; has not intervened in the Augment War
Captain America, the Black Widow, Thunderstrike, War Machine, the Black Knight, Crystal, Hercules and others
pages.html:
The Avengers are a team of superhumans founded in New York in 1963. With the Justice League they are one of the two largest superhuman organisations in the world. They work under an accord with the United Nations, which kept them out of the Augment War in 1993, and in August 1994 an Avengers delegation stood with Superman before the Security Council. Of the famous early Avengers, only Captain America, who first fought the Nazis in 1940, is still on active service.

The war years

No team called the Avengers existed before 1963, but its oldest member had fought in one very like it twenty years before. Steve Rogers was born in New York on 4 July 1920. Weapon I made him a super-soldier in 1940, and in December of that year he came to public notice as Captain America, with a teenage partner called Bucky. Once America was in the war he fought beside the Sub-Mariner, Namor, who had been born the same year. He fought beside the Human Torch as well, the android that Phineas Horton had built, and beside the Torch's young partner, Toro.

The four of them, with Bucky, saved Winston Churchill from the Nazi superman called Master Man. Churchill suggested afterwards that they ought to be a team, and they fought the rest of the war as the Invaders. Later they were joined by two British heroes, Union Jack and Spitfire. Miss America and the Whizzer followed.

The Invaders went where the strongest heroes of the All-Star Squadron could not: into occupied Europe, against the Red Skull, Baron Heinrich Zemo and the armies of the Axis. Captain America and Bucky also fought beside Sergeant Nick Fury's Howling Commandos.

In the last weeks of the war in Europe in 1945, Rogers and Bucky tried to stop an explosive-laden drone that Zemo had launched. It blew up in the air. Bucky was lost. Rogers fell into the North Atlantic, where the serum kept him alive, frozen in a block of ice, for nineteen years.

After the war

The public was not told that Captain America was gone. At the government's request, other men wore the costume to keep the symbol alive. The first, William Naslund, who had fought in the war as the Spirit of '76, led a new team in 1946, the All-Winners Squad. With him were the Human Torch, Toro, the Sub-Mariner, the Whizzer, Miss America and a new Bucky, Fred Davis. Naslund was killed in 1946. Jeff Mace, the Patriot, wore the costume after him until 1949.

In 1953 and 1954 yet another Captain America appeared, hunting communist agents in the McCarthy years. He called himself a commie-smasher. He was William Burnside, a young scholar obsessed with Rogers, who had taken a version of the super-soldier serum without the Vita-Rays that made it safe. It drove both him and his partner mad. They were put into suspended animation. When Burnside was revived in 1972 he fought the real Captain America, and lost.

In 1959 Nick Fury, then of the Central Intelligence Agency, led a covert team that hunted surviving Nazis under the name of the Avengers. Its members included Dum Dum Dugan, Namora, Dominic Fortune, Ulysses Bloodstone, Kraven the Hunter and the man later called Sabretooth. It was never made public, so the name was free when the Avengers of 1963 took it.

The founding, 1963

The Avengers came together in the summer of 1963, almost by accident. Loki, Thor's adopted brother, cast an illusion that made the Hulk seem to have wrecked a train, in the hope of tricking Thor into fighting him. Rick Jones, the teenager whose life Bruce Banner had saved at the gamma bomb test in 1962, sent out a radio call to the Fantastic Four for help. It was answered instead by Thor, Iron Man, Ant-Man and the Wasp.

They found that the Hulk was not the real enemy. They beat Loki together, and they stayed together. The Wasp gave them their name. Tony Stark, who was then presented to the public as Iron Man's employer, gave the team his family's mansion on Fifth Avenue for its headquarters, with the Stark butler, Edwin Jarvis, to run it. He paid its bills through a foundation named after his mother. The Hulk left within weeks, distrusted by the others and distrusting them.

Thor is an Asgardian, and does not age as men do. Stark had come to public notice in his armour only at the end of 1962, and Pym earlier the same year. Janet van Dyne, a young heiress, had become the Wasp in 1963 after her father's murder.

The 1960s

Early in 1964 the Avengers found Captain America frozen in a block of ice in the North Atlantic, where the Sub-Mariner had thrown it in a temper. By the calendar Rogers was forty-three, but in body he was still the young man of 1945. He joined at once and soon led the team. The same year Baron Heinrich Zemo, the man who had launched the drone of 1945, gathered the first Masters of Evil against the Avengers. In 1965 he was killed in a rockslide in South America during a fight with Rogers.

In 1965 the founders stepped down. They left Captain America in charge of three newcomers with criminal records. One was Hawkeye, the circus archer Clint Barton. The other two were mutant twins, Pietro and Wanda Maximoff, who had been members of Magneto's Brotherhood of Evil Mutants. They called themselves Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch. The team survived, and from then on it was always a shifting roster rather than a fixed band.

Pym was soon back as Goliath, and later as Yellowjacket, with Van Dyne beside him. They married in 1968. Hercules of Olympus joined in 1967. In 1968 the Black Panther joined: T'Challa, king of the African nation of Wakanda, and the team's first Black member. The Vision joined the same year. He was an android built to destroy the team by Ultron, the robot Pym had made and lost control of. The Black Knight, Dane Whitman, joined in 1969. Kang the Conqueror, a warlord from the far future, became one of the team's most persistent enemies.

The 1970s

In 1971 the Avengers were drawn into the war between the Kree and Skrull empires, which is described below. For a time they were disbanded by Skrull impostors. The Black Widow, Natasha Romanoff, a Soviet agent who had defected in the 1960s, joined in 1973. That year Loki and the demon Dormammu tricked the Avengers into a war with the Defenders. In 1975 the Vision married the Scarlet Witch. In 1976 the Beast, Hank McCoy, formerly of the X-Men, joined.

In 1974 Captain America was hounded by the Secret Empire, and for a time he gave up his name. From 1977 the team was put under the scrutiny of Henry Peter Gyrich, the National Security Council's liaison. Both stories are told below. In 1979 Ms Marvel, Carol Danvers, joined, while the Falcon, Sam Wilson, was made a member under Gyrich's rules.

In 1973, while the Avengers and Captain Mar-Vell fought Thanos for the Cosmic Cube, the Justice League was holding off Darkseid's Parademons over the Pacific coast. In 1977 the Avengers brought Thanos down with Adam Warlock's help, on information Darkseid had sent to the League for his own ends.

The 1980s

Wonder Man joined in 1980, Tigra in 1981, She-Hulk in 1982 and Captain Marvel, the New Orleans harbour patrol officer Monica Rambeau, in 1983. The Wasp chaired the team for much of the decade. Captain Marvel succeeded her in 1987. In 1984, under the Vision's chairmanship, a second branch opened on the west coast. Hawkeye chaired it from a compound at Palos Verdes, California. With him were Mockingbird, Wonder Man, Tigra and Iron Man, who was then James Rhodes inside the armour, though the public did not know it.

In 1984 most of the Avengers were among the heroes the Beyonder carried off to Battleworld in the Secret Wars. Captain America led the heroes' side there. That summer the demon Nightmare broke the Hulk's mind. The Hulk smashed his way across America to New York, where he fought the city's heroes, Thor among them, through the streets and across Central Park. A family's picnic was one of the things in his way. Namor joined the team in 1985.

In 1986 Baron Helmut Zemo, Heinrich's son, led a new Masters of Evil in a siege of Avengers Mansion. They seized the mansion, wrecked it, beat Jarvis nearly to death and left Hercules in a coma. That winter, when President Reagan grounded every costumed hero in America, the order applied to the Avengers as much as to the League. In 1987 the team moved to Hydrobase, an artificial island off the coast, while the mansion was rebuilt.

In 1987 Rogers gave up the name and costume of Captain America rather than serve as the agent of the government's Commission on Superhuman Activities. The Commission gave them to John Walker. Rogers took them back in 1989, when Walker became the U.S. Agent. At the end of 1989 Hydrobase sank, and the team went back to the rebuilt mansion.

1990 to 1992

Sersi, one of the immortal Eternals, joined at the turn of 1990. Early that year Spider-Man, then a man of about forty-three, joined too, as a reserve member. In late 1991, when Odin banished Thor, the architect Eric Masterson served in his place among the Avengers, as Thor. In 1992 the team was caught up in Operation Galactic Storm, the war between the Kree and the Shi'ar that spilt over into Earth's part of space. It split over Iron Man's decision to execute the Kree Supreme Intelligence. Captain America opposed it, but it went ahead without him. The same year the Black Widow, then a woman in her early fifties, became the team's chairwoman, an office she still holds.

Crystal of the Inhumans joined in 1991.

When the Shi'ar took over the broken Kree Empire, they found Goa'uld ships on the Kree frontier and drove them off. The Avengers never saw them.

As the Cold War ended, the American charter under which the Avengers had worked was given up under a treaty between Washington and Moscow. The team took a charter from the United Nations instead. It is the accord under which the Avengers still operate. In 1992 Tony Stark, whose nervous system was failing, faked his own death. He left Rhodes a heavier suit of armour, War Machine.

In 1991 the Avengers went into space with the Justice League, under Captain America, against Thanos and the Infinity Gauntlet, on a day that was afterwards undone.

1993 and 1994

Thor came back at the end of 1992, and Odin gave Masterson an enchanted mace of his own, Thunderstrike. Thor has since been called away from Earth to command Asgard's fleet in its war with the Replicators. Masterson, as Thunderstrike, stands among the Avengers in his place. Stark returned early in 1993 but has since retired. Rhodes has kept the War Machine armour, and with it his old friend's place. Spider-Man announced his retirement at the start of the summer of 1993, at about forty-six. The west coast branch was wound up at the end of 1993.

On 30 July 1993, with Khan Noonien Singh's forces in New Delhi, the Avengers and the Justice League issued a joint statement from New York. The United Nations accord under which they operated, it said, expressly prohibited unilateral action in any ongoing conflict between sovereign states. They would act only at the request of the Security Council, and under its authority. The Council made no such request. When the coalition offensive went into India in the spring of 1994, it went without them.

On 19 August 1994 an Avengers delegation stood at the Security Council, a little apart from the League, behind Superman as he asked for leave to act in the Balkans. Captain America was there, seventy-four by the calendar, looking no more than thirty. Thunderstrike and War Machine stood beside him. He was not the team's chairman; since 1992 that office had been held by the Black Widow. By then none of the others who had made the team famous in the 1960s was on its active roster. Thor was at war among the stars. Stark had retired. The Hulk had been a fugitive for thirty years. Pym, Van Dyne, Hawkeye, Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch were no longer on active service with it.

The Council adjourned without a vote. Russia had said that it would veto any resolution sending superhumans into Serbia without Belgrade's consent. China had said that it would oppose any resolution allowing superhumans to act on a nation's soil without its government's consent.

The Avengers and the world

The Avengers were born into the Cold War, and the first of them to wear armour was made in Vietnam. At the end of 1962 Tony Stark was demonstrating his weapons to the American forces there when a booby trap wounded him. A local warlord took him prisoner, and he built the first armour to escape. James Rhodes, the Marine helicopter pilot who flew him out, became his closest friend and in time his successor. Through the 1960s the team fought communist agents and Soviet armoured men. Two of its own members, Hawkeye and the Black Widow, began on the wrong side of that struggle.

The team also reflected the struggle for civil rights. The Black Panther joined in 1968. The Falcon, a Harlem social worker who had fought beside Captain America since 1969, was made a member in 1979 by government order, when Gyrich insisted that the reduced roster must include a Black member. He served for some months and then resigned, because he would not be a token.

The Kree-Skrull War of 1971 to 1972 began as a political scandal. The Avengers had sheltered the Kree officer Captain Marvel. Senator H. Warren Craddock opened hearings of an Alien Activities Commission into the alien presence on Earth, in the manner of the investigating committees of the 1950s. When the Avengers refused to hand Captain Marvel over, Craddock turned public anger against them. Pickets gathered at the mansion. Three men who looked like Captain America, Thor and Iron Man announced that the team was disbanded; they were Skrulls. S.H.I.E.L.D., under Nick Fury, hunted Captain Marvel. The real Avengers re-formed and followed the war into space. It was ended by Rick Jones, who called up out of himself a power that the Kree Supreme Intelligence had woken in him. Craddock was revealed as a Skrull, and a mob killed him.

The Skrull impostors were three of the cows of 1961; Craddock's double was the fourth.

In 1974, the year of Watergate, Captain America was the target of the Secret Empire, a subversive organisation that planned to seize the government. It smeared him through a front called the Committee to Regain America's Principles, then framed him for murder. Rogers followed its leader, Number One, into the White House, where Number One, a man high in the American government, shot himself. Disillusioned, Rogers gave up the name for a time. He fought as Nomad, the man without a country, before taking up the shield again at the turn of 1975.

From 1977 the Avengers answered to the government through Henry Peter Gyrich, the National Security Council's liaison. Gyrich disliked superhumans. He held the team's priority clearance: its right to fly its Quinjets through American airspace, and to act with official sanction. At the turn of 1979 he cut the active roster to seven: Captain America, Iron Man, the Vision, the Scarlet Witch, the Beast, the Wasp and the Falcon. Gyrich later served on the Commission on Superhuman Activities, which in 1987 took Captain America's name away from Rogers. In the winter of 1986 to 1987 the Avengers, like every other costumed hero in America, were grounded by President Reagan's executive order.

At the end of the Cold War the team exchanged its American charter for one from the United Nations, and with it took on the limits that kept it out of the Augment War in 1993. The anger at superhumans that filled the streets outside the United Nations on the night of 19 August 1994 had older roots than Khan. One bedsheet there read HULK KILLED MY DAD, painted under a big green fist. The Hulk, a founding Avenger for a few weeks in 1963, had killed two people at a picnic in Central Park in the summer of 1984. One of them was a boy of six.

Line-ups

Founding line-up, 1963: Thor, Iron Man, the Hulk (who left within weeks), Ant-Man and the Wasp. Rick Jones and his Teen Brigade helped them.

1964 to 1965: Captain America (from early 1964). After the founders stepped down in 1965: Captain America, Hawkeye, Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch.

The later 1960s: Goliath (Pym), the Wasp, Hercules (1967), the Black Panther and the Vision (1968), the Black Knight (1969).

The 1970s: the Black Widow (1973); Mantis, the Beast and Moondragon (1976). In 1979, Gyrich's seven: Captain America, Iron Man, the Vision, the Scarlet Witch, the Beast, the Wasp and the Falcon. Ms Marvel served beside them.

The 1980s: Wonder Man, Tigra, She-Hulk, Captain Marvel (Monica Rambeau), Starfox, Namor and Doctor Druid. The west coast branch, from 1984: Hawkeye, Mockingbird, Wonder Man, Tigra and Iron Man (James Rhodes).

1990 to 1992: Sersi, Spider-Man (reserve), Rage, Quasar, Crystal and Thor (Eric Masterson), with the Black Widow as chairwoman from 1992.

1994: the Black Widow (chairwoman, in her mid-fifties), Captain America (seventy-four, looking thirty), Thunderstrike (Eric Masterson, in his thirties), War Machine (James Rhodes, in his forties), the Black Knight (Dane Whitman, in his fifties), Crystal (in her forties), Hercules (immortal) and others.

Deaths, retirements and successors: Bucky was lost in 1945. In Captain America's absence his costume was worn by William Naslund, who was killed in 1946, by Jeff Mace until 1949 and by William Burnside from 1953 to 1954. From 1987 to 1989 John Walker wore it. Pym gave up the name of Ant-Man, which passed to Scott Lang in 1979. James Rhodes wore the Iron Man armour from 1983 to 1985, and has worn War Machine since 1992; Stark has retired. Eric Masterson served as Thor from 1991 to 1992, and has carried the mace Thunderstrike since; Thor is away at war. Spider-Man retired in the summer of 1993. The Hulk left in 1963, and he has been hunted ever since.

In the saga

Book Three, Chapter Two: the Muggle news of 31 July 1993 reports a joint statement issued in New York late the night before by the Avengers and the Justice League. The statement says that the United Nations accord under which they operate expressly prohibits unilateral action in any ongoing conflict between sovereign states. They will act in India only at the request of the Security Council, and under its authority. The statement is greeted with anger in Delhi.

Book Four, Chapter Three: on the news of Saturday 20 August 1994 the Avengers stand a little apart from the Justice League at the United Nations, behind Superman, as he asks the Security Council for leave to act against Khan's forces in the Balkans. Harry notices that they look nothing like the Avengers on Dudley's old lunchbox. The man with the hammer has been replaced by a big blond man with a mace. The red and gold armour has given way to a heavier gunmetal suit bristling with guns, with a different man inside it. Only Captain America, in his blue mask with the white A, with the round shield on his back, is the same as ever. Everybody knows, Harry reflects, that they gave him something that stopped him getting any older, and he does not look a day over thirty. Spider-Man is not there; he retired the summer before, which Dudley still has not forgiven him for. Outside the United Nations that night, a protester carries a sheet reading HULK KILLED MY DAD.
