infobox: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (16 July 2005)
pages.html:
Lucius Malfoy's father, Abraxas Malfoy, held the old pure-blood prejudices of his kind, and the young Lucius learnt them from him. Lucius repeated them in the Slytherin common room, sounding exactly like his father. Abraxas is also Dracina Malfoy's grandfather, and by the family's account he was never second at anything.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, John Constantine remembered his schooldays with Lucius in Slytherin. In public Lucius always said what every other Slytherin said. Blood mattered. Some families were better than others. Muggle-borns were a pity at best, and a danger at worst. John heard him say it in the common room a hundred times, with his chin up, sounding exactly like his father. In private Lucius always said the same thing afterwards: ‘You're d-different, though, John. You know that. You're an exception.’

pages.title: The stern witch with a bun
infobox: Stern, with her hair in a bun
Took charge of the first-years at the Sorting, 1964
pages.html:
The stern witch with a bun was the member of the Hogwarts staff who took charge of the first-years on the night of the Sorting in September 1964, the year John Constantine started at the school. Her name is not recorded. She calls Minerva McGonagall to mind, but McGonagall did not join the staff until about 1970.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, John remembered waiting in a small chamber off the Entrance Hall with the rest of the first-years, thirty or forty of them, all in brand new black robes, packed in tighter than the Kop on derby day. A stern witch with her hair in a bun had told them to smarten themselves up. Then she had gone away, leaving them to frighten each other. When she came back, she led them out into the Great Hall. She lowered the Sorting Hat over John's head. It had barely touched his hair before it shouted "SLYTHERIN!"

pages.title: The twins in Constantine's compartment
pages.html:
The twins in Constantine's compartment were two Hogwarts students who shared a compartment on the Hogwarts Express with the eleven-year-old John Constantine, on his first journey to school in 1964. They had cousins in every house, so they could tell him what each house was for.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, John remembered 1964. Between the twins on the train and the older students in the corridors, he had worked it all out before he reached the castle. Gryffindor was for the brave ones, which meant the thick ones who did not know any better. Hufflepuff was for the nice ones, Slytherin for the posh ones with long family trees, Ravenclaw for the clever ones. John knew he was clever, so he had more or less made up his mind to be a Ravenclaw. The Sorting Hat put him in Slytherin almost before it touched his hair.

pages.title: The Slytherin prefect of 1964
infobox: Harry Potter and the Imprisoned Girl, Interlude
pages.html:
The Slytherin prefect of 1964 sat at the top of the Slytherin table at the start-of-term feast that September. At the pudding he asked the new boy, John Constantine, what his father was, and John's answer silenced the whole table.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, John Constantine remembered his first feast. The Sorting Hat had put him in Slytherin almost before it touched his hair. It took him until the pudding to notice the problem. The prefect at the top of the table was a tall, smooth, glossy sort of boy, with a voice like expensive cutlery. He did not know the name, so he asked what John's father was.

'A drunk,' said John. The prefect explained that he had meant what sort of wizard. 'He isn't one,' said John. 'He's a docker, when he's in work. Me mam's dead. She wasn't one either.' The laughter stopped all the way down the table.

pages.title: The Slytherin sixth-year who read Constantine's letter
infobox: Harry Potter and the Imprisoned Girl, Interlude
pages.html:
The Slytherin sixth-year who read Constantine's letter was an older boy who, in John Constantine's first term in 1964, read a letter from John's father aloud to the Slytherin table at breakfast. He never forgave John for what John did in return.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, John Constantine remembered his first weeks at Hogwarts. In the third week somebody stole the letter his dad had sent back with the school owl. A boy from the sixth year read it aloud to the Slytherin table at breakfast, doing the accent, while the whole table howled. 'Don't bother coming home at Christmas, lad,' he read. 'Nobody'll notice if you don't come home at all.'

John waited until Valentine's Day. Then he stole the boy's own love letter, a dreadful thing full of poetry, and pinned it to the noticeboard in the Entrance Hall with the girl's name in the margin. The girl laughed for a week. The boy never forgave him.

pages.title: The girl in the sixth-year's love letter
infobox: Being named in a love letter that John Constantine pinned up
pages.html:
The girl in the sixth-year's love letter was a Hogwarts student in the 1960s. A Slytherin sixth-year wrote her a dreadful love letter, full of poetry. On Valentine's Day 1965 the young John Constantine pinned it to the noticeboard in the Entrance Hall, with her name in the margin. She laughed for a week.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, John remembered his first year at Hogwarts. In the third week of term somebody stole the letter his father had sent back with the school owl, and a sixth-year boy read it aloud to the Slytherin table, doing the accent. John waited until Valentine's Day. Then he stole the boy's own love letter and pinned it up in the Entrance Hall for the whole school to read. The girl laughed for a week. The boy never forgave him.

pages.title: Augustus Rookwood
infobox: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (8 July 2000)
In Azkaban since the end of the first war
pages.html:
Augustus Rookwood is a wizard who was a Slytherin at Hogwarts in the 1960s, at the same time as John Constantine. He grew up to spy for Lord Voldemort from inside the Ministry of Magic, and he has been in Azkaban since the first war ended.

Later life

Rookwood became an Unspeakable in the Department of Mysteries. Through the first war he passed what he learnt there to the Dark Lord. After Voldemort's fall in 1981 the captured Death Eater Igor Karkaroff bought his freedom with names, and Rookwood's was one of them. He has been in Azkaban ever since.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, John Constantine remembered his first weeks in Slytherin in 1964. A boy called Rookwood shrank all of John's robes to the size of a doll's, so that John went to his first Potions lesson in his school jumper. John put an itching powder from the potions cupboard into Rookwood's underpants. Rookwood scratched for a month.

pages.title: Horace Slughorn
infobox: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (16 July 2005)
Potions master; Head of Slytherin House
pages.html:
Horace Slughorn is a wizard who taught Potions at Hogwarts for about fifty years, until he retired in 1981. He was Head of Slytherin House. He liked to gather the most promising students in the school about him, in a circle known as the Slug Club.

At Hogwarts

He is a large, comfortable wizard with a walrus moustache and a weakness for crystallised pineapple. The young Tom Riddle was among his favourites. When he retired, Severus Snape took over the Potions post.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, John Constantine remembered his first days at Hogwarts in September 1964. On his second morning he found that every one of his school robes had shrunk to the size of a doll's; a boy called Rookwood had done it. So he had to go to his first Potions lesson in his school jumper and grey flannel trousers. The whole class sniggered, while old Slughorn peered at him over his waistcoat as though he were an interesting stain.

pages.title: Apollyon Pringle
infobox: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire (8 July 2000)
pages.html:
Apollyon Pringle was the caretaker of Hogwarts before Argus Filch, known to the students as Old Pringle. Molly Weasley remembers that he once caught her and Arthur coming back to the castle in the middle of the night, when they were at school.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, John Constantine remembered how his feud with Lucius Malfoy came to blows in March 1971, their seventh year. Lucius had wanted a Ravenclaw girl who was going out with John. One night, in an empty corridor on the fourth floor, he stepped out in front of John with his wand drawn and called him a Mudblood. It began as a duel, a nasty one. It ended with both their wands across the corridor, while the two of them rolled about on the flagstones punching each other in the face.

Old Pringle, the caretaker, found them at last, both bloody, both still swinging. He had them by the collars, one in each fist, when Lucius spat blood on to the flagstones. "On my b-blood, Constantine," Lucius said. "You'll p-pay for this. Every drop."

pages.title: The Ravenclaw girl Constantine loved
infobox: Harry Potter and the Imprisoned Girl, Interlude
A laugh you could hear across the Great Hall
pages.html:
The Ravenclaw girl Constantine loved was a Hogwarts student with a laugh you could hear across the Great Hall. She went out with John Constantine in his seventh year, 1970 to 1971. Lucius Malfoy wanted her too, and it was over her that the two boys fought their duel.

The duel

One night in March 1971, in an empty corridor on the fourth floor, Lucius stepped out in front of John with his wand drawn. 'She's too good for you,' he said. 'You know she is. She's too good for a M-Mudblood.'

The duel ended with both boys rolling about on the flagstones, punching each other in the face, until Pringle the caretaker took them by the collars. Each swore on his blood that the other would pay. Neither ever took it back.

Afterwards

She chucked John anyway, a month after they left school. He had been in love with her, or thought he was, and had written her a letter about it that he still blushed to remember. These days he calls it puppy love.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, riding the Knight Bus in August 1993, John Constantine remembered her, though not by name.

pages.title: Ephraim Shacklewell's father
infobox: Selling a scouring potion to Arizona copper mines as a miracle cleaning fluid
pages.html:
Ephraim Shacklewell's father, an American pure-blood wizard, made the Shacklewell family's fortune in the 1960s. He sold a scouring potion to the copper mines of Arizona, through a string of front companies, as a miracle cleaning fluid. Nobody at the Magical Congress of the United States of America ever quite managed to prove it.

The fortune

The Shacklewells had been in America for generations, but for most of that time they had not been rich. His chance came after 1965, when MACUSA at last did away with Rappaport's Law, which had forbidden American wizards almost any dealings with No-Majs. His son Ephraim has since spent the money on Shacklewell House in New Mexico, on its swimming pool and on the most expensive wards that MACUSA's own security men could be bribed into building.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, John Constantine knew the whole story of the money. He had done his reading on the family before he broke into Shacklewell House in August 1993.

pages.title: The first Shacklewell in America
infobox: A wand, and a price on his head
pages.html:
The first Shacklewell in America was Ephraim Shacklewell's great-great-grandfather. He stepped off a ship in Boston with a wand in his pocket and a price on his head. The American Shacklewells all descend from him.

History

What he had done to earn the price, and who had set it, is not recorded. Nor is the year he landed. He was a pure-blood, like every Shacklewell after him. For most of the years since, the family was not rich. The money came only in the 1960s, when his great-grandson, Ephraim's father, sold a scouring potion to the copper mines of Arizona.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, in August 1993, John Constantine went over the family's history in his head as he looked at Shacklewell House from the road, on the night he broke into it.

pages.title: The digger who sold the Myst book
infobox: Digger on the excavation at the Cleft, New Mexico
The Linking Book to Myst Island, for fifty dollars
pages.html:
The digger who sold the Myst book was a man working on the excavation at the Cleft, in New Mexico. He came by the Linking Book to Myst Island there and sold it to the wizard Ephraim Shacklewell for fifty dollars. Neither the hole nor anything in it belonged to him.

The sale

Shacklewell kept the book in a glass case next to a hubcap, because it had a pretty picture in it that moved.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, in August 1993, John Constantine took the book from Shacklewell House for Albus Dumbledore. When John said that Shacklewell had paid for it fair and square, Dumbledore's answer was about the digger. 'He paid fifty dollars to a man who dug it out of a hole in the ground,' said Dumbledore. 'The hole did not belong to that man. Neither did anything he found in it.'

pages.title: The demon that fed on light
pages.html:
The demon that fed on light was a very old, very powerful demon that threatened the world in 1985. John Constantine beat it with the Deluminator he had stolen from Albus Dumbledore, and put it away where it would not trouble anyone for a thousand years.

History

The demon turned up in 1985. It was large and very old. It fed on light the way some things feed on fear, and it threatened to take the world's light for itself.

To beat it Constantine needed something that could take the light away from it first. He knew of only one such object: the Deluminator belonging to the Headmaster of Hogwarts, a device like a silver cigarette lighter which, with one click, draws every light in a street into itself. He took it out of Dumbledore's own pocket at a Ministry dinner, which he gatecrashed for the purpose. With it he defeated the demon, and shut it away somewhere it would not trouble anybody for a thousand years. He gave the Deluminator back the next week, scorched on one side.

Consequences

Constantine tried to apologise to Dumbledore in the back room of the Hog's Head, with a goat looking in at the window. Dumbledore let him get about three words out, then shouted him down, in language Constantine would not have thought a headmaster knew. He promised to turn Constantine's liver into a pair of slippers. Until the summer of 1993 it was the only time Constantine had ever seen him angry.

He did not quite hex him. Instead he put the matter away, like a good cheque saved for a rainy day. Years later he wrote to Constantine that he thought of him often, and of his Deluminator too.

In the saga

Constantine remembered the affair in August 1993, on his way to Hogwarts with a D'ni book for Dumbledore. He had needed that book even more badly than he had once needed the Deluminator. The last time, he reflected, only the world had been at stake; this time it was him.

In the Headmaster's office Constantine accused Dumbledore of sending him, out of spite, on a job that could easily have got him killed. For a moment Dumbledore's face changed into the one Constantine had seen in the Hog's Head. Later in the same interview Constantine complained of the old grudge to his face: 'Eight years you've had a cob on with me over a ciggy lighter.'

pages.title: The Duke of Hell from Soho
infobox: Harry Potter and the Imprisoned Girl, Interlude
Across a card table in Soho, London
pages.html:
The Duke of Hell from Soho is one of the infernal dukes who serve the Devil. He once sat down to cards with John Constantine in Soho, and lost his shirt.

Rank

Dukes are among the high lords of Hell, although every one of them ranks below the First of the Fallen.

In the saga

In the Interlude of Book Three, in August 1993, John Constantine looked at Stan Shunpike, the conductor of the Knight Bus, over an unlit cigarette. It was the same look he had once given a Duke of Hell across a card table in Soho, shortly before the Duke lost his shirt.

pages.title: Andromalius
infobox: Ars Goetia, in The Lesser Key of Solomon (seventeenth century)
A man holding a great serpent
pages.html:
Andromalius is a Great Earl of Hell, the seventy-second and last of the spirits named in the old grimoire of Solomon. He appears as a man with a great serpent in his hand. His particular talent is the catching of thieves and the return of stolen property. He also uncovers wickedness, underhand dealing and hidden treasure.

Rank

Andromalius commands thirty-six legions of spirits. Like every lord of Hell, he serves the Devil, the First of the Fallen, and ranks far below him.

In the saga

In the Interlude of Book Three, in August 1993, John Constantine broke into Shacklewell House in New Mexico. He drew the seal of Andromalius in chalk over the strongest line of the wards, then pricked his thumb and went over the chalk in his own blood. As far as the wards were concerned, he was now the household's own thieftaker. John thought there was a certain poetry in that.

pages.title: The three claimants to Constantine's soul
aliases: the First, the Second and the Third of the Fallen
infobox: The First of the Fallen; the Second of the Fallen; the Third of the Fallen
Each believes John Constantine's soul is his alone
pages.html:
The three claimants to Constantine's soul are the three lords of Hell who, in 1993, each believed that John Constantine's soul belonged to him alone. They are the First of the Fallen, who is the Devil, the Second of the Fallen and the Third. Every one of them knows about the other two, so none can collect without starting a war in Hell. That is the only reason John is still alive.

The three

The First of the Fallen is the Devil himself, the first angel to rebel, who has also gone by the names of Lucifer, Satan, Morgoth and Mephisto. The Second and the Third of the Fallen are lesser lords, who shared the rule of Hell with him. The Third is a shape-changer called the Lord of a Billion Faces.

The bargain

In 1991 John Constantine was dying of lung cancer, and the First of the Fallen, who bore him a grudge, was waiting for him. John sold his soul to the Second and to the Third, separately, then cut his wrists. When the First came to collect him, the other two arrived to claim their purchase. A war among the three over a single soul would have torn Hell apart. So the First healed John's cancer and let him live.

The arrangement still held in August 1993. The claimants watch one another, and they watch John. He knows that any of them would take him the moment the balance shifted.

In the saga

Riding the Knight Bus north in August 1993, John reflected that he had better enemies than Lucius Malfoy, and far bigger ones. Three of them were each under the firm impression that his soul belonged to them alone. Every one of them knew about the other two, which was the only reason he was still breathing.

pages.title: The cardinal who lied to Constantine
infobox: Lying to John Constantine, rather well
pages.html:
The cardinal who lied to Constantine is a prince of the Church, and one of the many liars John Constantine has met in his line of work. Whatever the lie was, he told it better than Harry Potter told his on the Knight Bus.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, in the summer of 1993, Constantine was riding the Knight Bus on the night Harry Potter ran away from Privet Drive. When Stan Shunpike asked about the mark on Harry's forehead, Harry said quickly that he had fallen over when he was six. John closed his eyes in pain. It was the worst lie he had heard in a month. He had been lied to by the police, by a cardinal, by three separate demons, by the Devil himself and by a man who sold second-hand cars in Croydon. Every one of them had made a better job of it.

pages.title: The Croydon car salesman
infobox: Lying to John Constantine, rather well
pages.html:
The Croydon car salesman is a man who sold second-hand cars in Croydon, and one of the many liars John Constantine has met. Whatever he told Constantine, he made a better job of it than Harry Potter did on the Knight Bus.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, in the summer of 1993, Constantine heard Harry tell Stan Shunpike that he had got the mark on his forehead falling over when he was six. It was the worst lie Constantine had heard in a month. He had been lied to by the police, by a cardinal, by three separate demons and by the Devil himself, as well as by the man from Croydon. Every one of them had made a better job of it.

pages.title: Death of the Endless
infobox: Death; Death herself; Mistress Death; Lady Death; Didi
Captain Marvel #26 (June 1973), as Mistress Death; The Sandman #8 (August 1989), as Death of the Endless
One of the Endless; the embodiment of death
Destiny, Dream, Destruction, Desire, Despair and Delirium
A pale young woman in black with an ankh at her throat; to some, a hooded woman of bone
Thanos, the Mad Titan, who has courted her all his life
pages.html:
Death is the second eldest of the Endless, the seven beings who embody what the living world is made of. She is death itself. She meets every living thing at the end of its life and takes it on to whatever comes next. Most of those who see her find a pale, cheerful young woman in black, with an ankh at her throat. To the cosmic powers, and to Thanos, the Mad Titan, she has shown herself as a hooded woman of bone. They are the same lady. Thanos has loved her for most of his life. In 1982 she came in person for a dying hero, and once in every hundred years she lives a single day as a mortal.

The Endless

The Endless are a family of seven, older than the gods: Destiny, Death, Dream, Destruction, Desire, Despair and Delirium. Each of them is the thing they are named for, and each keeps a realm of their own. Death is the second of them, after Destiny, and much the steadiest. She is kind, practical and funny. She has no patience with self-pity, least of all her brother Dream's.

In 1916 an English occultist called Roderick Burgess tried to capture Death, so that he would never have to die himself. He caught Dream instead, and kept him in a glass prison for seventy-two years. All that time the world went without the proper keeper of its sleep, and a sleeping sickness spread across it. Dream escaped in 1988. Afterwards Death found him sulking in a park. She walked him through a day of her work, and by the end of it he understood what he still had.

The one face and the other

Death wears whatever face suits the one she has come for. The Endless know the pale girl in black. The cosmic powers know the hooded woman of bone who rules the realm of the dead beyond the stars. Those who have met both seldom compare notes, and for a long time the heroes of the world believed there were two Deaths. There has only ever been one.

Thanos

Thanos, the Mad Titan, fell in love with Death as a young man, and he has spent his life trying to win her. He has offered her worlds. Over 1973 and 1974 he went to war for the Cosmic Cube for her sake. Captain Mar-Vell and the Avengers stopped him. She has never once returned his love.

In 1982 Mar-Vell, the Kree warrior who had become Earth's Captain Marvel, lay dying of cancer. Death came for him in person. With her came Thanos, who had died himself in 1977, as her servant, to lead the man who had beaten him into her keeping.

At the end of 1989 Death raised Thanos from the dead to put right the balance between the living and the dead. In 1991 he gathered the six Infinity Gems. To prove his devotion to her, he snuffed out half of all life in the universe with a snap of his fingers. She still would not have him. The deed was undone soon afterwards and the lost came back, so that almost nobody now remembers it ever happened.

A day among the living

Once in every hundred years Death takes on mortal flesh and lives a single day as a human being, so that she will know what it is she takes from people. In 1993 she spent hers in New York as a sixteen-year-old girl who called herself Didi. At the end of it she died, as every mortal does.

In the saga

In the summer of 1993 John Constantine reflected that he had looked Death herself in the eye. He thought her a lovely girl, all things considered, who had always been nice to him. All the same, he knew she would come for him in the end, and that he was a long way overdue. He also knew that an enormous purple alien, quite mad, had been mooning after her for longer than John had been alive, writing her very bad poetry.

pages.title: Thanos
infobox: Death of the Endless object of devotion
Eternal of Titan, born with the Deviant syndrome
pages.html:
Thanos, the Mad Titan, is an enormous purple-skinned conqueror born on Titan, the moon of Saturn. He has been in love with Death of the Endless for almost the whole of his life. More than once he has tried to wipe out life across the universe as an offering to her. John Constantine, who knows Death, thinks of him as the mad purple alien who has been mooning after her for longer than John has been alive, writing her very bad poetry.

Life

Thanos was born on Titan to the Eternals A'Lars and Sui-San. He had the grey-purple skin and massive frame of a Deviant, which made him a stranger among his own people. As a young man he fell in love with Death, and he has been trying to win her ever since. He killed most of the people of Titan, then turned to conquest among the stars.

He first came to notice on Earth at the end of 1972. In 1973 he seized the Cosmic Cube, which made him very nearly all-powerful until the Kree warrior Captain Mar-Vell broke its power. Darkseid, the Lord of Apokolips, had wanted the Cube for himself, and the two of them have been enemies ever since. In 1977 Thanos gathered the Soul Gems to snuff out the stars, and was turned to stone by Adam Warlock. That was not the last of him. When Mar-Vell lay dying of cancer in 1982, it was Thanos who came for his old enemy at the end, to lead him to Death.

The Infinity Gauntlet

At the end of 1989 Death herself brought Thanos back to life, to restore the balance between the living and the dead. In 1991 he gathered all six Infinity Gems into a single gauntlet, which made him master of the universe. Then, to please her, he wiped out half of all living things with a gesture.

Earth's heroes fought him, as did the cosmic powers. His granddaughter Nebula seized the gauntlet from him and undid the day, so that almost nobody remembers it. Thanos afterwards withdrew to a quiet life on a distant world, and he has since been seen fighting on the side of the heroes more than once. Death has never returned his love.

Darkseid

Thanos's bitterest enemy is Darkseid, the Lord of Apokolips. Their feud began in 1973, when Darkseid sent his son Kalibak to take the Cosmic Cube from him; Thanos broke Kalibak's jaw, and lost the Cube to Mar-Vell in the confusion. Each has blamed the other ever since.

In 1977 Darkseid helped the heroes bring Thanos down, so that he could steal the Soul Gems from the wreck. In 1990 the two raced each other for the Infinity Gems, and Thanos won every race. In 1991, wearing the Infinity Gauntlet, Thanos turned Darkseid into a statue of glass, which he called a fair exchange for his own years as stone. Apokolips believes he showed Doomsday the way there in 1994. He has never troubled to deny it.

In the saga

Book Three, Interlude: in 1993 John Constantine reflects that he has looked Death herself in the eye. She is a lovely girl, all things considered, and has always been quite nice to him, but she has shocking taste in admirers: an enormous purple alien, quite mad, who has been mooning after her for longer than John has been alive, writing her very bad poetry.

pages.title: Victor von Doom
infobox: Doom; Doctor Doom; Victor Von Doom
In a Romani camp near Haasenstadt, Latveria
Reed Richards and the Fantastic Four
pages.html:
Victor von Doom is the armoured absolute ruler of Latveria, a small country in the Balkans. He is a scientific genius, a sorcerer and the oldest enemy of the Fantastic Four. John Constantine counts him as one of at most three people alive who could have broken into Shacklewell House in 1993 the way Constantine did, though Doom would never have bothered.

Life

Doom was born among the Romani of Latveria. His mother, Cynthia, was a witch who sold her soul for power to Mephisto, one of the many faces of the Devil. She died when Victor was a small boy. His father, a healer, died fleeing the soldiers of the local baron. The boy found his mother's books of magic and taught himself from them.

As a young man his gift for science won him a scholarship to a university in New York, where he met Reed Richards and despised him. A machine he built to reach his mother's soul blew up in his face and scarred him. He was expelled.

He travelled to Tibet and studied with a hidden order of monks, who forged him a suit of armour. He put on its mask before it had cooled, and he has hidden his ruined face behind it ever since. He went home to Latveria, overthrew its rulers and made himself monarch. In 1962 he came to public notice attacking Richards and the Fantastic Four in New York.

In the Secret Wars of 1984 he stole the power of the Beyonder himself for a time, before it was taken back. In 1989 he went down into Hell with Doctor Stephen Strange, and at last won his mother's soul back from Mephisto.

Abilities

Doom is one of the very few people in the world who have both a wizard's innate magic and a lifetime's learning in the occult. Fewer still have the skill to make each do what the other cannot. He is also among the greatest scientists alive, the inventor of time machines and of robot doubles, so that nobody facing Doom can ever be entirely sure that it is Doom. His armour makes him the equal in a fight of most superhumans.

He rules Latveria with absolute authority. His diplomatic immunity has kept him out of every courtroom in the world.

In the saga

Book Three, Interlude: as he prepares to break into Shacklewell House in New Mexico to recover a book for Albus Dumbledore, John Constantine reflects that there are three people at the very most who could walk into the house that night. One is Victor von Doom, who would never have bothered. The others are Stephen Strange and Constantine himself. Doctor Fate does not count, on account of his helmet having been asleep for a while.

pages.title: Stephen Strange
aliases: the Master of the Mystic Arts
infobox: The Sanctum Sanctorum, 177A Bleecker Street, Greenwich Village, New York
pages.html:
Stephen Strange, known as Doctor Strange, is the Sorcerer Supreme: a former surgeon who became Earth's foremost defender against threats from other dimensions. John Constantine counts him as one of at most three people with enough innate magic and occult learning to have broken into Shacklewell House as Constantine did, though Strange would never have stooped to it.

Life

Strange was a brilliant, wealthy, arrogant neurosurgeon in New York until a car crash damaged the nerves of his hands so badly that he could never operate again. He spent his fortune on cures that failed. At last he travelled to the Himalayas to look for the Ancient One, a sorcerer who was said to be able to heal anything. The old man would not heal him, but he took him as a pupil, and Strange learnt humility along with the mystic arts. He foiled a plot against his teacher's life by the treacherous disciple Baron Mordo, who has been his enemy ever since.

Back in New York, he set up house in the Sanctum Sanctorum on Bleecker Street, in Greenwich Village, with his friend and manservant, Wong. The wider world first heard of him in 1963. When the Ancient One died in 1974, Strange succeeded him as Sorcerer Supreme, the chief guardian of the Earth against magical attack. He has fought the dread Dormammu and many other powers from beyond. He has also loved Clea, who is Dormammu's niece, which has done nothing to improve his relations with her uncle.

Abilities and associations

Strange is one of the very few people alive who have both a wizard's innate magic and a lifetime's learning in the occult. Fewer still have the skill to make each do what the other cannot. He carries the Eye of Agamotto, an amulet whose light reveals the truth, and he wears the Cloak of Levitation.

In 1971 he founded the loose band of heroes called the Defenders, with the Hulk and the Sub-Mariner. In 1984 it was Strange who finally banished the rampaging Hulk from New York into another dimension. In 1989 he went down into Hell with Victor von Doom, to free the soul of Doom's mother from Mephisto.

In the saga

Book Three, Interlude: preparing in 1993 to break into Shacklewell House in New Mexico, John Constantine reflects that only three people at the most could walk into that house unseen. One is Victor von Doom, who would never have bothered. One is Stephen Strange, who would never have stooped to it. The third is Constantine himself. Doctor Fate does not count, on account of his helmet having been asleep for a while.

pages.title: Doctor Fate
infobox: The Helmet of Fate; the Amulet of Anubis; the cloak
Kent and Inza Nelson aged and retired; the helmet, amulet and cloak scattered in Zero Hour
pages.html:
Doctor Fate is the sorcerer of the golden helmet, champion of Nabu, an ancient Lord of Order. He first appeared in 1940 in the person of Kent Nelson, and was one of the founders of the Justice Society. By 1993 the helmet had been asleep for some while, which is why John Constantine did not count Doctor Fate among the few who could have robbed Shacklewell House. In July 1994, during Zero Hour, the time-mad Extant aged Kent and Inza Nelson to their true years. He tore them from the power of Fate, scattering the helmet, amulet and cloak.

Kent Nelson

In 1920 a twelve-year-old American boy, Kent Nelson, was exploring the Valley of Ur in Mesopotamia with his father, the archaeologist Sven Nelson. There he opened the tomb of Nabu, a sorcerer of Babylon and an agent of the Lords of Order. The gas that came out of the tomb killed his father. Nabu raised the orphan and taught him the arts of order. He gave him a golden helmet, an amulet and a cloak. In 1940 Kent Nelson came to public notice as Doctor Fate.

Late in 1940 he was one of the founders of the Justice Society. For decades he was the most powerful sorcerer among the world's heroes. Nabu's power kept him young long past his natural span, and his wife, Inza, with him.

The helmet after 1987

Doctor Fate joined the new Justice League in 1987. That same year Kent Nelson's long service came to an end, and he was struck down. For a time the helmet passed to new hosts: Eric Strauss and his stepmother Linda, who joined to become Doctor Fate together. Both of them died. In 1991 Kent and Inza Nelson came back to life in younger bodies. This time it was Inza who took up the work of Fate.

By 1993 Nabu's helmet had gone quiet, and among those who know about such things it was said to be asleep.

In July 1994, at Vanishing Point during Zero Hour, Extant aged Kent and Inza Nelson to their true years in a matter of moments. He tore them from Nabu's power as well. The helmet, the amulet of Anubis and the cloak were scattered. The Nelsons, old at last, have retired.

In the saga

In 1993, while he was robbing Shacklewell House in New Mexico, John Constantine reckoned that three people at the very most could have done it his way, by joining real wizardry to old occultism. They were Victor von Doom, who would never have bothered; Stephen Strange, who would never have stooped to it; and himself. Dr Fate, he decided, did not count, on account of that helmet being asleep for a while.

pages.title: Magneto
aliases: The mutant on the space station
infobox: The mutant on the space station; Max Eisenhardt; Erik Lehnsherr
Command of magnetism and the electromagnetic spectrum
Brotherhood of Evil Mutants; the Acolytes
Asteroid M; later the space station Avalon
pages.html:
Magneto is the most famous and most feared mutant in the world. He survived the Nazi death camps, and came out of them convinced that mutants must rule rather than be hunted. In August 1993, from his space station Avalon, he answered a United Nations measure against him with a pulse that blacked out the whole planet. People died all over the world, among them eleven patients on one floor of Bellevue Hospital in New York.

Early life

Magneto was born Max Eisenhardt, to a Jewish family in Germany. As a boy he was sent with his family to the Warsaw Ghetto, and then to Auschwitz. His parents and his sister died there, but he survived.

After the war he married a Romani survivor, Magda, and they had a daughter, Anya. Anya died in a fire while a mob held her father back. In his grief his power broke loose and killed the mob. Magda fled from him in horror. Afterwards he lived under the name Erik Lehnsherr.

In the 1950s he worked in a hospital in Haifa among survivors of the camps. There he met a young telepath, Charles Xavier, and the two became friends. They argued for nights on end about what humanity would do to mutants once it knew of them. Xavier believed in peace. Lehnsherr had seen what people did to those they feared, and he did not.

The war with mankind

Magneto came to public notice in 1963, when he seized the American missile base at Cape Citadel. Xavier's new team, the X-Men, drove him off. In 1964 he gathered the Brotherhood of Evil Mutants. Among its members were his own twin children, though none of them knew it then. Pietro was Quicksilver and Wanda the Scarlet Witch. He built an orbiting fortress, Asteroid M.

In 1984 he was among those taken to Battleworld in the Secret Wars, where at first he stood with the heroes. In 1985 he gave himself up to stand trial before an international court in Paris. While Xavier was away from Earth, Magneto ran Xavier's school. It did not last. By 1991 he had broken with the X-Men again and was gathering a band of devoted followers, the Acolytes.

In 1974 his son Pietro, Quicksilver, married Crystal of the Inhumans.

Avalon and the blackout

In 1993 Magneto built a new refuge for mutants in orbit, the space station Avalon. In August the United Nations Security Council answered by switching on the Magneto Protocols, a field round the Earth that stopped him using his powers on the planet's surface. He replied with an electromagnetic pulse that shut down electrical power over the entire world in a single night. Lights, monitors and ventilators failed all at once, together with the generators meant to back them up. People died wherever their lives depended on machines.

When the X-Men went up to Avalon, he tore the adamantium out of Wolverine's skeleton. Xavier then went into Magneto's mind and shut it down, leaving him in a coma. Nothing has been heard from him since. To the public his name still stands for mutant terror.

In the saga

Book Three, Chapter Eighteen: in the Shrieking Shack in June 1994, Sirius Black insists that the witnesses to Peter Pettigrew's death did not see what they thought they saw. Harry answers sarcastically that they thought they saw a mutant attack, 'Bloody Magneto or whoever it is nowadays'.

Book Four, Chapter Three: at the protest outside the United Nations in August 1994, a young nurse describes the blackout of the previous August. She was in intensive care at Bellevue that night when the lights, the monitors, the ventilators and the generators all went off together. With two other nurses she bagged the patients by hand in the dark, all night. They lost eleven people on her floor. That, she says, was one mutant: one man, up in a space station, having a tantrum. Harry, at the Leaky Cauldron, slept straight through it.

pages.title: Atrus
aliases: the writer of the Myst book
infobox:
Albus Dumbledore correspondent
Achenar son
Sirrus son
Catherine wife
Yeesha daughter
The Cleft, New Mexico, after the Fall of D'ni
pages.html:
Atrus is a Writer of the D'ni Art and one of the last of his people. He wrote the linking book for Myst Island, and the small leather book that carried Harry Potter's party home from it. He was born in the Cleft, in the New Mexico desert, after the Fall of D'ni. He has been writing books that link to other worlds for longer than Albus Dumbledore has been alive. Dumbledore, who calls him a very old acquaintance, has exchanged letters with him about the Art.

Birth and childhood

Atrus was the son of Gehn, who was the son of Anna and the D'ni Aitrus. His mother, Keta, was a woman of the surface. Keta fell gravely ill while she was carrying him. Gehn brought her to his mother in the Cleft, the fissure beside an old volcano where Anna had made her home after the Fall, but Anna could not save her. Keta died giving birth, and Gehn went away without naming the child. Anna named him after his grandfather and raised him herself.

He grew up in the Cleft, where his grandmother taught him to watch, to measure and to reason. From her, too, he learnt to love the desert and the rock. He knew nothing of D'ni beyond her stories until he was about fourteen, when his father came back for him.

Gehn and Riven

Gehn took Atrus down into the ruined city and taught him the Art. Atrus was awed at first, then horrified. Gehn believed that a Writer created the worlds he wrote, and owned them. He used the peoples of his Ages as he pleased. When Atrus wrote his first Age, Gehn destroyed it because it did not suit him. When Atrus tried to escape, Gehn shut him in a locked chamber with only one way out, to Gehn's Fifth Age, Riven, a broken world whose people Gehn ruled as a god.

On Riven Atrus met Catherine, a woman of that Age, and fell in love with her. With Catherine, and with Anna's help, he stranded Gehn on Riven by destroying every linking book out of it. Atrus escaped by leaping into the Star Fissure, a rift in Riven that opened on a starry sky, and linked to Myst Island as he fell. His Myst linking book went on falling. He had meant it to be destroyed in the fissure. He never stopped wondering whose hands might one day hold it.

Myst and his sons

Atrus and Catherine made their home on Myst Island, an Age Anna had written as a refuge for the family. There they raised two sons, Sirrus and Achenar. From the island's library Atrus wrote and visited Age after Age, taking his sons with him. As they grew, they began to plunder his Ages for riches and power, ruining the peoples of some of them.

Early in the nineteenth century the brothers turned on their parents. They took Catherine to Riven, where Gehn held her prisoner. They stranded Atrus in D'ni by tearing a page out of the book that would have brought him home.

A traveller from the surface, remembered only as the Stranger, then found Atrus's lost Myst book and came to the island. He refused both brothers, found the missing page and took it to Atrus. Atrus came home to Myst and dealt with his sons. He wrote the Stranger a small leather linking book to take him home, and in 1806 he sent him to Riven with a prison book. There the Stranger freed Catherine and trapped Gehn. Atrus and Catherine left Riven as it began to fall apart. The Stranger himself went home through the Star Fissure, without ever using Atrus's book.

Later life

Atrus and Catherine made a new home on the Age of Tomahna, where their daughter Yeesha was born in 1815. Atrus wrote the Age of Releeshahn as a home for the D'ni survivors he had found. In 1816 Saavedro, a man of an Age the brothers had ruined, stole the Releeshahn book in revenge, and the Stranger came back to recover it. Some ten years later Atrus let his sons out of the separate prison Ages in which he had held them for twenty years. Sirrus kidnapped Yeesha, and both brothers were dead before she was safe.

Atrus grew very old. He mourned his sons, and in time his wife, while he worked on towards the restoration of D'ni. Being of D'ni descent he has lived far longer than any surface man. He is alive in the twentieth century, and still writing.

Character

Atrus holds to the old D'ni teaching that a Writer describes worlds that already exist, and has no right to rule them. He is patient, precise and courteous. He is slow to trust and slower still to condemn: even his sons he imprisoned rather than killed. Dumbledore admits that his own letters to Atrus have been rather long. The replies have been short and very courteous, in a far steadier hand than Dumbledore's.

In the saga

Book Three: Atrus never appears. In the summer of 1993 Dumbledore told John Constantine that the Myst book had been written by a very old acquaintance, to whom it belonged, and that its owner would be extremely glad to know it was safe. The two of them had exchanged a few letters about the Art. Dumbledore meant to return both books to him: 'One way there and one way home.'

In the hospital wing in June 1994 Dumbledore gave Harry the small leather book. It had been written, he said, by a very old acquaintance, a great deal older than Dumbledore himself. On Myst, after Harry had gone, the woman Sirius had met there picked up the small book. She knew it at once as her father's.

Book Four: in the summer of 1994 Hermione played the Muggle game Myst to all four endings. In the game the island belongs to Atrus, whose journals are found in the library and who writes books linking to worlds he calls Ages. His sons have trapped him in an Age he cannot leave, because a page is missing from his book. If the player brings it, he comes back to deal with his sons. He says that his wife, Catherine, is held prisoner in another world. In one ending he says 'Welcome to D'ni'. After that Hermione was nearly certain that he was D'ni, although Anna's journal never mentions anybody called Atrus.

In their own words

Welcome to D'ni.Atrus (in the game Myst) · B4 Ch2

pages.title: The Stranger
infobox: Freeing Atrus; rescuing Catherine and imprisoning Gehn on Riven, 1806
The small leather linking book, handed down in his family
pages.html:
The Stranger is the traveller from the surface who found Atrus's lost Myst linking book early in the nineteenth century. He freed Atrus from the trap his sons had laid for him. In 1806 he rescued Catherine from Riven and imprisoned Gehn there. Atrus wrote him the small leather linking book to take him home from Myst Island. He never used it, and it came down through his family to Albus Dumbledore.

Myst

Nothing is recorded of the Stranger before the day he found a book with a moving picture in it. He laid his hand on the picture and arrived on the wooden dock of Myst Island, out of nowhere, with nothing in his hands at all. The island was empty. He worked his way through its machines and its Ages. In the library he found Atrus's sons trapped in two books, Sirrus in a red one and Achenar in a blue. Each begged for his missing pages; each blamed the other. He believed neither. He found the page Atrus needed and took it to him in D'ni. Atrus came home and dealt with his sons.

For that very great service Atrus wrote him a small linking book, no bigger than a pocket diary, to lead from the island back to his own world and take him home.

Riven

Atrus asked one more thing of him. In 1806 he sent the Stranger to Riven, Gehn's broken Fifth Age, with a prison book disguised as a linking book. The Stranger freed Catherine, tricked Gehn into the prison book and signalled Atrus, who came for his wife. As Riven began to break apart, the Stranger, who had no book out of the Age, threw himself into the Star Fissure, the rift that opens on a starry sky. He fell through it into his own world. It was a rather more alarming road home than the one Atrus had written for him.

Later life

The Stranger kept Atrus's little book all the same. He came back to help Atrus's family more than once. In 1816 he recovered the book of Releeshahn after Saavedro stole it from Tomahna. Some ten years later he helped to save Atrus's daughter Yeesha from her brother Sirrus. The little book stayed with his family after him. It was handed down for a great many years, from one person who did not know what it was to the next, until at last it came to Dumbledore.

In the saga

Book 3: In the summer of 1993 Dumbledore told John Constantine about the small leather book. It had been written long ago, he said, for a traveller who had done its writer a very great service, and it led from his island back to this world. The traveller had never used it, having found his way home by another road entirely, a rather more alarming one. People do keep things, Dumbledore said.

In June 1994 Harry Potter stood, without knowing it, on the very planks of the dock on Myst where that traveller had once arrived. The traveller had wondered, exactly as Harry did, where on earth he was. After Harry had gone home by the little book, Yeesha picked it up and knew it. Her father had written it for a stranger who had done him a very great service, and it had been lost to him for longer than she had been alive.

pages.title: Remus Lupin's parents
infobox: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (8 July 1999)
Lyall Lupin, a wizard; an authority on Boggarts, poltergeists and other non-human spirits
Hope Lupin, born Hope Howell, a Muggle
pages.html:
Remus Lupin's parents were Lyall Lupin, a wizard, and Hope Howell, a Muggle. Their only son was bitten as a very small boy by Fenrir Greyback, which made him a Garou. They tried everything they could think of to help him. In those days there was no cure.

The bite

Lyall was an authority on Boggarts, poltergeists and other non-human spirits. In the 1960s he questioned Greyback at a hearing of the Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures, where Greyback passed himself off as a Muggle vagrant. Lyall told the hearing that werewolves were soulless, evil things, fit for nothing but death. Greyback took his revenge on Lyall's son. He found the boy asleep in his bed, and bit him.

Afterwards

His parents could not cure him, and the Wolfsbane Potion was not discovered until long afterwards. When he went to Hogwarts, Remus told his friends that his mother was ill.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Eighteen, in the Shrieking Shack, Lupin told Harry Potter, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger how it had all begun. He had been a very small boy when he was bitten. His parents had tried everything, but in those days there was no cure.

pages.title: The Shropshire Muggle-baiter
infobox: Harry Potter and the Imprisoned Girl, Chapter Eighteen
Nine hours, of a fifteenth-century blood-boiling curse
pages.html:
The Shropshire Muggle-baiter was a wizard who tormented Muggles for sport, and who died of a fifteenth-century curse that boils the blood, starting at the feet. It took him nine hours. He was awake for every one of them.

Record

His death is recorded in a footnote to Moste Potente Potions, the potion book kept in the Restricted Section of the Hogwarts library. The footnote does not give his name.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Eighteen, on the night of 6 June 1994, Hermione Granger told everybody in the Shrieking Shack, brightly, about the slow killing spells she knew, for the benefit of Peter Pettigrew. One was a fifteenth-century curse in a footnote to Moste Potente Potions, which she had taken out of the Restricted Section for the Polyjuice Potion. It boiled the blood, starting at the feet. The footnote said that a Muggle-baiter in Shropshire took nine hours to die of it, and that he was awake for every one of them.

Pettigrew had already made a faint gurgling noise behind his gag. ‘Everybody likes her,’ said Harry, ‘until she gets to the footnotes.’

pages.title: John Constantine's old parish priest
infobox: In Liverpool, where John Constantine grew up
pages.html:
John Constantine's old parish priest was the priest of the Liverpool parish where Constantine grew up. Constantine left the faith long ago. He would still not have wanted his priest to hear what he did at the door of Shacklewell House in August 1993.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, Constantine broke into Shacklewell House in New Mexico. He turned his back on the front door and walked in backwards, reciting the Lord's Prayer backwards under his breath, from Amen to Father. Wards look very hard at the people coming in, and hardly ever at the ones they think are going out. It worked. It was also a thing he would not have wanted his old parish priest to hear.

pages.title: West Tower
infobox: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (8 July 1999)
pages.html:
The West Tower is one of the towers of Hogwarts. Professor Flitwick's office is on its seventh floor, a small study crammed with books from floor to ceiling, behind the thirteenth window from the right.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty, in June 1994, Sirius Black was locked in Flitwick's office to wait for the dementors. Dumbledore told Harry and Hermione which window to make for. Dracina Malfoy flew them up to it on Buckbeak, low across the lake and round the back of the castle in the shadow of the towers. 'The West Tower,' Dracina called back over her shoulder. 'Count for me, Potter. Thirteen from the right.' Harry reached out and pushed. The window swung inwards at once: Dumbledore had left it unlatched. There was no sign of Sirius at all. A coil of rope lay on the floor beside the chair. On the desk, by itself, lay a tall, heavy book bound in old brown leather, with a single word on the cover in tarnished gold: MYST.

pages.title: Professor Flitwick's office
infobox: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban (8 July 1999)
The West Tower of Hogwarts, seven floors up
A very low desk; a cushion on the chair; library steps
pages.html:
Professor Flitwick's office is a small study seven floors up in the West Tower of Hogwarts, behind the thirteenth window from the right. It belongs to Filius Flitwick, the Charms master. In June 1994 Sirius Black was locked in it to await the Dementor's Kiss. He was gone by the time Harry Potter, Hermione Granger and Dracina Malfoy reached its window on a hippogriff.

The office

It is crammed with books from floor to ceiling: on the shelves, on the chairs and in stacks on the floor. There is a very low desk, with a cushion on the chair in front of it, and a little set of library steps beside the shelves for reaching the high ones.

In June 1994 a small, plain leather book with nothing on its spine sat on a low shelf, wedged between two fat volumes on Charms. It was very like the one Dumbledore had given Harry.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Twenty, Albus Dumbledore sent Harry and Hermione back in time to save Sirius. He put a small book bound in plain leather into Harry's hands; another book, he said, would be waiting in the office. Harry, Hermione and Dracina flew up to the window on Buckbeak. There was no sign of Sirius, who had been held there supposedly bound and alone. A coil of rope lay neatly on the floor by the chair. 'So much for Dumbledore's wonderful plan,' said Dracina. 'Your mass murderer appears to have let himself out. Perhaps he simply asked nicely.' On the desk lay the big brown linking book called Myst, with grubby grey fingermarks round its edge, the same filthy grey as the dirt under Sirius's broken nails.

In Chapter Twenty-One the three of them followed Sirius through the big brown book to Myst Island. They came home by Dumbledore's little book, whose picture showed the office just as they had left it. Sirius could not face seven floors of stairs with the dementors about, so Dracina leant out of the window and whistled for Buckbeak. From Flitwick's window Sirius flew away on the hippogriff, over the Forbidden Forest.

Harry stayed at the window, shaking with a hard, hot anger at the whole wizarding world. Dracina came to stand beside him and took his fist in her cold fingers. 'You'll make them all pay, Harry,' she said quietly. Through a gap in the clouds a single white star, low in the west and far brighter than any star had a right to be, shone straight in through the window. Harry felt it on his face, warm as a fire, and made up his mind that the wizarding world must be made to change. 'Did you see that?' Dracina whispered. Hermione, who had been watching the time, had not. She shut the big brown book and left it on the desk for Dumbledore.

In Chapter Twenty-Two Lupin told Harry that the Invisibility Cloak had been found folded very neatly in the Shrieking Shack. Harry thought of the coil of rope on the floor of Flitwick's office, wound up as tidily as a hosepipe, and said nothing.

pages.title: Godric's Hollow
infobox: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (26 June 1997)
Bathilda Bagshot; formerly the Dumbledores and the Potters
pages.html:
Godric's Hollow is a village in the West Country, on the wild moors that Godric Gryffindor came from, and it still bears his name. Albus Dumbledore spent the summer of 1899 there with Greta Grindelwald. On 31 October 1981 Lord Voldemort came to the Potters' house in the village, and Lily Potter died there for her son.

The summer of 1899

Bathilda Bagshot, the historian, has lived in Godric's Hollow for most of her long life. The Dumbledores were her neighbours when Albus was young. In the summer of 1899 her great-niece, Greta Grindelwald, came to stay, and there she met the young Albus Dumbledore. The summer ended in a three-cornered duel with his brother Aberforth, in which their sister Ariana was killed.

The Potters

James and Lily Potter went into hiding at Godric's Hollow with their baby son. On 31 October 1981, acting on Peter Pettigrew's betrayal, Voldemort came to the house. James held him off in the hall so that Lily could run with Harry. Voldemort killed him, then killed Lily upstairs as she stood between him and her son. His curse rebounded from Harry, and the house was wrecked, its roof torn away.

Nobody ever told Harry the name of the village. He grew up at the Dursleys' without knowing it, and he first heard it in June 1994, from Sirius Black.

In the saga

In Book Three, Chapter Nineteen, Sirius, walking back through the tunnel from the Shrieking Shack, told Ron Weasley that he had never properly mourned James and Lily. Every time a Dementor passed his cell, it had been that night all over again: 'I'd be standing in the lane at Godric's Hollow, with the roof gone off the house. I'd be finding James in the hall, and Lily upstairs. I'd be begging Hagrid to give me Harry, with Hagrid saying no.' Harry, walking behind them, said nothing at all. He was thinking of the cold on the train, and of a woman screaming. Later that night, sure that Lupin was about to kill him on the grass, Harry thought that his mother had died for him in Godric's Hollow all for nothing.

In Chapter Twenty-Two, in June 1994, Dumbledore looked into Harry's face and saw something he had last seen on a summer evening in Godric's Hollow, nearly a hundred years before. It was the same burning, righteous anger that had once been in Greta Grindelwald's eyes.

pages.title: Liverpool
pages.html:
Liverpool is the great port city on the Mersey, in the north-west of England. John Constantine was born there in 1953 and grew up in a terraced house in the Dingle. When he is angry, his voice goes straight back to it.

John Constantine's Liverpool

His father blamed him, every day of his life, for his mother's death in giving birth to him, and knocked him across the kitchen more times than he could count. John left for Hogwarts in 1964, at eleven, small for his age and frightened.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, on a rainy night in August 1993, John flagged down the Knight Bus on a soaking wet corner in Liverpool, bound for Hogsmeade. Stan Shunpike, the conductor, tried his patience on the way. 'One of these days, soft lad,' John said under his breath, in a voice that went straight back to the Dingle, 'I'll feed you to somethin' with a lorra teeth. An' I'll sell tickets.'

pages.title: Lime Street station
pages.html:
Lime Street is the main railway station of Liverpool, a great Victorian terminus in the middle of the city. In August 1993 John Constantine bought a battered Jackie Collins paperback there for one particular purpose: to leave behind in place of the Linking Book to Myst Island when he stole it.

In the saga

In the Book Three Interlude, John burgled the house of a wizard collector in New Mexico. In the long room of glass cases he laid the paperback on the red velvet cushion where the book had been, then closed the lid of the case.

When Hagrid met him at Hogwarts afterwards, he told John that he looked terrible, then asked whether he was eating properly. 'I had a butty at Lime Street,' said John. 'Tuesday, I think.'

pages.title: The Soho pub
infobox: Harry Potter and the Imprisoned Girl, Interlude
pages.html:
The Soho pub is little known, even in Soho, and nobody there asks anybody's name. John Constantine chose it for exactly that reason. A man can sit in a corner of its back bar for six hours with one pint and a crossword.

In the saga

In the Interlude of Book Three, at two o'clock on a Tuesday afternoon in the summer of 1993, an owl found John there anyway. It came in through a window that did not open, landed in his pint and looked at him as though the whole thing were his fault. The letter it carried was in green ink, from Albus Dumbledore, asking him to fetch a book from Ephraim Shacklewell in New Mexico. John sat a long time without opening it, then bought a whisky. It was in that pub, too, that he admitted to himself that he was afraid of Dumbledore.

pages.title: New Mexico
infobox: The cavern of D'ni; the Cleft; Shacklewell House
pages.html:
New Mexico is a desert state in the south-west of the United States. Under its desert lies the vast cavern of D'ni, reached from the Cleft, a crack in the ground beside an old volcano. In the 1990s a small, secretive excavation is digging its way into the dead city.

History

In 1540 the Spanish explorer Francisco Vásquez de Coronado led an army north into New Mexico in search of the Seven Cities of Cíbola. They were supposed to be made of solid gold, and they did not exist. A few wizards marched with him unrecognised. In 1541, experimenting with long-distance Apparition across the desert, they arrived by accident in the cavern of D'ni. Its people sent them back to the surface and told them never to return. Two centuries later Anna, a Muggle woman of the New Mexico wilds, found her own way down.

New Mexico became a state of the Union in 1912, with its capital at Santa Fe. In July 1945 the first atomic bomb was exploded at Trinity, in the desert of the Jornada del Muerto, after being built in secret at Los Alamos.

Wizards in New Mexico answer to the Magical Congress of the United States of America. Not all of them are respectable. Ephraim Shacklewell is a pure-blood whose father made his fortune in the 1960s, selling a scouring potion to the copper mines of Arizona. Some miles south of the Cleft he built Shacklewell House, a pink adobe mansion with towers, a Thunderbird fountain and a swimming pool shaped like a Golden Snitch. To any No-Maj driving past, it looks like a derelict filling station with a sign reading LAST GAS FOR 90 MILES. His trophy room holds, among other things, a lump of metal labelled as a fragment of the Roswell flying saucer of 1947.

The excavation

In 1987 the artefact hunter John Loftin found D'ni tunnels and machines under the desert. In 1988 Elias Zandi began buying the land round the Cleft. In the 1990s the dig is small and secret. It goes on behind a wire fence, with a hand-painted geological-survey sign. All the same, D'ni artefacts have leaked from it to Muggle and wizard collectors across America. Strangers watch the place: in 1993 a black van with no number plates waited a mile down the road. The D'ni Restoration Council was founded there in 1997.

In the saga

Book 3: John Constantine arrived in New Mexico in the summer of 1993, at a desert crossroads a little after midnight. He walked past the dig at the Cleft and burgled the Myst linking book from Shacklewell House. On Myst Island in June 1994 Hermione Granger told Harry and Dracina that the D'ni had lived in a cavern under the desert in New Mexico.

Book 4: In the summer of 1994 Hermione found Muggles on a newsgroup who could not stop thinking about a desert they had never seen. Some talked about going to New Mexico, and one got as far as a fence where men told him to go home. Nobody, Hermione wrote, should know about New Mexico. In August 1994 Dr Richard Watson spoke to the Muggle news from New Mexico about his friend Daniel Jackson.

pages.title: The Cleft
infobox: The New Mexico desert, beside an old volcano
Elias Zandi; his son Jeff from 1996
Fenced, with tents, a caravan and a survey sign
pages.html:
The Cleft is a deep crack in the ground at the foot of a long black ridge, beside an old volcano in the New Mexico desert. Anna made her home there after the Fall of D'ni, and Atrus grew up there. Since the 1980s it has been the way down to the excavation of the D'ni cavern.

History

The Cleft is a fissure of volcanic rock above the cavern of D'ni. It lies near the place where Anna first found her way down in the eighteenth century, and where she came up again with her son Gehn after the plague. She made her home in it. There was water, a tree and shelter from the desert sun. Gehn brought his dying wife, Keta, to her there. Anna raised their son Atrus in the Cleft until Gehn came back for him, when the boy was about fourteen.

In 1993 the Muggle game Myst, made from Catherine's journals, began to draw people of D'ni blood towards the Cleft, as Yeesha had meant it to.

In 1987 the artefact hunter John Loftin found D'ni tunnels and machines in the desert. On 19 March 1988 he took Elias Zandi down with him. Zandi bought the land round the Cleft and brought in Dr Richard Watson, after which the small group began to dig. When Zandi died in 1996 the land passed to his son Jeff; the following year the excavators formed the D'ni Restoration Council. In later years the Cleft became the place where the explorers who felt called to the desert first arrived.

In the saga

Book 3: In the summer of 1993 John Constantine walked past the dig at night on his way to Shacklewell House. There was not much to see: a wire fence round a patch of desert at the foot of a long, black, broken ridge, a hand-painted sign about a geological survey, a couple of tents, a caravan in darkness and a deep crack in the ground with a ladder going down into it. In Dumbledore's letter it was the place the people digging there called the Cleft. A mile further on, a black van with no number plates waited by the road. Books and other things dug out of the Cleft were leaking into the hands of whoever would pay. The Myst linking book was one of them. As Constantine walked back at dawn with the book, the sun came up behind the black ridge of the Cleft.

Book 4: In 1994 one poster on a Muggle newsgroup kept dreaming of an old volcano with a crack in the ground beside it. Another got as far as a fence in the middle of nowhere, where men told him to go home. In August 1994 Dr Richard Watson spoke to the Muggle news from New Mexico, with the corner of a caravan behind him.

pages.title: D'ni
infobox: A vast cavern deep beneath the New Mexico desert
About 1788, to the plague of A'Gaeris
The Art: books that link to other worlds
Atrus, Yeesha and a few others
The 1980s, by way of the Cleft
pages.html:
D'ni is the name of an ancient people, and of the city they built in an enormous cavern deep beneath the New Mexico desert. There they lived apart from Muggles and wizards alike for nearly ten thousand years. They were masters of the Art, the writing of books that open on other worlds. They fell to the plague of A'Gaeris about two hundred years before the 1990s. Their empty city is now being quietly dug out, and things from it have been leaking into the world ever since the work began.

Origins

The D'ni came to Earth nearly ten thousand years ago. Their ancestors were the Ronay of the Age of Garternay. Their founder, Ri'neref, brought them through a linking book into a great cavern far under the desert of what is now New Mexico. They gave one name, D'ni, to the cavern, to the city they raised in it and to themselves.

The city climbed in terraces round a great underground lake, with the island of Ae'gura at its heart. Visitors from the surface wrote of lamps that burnt without fire, and water that ran uphill. The handful of scholars who care about such things still argue over whether the D'ni were a magical race or an offshoot of humanity. To the few outsiders who met them they looked like ordinary people, only very pale, with odd eyes. They lived far longer than any people of the surface.

Society and the Art

For most of their history the D'ni were ruled by kings, and afterwards by a council of lords. Daily life, though, was ordered by the great guilds. The Guild of Writers wrote Ages, and the Guild of Maintainers inspected them for safety. Other guilds made inks, made paper, surveyed the rock, healed the sick and kept the law. The D'ni had a language and a script of their own. They counted in twenty-fives.

Their wealth came from the Art. A good enough Writer could describe a world so exactly that a book would link to it. The D'ni wrote thousands of these worlds, which they called Ages, for food, timber, stone and ore. Their priests taught that a Maker had made every world that could possibly be, branching like the leaves of an enormous tree, and that a Writer only described a world that already existed.

Many D'ni behaved as though they owned the worlds they wrote, peoples and all. Some came to believe they had made them, which the priests called heresy. Anna, the one outsider who lived among them for long, thought it was pride that destroyed them. They had thousands of years of rules, they were sure they were right, and they never asked questions about the Art itself.

Contact with the surface

The D'ni kept themselves to themselves. In 1541 the army of Francisco Vásquez de Coronado came north looking for the golden Seven Cities of Cíbola, and a few Spanish wizards were travelling with it, unrecognised. They slipped away to experiment with long-distance Apparition across the desert, and arrived in the cavern by accident. The D'ni talked with them for a few hours through an interpreter. Then they sent them back up to the surface, firmly and rather rudely, telling them never to return. The Spaniards wrote it all down afterwards, which is the only reason anybody knows of the meeting. They did not think the D'ni were magical at all.

In the eighteenth century a Muggle woman named Anna found her own way down through the rock. The D'ni took her prisoner, then took her in. She married Aitrus, a D'ni, and learnt the Art. She took the name Ti'ana and bore a son, Gehn.

The Fall

About 1788, a few years after Anna came to live among them, a plague loosed by the renegade A'Gaeris went through the cavern and its Ages. It killed nearly every D'ni. Anna escaped to the surface with Gehn, and the Art was lost with the D'ni, more or less. The city stood empty for two hundred years.

A few D'ni survived, scattered across their Ages. Anna's grandson Atrus later gathered some of them together, and wrote the Age of Releeshahn as a new home for them. In the twentieth century the D'ni are all but extinct. Atrus, his daughter Yeesha and a few survivors are all that is left of them. D'ni lives are long enough for that to be possible.

Rediscovery

In the 1980s a small group of Muggles, among them John Loftin, Elias Zandi and Dr Richard Watson, found a way down from the Cleft, a deep crack beside an old volcano in the New Mexico desert. They began to dig. In the 1990s the excavation is still small and secretive. All the same, a great many artefacts have leaked out of it to Muggle and wizard collectors in America, at least one working linking book among them. Anna's journal, which turned up in America about 1985, is the source of most of what is known about the D'ni.

Yeesha, the daughter of Atrus, gave Catherine's journals to the brothers Rand and Robyn Miller of Cyan, a small American games company. From them the brothers made the computer game Myst, released on 24 September 1993, and the games that followed it. It was all Yeesha's plan, meant to draw people of D'ni blood to the Cleft and the D'ni caverns. After Zandi's death in 1996 the excavators carried on, and in 1997 they formed the D'ni Restoration Council to see the work through.

In the saga

Book Three: John Constantine, carrying the Myst linking book across Britain in 1993, knew as much about the D'ni as anybody who cared to know. They had been a people who lived for ten thousand years in a cavern under New Mexico, cut off from Muggle and magical peoples alike, writing books that were doors. About two hundred years before, a disease had spread and killed them. He passed the dig at the Cleft and judged that it was run by a handful of well-meaning amateurs with clipboards.

In June 1994 Hermione Granger recognised the big brown book in Flitwick's office as D'ni. She had read about linking books in at least three books, starting from a footnote in Lost Civilisations of the Ancient World. On the dock on Myst Island she told Harry and Dracina about the Spanish wizards. She went on to Anna, the Art and the plague. There were rumours too, she said, that Muggles had found the cavern again and had been digging there quietly for years, while odd D'ni things turned up on the black market. Dracina concluded that the D'ni had been very advanced Muggles, and Hermione agreed with her.

Book Four: in the summer of 1994 Hermione found six people on a Muggle newsgroup, in different countries and unknown to each other, who described a calling towards a desert they had never seen. One of them had got as far as a fence in the middle of nowhere, where men told him to go home. Hermione thought nobody should know about New Mexico. She wondered whether Anna had borne a child among the D'ni, so that people might be walking about with a little D'ni blood in them without knowing it.

pages.title: Shacklewell House
infobox: Harry Potter and the Imprisoned Girl, Interlude
The New Mexico desert, some miles south of the Cleft
Pink adobe, in the Spanish manner
Wards against wand magic; a six-legged Wampus cat
pages.html:
Shacklewell House is the desert home of Ephraim Shacklewell, a pure-blood American wizard, some miles south of the D'ni dig at the Cleft in New Mexico. To No-Majs it looks like a derelict filling station. Behind the illusion stands a vast pink adobe mansion in the Spanish style, built with the fortune his father made selling a scouring potion to the copper mines of Arizona.

The house

From the road there is nothing to see but a single rusted pump on the forecourt and a sign hanging off one hinge. The sign reads LAST GAS FOR 90 MILES, creaking in the hot wind. Any No-Maj who drives past feels a sudden urge to keep going, and remembers an urgent appointment somewhere else.

Inside the illusion are towers, balconies and a long colonnade. There is a fountain shaped like a Thunderbird, with a swimming pool shaped like a Golden Snitch. The wards were built by MACUSA security men whom Shacklewell bribed, and they are made to detect wand magic. A six-legged Wampus cat sleeps across the foot of the stairs.

The trophy room

The panelled trophy room on the first floor holds Shacklewell's collection, every piece in a glass case with a label. A lump of twisted grey metal is labelled as a fragment of a No-Maj flying saucer from Roswell, 1947; it is half a hubcap off a Ford. A shrunken head carries a label saying that it talks, occasionally. There is a stuffed jackalope, a pair of boots that belonged to somebody called Wild Bill, and a jar of something that moves.

Until the summer of 1993 the last case held the Myst book, on a cushion of red velvet. Its label called it a No-Maj picture book with a charmed photograph inside, from the dig, priced at fifty dollars. That was what Shacklewell had paid a digger for it.

In the saga

In the Interlude of Book Three, one night in the summer of 1993, John Constantine let his eyes go soft in front of the filling station until he could see through it. He burgled the house for Albus Dumbledore. In the trophy room he slid the Myst book into a carrier bag, leaving a battered Jackie Collins paperback on the velvet in its place. Shacklewell found him there, in a silk dressing gown, a hairnet and monogrammed slippers. He had a wand in one hand, with a glass of warm milk in the other.

John held up his old Liverpool library card, which carried a very small glamour, and announced himself as MACUSA. He was confiscating the book, he said, and would say no more about the business with the copper mines. Shacklewell's face filled with relief. He offered his visitor a cup of coffee, then asked whether there was some kind of receipt. John wrote him one on the back of an envelope, in large clear capitals, and signed it J. Lennon, MACUSA.

pages.title: Myst Island
infobox: Anna (Ti'ana); its linking book by Atrus
pages.html:
Myst Island is a small Age of grey rock and dark pines in an empty grey sea. It was once the home of Atrus and his family. Its linking book, written by Atrus, carried Sirius Black there from Flitwick's office in June 1994. Harry, Hermione and Dracina followed him.

Description

The island is the whole of its world. From the end of the dock nearly all of it can be seen at once. Beyond it there is only grey water in every direction, meeting a sky of the same colour, with no land on any horizon. A long wooden dock runs out from a rocky cove. Beside it lies a sunken wooden sailing ship with a single leaning mast, and on a post at the shore end stands a small brass switch. Offshore a squat stone tower rises out of the water, with a clock face as big as a cartwheel.

A path climbs from the cove past an enormous stone gear, as tall as a house and half sunk into the hill. It goes on past a little pool with a perfect model ship in it, to a long, low library with stone pillars. There is also a round domed building, a tall silvery thing like a rocket, a brick chimney and, on the summit, a tree so enormous that it makes the pines look like weeds. The library is panelled in dark wood. One wall holds a great map of the island, and at the far end are two small stone stands, rather like lecterns.

History

Anna wrote the Age as a refuge for her family, and Atrus wrote its linking book. When Atrus and Catherine escaped Riven through the Star Fissure, Atrus linked to Myst as he fell. The family lived on the island for years. Atrus kept his books in the library. By the island's machines he joined it to the Ages he wrote: the rocket to Selenitic, the ship to Stoneship, the clock tower to the Mechanical Age, the great tree to Channelwood. Small brass switches on posts about the island marked the places that mattered.

Early in the nineteenth century Atrus's sons, Sirrus and Achenar, turned on their parents. When the Stranger arrived on the dock with nothing in his hands, he found the island empty. Many of the library's books had been burnt. The two brothers were trapped on the stands, one in a red book and one in a blue. The Stranger freed Atrus, who came home and removed his sons' books. After that the island was left to itself.

In the saga

Book 3: Harry, Hermione and Dracina linked to Myst Island from Flitwick's office in June 1994, just as the Aurors opened the door. They found it decaying.
