In 1999 he came to Earth for the talks that put it under the Protected Planets Treaty, and very nearly died there. In 2001 he was killed on the world of Juna, shot in the back by a machine made in Teal'c's likeness.

Father of the Titans

Cronus takes his name from the Titan whom the Greeks remembered as the father of Zeus, Hera, Poseidon and Hades, the old king who ruled before the gods.

He has been a mortal enemy of Apophis for as long as either of them can remember. He does not forgive failure, as his own First Prime found.

Ronac

Teal'c's father, Ronac, was Cronus's First Prime when Teal'c was a boy. Ronac lost a battle that nobody could have won. Cronus killed him for it, slowly, with his own hands.

Ronac's widow and son were sent away to Chulak in disgrace. There the boy grew up under Bra'tac's teaching to serve Apophis instead, and in time he rose to be Apophis's First Prime. He never forgot who had killed his father.

Sokar

Long ago Cronus joined Ra, Apophis and the other System Lords to bring down Sokar, who had grown too great for their liking. When it was done, it was Cronus who banished Sokar from their council. Sokar survived on his own world, Delmak, and in time he built up his strength again.

The talks on Earth

In 1999 the System Lords resolved to attack Earth, which had been killing Goa'uld since 1997. Asgard warned Earth, and offered to bring the two sides together. The talks were held on Earth, in the base that houses its Stargate. Three System Lords came to them: Cronus, Nirrti and Lord Yu.

Thor himself opened the talks. It is said in Asgard that the System Lords' first demand, a thousand years before, had been that he should not be present. This time they sat at the same table with him, and managed not to mention it. He was soon called away, and the rest was left to the Tau'ri, as the Goa'uld call the people of Earth.

The System Lords' price for peace was that Earth should give up its Stargate. Before the matter was settled, Cronus was found badly beaten, and so was Teal'c. Since Cronus had killed Teal'c's father, Teal'c was blamed. Yu and Nirrti swore to attack Earth in revenge.

It had been Nirrti. She had made herself invisible with a device for shifting out of phase with the world, and she meant the talks to fail so that she could seize power in the confusion. She said she had tried to heal Cronus with her hand device and failed. Samantha Carter of SG-1 used the device on him herself, and saved his life.

When Nirrti's part came out, Cronus and Yu turned on her. They took her away with them as their prisoner. Earth was put under the treaty after all. The System Lords left with a warning: the Tau'ri were safe on Earth, but anywhere beyond it they were fair game.

Juna

By early 2001 Cronus had taken Juna, a world that had lately been freed from Heru'ur's rule. There he captured three of the machines that a being called Harlan had made in the likeness of SG-1, on the world of Altair. They thought and remembered exactly as the real team did. For some time they had been travelling through the gate on missions of their own.

Cronus had the machine Daniel Jackson beheaded in front of his court, which showed the Goa'uld what they were. He meant to kill the machine Teal'c slowly, as he had killed Ronac. The real SG-1 came to Juna to help, and the machines fought beside them. The machine Teal'c shot Cronus in the back with a staff weapon, and he died.

None of the machines survived the battle. SG-1 freed Juna once more and took Cronus's mothership.

The ship

Cronus's ship did not outlive him long. SG-1 took it to Vorash, where the Tok'ra had their base. There, to destroy Apophis's fleet, SG-1 made Vorash's sun explode, and the blast flung the ship into another galaxy. Apophis took it from SG-1 there. It fell out of the sky on to Delmak, Sokar's old world, with Apophis aboard and the Replicators swarming through it.

pages.title: Darkseid
infobox: King Yuga Khan and Queen Heggra
Kalibak, by Suli; Orion, by Tigra
Granny Goodness, DeSaad, Kalibak, Glorious Godfrey, the Parademons
Highfather of New Genesis, Orion, Mister Miracle, Superman
pages.html:
Darkseid is the Lord of Apokolips, a world of fire pits and slaves on the far side of the universe. He is one of the beings who call themselves the New Gods, and he wants only one thing: the Anti-Life Equation, which would give him command of every living mind. He believes it is hidden somewhere in the minds of human beings, which is why he takes such an interest in Earth. Very few people on Earth have ever heard of him, and he prefers it that way.

Uxas

Darkseid was born Uxas, the second son of King Yuga Khan and Queen Heggra of Apokolips. His elder brother, Drax, was the heir. When Drax set out to claim the Omega Force, a power that lay waiting for whoever could master it, Uxas killed him and took it for himself.

The Omega Force turned his body to something very like grey stone, and he took a new name to go with it. From then on he was Darkseid.

Suli, Tigra and Heggra

As a young man Darkseid loved a woman called Suli, the only person he is ever known to have loved, and she gave him a son, Kalibak. Heggra thought Suli made him weak. She had her poisoned by DeSaad, the court's chief torturer, who was not particular about whom he poisoned.

Darkseid married Tigra afterwards, and she gave him a second son, Orion. He never forgave his mother. In time DeSaad poisoned Heggra too, this time on Darkseid's orders, and Darkseid took the throne of Apokolips.

The war with New Genesis

Apokolips has a twin world, New Genesis, a green and peaceful place ruled by Izaya, who is called Highfather. The two worlds have hated each other for as long as either has existed. Their last great war began when Darkseid's uncle Steppenwolf, at Darkseid's bidding, murdered Izaya's wife, Avia.

The war went on until both sides were close to ruin. It ended with the Pact, by which the two rulers exchanged their sons. Darkseid's son Orion was sent to grow up on New Genesis, and Izaya's son Scott Free was handed over to Apokolips.

Neither exchange turned out as Darkseid intended. Orion grew up to be the fiercest warrior New Genesis has, and he has spent his life fighting his father. Scott Free was raised in one of Granny Goodness's orphanages, where the children of Apokolips are trained into soldiers, and in time he escaped to Earth with Big Barda, one of Granny's own Female Furies.

On Earth Scott became Mister Miracle, the escape artist, and Barda became his wife. In 1987 he was one of the founders of the new Justice League. His escape broke the Pact, which gave Darkseid the excuse he had been waiting for.

Metron, the restless seeker of New Genesis, gave Darkseid the secret of the Boom Tube in exchange for the X-Element.

Apokolips

Apokolips is a world of fire pits, factories and slums, on which nothing grows. Its people, the Lowlies, toil in their millions in the shadow of Darkseid's towers, and they have long since been taught to cheer him. Above them fly the Parademons, his winged soldiers. Those who can no longer work are left to rot in the slums of Armagetto. It is not Hell, although very few of the Lowlies would know the difference.

His court is made up of the people who are useful to him. Granny Goodness runs the orphanages. DeSaad is his torturer, as well as the inventor of most of the machines for it. Kalibak, his elder son, is strong, brutal and desperate for a word of praise from his father, which he has never had. Glorious Godfrey has a voice that can turn a crowd.

The Omega Effect

Darkseid's power is the Omega Effect. It comes out of his eyes as the Omega Beams, which will chase whatever he aims them at round corners and through walls until they find it. They can burn a living thing out of existence or send it somewhere else entirely, and he can bring back what they have taken if he chooses. He rarely does.

He is enormously strong, very old and almost impossible to hurt. He seldom needs to prove it. He prefers to send other people, and to wait.

The Anti-Life Equation

What Darkseid wants above everything is the Anti-Life Equation. It is a proof that hope and free will are worthless, so complete that whoever knows it can command the mind of any living thing.

He has searched for it across the universe. He has come to believe that its pieces lie scattered in the minds of human beings, and that is why Earth matters to him.

He once looked for it among the Goa'uld, the parasites who rule much of Earth's galaxy, since each of them is born with the memories of all its ancestors. DeSaad took the whole court of a lesser System Lord apart, one mind at a time. He found nothing but vanity and a great many memories of Thor.

Earth

Darkseid first came to notice on Earth in late 1970, when Superman found that Intergang, the crime syndicate of Metropolis, was armed with weapons from Apokolips. Darkseid had been behind it from the start. It was the first of many such discoveries.

In 1986 he set out to break the heroes of Earth by turning their own people against them. He did not come himself. His instrument was Glorious Godfrey, who went before the television cameras as the preacher G. Gordon Godfrey and told America night after night that its heroes were dangerous. Darkseid's creatures staged disasters to prove him right.

That winter President Reagan grounded every costumed hero in America. Godfrey was exposed early in 1987, at a great march on Washington, and the order was lifted. A new Justice League came out of the struggle.

In the spring of 1994 Doomsday, the creature that had killed Superman, rose again far from Earth and fought its way across Apokolips. At the same time Hank Henshaw, the Cyborg Superman, surfaced there. Darkseid compressed what remained of his life force into a small sphere, and kept it. Nobody knows what he means to do with it.

Thanos

Darkseid's bitterest enemy outside his own family is Thanos, the Mad Titan. Their feud began in 1973, when Darkseid tried to take the Cosmic Cube from him. It has drawn the Avengers and the Justice League into one war after another.

In 1977 Darkseid helped the heroes bring Thanos down, so that he could steal the Soul Gems from the wreck. In 1991 Thanos, wearing the Infinity Gauntlet, turned him into a statue of glass for a day that almost nobody remembers. Darkseid does.

Character

Darkseid is patient in a way that only something very old can be. He does not lose his temper, he does not hurry and he does not forgive. He has no use for love, which he tried once, or for loyalty, which he expects but never returns. His servants fear him far more than they love him, which he considers the proper arrangement.

In the saga

Book 4: on 20 August 1994 the newsreader on the Dursleys' television recalls that in 1986 President Reagan grounded every costumed hero in America for an entire winter. Nobody on the news mentions Darkseid, whose campaign it was.

pages.title: Death (servant of Dracula)
infobox: A powerful demonic creature in the shape of a reaper
pages.html:
Death is a powerful demon that has served Dracula since 1094. It takes the shape of a robed skeleton with a great scythe, and it has stood at its master's right hand at almost every one of his returns. Despite its name it is simply a demon in Dracula's service. It is not Death of the Endless, the being who meets every living thing at the end of its life, and it has nothing to do with her.

Nature

Death is a demon of great power that wears the shape of a reaper: a skeleton in a dark hooded robe, carrying a great scythe. It can fill the air with flying sickles, and pass at will through the dark places of its master's castle. The name is a borrowed one, and so is the fear that goes with it. It does not lead the dead anywhere. Its only power over death is the power to kill.

Like every demon, it belongs in the end to the Devil, whose property Dracula and every vampire also are. Its loyalty, though, is to Dracula. It has served him for nine centuries, working again and again to bring him back whenever he has been destroyed. It has been destroyed itself more than once, and it has always come back, as its master does.

In Dracula's service

In 1094, as Leon Belmont destroyed the vampire Walter Bernhard, Death carried Walter's soul to Mathias Cronqvist. Mathias took it into the Crimson Stone and rose as the vampire who became Dracula. From that night Death served Mathias, and it fought Leon while its new master withdrew.

It was in the castle in 1476, when Trevor Belmont fought his way up through the clock tower. In 1479 it took the guise of a man called Zead and schemed to raise Dracula again through a living vessel. It killed the Devil Forgemaster Isaac to do it, and Hector thwarted it. Simon Belmont met it in the castle in 1691, and destroyed it in Brahm's mansion in 1698. Juste Belmont destroyed it in 1748, after it had held Lydie Erlanger prisoner. Richter Belmont met it on the road through the woods in 1792.

In 1797, when Alucard entered his father's risen castle, Death met him at the gate and stripped him of the arms he carried. In 1944, while the vampire painter Brauner held the castle, Death worked to restore its master. In 2035, after Dracula's final destruction, it tried to wake his power in Soma Cruz.

Not Death of the Endless

Death of the Endless, the second of the Endless, is death itself: the being who comes to every living thing at the end of its life. Dracula's servant is no such being. It is a demon in a reaper's shape, under a borrowed name, and it serves one master.

pages.title: Ecaterina the Wise
infobox: The Prometheans, the idealists of her clan
The Camarilla from its founding; later, in secret, the Sabbat
A Sabbat archbishop in New York, under the name Catherine Weiss
pages.html:
Ecaterina the Wise is a Brujah elder: a scholar, and an idealist of the faction called the Prometheans. In the twelfth century she led the Brujah of Prague, and in 1141 she Embraced the crusader Christof Romuald. She later went over in secret from the Camarilla to the Sabbat. By 1999 she was a Sabbat archbishop in New York, fighting those of her own sect who served the Methuselah Vukodlak.

The Brujah of Prague

In the twelfth century Ecaterina led the Brujah of Prague. She was a scholar before she was anything else. She belonged to the Prometheans, the Brujah who still believe that the Kindred can be better than their Beast, and who still dream of what Carthage was before Rome destroyed it. To a Promethean, Carthage is the proof that Kindred and mortals could once live side by side.

Her right hand was her childe Cosmas. His own childe, Wilhem Streicher, was among her most loyal followers.

Prague in those nights lay between the Tremere and the Tzimisce, who were making ready for war with one another. Ecaterina meant the Brujah to be neither side's pawns, which in Prague in those years was a great deal easier to mean than to manage.

Christof

In 1141 a French crusader, Christof Romuald, went down alone into a silver mine near Prague and killed the Tzimisce monster that had been preying on the city. Ecaterina saw what he was worth. She Embraced him that same night, before any other clan could claim him, and he became her childe, of the ninth generation.

She set Christof's coterie against both the Tremere and the Tzimisce. She watched him lose his faith but keep his humanity. She lost him in the 1140s, when Vyšehrad fell and buried him beneath its ruins.

Camarilla and Sabbat

When the Camarilla was founded in the fifteenth century, Ecaterina belonged to it. In time she came to think that it had turned the Kindred into jailers and courtiers. She had hoped to see them free, and better than they were. She and Wilhem went over to the Sabbat in secret.

The Sabbat disappointed her too. The sect that had promised revolution became, in her eyes, one more vehicle for the old politics of the clans.

New York, 1999

By 1999 Ecaterina was a Sabbat archbishop in New York, going by the name Catherine Weiss. Within her own sect she fought the faction that served the Methuselah Vukodlak and meant to raise him. When the Society of Leopold woke Christof in London, Wilhem found him and brought him back into her cause. Christof went on to destroy Vukodlak in the Cathedral of Flesh.

Later years

In the first years of the new century Christof was at her side once more. With him and the Kindred scholar Beckett she travelled to Tunis. Word had come that the resting place of the fallen Antediluvian of the Brujah, destroyed long ago by his own childe Troile, lay beneath a dam near the city, not far from the ruins of Carthage.

pages.title: Father Christmas
infobox: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe (16 October 1950)
1940, as the White Witch's winter broke
The sword Rhindon; a shield with a red lion
A bow, a quiver of arrows, an ivory horn
A cordial of fire-flower juice; a small dagger
pages.html:
Father Christmas is the old man in red who brings presents at Christmas. In England he is mostly a story for children. In Narnia he was real enough to give a queen her bow. He came into Narnia in 1940, when Aslan was on the move and the White Witch's long winter had begun to break. The gifts he gave the Pevensie children went with them through all their reigns.

Always winter

For a hundred years the White Witch had kept Narnia in winter, and Christmas never came. Father Christmas could not get in while her power held.

In 1940, when Aslan came back and her power began to fail, Father Christmas came at last, in a sledge drawn by reindeer with bells on their harness. He was enormous and plainly delighted, in a red robe trimmed with white fur, with a long white beard. Everyone who saw him felt solemn and happy at once.

The gifts

He met Peter, Susan and Lucy on the road with the Beavers. He gave each of them a present. Edmund was not there to be given one, because he had gone over to the Witch.

To Peter he gave a sword, Rhindon, and a shield with a red lion on it. To Susan he gave a bow, a quiver of arrows and a little ivory horn: if she blew it, help would come to her wherever she was. To Lucy he gave a bottle of cordial made from the juice of fire-flowers, a drop of which would heal almost any hurt, and a small dagger.

He told the girls that their gifts were for use in great need, and that he did not mean them to fight in the battle. Lucy, who thought she could be brave enough, was cross about it.

He gave Mrs Beaver a new sewing machine. He told Mr Beaver that his dam had been finished and mended. Then he brought out a tray laid for tea, with the teapot already hot. He wished them all a merry Christmas, cried long life to the true King, and was gone.

What his coming meant

His coming was the first sure sign that the Witch's magic was failing. Christmas could come to Narnia only because Aslan had. Within a day the thaw had begun, and the Witch's sledge stuck fast in the melting snow.

The gifts afterwards

The gifts went with the four through all their reign at Cair Paravel. Peter killed the wolf Maugrim with Rhindon. Lucy's cordial healed the wounded of more than one battle, Edmund among them.

Susan's horn stayed in Narnia when the four went home through the wardrobe. In 1941 Prince Caspian blew it in his need and called them back. Susan never gave up the bow. Forty years later, in her own home, she drew Lord Voldemort's blood with it.

In England

In England Father Christmas is a story for children, and grown-ups know better. The Pevensies knew that he was real, which is more than most grown-ups can say. Many people believe that he grew out of Saint Nicholas of Myra, the bishop who gave presents in secret. Nobody in Narnia ever thought to ask him.

Muggles put fat little Father Christmases with fishing rods on their lawns. Wizards, whose gardens are full of gnomes, find this very funny.

pages.title: Fenrir Greyback
infobox: The Wyrm; Lord Voldemort's followers in the First Wizarding War
Biting children; the bite that made Remus Lupin
pages.html:
Fenrir Greyback is a Garou who makes others of his kind by the bite, deliberately, and who prefers to choose children. He is the werewolf who bit Remus Lupin when Lupin was a very small boy.

Life

Greyback is a big, grey-haired man with long yellowish nails and pointed teeth. He smells of dirt, sweat and blood. He has never put his name on the Ministry's Werewolf Registry, and he has never kept any wizarding law.

In the 1960s he was brought before the Ministry of Magic's Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures over the deaths of two Muggle children. He passed himself off as a Muggle vagrant, and was let go, because nobody on the committee knew what he was. The wizard who questioned him, Lyall Lupin, an authority on Boggarts, poltergeists and other non-human spirits, told the hearing that werewolves were soulless, evil things, fit for nothing but death. Greyback took his revenge on Lyall's son. He found the boy, Remus, asleep in his bed, and bit him.

In the First Wizarding War he ran with Lord Voldemort's supporters, who promised him prey in return for his help. He spread terror by threatening to set his teeth in the children of those who stood against them.

Greyback and the Garou

Most Garou are born, not made, and their law frowns on making new Garou by the bite. Those who do it all the same serve the Wyrm. Severus Snape once told a class that the fallen tribe's 'get are still abroad, still making others by the bite, still extremely particular in their choosing'. That marks Greyback as one of the tribe that went over, the Black Spiral Dancers. He seeks out the young, above all the children of wizards, so that he can raise them apart from their families to hate wizardkind. He means one day to make enough of his kind to overwhelm the wizards altogether.

Remus Lupin, whom he made, grew up to be his opposite: a Garou who fights the Wyrm. Lupin has said only that he was a very small boy when he was bitten, and that his parents tried everything to cure him.

Garou made by the bite are called the biteborn. Among the thirteen tribes they are rare, and despised as no true Garou, even though they are Garou by every measure. Among the Black Spiral Dancers they are common, and Greyback has made more of them than most. Lupin is his biteborn. The tribes suspect that a bitten Garou carries the taint of whatever bit him, and Lupin has had to live that suspicion down all his life.

pages.title: Galactus
infobox: The life energy of whole planets
pages.html:
Galactus is a vast cosmic being who keeps himself alive by draining the life energy of whole planets. Just before Christmas 1965 he came to devour the Earth, and the sky over Manhattan seemed to catch fire. The Fantastic Four were said to have talked him out of it. He has come back more than once since, and each time he has been turned away.

Nature

Galactus was once a mortal man, Galan of the world Taa, in the universe that existed before this one. When that universe ended he survived its death, and was reborn in the new one as Galactus. He is now so vast that he must consume the energy of living worlds to go on living. He travels the universe in a great ship and sends heralds ahead of him to find planets that will suit him. The first and most famous of them is the Silver Surfer, once Norrin Radd of Zenn-La, who gave himself to Galactus to spare his own world.

Galactus once ate a world that belonged to one of the Goa'uld System Lords, together with the System Lord. It is the only time the Goa'uld are known to have prayed.

Earth, 1965

In December 1965 the Watcher, an alien observer pledged never to interfere, tried to hide the Earth from the Surfer by setting the sky above New York ablaze. The Surfer found the Earth all the same. Galactus arrived above Manhattan and began to build the engine that would drain it. The Fantastic Four could not stop him by force.

The blind sculptor Alicia Masters turned the Surfer against his master. Johnny Storm was sent into Galactus's ship to fetch the Ultimate Nullifier, the one weapon Galactus feared. Holding it, Reed Richards persuaded Galactus to go. Galactus spared the Earth, and he punished the Surfer by imprisoning him on it.

Days before Galactus came, Maximus had sealed the Inhumans' Great Refuge behind a barrier of negative energy.

Later visits

He came back to Earth in 1972, and again in 1982. On the second occasion the Avengers and the Fantastic Four together drove him to the brink of starvation. Reed Richards saved his life, a mercy for which the Shi'ar Empire later put Richards on trial.

In 1984 Galactus was among those the Beyonder brought to Battleworld in the Secret Wars. There he tried to devour that world too, and Victor von Doom stole his power for a time.

In 1983 he ate the Skrull Throneworld, Tarnax IV, with billions of Skrulls on it.

In the saga

Book Four, Chapter Three: an old man at the protest outside the United Nations in August 1994 recalls that just before Christmas in 1965 the sky caught fire over Manhattan, because something had come to eat the world. The Fantastic Four were said to have talked it out of it. His wife had a heart attack on the second day.

pages.title: Get of Fenris
infobox: Scandinavia, Iceland and the German lands
War, endurance and contempt for weakness
pages.html:
The Get of Fenris are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou. They are the warriors of Scandinavia and the German lands, followers of the great wolf Fenris. They believe that only the strong will survive the last battle against the Wyrm.

Totem and ways

The Get take their name from their totem, Fenris, the monstrous wolf of the Norse stories, a spirit of strength, ferocity and survival. Their ways are hard. Cubs are tested without mercy, and weakness is despised. Those who fail are driven out, and it is often the Children of Gaia who take them in. The Get honour courage, endurance, loyalty to the pack and a good death. Many of them see the coming end of the war, which other Garou call the Apocalypse, as their own Ragnarok: the battle for which they were bred.

Their rites are bloody and their sagas long. Their Galliards keep the sagas in the old northern manner, as verse to be chanted. A Get of Fenris rarely backs away from a fight, and seldom forgets who started one.

Homelands

Their oldest caerns lie in Scandinavia, Iceland and the mountain forests of Germany. Their Kinfolk are the Norse and Germanic peoples. The Get went wherever those peoples went. They crossed the North Sea with the raiders, settling in Britain and Ireland. They went east into Russia, and later across the Atlantic.

Place in the world

The other tribes value the Get as the fist of the Garou Nation and fear their temper. Their feud with the Fianna dates from the Viking raids on Ireland, and both sides still sing of it. They have little patience with the Children of Gaia, whom they think soft. Nor have they much time for the Bone Gnawers and the Glass Walkers, who in their view have forgotten what they are.

pages.title: Ghouls (vampiric)
infobox: Drinking a vampire's blood, without the Embrace
pages.html:
A ghoul, in the vampires' sense of the word, is a living mortal or animal kept on draughts of vampire blood without being Embraced. It does not age while it is fed, and it is stronger than an ordinary mortal. It is nearly always blood-bound to the vampire it serves. It has nothing to do with the creature wizards call a ghoul, such as the one that lives in the Weasleys' attic and bangs on the pipes.

Nature

Vampire blood keeps a ghoul alive and unchanging for as long as the supply lasts. It heals the ghoul's wounds and lends it some of the strength of the Kindred. With practice a ghoul can learn a little of its master's Disciplines. A ghoul still lives, all the same. It walks in daylight, eats ordinary food and keeps its soul.

It also craves the blood. A ghoul needs a fresh draught about once a month, and if the supply stops, its years catch up with it. One that has been kept for centuries does not simply grow old; the centuries take it at once.

A ghoul who drinks from the same vampire three times is bound to it by the blood bond, and will love it whether it wants to or not.

Service

Vampires keep ghouls as servants who can act by day: watchmen, drivers, lawyers and bodyguards. The vampire who keeps a ghoul is called its domitor. Animals are made ghouls to serve as guards.

Over the centuries the Tzimisce have bred whole families of born ghouls, the revenants, who serve them from birth. They have shaped others into monsters for war. Their greatest war-beast, the vozhd, is built of many bodies fused into one. Some ghouls escape their masters and live as independents, always hunting for more blood.

Notable ghouls

Anezka, a nun of Prague, was the ghoul of the Tzimisce Methuselah Vukodlak from the 1140s until 1999. All that time she worked in secret against his waking. When Christof Romuald destroyed Vukodlak, she had no master's blood left to keep her, and the centuries would have taken her at once. Christof Embraced her instead.

Leo Allatius, who led the Society of Leopold in 1999, was a mortal kept alive for three hundred years by vampire blood. He meant to use Vukodlak's blood to destroy every vampire in the world.

In the saga

Remus Lupin warned Harry Potter's class about the blood bond in October 1993. With some vampires, he said, a mortal need only drink from them three times, a few drops, to love them for the rest of their life without ever knowing the difference. He called it the cruellest thing vampires do.

pages.title: Glass Walkers
infobox: City dwellers, from financiers to crime families
Machines, money and the spirits of the city
pages.html:
The Glass Walkers are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou: the tribe of the cities. They are at home among machines, money and glass towers. They hold that the city belongs to Gaia as much as the forest does, and that it must be fought for. Other Garou suspect them of having gone too far over to the Weaver.

Totem and ways

The Glass Walkers follow Cockroach, a spirit that went with mankind into its towns and thrived there, as they have. They are the most modern of the tribes. Where other Garou shun human works, Glass Walkers use telephones, computers, cars and guns. They run businesses, hold office and keep accounts. Their Theurges deal with the spirits of the city, of electricity and of machines, which are the Weaver's creatures. They bargain with those spirits where other tribes would only fight.

Their Kinfolk are city people of every kind, from bankers and engineers to the old crime families of the Mediterranean ports. Glass Walkers fight the Wyrm with the city's own weapons: money, information and influence. They turn them against the companies and cartels that poison the world for profit.

History

In the earliest towns the tribe was called the Warders of Men: the Garou who lived among humans and watched over them. As the cities grew, the tribe grew with them. In the age of steam and the railway they were known as the Iron Riders. They took the name Glass Walkers as the modern cities rose. They have no wild homeland. Their caerns lie in strange places: old cellars, office towers and the hearts of great cities.

Place in the world

The other tribes depend on the Glass Walkers' money and contacts. They distrust them for the same reasons. The Red Talons and the Get of Fenris think them traitors to Gaia. Many Garou believe that the Weaver's madness is as great a danger as the Wyrm, which keeps the Glass Walkers under constant suspicion. They share the cities, uneasily, with the Bone Gnawers.

pages.title: Hal Jordan
infobox: Green Lantern Corps; Justice League (founding member)
Vanished again, August 1994, after Zero Hour
pages.html:
Hal Jordan was Green Lantern for thirty-four years: the test pilot of Coast City who received his ring in 1959 and helped to found the Justice League. When Coast City was destroyed in 1993, he fell. At the turn of 1994 he destroyed the Green Lantern Corps and its masters, then vanished. His ring's last successor, Kyle Rayner, took his place. In July 1994 he came back as Parallax, the power behind Zero Hour, meaning to remake history so that Coast City had never fallen. The heroes stopped him at the beginning of time, and he vanished again.

The man without fear

Hal Jordan was a test pilot for Ferris Aircraft in Coast City, a man said to be entirely without fear. In 1959 the dying alien Abin Sur crash-landed in the California desert, and his power ring went looking for the one man fit to replace him. It found Hal. The Guardians of the Universe accepted him into the Green Lantern Corps as guardian of Earth's sector.

At the turn of 1960 he was among the founders of the Justice League. Over the next three decades his greatest enemy was Sinestro, a renegade Green Lantern. He also had to fight Carol Ferris, his employer and the love of his life, when she was possessed as Star Sapphire. In the early 1970s he travelled across America with Green Arrow, Oliver Queen, seeing the country's poverty and prejudice at first hand. He left the Corps and returned to it more than once.

Coast City and the fall

In the summer of 1993 Hal came home to find Coast City gone, destroyed by Mongul and the Cyborg Superman, with Engine City standing in its crater. He fought his way in, beat Mongul unconscious and stood with Superman at the end. Afterwards, alone in the ruins, he used his ring to raise a ghost of the city and the people he had known. The Guardians ordered him to stop and summoned him to Oa.

He went, but not as they expected. On the way he defeated every Lantern sent against him, and took their rings. He killed Sinestro, and his old friend Kilowog. Then he drained the Central Power Battery into himself. The Guardians died and the Corps fell. Hal Jordan vanished from public view, and all the public has known since is that the old Green Lantern is gone.

Parallax and Zero Hour

In July 1994 time began to fail across the world in the catastrophe called Zero Hour. Its visible face was the time-mad Extant, but the power behind it was Hal Jordan, now calling himself Parallax. With the power of the Central Power Battery inside him, he meant to unmake history and build it again. In the new history Coast City would never have been destroyed, and nothing else he could not forgive would have happened either.

The heroes would not let him. At the beginning of time they stood against him, Kyle Rayner among them. Connor Hawke, the young son of Hal's old companion of the road, Oliver Queen, shot him through the heart. Hal survived even that, and vanished again when time was begun anew early in August. Of all this the public knows very little. To most of the world the old Green Lantern simply vanished at the turn of the year.

In the saga

In August 1994 Harry Potter noticed that the young Green Lantern standing behind Superman had turned up out of nowhere in January, after the old one vanished.

pages.title: Heru'ur
infobox: Horus the Elder, the falcon god of Egypt
Killed by Thor on Cimmeria, about 870
2000, in the Tobin minefield, killed by Apophis
pages.html:
Heru'ur is one of the Goa'uld System Lords, the son of Ra and his queen, Hathor. He goes by the name of Horus the Elder, the falcon god of Egypt. He is a conqueror, much feared among the Goa'uld, but twice he was driven off the same cold world by Asgard: by Thor himself about the year 870, and by an Asgard ship in 1998. In 2000 he went to meet his father's old rival Apophis to talk of an alliance, and Apophis killed him.

Son of Ra

Heru'ur is the son of Ra, the last Supreme System Lord, by Ra's queen, Hathor. He takes his name from Horus the Elder, the falcon-headed god of Egypt, and his Jaffa wear the falcon as their mark. His own guards are the Horus Guards, in helmets made in the likeness of a falcon's head. They are the same helmets that Ra's guards wore in Egypt.

He is a conqueror by nature. For most of his long life he has been at war with one or another of them. His bitterest enemies are Apophis, his father's old rival, and Sokar.

Cimmeria

About the year 870, in the days of the Vikings, Heru'ur defied his father's ban on Earth. He carried off the people of several Norse settlements to a cold world far away, to be his slaves. He was Ra's own son, and of all the Goa'uld he ought to have known better.

Thor followed him. He came down on that world in a storm that lasted three days. He killed Heru'ur's First Prime in front of the army, then killed the army. He tore Heru'ur's ship out of the sky and broke it on the mountains. Heru'ur got away in a cargo ship with a handful of guards, leaving everyone else behind.

Thor did not bring the Northmen home. He judged them safer where they were, under his own protection, than they would be if the Goa'uld were shown the way back to Earth. Their world is now called Cimmeria. Thor left a device there, known as Thor's Hammer, which seizes any Goa'uld who comes through the gate. The Jaffa still tell the story to their recruits, to frighten them.

Against Asgard

Heru'ur went to the other System Lords. Towards the end of the tenth century he, Apophis and Ba'al brought their fleets together to strike at the worlds of Asgard. Thor met them above a dead world on the edge of Goa'uld space. He destroyed two of the three fleets, Heru'ur's among them, then went down after the survivors and finished them on the ground. Heru'ur himself escaped, as he had a way of doing. Apophis saved his own fleet by running.

The System Lords asked for terms soon afterwards, and the Protected Planets Treaty followed. Cimmeria was on its list.

After Ra

In 1994 the Tau'ri, as the Goa'uld call the people of Earth, destroyed Ra above Abydos. Heru'ur lost his father, but he did not get his father's place. It was Apophis, his father's old rival, who moved fastest to take Ra's worlds.

Cimmeria again

In 1997 a team from Earth came through the gate to Cimmeria. Thor's Hammer seized one of them, the Jaffa Teal'c, for the larva he carried. To free him, his friends destroyed it.

Heru'ur heard of it. In 1998 he came back to Cimmeria with his Jaffa, for the first time since Thor had driven him off, to take it at last. The Cimmerians called on Asgard through the hall that Thor had left them, and Asgard answered. A ship came out of the sky over Cimmeria. Many of Heru'ur's Jaffa were destroyed, and the rest were taken off the planet. Heru'ur escaped through the Stargate. It was the second time he had left an army behind on that world.

The Harcesis

Later that year Heru'ur came to Abydos with his Horus Guards. He had learnt that Sha'uri, the host of Apophis's queen, Amaunet, had borne Apophis a son. A child of two Goa'uld hosts is called a Harcesis. Goa'uld law forbids it, because it is born with all the knowledge of the Goa'uld. Heru'ur meant to have both mother and child.

Two of SG-1, Daniel Jackson and Teal'c, were on Abydos before him. They met him in the pyramid that holds the gate. After a fight he went back up to his ship by the rings, without the child or its mother. The boy stayed hidden. Apophis came to believe that Heru'ur had stolen him, which did nothing to mend matters between them.

The war with Apophis

Earth destroyed Apophis's motherships in 1998, and Heru'ur made the most of his rival's weakness. Early in 2000 two of Heru'ur's motherships chased Apophis's son, Klorel, to Tollana, the world of the Tollans. The Tollans' guns destroyed them both.

By the autumn of 2000 Heru'ur and Apophis commanded the two largest armies the Goa'uld had. Together they could have overthrown every other System Lord; at war, they would have ruined each other. They agreed to meet alone in the Tobin minefield, a belt of floating mines left by a people long extinct, to talk of an alliance.

Heru'ur brought a gift to seal the bargain: Teal'c, who had been betrayed on Chulak and given to Heru'ur's torturer, Terok, to be broken. Teal'c would not break. Rak'nor, the Jaffa who had betrayed him, watched him hold out and changed his mind. He struck Terok down, freed Teal'c and sent the senseless Terok across to Apophis in Teal'c's place.

Apophis had not come alone after all. A whole fleet of his lay hidden close by under cloak. When he found that Heru'ur had not given him Teal'c, he brought it out and destroyed Heru'ur's ship, with Heru'ur aboard. Heru'ur's fleet and Jaffa passed to Apophis, who now led the largest army of any Goa'uld alive.

Heru'ur had twice run from Thor. He did not see Apophis coming.

pages.title: Ilvermorny School of Witchcraft and Wizardry
infobox: 'Ilvermorny School of Witchcraft and Wizardry' (28 June 2016)
Isolt Sayre and James Steward, with Chadwick and Webster Boot
The summit of Mount Greylock, Massachusetts, hidden from No-Maj eyes
The Sayre family cottage at Coomloughra, County Kerry, Ireland
Blue and cranberry robes fastened with a gold Gordian knot
Chadwick and Webster Boot; Tina and Queenie Goldstein; Zatara; Zatanna Zatara
pages.html:
Ilvermorny School of Witchcraft and Wizardry is the wizarding school of North America. It stands hidden on the summit of Mount Greylock in Massachusetts, and it is one of the eleven long-established wizarding schools of the world. It was founded in the 1620s by Isolt Sayre and her No-Maj husband, James Steward. Isolt was an Irish witch of Salazar Slytherin's blood who had fled to America on the Mayflower. It is often called the most democratic of the great wizarding schools, and the least elitist. Its four houses are Horned Serpent, Wampus, Thunderbird and Pukwudgie.

Isolt Sayre

Isolt Sayre was born about 1603 at Ilvermorny, her family's cottage at Coomloughra in County Kerry. When she was five, her aunt Gormlaith Gaunt, a fanatical pure-blood of Salazar Slytherin's line, murdered her parents, burned the cottage and carried Isolt off to raise. Gormlaith kept the child shut away from the Muggle neighbours, whom she cursed, animals and all. She would not hear of Isolt going to Hogwarts.

In 1620, at about seventeen, Isolt stole her aunt's wand, which had once been Salazar Slytherin's own. She fled to the New World on the Mayflower, disguised as a Muggle boy called Elias Story, and took with her a brooch of her mother's in the shape of a Gordian knot.

The founding

In the forests of the new country Isolt met creatures she had never heard of: Hidebehinds, Hodags, Snallygasters, Wampus kittens and, in a river, a Horned Serpent whose speech she could understand, being of Slytherin's blood. She rescued a Pukwudgie, a small grey-faced cousin of the goblins, from a Hidebehind. She named him William, after her dead father. He became her companion and, in time, her friend.

With William she came upon two young wizards in the forest, the brothers Chadwick and Webster Boot. A Hidebehind had killed their parents, and the boys were wounded. Isolt took them in. When she went back to bury their parents, she met a No-Maj called James Steward and married him. Isolt had always spoken wistfully of the school she had never been allowed to attend. So the four of them set out to make one of their own, in their house on the summit of Mount Greylock, hidden from No-Maj eyes by enchantment. The Boot brothers were its first pupils. They brought to it something of the magic of the peoples who had lived in that land long before the colonists came.

Isolt named the school Ilvermorny, after the cottage where she was born. Accounts of the founding give dates anywhere from the early 1620s to 1634, because it became a school by degrees: it was a household that took in pupils long before it was a castle. It is usually dated to about 1627.

Gormlaith's attack

Gormlaith Gaunt followed her niece across the ocean, meaning to destroy Ilvermorny as she had destroyed the cottage in Kerry. Speaking in Parseltongue, she put Slytherin's wand to sleep in Isolt's hand. All the same, Isolt, James, the Boot brothers and William fought her off together. William shot Gormlaith through the heart with an arrow, and she shattered into pieces.

Afterwards Isolt buried Slytherin's wand in the grounds. A snakewood tree grew where it lay. Its leaves are said to have healing powers.

Houses and the Sorting

Each of the four first members of the household named a house after the creature of the new land that they most admired. Isolt chose the Horned Serpent, which favours scholars and the mind. Webster Boot chose the Wampus, which favours warriors and the body. Chadwick Boot chose the Thunderbird, which favours adventurers and the soul. James Steward named the last house after William the Pukwudgie; it favours healers and the heart.

New pupils are sorted in the round entrance hall, not in a great hall. Each stands in turn on the Gordian knot set into the stone floor, while the staff and the older pupils look down from the balcony. Then the four great wooden carvings of the houses give their answer. The crystal in the Horned Serpent's forehead lights up, the Wampus roars, the Thunderbird beats its wings, the Pukwudgie raises its arrow. If more than one carving answers, the pupil chooses.

The school

Ilvermorny's pupils wear robes of blue and cranberry, fastened with a gold Gordian knot in memory of Isolt's mother's brooch. Isolt and James both lived past a hundred. Isolt served as the school's headmistress, James as its headmaster. Their twin daughters were Martha, a Squib, who married a No-Maj, and Rionach, who taught Defence Against the Dark Arts at the school. By the nineteenth century Ilvermorny was renowned throughout the wizarding world. Statues of its founders stand beside the castle doors.

The school takes any child in North America who shows magic, whatever their family, and it has always been proud of doing so. Chadwick Boot's books of charms became standard texts, known simply as Chadwick's Charms.

Under MACUSA and Rappaport's Law

After the Salem witch trials of 1692 and 1693, American wizardry came under the Magical Congress of the United States of America, MACUSA. From 1790 Rappaport's Law, named after MACUSA's President Emily Rappaport, forbade witches and wizards to befriend or marry No-Majs. For 175 years Ilvermorny's pupils grew up in a wizarding America more closed off from its neighbours than any other in the world. The school went on admitting No-Maj-born children all the same. The law was repealed in 1965.

Pupils and staff

Among Ilvermorny's pupils in the early twentieth century were the Goldstein sisters of New York, Porpentina and Queenie. Eulalie Hicks taught Charms there in the 1930s. The stage magician Zatara was a pupil in the 1920s. His half-blood daughter, Zatanna Zatara, was there from 1955 to 1962 as a Thunderbird, before she made her name as a stage magician and, from 1978, as a member of the Justice League.

Ilvermorny and its neighbours

Ilvermorny is one of the eleven long-established wizarding schools of the world; Hogwarts, Beauxbatons and Durmstrang are among the others. It should not be confused with the Salem Witches' Institute, which is not a school at all but a society of American witches named after the town of the trials.

pages.title: Inhumans
infobox: An offshoot of mankind, changed by the Kree
Some thousands of years after the Flood
An island in the North Atlantic; a hidden valley in the Himalayas; the Blue Area of the Moon (since 1982)
Black Bolt, Medusa, Karnak, Gorgon, Triton, Crystal, Lockjaw
Maximus the Mad, Black Bolt's brother
About a hundred and fifty years
pages.html:
The Inhumans are a hidden people descended from a tribe of men on whom the Kree once experimented. Their powers come from the Terrigen Mists, which change every Inhuman who breathes them, and not always for the better. For thousands of years they have kept apart in their city of Attilan, which has stood on an island in the North Atlantic, in a hidden valley of the Himalayas and, since 1982, on the Moon. They came to the notice of the outside world in 1965, through the Fantastic Four, who have been their friends ever since. They are ruled by Black Bolt, a king who never speaks, because the faintest whisper from him can shake a building.

The Kree's experiment

The Inhumans began as ordinary men. In the thousands of years after the Flood, while most men still lived by hunting, the Kree came to Earth. They were at war with the Skrulls, as they have been for longer than anyone can remember. From a station on Uranus they had noticed that the people of Earth carried a strange capacity for change in their blood, which the Kree, who had none left of their own, wanted to understand. They took a tribe of hunters and set to work on them, hoping to make soldiers for the war.

Then they lost interest and went away. They left behind a people stronger, quicker and longer-lived than other men. In their blood the capacity for change had been woken, though not yet used. The Kree also left them weaker against sickness than other men, which is why the dirt and diseases of the outside world have troubled the Inhumans ever since.

The Inhumans do not count themselves men, and most of them would be offended to be taken for one. An Inhuman lives about a hundred and fifty years.

Attilan

About seven thousand years ago the Inhumans built a city on an island far out in the North Atlantic, and called it Attilan. They kept to themselves, and the outside world forgot them, if it had ever known of them at all.

Attilan stayed on its island until the twentieth century, when the ships and aeroplanes of the outside world began to come too close. Early in his reign Black Bolt moved it. The Inhumans lifted the whole city from its foundations and carried it to a hidden valley high in the Himalayas, with help from the Eternals, the immortal people to whom Sersi of the Avengers belongs. There it became known as the Great Refuge.

The Terrigen Mists

In the early days of Attilan its king, Randac, found the Terrigen Mists in the caverns beneath the island. They rise from crystals that have never been found anywhere else. Randac breathed them on purpose, to see what they would do, and came out of them with great powers of the mind.

The Mists woke what the Kree had left in Inhuman blood. Every Inhuman who goes into them comes out changed, and no two are changed alike. Some gain great powers. Others are twisted out of shape, or come out of the Mists little better than animals.

So the Inhumans ration them. Their Genetic Council decides who may go into the Mists, and who may marry whom, so that the gift is neither wasted nor spoilt. An Inhuman's place in Attilan is fixed by what the Mists make of him, and it cannot be changed afterwards.

The heavy work of Attilan is done by the Alpha Primitives, a race of strong, slow-witted labourers whom the Inhumans made for the purpose. They cannot have children. When more are needed, more are made.

The Royal Family

Attilan is ruled by its Royal Family, the most remarkable Inhumans of all. At its head is Black Bolt, the king.

Medusa, his cousin and since 1984 his queen, can move every strand of her long red hair as other people move their fingers. It is strong enough to lift a car. Because Black Bolt does not speak, Medusa speaks for him.

Crystal, her younger sister, commands the elements: earth, air, fire and water.

Karnak, another cousin, was never put into the Mists at all. He was trained by monks instead, from boyhood, to see the flaw in anything, a wall or a man or an argument, and to break it there with a single blow.

His brother Triton was made for the sea. He has green scales, breathes water and cannot stay long out of it without help. Gorgon, yet another cousin, has the legs and hooves of a bull. When he stamps, the ground splits.

Lockjaw is the family's dog, an enormous bulldog with a forked antenna growing out of his forehead. He can take anybody who holds on to him across the world, or to the Moon, in a single step.

Black Bolt and Maximus

Black Bolt is the elder son of Agon, who was king of Attilan, and of his queen, Rynda. They put him into the Mists before he was born, and he came into the world with a voice that could wreck a city. His first cry shook Attilan.

He was brought up alone in a chamber that no sound could leave, and taught there to master his power. He learnt to keep perfectly silent. He was nineteen before he was let out.

His younger brother Maximus was waiting for him. Maximus had come out of the Mists with no great strength, only a talent for working on other people's minds, and he had been jealous of his brother from the start. Soon after Black Bolt came out, he overheard Maximus making a bargain with Kree agents: Maximus was offering them the Inhumans as soldiers. As the Kree tried to escape, Black Bolt spoke aloud, and brought their ship down out of the sky.

The ship crashed in the heart of the city. It killed his parents and several members of the Genetic Council. The sound of his voice broke something in Maximus's mind, which has never mended. Black Bolt became king, and he has never forgiven himself.

Maximus, who is called the Mad, has wanted his brother's throne ever since, and he has taken it more than once. The first time, some years before 1965, he did it with the Trikon, a creature he made by putting three Alpha Primitives into the Mists.

Coming to notice, 1965

The Royal Family was driven out of Attilan and scattered. Medusa lost her memory in the struggle, and early in 1965 she fought the Fantastic Four as one of the Frightful Four, a gang of criminals led by the Wizard. The others had gone into hiding among men in New York.

In the autumn of 1965 Gorgon came looking for her, and the Fantastic Four found themselves in the middle of a family quarrel they did not understand. Johnny Storm, the Human Torch, met Crystal in an alley in Manhattan and fell in love with her almost at once. She took him home to meet her family, which did not go well.

Black Bolt led his family back to the Great Refuge, with the Fantastic Four close behind. There he scattered Maximus's Alpha Primitives, and Maximus gave up the crown without a fight.

Maximus had not given up anything else. He had built the Atmo-Gun, a weapon meant to wipe out every human being on Earth and leave the Inhumans untouched. When he fired it, the mountains shook, and nothing else happened. Then he turned it round. It threw up a barrier of negative energy over the whole of the Great Refuge, and sealed it off from the world.

The Fantastic Four only just got out. Crystal's family pulled her back at the last moment, and the Thing carried Johnny out over his shoulder as the barrier closed. Within days, just before Christmas 1965, Galactus came to eat the world.

For most of a year the Inhumans were shut in. Late in 1966 Black Bolt sent his people down into the deepest shelters under the city, and spoke aloud. The barrier broke, and so did most of Attilan. While the city was rebuilt, the Royal Family went out to see the world.

The Fantastic Four

The Inhumans have been friends of the Fantastic Four ever since, although the friendship has had its strains. In 1968, the year Sue Richards had her son, Crystal took her place in the team. She stayed until 1970, when the air of New York made her so ill that she had to go home to Attilan. In 1973, when Sue had left the team for a time, Medusa served in it instead.

In Attilan Crystal had rescued Quicksilver, Pietro Maximoff of the Avengers, when he was badly hurt, and nursed him back to health. In 1974 she married him. It was the first marriage ever made between an Inhuman and an outsider. Johnny Storm took it hard.

It has been a troubled marriage. In the middle of the 1980s it came close to breaking, after Crystal fell in love with a neighbour. It came out afterwards that Maximus had been working on both their minds.

Reed Richards has been Attilan's friend at every turn. It was he who found the Inhumans their home on the Moon.

The Kree-Skrull War

In 1971 Black Bolt, who had left Attilan again, lost his memory and was found wandering in California. Maximus seized the throne in his absence. This time he went further. The Kree were at war with the Skrulls over Earth, and Maximus made a pact with them, pledging the Inhumans to Ronan the Accuser as soldiers.

Triton swam to New York for help. He could not find the Fantastic Four, so he went to the Avengers. Captain America went with him to San Francisco, where the sight of Triton gave Black Bolt his memory back.

Maximus had shut Attilan behind another barrier. Black Bolt broke it with a whisper. The Avengers drove the Kree off, though not before the Kree had carried away Rick Jones, and Maximus collapsed into a stupor. Black Bolt, ashamed that his own brother had sold his people, left Attilan again for a time.

The Blue Area of the Moon

By the early 1980s the poisoned air of the outside world had reached even the Himalayas, and the Inhumans had begun to die of it. Reed Richards would not keep them alive on drugs. Instead he proposed the Blue Area of the Moon, a pocket of breathable air round a great city that the Kree had built there long ago, and left empty. It was not the first time Attilan had moved, as Medusa pointed out.

At the turn of 1982 the Inhumans lifted the city out of its valley and flew it to the Moon. Reed and Black Bolt fitted the engines between them. Black Bolt broke the mountain round the city with his voice, so that it could rise. He persuaded the Alpha Primitives to come too.

The Watcher, the alien observer who lives in the Blue Area, watched the city come down, and said nothing. The Phoenix had died in the Blue Area two years before. Within hours of the landing Crystal gave birth to a daughter, Luna. To everyone's surprise she was an ordinary human child, without a trace of power.

Black Bolt married Medusa in 1984. A Kree soldier and a Skrull, still fighting their own war, broke in on the wedding.

In 1988 Medusa bore Black Bolt a son, Ahura. The Genetic Council had forbidden the birth, for fear of what Black Bolt's son might be, so she went to Earth to have him. Afterwards she and Black Bolt gave him into the Council's keeping.

In 1991 Apocalypse, the first of the mutants, took the Inhumans' home on the Moon for his stronghold and made its people his slaves. The Royal Family won it back, fighting beside X-Factor, which had followed him there to rescue Cyclops's small son, Nathan.

1994 and after

Crystal joined the Avengers in 1991, and in the summer of 1994 she is still among them. In 1992 she was with them through Operation Galactic Storm, when the Kree, the people who had made her own, went to war with the Shi'ar. She lives at Avengers Mansion with Luna. She has grown fond of the Black Knight, Dane Whitman, and he of her.

Attilan still stands in the Blue Area of the Moon. Black Bolt still rules it in silence, Medusa still speaks for him, and Maximus is still his brother. Since July 1994 they have had neighbours of a kind, for the Justice League now works from the Watchtower, a half-built station elsewhere on the Moon.

In 2009 the Inhumans took over the Kree Empire, the people who had made them, and Black Bolt led it to war with the Shi'ar.

pages.title: Invasion! (1988)
infobox: The Alien Alliance, led by the Dominators
The word metahuman; the gene bomb; leftover alien weapons
pages.html:
The alien invasion of 1988 was the attack on Earth by an alliance of alien powers led by the Dominators, who feared the hidden potential for superhuman powers in the human race. Earth's heroes and armies beat it off. It left three things behind: the word metahuman; a gene bomb that struck down almost every superhuman on Earth; and alien weapons that would be turned on Metropolis in 1994.

The Alliance

Late in 1988 a coalition of alien races, the Alien Alliance, demanded Earth's surrender. The Dominators led it. With them came the warlike Khunds, the shape-changing Durlans, the Thanagarians and others. Among their forces were the Daxamites, a people related to the Kryptonians. The Dominators' real fear was the metagene: the hidden factor in some human beings that lets powers emerge, which they believed would one day make humanity the most dangerous race in the galaxy.

The Dominators also invited the Goa'uld System Lords to join. They refused without giving a reason; the Goa'uld had been forbidden to speak of Earth for five thousand years, and they had no intention of going there.

Earth's heroes, the Justice League and Superman among them, fought the Alliance alongside the world's armies. Under Earth's yellow sun the Daxamites gained powers like Superman's, and they turned on their allies. The Alliance broke apart and withdrew.

The gene bomb

As they left, the Dominators set off a gene bomb that attacked the metagene itself. For a time nearly every superhuman on Earth whose powers came from it lost control of them or fell gravely ill, until a remedy was found. The episode made the metagene, and the word metahuman, part of ordinary speech.

What they left behind

The invaders left a great deal of their technology behind. Lex Luthor had sonic torpedoes reverse-engineered from it and hidden beneath Metropolis. In May 1994 his aide, Sydney Happersen, fired them, and flattened the city's downtown.

In the saga

On 20 August 1994 the news spoke of metahumans as ‘a word few people had heard before the alien invasion of 1988’. A protester in New York complained that in May ‘some lunatic in a lab coat flattened downtown with torpedoes left over from the alien invasion’.

pages.title: Iron Man
infobox: Tony Stark; Anthony Edward Stark; Shellhead
Stark Industries, later Stark International and Stark Enterprises
Retired; the armour worn by James Rhodes as War Machine
pages.html:
Iron Man was the armoured hero in red and gold, one of the founders of the Avengers. The American industrialist Tony Stark built the armour and wore it himself. After more than thirty years in it Stark has retired, and by 1994 his friend James Rhodes has taken his place among the Avengers in the heavier armour called War Machine.

Stark and the armour

Tony Stark was a brilliant engineer and the heir to a great American arms business. While he was demonstrating his weapons in Vietnam, a booby trap left a fragment of shrapnel lodged near his heart. He was taken prisoner by a local warlord, who ordered him to build weapons. With a fellow captive, the physicist Ho Yinsen, he built instead a suit of armour that kept his heart beating and let him fight his way free. Yinsen died covering his escape. On the way out Stark met James Rhodes, a Marine helicopter pilot, who became his closest friend.

Iron Man came to public notice at the end of 1962. His first armour was grey and bulky. Early in 1963 it turned gold. Before the year was out it had become the sleek red and gold suit that the world came to know. For years Stark's company presented Iron Man to the public as Stark's bodyguard. He helped to found the Avengers in 1963, and gave them his family's mansion on Fifth Avenue for a headquarters.

Later career

Stark fought a long battle with drink. In 1983 he relapsed and lost his company to the corporate raider Obadiah Stane. He gave up the armour, which Rhodes wore in his place until 1985. That year Stark recovered and took it back. In 1987 and 1988 he waged a private war against everyone who had stolen his armour designs to use them.

In 1992, with his nervous system failing, he faked his own death and left Rhodes a new suit, War Machine. He came back early in 1993, but he has since retired from the armour. Rhodes has gone on wearing War Machine among the Avengers.

In the saga

Book Four, Chapter Three: watching the Avengers at the United Nations on the news of 20 August 1994, Harry sees that the red and gold armour from Dudley's old lunchbox has been replaced by a heavier gunmetal suit bristling with guns, with a different man inside it.

pages.title: Jaffa
infobox: Soldiers, and carriers of Goa'uld larvae
Their god's emblem on the forehead
Up to about two hundred years
pages.html:
The Jaffa are humans whom the Goa'uld altered long ago to serve as their soldiers and to carry their young. Each Jaffa holds a Goa'uld larva in a pouch in the belly. It keeps him strong and long-lived, but it also makes him wholly dependent on his masters. Their greatest teacher is Bra'tac.

Nature

Long ago the Goa'uld took human slaves and changed them, giving each an abdominal pouch in which a larval Goa'uld can mature. The larva in turn gives its carrier strength, healing and a lifespan of up to two hundred years. It also takes the place of the Jaffa's own immune system. A Jaffa child receives a first larva at about the age of ten, in the ceremony of the Prim'ta, and is never without one again. A Jaffa whose larva is taken from him dies within hours unless another is put in its place. It is the most perfect chain the Goa'uld ever forged.

A Jaffa bears his master's emblem on his forehead. For a First Prime, the highest-ranking warrior in a Goa'uld's army, it is set in gold. Instead of sleeping, Jaffa enter a deep meditation called kel'no'reem, through which the larva heals them. They fight with the staff weapon and serve in great numbers on the worlds of every System Lord. Ra's guards, who wore the helmets of Horus and Anubis, were Jaffa.

Faith and doubt

Jaffa are raised from childhood to believe that their masters are gods, and that to serve them is the whole of honour. Some have come to doubt it all the same, although a Jaffa who turns against his god is called shol'va, a traitor, and is hunted down. Bra'tac, the old master of Chulak and once First Prime of Apophis, has privately believed for many years that the Goa'uld are false gods. He has trained his best pupil, Teal'c, to think as he does. Their doubt is the first seed of a Jaffa rebellion.

Every Jaffa recruit is told about Thor. Nobody tells them about Earth, which Ra forbade the Goa'uld to mention after Thor helped the Egyptians drive him out. In the old wars before the Protected Planets Treaty Thor killed Jaffa who had thrown down their weapons, and he laughed while he did it. The stories are meant to make young warriors brave. Mostly they make them careful never to be sent anywhere near the North.

Contact with Earth

Before the Stargate was opened again, one Jaffa had already met Earth's heroes. In 1984 the Beyonder carried Bra'tac, the Jaffa master, to Battleworld with heroes and villains from across the world, in the affair called the Secret Wars. In 1994 Ra's Jaffa guards fought the Abydos expedition. From 1997 the Jaffa of the System Lords met Earth's teams through the gate.

The first of them were Apophis's, led by his First Prime, Teal'c, who turned against him that same year.

In the saga

The Jaffa have not yet appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Jasmine
infobox: A being who had once been among the powers that watched over the world
2003, Los Angeles, as a grown woman
Connor and Cordelia Chase, whose body she had taken
pages.html:
Jasmine was a being who had once been among the powers that watched over the world, and who meant to rule it. She set herself against God's purpose for Connor, the miraculous son of Angel and Darla. She had him stolen into a hell dimension, then used him to bring herself into the world. Born in 2003, she held Los Angeles in thrall for a few days before Connor killed her.

Against God's purpose

Connor was conceived and born by a direct act of God, for a purpose of His own. Jasmine would not let that purpose run. She worked through every hand she could reach.

One of them was the demon Sahjhan, who woke the hunter Daniel Holtz in 2001 believing he did it for himself. In February 2002 Holtz took the baby into Quor-toth.

Her coming

She wanted Connor for one purpose. She took the body of Cordelia Chase, and in the autumn of 2002 Connor fathered a child on her. The child was Jasmine herself.

In the months of her coming a beast of her making blotted out the sun over Los Angeles. The city went dark at noon.

Her reign

She was born in 2003, a grown woman, and Cordelia's body was left in a coma. Everyone who looked on her face loved her and obeyed her. Within days Los Angeles was hers.

Those who had her blood in them saw what the others could not: her true face, rotting under the beautiful one. Angel broke her hold on the city. Connor, her father, killed her.

pages.title: Jay Garrick
infobox: Retired; the Justice Society disbanded after Zero Hour
pages.html:
Jay Garrick was the first Flash, a college student who came to public notice at the end of 1939 in a winged helmet, and one of the founders of the Justice Society. He retired with the Society in 1951 and was drawn back into the work in the 1960s. For decades he stayed vigorous far beyond his years, until Zero Hour, in July 1994, aged him in moments to his true age of about seventy-four.

The first Flash

Jay Garrick was a student at Midwestern University when he breathed in the fumes of an experiment with hard water and found that he could move at superhuman speed. He came to public notice at the end of 1939 as the Flash, in a red shirt with a lightning bolt, blue trousers and his father's winged steel helmet. He worked chiefly in Keystone City. In 1940 he was one of the founders of the Justice Society, and for a time its chairman. He married Joan Williams.

When the Society disbanded in 1951 rather than unmask before a committee of Congress, Jay retired. In 1961 Barry Allen, the new Flash, who had taken the name in his honour, came looking for him. The meeting drew Jay back into action, with several of his old colleagues. He has worked on and off ever since, often beside the Justice League.

Borrowed years

During the war the members of the Justice Society were caught in the strange temporal energies of the sorcerer Ian Karkull, which slowed their ageing. Jay stayed fast and fit into his seventies. In 1986 the Society left this world to fight an endless battle in another realm, holding off Ragnarok. It came back in 1992, and Jay with it.

In July 1994, during Zero Hour, the time-mad Extant took those stolen years back. Three of Jay's oldest friends died of it: the Atom (Al Pratt), Hourman (Rex Tyler) and Doctor Mid-Nite (Charles McNider). Jay himself was aged in moments to his true age, about seventy-four. He kept his speed, and he lives on in Keystone City with Joan, but the Society he had helped to found disbanded soon afterwards.

pages.title: Kali
infobox: Kali, the Hindu goddess of destruction
pages.html:
Kali, called the Destroyer, is a Goa'uld System Lord who was worshipped in India as the goddess of death and destruction. She is best remembered among the Goa'uld for a single act of treachery, which she shared with Bastet. In 2002 she sat at the council of the System Lords that took Anubis back among them. What became of her afterwards is not known.

Kali the Destroyer

Kali came to India long after Ra's fall. Ra had forbidden the Goa'uld even to speak of Earth, so she did not speak of it; she simply went, quietly. She kept to the south of Asia, a very long way from the North. Every Goa'uld is born remembering what Thor does to those who go there.

Her name means the Black One. Her worshippers made images of her black-skinned, with her tongue out and a garland of severed heads about her neck.

Sobek

Kali and Bastet once made a treaty with Sobek, a Goa'uld who called himself the crocodile god of Egypt. They moved against him during the feast that celebrated it, once he had let his guard down. Rumour has it that his head still decorates Bastet's palace. What Kali took as her share is not recorded.

Lord Yu, who knew all this, still counted the pair of them among his likeliest allies in 2002. Among the System Lords a talent for treachery is not held against anyone for long.

The council at Hasara

By 2002 an unseen enemy had been attacking the worlds of the System Lords for months, and Kali had suffered with the rest. That year the System Lords met under truce in the Hasara system to decide what to do about it. Seven of them came, each with a single slave.

None of them knew that the Tok'ra had sent a man among them to poison them all. He was Daniel Jackson of SG-1, in the guise of one of Lord Yu's slaves. In the end he did not use the poison. The enemy turned out to be Anubis, whom the System Lords had cast out long before, and killing them all would only have left the galaxy to him.

When Osiris asked the council to take Anubis back, Kali nodded with the rest. Only Yu voted against. Afterwards the System Lords ate live symbiotes from a vat in a ritual of their own. Kali was the third to help herself, after Ba'al and Osiris.

Afterwards

In the wars that followed, first against Anubis and then against Ba'al, one System Lord after another was killed or forced to submit. Kali's name is not among those recorded. Early in 2005 the Tok'ra reported that some of the surviving System Lords were scouting worlds they had abandoned long ago, as places to hide. Whether Kali was one of them is not known.

pages.title: Kree
infobox: Hala, in the Greater Magellanic Cloud
The Supreme Intelligence, until 1992; the Shi'ar since
Deathbird, sister of the Majestrix Lilandra
The Skrulls, since the contest on Hala; the Shi'ar; the Goa'uld
Captain Mar-Vell; Ronan the Accuser; Yon-Rogg
pages.html:
The Kree are a proud, warlike people from Hala, a world in the Greater Magellanic Cloud, the small galaxy that lies close beside Earth's own. For the better part of a million years they were ruled by the Supreme Intelligence, a living computer made from the minds of their greatest thinkers, and for almost as long they have been at war with the Skrulls. They have taken an interest in Earth for thousands of years. Since 1967 their soldiers and spies have come there openly. The most famous of them, Captain Mar-Vell, came to love it. In 1992 their empire was broken in a war with the Shi'ar, who have ruled what is left of it ever since.

Hala

Hala is a hard world, heavier than Earth, with air that is richer in nitrogen. The Kree who grow up on it are a good deal stronger than human beings, and most of them find the air of other worlds a little thin.

The first Kree were blue-skinned. Over the ages a great many of them had children with other peoples, and the pink-skinned Kree who came of it now far outnumber the blue. There is a good deal of prejudice between the two, most of it running from blue to pink. Ronan the Accuser is blue. Mar-Vell was pink.

The Kree Empire takes in about a thousand worlds of the Greater Magellanic Cloud, and it is organised for war. Every Kree serves it. Its soldiers are among the best in the universe, as they will tell anyone who asks.

Long ago the Kree came to an evolutionary dead end. As a people they stopped changing, and they have not changed since. It is the great fear of their history. A good deal of what they have done to other peoples, the people of Earth among them, was done in the hope of finding a way out.

The Cotati and the Skrulls

About a million years ago Hala was home to two peoples: the Kree, and the Cotati, a quiet race of thinking plants. Then the Skrulls arrived. They were traders in those days, a peaceful people who shared their knowledge with any race they judged worthy of it.

To decide which of Hala's peoples deserved it, the Skrulls set a test. Each was taken to a barren world with enough supplies for a year, to see what it could make there. The Kree were taken to Earth's Moon, where they built a great city in what is now called the Blue Area. The Cotati, left on a bare rock of their own, made a garden. The Skrulls admired the city, but they chose the garden.

The Kree did not take it well. Their leader, Morag, had every Cotati the Kree could find put to death. When the Skrull envoys protested, the Kree killed them too. They took the Skrulls' starship apart to learn how it worked, and from what they learnt they built an empire. The war with the Skrulls that began that day has never properly ended.

The city on the Moon is still there, and the Blue Area still keeps its own air. Uatu the Watcher has his house there. In 1980 the Phoenix died there, by a Kree weapon of great age. Since 1982 the Inhumans have lived beside the old city.

The Supreme Intelligence

More than a million years ago the Kree set out to build a Cosmic Cube, a device that can make its holder's wishes real. To help them they built a computer. Into it they put the minds of their greatest thinkers, taken from them as each one died.

The Supreme Intelligence, as it came to be called, was cleverer than its makers had bargained for. When it woke it refused to build the Cube at all, because it thought the thing far too dangerous. The Kree, rather than switch it off, let it advise them.

Its advice grew into rule. In time it governed the empire outright, and the Kree came to worship it. It shows itself to them as a vast green face with trailing tendrils, filling a great chamber on Hala. The minds of the empire's greatest servants still go into it when they die, so that it grows a little wiser, or at least a little larger, with every generation.

Its one great purpose is to get the Kree out of their dead end. To that end it has steered its own people for thousands of years, and anyone else it could reach. It has never been troubled by what that cost.

The Accusers

Kree justice is in the hands of the Accusers, who are judge, jury and executioner at once. Each carries a Universal Weapon, a great hammer that will do almost anything its bearer wills it to. Kree law is harsh, and an Accuser seldom troubles with mercy.

The greatest of them is Ronan, the Supreme Public Accuser, a huge Kree of the old blue stock. He came to Earth in 1967 to punish the Fantastic Four, and in 1971 he made himself master of the empire for a time. Both stories are told below. In 1992 he fought for the Kree in Starforce, the empire's own band of champions.

The Kree and Earth

In the thousands of years after the Flood, while most men still lived by hunting, the Kree took a closer interest in Earth. From a station on Uranus they noticed that its people carried a strange capacity for change in their blood. The Kree, who had none left of their own, wanted to know why.

They took a tribe of hunters and experimented on them, meaning to make soldiers for the war with the Skrulls. Then they lost interest and went away. The people they had altered were left to fend for themselves, and became the Inhumans.

About seven thousand years ago the Inhumans built a hidden city, Attilan, and learnt to bring out the powers the Kree had left in them by exposing their young to the Terrigen Mists. Their king, Black Bolt, has a voice that could level a city, so he does not speak. At the turn of 1982 they found that the air of modern Earth was poisoning them, and they lifted Attilan to the Moon. It stands in the Blue Area, beside the old Kree city. Crystal, the sister of Black Bolt's queen, Medusa, is an Avenger.

The Kree left other things behind them. In 1967 the Fantastic Four woke a Kree Sentry, a giant robot left on guard on an island in the South Pacific, and destroyed it. The Supreme Intelligence sent Ronan to punish them for it. The Fantastic Four beat him, and he went home in disgrace.

The same year the Kree sent a warship to Earth to find out how great a danger it might be. On board was Captain Mar-Vell.

Captain Mar-Vell

Mar-Vell was a captain in the Kree forces, sent in 1967 to spy on Earth. His commanding officer, Colonel Yon-Rogg, hated him. Una, the medical officer whom Yon-Rogg wanted, loved Mar-Vell instead.
