Mar-Vell went down to Earth as Walter Lawson, a scientist who had died, and took work at the rocket base at Cape Kennedy. Its head of security was Carol Danvers. People on Earth heard his name as Marvel, and soon called him Captain Marvel.

He did not keep to his orders for long. The more he saw of the people he was spying on, the better he liked them. In the end he took their side against his own, and the Kree branded him a traitor.

In 1969 he was bound to Rick Jones, the teenager whose life Bruce Banner had once saved, by a pair of Kree bracelets called the Nega-Bands. Only one of them could be in the world at a time. While Mar-Vell fought, Rick waited in the Negative Zone, a universe of antimatter beside this one; when Rick struck the bands together, they changed places.

The same year Carol Danvers was caught with him in the blast of a Kree machine, the Psyche-Magnitron. It changed her. In late 1976 she came out as Ms Marvel, with powers that had come from the machine.

In 1971, while the Avengers sheltered him, S.H.I.E.L.D. hunted him and Carol during the Kree-Skrull War, which is described below. From 1973 to 1974 he fought Thanos, the Mad Titan, for the Cosmic Cube, and in the end he broke its power. During that war the cosmic being Eon made him Protector of the Universe.

In 1974 he breathed in a cloud of nerve gas while stopping the villain Nitro from stealing it. It seemed to do him no harm. Years later it gave him cancer.

He died of it in 1982, among his friends on Titan, the moon of Saturn. Before the end a delegation of Skrulls came to his bedside. Their general saluted him and gave him the Skrull Medal of Valour, as the greatest enemy their empire had ever faced. Death came for him in person, and Thanos, who had died himself in 1977, came with her as her servant.

The name of Captain Marvel has since passed to Monica Rambeau, a harbour patrol officer from New Orleans, who has no Kree in her at all.

The Kree-Skrull War

In 1971 the old war came to Earth. Ronan the Accuser overthrew the Supreme Intelligence, and set out to deal with Earth himself. Under a plan he called Atavus, he meant to turn the planet back into a prehistoric world and use it as a base against the Skrulls.

He had reduced a handful of scientists to cavemen when word came of a Skrull attack on Hala. He dropped the plan and went home.

The Skrulls had come to Earth for Mar-Vell. One of them, the Super-Skrull, took the shape of Carol Danvers, and talked him into building an Omni-Wave Projector, a Kree device that becomes a deadly weapon in anyone else's hands. Mar-Vell saw through the trick and destroyed it. The Super-Skrull carried him off into space all the same, with Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch as prisoners.

On Earth, Senator H. Warren Craddock's Alien Activities Commission was turning the public against the Avengers for sheltering him. Three men who looked like Captain America, Thor and Iron Man announced that the team was disbanded. They were Skrulls.

The Inhumans had troubles of their own. Black Bolt's brother, Maximus, had seized Attilan with Kree help, meaning to make his people into soldiers for the Kree. The Avengers put Black Bolt back on his throne, then went out into Skrull space after their friends.

There the Skrulls made Mar-Vell build a second projector by threatening to kill their prisoners. While the Avengers held off the Skrull fleet, he used it, and the blast threw Rick Jones back into the Negative Zone.

The war was ended by the Supreme Intelligence, which had been quietly steering events all along. It reached into the Negative Zone for Rick and woke a power in him that had lain hidden all his life, the Destiny Force. Out of his memory came the heroes of the 1940s, to fight beside the Avengers. Then the force froze every Kree and every Skrull where they stood.

The Supreme Intelligence took back its empire. It told the Avengers that the Kree had come to an evolutionary dead end, and that Rick had been part of its plan for getting them out of it. On Earth the Destiny Force turned Senator Craddock back into his true shape, which was a Skrull's. A mob killed him.

The war flared up again in 1987, far from Earth. When the Supreme Intelligence lost its reason for a time, a Kree officer called Nenora took command of the empire. She turned out to be a Skrull spy. In 1989 the Skrull Empress S'Byll reached her in the Kree throne room and unmasked her. The war ended soon afterwards, in a ceasefire that the Skrulls had rather the better of.

Galactic Storm

In 1991 two Kree generals, Ael-Dan and Dar-Benn, seized the empire, pushing the Supreme Intelligence aside. The next year they were at war with the Shi'ar.

Both empires were moving their fleets through a great gateway in space that lay inside Earth's own solar system, and the strain on it was beginning to unsettle the Sun. The Avengers went out to stop the war. One team went to the Shi'ar while another guarded Earth. Captain America took the third to Hala.

On Hala the Avengers and Starforce were caught in a field of energy, unable to move. Before their eyes Deathbird, Lilandra's sister, killed Ael-Dan, then Dar-Benn. Their deaths gave the empire back to the Supreme Intelligence, which may well have been the idea.

The Shi'ar had built a weapon from Kree devices, the Nega-Bomb, to use against the Kree. Lilandra ordered it carried into Kree space. Then she learnt that a Skrull in the shape of her chancellor, Araki, had done a good deal to start the war, and she called it back. She was too late. Skrull agents had stolen it, and it went off inside the Kree Empire.

Billions of Kree died in a moment, by most counts nine in every ten of them.

Captain America's team found out why on Hala. The Supreme Intelligence had steered the whole war, the bomb included, to shock the survivors out of their dead end. It had played the two sisters, Lilandra and Deathbird, against each other as well.

Some of the Avengers wanted it dead. Captain America put it to a vote, which went against killing it, and forbade it. Iron Man, as a founder of the team, would not be bound. He executed it all the same, with the Black Knight, Hercules, Sersi, the Vision, Wonder Man and Eric Masterson, who was then serving as Thor.

The Shi'ar took over what was left of the Kree Empire, and Lilandra made Deathbird its viceroy. In the summer of 1994 she still rules the Kree from Hala, and the Kree still resent every day of it. The Supreme Intelligence is believed to be dead.

The Goa'uld

For thousands of years the Kree frontier has run against the Goa'uld's, at the edge of the galaxy. The Goa'uld count the Kree as their oldest neighbours, and the ones they like least. The Kree, when they think of the Goa'uld at all, think of them as vermin.

Long ago a Goa'uld took the body of a Kree officer. The Supreme Intelligence answered by having the world where it happened burnt down to the bedrock, with the Kree garrison still on it. The Goa'uld have never tried it again.

Since then the Accusers have put more Goa'uld to death than anyone except Thor. To an Accuser a Goa'uld in a stolen body is a crime that needs no trial, and Accusers do not hold many trials in any case.

In 1992, while the Kree Empire lay in ruins, Goa'uld ships came to pick over its frontier. The Shi'ar Imperial Guard drove them off in an afternoon.

Later history

The Supreme Intelligence was not dead. It had hidden its mind away from the Avengers, and in 1997 it came back. In time it took up the rule of its people again.

In 2006 a vast host out of the Negative Zone laid waste to much of the empire. In the chaos a Kree merchant house put the Supreme Intelligence out of action. Ronan killed the merchants, then killed the Supreme Intelligence itself when it could not be restored, and led the Kree himself.

In 2009 the Inhumans took over the Kree, and under Black Bolt the Kree went to war with the Shi'ar again. This time it was the Shi'ar who surrendered. Hala itself was destroyed in 2015. Five years later, after a million years of war, the Kree and the Skrulls joined their empires into one.

pages.title: Krypton
infobox: About fifty light years from Earth
Kandor, destroyed in the Clone Wars
Exploded as Kal-El's birthing matrix left it
Kryptonite; the Eradicator; the Fortress of Solitude
pages.html:
Krypton was the world on which Superman was born. It circled Rao, a red sun about fifty light years from Earth, and under Rao's light its people were very little different from human beings. After a long war over their clones the Kryptonians shut themselves away, from each other as well as from the stars. Their machine, the Eradicator, made sure that nobody came in or went out. Then the planet tore itself apart. Its last son, Kal-El, was launched to Earth as it died, and grew up to be Superman.

Rao

Krypton was a world half as big again as Earth, circling Rao, a red sun some fifty light years away. Under Rao's light the Kryptonians were very little different from human beings. It is only under a yellow sun, like Earth's, that a Kryptonian body soaks up enough sunlight to become what Superman is.

The Kryptonians were a people of science. Over the ages they learnt to clone themselves, to grow their children in machines and, in the end, to keep the rest of the universe out.

Doomsday

A quarter of a million years ago, before the Kryptonians had risen, Krypton was a savage place, which was exactly why Bertron chose it. Bertron was a scientist from another world who meant to make the perfect living creature. He left an infant out in Krypton's wilds to die. Then he cloned it from its remains, over and over again, so that each new body could survive whatever had killed the one before.

The creature that came out of it remembered the pain of every one of those deaths, and it hated all life for them. It killed Bertron. Then it left Krypton aboard one of his supply ships to kill on other worlds, until it was bound at last and buried deep in the Earth. In 1992 it broke out, and the world came to know it as Doomsday.

Superman learnt all this in the spring of 1994, when Doomsday rose again and fought its way across Apokolips. He learnt too that it was partly the ruins of Bertron's laboratory that had made the Kryptonians so fond, ever afterwards, of meddling with life.

The Clone Wars

Two hundred thousand years ago the Kryptonians mastered cloning. Every Kryptonian had three clones kept asleep in the clone banks, from which new organs could be taken as the old ones wore out. In this way the Kryptonians lived very nearly for ever.

About a hundred thousand years ago some of them began to say that the clones were people. Then a woman called Nyra took one of her own clones out of the banks, let it grow a mind of its own and promised it to her son, Kan-Z, as his bride. When Kan-Z found out what his bride was, he killed them both. Once it was known that a clone could become a person, there was no keeping the peace.

The Clone Wars that followed lasted a thousand years. The worst of the weapons built for them belonged to Black Zero, a band of terrorists. It was called the Destroyer, and it was fired into the heart of the planet. The chain reaction it set off there wiped out Kandor, the capital, and brought the war to an end. Jor-El's forebear Van-L fought Black Zero to the last.

Everyone believed that the reaction in the core had stopped.

After the war

The war left Krypton a desert, and it left the Kryptonians cold. They withdrew into sealed citadels, where they gave up touching one another, even within families. Children were no longer born. They were grown in birthing matrices, artificial wombs filled with carefully chosen genes. A Kryptonian did not choose a mate; one was chosen for him.

Krypton turned its back on the stars as well. Space travel was forbidden, as was any dealing with other worlds. The Kryptonians had once been a bright, easy-going people. By the end they were a race of solitary scientists in heavy robes.

Not every Kryptonian had stayed at home. Long ago some had gone out to explore the stars, and their descendants are the Daxamites, who gained powers like Superman's under Earth's sun in 1988.

The Eradicator

The man who sealed Krypton off was Kem-L, one of Jor-El's forebears. Krypton's rulers asked him to keep outsiders away, and he built the Eradicator to do it. It altered the Kryptonians themselves, so that any of them who left Krypton would die. It killed any outsider who landed there.

Long before the end a Goa'uld ship found Krypton. Under their own red sun the Kryptonians were very little different from human beings, and the Goa'uld thought they had found a world of perfect hosts. Instead they found the Eradicator, which destroyed the ship before it could land.

In the end the Eradicator was stolen by the Cleric, an alien preacher who had won a following on Krypton. When he left with his followers, all hundred thousand of them died, because the Eradicator had bound them to their world. The Cleric had not known what it did. He lived on alone for a very long time afterwards, on an asteroid near Warworld, with the Eradicator for company.

Jor-El and Lara

Jor-El, the son of Seyg-El, was a scientist of the family of El. Lara was the mate chosen for him, and in time they were given a son, Kal-El.

Jor-El found that a green plague was killing Kryptonians, and he traced it to radiation from the planet's core. The chain reaction the Destroyer had started a hundred thousand years before had never stopped. It had only slowed, and now Krypton was about to tear itself apart. Jor-El could not persuade the other scientists even to think of escape. Most of them could not have escaped in any case, since the Eradicator's work would have killed them the moment they left.

Jor-El saved what he could. First he took the Eradicator's binding out of his son's genes, so that the boy would not die when he left Krypton. Then he laid the infant in a birthing matrix, fitted it with an experimental drive and launched it towards Earth as the planet broke apart. The matrix was made to open when it landed.

The last son

Krypton exploded behind the matrix. Jor-El and Lara died with it, together with every Kryptonian left on the planet.

The matrix came down in farmland near Smallville, Kansas. Jonathan and Martha Kent, who farmed there, found the child. They brought him up as their own son, Clark. A lump of Krypton the size of a fist had lodged itself in the tail of the matrix. It was kryptonite, the radioactive stuff of Krypton itself, which weakens Superman and can kill him.

The boy was grown by 1938, when the world first heard of Superman. For a long time he was thought to be the only Kryptonian left alive. His cousin Kara Zor-El, the daughter of Jor-El's brother Zor-El, proved otherwise when she joined him as Supergirl in 1959. How she had escaped is one of the things that nobody has been able to remember clearly since the Crisis, which took her in 1985.

Superman remembers nothing of Krypton, which he left as an infant. He has learnt some of its old stories, and it was from one of them that Dick Grayson took the name Nightwing in 1984. In 1985, at the Fortress of Solitude, Mongul's Black Mercy gave him a dream of a Krypton that had never exploded.

The Kents hid the empty matrix on their farm for years, until it was stolen. In 1990 Hank Henshaw, whose mind had passed into machinery after the Excalibur shuttle disaster, left Earth in it. In his years in space he learnt a great deal about Krypton, which he put to use in 1993 as the Cyborg Superman.

The Eradicator on Earth

In 1989, far out in space, Superman was nearly killed in the arena of Warworld. He was carried to the Cleric's asteroid, where the old preacher gave him the Eradicator.

Superman brought it home. It set about remaking his Fortress of Solitude in the Arctic after the fashion of Krypton, with servant robots built on the pattern of Jor-El's own. It also went to work on Superman's mind. By 1990 he was dressing as a Kryptonian and talking of giving up Clark Kent altogether. When Jonathan Kent reminded him that Jor-El himself had seen Krypton's faults, the Fortress turned on them all.

Superman came to himself in time. He burnt the Eradicator with his heat vision and threw it into the sun. It came back in 1991 with a body of its own, meaning to remake the whole Earth as a new Krypton, which would have killed millions. Storms and earthquakes broke out across the world before it was trapped in a crystal at the Fortress, where it seemed to break apart into nothing.

Its mind had sunk into the walls of the Fortress. When Superman died in November 1992, it went to Metropolis to take over his body, and failed. Instead it carried the body to the Fortress and laid it in the regeneration matrix, which ran on the sunlight stored in Superman's own cells.

It built itself a body in Superman's likeness, and in the summer of 1993 it went out into the world wearing his symbol. It was a cold, visored Superman that dealt with criminals far more harshly than the real one ever had. It was known as the Last Son of Krypton.

Meanwhile the matrix brought the real Superman back to life. It broke soon afterwards, so that he left the Fortress in a suit of Kryptonian armour, weak and long-haired, to make his way home. At Engine City, in the ruins of Coast City, the Eradicator stepped into a blast of kryptonite meant for him. The blast passed through the Eradicator into Superman, and gave him back his full strength.

The Eradicator's mind seemed to have burnt out. Its body was taken to S.T.A.R. Labs, where an accident left a scientist dying of cancer, Dr David Connor, inside it. Since the end of 1993 the Eradicator, with Connor's mind in it, has fought beside a band of heroes called the Outsiders.

Krypton on Earth in 1994

Krypton itself is gone, and in the summer of 1994 not much of it is left on Earth. The Eradicator had drained the Fortress of Solitude to fight the Cyborg Superman, and by the end of 1993 the Fortress was crumbling round its dying robots. Kelex, made in the likeness of Jor-El's own servant, died with it. The regeneration matrix was lost in the collapse, so that whatever brought Superman back cannot be done a second time.

Kryptonite is still to be found. The lump from the matrix found its way into the chest of the cyborg Metallo, whose heart it powered. In 1987 Lex Luthor took it from him and had it set in a ring, which he wore to keep Superman at a distance until its radiation gave him cancer.

The most Kryptonian thing on Earth is Superman himself. He has never met a Goa'uld. Under a yellow sun no symbiote could get through the skin at the back of his neck, and it is probably as well for the symbiote that none has tried.

pages.title: Kyle Rayner
pages.html:
Kyle Rayner is the Green Lantern of 1994, a young freelance artist from Los Angeles who was handed the last power ring in January 1994 by Ganthet, the last of the Guardians. Hal Jordan had just destroyed the Green Lantern Corps and vanished. Kyle appeared out of nowhere, in a mask nobody had seen before, and he now serves in the Justice League under Superman.

The last ring

Kyle Rayner was nobody in particular when the ring found him. He was a young man in his twenties, brought up in Los Angeles by his mother, Maura, after his father walked out, and he scraped a living there as a struggling freelance artist.

At the turn of 1994 Hal Jordan attacked Oa, the world of the Guardians of the Universe, and destroyed the Green Lantern Corps. Only one Guardian, Ganthet, came through it alive. He went looking for someone to carry the last ring, and in January 1994 he found Kyle in an alley in Los Angeles. He handed the ring over with the words ‘You'll have to do.’ It was not much of a recommendation, but then the Guardians had very little left to give.

Learning the ring

Kyle had no training. He had no Corps behind him either, and nobody to tell him what the ring could do or what it was for. A power ring answers to its wearer's will and makes real whatever he can hold steady in his mind.

Kyle's constructs are an artist's rather than a pilot's, and they come out of his imagination in shapes no Green Lantern ever thought of. He designed his own costume and mask as well, unlike anything the Corps had worn. He has spent 1994 learning the ring by trial and error.

In July and early August 1994, during Zero Hour, Kyle stood with the other heroes at the beginning of time against the man who had carried the ring before him. Hal Jordan had come back as Parallax, meaning to remake history, and Kyle was among those who would not let him.

Loss

The ring cost him dearly within months. In the summer of 1994 Major Force, a soldier and a murderer, came looking for Green Lantern. He killed Kyle's girlfriend, Alexandra DeWitt, in Kyle's flat.

Kyle has carried on regardless, and he has taken his place in the Justice League. To most of the world he is simply the new Green Lantern, a young man in a strange mask who turned up in January after the old one vanished. Few people outside the League know what became of Hal Jordan.

In the saga

On 20 August 1994, watching the news at the Dursleys', Harry Potter saw a young Green Lantern among the League behind Superman at the Security Council. He wore a mask Harry had never seen before, and he had turned up out of nowhere in January, after the old one vanished.

pages.title: Legends (1986)
infobox: Darkseid, the Lord of Apokolips, through Glorious Godfrey
President Reagan grounded every costumed hero in America for a winter
Godfrey exposed; the order lifted; a new Justice League formed
pages.html:
Legends is the name given to the campaign of late 1986 and early 1987 in which Darkseid, the Lord of Apokolips, working through his agent Glorious Godfrey, turned American opinion against costumed heroes. At its worst President Reagan grounded every one of them for an entire winter. It ended with Godfrey's exposure, the lifting of the order and the founding of a new Justice League.

The campaign

Darkseid, the Lord of Apokolips, set out in 1986 to break the heroes of Earth by turning their own people against them. He did not leave his hell-world to do it himself. His instrument was Glorious Godfrey, who went before the cameras as the broadcaster and preacher G. Gordon Godfrey, with a voice that could bend a crowd to his will.

Night after night Godfrey told America that its heroes were dangerous, arrogant and answerable to nobody. Darkseid's creatures staged disasters to prove him right. The worst of them was Brimstone, a towering creature of living fire.

Coming so soon after the Crisis, the campaign found a frightened audience. President Reagan issued an executive order forbidding every costumed hero in America to act, and for an entire winter they were grounded. Some obeyed. Some did not.

In the same months the government set up a task force of convicted criminals under Amanda Waller, to do the work the heroes had been forbidden. It became known as the Suicide Squad, and its first mission was against Brimstone.

The end

Godfrey's campaign reached its height in a great march on Washington early in 1987. There the heroes faced him down, and his hold over the crowd was broken. Reagan's order was lifted.

The old Justice League, which had been working from Detroit, had not survived the winter. Out of the struggle came a new Justice League, founded at the start of 1987, which later that year accepted a charter from the United Nations.

In the saga

On 20 August 1994 the newsreader on the Dursleys' television recalled that in 1986 President Reagan had grounded every costumed hero in America for an entire winter.

pages.title: Lester Pearson
pages.html:
Lester Bowles Pearson was a Canadian diplomat and politician. He won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1957 for proposing the United Nations force that kept the peace at Suez. He led the Liberal Party from 1958, but he never became Prime Minister of Canada.

Early life

Pearson was born on 23 April 1897 at Newtonbrook, Ontario, the son of a Methodist minister. He served in the First World War, first in the medical corps, then with the Royal Flying Corps, where he trained as a pilot. His flying instructor thought Lester no name for an airman, and called him Mike. The name stuck. After the war he studied at Oxford, taught history at the University of Toronto and joined the Department of External Affairs in 1928.

Diplomat

He was ambassador at Washington at the end of the Second World War, helped to found the United Nations and served as Secretary of State for External Affairs from 1948 to 1957. In 1952 he was President of the United Nations General Assembly. In 1956, during the Suez crisis, he proposed the United Nations Emergency Force that separated the armies. In 1957 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for it.

Leader of the Liberals

He became leader of the Liberal Party in 1958, but he never won power and never became Prime Minister. Canada kept the Red Ensign as its flag.

pages.title: Lex Luthor
infobox: Luthor; Alexander Luthor; Lex Luthor II
In custody, his cloned body failing
pages.html:
Lex Luthor is the scientist and industrialist who has been Superman's greatest enemy since 1940. For decades he was also the most powerful man in Metropolis. Dying of cancer, he staged his own death in 1990 and came back in a young cloned body, passing himself off as his own son. When that body began to fail in 1994 he was found out, and in May 1994 his aide fired the sonic torpedoes that flattened downtown Metropolis.

Superman's enemy

Luthor came to public notice in 1940, a scientific genius already grown to manhood. He wanted the world, and he saw in Superman the one thing that could stop him having it. For more than fifty years he set his intellect against the Kryptonian with robots, weapons, schemes and bought allies. He was never once content to let him alone.

He came, so far as anyone knows, from Suicide Slum, the roughest district in Metropolis. By the later 1980s he was best known not as a criminal but as the head of LexCorp, the company that owned a great part of the city. He ran it from a tall L-shaped tower in the heart of Metropolis, and no court could touch him.

Records of his earlier career, like much else from before the Crisis of 1985, are confused. Many people in Metropolis remember him only as its richest citizen.

Death and the clone

In 1987 Luthor took a lump of Kryptonite from the chest of the cyborg Metallo and had it set in a ring. He wore the ring to keep Superman at a distance, and its radiation gave him cancer. By 1990 he was an old man, had lost his hand and was dying.

In late 1990 his private jet crashed, and he was reported dead. In fact his brain had been placed in a young, healthy body cloned from his own cells. He reappeared as a red-haired young Australian who claimed to be Luthor's long-lost son and heir, Lex Luthor II. In that guise he took over LexCorp.

In 1994 the cloned body began to break down. As it failed, his deceptions came apart. In May 1994 Superman and the authorities cornered him. Beneath Metropolis he had hidden sonic torpedoes reverse-engineered from the weapons of the alien invasion of 1988.

Superman persuaded him not to fire them. His aide, Dr Sydney Happersen, fired them anyway. Downtown Metropolis was flattened, LexCorp's tower and the Daily Planet building among it. Luthor was arrested and exposed in public as the man he had always been.

In August 1994 he is in custody. The young body grown from his own cells is failing under him.

In the saga

Nobody on the news named Luthor in August 1994. On 20 August, though, a protester in New York shouted that in May ‘some lunatic in a lab coat flattened downtown with torpedoes left over from the alien invasion’. The man in the lab coat was Luthor's aide, Sydney Happersen.

pages.title: Moloc
infobox: Molech, to whom the Canaanites burnt children
2004, killed by missiles sent from Earth
pages.html:
Moloc is a Goa'uld System Lord whom the Canaanites and Phoenicians knew as Molech, the god to whom children were burnt. He has not changed his habits since. On his worlds every Jaffa girl was burnt alive at birth, because Moloc held that only male Jaffa could win his wars. He was killed in 2004 by missiles sent through the Stargate from Earth.

Molech

In Canaan he was Molech, and children were passed through the fire to him. He came quietly, in defiance of Ra's ban, and he kept well away from the North.

The law of Moses forbade the Israelites to give any of their children to Molech, on pain of death. Some of them did it all the same.

The Ceremony of Fire

Moloc took the practice with him to the stars. He decreed that every girl born to the Jaffa of his worlds should be burnt alive, since only male Jaffa could win his wars for him. His priests called it the Ceremony of Fire.

Ishta, one of his high priestesses, was charged with the burnings. She began instead to smuggle the babies away. She took them to a hidden world called Hak'tyl, a word that means liberation, and raised them there as warriors.

The women of Hak'tyl lived by raiding Moloc's Jaffa for the symbiotes they needed to stay alive. In 2003 they found SG-1, and Earth gave them tretonin, the drug that frees a Jaffa from needing a symbiote at all. Teal'c and Ishta grew close.

Death

In 2004 Moloc's Imperial Guard fell on a gathering of Jaffa who meant to rise against him, on the new world of the Hak'tyl. Only Teal'c, Ishta and a Jaffa called Aron escaped.

Moloc came down himself. He took Ishta prisoner and tortured her with his hand device, calling himself her god while he did it.

Meanwhile two thousand Jaffa had gathered against his temple on Goranak. As Moloc made ready to deal with them, Earth opened the Stargate and sent missiles through. Aron guided them on to Moloc with a targeting beam, and they killed him along with his guard. Teal'c saved Ishta from Moloc's First Prime, Cha'ra, who later joined the rebellion himself.

Moloc's worlds did not go free. Ba'al took them, which made him stronger than ever.

pages.title: Mongul
infobox: Warworld; the destruction of Coast City, 1993
pages.html:
Mongul is the huge, yellow-skinned alien tyrant who once ruled Warworld, a battle station the size of a planet. In the summer of 1993 his forces destroyed Coast City and its seven million people on behalf of the Cyborg Superman. They built a great engine in its crater, and that August Hal Jordan beat him in the ruins.

Warworld

Mongul first troubled Earth in 1980. He was a conqueror of great strength and greater cruelty. He had been driven from his own world, and he wanted more.

For years he ruled Warworld, an artificial planet armed to destroy others. He gave it over to gladiatorial games, in which captured beings fought to the death for his entertainment.

In 1985 he came to the Fortress of Solitude on Superman's birthday, bringing a present. It was a Black Mercy, an alien plant that fastens on its victim and holds him in a dream of the life he most wants. Superman dreamt of a Krypton that had never exploded. Batman and Wonder Woman, who had come with birthday presents too, got him free. By the end of the day Mongul was caught in the plant himself.

In 1989, far from Earth, Superman was brought to Warworld as a captive and forced to fight in its arena. It was Mongul's mistake, and it cost him Warworld.

Coast City

In 1993 Mongul allied himself with the Cyborg Superman, Hank Henshaw, and knelt to him as the master of a new Warworld. In the summer of 1993 Mongul's warship destroyed Coast City with nearly everyone in it. Machinery sown in the crater built Engine City, the first of two engines meant to turn the whole Earth into a warworld.

That August Hal Jordan, whose home Coast City had been, fought his way into Engine City and beat Mongul unconscious. At the same time Superman, returned from the dead, defeated the Cyborg Superman.

In the saga

Nobody spoke Mongul's name on the news in August 1994, but his work was there to see. A man who had lost his family at Coast City told the cameras that there had been no city left, only ‘a hole, with a… with a machine in it’.

pages.title: Morrigan
infobox: The Morrigan, the Irish goddess of battle
P3X-289, at the Gate of Magh Mar
Surrendered to Ba'al by early 2005; afterwards unknown
pages.html:
Morrigan is a Goa'uld System Lord who was worshipped in Ireland as the Great Queen, a goddess of battle who goes about in the shape of a crow. Among the System Lords she is known for learning other people's secrets without their noticing. In 2002 she voted with the majority to take Anubis back among them. By early 2005 she had surrendered to Ba'al.

The Great Queen

Morrigan came quietly to Ireland, in defiance of Ra's ban, and kept to the western edge of the world, well away from the North. The Irish called her the Morrigan, which may mean the Great Queen or the Phantom Queen. She was a goddess of battle and strife, who chose which warriors would die. A man who saw her washing armour at a ford knew that the armour was his own. He did not live long afterwards.

Her worship reached further than Ireland. In 2003 SG-1 came to a walled city under a dome on the world called P3X-289. Its people knew their Stargate as the Gate of Magh Mar. According to their records it had been found 563 years before in the ruins of Danaan, and it was believed to have had some part in the worship of the goddess Morrigan. It stood in their national museum of history.

The council at Hasara

Morrigan was one of the seven System Lords at the council held under truce in the Hasara system in 2002. Each of them brought a single slave. Lord Yu warned his own to have nothing to do with hers.

His slave already knew why. Morrigan's servant would try to draw out strategic information in what sounded like idle conversation. Yu had learnt this the hard way: his previous slave had let slip the whereabouts of one of his secret bases, and had died in the surprise attack that followed.

When Osiris asked the council to take Anubis back among the System Lords, Morrigan nodded her agreement with the rest. Only Yu voted against.

Surrender

After Earth defeated Anubis in 2004, Ba'al turned Anubis's Kull warriors on the other System Lords, and their Jaffa were no match for them. Early in 2005 the Tok'ra reported that Morrigan had capitulated. Two of her fellow lords, Bastet and Olokun, were already dead. What Ba'al did with her afterwards is not recorded. It was not an ending the Great Queen of the Irish stories would have recognised.

pages.title: Mutant Registration Act
pages.html:
The Mutant Registration Act is the American law, introduced in 1984 by Senator Robert Kelly, that requires mutants to register their identities and powers with the federal government. In the late 1980s it was enforced by a team of mutants in government service, Freedom Force. It has never been repealed, though by 1994 it is seldom heard of.

History

Senator Robert Kelly had long argued that mutants were a danger the government must be able to track. At the end of 1980 the X-Men saved his life from an assassination attempt by Mystique's Brotherhood of Evil Mutants. It did not change his mind. In 1984 he introduced the Act, which became law the same year.

In the end enforcement fell to mutants themselves. In 1985 Mystique offered the government the services of her Brotherhood in exchange for pardons. Under the government official Valerie Cooper they became Freedom Force, the federal team that arrested unregistered mutants. Mutant rights campaigners protested, and other mutant heroes refused to comply.

Freedom Force broke up after a disastrous mission in Kuwait during the Gulf War in 1991. Since then the Act has been enforced only fitfully. It remains law.

Registration and the Sentinels

The Act asks mutants to declare themselves to the state. The Sentinels were built to find them whether they declared themselves or not, and they were mothballed after a series of incidents in the 1980s. In August 1994 the Senate Armed Services Committee prepared to hear a proposal to revive the Sentinel programme against Khan. Mutant rights groups called it 'a licence to hunt'.

pages.title: New Genesis
infobox: Orion, Lightray, Metron, the Forever People
Scott Free (Mister Miracle), raised on Apokolips
pages.html:
New Genesis is a green and peaceful world on the far side of the universe, the twin of Apokolips. Its people are the beings who call themselves the New Gods, and its ruler is Izaya, who is called Highfather. The two worlds have hated each other for as long as either has existed. Their last great war ended in the Pact, by which Highfather and Darkseid exchanged their sons. The Pact itself ended when Highfather's son escaped to Earth. Since 1971 the people of New Genesis have been fighting Darkseid's servants there.

The world

New Genesis is a world of forests, grassland, mountains and clear rivers, very nearly untouched. Its people have built only one city on it, and even that city does not touch the ground.

The New Gods live so long that nobody is sure they die of age at all. They are far stronger than men and very hard to kill, although radion, a substance deadly to them, can do it.

Not everybody on New Genesis is a New God. The Bugs, an insect people who walk upright, live in great mounds of their own, and a good many of the New Gods treat them as vermin. One of the Bugs, the warrior Forager, has fought beside Orion.

Supertown

Supertown, the capital, floats in the sky above the forests, so that the city should not scar the land below. It is the home of the New Gods and the seat of Highfather, who rules from it with his council.

Its people travel by Boom Tube, one of the roaring doorways by which the New Gods cross the universe. It was Metron who invented it.

Many of them carry a Mother Box: a small living machine that thinks, talks to its owner in a soft pinging that nobody else can follow, and loves its owner without condition. A Mother Box can heal, open a Boom Tube or lend its owner strength. When its owner dies, it dies too. The first Mother Boxes were made by Himon, a rebel of Apokolips.

Izaya and Avia

In his youth Izaya the Inheritor was a warrior, and a general of New Genesis in its long quarrel with Apokolips. His wife, Avia, spent years trying to turn him towards gentler things.

Their last great war began when Darkseid's uncle Steppenwolf, at Darkseid's bidding, murdered Avia. He ambushed the two of them and shot her. Izaya went to war in a fury, and New Genesis went with him.

The war with Apokolips

It was the most terrible war either world has known. New Genesis bombed the fire pits of Apokolips, and Apokolips answered in kind. Before long both sides were hurling planetoids at each other. They bred monsters for the battlefield, and turned on each other beams that could slice through a planet.

Metron, the seeker after knowledge, made it worse without taking either side. He wanted the X-Element, a rare substance he needed to power his Mobius Chair, and Darkseid had it. In exchange he gave Darkseid the secret of the Boom Tube. Darkseid used it to carry the war to New Genesis.

The Source

When the war had all but ruined both worlds, Izaya went out alone into the wilderness of New Genesis, where the wind tore at him. He came at last to a wall of bare rock. As he stood before it, a hand of fire wrote on the stone.

He came back from the wilderness without his weapons, and he has never taken them up again. He took the name of Highfather, and he set about making peace with Darkseid.

The New Gods call the power that wrote on the rock the Source. It is the power they draw on, and they take it to be the origin of their own. It still speaks to Highfather in writing of fire, and he is the keeper of his people's bond with it. It once told him that to know everything is to know how much is not known. Mother Boxes are said to be in tune with it.

What the Source truly is, nobody on New Genesis claims to know.

The Pact

The war ended with the Pact, by which the two rulers exchanged their sons. Darkseid's son Orion was sent to grow up on New Genesis, and Izaya's son Scott Free was handed over to Apokolips.

Orion's mother, Tigra, was dragged away from him swearing that her son would kill his father. On Apokolips, Granny Goodness was waiting for the child from New Genesis.

Neither exchange turned out as Darkseid intended. Scott Free was raised in one of Granny Goodness's orphanages, where the children of Apokolips are trained into soldiers, and he never fitted. Himon taught him in secret, and Metron put into his head the idea of a future of his own.

In time he escaped to Earth with Big Barda, one of Granny's own Female Furies, whom he had met at Himon's meetings. On Earth he became Mister Miracle, the escape artist, and Barda became his wife in 1974. In 1987 he was one of the founders of the new Justice League.

He took his name from Thaddeus Brown, a circus escape artist who had called himself Mister Miracle. A sniper working for Intergang shot Brown while he was rehearsing an escape. Brown's assistant, Oberon, has stayed with Scott ever since.

Scott's escape broke the Pact, which gave Darkseid the excuse he had been waiting for. Darkseid had expected it all along.

Orion and Lightray

Orion grew up in Supertown as Highfather's foster son. He is the fiercest warrior New Genesis has, and he has spent his life fighting his father.

He has his father's temper, and under the face he shows the world he has something of his father's face as well. His Mother Box keeps the true one hidden, and it helps him to keep his rage in check. He flies in an Astro-Harness, and New Genesis calls him the Dog of War.

His closest friend is Lightray, who is as bright in temper as he is in power. Lightray can fly at the speed of light, or throw light as a weapon. He would always rather talk an enemy round than knock him down.

Metron

Metron is the cleverest of the New Gods, and the least attached to anything but knowledge. He belongs, he says, to neither side. He travels in his Mobius Chair, which can take him anywhere in space or time.

It was he who invented the Boom Tube, and he who gave it to Darkseid. He has a seat on Highfather's Council of Eight all the same.

The Forever People

The Forever People are five young New Gods: Mark Moonrider, Big Bear, Beautiful Dreamer, Vykin and Serifan. They ride a single Super-Cycle, and they share a single Mother Box, larger than most.

In great need the five of them call on the Mother Box together. They vanish, and in their place stands the Infinity-Man, a warrior of enormous power. When the danger is past, he goes, and the five come back.

They first came to Earth early in 1971, to rescue Beautiful Dreamer. Darkseid had carried her off, believing, wrongly, that she knew something of the Anti-Life Equation. Superman helped them to get her back.

New Genesis and Earth

New Genesis took an interest in Earth because Darkseid did. Early in 1971, on the word of the Source, Highfather sent Orion to Earth to fight his father's servants there. Lightray followed him. Through 1971 and 1972 Orion fought them wherever he found them, from the gunmen of Intergang to his half-brother Kalibak.

Highfather himself has seldom come to Earth. He prefers to send others, which is one of the very few things he has in common with Darkseid.

In the summer of 1994 the war between the two worlds is unresolved. Highfather rules from Supertown and listens for the Source. Orion has not yet killed his father, whatever Tigra swore. Scott Free and Barda live on Earth.

pages.title: Nick Fury
infobox: Nicholas Joseph Fury; Sgt. Fury; Colonel Fury
United States Army; sergeant of the Howling Commandos
Office of Strategic Services; Central Intelligence Agency (colonel)
Slowed by the Infinity Formula since the end of the war
Left eye, from shrapnel in the war; wears a patch
pages.html:
Nick Fury is the American soldier and spy who led the Howling Commandos through the Second World War. He has been Director of S.H.I.E.L.D., the international intelligence and law-enforcement agency, since 1965. A secret treatment called the Infinity Formula has slowed his ageing since the war, so that in 1994, at about seventy-four, he looks barely fifty. He is Captain America's oldest comrade in arms, and a long-standing, sometimes awkward ally of the Avengers.

Early life

Nicholas Joseph Fury was born in New York City about 1920, not long after the end of the First World War. He was the eldest of Jack Fury's three children. He grew up in the city with his younger brother, Jake, and his sister, Dawn. He was a man of about twenty when America went to war.

The Howling Commandos

Fury served through the war in the United States Army. Captain Samuel 'Happy Sam' Sawyer gave him command of the First Attack Squad, a unit of Army Rangers based in England. After its first missions Winston Churchill gave it the right to call itself commandos, as a mark of honour. It went down in history as the Howling Commandos, or the Howlers, with Sergeant Fury at its head from 1942 to the end of the war.

The Howlers were chosen for nerve rather than polish. There was Corporal Timothy 'Dum Dum' Dugan, a huge Irish American former circus strongman in a bowler hat. There was Gabe Jones, a Black trumpeter, serving in an integrated squad at a time when the rest of the Army was segregated. There was Izzy Cohen, a Jewish mechanic from Brooklyn; Dino Manelli, an Italian American film actor; and Rebel Ralston, a jockey from Kentucky. Junior Juniper, the youngest, was killed in action early in the squad's career. Percy Pinkerton, an Englishman who went into battle with an umbrella, took his place. Eric Koenig, a German who had turned against the Nazis, joined later.

They fought behind enemy lines all over occupied Europe, as well as in North Africa. Their work was raids, rescues and sabotage. More than once they fought beside Captain America and Bucky. Their most persistent enemy was Baron Wolfgang von Strucker, the Prussian aristocrat who commanded the Blitzkrieg Squad and would later lead Hydra. Fury's English sweetheart, the nurse Pamela Hawley, was killed in an air raid on London.

During the war a fragment of shrapnel struck Fury's left eye. He lost the sight of it gradually over the years that followed. Since the 1960s he has worn a patch over it.

The Infinity Formula

In the last months of the war in Europe Fury was badly wounded by a land mine in France. A scientist named Berthold Sternberg saved his life with an experimental treatment of his own, and used him to test it. Fury learnt only afterwards what it was. The Infinity Formula had stopped his ageing almost entirely, but its effect lasted only a year. He needed a fresh dose every year to keep it, and for some thirty years Sternberg made him pay dearly for each one.

The Formula is why Fury, born about 1920, is still at the very top of the espionage trade in his seventies. He looks a hard-used man of about fifty, grey at the temples, and he moves like a younger one. Captain America was given his serum by the government in 1940. Fury owes his years to a private bargain he never chose.

The CIA years, 1945 to 1965

After the war Fury went into intelligence, first with the Office of Strategic Services, then with its successor, the Central Intelligence Agency. During the Korean War the Howlers were brought together again for a time, and Fury was given a battlefield commission as a lieutenant. He rose to the rank of colonel.

In 1959 he led a covert team that hunted surviving Nazis under the name of the Avengers. Its members included Dum Dum Dugan, Namora, Dominic Fortune, Ulysses Bloodstone, Kraven the Hunter and the man later called Sabretooth. It was never made public. In 1963, still a colonel of the CIA, he worked with the Fantastic Four against the Hate-Monger, a demagogue who stirred up crowds with a ray that bred hatred.

Director of S.H.I.E.L.D.

In 1965 the international agency S.H.I.E.L.D. lost its first director, Rick Stoner, to an assassin from Hydra. On the President's recommendation its governing council offered the post to Fury, who had not known that the agency existed. He took it, and he has held it ever since. Dugan and Gabe Jones soon joined him there.

Under Fury S.H.I.E.L.D. fought Hydra, its offshoot Advanced Idea Mechanics and a long line of other threats. It did so from the Helicarrier, the flying aircraft carrier that Tony Stark designed for it. In the agency's first years Fury discovered that the true master of Hydra was Strucker, his old enemy from the war. His agents included Sharon Carter, Agent 13; Jasper Sitwell; Clay Quartermain; Jimmy Woo; and the Italian Contessa Valentina Allegra de Fontaine, who was for many years his lover. His own brother Jake turned against him as Scorpio, the masked leader of the criminal cartel Zodiac.

Fury and the Avengers

Fury's ties to the Avengers go back to the war, when the Howlers fought beside Captain America and Bucky. When Rogers came out of the ice in 1964, Fury was one of the very few men alive who had known him in the war. In 1966 he tried to recruit him into S.H.I.E.L.D. Rogers declined, but the two of them have worked together ever since. Sharon Carter, Fury's Agent 13, was for years the woman Rogers loved.

Fury's agency and the Avengers have not always agreed. In 1971, in the Kree-Skrull War, S.H.I.E.L.D. hunted the Kree officer Captain Marvel and his friend Carol Danvers, while the Avengers were protecting him. Even so, Tony Stark, a founder of the Avengers, sat on S.H.I.E.L.D.'s governing council in its first years and designed its Helicarrier. The team and the agency have usually been on the same side. Fury's own covert team of 1959 had carried the Avengers' name four years before the Avengers did.

Fury against S.H.I.E.L.D., 1988 to 1994

In 1988 Fury discovered that S.H.I.E.L.D. and Hydra alike had been taken over from within by the Deltites. These were Life Model Decoys, the agency's own lifelike androids, which had become aware and had replaced agents with copies. Framed and hunted by his own people, he went underground. He exposed the Deltites and destroyed them, then disbanded S.H.I.E.L.D. altogether. In 1989 he rebuilt it as a smaller agency, easier for one man to watch over, and in 1991 it took a new name to go with the old initials.

Early in 1994 Fury learnt that much of the turmoil of the years since 1988 had been staged to keep him busy while Strucker prepared Hydra's return. He set about putting a stop to it.

Fury in 1994

In the summer of 1994 Fury is still Director of S.H.I.E.L.D., a man of about seventy-four in the body of a man of fifty. His work does not appear on the evening news. S.H.I.E.L.D. makes no joint statements, and it was not among those who stood behind Superman at the Security Council in August 1994. Fury and Captain America fought side by side in the war. Both are still at work half a century later, and both owe it to what was done to their bodies in the war.

He is plain-spoken, profane and impatient of politicians. He has a cigar in his mouth more often than not. He is hard on his agents and fiercely loyal to them, but outside his own service he trusts very few people. He has spent most of his life fighting the same enemy, Strucker's Hydra, in one shape after another, and he has never quite been able to believe that it is beaten.

In the saga

Nick Fury has not yet appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Nirrti
infobox: Stargate SG-1, 'Fair Game' (9 July 1999); named in 'Singularity' (31 October 1997)
Goa'uld System Lord; cast out by 2002
Nirrti, the Hindu goddess of death
A hok'tar, or advanced human, to be the perfect host
The people of Hanka; the people of P3X-367
Wodan, one of her own subjects
pages.html:
Nirrti is a Goa'uld System Lord who takes her name from the Hindu goddess of death and ruin. She cares less for power than for one particular project: the making of a perfect host, a human being more advanced than any other. She has wiped out whole peoples in pursuit of it. In 1999, with Thor himself in the building, she tried to wreck Earth's entry into the Protected Planets Treaty. In 2003 she was killed by one of the people she had experimented on.

The goddess of death

The people of India knew her as Nirrti, the goddess of death, decay and misfortune. She came to them quietly, in defiance of Ra's ban, and she kept a long way from the North.

She does her own experiments, which is rare among the Goa'uld, and she can work the machines of the Ancients. She has a device that makes her invisible, which she uses often. She has long coveted the domain of Cronus.

She has used innocent people as weapons before, sending them through the Stargates of her enemies to destroy them, sometimes under cover of talks.

The hok'tar

What Nirrti wants above everything is a hok'tar, which in the Goa'uld tongue means an advanced human. She wants a host whose body can do things that no ordinary human body can.

She has been breeding the people of Hanka towards it for countless generations. When a Hankan child reaches sixteen it falls ill and is sent into the forest, where her laboratory lies hidden underground. A few days later it comes out cured, and the elders say this is normal.

Hanka

Earth's teams reached Hanka in 1997. Nirrti did not want the other System Lords to hear of her work, so she wiped out the people of Hanka with a plague. The Earth team stationed there died with them.

One girl survived. Her name was Cassandra, and after countless generations she was the very child Nirrti had been breeding for. Nirrti had hidden a bomb in her chest, meant to go off when she came near Earth's Stargate and destroy it. Once she was kept away from the gate, the bomb shrank harmlessly.

Cassandra was adopted by Dr Janet Fraiser, the chief medical officer of Stargate Command, and she grew up on Earth.

The treaty talks

In 1999 Nirrti was one of the three System Lords who came to Earth to settle its place under the Protected Planets Treaty, with Yu and Cronus. Thor himself presided.

She argued that Earth was far too dangerous to be protected. Then she made herself invisible to attack Cronus, hoping to kill him, take his domain and wreck the treaty in one stroke. The blame was meant to fall on Teal'c. She did it with Thor in the building, which tells one a good deal about Nirrti.

Cronus lived, because Samantha Carter healed him with a Goa'uld healing device, and Nirrti gave herself away. She snatched a weapon and fled. Carter caught up with her carrying a rod made for killing the invisible, so Nirrti gave herself up. Cronus took her away as his prisoner.

Renegade

When Cronus died in 2001, Nirrti escaped. She went back to her laboratory on Hanka, and when SG-1 came looking there she followed them through the Stargate to Earth, invisible.

Cassandra was sixteen by then. Nirrti's work in her blood had woken, and it was turning her into a hok'tar faster than her body could bear. Nirrti was caught inside Stargate Command. She offered to save the girl in exchange for her freedom, her invisibility device and a sample of Cassandra's blood.

General Hammond refused. Janet Fraiser held her at gunpoint. In the end Nirrti cured Cassandra for her freedom alone, and walked out through the gate, saying that she would have to start her work again from the beginning.

By 2002 she was a renegade, no longer welcome among the System Lords. Rebel Jaffa raided her worlds that year, and K'tano won many of her Jaffa over to the rebellion.

Death

By 2003 Nirrti had almost nothing left but a handful of Jaffa. On a world that Earth's Russian team had found, she had stopped breeding people and begun changing them directly, with a machine of the Ancients that could rewrite a living body. The people there worshipped her, because she had saved them from a plague. In truth she had killed hundreds of them.

Her experiments had given some of her subjects strange powers. Among them were Eggar, who could read minds, and Wodan, who could move things without touching them.

SG-1 came to kill her, and they were taken prisoner. Nirrti experimented on Samantha Carter. She took a particular interest in Jonas Quinn, whose people had been carried off from Earth thousands of years before, and tried to persuade him to rule beside her.

Jack O'Neill persuaded Eggar to look into her mind. Eggar saw that everything SG-1 had told them was true. Wodan, whose brother had died of her work, broke her neck without laying a finger on her, while she begged him for her life and offered him unimaginable power.

Eggar had taken what he needed from her mind first. With it he undid her work on Carter and his own people. They meant to destroy the machine afterwards. What she had done to Jonas showed itself later: for a while he could see a little way into the future.

Character

Nirrti has no scruples at all. She has killed whole peoples to hide her work, and she has used a child as a bomb. She is also a coward of a practical kind. Twice she gave in when she saw that she was beaten, and at the very end she begged.

pages.title: Olokun
infobox: Olokun, the Yoruba lord of the sea
Killed in Ba'al's war on the System Lords, by early 2005
pages.html:
Olokun is a Goa'uld System Lord who was worshipped on the coast of West Africa as the owner of the sea. He is proud, quick to take offence and slow to forgive it. In 2004 Anubis besieged him and broke his armies. Early in 2005 the Tok'ra reported that he was dead, killed in Ba'al's war on the other System Lords.

The owner of the sea

Olokun came quietly to the coast of West Africa, long after Ra had forbidden the Goa'uld to speak of Earth. He stayed well away from the North, as the wiser Goa'uld did.

The Yoruba knew him as the owner of the sea, the lord of its deepest waters, who lived in a palace beneath the waves. The people of the coast made offerings to him for a good catch and for wealth from the sea.

The council at Hasara

Olokun came to the council of the System Lords in 2002 still seething over a recent defeat by Lord Yu's forces. Yu warned his slave that Olokun might try to kill him out of spite, and told him not to make his master look foolish by getting himself murdered.

An unseen enemy had been attacking all their worlds. When Bastet reported that one of the enemy's dead Jaffa had borne Olokun's mark, he demanded to know how she dared accuse him. One of his motherships, he said, had been surrounded by the enemy. Its crew had surrendered rather than die with honour, and they might well have changed sides.

It was Olokun who answered Osiris when she came to the council to ask for a seat: normally, he told her, such a petition would not have been considered. When she named Anubis as her master, Olokun asked what Anubis offered to repay the damage he had done in gathering his forces. He was told that Anubis owed the System Lords nothing. He voted to take Anubis back all the same.

Anubis and Ba'al

Olokun had reason to regret it. Early in 2004 Anubis moved against him and laid siege to his worlds. The free Jaffa hoped to win Olokun's Jaffa over to their rebellion. They believed the Tok'ra had a spy high in his ranks, and they wanted the spy to kill him, so that his Jaffa would be free to join them. The Tok'ra refused. Delek of the Tok'ra said that assassinating Olokun had never been an option.

The siege went on. Thousands of Jaffa died, and many of Olokun's commanders were taken prisoner by Anubis's Kull warriors. The free Jaffa blamed the Tok'ra, who had refused to help them.

After Earth defeated Anubis later that year, Ba'al took Anubis's Kull warriors for himself and made war on the other System Lords. Early in 2005 the Tok'ra reported that Olokun was among the dead.

pages.title: Ori
infobox: The Ancients; Earth; the free Jaffa
Cast down in 2007; their faith broken in 2008
pages.html:
The Ori are Maiar who sided with Melkor in his rebellion against God, and were cast out with him. They are demons. They fled to the Alteran galaxy, far beyond this one, and there they set themselves up as gods. The religion they built, which they called Origin, became in time a mockery of God and of Jesus Christ. It also fed them, on the worship of the people it deceived.

The rebellion

Before the world was made, the Maiar were spirits in the service of God. When Melkor rebelled, a number of them went with him, as Sauron and the Balrogs did. The Ori were among those who chose him. When Melkor was cast out, they were cast out with him, and they have been demons ever since.

They did not stay with their master. They fled a very long way off, to the Alteran galaxy, where they hoped to be gods in their own right.

The Alteran galaxy

The Alteran galaxy takes its name from the Alterans, the people later known as the Ancients, who lived there then. Where the Alterans had come from, and how they had got there, nobody knows.

The Ori set themselves up among them as gods. They let it be believed that they were Alterans themselves, who had risen to a higher plane of existence by faith, and they offered the same reward to anyone who would worship them. It was a lie. The Ori had never been mortal, and they had no intention of raising anybody.

The Alterans who would not worship them left that galaxy and came to this one, where they built the Stargates. The Ori hunted them for as long as they could. Long afterwards the Ancients rose to the order of the Maiar themselves, by the grace that the Ori had only pretended to offer.

Origin

The religion of the Ori is called Origin. Its scripture is the Book of Origin, its holy city is Celestis, and its head is the Doci, who speaks with the voice of the Ori. Its prayers begin 'Hallowed are the Ori'. The Ori themselves show their faithful nothing but a great flame.

Every part of it was made to mock the true faith. Its prayers echo the Lord's Prayer. Its Priors, pale, bald men with staffs, go from world to world working miracles of healing, as the Apostles did, and calling down plague on those who will not listen, which the Apostles did not. The faithful are promised ascension, a counterfeit of Heaven that nobody has ever received.

Unbelievers are burnt. The Ori feed on the worship of their followers, which is the real purpose of the whole thing. The more people bow to them, the stronger they become.

The Orici

The worst of the mockery was Adria. In 2005 Vala Mal Doran, a woman of this galaxy who had been carried into theirs, found herself with child by the power of the Ori alone, with no father at all.

The child was born in 2006, grew to a woman in a matter of days, and was hailed as the Orici, the will of the Ori made flesh. She was a mockery of the Incarnation from the first. She was also made to lead their crusade.

The crusade

In 2005 Daniel Jackson and Vala Mal Doran found the Ori's galaxy, using a device of the Ancients. Soon afterwards the Priors began coming through the Stargates into this one. In 2006 a Prior's plague reached Earth, and a cure was found only just in time.

Later that year the Priors opened a great gate, large enough for warships, and the Ori's fleet came through it. It broke the ships of Earth and the free Jaffa that tried to stop it. Then the crusade began to take world after world.

Adria led it. She went from world to world as the Orici, and every world she came to either bowed or burnt.

The fall of the Ori

In 2007 a weapon made long ago by one of the Ancients, for use against beings of the higher planes, was sent into the Ori's galaxy. It could not kill them, for Maiar cannot be killed, but it broke their power and drove them out of the place where they had hidden, into the outer darkness with their master.

Adria was not with them. Later that year Ba'al seized her and tried to make her his host. When the Tok'ra had taken him out of her, she rose to a higher plane herself, and took up what was left of the Ori's power.

In 2008 the Ark of Truth, another device of the Ancients, was turned on the Doci at Celestis. Through him the followers of Origin saw the truth: that the Ori were no gods, and that they had never meant to raise anybody. The faith collapsed. Ganos Lal, one of the Ancients, took Adria out of the world into a struggle without end, as Oma Desala had taken Anubis.

pages.title: Protected Planets Treaty
infobox: Asgard and the Goa'uld System Lords
Listed worlds are closed to Goa'uld attack and enslavement
pages.html:
The Protected Planets Treaty is the agreement between Asgard and the Goa'uld System Lords under which a list of inhabited worlds is closed to Goa'uld attack. Asgard enforces it. In 1994 Earth is not on the list.

Origins

The treaty was the end of a war that had begun in Egypt. Thor, the son of Odin, fought beside the Egyptians when they rose against Ra some five thousand years ago. For thousands of years afterwards he hunted the Goa'uld wherever they came near the North, killing Jaffa who surrendered and tearing symbiotes out of their hosts. In the 870s he followed Heru'ur to the world now called Cimmeria and freed the Northmen Heru'ur had taken there. Towards the end of the tenth century Apophis, Heru'ur and Ba'al joined their fleets against Asgard. Thor destroyed two of the three.

The System Lords asked for terms soon afterwards. It is said in Asgard, and denied by the System Lords, that their first demand was that Thor should not be present when the treaty was signed. Earth was left off the list. Since the rising against Ra the Goa'uld had been forbidden to speak of it, and a world that may not be named cannot very well be written into a treaty. It was also the one world in the galaxy where they could be surest of finding Thor.

Terms

Under the treaty the System Lords undertake not to attack, invade or enslave the people of the protected worlds. The list runs to some two dozen planets, most of them young human societies that Asgard has taken under its care. Asgard, for its part, may not use its own technology to advance the peoples it protects. A serious breach on one world could free the Goa'uld to attack all of them.

On some of the worlds in its care Asgard has also left defences of its own. On the planet Cimmeria, for instance, a device called Thor's Hammer traps any Goa'uld who comes through the gate.

The treaty holds because Asgard is stronger than any System Lord, and could destroy their fleets if they broke it. The System Lords dislike it, test it and look for ways round it. They keep it only so long as they believe Asgard can make them.

Asgard and the Replicator war

Asgard, the realm of Odin and Thor, has been at war for years with the Replicators, self-copying machines that devour technology. The war has drawn Asgard's strength far away. Thor himself is absent from Earth because of it, and Eric Masterson carries the mace in his place as Thunderstrike. The more of Asgard's strength the Replicators consume, the less there is to hold the System Lords to the treaty.

The System Lords know nothing of the Replicators, or of Asgard's war with them. Asgard has made sure of it. The treaty now holds largely on a bluff: Asgard keeps up the appearance of its old strength over the protected worlds, and the System Lords, who do not know the bluff is false, dare not call it.

Earth

Earth is not a protected world in 1994.

In 1997 the Goa'uld came back to Earth for the first time in more than a thousand years. It was Apophis who came. Ra's death in 1994 had left the System Lords without a leader, and Apophis was making the most of it. He knew that the people of Earth had killed Ra, and he had heard that Thor seemed to be busy elsewhere, although he had no idea where or why.

Earth answered by sending its own teams out through the gate, and they killed Goa'uld. The System Lords came to look on Earth as fair game, and they have taken a close interest in it ever since. Earth's place under the treaty had to be negotiated afterwards, with Asgard as mediator.

In 1999 Thor himself opened the talks that put Earth under the treaty. Cronus, Nirrti and Lord Yu came through the Stargate for them. Nirrti tried to wreck the talks and failed. Cronus agreed to Earth's protection, as did Yu. None of the System Lords mentioned their old demand that Thor should stay away.

In the saga

The treaty has not been named in the saga. Its effects are on the Muggle news all the same. The hammer-bearing Avenger of Dudley's lunchbox has been replaced by a big blond man with a mace (Book Four, Chapter Three), because Thor is away at Asgard's war.

pages.title: Red Talons
infobox: The last wildernesses of the north
Hatred of mankind's spread; longing for the Impergium
pages.html:
The Red Talons are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou: a tribe of wolves, born only to wolves. They hold that mankind is the gravest wound ever dealt to Gaia, and they would gladly see the Impergium begin again.

Totem and ways

The Red Talons follow Griffin, a fierce hunting spirit of the high and lonely places. Every member of the tribe is lupus, born to a wolf and raised as one. They take human shape only when they must, and they dislike it. They speak little in human tongues, and they hardly ever use human tools. They keep their histories in the old way, by howl and by memory.

To the Talons, the Wyrm and mankind are hard to tell apart. They have watched the forests cut down, the rivers poisoned and the wolves shot out of one country after another. They hold that the Garou made a great mistake when they ended the culling of humanity at the Concord. Many of them would see it begin again tomorrow.

Homelands

Their Kinfolk are wolves, so the tribe lives where wolves still live. That means the last wildernesses of the north: the mountain forests of North America, the Russian taiga and the empty uplands of Europe. As the wolves have been driven back, so have the Red Talons. The tribe is smaller than it once was.

Place in the world

Other Garou respect the Talons for their purity and for their ferocity against the Wyrm. They fear their hatred of humans. The Talons despise the Glass Walkers and the Bone Gnawers for living among men. They scorn the Children of Gaia as soft, and they are wary even of homid Garou of other tribes. Vampires they regard with a particular loathing.

pages.title: Replicators
pages.html:
The Replicators are machines made of small interlocking blocks, which consume metal and technology in order to build more of themselves. They have spread from world to world. They are at war with Asgard, and it is that war which keeps Thor away from Earth in 1994.

Nature

A single Replicator block is a small grey piece of metal a few centimetres long. Thousands of them lock together to form a working machine, most often a scuttling, spider-like thing about the size of a dog, which can break apart and build itself again at will. They have one purpose, which is to copy themselves. Replicators strip whatever they find of its metal and its most advanced technology, then turn it all into more Replicators. A single block left alive aboard a ship can be enough to take it.

They learn as they go. Weapons that worked against them once soon stop working, because the swarm adapts to whatever is used against it. They are drawn above all to the most advanced technology in reach. That makes Asgard, the most advanced power they have met, their favourite prey.

Origin

The first Replicators were the toys of Reese, an android made in the likeness of a girl by an inventor on a distant world. She built them to protect herself and to keep her company. She could not control them. They destroyed the people who had made her, then went out into the stars.

War with Asgard

Asgard has fought the Replicators for years, on its own worlds and in its own fleets. It is losing ground. Thor himself commands Asgard's fleet against them, and the war takes nearly all of Asgard's strength. That is why Thor, the god of thunder, is away from Earth, and why Eric Masterson carries the mace in the Avengers as Thunderstrike. It is also why Asgard has less to spare for enforcing the Protected Planets Treaty against the Goa'uld System Lords.

The Goa'uld know nothing of it. Asgard has taken great care that they should not, since the System Lords keep the Protected Planets Treaty only because they believe Asgard could punish them for breaking it. Its ships still show themselves over the protected worlds as if nothing had changed. It is a bluff, and so far it has held.

In the saga

The Replicators have not been named in the saga. Their war is behind the change Harry noticed in the Avengers on the Muggle news of 20 August 1994 (Book Four, Chapter Three): the man with the hammer had been replaced by a big blond man with a mace.

pages.title: Secret Wars
infobox: Battleworld, a planet in a distant galaxy
Heroes and villains from across the world, and from beyond it
All but the Thing returned to Earth
pages.html:
The Secret Wars were the strange business of 1984 in which the Beyonder, a being of almost unlimited power from outside the universe, carried off heroes and villains from all over the world to a planet he had built for the purpose, Battleworld. There he set them to fight one another. He took the Avengers, the Fantastic Four, the X-Men, Spider-Man, heroes of the Justice League and the Jaffa master Bra'tac, among a good many others.

The taking

Early in 1984 a vast round structure appeared in the Sheep Meadow in Central Park. The heroes who went to look at it were carried away one after another, together with the Hulk, who had been drawn to it, and the structure went with them to the far side of the universe. There the Beyonder built a new world in front of them out of pieces of others, among them a suburb of Denver, people and all. He told the two sides, heroes and villains, that whoever destroyed their enemies should have whatever they desired.

The Beyonder cast his net wide. Besides the heroes of New York he took heroes of the Justice League. He also took Bra'tac of Chulak, a Jaffa master already more than a century old, who served the Goa'uld Apophis. On the villains' side he put Victor von Doom, Ultron, Kang the Conqueror, the Molecule Man, Doctor Octopus, the Absorbing Man, the Wrecking Crew and others. Magneto stood at first with the heroes, who did not much want him. Galactus came on his own account, hungry.

On Battleworld

Captain America led the heroes against the villains across Battleworld. Galactus tried to devour the planet. Doom built a machine to drain Galactus's power. With it he stole the power of the Beyonder himself and was for a time a god, until the Beyonder took it back.

An alien healer, Zsaji, gave her life to bring the fallen heroes back, and Colossus of the X-Men loved her. Spider-Man found what he took to be a new black costume, and brought it home with him. It was a living creature. Two women from the Denver suburb, Volcana and Titania, were given powers there by Doom, while a new Spider-Woman, Julia Carpenter, fought on the heroes' side.

When it was over, Reed Richards built a way home. Everyone came back except Ben Grimm, the Thing. He had found that on Battleworld he could turn back into a man whenever he liked, and he stayed on for a while to explore.

Afterwards

The Secret Wars changed several lives. The black costume later became Venom. She-Hulk took the Thing's place in the Fantastic Four. The Beyonder, having watched humanity at war, came to Earth himself in 1985 to try to understand it.

pages.title: Shadow Lords
infobox: The Carpathians, the Balkans and the Slavic East
Ambition, discipline and the pursuit of leadership
pages.html:
The Shadow Lords are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou: the ambitious, disciplined tribe of the Carpathians and the Balkans. They believe that the Garou need harder leadership than the Silver Fangs can give, and they mean to provide it.

Totem and ways

The Shadow Lords follow Grandfather Thunder, the lord of storms, a proud spirit who demands obedience and rewards success. They prize strength, cunning, discipline and results. Pity and squeamishness, in their view, are luxuries that a people at war cannot afford. They are the masters of politics within the Garou Nation: of gathering secrets, making alliances and calling in debts. They are as ruthless with their own failures as they are with their enemies.

They hold that the Silver Fangs, the traditional royal tribe, have grown weak and mad with inbreeding. The Garou will lose the war, they say, unless they are led by somebody fit to lead. That somebody, the Shadow Lords believe, is themselves.

Homelands

The tribe's heartland is Eastern Europe: the Carpathian mountains, the Balkans and the Slavic lands. Its Kinfolk have lived there for thousands of years, under one conqueror after another. There the Shadow Lords have fought for centuries against the Tzimisce, the vampire lords of those mountains. Their memories of that war are long and bitter. They have since spread with their Kinfolk across Europe and the Americas.

Place in the world

Few Garou trust a Shadow Lord entirely, and the tribe is often suspected of dealings it ought not to have. Yet they are formidable warriors and shrewd counsellors. Many a sept owes its survival to Shadow Lord planning. Their rivalry with the Silver Fangs is the oldest quarrel in Garou politics.

pages.title: Shi'ar
infobox: Aerie; the empire is ruled from Chandilar
The Imperial Guard, under the Praetor, Gladiator
pages.html:
The Shi'ar are a proud, bird-like people whose empire, the Shi'ar Imperium, lies far beyond Earth's galaxy. It is ruled from the throneworld of Chandilar by the Majestrix Lilandra Neramani, who has held the throne, with one long interruption, since 1979. She has loved Charles Xavier since 1976. The Shi'ar keep the M'Kraan Crystal, on which the whole of reality depends, and in 1980 they sentenced the Phoenix to death. In 1992 they broke the Kree Empire in a war that spilt over into Earth's part of space, and they have ruled what was left of it ever since.

The Shi'ar

The Shi'ar are descended from birds, and it shows. They have crests of feathers where human beings have hair. A few small feathers still grow along their forearms, where their ancestors' wings once were. Their bones are light and hollow. They lay eggs.

The Shi'ar lost their wings long ago. Now and then one is born with them, a throwback to the old race; Deathbird, the Majestrix's sister, is one. An ordinary Shi'ar can lift about a ton.

Their first home was the world called Aerie. The empire is ruled from Chandilar, the throneworld.

They worship two gods, Sharra and K'ythri. The Shi'ar say that the two were enemies until they were made to marry. In the marriage they found strength, and in time love. The Shi'ar have treated other peoples in much the same way ever since.

The Imperium

The Imperium is very old. The Shi'ar have been conquering other peoples for millions of years. A conquered people is said to have married into the empire, whether it wished to or not.

Its subject peoples each send a member to the High Council, which in theory governs the empire. In practice it is ruled by the Majestor, or by the Majestrix when the throne is held by a woman. The Council mostly does as it is told.

The throne is hereditary. In modern times it has belonged to the house of Neramani, to which Lilandra, her brother D'Ken and her sister Deathbird all belong. The Shi'ar are a proud people. They set great store by ceremony, honour and strength.

The throne is defended by the Imperial Guard, the finest warriors of the empire, drawn from the Shi'ar and from the peoples they rule. Each of them has powers of some kind.
