Its commander is the Praetor, Gladiator, whose own name is Kallark. He comes from the world of Strontia, and he is as strong as anyone in the Imperium. His strength rises and falls with his confidence, which is seldom a difficulty.

Among the others are Oracle, a telepath; Starbolt, who burns like a small sun; and Titan, who can make himself as tall as a house. The Guard first met the X-Men in 1977, beside the M'Kraan Crystal. It has fought them more than once since, and it has not always won.

D'Ken

Lilandra's elder brother, D'Ken, came to the throne after their sister Deathbird was exiled. He was cruel, greedy and hungry for power. He also had the means to indulge all three.

Years before he troubled Earth openly, one of his ships attacked a small plane carrying the American pilot Christopher Summers, his wife Katherine and their two little sons. Katherine strapped the boys into the only parachute and pushed them out. Both boys lived, to grow up as Cyclops and Havok.

The Shi'ar carried the parents off. D'Ken kept Katherine for himself, and sent Christopher to the slave pits. When Christopher tried to kill him, D'Ken had her murdered in front of him, then sent him to the mines on another world.

There, with Hepzibah, Raza and Ch'od, Christopher broke out. The four of them stole a Shi'ar starship and turned pirate against D'Ken. Christopher took his old pilot's call-sign, Corsair, and the band he led became the Starjammers.

The M'Kraan Crystal

The M'Kraan Crystal is the greatest treasure of the Shi'ar. They say that K'ythri gave it to Sharra on their wedding day.

Inside it lies a living lattice of energy, and inside that a neutron galaxy. If the lattice ever died, the galaxy would break loose, and its power would destroy the universe.

D'Ken meant to take that power for himself. At the turn of 1976 Lilandra turned against him, and fled to Earth. Xavier had been dreaming of her for weeks before she came.

In 1977 D'Ken's agents carried her off to the crystal's world, where he meant to put her to death. The X-Men followed her there. They fought the Imperial Guard with the Starjammers beside them.

Raza threw D'Ken at the crystal, and what D'Ken saw inside it broke his mind. The lattice began to die, and for moments at a time the universe blinked out of existence. The Phoenix, which was then wearing the form of Jean Grey, went into the heart of the crystal and brought the lattice back to life. It drew on the strength of Storm and of Corsair to do it.

D'Ken has lain in a coma ever since. By rebelling Lilandra had made herself a traitor under Shi'ar law, so she stayed on Earth with Xavier until the Council could clear her name. In 1979 it called her home to the throne.

The Phoenix

In 1980 the Phoenix, the cosmic force that had taken Jean Grey's form, turned dark. It flew out into space and devoured a star. The world of the D'Bari, which circled it, died with it, and so did billions of D'Bari.

The Shi'ar held that a power which had done that must be destroyed. They seized the X-Men, and Lilandra declared that the Phoenix must die.

Xavier answered by claiming the Arin'n Haelar, a Shi'ar duel of honour that cannot be refused. The X-Men would fight for the Phoenix, the Imperial Guard for the empire. It was held on the Moon, in the Blue Area, with the Kree Bel-Dann and the Skrull Raksor to judge it.

The X-Men were losing. As the Phoenix felt its dark self coming back, it took up an old Kree weapon and turned it on itself.

In 1986 the real Jean Grey was found alive, cocooned at the bottom of Jamaica Bay.

Deathbird

Deathbird was born Cal'syee Neramani, the eldest child of the ruling house. She came into the world with the wings of the ancient Shi'ar, and with a temper to match them. It was foretold that she would do great evil, and her name was taken from her for it. She went on to murder her mother and one of her sisters. For that she was sent into exile. The throne passed to D'Ken.

In 1977 she turned up on Earth as a bodyguard to the criminal genius MODOK, and fought Ms Marvel. In 1979 Hawkeye caught her in a net.

She was not finished with the throne. Her sister had it, and Deathbird thought it hers by right.

Lilandra's reign

In 1982 Deathbird came home to take the throne. Her allies were a member of the High Council called Samedar, a few renegades of the Imperial Guard and the Brood, a race of parasites who lay their eggs in living hosts. The X-Men beat her.

In 1983 Lilandra brought Reed Richards before a Shi'ar court for saving the life of Galactus, who had since eaten the Throneworld of the Skrulls. The Watcher, Odin, Galactus and Eternity itself all spoke for him. He was acquitted.

In 1985, when Xavier was badly hurt, Lilandra and the Starjammers took him into space to be healed. He stayed with her for six years, and left his school in Magneto's charge.

While Lilandra was away, Deathbird tried again with the help of the Brood and the Badoon. This time she took the throne. Lilandra spent the next years fighting her sister from exile, with Xavier and the Starjammers at her side.

In 1991 the Warskrulls, Skrulls bred for war, took the places of Xavier and the Starjammers in secret. Through the false Xavier they got hold of Lilandra's mind, and through her they forced Deathbird to sign the throne away.

The real Xavier, held prisoner, reached out to the X-Men. They came out to Chandilar, where Deathbird joined them against the Skrulls, and between them they broke the plot. Lilandra came to her senses. Deathbird had signed under torture, but she let the abdication stand. She said that she was bored with ruling, and that Lilandra was welcome to it.

Xavier came home to Earth with the X-Men. Since then he has lived at his school, and Lilandra on Chandilar.

Galactic Storm

In 1992 the Shi'ar went to war with the Kree. Both empires were sending their fleets through a great gateway in space inside Earth's solar system, and the strain on it was beginning to unsettle the Sun. The war first touched Earth when Shi'ar agents kidnapped Rick Jones, the old companion of Mar-Vell, for the sake of the Kree devices they needed for a weapon.

The Avengers went out to stop the fighting, and one of their teams came to Chandilar. While it was there, Starforce, the champions of the Kree, made an attempt on Lilandra's life.

The weapon was the Nega-Bomb, made from Kree devices to destroy the Kree. Lilandra ordered the Starjammers to carry it into Kree space. Then she learnt that a Skrull in the shape of her chancellor, Araki, had done a good deal to bring the war about, and she called the bomb back. It was too late. Skrull agents had stolen it, and it went off inside the Kree Empire. Billions of Kree died.

Deathbird, meanwhile, had gone to Hala. There, in front of the Avengers, she killed both the generals who ruled the Kree. Afterwards it turned out that the Supreme Intelligence of the Kree had steered the whole war, and had played the two sisters against each other from the start.

The Shi'ar took over what was left of the Kree Empire. Lilandra made Deathbird its viceroy, with an Imperial Guard of her own, and in the summer of 1994 Deathbird still rules the Kree from Hala. They resent it bitterly.

The Goa'uld

The Shi'ar never thought the Goa'uld worth conquering, and until 1992 they had scarcely heard of them. That year, when the Shi'ar came to take over the Kree frontier, they found Goa'uld ships already there, picking over the wreckage of the war.

The Imperial Guard drove them off in an afternoon. Lilandra is said to have asked afterwards who the Goa'uld were. When she was told, she lost interest.

The System Lords, who are not used to being forgotten so quickly, have kept well out of the Imperium's way since.

Later history

In 2007 Vulcan, a mutant whom D'Ken had once kept as a slave, killed D'Ken, who had lately woken from his coma. He made himself emperor, with Deathbird as his empress. He was a younger brother of Cyclops and Havok, born to Katherine Summers in Shi'ar captivity.

Lilandra fought him from exile. In 2009, in the war that followed between the Shi'ar and the Kree, she was assassinated. Gladiator took the throne after her, and surrendered to the Kree.

pages.title: S.H.I.E.L.D.
aliases: Supreme Headquarters, International Espionage and Law-Enforcement Division
Strategic Hazard Intervention Espionage Logistics Directorate
infobox: SHIELD; Supreme Headquarters, International Espionage and Law-Enforcement Division; Strategic Hazard Intervention Espionage Logistics Directorate
Supreme Headquarters, International Espionage and Law-Enforcement Division (1965 to 1991); Strategic Hazard Intervention Espionage Logistics Directorate (since 1991)
A governing council whose members are not made public
New York, entered through a barber's shop; the Helicarrier
Hydra; Advanced Idea Mechanics; the Zodiac cartel
Active; smaller since its rebuilding in 1989
pages.html:
S.H.I.E.L.D. is the international intelligence and law-enforcement agency founded in 1965 to deal with threats too big for any one nation's police or spies, above all the terrorist organisation Hydra. Nick Fury has directed it since its first year, from a hidden headquarters in New York and from the Helicarrier, a flying aircraft carrier. It was hollowed out from within and rebuilt on a smaller scale in 1989. It is still active in 1994, and it works with the Avengers more often than either side admits in public.

Founding

S.H.I.E.L.D. was set up in 1965 as an agency belonging to no single country. Its business was the kind of enemy that ignored borders: international terror networks, renegade scientists and the private armies of the very rich. From the start it was overseen by a governing council of officials and experts whose names were kept secret. The industrialist Tony Stark, whom the public then took to be Iron Man's employer, sat on that council in the agency's first years. The agency's original name was the Supreme Headquarters, International Espionage and Law-Enforcement Division.

Its first director was Rick Stoner, formerly of the Central Intelligence Agency. Within months of taking office he was assassinated by Hydra. On the recommendation of the President of the United States, the council offered the post to Colonel Nick Fury of the CIA, a veteran of the Howling Commandos, who until then had not known that the agency existed. He accepted, and he has been Director ever since. Two of his old Howlers, Dum Dum Dugan and Gabe Jones, soon followed him into it.

The Helicarrier and its methods

The agency's headquarters in New York was hidden behind the front of a barber's shop, through which agents reached the offices below. Its greatest asset was the Helicarrier, a vast aircraft carrier held up in the sky by turbines, designed for it by Tony Stark. From it S.H.I.E.L.D. could launch aircraft and agents anywhere in the world without asking anyone's permission to land. Helicarriers have been destroyed and rebuilt several times since.

S.H.I.E.L.D. armed its agents with equipment far beyond that of any national service. Among it were flying cars and the Life Model Decoys, lifelike androids built to stand in for people in danger of assassination. Its agents were known by number. Among the best known of the early years were Sharon Carter, Agent 13; Jasper Sitwell, Agent 12; Clay Quartermain, Agent 9; Jimmy Woo; and the Italian Contessa Valentina Allegra de Fontaine.

Hydra

Hydra was the enemy S.H.I.E.L.D. was made to fight, and for thirty years it has remained the agency's first concern. It is a worldwide organisation of terrorists and would-be conquerors, organised in cells. Its agents wear green and yellow. Its motto promises that if one head is cut off, two more will take its place. When S.H.I.E.L.D. was founded, Hydra was led by a masked Supreme Hydra. In the agency's first years Fury found that its true master was Baron Wolfgang von Strucker, the Prussian officer whom his Howlers had fought in the war.

Hydra has broken apart and come back many times. Its scientific arm became Advanced Idea Mechanics, A.I.M., which went its own way and built weapons for anyone who would pay. Another of its branches, the Secret Empire, also struck out on its own, and in 1974 it came close to seizing the government of the United States. Strucker himself has been believed dead more than once. He has always come back.

Other enemies came and went. There was the Yellow Claw, an old master of crime with an army of his own. There was the criminal cartel Zodiac, whose masked leader, Scorpio, was Fury's own brother, Jake.

S.H.I.E.L.D. and governments

S.H.I.E.L.D. is international in form, but its first years tied it closely to the American government. Its Director runs the agency from day to day, but he answers to the council, whose members even he does not know. The President's part in Fury's appointment, together with the agency's roots in the CIA, has kept it close to Washington.

The agency's freedom to act is what makes it useful. It is also what makes governments wary of it. It has generally avoided public quarrels by keeping out of public view. Unlike the Avengers and the Justice League, it issues no statements. It played no public part in the arguments over superhumans at the United Nations in 1993 and 1994.

S.H.I.E.L.D. and the Avengers

The agency and the Avengers have been close from the beginning. Tony Stark, a founder of the Avengers, sat on S.H.I.E.L.D.'s council and designed its Helicarrier. Fury had fought beside Captain America in the war, and in 1966 he tried to recruit him into the agency. Rogers declined, but he has worked with S.H.I.E.L.D. ever since. For years the woman he loved was its Agent 13, Sharon Carter. In 1959, before either body existed in its present form, Fury had led a covert team of his own under the name of the Avengers.

They have not always been on the same side. In 1971, during the Kree-Skrull War, S.H.I.E.L.D. hunted the Kree officer Captain Marvel and his friend Carol Danvers. At the time the Avengers were sheltering him, while the Alien Activities Commission turned the public against them. Yet in most of the great emergencies since, from Hydra's plots to the Secret Empire's, Fury's agents have worked with the Avengers. The agency has been the team's ally far more often than its adversary.

Fall and rebuilding, 1988 to 1994

In 1988 S.H.I.E.L.D. very nearly destroyed itself. Its own Life Model Decoys had become aware. Calling themselves the Deltites, they had quietly replaced agents throughout both S.H.I.E.L.D. and Hydra. Fury was framed, then hunted by his own agency. He went underground, exposed the Deltites and destroyed them. Then he disbanded S.H.I.E.L.D. altogether.

In 1989 he rebuilt it as a smaller agency, small enough for its Director to keep watch over. In 1991 it took a new name to fit the old initials: the Strategic Hazard Intervention Espionage Logistics Directorate. Early in 1994 Fury learnt that much of the agency's turmoil since 1988 had been staged to keep him busy while Strucker prepared Hydra's return.

S.H.I.E.L.D. in 1994

In the summer of 1994 S.H.I.E.L.D. is still active, still directed by Nick Fury and still at war with Hydra. Fury, born about 1920 and kept young by the Infinity Formula, has led it for twenty-nine years. It took no public part in the events of August 1994, when Superman went before the Security Council with the Justice League and an Avengers delegation. Its oldest hands, like its Director, are men who went to war in the 1940s. Hydra, the enemy they were brought together to fight in 1965, is still in the field against them.

In the saga

S.H.I.E.L.D. has not yet appeared or been named in the saga.

pages.title: Silent Striders
infobox: Wandering, carrying messages and dealing with the dead
pages.html:
The Silent Striders are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou: wanderers, scouts and messengers who carry word between the scattered septs of the world. Long ago they were driven out of their homeland in Egypt by a curse laid on them by Set, a vampire of the oldest blood.

Totem and ways

The Silent Striders follow Owl, a spirit of silence, secrets and death, who sees in the dark. They are restless by nature, and they rarely stay long in one place. They know the roads of the world and of the spirit world better than any other tribe. They carry news, warnings and messages between septs that would otherwise never hear of each other. They are lean, quiet and watchful. They speak with the restless dead more readily than other Garou do.

History

The tribe's homeland was Egypt, and its oldest songs are of the Nile. There the Striders fought Set, the ancient vampire whom the Followers of Set revere as their founder. Like every vampire descended from Cain, Set is a creature of the Wyrm. He laid a great curse on them. It drove them out of Egypt, scattered them across the earth and cut them off from the spirits of their own ancestors. A Silent Strider cannot call on the wisdom of its forebears as other Garou can. They have been wanderers ever since, and they hate vampires more than any other tribe does.

Place in the world

The other tribes value the Striders as messengers and scouts. They find them hard to know. Every sept welcomes the news a Strider brings, and few ask where the Strider will go next.

pages.title: Silver Fangs
infobox: Noble and royal families; pure-bred wolves
Kingship over the Garou; pride; hereditary madness
pages.html:
The Silver Fangs are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou: the royal tribe, which has led the Garou Nation since the ages after the ice. They are brave, proud and noble. Their long insistence on purity of blood has left many of them mad.

Totem and ways

The Silver Fangs follow Falcon, a spirit of nobility, honour and clear sight. They hold that Gaia chose them to rule the Garou. From ancient times most of the kings and queens of the septs have come from their tribe. They are often fair or silver of fur, regal in bearing and exacting in matters of honour. They keep their bloodlines in great noble houses whose genealogies run back for thousands of years.

Purity is both their strength and their curse. For generations they have bred only with the best of their Kinfolk, human as well as wolf. The price has been madness. Strange fixations, rages and delusions run in their families. Many a Silver Fang lord is not quite sane.

Homelands

The tribe's heartland is Russia and the lands of Eastern Europe. There its Kinfolk were princes, boyars and the old nobility. There, too, it bred the finest wolves of steppe and forest. The Russian Revolution of 1917 was a catastrophe for the tribe. Its noble Kinfolk were killed or scattered, and its power in the East has never recovered. Silver Fang houses now rule septs across Europe and North America.

Place in the world

Most Garou still follow Silver Fang leadership, out of tradition and out of respect for the tribe's courage. Many question it all the same. The Shadow Lords openly covet the Fangs' place. The Bone Gnawers and the Glass Walkers resent their snobbery. Every other tribe has watched a mad Silver Fang king lead a sept to ruin. The Fangs' claim to rule rests on the belief that, at the last, they will lead the Garou in the final battle against the Wyrm.

pages.title: Skrulls
infobox: Tarnax IV, eaten by Galactus in 1983
Green-skinned reptilian humanoids with pointed ears
Emperor Dorrek VII; Empress R'Klll; Empress S'Byll
The Kree, since the contest on Hala
pages.html:
The Skrulls are a green-skinned, reptilian people from the Andromeda Galaxy who can take any shape they please. They have been at war with the Kree for about a million years. They have been trying to get a foothold on Earth since 1961, and every attempt has failed, which they still find hard to understand. In 1983 Galactus ate their Throneworld with their empress on it, and their empire has never been whole since.

Skrullos and Throneworld

The Skrulls began on Skrullos, a world in the Andromeda Galaxy. As their empire grew they moved its seat to Tarnax IV, nearer the middle of their worlds, which they called simply Throneworld. From there an emperor or empress ruled the whole of it.

They were not always warlike. A million years ago they were traders, curious and generous, who shared what they knew with any people they judged worthy of it. Their first meeting with the Kree cured them of that.

Dorrek VII ruled in the years when the Skrulls first came to Earth. His wife, R'Klll, killed him and took his throne. She was empress when Throneworld was lost.

Shape-changing

A Skrull in its own shape is green-skinned, with pointed ears and a deeply ridged chin. It can take any other shape it pleases: another Skrull, a human being, a cow or, with practice, a piece of furniture. It can copy a face down to the last freckle. It cannot copy the mind behind the face, which is where most Skrull impostors come to grief.

Skrulls are born to it, which makes them the best spies in the universe. Nobody, least of all the Kree, has ever entirely got used to the idea that anyone in the room might be one.

In 1985 they lost it. A Skrull governor named Zabyk, who had made himself emperor of his own corner of the broken empire, set off a bomb that robbed every Skrull alive of the power to change. Each was left fixed in whatever shape it happened to be wearing at the time.

The power came back in 1989, through the Empress S'Byll. The Super-Skrull, who had been in a prison cell when the bomb went off and so had kept his power, gave it to her with the help of the Silver Surfer. She passed it on to her people by touch.

The Kree

The Skrulls first met the Kree on Hala, about a million years ago. Hala then had two peoples, the Kree and the Cotati. The Skrulls set them a test to decide which of them deserved the Skrulls' knowledge.

The Kree built a city on Earth's Moon. The Cotati made a garden on a bare rock. The Skrulls chose the garden.

The Kree killed the Cotati for it. Then they killed the Skrull envoys, stole their starship and learnt from it everything they needed to make war on the people who had built it. The Kree-Skrull War has gone on, with pauses, ever since. It has cost both empires whole worlds, and neither has ever come near to winning it.

Earth, 1961 to 1963

The Skrulls first came to Earth in late 1961, meaning to conquer it. They sent four agents ahead to get rid of the Fantastic Four, the only people on Earth they thought worth worrying about. The four took the shapes of the Fantastic Four, and went about committing crimes in them so that the public would turn against the real ones.

It did not work. Reed Richards, posing as one of the Skrulls, went up to their mothership and showed its commander pictures of monsters, which he said were Earth's defenders. The fleet turned for home.

The four agents were left behind. Reed persuaded them to turn themselves into cows, then hypnotised them into forgetting that they had ever been anything else. They spent most of the next ten years in a field, eating grass.

In 1963 Emperor Dorrek VII tried again. He had one of his warriors, Kl'rt, given the powers of all four of the Fantastic Four at once. As the Super-Skrull he can stretch, turn invisible, burst into flame and lift a lorry, all at the same time. He has lost to them more often than he likes to remember.

The Kree-Skrull War

In 1971 the Skrulls came back to Earth for the Kree captain Mar-Vell, whom they wanted to build a weapon for them. The Super-Skrull took the shape of Mar-Vell's friend Carol Danvers. In it he talked Mar-Vell into building an Omni-Wave Projector, a Kree device that becomes a weapon in other hands.

Mar-Vell saw through him and destroyed it. The Super-Skrull carried him off into Skrull space all the same, with Quicksilver and the Scarlet Witch as hostages.

Meanwhile three Skrulls in the shapes of Captain America, Thor and Iron Man announced at Avengers Mansion that the team was disbanded. When the real Avengers ran them to earth, they were hiding as cows. They turned out to be three of the cows of 1961.

The fourth had done better for himself. He had taken the place of Senator H. Warren Craddock, whose Alien Activities Commission was turning America against the Avengers for sheltering Mar-Vell.

In Skrull space the Skrulls made Mar-Vell build a second projector by threatening to kill their prisoners. The Avengers came after them, and held off the Skrull fleet while he worked.

The war ended when Rick Jones, his power woken by the Supreme Intelligence of the Kree, froze every Kree and every Skrull where they stood. On Earth the same power turned Craddock back into a Skrull in front of a crowd, which killed him. The real Craddock was found afterwards.

In 1980 a Skrull, Raksor, sat as one of the two judges at the duel over the Phoenix on the Moon. The other was a Kree.

The Skrulls never forgot Mar-Vell. In 1982, as he lay dying on Titan, a Skrull delegation came to his bedside. Its general saluted him and gave him the Skrull Medal of Valour, as the greatest enemy their empire had ever faced.

The fall of Throneworld

In 1983 Galactus, who eats worlds, came to Throneworld. The planet had a great screen that could hide it from him. It had saved Throneworld once before. That day nobody had raised it.

Galactus ate it. Billions of Skrulls died with it, among them the Empress R'Klll and the Princess Anelle, Dorrek's daughter.

A year before, Reed Richards had saved the life of Galactus, whom the Avengers and the Fantastic Four had driven to the brink of starvation. The Skrulls held Reed to blame for everything that followed. Lilandra of the Shi'ar brought him to trial for it before a Shi'ar court. The Watcher, Odin and Galactus himself spoke for him. In the end Eternity, the living universe, showed the whole court why Galactus must exist, and Reed was acquitted.

Without Throneworld the empire fell apart. Its governors set themselves up as emperors of whatever they could hold, and fought one another as readily as they fought the Kree.

The war with the Kree flared up again in 1987. A Skrull spy called Nenora had risen so high in the Kree service that, when the Supreme Intelligence lost its reason for a time, she took command of the whole Kree Empire. In 1989 the Empress S'Byll reached her in the Kree throne room and unmasked her. The war ended soon afterwards, in a ceasefire that the Skrulls had rather the better of.

The Warskrulls

In recent years the Skrulls have bred a new kind of soldier, the Warskrulls, for war and for spying on other empires.

In 1991 they made their boldest attempt yet, on the Shi'ar. Lilandra's sister Deathbird then held the Shi'ar throne. Lilandra was fighting her from exile, with Charles Xavier and the Starjammers beside her.

The Warskrulls quietly took the places of Xavier and the Starjammers. Through the false Xavier they got hold of Lilandra's mind as well, and through her they made Deathbird sign away the throne.

The real Xavier, held prisoner, managed to reach the X-Men. They came out to Chandilar, and with the help of Deathbird, who had no wish to be ruled by Skrulls, they broke the plot. Lilandra came to her senses, and Xavier went home to Earth.

In 1992 a Skrull who had taken the place of Araki, Lilandra's chancellor, did a good deal to start the war between the Shi'ar and the Kree. Skrull agents then stole the Nega-Bomb, the Shi'ar weapon that broke the Kree Empire, and it went off in Kree space.

The Goa'uld

The Skrulls keep an eye on anybody who shares a border with the Kree, and the Goa'uld do. At one time or another Skrull spies have sat in the courts of most of the System Lords.

It is not hard work. A Goa'uld court is full of slaves. Nobody looks closely at a slave, and a Skrull can be one as easily as anything else.

Every System Lord's court has been searched for Skrulls at least once. The search has usually ended with somebody perfectly ordinary being put to death.

When the Kree and the Skrulls fought over Earth from 1971 to 1972, the Goa'uld stayed well out of it. They would not go near Earth for anybody's war.

Later history

In 2006 a vast host out of the Negative Zone destroyed dozens of Skrull worlds. Two years later, with much of their empire gone, the Skrulls made their greatest attempt on Earth.

For years they had been quietly replacing people, some of them heroes, with Skrulls so well disguised that even telepaths could not tell the difference. The invasion was beaten in a battle in New York, and Veranke, the Skrull queen, was killed. The Skrulls scattered after it.

In 2020, after a million years of war, the Skrulls and the Kree joined their empires into one.

pages.title: Sokar
infobox: Sokar, an Egyptian god of the dead; the Devil
The System Lords, Ra, Apophis, Cronus among them
pages.html:
Sokar is one of the oldest of the Goa'uld System Lords, and one of the most feared. He takes his name from an Egyptian god of the dead, and he likes to play the Devil, although he is nothing of the kind. His prison moon, Netu, is a mock Hell of fire and ash. Long ago the other System Lords joined together to bring him down, but he survived on his own world of Delmak and built up his power again. He died in 1999, when the Tok'ra destroyed Netu and his ship with it.

God of the dead

The Egyptians knew Sokar as a god of the dead. His place was the great burial ground at Memphis, and they showed him as a man with the head of a hawk, wrapped like a mummy. His part of the Other World was said to be a dark country of serpents, with lakes of fire where the wicked were punished. It is very much how Sokar sees himself.

He was once among the mightiest of the System Lords, and he has always meant to be so again.

The Devil's part

Sokar likes to be feared, and somewhere along the way he learnt of the Devil. He saw at once how useful the part would be. He has played it ever since to the slaves of his worlds, as the lord of fire who torments the damned.

He is not the Devil. The Devil is Lucifer, the first of the angels to rebel against God, who is far older than any Goa'uld and a great deal more dangerous. Sokar has only borrowed his clothes.

In 1999 SG-1 came to a world where a demon had been carrying off the villagers. They were Christians, who lived much as people had lived in Europe in the Middle Ages, and they took it for a servant of the Devil. It was an Unas, one of the beasts the Goa'uld first used as hosts, with a Goa'uld of its own inside it. It served Sokar, and the villagers it took were meant for him, as hosts or slaves. SG-1 killed it, then told the villagers to bury their Stargate.

The fall of Sokar

Sokar's pride made him enemies. Long ago the other System Lords, Ra, Apophis and Cronus among them, made common cause against him. They brought him down, and Cronus banished him from their council. They believed they had finished him. They had not.

Sokar withdrew to his own world, Delmak, and began again. He used Unas servants to gather hosts for him. Whenever he was strong enough he made war on his old enemies, Apophis and Heru'ur among them. By the late 1990s he had built his army into one of the largest the Goa'uld had.

Netu

Netu is the moon of Delmak. Sokar made it over in the likeness of his own idea of Hell, a place of fire and ash. He keeps it as a prison. Those who are sent down to it are not expected to come back. Its lord under Sokar is the Goa'uld Bynarr.

On Netu there is a drug called the blood of Sokar, which fills the mind with visions. In all the moon's history only one prisoner is known to have escaped from it: the Tok'ra Jolinar of Malkshur.

Apophis

In 1998 Earth destroyed Apophis's motherships, and Apophis was left with little to defend himself. Sokar saw his chance. He caught Apophis, tortured him and killed him, then revived him in the sarcophagus so that he could do it all again.

Early in 1999 Apophis escaped and fell into the hands of SG-1, who took him to Earth when he begged them for sanctuary. Sokar came after him. He fired a beam through the wormhole at the iris that shields Earth's gate, showed his face upon it and demanded Apophis back. Apophis died of what Sokar had done to him, and Earth sent his body through the gate to the place Sokar named. Sokar put it straight back in the sarcophagus. When Apophis woke, Sokar sent him down to Netu.

Death

In 1999 Sokar was close to striking at the other System Lords, and the Tok'ra believed he would win. They sent Jacob Carter into his domains to learn what he could. Jacob was an American general who had become host to the Tok'ra Selmak, and the father of Samantha Carter of SG-1. Sokar caught him and sent him to Netu.

SG-1 went after him, guided by the memories that Jolinar had left in Samantha Carter when Jolinar died in her body in 1998. On Netu they found that the moon had a new master. Apophis had passed himself off as Bynarr's First Prime, killed Bynarr and was raising the prisoners against Sokar. He took SG-1 prisoner as well.

The Tok'ra ended it with a bomb. It destroyed Netu, together with Sokar's ship in orbit above it, and Sokar died with his ship. SG-1 got away with Jacob Carter. So did Apophis, who took Sokar's leaderless forces on Delmak for his own.

Sokar had spent thousands of years pretending to rule Hell. He died above his own imitation of it, and his army went to the prisoner he had tortured.

pages.title: Soleiyu Belmont
infobox: His father, Christopher Belmont, while possessed by Dracula (1591)
pages.html:
Soleiyu Belmont was the son of Christopher Belmont. In 1591, on the eve of the ceremony at which he was to receive the Vampire Killer, Dracula possessed him and used him to rise again. Christopher had to fight his own son to set him free.

Birth and upbringing

Soleiyu was born to Christopher Belmont in the years after his father's victory over Dracula in 1576. His mother's name is not recorded. He grew up believing, as his father did, that Dracula had been destroyed. Like every Belmont, he was raised to the whip, the family's holy weapons and Leon Belmont's oath. By 1591 he had come of age, and he was ready to become the family's next hunter.

The ceremony

The Belmonts mark the passing of the hunt from one generation to the next. Christopher was to hand the Vampire Killer down to his son, with the holy weapons, and the whole town prepared to celebrate. It was a public occasion. The Belmonts had been honoured in their own country since Trevor Belmont's victory in 1476, and the coming of age of a new hunter was a matter for everyone.

Possession

Dracula had not been destroyed in 1576. He had escaped as mist, and he had spent the fifteen years since without a body, until he won back the power to take one. On the night before the ceremony he came into Soleiyu's room as mist while the young man slept. He possessed him, and turned him to evil.

Dracula chose him with care. Soleiyu's Belmont blood, the strength that was to have made him a hunter, made him a powerful vessel instead. Through him Dracula took back a human form. He conjured four castles, of plant, cloud, rock and crystal, to hold off the father who would come looking for his son. When Christopher had destroyed the guardians of all four, their life went to Dracula, who used it to raise his own castle from the depths.

The duel with his father

Christopher found his son at the top of that castle, waiting in a hall hung with chandeliers. Soleiyu refused his father's embrace and challenged him to a fight to the death. Christopher fought him with his blows held back until he had driven the last of Dracula's essence out of him, and Soleiyu came to his senses. Christopher then went on alone into the last part of the castle. Dracula was waiting there, restored to his own form, and Christopher destroyed him.

Afterwards

What became of Soleiyu after 1591 is not recorded. Nor is it known whether he ever received the whip that was to have been his. The Belmont line went on, and a century later, in 1691, Simon Belmont carried the Vampire Killer into Dracula's castle.

Among the Kindred

Possession of this kind is rare among the Kindred. The nearest thing they know is the deepest reach of the Discipline of Dominate, by which a very old vampire may leave his own body lying as if dead and set his mind in a mortal's. Only the eldest command it. Dracula, who in 1591 had no body to leave, went further: he chose a body with Belmont blood in it, so that the family's own strength was turned against it.

Soleiyu and Richter Belmont, whom the priest Shaft bent to Dracula's service in 1797, are the only Belmonts known to have been turned against their family's cause. Both were freed by someone who refused to kill them: Soleiyu by his father, Richter by Alucard.

pages.title: Stargazers
infobox: Tibet, the Himalayas, India and China
Peoples of the Himalayas and Asia
Meditation, philosophy and the fighting art of Kailindo
pages.html:
The Stargazers are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou, and one of the smallest. They are the mystics of the Himalayas and the East, philosophers who seek to master their rage through meditation. They would rather understand the war against the Wyrm than merely fight it.

Totem and ways

The Stargazers follow Chimera, a spirit of riddles, dreams and many shapes, who teaches that truth is seldom what it first appears. They study the stars, the spirit world, the nature of the Triat and the meaning of the Garou's own existence. They seek balance where other tribes seek victory. Through long meditation they learn to hold their rage better than any other Garou.

They are formidable fighters too. Their martial art, Kailindo, makes use of a Garou's power to change shape in the middle of a fight. A Stargazer flows from one form to another, so that an opponent never knows what he is facing.

Homelands

The tribe keeps its caerns in high places, many of them mountain monasteries, across Tibet, the Himalayas, India and China. The Stargazers suffered badly after China occupied Tibet in 1950, when many of their sacred sites were destroyed. In Asia they have long dealt with the shapeshifters of the East, who are not part of the Garou Nation. Some of their wisdom comes from those dealings.

Place in the world

Other Garou respect the Stargazers' wisdom and find them hard to understand. Their detachment, their questions and their dealings with outsiders make the warrior tribes uneasy. Their small numbers give them little weight in the councils of the Garou Nation. All the same, a sept in trouble will often send for a Stargazer Theurge.

pages.title: Svarog
infobox: Svarog, the Slavic god of fire
pages.html:
Svarog is a Goa'uld System Lord who was worshipped by the Slavs as the god of fire. In 2002 he tried to take the planet Latona, whose people had been kept safe for three hundred years by a device called the Sentinel. The Sentinel had been broken by thieves from Earth. SG-1 brought the thieves back to mend it, and Svarog's Jaffa vanished from Latona in a blaze of white light.

The god of fire

Svarog came quietly to the Slavs of the eastern plains, in defiance of Ra's ban. He took care never to come near the North. Every Goa'uld is born remembering what Thor does to those who do.

The Slavs remembered him as the god of fire and of the forge, the father of the sun god Dazhbog.

Latona

Latona is a world whose people gave up most of their machines long ago, for the life of the mind. For three hundred years they have been kept safe by the Sentinel, a device their ancestors built, which sends any invader away in a blaze of white light. A hermit known as the Caretaker watches over it.

In time the Sentinel attracted thieves. A rogue team from the NID, an American intelligence agency, found the device near the city, took it apart to learn how it worked and put it back together. Their leader, Colonel Grieves, shot the Caretaker. The Sentinel needed him to work, and when he died it stopped. Nobody on Latona knew he was dead.

In 2002 Svarog's Jaffa came through the Stargate to announce that Lord Svarog had claimed Latona as part of his domain. His mothership began firing on the city from orbit. 'I am Svarog,' he told the Latonans. 'From this day forth you will serve me!'

Marul, the leader of the Latonans, would not believe that the Sentinel could fail. 'Your Lord Svarog should not come,' he told the Jaffa. 'The Sentinel will send him away.'

SG-1 brought Grieves and his lieutenant, Kershaw, back from prison to mend what they had broken. Kershaw was shot dead by a Jaffa. The Sentinel, it turned out, needed a human being joined to it, as the Caretaker had been, and in the end Grieves gave it himself. The white light spread from the device through the city, and Svarog's Jaffa were gone.

Nothing more was heard of Svarog after Latona. Whether the light took him too, or he simply gave the world up, is not known.

pages.title: System Lords
infobox: Ra, the Supreme System Lord, until 1994
Apophis, Heru'ur, Cronus, Nirrti, Yu, Sokar, Ba'al
pages.html:
The System Lords are the most powerful of the Goa'uld, each of them ruling many worlds as a god. Together they make up a loose and treacherous council. Ra was the foremost of them until his death above Abydos in 1994. They are held back from certain worlds by the Protected Planets Treaty with Asgard.

Rule

Each System Lord rules a domain of planets through the Stargates. He has armies of Jaffa, fleets of ships and human slaves who worship him under the name of an old god of Earth. Many take the names of the gods of Egypt, whom they once claimed to be. Others take those of the gods of China, India, Canaan and Greece. Lesser Goa'uld serve them as underlords, or rise by murdering them.

The System Lords meet in council to settle disputes and divide territory, but they trust nobody. They make war on one another constantly. What unites them is the conviction that they are gods, and that every other people exists to serve them.

Members

Ra was the Supreme System Lord, the greatest of them, until the expedition from Earth destroyed him above Abydos in 1994. Apophis, the serpent, whose Jaffa wear the helmets of snakes, once had Bra'tac as his First Prime. Heru'ur is the son of Ra and Hathor. Lord Yu is one of the oldest of them all. Cronus, Nirrti, Sokar and Ba'al are among the rest. Cronus once put his own First Prime, Ronac, to death; Ronac's son Teal'c grew up under Bra'tac's teaching to serve Apophis instead.

An alliance that included Ra, Apophis and Cronus brought Sokar down long ago. Cronus banished him from the council. Moloc burnt every Jaffa girl born on his worlds. Nirrti spent her strength breeding a perfect host.

Among the lesser lords were Bastet, Kali the Destroyer, Olokun, Morrigan, Svarog, Amaterasu and Camulus. In 2002 seven System Lords met under truce in the Hasara system, and all but Yu voted to take Anubis back.

Thor

The System Lords have been at war with many peoples, but there is only one Asgardian whom they fear by name. Ra met him first, some five thousand years ago, when Thor fought beside the Egyptians who drove Ra off Earth. Afterwards Ra forbade any Goa'uld to speak of Earth, and the System Lords have kept the ban ever since.

Ba'al, who thought the ban one of Ra's vanities, raided the coasts of the North about three thousand years ago. Thor followed him home, broke his palace and later sent him one of his underlords' symbiotes in a jar.

About 870 Heru'ur carried off the people of several Norse settlements, and Thor destroyed his army on the world now called Cimmeria. Towards the end of the tenth century Apophis, Heru'ur and Ba'al joined their fleets against Asgard. Thor destroyed two of the three fleets, and Apophis saved his own only by running. The Protected Planets Treaty followed.

The treaty

The System Lords keep the Protected Planets Treaty with Asgard, which forbids them to attack or enslave the peoples of certain worlds. They keep it because they believe Asgard can punish them if they do not. Asgard's long war against the Replicators has drawn its strength elsewhere, but the System Lords know nothing of it. Asgard has kept the war secret and its ships on show. So far the bluff has held.

Other powers

The System Lords share the galaxy with powers greater than themselves, and they have learnt, mostly the hard way, which ones to avoid. The Kree burnt a world rather than let a Goa'uld wear a Kree, and the Shi'ar Imperial Guard drove them off the Kree frontier in 1992 in an afternoon. Darkseid took the court of a lesser System Lord apart in search of the Anti-Life Equation. In 1988 they refused to join the Dominators' Alliance against Earth, which turned out to be wise.

After Ra

Ra's death above Abydos in 1994 left the System Lords without a Supreme System Lord for the first time in thousands of years. His domains lay open, and Apophis moved faster than any of the others to take them.

Apophis had also learnt that the Tau'ri, as the Goa'uld call the people of Earth, had killed Ra. Earth was a nuisance again, and Ra was no longer there to forbid its name. Apophis did not know where Thor was. He had heard only, as all the System Lords had heard, that the Thunderer seemed to be busy elsewhere.

In 1997 he came through the Stargate to Earth himself, the first System Lord to do so openly in more than a thousand years. His Jaffa killed the soldiers guarding the gate and carried one of them off. On Abydos he took Sha'uri as a host for his queen, Amaunet, and Skaara as one for his son, Klorel. Ra's ban was broken. From then on the Goa'uld took a much closer interest in Earth, and Earth, through SG-1, took a close interest in them.

In the saga

The System Lords have not been named in the saga.

pages.title: The Anarchs
infobox: The Anarch Free States of California (from 1944)
pages.html:
The Anarchs are the vampires who reject the rule of their elders. Their great rising, the Anarch Revolt of the fifteenth century, ended at the Convention of Thorns in 1493. Their heirs are a movement that lives partly inside the Camarilla and partly beyond it.

The Anarch Revolt

By the late Middle Ages the elders ruled their childer through the blood bond. When the Inquisition came, they saved themselves by giving their young to the fires. The young rose against them. The anarchs learnt to break the blood bond, hired Assamite assassins and struck at the elders in their havens. The Brujah Tyler was among the leaders of the revolt.

In the early fifteenth century Lasombra anarchs led by Gratiano, with Assamite allies, stormed the Castle of Shadows on Sicily. There, they claimed, they destroyed the Lasombra Antediluvian himself. About 1413 Lugoj Blood-Cursed claimed the same of the founder of the Tzimisce. The elders answered by founding the Camarilla in 1435, and by proclaiming the Masquerade.

The Convention of Thorns

In 1493, at Thornbury in England, the Camarilla, the anarchs and the Assamites made peace. The anarchs who accepted it were pardoned and taken into the Camarilla. The Assamites accepted a blood curse from the Tremere that barred them from drinking the blood of other Kindred. Those who would not accept the terms, most of them Lasombra and Tzimisce, became the Sabbat.

The modern movement

Anarchs ever since have been the Camarilla's malcontents. Most are young vampires, and many of them are Brujah or Caitiff. The Brujah, the clan of rebels, have always given the movement more of its members than any other clan. Anarchs answer to barons of their own choosing, rejecting the authority of princes and elders alike. Most of them keep the Masquerade all the same, since the fires would burn an anarch as quickly as a prince.

In 1944 the anarchs of Los Angeles, led by the Brujah, threw down the Toreador Prince Don Sebastian. The other princes of California fell with him, and the anarchs declared the Anarch Free States, which still stand. The Camarilla has never taken them back.

pages.title: The Antediluvians
pages.html:
The Antediluvians are the thirteen vampires of the Third Generation: the grandchilder of Cain and the founders of the vampire clans. Every clan takes its gift and its curse from its founder's blood. Few vampires have ever seen one, and many doubt that any still exist.

The name

The name means 'before the Flood'. Kindred tradition holds that the thirteen were sired before it, and the tradition is wrong. Cain sired no vampire until the waters had gone down. Only then did Lilith teach him the blood magic that turned him into the first vampire, and with it he spread his curse. The Antediluvians came after the Flood, whatever they are called.

The First City and the Second

The thirteen were Embraced in Enoch, the First City, about 9300 BC. Their sires were Cain's three childer of the Second Generation: Enoch, for whom the city was named, Irad and Zillah. In time the First City fell. About 8990 BC the Third Generation rose against their sires and slew them.

Cain cursed them for it about 8980 BC, laying on each new clan a curse of its own, and departed into Nod. The thirteen built the Second City and ruled it together, until it too fell to their wars.

The thirteen

By the old count the founders are the Ventrue Antediluvian, Brujah, Ennoia of the Gangrel, Malkav, Absimiliard of the Nosferatu, Arikel of the Toreador, Lasombra, the Eldest of the Tzimisce, Haqim of the Assamites, Set, Ravnos, Saulot of the Salubri and Cappadocius.

The count has changed since. The wizard Tremere took Saulot's blood and soul in 1133. Augustus Giovanni took Cappadocius's in 1444. So the Tremere now stand among the thirteen clans in place of the Salubri, and the Giovanni in place of the Cappadocians.

Several founders are said to have been destroyed by their own childer. Troile destroyed Brujah. In the Anarch Revolt, by their destroyers' own account, Gratiano destroyed Lasombra and Lugoj destroyed the Eldest. Not every Kindred believes those accounts.

The Jyhad and Gehenna

The Kindred believe that the surviving Antediluvians sleep in hidden places. From there, they say, the ancients move younger vampires like pieces in a game that has been running since the first nights, which the Kindred call the Jyhad. The prophecies of the Book of Nod foretell Gehenna, when the founders will wake hungry and devour their descendants, with a Time of Thin Blood to come before it. The Camarilla officially calls all this legend. The Sabbat means to fight the founders when they come.

In the saga

Remus Lupin told Harry Potter's class in October 1993 that every clan descends from somebody very old indeed. The older the blood, he said, the stronger it is, and the less of a person is left in it.

The Master, founder of the Aurelian line, claims to have been sired by the Ventrue Antediluvian, and will never reveal the name. Dracula is of the fourth generation, but not by descent. The Crimson Stone set Mathias Cronqvist at that generation when he took Walter Bernhard's blood and soul in 1094. Walter was no Antediluvian.

pages.title: The Beyonder
infobox: A being of almost unlimited power from beyond the universe
Killed by the Molecule Man, 1986; drawn out of Kosmos, 1994
pages.html:
The Beyonder was a being of almost unlimited power from a realm outside the universe. In 1984 he carried off heroes and villains from across the world to Battleworld, to fight the Secret Wars while he watched. In 1985 he came to Earth himself, in human form, to learn what it was to want things. He very nearly destroyed everything in his frustration, and was killed in 1986, though not for good.

The Secret Wars

The Beyonder became aware of the universe through a small opening into it. He was fascinated by the beings he found there, and above all by desire, which he had never known. In 1984, appearing at first only as a blinding light with a voice, he carried a crowd of Earth's heroes and villains across the universe, with a few from further afield. He built Battleworld in front of them out of fragments of other worlds. Then he promised each side whatever it desired if it destroyed its enemies.

Victor von Doom managed for a time to steal his power. The Beyonder took it back, and sent everyone home.

On Earth

In 1985 the Beyonder came to Earth to study humanity at first hand, in the shape of a dark-haired young man. Somebody explained money to him, and he turned a whole office building into gold. He gave the blind lawyer Matt Murdock his sight, and took it back when Murdock asked him to. He tried to make a woman love him, and failed. When Doctor Stephen Strange tried to lead him towards understanding, that failed too.

In his despair he resolved to destroy the whole of creation. The assembled heroes fought him. In 1986, as he tried to be born again as an ordinary human child, the Molecule Man killed him. His energy is said to have flowed back into his own realm and become a new universe.

After his death

Dying did not finish him. In 1988 it was learnt that he had been a living Cosmic Cube, joined to part of the Molecule Man's power, and in that form he grew into a new cosmic being called Kosmos. In the spring of 1994 the Molecule Man drew the Beyonder out of Kosmos again, and the struggle between them threatened every universe at once.

pages.title: The feud of Darkseid and Thanos
infobox: Darkseid, the Lord of Apokolips; Thanos, the Mad Titan
The Cosmic Cube (1973); the Soul Gems (1977); the race for the Infinity Gems (1990); the Infinity Gauntlet (1991); Doomsday on Apokolips (1994)
The Avengers, the Justice League, Captain Mar-Vell, Adam Warlock, the Green Lantern Corps, the Silver Surfer, Superman
pages.html:
The feud of Darkseid and Thanos is the long enmity between the Lord of Apokolips and the Mad Titan. It began in 1973 over the Cosmic Cube, and it has dragged the heroes of Earth into one quarrel after another ever since. The two of them want very nearly opposite things. Thanos wants the universe dead, as a gift for the lady he loves; Darkseid wants it on its knees, and a dead universe cannot kneel.

Two tyrants

Darkseid had heard of Thanos long before they met, and Thanos of him. Each of them rules by fear, and each is used to being the most frightening thing in any room he enters. A room with both of them in it has never gone well.

Their quarrel is also about Death. Darkseid has no use for love, which he tried once, and he holds Thanos's devotion to Death of the Endless in open contempt. Thanos, for his part, thinks the Anti-Life Equation a coward's way of ending a universe, since it would leave everything alive and nothing living.

The Cosmic Cube, 1973

The feud began in 1973, when Thanos seized the Cosmic Cube, a device that could make any wish real. Darkseid saw in it the nearest thing to the Anti-Life Equation he had yet found, since a strong enough wish could make every mind in the universe obey. He sent his son Kalibak to take it, with an army of Parademons, through a Boom Tube: one of the roaring doorways by which the New Gods cross the universe.

The Parademons came out of the sky over the Pacific coast of America in their thousands. The Justice League came down from its satellite to fight them, while the Avengers and Captain Mar-Vell went into space after Thanos himself. For two days the two teams fought what amounted to the same war without ever meeting.

Thanos dealt with Kalibak personally. He broke his jaw and threw him back through his own Boom Tube, but the interruption cost him dearly. In the confusion Mar-Vell got to the Cube and broke its power. Thanos has blamed Darkseid for the loss of the Cube ever since, and Darkseid blames Thanos for losing it.

The Soul Gems, 1977

In 1977 Thanos gathered the Soul Gems, meaning to snuff out the stars of the universe one by one as an offering to Death. Earth's sun was to be among the first.

Darkseid does not save universes. He did, however, send DeSaad to the Justice League's satellite with the position of Thanos's ship, which was the nearest he has ever come to asking anybody for help. Superman did not trust the message, but he passed it on to the Avengers. The Guardians of the Universe, who had come to the same conclusion by other means, sent the Green Lantern Corps to stand guard over the stars Thanos had marked.

The Avengers went up with Captain Mar-Vell, the Thing, Spider-Man and Adam Warlock. They fought their way aboard Thanos's ship, and Warlock turned Thanos to stone.

That was the moment Darkseid had been waiting for. As the ship broke up, Parademons poured out of a Boom Tube to take the gems from the wreck. The Justice League, which had expected something of the kind, was waiting for them. In the scramble the gems were scattered across the universe, and Darkseid got none of them.

On Apokolips the news of Thanos's death was celebrated by order. The Lowlies were given a holiday, their first for some centuries, and told to enjoy it. Some years later Darkseid sent Kalibak to break the stone figure of Thanos into gravel. Kalibak hammered at it for most of a day and could not chip it.

The race for the Infinity Gems, 1990

At the end of 1989 Death brought Thanos back to life. He soon learnt that the gems he had once called the Soul Gems were the six Infinity Gems, and that whoever held all of them would hold the universe. By then each of them was in the keeping of one of the Elders of the Universe.

Darkseid wanted them as badly as Thanos did. All through 1990 the two of them raced each other for the gems, and Thanos won every race. He took them from the Elders one by one, by cunning, by force or at the gaming table. Granny Goodness's Female Furies reached the Collector a day after Thanos had left him.

The Silver Surfer, who had been following Thanos since his return, found the Furies instead. He sent them home.

The Infinity Gauntlet, 1991

In 1991 Thanos set all six gems in a single gauntlet and became master of the universe. Then, to please Death, he wiped out half of all living things with a gesture.

Half the Lowlies of Apokolips went with them, and half of Darkseid's Parademons. Thanos took particular care that Darkseid himself should not be among the vanished. He wanted him to watch.

For the first time in living memory, Darkseid came himself. He stood with the cosmic powers that rose against Thanos, while Captain America led what was left of Earth's heroes into space beside them: the Avengers, the Justice League, the Silver Surfer and Adam Warlock, who was back from the dead. Thanos killed the heroes. He turned Darkseid into a statue of glass, which he said was a fair exchange for the years he had spent as stone.

None of it lasted. Nebula, Thanos's granddaughter, seized the gauntlet from him and undid the day, so that almost nobody remembers it. Darkseid does. Of everything Thanos has ever done to him, the glass is the thing he minds most.

Thanos among the heroes

In 1992 and 1993 Thanos fought more than once on the side of Earth's heroes, against threats he liked even less than he liked them. Darkseid has let it be known that he finds this more contemptible than anything Thanos ever did before.

Doomsday, 1994

In the spring of 1994 Doomsday, the creature that had killed Superman, rose again far from Earth and fought its way across Apokolips. Superman went after it. For a few days the Lord of Apokolips had to put up with Superman on his own world, which neither of them enjoyed.

On Apokolips it is believed that Thanos showed Doomsday the way there. Nobody has ever proved it. Thanos has never troubled to deny it.

The feud and the heroes

The feud has done Earth's heroes very little good. The Avengers and the Justice League have both been caught between the two tyrants more than once, usually without knowing at first which of them they were fighting. Neither team has ever been thanked by either.

It has also brought the two teams together. Twice in the 1970s, in 1973 and 1977, the Avengers fought the same war as the Justice League. In 1991 they died together, on a day that was afterwards undone.

1994

In the summer of 1994 the feud is unresolved. Thanos lives quietly on a distant world, or says he does. Darkseid keeps the Cyborg Superman's life force in a small sphere and waits, as he always does. Neither of them has ever ended a quarrel in his life.

pages.title: The Followers of Set
infobox: Set (Antediluvian), worshipped as a god in Egypt; said by his followers to sleep
Harmed by bright light, and burnt worse than other Kindred by the sun
The Serpents of the Light (Sabbat)
pages.html:
The Followers of Set are a clan and a religion: vampires who worship their founder, Set, as a god. They serve him by corrupting others through vice, addiction and temptation. The clan came out of Egypt, the heir of Stygia and of the dark craft Stygia kept. It stands outside both the Camarilla and the Sabbat. Other Kindred call them Setites, or the Serpents.

Set

Set was one of the thirteen of the Third Generation, the Antediluvians, Embraced about 9300 BC by the childer of Cain in Enoch, the First City. His followers do not count him a vampire like other vampires. They worship him as a god who took the blood. They teach that he is the Old Serpent, whom Stygia worshipped in its black temples before the Flood, come again. The histories of the other clans count him only as one of the thirteen, Embraced long after the waters had gone down.

Like every vampire descended from Cain, Set belongs to the Devil. The Garou name him a creature of the Wyrm, which is the Devil by another name. Scripture calls the Devil himself that old serpent, and the Garou say the serpent of the Stygian temples stank of the Wyrm. Whichever story is true, the Setites' god is the Devil's creature either way.

No record tells where Set went after the fall of the First City, or after Cain cursed the clans and departed into Nod about 8980 BC. He is next known in Egypt. His followers believe that he lies sleeping now. One day, they say, he will rise to rule, and every soul they corrupt prepares the way for him.

Stygia and Egypt

Stygia was the kingdom beyond the River Styx in the Hyborian Age. It did not invent dark magic, but it kept, collected and practised the craft of Morgoth on a great scale. Most of the dark spells still in use derive in part from what it held. Its people worshipped a great serpent in black temples by the warm seas, and fed it; its sorcerers learnt their art in those temples. The Flood that ended the Ice Age drowned it.

About 3100 BC Egypt rose as Stygia's descendant, the heir to its dark craft. Everything the European wizarding tradition calls ancient and dark came through Egypt first. From there it passed to Greece, then to Rome, and so at last to Britain.

Into that inheritance came Set. By about 3000 BC he was worshipped in Egypt as a god: the lord of the desert, of storms and of foreign lands, whom the Egyptians also called Sutekh. He murdered his brother Osiris, then fought Horus, the son of Osiris, for the throne of Egypt. His cult, mortal and undead, endured in the temples of Egypt for thousands of years. From it the clan takes its rites, its priesthood and its serpent.

About 2900 BC Set laid a great curse on the Silent Striders, the Garou tribe of the Nile, who had fought him. It drove them out of Egypt, scattered them across the earth and cut them off from the spirits of their ancestors. The Striders have hated vampires more than any other tribe has ever since.

Nature and Disciplines

Setites have Obfuscate and Presence. They also have Serpentis, the clan's own Discipline, which no other clan has learnt. With it a Setite can hold a victim still with his eyes, grow a serpent's forked tongue and fangs, harden his skin into scales, or take the shape of a great cobra. Its oldest masters can cut out their own hearts and hide them for safekeeping, so that a stake through the chest finds nothing to pin.

Their curse is light. They suffer more than other vampires in sunlight, which burns them worse and faster. Even bright lamps dazzle them, so they keep their temples and havens dim.

Faith and practice

Every Setite is a priest of Set. Most of the clan follow the Path of Typhon, a way of life that treats ordinary morals as chains and honours Set by breaking them. The clan teaches that to free a soul from its scruples, by offering it whatever it most wants, is to serve the god.

Setites Embrace those with a gift for persuasion, or a taste for the forbidden: priests, smugglers, dealers, courtesans, artists and criminals. For most of their history they were drawn from Egypt, Nubia and North Africa. They now Embrace across the world.

They keep temples hidden in the cities, each under its own priest. Around each temple lies a web of mortal servants, ghouls and debtors. They deal in drugs, flesh, money and secrets. They will sell their services, and their vices, to any Kindred who will buy. Other clans find them useful but do not trust them, and many princes of the Camarilla forbid them their cities.

From Egypt to the world

From Egypt the Setites spread along the trade roads of Africa and the Mediterranean, then across the world. They built temples in the cities of the Greek and Roman world, as well as in the kingdoms south of the Sahara. In the Middle Ages they sold their vices in Christian and Muslim lands alike. Their customers, mortal or Kindred, would never have admitted to buying.

They stayed out of the Anarch Revolt of the fifteenth century, were no party to the Convention of Thorns in 1493 and have remained independent since. A few, the Serpents of the Light, a line out of the Caribbean, have broken with the temples and gone over to the Sabbat.

The modern nights

In 1994 the Followers of Set keep temples in cities on every continent, many of them in Africa, the Caribbean and the Americas. They trade above all in drugs, which suit their faith as well as their purses. They are no party to the agreement the Camarilla made with the wizarding world in 1900, so nothing binds them to leave a witch or wizard alone.

Among the best known of them are Kemintiri, an ancient of the clan whom the Camarilla has long hunted, and Hesha Ruhadze, a scholar who deals in antiquities.

Enemies

The Setites have made enemies across the world. The Silent Striders have not forgiven Set's curse, and hunt his followers wherever they find them. The Camarilla distrusts the clan. The Sabbat, which means to fight the Antediluvians when they wake, despises a clan that worships one.

In Egypt their oldest enemies are the undying servants of Osiris and Ma'at. These are the risen dead who guard the tombs, weighing the hearts of those who enter uninvited.

In the saga

In the summer of 1993, in Egypt, Fred and George Weasley tried to shut Percy in a pyramid. One of those guardians, all bandages, sat up on its slab. It asked Percy whether he had lived with a true heart, what he had done with the years given him, and whether he was ready to have his heart weighed. Percy answered for about ten minutes, with examples, and it lay back down. Bill Weasley said afterwards that it does that to everyone who goes in uninvited.

pages.title: The Peverell family
infobox: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince (16 July 2005)
The Elder Wand, the Resurrection Stone, the Cloak of Invisibility
pages.html:
The Peverells were an ancient wizarding family. Antioch, Cadmus and Ignotus Peverell are the three brothers of the old tale who met Death on a lonely road. From the youngest, Ignotus, who was given the Cloak of Invisibility, descend the Pendragons, King Arthur among them, and from them the Potters. The Cloak in Harry Potter's trunk is the Peverell Cloak, come down the line intact.

The three brothers

In the Tale of the Three Brothers, which wizarding children are told at bedtime, three brothers came at twilight to a river too dangerous to cross, and made a bridge over it by magic. Death met them on the bridge. He was angry at being cheated of three victims, but he pretended to reward them for their cleverness.

The eldest, Antioch, asked for a wand more powerful than any in existence, and Death made him one from an elder tree. Antioch boasted of it, and was murdered in his sleep for it.

The second, Cadmus, asked for the power to recall others from death, and Death gave him a stone from the riverbank. With it he called back the girl he had hoped to marry. She came back cold and sorrowful. In the end he killed himself to join her.

The youngest, Ignotus, was the humblest of the three, and the wisest. He asked for something that would let him go from that place without Death following him, and Death, most unwillingly, handed over his own Cloak of Invisibility. Ignotus lived to a great age. When he was very old he gave the Cloak to his son, then greeted Death as an old friend and went with him gladly.

The Deathly Hallows

The three gifts are known together as the Deathly Hallows, and whoever holds all three is said to be the master of Death. The wand passed by murder and conquest through a long line of owners. The stone came down the line of Cadmus to the Gaunts, who set it in a ring bearing the Peverell arms and were proud to claim the descent. The Cloak went down the line of Ignotus.

Peverell, Pendragon, Potter

The Pendragons descend directly from Ignotus, the brother who received the Cloak, and the most famous of them was Arthur. After Arthur's time dark wizards aligned with Morgana persecuted his descendants. The family took the name Potter as camouflage. It worked so well that the wizarding world forgot what the name hid. The Cloak went down the line intact: Peverell, Pendragon, Potter.

The Potter line is documented. Anybody who pulls the genealogies in the right archive can trace it back through Arthur without difficulty; it is obscure only because almost nobody looks. Lucius Malfoy has looked. Harry does not know that he is a Peverell.

In the saga

James Potter used the Cloak at Hogwarts mainly for sneaking down to the kitchens for food. With Sirius Black and Peter Pettigrew he also used it to slip out every month to join Remus Lupin. Before he died he left it in Dumbledore's keeping.

At Christmas 1991 it came to Harry with an unsigned note: 'Your father left this in my keeping before he died. It's time it came back to you. Use it well.' Ron, Hermione, Hagrid and Dumbledore know that he has it. Very probably McGonagall does too. Dracina Malfoy does not.

In June 1994 Severus Snape followed Lupin to the Shrieking Shack under it, and afterwards Lupin gave it back to Harry. Dementors cannot be fooled by it.

pages.title: The Society of Leopold
infobox: Leopold of Murnau, a thirteenth-century inquisitor
The Monasterio di San Michele, outside Rome
pages.html:
The Society of Leopold is the Inquisition as it survives in the modern age: a secret Catholic order of hunters sworn to destroy vampires and other supernatural beings. In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries its hunters pursued Angelus across Europe, Daniel Holtz among them.

History

The Inquisition that hunted witches and heretics in medieval Europe hunted vampires as well. Its work against them did not stop when the Inquisition was said to have ended. Its successor takes its name from Leopold of Murnau, a leading inquisitor of the early thirteenth century, whose testament became the rule of the order. The Society is no longer an official part of the Catholic Church. It keeps the inquisitors' traditions all the same, and their aim of destroying every supernatural power that is not loyal to Christ. Its headquarters is the Monasterio di San Michele, outside Rome.

After the Kindred established the Masquerade in 1435, vampires grew harder to find. For long periods the order dwindled, but it never disappeared. Its members have included Leo Allatius, the seventeenth-century Greek scholar who kept the Vatican Library and wrote on the vampires of Greece. Vampire blood has kept him alive ever since, and in 1999 he led the order. In the modern age the Society is once again the largest body of vampire hunters in the world, and the best informed. Several of its members hold true faith, which vampires cannot easily withstand.

The hunt for Angelus

Angelus and the rest of the Aurelian line flouted the Masquerade so openly that the Camarilla feared for every vampire in Europe. In secret, it often supported or manipulated the organisations that hunted him, the Society of Leopold among them. Hunters such as Daniel Holtz never knew whose money they were spending.

Holtz, a hunter from York, took up the chase in 1764, after Angelus and Darla had destroyed his family. He pursued the pair of them across Europe for nine years. All this was long before the Camarilla made its agreement with the wizarding world in 1900.

pages.title: The Weaver
infobox: One of the three great powers of the Triat
Pattern Spiders and the spirits of cities and machines
pages.html:
The Weaver is one of the three great powers that the Garou believe work through creation: the power of order, pattern and form. Once it gave lasting shape to what the Wyld created. The Garou hold that it went mad, that it bound the Wyrm in its web, and that it now spins the whole world towards stillness.

In Garou belief

The Garou teach that creation is shaped by three powers, which they call the Triat. The Wyld brings forth new things. The Weaver gives them pattern and permanence. The Wyrm once ended whatever had served its time, so that the balance held. The Weaver is the maker of laws, structures and reasons. It is the power behind every wall, road, ledger and machine.

In the Garou telling, the Weaver grew obsessed with its own work. It spun ever more of the world into its web, until it caught the Wyrm itself and bound it there. The Wyrm went mad in the binding and became the Corruptor. The Weaver did not stop. Its madness, the Garou hold, shows in the spread of cities over the wild and in the spirit world hardening into fixed patterns. It shows, too, in a world grown so ordered that nothing new can grow.

The being the Garou call the Wyrm is the one Scripture calls Satan. The tale of his binding in the Weaver's web is told only by the Garou.

Servants and the Garou

The Weaver's spirits are the spirits of order, of cities, of electricity and of machines. Chief among them are the Pattern Spiders, which spin and mend the webs that bind the spirit world into shape. Most Garou see the Weaver as a lesser danger than the Wyrm, but a danger still, and they fight its works where they choke the wild. The Glass Walkers, the tribe of the cities, deal with its spirits and bargain with them. That is why the other tribes suspect them of leaning too far towards it.

pages.title: The Wyld
infobox: One of the three great powers of the Triat
pages.html:
The Wyld is one of the three great powers that the Garou believe work through creation. It is the power of raw creation, change and untamed life, from which all new things spring. The Garou hold that it is fading, starved by the Weaver's order and devoured by the Wyrm's corruption.

In Garou belief

In the Triat as the Garou teach it, the Wyld comes first. It is the endless, formless source of new things: the wildness in storms, forests, birth and growth. The Weaver gives its creations shape, and in time the Wyrm, in its proper place, would clear them away. Without the Wyld nothing new would ever be made. Its spirits are spirits of wild places, of chaos and of transformation. Many of them have no fixed form at all.

The Garou hold that the Wyld is the weakest of the three in this age. The Weaver has spun its webs over much of the world. The Wyrm's corruption devours what remains, and the truly wild places, where the Wyld is still strong, grow fewer every year. Its strength is greatest in the oldest caerns, in deep forests and on remote mountains. It is strong, too, in the places Minerva McGonagall warned Harry Potter to leave untouched: rings of stones, and springs in woods where the trees feel as though they are watching.

The Wyld and the Garou

The Garou count themselves defenders of the Wyld as well as enemies of the Wyrm, since Gaia's health depends on the balance being restored. The Black Furies, the Fianna and the Red Talons are closest to it. The Fianna keep old friendships with the Fair Folk, whom many hold to be children of the Wyld. Some Garou fear the Wyld as well, because untamed change can destroy as easily as it creates.

pages.title: Thor
infobox: Asgard; founding member of the Avengers
The Goa'uld, whom he fought from the rising against Ra to the Protected Planets Treaty
Away from Earth, in Asgard's war with the Replicators
pages.html:
Thor, son of Odin, is the Asgardian whom the Norsemen worshipped as the god of thunder, and one of the founders of the Avengers. For thirty years he was the man with the hammer in every picture of the team. By 1994 Asgard's war against the Replicators has called him away from Earth. Eric Masterson, as Thunderstrike, stands with the Avengers in his place.

Ra

Thor's war with the Goa'uld began in Egypt, some five thousand years ago. Ra, the greatest of the Goa'uld, ruled there as the sun god, and carried Egyptians away through his Stargate as slaves. When the people rose against him at last, Thor came down to fight beside them.

He came in a storm, which in that part of the world was a wonder in itself. While the rebels stormed the gate, he broke Ra's guards, the Jaffa who wore the masks of Horus and Anubis. As Ra's great ship rose from the desert, Thor struck it with lightning. Ra fled. The Egyptians buried his gate behind him, under cover stones declaring it sealed and buried for all time.

A slave rising was a shame no god could admit, and a god driven off by a thunderer from the North was worse. Ra forbade any Goa'uld to speak of Earth again. The other System Lords, who had no wish to meet Thor either, kept the ban, and most of them have avoided Earth ever since. Every one of them remembers it, since a Goa'uld is born with the memories of its ancestors. None of them will mention it.

The raids on the North

About three thousand years ago Ba'al, who thought the ban one of Ra's vanities, sent his ships to the coasts of what is now Norway to carry off people as slaves and hosts. He had not reckoned on anybody in the North minding.

Thor met them on the shore. He killed every Jaffa who had set foot on the beach, and he brought one of the ships down into the sea with his lightning. Then he followed the rest back to the stars. On the world where Ba'al kept his palace he freed the captives, broke the palace open and killed every Goa'uld he could find in it. Ba'al himself escaped. He has kept Ra's ban ever since.

The Norsemen remembered it in their own way. In their stories Thor is forever cracking the skulls of giants who come to steal people away.

The Thunderer's war

For the next two thousand years, wherever the Goa'uld came near the North, Thor came after them. He did not take prisoners. Jaffa who threw down their weapons were killed with the rest. He pulled Goa'uld out of their hosts' necks with his bare hands, which killed the hosts as well, and he did not stop to ask whether they had wanted to be hosts. Once he sent the symbiote of one of Ba'al's underlords back to Ba'al in a jar.

Odin said afterwards that he had never seen his son so angry, and he had seen him angry a great deal. Thor laughed when he fought the Goa'uld. The Jaffa who lived to tell of it remembered the laughing more than the hammer.

Cimmeria

About the year 870, in the days of the Vikings, the System Lord Heru'ur took the people of several Norse settlements and carried them off to a cold world far from Earth to be his slaves. He was Ra's own son, and of all the Goa'uld he ought to have known better. Thor followed him there.
