What he did on that world the Jaffa still tell their recruits, to frighten them. He came down in a storm that lasted three days. He killed Heru'ur's First Prime in front of his army, and then the army. He tore Heru'ur's ship out of the sky, and broke it on the mountains. Heru'ur got away in a cargo ship with a handful of guards, and left everyone else behind.

Thor did not bring the Northmen home. He judged it safer to leave them where they were, under his own protection, than to show the Goa'uld the way back to Earth. Their new home is the world now called Cimmeria. Thor left a device there, known as Thor's Hammer, which seizes any Goa'uld who comes through the gate and shuts it in the labyrinth under the mountain.

The war with the System Lords

Heru'ur went to the other System Lords. Towards the end of the tenth century they did a thing they have seldom done before or since: they made common cause. Apophis, Heru'ur and Ba'al brought their fleets together to strike at the worlds of Asgard, reasoning that Thor could not be everywhere at once.

Odin gave Thor command of Asgard's ships. He met the three fleets above a dead world on the edge of Goa'uld space, which the Jaffa still will not name. Of the three, only Apophis's fleet survived, and that only because Apophis turned it round before the end. Thor went down after the survivors of the others and finished them on the ground. It is still the worst defeat the Goa'uld have ever suffered.

The treaty

Soon afterwards the System Lords asked Asgard for terms, and the result was the Protected Planets Treaty. It closed a list of worlds to the Goa'uld, Cimmeria among them, with Asgard to enforce it. It is said in Asgard, and denied by the System Lords, that their first demand was that Thor should not be present when it was signed.

Earth was not on the list. The Goa'uld had been forbidden to speak of it for four thousand years, and a world that may not be named cannot very well be written into a treaty. Besides, it was the one world in the galaxy where they could be surest of finding Thor. In 1994, with Thor away at the Replicator war, that is less true than it was.

The fear of Thor

The System Lords fear Asgard as a power. They fear Thor as a person. Because every Goa'uld is born remembering what its ancestors saw, every Goa'uld alive remembers him, including those who have never met him. A System Lord who hears thunder in a clear sky over a world he means to take has been known to turn his fleet round.

Odin was not pleased with his son. It was not the killing of Goa'uld that troubled him, but the pleasure Thor had taken in it. Many in Asgard count it among the reasons why, centuries later, Odin sent Thor to Earth as Donald Blake to learn humility.

On Earth

Thor is the son of Odin All-Father, the ruler of Asgard. The Norse knew him long before the modern world did, and the old tales of Thor the thunderer are memories of him. To teach his proud son humility, Odin sent him to Earth in the body of a lame American doctor, Donald Blake, with no memory of who he was.

In 1962, on holiday in Norway, Blake took shelter in a cave and found an old walking stick there. When he struck it on the ground it became Mjolnir, the hammer forged of the metal uru. It bears the promise that whoever holds it, if he be worthy, shall have the power of Thor. Blake became Thor.

He came to public notice that summer. The following year he helped to found the Avengers, when his adopted brother Loki tried to use the team's first battle against him. With Mjolnir he commands storm and lightning. He can fly with it, and open ways between the worlds.

He fought beside the Avengers for most of the next quarter of a century, against Loki, the Enchantress, the fire demon Surtur and a great many others. In 1984 he was among the heroes taken to Battleworld in the Secret Wars. That summer, back in New York, he was one of the heroes who fought the maddened Hulk through the streets.

Absence

From 1989 Thor's life was bound up with that of Eric Masterson, a New York architect whose life he had saved by merging with him. When Odin banished Thor himself at the end of 1991, Masterson served as Thor in his own right for more than a year. When Thor came back at the end of 1992, Odin gave Masterson an enchanted mace of his own.

Since then Thor has been away from Earth. Asgard is at war with the Replicators, machines that devour technology to make more of themselves, and Thor is the supreme commander of Asgard's fleet in that war. It is the same fleet that stands behind Asgard's Protected Planets Treaty with the Goa'uld System Lords. The war is a heavy drain on it.

The Goa'uld do not know about the war. Asgard has kept it from them, and keeps its ships on show over the protected worlds as though nothing had changed. The System Lords have heard rumours that Thor is busy somewhere. They do not know where, or with what. In 1997 Apophis gambled on the rumours and came to Earth.

In 1999 he opened the talks that put Earth under the Protected Planets Treaty, before he was called away. In 2002 Anubis, half-ascended through the Devil's trick, took Thor prisoner over Adara II and tried to read his mind. Thor turned the link against him, and SG-1 got him out. No other Goa'uld has ever laid hands on him.

In the saga

Book Four, Chapter Three: watching the Avengers at the United Nations on the news of 20 August 1994, Harry notices that they look nothing like the Avengers on Dudley's old lunchbox. The man with the hammer has been replaced by a big blond man with a mace.

pages.title: Uktena
infobox: North America, and the Americas beyond
The native peoples of the Americas
Mysticism, secret lore and the binding of evil spirits
pages.html:
The Uktena are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou, and one of the Pure Ones, the tribes native to the Americas. They are mystics and keepers of secrets. They guard the evil spirits bound beneath the land, and they seek out hidden knowledge that other Garou would rather leave alone.

Totem and ways

The tribe follows Uktena, the great horned serpent of the waters and the underworld. It is a spirit of secrets, magic and patience. The Uktena know more than any other Garou about the lore of spirits and the binding of them. Their great duty is the watch over places where Wyrm spirits were bound in ancient times, beneath mountains, lakes and mounds, so that those spirits never wake.

The Uktena believe that a weapon is best understood before it is used. They gather knowledge of every kind, dark lore and the secrets of the Wyrm among it. The habit gives them power, and it makes them suspect.

Homelands

Their homelands are the forests, deserts, rivers and mountains of North America. Their Kinfolk are the native peoples of the continent. Over the centuries they have taken in Kinfolk from many other native peoples of the Americas. In later times they have also taken in Kinfolk from other peoples who have lost their own lands. With the Wendigo they are the Pure Ones, the tribes that were in the Americas before the European Garou came.

Place in the world

European settlers brought their own Garou with them, whom the Pure Ones call Wyrmcomers. Their coming cost the Uktena many caerns and many lives. The old grievance has not healed. Other tribes value the Uktena's knowledge and fear what they keep hidden. Some whisper that the tribe has studied the Wyrm so closely that it has been touched by it.

pages.title: Vampirism
pages.html:
Vampirism began with the curse God laid on Cain for the murder of his brother Abel. That curse left Cain deathless and soulless, but he was not yet a vampire. After the Flood, the blood magic Lilith taught him turned him into the first of them, and with it he passed his curse on. Every vampire descends from him. A vampire's soul is destroyed when it is sired, and the Beast fills the place where the soul was.

Origin

God's sentence on Cain had three parts. He would not die. The sun would repel him and burn him. He would wander for ever, without rest or home. Beneath all three it meant soullessness, which was the real sentence. It gave him no powers at all.

In that state he wandered through the ages of Middle-earth and the Hyborian Age. The Flood did not take him, since God does not revoke His own sentences: he could not drown.

After the Flood, Lilith came to him. She called herself Adam's first wife, which was a lie; she was in truth a servant of Morgoth. She led him into blood magic, and the magic turned him into the first vampire, of the First Generation. With it he sired others like himself. The bargain put Cain, and every vampire after him, under Morgoth's will.

Cain's three childer, Enoch, Irad and Zillah, were the Second Generation. They sired the thirteen Antediluvians of the Third, the founders of the clans, in Enoch, the First City. The older the blood, the stronger it is, and the less of a person is left in it.

Nature

A vampire is sired through the Embrace. Its sire drains a mortal of blood, then gives back a little of its own. The childe must drink blood to go on existing, and human blood is what it craves. Its blood carries powers called Disciplines, which differ from clan to clan.

A mortal who drinks a vampire's blood three times is bound to love it for life; this is the blood bond. A mortal kept on lesser draughts becomes a ghoul. A vampire that drinks another to the last drop, soul and all, takes its generation. The Kindred call this diablerie, and count it among their worst crimes.

Fire and sunlight destroy every vampire, though the very oldest can bear the sun for a few seconds. A stake through the heart paralyses a vampire rather than killing it. Garlic is mostly folklore. Running water and mirrors trouble some lines, but not others. No vampire may enter a home uninvited. A cross held by somebody who believes in Jesus Christ repels them, because the curse was God's and the sign is His.

Society

Vampires call themselves the Kindred, or Cainites. Since 1435 they have hidden from mortals under the Masquerade. Most clans belong to the Camarilla, or say they do. The Sabbat rejects it, and the Anarchs reject their elders. The Assamites, the Followers of Set, the Giovanni and the Ravnos stand apart from both sects. The clanless are called Caitiff. Dracula answers to nobody. Neither does the Aurelian line of the Master and Angelus.

In 1900 the wizarding governments of the world lent the Camarilla their concealment charms, in return for a promise that no Camarilla vampire would ever harm or feed on a witch or wizard.

Children of the blood

Vampires cannot give life. Only the thin-blooded of the last generations, the fifteenth and after, the furthest from Cain, keep enough of the living body to father or bear a child. Their children are dhampirs: mortal at the last, but born with something of the vampire in them. The Kindred count those births among the signs of the Time of Thin Blood before Gehenna.

There are exceptions. Alucard, the son of Dracula, is a dhampir through the Crimson Stone. Blade is one because the vampire Deacon Frost fed on his mother while she was in labour. Connor, the son of Angel and Darla, was something else again. He was the one human child ever born to vampires, and a direct act of God.

In the saga

Hermione Granger took up vampires in September 1992 with Voyages with Vampires. In October 1993 Remus Lupin taught Harry Potter's class about the Masquerade, the sects, the clans, the Beast and the blood bond. He taught them a Fire-Making Charm, and a charm for a brief patch of sunlight. Then he made them repeat three times, 'Never ask one in.' He had never met a vampire, he said, that he would turn his back on.

pages.title: Vukodlak
infobox: A faction of the Sabbat; the Assamite assassin called Pink; smugglers of the Followers of Set
By the elders of the Tzimisce, in the 1140s
1999, in the Cathedral of Flesh in New York, by Christof Romuald
pages.html:
Vukodlak is a Methuselah of the Tzimisce, a voivode of the old Carpathian lords, who meant to rise above the Antediluvians themselves and make himself the equal of the clans' ancestors. Since the twelfth century he has slept beneath the castle of Vyšehrad above Prague, bound there by his own clan. His followers carried him to New York in 1999. He woke there in the Cathedral of Flesh, and Christof Romuald destroyed him.

The voivode

Vukodlak is among the oldest and most powerful of the Tzimisce, a voivode of the clan's old lords in the East. He is a master of Vicissitude, the clan's art of shaping flesh and bone. He took his name from the old Slavic word for a creature that is half wolf and half the walking dead.

His ambition is the greatest any Methuselah of his age is known to have held. He means to rise above the Antediluvians, the thirteen of the Third Generation from whom every clan descends, and to make himself their equal or their master.

Vyšehrad and Anezka

By the 1140s he lay asleep beneath Vyšehrad, the Tzimisce castle above Prague. In the war between the Tremere and the Tzimisce, his servants took a young nun, Anezka, to be his ghoul. When the crusader-turned-Brujah Christof Romuald came to Vyšehrad for her, she went to wake her master instead. Before she could, mortal forces stormed the castle and brought it down on them all, burying Christof in torpor.

The elders of Vukodlak's own clan feared him as much as anybody did. When the castle fell, they bound him in a sleep from which he was never meant to wake.

The long sleep

He slept for more than eight hundred years, and in all that time his followers never gave him up. Anezka stayed at his side as his ghoul, living on his blood. In secret, though, she worked against his waking, and undid what she could of their work.

By the end of the twentieth century a whole faction of the Sabbat served him. His followers took Vyšehrad back, and the Followers of Set smuggled the treasures of the castle to New York. An Assamite assassin called Pink, posing as a Brujah, worked for him. The Society of Leopold wanted him too. Its leader, Leo Allatius, meant to take Vukodlak's blood and use it to destroy every vampire in the world.

The Cathedral of Flesh

In 1999 his followers carried him to New York, where they hid him beneath the Cathedral of Flesh, a temple of shaped and living flesh. There he woke. Christof Romuald, woken himself in London that year, came looking for Anezka. Vukodlak offered her to him, since she now lived only by the Methuselah's blood, if Christof would serve him. Christof refused, and Vukodlak flung him into the tunnels beneath the Cathedral.

Christof came back up, and in the Cathedral of Flesh he destroyed Vukodlak. With the Methuselah gone, Christof Embraced Anezka so that she would not die.

pages.title: Wally West
infobox: The Flash; Kid Flash; Wallace West
pages.html:
Wally West is the third Flash. As a boy he ran beside Barry Allen as Kid Flash from 1959. After Barry died in the Crisis of 1985, Wally took up his name, his costume and his city. In August 1994, a man of about forty-five, he stood behind Superman at the United Nations Security Council.

Kid Flash

Wally West grew up in Blue Valley, Nebraska. In 1959, when he was about ten, he was visiting the laboratory of Barry Allen, who was courting his aunt Iris. Lightning struck the same rack of chemicals that had given Barry his speed, and it gave the same speed to Wally.

He became Kid Flash, Barry's partner, in a smaller copy of the red suit. Later he wore a yellow and red costume of his own.

In 1964 he was one of the founders of the Teen Titans, with Robin (Dick Grayson) and Aqualad. He grew up as a hero, working his way through his years in the Titans and through his own doubts. He was never far from his uncle.

The Flash

After Barry Allen's death in 1985 Wally West put on his uncle's costume and became the Flash. For some years he was markedly slower than Barry had been, and he had to learn the work of the name for himself. By the early 1990s he had grown faster than ever.

He has served with the Justice League in its various forms since the late 1980s, including its European branch. In 1994 he is one of its core members under Superman.

He is the first Flash to have grown up in the job, and his public career is now longer than his predecessor's. Unlike Barry, he has never hidden much about himself.

In the saga

In the spring of 1994 Harry Potter remembered seeing a man in a red suit on the news from America, so fast that the cameras caught only a streak of light.

On 20 August 1994 the Flash stood with the League behind Superman at the United Nations, in red with a lightning flash on his chest. He was not the Flash of Dudley's annuals but the boy who used to run beside him, grown into a man of forty-five or so.

pages.title: The Watchers' Council
infobox: Buffy the Vampire Slayer, 'Welcome to the Hellmouth' (10 March 1997)
Finding, training and guiding the Slayer
The men who made the first Slayer after the Flood
pages.html:
The Watchers' Council is an old society of Muggle scholars and occultists, based in London. It finds, trains and guides the Slayer. It knows of the wizarding world and deals with it when it must. Like everything else it knows, it keeps that secret from the world at large. Witches and wizards who know of the Council at all look down on its members as pretenders: Muggles dabbling with dark forces they do not understand.

Origins

The Council descends from the men who made the first Slayer in the ages after the Flood, whom it remembers as the Shadow Men. It has kept watch over the line of Slayers ever since.

Each Slayer is given a Watcher, who finds her when she is called, trains her, advises her and records her deeds. The Council's library of the dark is among the greatest in the world, and it keeps its own counsel about what is in it.

Muggles and magic

Every member of the Council is a Muggle. What its members know of magic is occultism: learned, ritual and borrowed. It is the craft of men and women who have studied the darkness for centuries without being born to wield it, which makes it dangerous in their hands.

Some Watchers have meddled with it in their youth and paid for it. As a young man in London, Rupert Giles raised a demon called Eyghon with his friends, for their own amusement. Years afterwards it came back for them.

The Council and the wizarding world

The Council knows that the wizarding world exists. It deals with witches and wizards when it must. It keeps that knowledge as close as it keeps everything else, so that the general population knows nothing of either.

Witches and wizards think little of it. Those who have heard of the Council see Muggles playing with dark forces they do not understand, pretenders to a gift they were not born with. A great many wizards do not know it exists at all.

In the 1990s

In the 1990s the Council was led by Quentin Travers. In 1996 its Watcher Merrick found the newly called Slayer, Buffy Summers, in Los Angeles.

After Merrick's death her Watcher was Rupert Giles. From 1997 he kept watch over her in Sunnydale, California, as the librarian of her school.

Later years

The Council has an old test, the Cruciamentum, which every Slayer who reaches her eighteenth birthday must face without her powers. Buffy faced it in January 1999. Giles was dismissed for trying to protect her, and in the spring of that year Buffy broke with the Council altogether.

In the autumn of 2002 the Council's headquarters in London was blown up, and Quentin Travers died with most of the Watchers inside it.

pages.title: Wendigo
infobox: Wendigo, the spirit of the cold north wind
Canada, Alaska and the far north of America
The native peoples of the north
Ferocity, endurance and distrust of the European tribes
pages.html:
The Wendigo are one of the thirteen tribes of the Garou, and one of the Pure Ones native to the Americas. They are hard warriors of the northern forests and the frozen north. They have never forgiven the European Garou who came with the settlers.

Totem and ways

The tribe takes its name from its totem, Wendigo, the spirit of the cold north wind, of winter and of hunger. To its enemies it is a terrible spirit. The Wendigo are hunters and warriors, used to hardship. The long winters of the north are nothing to them. Keeping to the old ways of their Kinfolk, they guard the forests and lakes of the north. Wherever the Wyrm reaches into their lands, in mines, pipelines or poisoned rivers, they fight it.

Homelands

Their lands are the far north of America, from Alaska across Canada to the northern reaches of the United States, forest and tundra alike. Their Kinfolk are the native peoples of those lands. With the Uktena they are the Pure Ones, the tribes that were in the Americas before the European Garou came.

Place in the world

When Europeans crossed the Atlantic, their Garou came with them, seized caerns and made war on the native tribes. The Pure Ones call those Garou Wyrmcomers, and the Wendigo have neither forgotten nor forgiven. They work with the other tribes when the Wyrm leaves them no choice, but they trust few outsiders. They see what has befallen their Kinfolk as part of the same war.

pages.title: X-Men
infobox: Xavier's School for Gifted Youngsters, Salem Center, Westchester County, New York
Cyclops, Marvel Girl, the Beast, the Angel, Iceman
pages.html:
The X-Men are a team of mutants, founded in 1963 by the telepath Professor Charles Xavier and trained at his school in New York State. They use their powers to protect a world that fears and hates them. They first came to public notice fighting Magneto. They have been fighting him ever since, along with the Sentinels and the suspicion of ordinary people, the last of which has proved the hardest to beat.

The first X-Men

Xavier opened his School for Gifted Youngsters in the family mansion in Westchester County, as a cover for training young mutants. His first five pupils, all teenagers in 1963, were Scott Summers (Cyclops), Jean Grey (Marvel Girl), Hank McCoy (the Beast), Warren Worthington (the Angel) and Bobby Drake (Iceman). Their first public battle came that same year, against Magneto at the missile base at Cape Citadel. In 1965 they faced the Sentinels, the giant robots Dr Bolivar Trask had unveiled on live television that year.

The new X-Men

In 1975 the original team was captured on Krakoa, an island that turned out to be alive. Xavier gathered a new team from all over the world to rescue them, among them Storm, Colossus, Nightcrawler and the Canadian Wolverine. Most of the originals left afterwards, and the new X-Men became the most famous mutants in the world.

In 1977 the X-Men fought the Shi'ar Imperial Guard beside the Starjammers at the M'Kraan Crystal, where the Phoenix saved the universe.

In 1980 the cosmic force called the Phoenix, wearing Jean Grey's form, destroyed a star and then died on the Moon. In 1984 the X-Men were among the heroes carried off to Battleworld in the Secret Wars. In 1986 the real Jean Grey was found alive, cocooned at the bottom of Jamaica Bay.

The Phoenix died in the Blue Area of the Moon, where the Inhumans have lived since 1982.

The 1990s

By 1991 the team had grown so large that it split into two squads. In August 1993, after Magneto's global blackout, the X-Men went up to his space station, Avalon. Wolverine lost the metal from his skeleton there. Xavier ended the battle by shutting down Magneto's mind, and Wolverine left the team soon afterwards.

In 1991 Apocalypse infected Cyclops's small son Nathan with a techno-organic virus. The boy was taken into the future to be cured, and he came back as Cable.

The original five, who were teenagers in 1963, are now in their forties. In 1994 the X-Men stand between mutants and a frightened public, at a time when the Senate is weighing the revival of the Sentinel programme.

In the saga

The X-Men have not been named in the saga. On Saturday 20 August 1994 the Muggle news Harry watched at Privet Drive showed old film from 1965, juddering, in black and white, of a bald man in a wheelchair arguing politely with a big, fierce man in a suit, until the Sentinels smashed through the studio wall. The same bulletin reported that the Senate Armed Services Committee would hear evidence the following week on reviving the Sentinels. Outside the United Nations a young nurse remembered the blackout of the August before: 'That was one mutant. One man, up in a space station, having a tantrum.'

pages.title: Lord Yu
infobox: The Jade Emperor, Lord Yu-huang Shang Ti
Yu the Great, founder of China's first dynasty
The far side of Goa'uld space from Earth
A Replicator in the likeness of Samantha Carter
pages.html:
Lord Yu is the oldest of the Goa'uld System Lords, and the most sensible. He calls himself the Jade Emperor. In China, long ago, he ruled as Yu the Great, the founder of its first dynasty. His worlds lie on the far side of Goa'uld space from Earth, which has always made him readier than most to deal with it. He took part in the talks that brought Earth under the Protected Planets Treaty in 1999, fought Anubis from 2002 and was killed by a Replicator in 2005.

The Jade Emperor

Yu's full title is the Jade Emperor, the exalted Lord Yu-huang Shang Ti. Unlike most Goa'uld he did not set himself up on Earth as a god. In China he ruled as a man, an emperor, and he is remembered there as Yu the Great, who founded the first of its dynasties more than four thousand years ago.

That was long after Ra's ban. Yu came quietly, in defiance of it, and he kept to the far east of the world, as far from the North as a Goa'uld could get.

He is very old. He sat on the council that banished Anubis long ago. He took no part in the war of the 990s, when Apophis, Heru'ur and Ba'al joined their fleets against Asgard.

Rule

Most of the other System Lords lie between Yu's domain and Earth. He is a practical ruler, more interested in keeping what he has than in conquering more. He believes in his own divinity, but he rarely troubles to insist on it.

He makes war on his neighbours as readily as any System Lord. In 2002 Olokun was still smarting from a defeat at his hands.

Earth found him, alone among the System Lords, a Goa'uld who kept his word. Twice he agreed to help Earth against another System Lord, and the only time he let Earth down was when his mind had begun to fail.

The treaty with Earth

In 1999 the System Lords meant to destroy Earth for killing Hathor. Thor offered Earth a place under the Protected Planets Treaty instead. Three System Lords came through the Stargate to settle the terms: Yu, Cronus and Nirrti.

Thor himself presided. The System Lords had once asked that he should not be present at the signing of the treaty. This time he was in the room, and none of the three looked at him more than they could help.

Yu favoured the treaty from the start, since Earth's survival would trouble his enemies a great deal more than it troubled him. The Goa'uld demanded Earth's Stargates as their price. Then Nirrti, invisible, struck down Cronus, and the blame fell on Teal'c. When she was found out, Yu flew at her in a rage, because she had put their peace with Asgard at risk.

Afterwards Yu and Cronus let Earth into the treaty without giving up its gates. Cronus warned that any of Earth's people caught on Goa'uld worlds would still be fair game.

The summit

By 2002 Apophis and Cronus were dead. The rest had worn themselves out fighting over what they left. They met in council on a space station to make peace. Yu believed that the slave who attended him there was his own lo'taur, Jarren. In fact it was Daniel Jackson, sent by the Tok'ra with a poison meant to kill every System Lord in the place, together with a drug that made Yu take him for Jarren.

Jackson never used the poison. Osiris arrived as the envoy of Anubis, and killing the System Lords would only have handed the galaxy to him. Yu was the only one of the seven System Lords there who voted against taking Anubis back. He alone was left of the council that had banished him.

Jackson also saw each of the System Lords eat a live symbiote from a tank, which horrified him more than anything else he saw there.

Yu came close to dying at the end of it. He caught Jackson trying to carry Osiris off in his cargo ship, and Osiris, thinking it Yu's doing, stabbed him with her dagger. Yu survived, and went to war with Anubis.

Teal'c and Ba'al

Later in 2002 K'tano, the leader of a band of rebel Jaffa, sent Teal'c to attack Yu, as a weak System Lord whose Jaffa were ripe for the taking. Teal'c was captured. Yu let him go, for reasons he kept to himself, and sent him back knowing enough to doubt K'tano. K'tano turned out to be Imhotep, a minor Goa'uld in disguise.

That year Earth asked for his help. Ba'al was holding Jack O'Neill at a fortress where he had been studying gravity in secret, and Yu had every reason to want it destroyed. Earth sent him its plans, asking only that he strike at its power first. He did, and O'Neill escaped.

The war against Anubis

Yu spent the next year rallying the System Lords against Anubis, and by 2003 he had persuaded them to act together. Their fleet met Anubis above Abydos, where Anubis had come for the Eye of Ra. Once he had it, he turned his new weapon on the fleet and destroyed most of it. Yu got away with the few ships that were left.

By then the sarcophagus had stopped working on Yu as it should. He spent most of his time in it. He could no longer take a new host, and his mind was going.

Later in 2003, just when his fleet was needed to destroy Anubis's ship, he sent it away to the far side of the galaxy. Teal'c, who argued, was put in a cell. Yu's First Prime, Oshu, began to doubt that his master was a god at all. He took command of Yu's armies to keep the domain from falling apart, leaving Yu on the throne. At Teal'c's urging he put the fleet under Ba'al, on condition that Ba'al used it to destroy Anubis.

Last years

In 2004, with Anubis beaten, Ba'al took Anubis's Kull warriors for himself. Yu went to Earth with his First Prime to ask for help against him. Camulus and Amaterasu went with them. The talks came to nothing, and while they were going on Ba'al destroyed the ship that had brought them.

Yu and Amaterasu fought on against Ba'al while the other System Lords fell, fled or surrendered. In 2005 Ba'al's envoy, Selkhet, met the last three System Lords of the High Council at the Hasara space station to offer them terms. A prisoner was brought in who looked like Samantha Carter. She was a Replicator. Her arm became a blade, and she ran it through Yu, who died at once.

He had outlived Ra, Apophis and Cronus. In the end it was a machine that killed him.

pages.title: Zatanna Zatara
infobox: Half-blood: her father a pure-blood wizard, her mother a No-Maj
The Justice League (from 1978; the Detroit League, 1984 to 1987)
Spells spoken backwards; a wand she seldom needs
pages.html:
Zatanna Zatara is an American witch, the daughter of the pure-blood stage magician Zatara and his No-Maj wife, Sindella, which makes her a half-blood. Like her father, she does real magic on stage in front of thousands of Muggles every week, by saying her spells backwards, and not one of them has ever believed it. She was schooled at Ilvermorny, searched America for her missing father in the 1960s, joined the Justice League in 1978, and lost her father for good in 1986, at a séance John Constantine had organised. She has not entirely forgiven him for it. She was, for a while, his lover.

Birth and schooling

Zatanna was born about 1944. Her parents' marriage was against the law at the time, since Rappaport's Law forbade any American wizard to marry a No-Maj. Zatanna grew up as the half-blood daughter of a couple most of wizarding America disapproved of. Her mother died when she was still small.

From 1955 to 1962 she was at Ilvermorny, where the Thunderbird carving beat its wings for her on her first evening, and she was sorted into the house of adventurers. She learnt the school's wand-work well enough. Her father taught her the family's own art at home: spells spoken backwards, which need no wand at all.

The search for Zatara

Her father vanished in the late 1950s. From 1964, already making her living as a stage magician, Zatanna went looking for him across America. Her search crossed the paths of one costumed hero after another: Hawkman, Hawkgirl, the Atom, Green Lantern, the Elongated Man and Batman. In 1967, with the Justice League beside her, she found him at last and broke the curse that had kept them apart.

The Justice League

Zatanna joined the Justice League in 1978, the first witch ever to do so, although the League took her for a sorceress of the stage like her father. When Aquaman broke up the old League in 1984 and moved it to Detroit, she was one of the few veterans who stayed. She served there until the Detroit League came to an end in 1987.

To Muggles she is a stage magician who also happens to fight crime, with powers nobody can quite explain. The hidden wizarding world behind her has never come out. MACUSA, which spent decades failing to catch her father, has left her alone since Rappaport's Law was repealed in 1965.

Constantine and the séance

In the 1980s Zatanna and John Constantine, the Liverpool occultist, were lovers for a time. In 1986 John gathered the most powerful magicians of the age for a séance, to guide the Swamp Thing against the darkness that had risen, and Zatanna came with her father. When the backlash of the darkness came at her, Zatara drew it into himself to save her. It killed him.

She has never entirely forgiven John, and he has never forgiven himself. She came to his fortieth birthday party in May 1993 all the same.

Later years

Zatanna has gone on performing, and on fighting beside the League whenever it needs a witch. In 2004, after a vote of the League, she used her magic to change the villain Doctor Light's mind and memories. When Batman found out, she did the same to him. It was a Memory Charm in all but name, and the most bitterly argued thing she has ever done.

pages.title: Zatara
pages.html:
Zatara was an American wizard of an old pure-blood family of Italian descent. From 1938 he worked in public as a stage magician in top hat and tails, doing real magic in front of packed theatres by speaking his spells backwards. He fought crime, served with the All-Star Squadron in the Second World War and broke Rappaport's Law every night for nearly thirty years. He married a No-Maj, Sindella, and was the father of Zatanna. He died in 1986 at John Constantine's séance against the darkness.

Life

Giovanni Zatara, always called John, was born about 1912 into a pure-blood family of Italian descent that had long been settled in America. He went to Ilvermorny in the 1920s. His family had an art of its own, which it had kept for generations: spells spoken backwards, which need no wand at all. He carried a wand on stage all the same, where everybody took it for a prop.

From 1938 he played the theatres of America as a stage magician. Off the stage he fought crime openly beside the first of the mystery men, and in the war he served with the All-Star Squadron.

Rappaport's Law

Rappaport's Law forbade American wizards any dealings with No-Majs, and every one of Zatara's performances broke it. So did his marriage, in the early 1940s, to Sindella, a No-Maj woman. MACUSA pursued him for years without ever convicting him. Not one No-Maj who saw his act believed the magic was real, and the Congress could hardly prove a breach of secrecy that nobody had noticed.

Their daughter, Zatanna, was born about 1944. Sindella died while the girl was still a child.

Disappearance and death

In the late 1950s Zatara vanished, kept from his daughter by a curse. From 1964 Zatanna searched for him across America, helped by one costumed hero after another. In 1967, with the Justice League beside her, she found him at last and broke the curse.

In 1986 John Constantine gathered the most powerful magicians of the age for a séance, to guide the Swamp Thing against the darkness that had risen, and Zatara was among them. When the backlash of that darkness came at Zatanna, he drew it into himself to save her, and it killed him. The sorcerer Sargon died with him.

pages.title: Zero Hour
infobox: The Atom (Al Pratt); Hourman (Rex Tyler); Doctor Mid-Nite (Charles McNider)
Time slips across the world; the dead, and people of other eras, walking the streets
Early August 1994, when time was begun again
pages.html:
Zero Hour, sometimes called the Crisis in Time, was the breakdown of time itself in July and early August 1994. For some weeks history came apart. The past leaked into the present, heroes of other eras walked the streets, and a wave of nothingness rolled back from the end of time, wiping out the ages in front of it. The Justice Society made its last stand against the time-mad Extant and was broken. The power behind the whole catastrophe turned out to be Hal Jordan, the lost Green Lantern, who now called himself Parallax. Time was begun again early in August, and most people remember those weeks only as a strange dream.

Time begins to fail

In July 1994 time began to go wrong all over the world. Clocks disagreed with one another. Whole districts of cities slipped into other years for an hour at a time, and people met the dead in the street, or their own younger selves. Heroes from other eras, some of them from histories that had never happened at all, appeared and vanished again.

Behind it all a wave of entropy was rolling back from the end of time, and the ages of the far future were going out ahead of it one after another, like lamps. The heroes of every nation gathered against it, Superman among the first. With them stood the Linear Men, who keep watch over history from Vanishing Point, a citadel beyond the end of time.

Extant and the Justice Society

The first face the enemy showed was Extant's. He had once been Hank Hall, the hero Hawk, and he had taken the powers of time for himself. At Vanishing Point the Justice Society, the oldest heroes in the world, stood against him.

Ever since the war the Society's members had been kept young by the temporal energies of the sorcerer Ian Karkull, and Extant simply took those stolen years back. The Atom (Al Pratt), Hourman (Rex Tyler) and Doctor Mid-Nite (Charles McNider) died of it. The others were aged to their true years in a matter of moments: the Flash (Jay Garrick), Starman (Ted Knight), the Sandman (Wesley Dodds), Johnny Thunder and Wildcat (Ted Grant). Wildcat had a heart attack under the strain. Kent Nelson and his wife, Inza, were torn from the power of Fate as well as aged to their true years. The helmet, cloak and amulet of Nabu were scattered. Hawkman (Carter Hall) and Hawkgirl (Shiera Hall) were merged into a single being. Only Alan Scott, the first Green Lantern, came through unchanged, because his ring's power held.

When it was over the survivors, old now in body as well as in years, agreed that the Society's day was done. They disbanded it.

Parallax

Extant was not working alone. The power behind the catastrophe was Hal Jordan, Green Lantern for thirty-four years, who had vanished at the turn of 1994 after destroying the Green Lantern Corps. He called himself Parallax now. He meant to unmake history and build it again, this time without the destruction of Coast City, with its seven million people, or any of the other wrongs he could not forgive.

The heroes would not let him. At the beginning of time they stood against him, his own successor Kyle Rayner among them. It was Connor Hawke, the young son of Oliver Queen, the first Green Arrow, who shot him through the heart. Hal Jordan survived even that. He vanished again, and nobody knows where he is.

Time begins again

Parallax was stopped before he could remake the universe to his own design. By then, though, there was too little of time left to save. The young hero called Damage, whose power was the energy of a new beginning, let it go at the dawn of all things. Time was begun again from it, with the heroes shaping what came after. Early in August 1994 the world simply went on, as though time had never broken.

What is remembered

Almost nobody outside the heroes' own circles remembers Zero Hour clearly. Most people recall a few strange weeks that summer and are not sure which parts of them were real. Those who were there agree that history came back very nearly as it had been. Not quite, though: a few small things are said to be different, and nobody can say for certain what they are.

By the middle of August the news was full of the Augment War again, and Zero Hour was hardly mentioned. What stayed were the deaths of the Atom, Hourman and Doctor Mid-Nite, together with the end of the Justice Society.

pages.title: Harry Potter and the Girl Who Noticed Him
pages.html:
Front page · The Books

Harry Potter and the Girl Who Noticed Him

Book One of the Malfoid Saga · 1991 to 1992 · Complete

Read Book OneFree at malfoid.lol

Chapters

Chapter 1The Girl Who Noticed

Hagrid had slipped off to the Leaky Cauldron to recover from the Gringotts cart ride, so Harry Potter went into Madam Malkin's Robes for All Occasions in Diagon Alley on his own, still wearing Dudley's cast-off clothes. He was put on a stool beside a girl with waist-length silver-blonde hair. She had silver eyes, said she was Dracina Malfoy and held out her hand to be kissed. Harry, who knew nothing of the custom, asked her quite seriously whether she was a princess, which made her blush. Then she talked about racing brooms, about Quidditch and about how certain she was of being sorted into Slytherin. Harry was strongly reminded of Dudley. When Hagrid appeared at the window with two ice-creams, she dismissed him as a drunken servant, and Harry coldly defended him. On learning that Harry's parents were dead, she asked whether they had been 'our sort' and said that Muggle-borns should not be let into Hogwarts. Harry left without telling her his surname. He did not see her watch him all the way to the door, or go on gazing after him once he had gone. He ate his ice-cream in silence, unable to make the two halves of her fit together.

Chapter 2The Wrong Sort

On the Hogwarts Express Harry shared a compartment with Ron Weasley, who told him about his five older brothers and his rat, Scabbers. Ron admitted that his family could not afford an owl. Harry bought a heap of sweets from the trolley and swapped pasties for Ron's corned beef sandwiches; his first Chocolate Frog card showed Albus Dumbledore. Neville Longbottom came looking for his lost toad. Hermione Granger watched Ron fail to turn Scabbers yellow with a dud rhyme he had got from George. Then Dracina Malfoy arrived with Crabbe and Goyle, having heard that Harry Potter was on the train. She was rude about the Weasleys and offered Harry her hand, along with her guidance on 'the wrong sort'. Harry refused both. Dracina warned him that he would end up like his parents. When Goyle grabbed at the Chocolate Frogs, Scabbers bit him on the knuckle, and the three of them fled. Dracina's eyes stayed on Harry as she went, like someone who had already decided to have a thing she had seen in a shop window. Ron told Harry afterwards that the Malfoys had claimed to have been bewitched after You-Know-Who's fall. His father did not believe a word of it.

Chapter 3Silver Eyes

Hagrid took the first-years across the lake by boat to Hogwarts, where Professor McGonagall told them about the four houses and the House Cup. While they waited, a crowd of ghosts frightened them all. Dracina screamed and clutched Harry's arm, then shoved him away as though he had bumped into her. The Sorting Hat sang its song and the Sorting began. Dracina was in Slytherin almost before the hat had touched her head. Harry begged the hat, 'Not Slytherin'. It remarked on his courage, his talent and 'so much pain' for one so young, then put him in Gryffindor. Dracina looked disappointed when he was sorted, then turned her back. At the feast Harry met Nearly Headless Nick and learnt that Slytherin had won the House Cup six years running. Seamus and Neville described their families. When Professor Snape looked at him past Quirrell's turban, Harry's scar burned. Dumbledore warned the school that the forest was out of bounds, and so was the right-hand corridor on the third floor. Then everybody sang the school song. Percy led the Gryffindors past Peeves to their tower. That night Harry dreamed that Quirrell's turban was urging him to go into Slytherin, and that Malfoy was laughing at him. When he woke, all he could remember was a pair of cruel silver eyes.

Chapter 4The Old Hogwarts Try

Harry's first week at Hogwarts was a struggle against moving staircases, Peeves and a school that would not stop staring at him. In Astronomy Hermione lectured him on astrology. In History of Magic Professor Binns read out pure-blood marriage lists, which set Ron and Hermione explaining wizarding ideas of blood. Hermione told Harry about the Norman wizarding families who had won the Conquest for William with dark magic. Dracina claimed that the Malfoys had been in Britain before Britain existed. When Hermione corrected her, Dracina mocked her hair, nose and teeth, then called her a Mudblood. Ron rebuked her for using such a filthy word. With Harry, Dracina was softer. She urged him to side with his own kind, the old pure families like his, but he told her she was not the sort of girl he wanted as a friend. All she could find to say back was 'pottyhead', which made him laugh. Charms, Transfiguration and a Defence lesson with the stammering, garlic-reeking Quirrell went little better. On Friday Hedwig brought Hagrid's invitation to tea. In double Potions Snape mocked Harry's fame, quizzed him on things he could not possibly know and took two points from Gryffindor. He praised Dracina's work. Neville, meanwhile, melted Seamus's cauldron and came out in boils.

Chapter 5The Seeker

Flying lessons with the Slytherins began in Harry's second week. At breakfast Dracina snatched Neville's new Remembrall, until Professor McGonagall stepped in. In the lesson Neville took off too early, fell and broke his wrist. While Madam Hooch was taking him away, Dracina found the Remembrall and flew off with it. Harry went after her on the first flight of his life. He charged at her, saw her for a moment as a frightened little girl, and caught the Remembrall she threw at the end of a fifty-foot dive. Professor McGonagall marched him off. Instead of expelling him, she introduced him to Oliver Wood as Gryffindor's new Seeker, the youngest house player in about a century. She told him that his father had been a fine Quidditch player. Dracina challenged Harry to a wizard's duel at midnight in the trophy room, with Ron and Crabbe as seconds. Hermione, who had been locked out of the tower, came along, and so did Neville, who had forgotten the password. Dracina never turned up. Filch did. Running from Peeves, the four of them opened a locked door with Hermione's Alohomora, and found a three-headed dog in the forbidden corridor on the third floor. Hermione noticed that it was standing on a trapdoor. Harry realised that it was guarding the package Hagrid had taken from vault seven hundred and thirteen at Gringotts.

Chapter 6The Yearning

The morning after the duel that never happened, Dracina came in to breakfast looking forlorn. She brightened when she saw Harry, then remembered to be angry that he had not been expelled. A week later Harry received a Nimbus Two Thousand from Professor McGonagall. Dracina tried to get him into trouble over it, but Professor Flitwick already knew of the special circumstances. Harry thanked her for getting him on to the team, and said he owed her a favour. It left her blushing, silently repeating the word to herself. That evening Oliver Wood taught Harry the rules of Quidditch on the pitch. Afterwards Harry found that Dracina had been watching from the stands. Their quarrel grew worse until Harry exploded. He shouted about Dudley hanging him off the school roof, and about Aunt Petunia's frying pan, then stopped, ashamed of having frightened her. Dracina's eyes shimmered and she began to speak, but Wood sent her off. Her whispered apology never reached Harry. On Hallowe'en Ron's cruelty sent Hermione crying into the girls' toilets. When Quirrell announced that there was a troll in the dungeons, Harry and Ron went to warn her. By accident they locked the troll in, with Hermione and Dracina still inside. Then they fought it. Harry jammed his wand up its nose, and Ron knocked it out with its own club. Both girls lied to the teachers to protect the boys, and each lost five points for her house. From then on Hermione was Harry and Ron's friend. Dracina watched the three of them from the shadows, seething with jealousy, thinking of her brave knight.

Chapter 7Secret Weapon

As November turned frosty, Harry got ready for his first Quidditch match, against Slytherin; Oliver Wood was keeping him hidden as Gryffindor's secret weapon. Hermione, grateful after the troll, began doing all of Harry's homework, and she was especially warm to him whenever Dracina was watching. Dracina repaid her with hostility. Harry noticed that Dracina never threw back at him any of the things he had shouted at her on the pitch, the ones that would really have hurt; she stuck to 'Pottyhead'. Snape, who was limping, confiscated Harry's library copy of Quidditch Through the Ages. When Harry went to ask for it back, he saw Snape's bloodied leg and heard him complain about watching three heads at once. That convinced him Snape had let the troll in to get past the dog. At the match Dracina watched Harry with plain worry. After Marcus Flint fouled him, Harry's broom began to buck so violently that he was left hanging from it by one hand. Hermione checked on Dracina first and found her white with fear. Then she spotted Snape muttering and set his robes alight, knocking Quirrell over on the way. Harry recovered, caught the Snitch in his mouth and won the match 170 to 60, while Dracina cheered in the Slytherin stand. Over tea Hagrid let slip that the three-headed dog was his, that it was called Fluffy, and that he had lent it to Dumbledore. Worse, he let slip that whatever it guarded was a matter for Dumbledore and Nicolas Flamel.

Chapter 8Desire Behind Glass

In snowbound December Dracina grabbed Harry's shoulder in a corridor, which brought back a flash of Dudley. She had come to give him her mother's invitation to spend Christmas at Malfoy Manor. Harry laughed, taking it for a prank, and she told him he was too stupid to see a good thing. In Potions she went on taunting him about having nowhere to go, dropping hints about the invitation. She goaded Ron into grabbing her robes, and Snape took five points from Gryffindor. In the decorated Great Hall Harry saw Dracina standing alone, staring at the mistletoe; she and Hermione glared at each other across the room. In the library, where Harry, Ron and Hermione were hunting for Nicolas Flamel, Dracina offered to help Harry by the Restricted Section, until Hermione towed him away. Harry stayed at Hogwarts for Christmas with the Weasleys. He received the first presents of his life, among them a Weasley jumper, a fifty-pence piece from the Dursleys and, from somebody who did not sign the note, his father's Invisibility Cloak. Under the Cloak he fled from a screaming book in the Restricted Section, then from Filch and Snape. While he was hiding from them he found a mirror. In it he saw his parents, two sets of grandparents, a little brother and a little sister. Ron saw himself as Head Boy and Quidditch captain. Harry, resentful, shoved him. On the third night Dumbledore found Harry at the mirror. He told him it was the Mirror of Erised, and that it showed the deepest desire of a person's heart. Harry's wish, he said, was for love and a family. Then he apologised to Harry, and asked him not to go looking for the mirror again.

Chapter 9Five Minutes

Harry did as Dumbledore asked and stayed away from the mirror. Instead he began to have nightmares of green light, with a woman screaming. When term began again, Dracina sat down beside him at breakfast while he was alone. She stayed until Ron and Hermione arrived, then retreated with an insult. Wood drove the team hard before the Hufflepuff match, which Snape, unexpectedly, was to referee. Harry made up his mind to play, whatever his friends feared. Dracina hit Neville with the Leg-Locker Curse, saying that she had been looking for someone in particular to practise on. Harry cheered him up with a Chocolate Frog, and its Dumbledore card gave them Nicolas Flamel's name; Hermione's library book showed that Flamel was the only known maker of the Philosopher's Stone. In Potions Dracina corrected Harry's stirring, which stopped his potion exploding. At the match, which Dumbledore came to watch, Dean Thomas led the Gryffindor stand in football chants. Dracina, sitting behind Ron, taunted him and Neville until Ron went for her. Neville fought Crabbe and Goyle single-handed. When nobody came to her rescue, Dracina mauled Ron. She bit his ear, screaming about Harry and the company he kept. Harry caught the Snitch in about five minutes, which put Gryffindor top of the House Championship, and Dumbledore quietly praised him. That evening Harry followed Snape into the Forbidden Forest on his broom. He overheard Snape pressing Quirrell about getting past Fluffy, and about Quirrell's 'hocus-pocus' protecting the Philosopher's Stone.

Chapter 10The Egg in the Fire

With Quirrell apparently still holding out against Snape, Harry, Ron and Hermione kept checking that Fluffy was still on guard. Hermione drew up revision timetables ten weeks before the exams, and seemed always to know where Harry was. Dracina put it about that Ron was a violent animal. When they spotted Hagrid in the library with books on dragons, the three of them went down to his sweltering hut. There Hagrid, coaxed by Hermione, listed the teachers who had set enchantments round the Stone, Snape among them. He also showed them a Norwegian Ridgeback egg, which he had won at cards from a stranger in the village. Dracina overheard that the egg was hatching, and spied on the newborn dragon through Hagrid's curtains. Harry tackled her on the lawn, but she got away by crying assault. Hagrid named the dragon Norbert, and Harry suggested sending him to Charlie Weasley in Romania. Norbert bit Ron's hand with his poisonous fangs. In the hospital wing Dracina threatened to tell what had bitten Ron unless he stopped being Harry's friend. She went off with a book that had Charlie's reply inside it. On Saturday night Harry and Hermione carried Norbert's crate to the tallest tower under the Invisibility Cloak. On the way they passed Professor McGonagall, who was giving Dracina a detention for being out of bed and would not hear a word about Harry having a dragon. Charlie's friends took Norbert away. Harry and Hermione, though, left the Cloak behind on the tower. Filch caught them at the foot of the stairs.

Chapter 11The Death of Beauty

Filch left Harry and Hermione in Professor McGonagall's study. She came in with Neville trailing behind her. Harry and Ron, she announced, had lured Dracina out of bed with a ridiculous story about a dragon. She rebuked Hermione for calling Dracina an evil harpy. Then she took fifty points each from Harry, Hermione and Neville. Alone with Harry, she produced Charlie's letter, the one Dracina had taken. She gave him the advice she had once given his father: that one is only punished for what one is caught doing. Afterwards Harry realised that she had covered for him. Gryffindor fell to last place, and Harry became the most hated boy in the school, with only Ron standing by him. A week before the exams Harry overheard Quirrell apparently giving in to someone, and decided not to meddle. Quirrell supervised the detention, which Dracina was serving too. He took them into the Forbidden Forest, supposedly to collect mushrooms along a silver trail. Quirrell, whose stutter vanished whenever he grew irritated, suddenly screamed and bolted into the trees with his lamp. Harry lost the others in the dark. Dracina found him there, holding the only lamp left in the Forest, and demanded that he escort her, reminding him of the favour he owed her. She clung to his hand, overjoyed that her knight was protecting her. A shimmering unicorn came up and let Dracina touch it. Then a hooded figure killed it with green light and began to drink its blood. Harry's scar blazed and Dracina fled. The centaur Firenze rescued Harry, defying Bane to do it, and hinted that Voldemort was drinking unicorn blood while he waited for the Stone. Back in the tower Harry found his Invisibility Cloak returned to him, with a note that read 'Just in case'.

Chapter 12Seven Bottles

Quirrell was found at dawn at the edge of the Forest, cut about and howling. The school blamed centaurs, but Harry was still suspicious of his lies and his vanishing stutter. Through the sweltering exams of June 1992 Harry suffered from pains in his scar and nightmares about the hooded figure. Dracina showed off in Potions. After the last exam she called Hermione a violent Mudblood, and Harry comforted Hermione. Then Harry realised that Hagrid's hooded card partner had learnt from him that music sent Fluffy to sleep. He tried to reach Dumbledore, but Professor McGonagall said the headmaster had been called to London by the Ministry, and insisted that the Stone was safe. Snape warned the three of them off. McGonagall caught Harry and Ron near the third-floor corridor. Harry made up his mind to go through the trapdoor that night. Ron and Hermione insisted on coming too. Dracina, who had been given the password by Neville, was waiting in the Gryffindor common room, apparently to apologise to Harry. Hermione, calling her Snape's spy, petrified her with the Body-Bind. Harry accepted Dracina's apology, apologised for Hermione and promised to come back for her. He saw a twinkle in her eyes that he would remember for years. Harry got rid of Peeves by pretending to be the Bloody Baron, and lulled Fluffy to sleep with Hagrid's flute. Hermione's fire freed the three of them from the Devil's Snare. Harry caught the winged key, and Ron sacrificed himself in a giant game of chess so that Harry could checkmate the king. They passed a stunned troll. Then Harry and Hermione solved Snape's logic puzzle of the seven bottles. Harry sent Hermione back for help and walked through the black flames into the final chamber. There he found neither Snape nor Voldemort.

Chapter 13Rage Against Evil

In the final chamber Harry found Quirrell, calm and without a trace of his stutter, standing in front of the Mirror of Erised. Quirrell told him that it was he, not Snape, who had jinxed Harry's broom; Snape had been muttering a counter-curse. Quirrell had let the troll in himself, and Lucius Malfoy had arranged for Dumbledore to be away in London. Quirrell had also used the students in detention as bait for the unicorn, which would never have come near a man like him. He bound Harry in conjured chains and confessed that he served Lord Voldemort, who had punished him for failing to steal the Stone from Gringotts. When Harry looked into the Mirror, his reflection put the blood-red Stone in its pocket, and the Stone dropped into Harry's real one. Harry lied about what he saw. Quirrell unwrapped his turban. On the back of his head was Voldemort's chalk-white, red-eyed face. Voldemort taunted Harry about his parents' deaths and demanded the Stone. But wherever Quirrell touched Harry's skin, his own hands and face blistered. Harry clung on through pain and hatred until he blacked out, seeing his parents in the Mirror, proud of him. He woke three days later in the hospital wing. Dumbledore explained that he had pulled Quirrell off him, and that the Stone had been destroyed with Flamel's agreement. Lily's love had left a protection in Harry's skin, he said. Lily might also descend from a very powerful magical line, and James had once saved Snape's life. Hagrid, in tears, gave Harry an album of photographs of his parents. Neville confessed that Dracina had been kind to him, and that was how she had got the password. At the end-of-year feast Dumbledore's last-minute awards to Ron, Hermione and Harry drew Gryffindor level with Slytherin. Then he took a hundred points from Slytherin for Dracina's trespass, and the House Cup went to Gryffindor. On the platform at King's Cross Dracina warned Harry, almost anxiously, to watch out next year. Harry left with the Dursleys, certain now that he could endure them.

How it differs from the original

  • The book opens at Madam Malkin's; there are no Privet Drive or Dursley chapters, no Hagrid letter-delivery scene, no Gringotts, Ollivander's, Leaky Cauldron or Diagon Alley tour on the page.
  • The platform departure happens offstage; Chapter 2 opens with the train already moving.
  • Draco Malfoy is Dracina Malfoy, a girl infatuated with Harry from first sight, so her antagonism plays as thwarted courtship and the Gryffindor boys repeatedly debate whether boys may hit girls.
  • Harry asks Dracina 'Are you a princess?' at Madam Malkin's, and she teaches him that a witch's hand is to be kissed.
  • Dracina watches Harry's first solo practice, and Harry shouts his abuse history at her; she begins an apology only Wood hears.
  • Dracina is in the girls' toilets with Hermione on Hallowe'en and is the troll's first target; Harry saves both girls, and Dracina lies to McGonagall to cover for Harry and Ron.
  • Narcissa invites Harry to Malfoy Manor for Christmas and Harry laughs it off as a prank.
  • Dean Thomas writes football terrace chants, and a brawl breaks out in the stands in which Neville beats Crabbe and Goyle and Dracina savages Ron.
  • The detention is not with Hagrid: Quirrell takes Harry, Hermione, Neville and Dracina into the Forest on a fake mushroom hunt and abandons them as bait for unicorns.
  • Dracina touches the dying unicorn, and Harry sees it killed by a green-light curse; Dracina runs.
  • On the final night Dracina gets the password from Neville to apologise, and Hermione Body-Binds her, not Neville.
  • Dumbledore docks Slytherin one hundred points for Dracina's trespass, which decides the House Cup; final points are Ron 50, Hermione 50, Harry 60, and Neville gets nothing.
  • Snape takes one point, not five, for Harry's impertinence, and Harry's answer is a sincere suggestion to ask Hermione.
  • Hermione's friendship becomes an obsessive, jealous attachment: she does all Harry's homework.
  • Gryffindor's second match is against Hufflepuff, won in five minutes, and they lose the third to Ravenclaw while Harry is in hospital.
  • Dracina, not Draco, is caught on the dragon night, and McGonagall knowingly calls the truth a lie to protect Harry.
  • McGonagall has a hidden military past: mujahideen, Kosovo, Kandahar and Zanzibar Land.
  • Harry's final fight is a mauling fuelled by hatred, and he senses Voldemort's fear.
  • Dumbledore reveals Lily descended from an unnamed, very powerful line of magic.
  • The Mirror of Erised shows Harry two sets of grandparents, a little brother and a little sister.
  • The Sorting Hat song, the seven-bottles riddle and Dumbledore's opening words are all new, and the password changes from Caput Draconis to Pig snout.
  • Dracina warns Harry at King's Cross, in a worried tone, to watch out next year.
  • Draco Malfoy is a girl here: Dracina Malfoy.
  • Dracina offers her hand to be kissed, not shaken, and Harry asks whether she is a princess.
  • The chapter closes on Dracina watching Harry go, a sign of her interest in him from their very first meeting.
  • Dracina again holds out her hand palm down, and Harry orders her out before Ron can finish his insult.
  • Ron's rhyme for turning the rat yellow is 'Buttercup, custard, morning sun'.
  • Dracina's long, possessive look at Harry as she leaves is new.
  • Dracina screams at the ghosts and grabs Harry's arm, then pushes him away.
  • The Sorting Hat remarks on Harry's pain as well as on his courage and talent.
  • Dracina is plainly disappointed when Harry is sorted into Gryffindor.
  • Harry's dream ends with Dracina's silver eyes, which stay with him after he wakes.
  • Hermione gives a history of the Norman dark wizarding families who won the Conquest, and says that William granted Armand Malfoy his land in Wiltshire.
  • When Dracina taunts Hermione about her looks, Harry remembers Aunt Petunia's prejudice. He starts to ask whether she means the Jews, before she says 'Mudbloods'.
  • Dracina urges Harry to side with the Malfoys because the Potters are an ancient, pure family. Her comeback, 'pottyhead', becomes a running joke.
  • Ron says that Charlie learnt a Shield Charm in his first year.
  • Ron keeps threatening to hit Dracina, girl or not. Hermione and Harry tell him off for it. Ron admits that he does not actually hit girls.
  • Harry sees Dracina for a moment as a frightened little girl in the air. There is also something in her voice when she speaks to him that an eleven-year-old would not notice.
  • Harry compares Crabbe and Goyle to Tolkien's Uruk-hai.
  • Dracina is in the girls' toilets with Hermione when the troll arrives, and the troll goes for her first.
  • Losing his temper, Harry blurts out to Dracina the details of Dudley's bullying and of the Dursleys' abuse.
  • Dracina whispers an apology to Harry that he never hears.
  • Hermione lies to McGonagall to protect Harry and Ron. So does Dracina, and Snape takes five points from Slytherin.
  • A rivalry over Harry between Hermione and Dracina is hinted at. Only Ron notices it.
  • Hermione writes the whole of Harry's homework for him. She is protective of him, believing that he will keep her safe.
  • Dracina is plainly worried for Harry during the match, and cheers when he beats her own house.
  • Dean wears a West Ham scarf, and Hagrid covers it with a Gryffindor one.
  • Hagrid bought Fluffy from a man with a caravan whom he took to be Greek; Harry doubts that he was Greek.
  • Quidditch Through the Ages describes an 1877 duel between the English and French managers that killed two hundred people.
  • Narcissa Malfoy invites Harry to Malfoy Manor for Christmas through Dracina, and Harry laughs it off.
  • When he is grabbed from behind, Harry has a flashback to Dudley's bullying.
  • In the mirror Harry sees a little brother and a little sister, as well as his parents with both sets of grandparents.
  • Harry's resentment of Ron's family and the voice of the Dursleys in his head are explored at length.
  • Dumbledore apologises to Harry and speaks of people like the two of them being burdened by destiny.
  • Dracina, not Draco, uses the Leg-Locker Curse on Neville, saying that she meant it for someone in particular.
  • Dracina helps Harry with his potion in class.
  • Dean Thomas leads football chants against Hufflepuff, among them 'Five minutes!' and 'Can we play you every week?'.
  • Ron fights Dracina instead of Draco, and comes off worse. She scratches him, bites him and pulls his hair, screaming about Harry the whole time.
  • Flamel lives in Devon with Perenelle.
  • Dracina, in Draco's role, spies on Norbert's hatching; Harry tackles her, and she escapes by crying assault.
  • Dracina's price for keeping quiet is that Ron must stop being Harry's friend.
  • Hermione seems always to know where Harry is, and she coaxes Hagrid with a smile that reminds Harry of Dracina.
  • Ron regrets fighting Dracina, saying his mum was right that you should not hit girls.
  • In public McGonagall treats Dracina's dragon report as a lie, but in private she shows Harry that she knows the truth. She advises him only to avoid being caught, as she once advised James.
  • McGonagall hints at a past involving feral mujahideen.
  • Quirrell, not Hagrid, leads the detention. He lies that the unicorn blood is a mushroom secretion, and runs off theatrically.
  • Dracina, not Draco, is paired with Harry in the Forest. She holds his hand. The unicorn comes up to her and lets her touch it.
  • Hermione calls Dracina an evil harpy, and hisses at her whenever she comes near Harry.
  • McGonagall alludes to a holiday in Kosovo, to a night spent warding a camp outside Kandahar, and to an old friend from Zanzibar Land who taught her to move silently.
  • Harry calls the man who sold Fluffy to Hagrid a Pikey, meaning that he was not Greek.
  • Dracina, not Neville, confronts the trio in the common room, where she is trying to apologise to Harry. Hermione petrifies her instead of Neville.
  • Harry pretends to be the Bloody Baron to get rid of Peeves.
  • Harry catches the winged key by spotting its crushed wing, overcoming the voice of the Dursleys in his head.
  • Quirrell says that Lucius Malfoy made sure Dumbledore was in London, and that he used the students in detention as bait because unicorns will not come to him.
  • Quirrell says that James Potter was a few years ahead of him at school, and meddled in 'our business'.
  • Dumbledore tells Harry that Lily, though Muggle-born, may descend from a very powerful magical line. The protection, he says, came from several things together, among them her dying spell and whatever anchors Voldemort to this plane.
  • Neville receives no points. Instead Dumbledore takes a hundred points from Slytherin because Dracina entered the Gryffindor common room, and that wins Gryffindor the Cup.
  • Dumbledore says that Snape and James loathed each other. He compares their loathing with what Harry believes lies between him and Dracina.
  • At King's Cross Dracina warns Harry to watch out next year, and on the train Hermione holds Harry's hand.

Characters introduced

  • Albus Dumbledore
  • Argus Filch
  • Arthur Weasley
  • Dean Thomas
  • Dracina Malfoy
  • Dudley Dursley
  • Filius Flitwick
  • Firenze
  • Fred Weasley
  • George Weasley
  • Ginny Weasley
  • Gregory Goyle
  • Harry Potter
  • Hedwig
  • Hermione Granger
  • Justin Finch-Fletchley
  • Lord Voldemort
  • Lucius Malfoy
  • Minerva McGonagall
  • Molly Weasley
  • Mrs Norris
  • Narcissa Malfoy
  • Nearly Headless Nick
  • Neville Longbottom
  • Oliver Wood

pages.title: Harry Potter and the Girl with the Diary
pages.html:
Front page · The Books

Harry Potter and the Girl with the Diary

Book Two of the Malfoid Saga · 1992 to 1993 · Complete

Read Book TwoFree at malfoid.lol

Chapters

Chapter 1Making No Noise

On 31 July 1992, Harry Potter's twelfth birthday, Vernon Dursley shouted at him over Hedwig's hooting. Breakfast turned to uproar when Harry said 'the magic word' by accident, then called the family malignant on purpose. He had come home from his first year at Hogwarts with a defiant streak, and had taken to goading the Dursleys. They had padlocked his school things in the cupboard under the stairs, and Hedwig in her cage. The Dursleys forgot his birthday entirely. Instead they rehearsed for a dinner party at which Vernon hoped to sell drills to a wealthy builder, Mr Mason, and his wife. Harry was ordered to stay in his room making no noise. Alone in the garden, he brooded. Not a single letter had come from Ron or Hermione, and an inner voice kept telling him that nobody had ever liked him. He caught himself missing Dracina Malfoy, and the twinkle in her silver eyes. Then he noticed two enormous green eyes watching him from the hedge. When Dudley jeered that he had no friends, Harry pretended to be turning the hedge into an Ent. Aunt Petunia swung a frying pan at him and kept him working in the garden until evening. All he was given to eat was bread and cheese. He went upstairs as the Masons arrived, and found somebody already sitting on his bed.

Chapter 2DMD: Dobby Must Die

The creature on Harry's bed was Dobby, a house-elf dressed in a pillowcase. He wept loudly at being treated as an equal, and battered his own head whenever he came close to betraying the wizarding family he served. Dobby warned Harry that a plot would make terrible things happen at Hogwarts that year, and that he must not go back. His Mistress, he added, had been very clear that Harry should be told. He gave Harry to understand that the danger did not come from He Who Must Not Be Named, and hinted at powers that no decent wizard used. Then Dobby admitted that he had been stopping Harry's letters from Ron, Hermione and Hagrid, in the hope that Harry would think himself friendless. He offered them back only if Harry promised not to return. When Harry refused, Dobby ran to the kitchen, levitated Aunt Petunia's pudding, dropped it on the floor and vanished with a crack. An owl then brought a Ministry warning from Mafalda Hopkirk about the Hover Charm. It dropped the letter on Mrs Mason, who was terrified of birds, and that was the end of the deal. Once Vernon learnt that Harry was not allowed to use magic outside school, he locked him in his room. He had bars fitted to the window, put a cat-flap in the door and fed him almost nothing. After three days of it Harry dreamed that he was in a cage at a zoo while Dracina laughed at him. He woke to find Ron Weasley outside his window.

Chapter 3Touchdown

Ron, Fred and George had come for him in their father's enchanted flying Ford Anglia. They ripped the bars from the window. The twins picked the lock on Harry's door with a piece of wire and fetched his trunk from the cupboard. As Harry escaped, Uncle Vernon seized his ankle; Harry clawed himself free, shouting that he hated him and would never come back. In the car Harry wept with relief and told the Weasleys about Dobby. The twins thought that someone with a grudge must have sent the elf. Harry and Ron named Dracina Malfoy at once. Fred and George described Lucius Malfoy as a former supporter of You-Know-Who, from a family of Dark wizards going back to the Norman Conquest. Harry remembered Dracina mentioning a house-elf in their first year. On the flight Ron told Harry about Errol, and about Percy's owl, Hermes. He explained that Percy had been behaving oddly ever since their mother took away a statue Charlie had given him. He told Harry, too, about his father's job in the Misuse of Muggle Artefacts Office. At dawn they landed at the Burrow, outside Ottery St Catchpole, where Molly Weasley confronted her sons in the yard. Overcome by exhaustion and guilt, Harry apologised to her, then fainted.

Chapter 4As Long As You Want

Harry woke on the Weasleys' sofa. Ron told his mother about the bars, the lock and the empty soup bowl. Molly Weasley had already seen the bruises Vernon's grip had left on Harry's ankle, and she asked him gently whether he had been hit. Harry could not lie to her. He let slip the frying pan first. Then out came the whole history of the beatings and the cupboard. He broke down sobbing. He said Ron was the best person he knew, and thanked her for the Christmas jumper. Molly held him and promised to make everything better, though inside she was growing furious with the Dursleys. She told him he could stay at the Burrow for as long as he wanted. Harry took in the Weasleys' cosy kitchen and met a painfully shy Ginny. He ate an enormous breakfast, then helped to de-gnome the garden once Molly had consulted Gilderoy Lockhart's Guide to Household Pests. Arthur Weasley came home from a night of Ministry raids, and Molly confronted him over the enchanted car. He admitted that he had written a loophole into the law himself. Ron showed Harry his orange bedroom, which was covered in Chudley Cannons posters. Harry declared the Burrow the best house he had ever been in.

Chapter 5The Wrong Grate

At the Burrow Harry got his strength back. He explained Muggle devices to Arthur, and noticed Molly's hints about Professor McGonagall's Muggle connections. The Hogwarts letters arrived with a booklist made up of Lockhart's titles. Molly firmly refused Harry's offers to pay for the Weasleys' books, and Hermione wrote to suggest meeting in Diagon Alley. On his first journey by Floo powder Harry came out in Borgin and Burkes in Knockturn Alley, and hid in a cabinet. From inside it he overheard Lucius Malfoy selling dangerous possessions ahead of the Ministry raids. Dracina complained about Harry, and was warned not to seem obsessed with him. Hagrid found Harry and took him back to Diagon Alley. At Gringotts, where Harry was reunited with Hermione and the Weasleys, he saw how little there was in the Weasleys' vault. At Flourish and Blotts, Gilderoy Lockhart pulled Harry into a photograph and announced that he would be teaching Defence Against the Dark Arts. Harry gave his free books to Ginny. Dracina was about to tell Harry something when Ginny stood up for him. Dracina turned and bullied Ginny instead. While Arthur and Lucius brawled, Ginny hurled books at her. Hagrid pulled the fathers apart. Dracina gathered up the spilt books, a small black one among them. She pressed one on Ginny, kept the rest and hissed at Ginny as the Malfoys left.

Chapter 6Due North

Harry spent the rest of the summer at the Burrow, where Molly kept telling him that he need never leave. She had written to Dumbledore to say where Harry would be living from now on, and to condemn him for leaving Harry with the Dursleys for eleven years. On 1 September 1992 Arthur proudly explained the Ford Anglia's many charms. The family was held up by forgotten fireworks, a broom and Ginny's diary. Molly forbade Arthur to fly to London. At King's Cross the barrier sealed itself against Harry and Ron. Harry blamed Dobby and Dracina. He spoke of revenge so violent that it alarmed Ron. Ron flew them to Hogwarts in the car, following the Hogwarts Express due north. But the engine died over the lake. They crashed into the Whomping Willow, and Ron's wand snapped. Harry thought Ron had been crushed, until Ron knocked him clear of a falling branch. The battered car threw out their luggage and fled into the Forbidden Forest. Snape caught them and showed them a Daily Prophet report that Muggles had seen the car. He fetched McGonagall and Dumbledore. They chose not to expel the boys, but they warned them and wrote to their families. McGonagall took no house points, though she gave both boys detentions. They learnt that Ginny had been sorted into Gryffindor. Then the house greeted them as heroes.

Chapter 7Freshly Caught

At breakfast on 2 September 1992 Hermione was full of the vampire lore in Voyages with Vampires: Angelus, William the Bloody, Dracula and the Belmont family. Then Ron received a Howler from his mother, which revealed that Arthur was facing an inquiry at work. Dracina Malfoy came over to Harry as if to tell him something. But when Ginny came near him, Dracina called him an idiot and told him to enjoy his girlfriend. Then she stormed off to berate Crabbe and Goyle. In Herbology, after Lockhart had lectured Harry on seeking publicity, Professor Sprout taught the class to repot Mandrakes, and they met Justin Finch-Fletchley. In Transfiguration Professor McGonagall remembered turning a vault of gold into beetles for a Scottish Muggle colleague, and Ron's damaged wand misfired. In the courtyard Colin Creevey asked Harry for a photograph. Dracina mocked Harry for giving out signed pictures, and Lockhart seized the moment for a double portrait. In Defence Against the Dark Arts Lockhart set a quiz about himself, then let loose Cornish pixies he could not control. Harry beat four of them off Dracina.
