Lockhart left Harry, Ron and Hermione to clear up. Afterwards Dracina sat alone in the wrecked classroom, writing in a small black book.

Chapter 8Some Pretty Thing

Over the next few days Harry dodged Lockhart and was followed everywhere by Colin Creevey, whom he came to like. Ron's wand struck Professor Flitwick and raised a boil. On Saturday Oliver Wood woke Harry at dawn for practice. But the Slytherin team arrived with a note from Snape, and their new Seeker turned out to be Dracina Malfoy. Her father had given the team seven Nimbus Two Thousand and Ones. When Harry asked whether 'some pretty thing' could make up for talent, Dracina blushed and asked whether he thought she was pretty. He said he had meant the brooms, and she thumped him. Hermione stepped in. Dracina called her a Mudblood, and the two girls fought until Harry pulled Dracina away. Ron's attempt to curse Dracina backfired, and he began belching slugs. At Hagrid's hut Ron explained the insult, and the idea of Squibs. Harry urged that all witches and wizards should stand together, whatever their blood. Hermione pledged herself to him, while Hagrid and Ron quietly understood that there was a rivalry over Harry. McGonagall gave out the detentions: Ron would polish trophies with Filch, and Harry would answer Lockhart's fan mail. During his detention Harry heard a cold voice threatening to rip, tear and kill, which Lockhart could not hear.

Chapter 9Black Candles and Horses

October 1992 brought a cold that went round the castle, and Percy forced Pepperup Potion on a peaky Ginny. Harry noticed that Dracina Malfoy looked pale and sleepless. She was writing in a small black book, and seemed to be reading replies. A few days before Hallowe'en, Nearly Headless Nick told Harry that he had been refused entry to the Headless Hunt yet again, and that Dracina had offered him mocking condolences. Filch caught Harry dripping mud and took him to his office, where Harry saw a Kwikspell correspondence course. Then Nick arranged for Peeves to crash a cabinet overhead as a distraction, and Harry got away unpunished. In gratitude Harry agreed to come to Nick's five hundredth Deathday Party, to Hermione's delight and Ron's dismay. On Hallowe'en evening Harry glimpsed Dracina running alone up the marble staircase. At the party the three of them met Brother Aldric, Moaning Myrtle and Peeves. Harry defended Nick in front of everyone against Sir Patrick Delaney-Podmore. As they were leaving, Harry heard the murderous voice again and followed it to the second floor. There they found a message announcing that the Chamber of Secrets had been opened, with Mrs Norris hanging stiff beneath it. Dracina pushed to the front of the gathering crowd and taunted Hermione. Nobody noticed the red stain on her finger. When Harry shielded Hermione, Dracina left muttering under her breath. The only word Harry caught was the last one, 'Mine'.

Chapter 10The Horror Within a Fairy Tale

On Hallowe'en night 1992 Argus Filch found his cat, Mrs Norris, Petrified beneath a message announcing that the Chamber of Secrets had been opened. He accused Harry Potter of killing her. In Gilderoy Lockhart's office Dumbledore examined the cat while Lockhart boasted of curses, African language parasites and a Transylvanian vampire cult. One by one, Professor McGonagall quietly exposed the boasts as lies. She shared a knowing look with Harry, and a wink. Dumbledore declared that Mrs Norris was Petrified, not dead. He took twenty points from Gryffindor after Harry mocked Filch's parentage, refused Snape's suggestion that Harry be dropped from the Quidditch team, and promised a Mandrake cure. Dracina Malfoy waited alone on the stairs to ask whether Harry was hurt. She told him off for standing in front of Hermione as though Dracina were a dragon. Over the following days Ginny Weasley grew distraught, and Justin Finch-Fletchley began avoiding Harry. Dracina tormented Hermione in Potions, then wrote in a small black book and read its reply. Hermione explained to Harry the warring magical cultures of early medieval Britain. She also persuaded Professor Binns to recount the legend of Slytherin's Chamber and its monster. Investigating the corridor, the three of them found scorch marks, fleeing spiders and Moaning Myrtle's bathroom. Percy Weasley took five points from Ron for being there. That night Hermione, convinced that Dracina was the Heir of Slytherin, proposed brewing Polyjuice Potion so that they could question her in the Slytherin common room. Harry guessed which teacher would sign for the recipe.

Chapter 11Rather Like a Princess

After Lockhart had let Cornish pixies loose on his class, Professor McGonagall forbade him in public to bring any creature into a classroom without her written permission. So he turned his lessons into re-enactments of his own exploits, with Harry as his prop. Hermione punctured his story of fighting the vampire called the Master: the Master, she pointed out, had been sealed beneath a Californian town since 1937. Her faith in Lockhart began to fail, though she still flattered him into signing a note for Moste Potente Potions. Dracina confronted Hermione in the library, and went white when Hermione claimed Harry as her own. The three of them studied the Polyjuice recipe in Moaning Myrtle's bathroom. McGonagall privately taught Harry the truth about werewolves, the Garou and the Delirium. At the Gryffindor match against Slytherin, Dean Thomas led a mocking terrace chant. A rogue Bludger hunted Harry. Dracina, by turns taunting, jealous of Hermione and tender, threw her broom in front of the Bludger to shield him. With his right elbow broken, Harry caught the Snitch from just above Dracina's head and crashed into the mud. Then Lockhart removed every bone from his arm. While Madam Pomfrey regrew them with Skele-Gro, a girl who gave no name left sugared violets and a note. Harry assumed they came from Ginny. In the night Dobby came. He admitted that he had sealed the barrier at King's Cross and bewitched the Bludger. He also let slip that the Chamber had been opened before. Then Dumbledore and McGonagall brought in the Petrified Colin Creevey, whose camera had melted inside. Dumbledore declared that the Chamber had been opened once more.

Chapter 12I'll Make You See

Leaving the hospital wing, Harry found Dracina waiting for him, haggard and ink-stained, to see whether his arm had healed. She muttered that someone had said, wrongly, that he would never fly again. Ron and Hermione had begun brewing the Polyjuice Potion in Myrtle's bathroom. Harry told them about Dobby's visit and Colin's Petrification. As panic spread, Dracina asked Ginny, 'Do you love him?', without saying whom she meant. She talked to an invisible Tom at dinner, and signed up to stay at Hogwarts for Christmas, telling McGonagall that she had the most wonderful dreams. In Potions she stirred Harry's Swelling Solution for him while Hermione growled. Harry's firework in Goyle's cauldron covered Hermione's theft of Boomslang skin and Bicorn horn from Snape's stores. At the new Duelling Club Snape paired Harry with Dracina. Their duel went far beyond disarming, until Dracina, exhausted and desperate, conjured a snake with Serpensortia. When Lockhart's bungling sent the snake at Justin Finch-Fletchley, Harry ordered it away in Parseltongue. Dracina gazed at him in rapture, whispering that it was him and always had been. Ron and Hermione explained that Parseltongue was Slytherin's famous gift. The school concluded that Harry was the Heir. The next day Ernie Macmillan accused him in the library. Then Harry, after hearing a girl singing a lullaby in a dark corridor, found Justin and Nearly Headless Nick Petrified. Peeves raised the alarm, and McGonagall took Harry to Dumbledore's office.

Chapter 13Interlude: Precisely When He Means To

On the night of the Duelling Club an old man in grey, who went at present by the name of Ambrose Greyhame, walked up from Hogsmeade with the first snow. He carried a long package wrapped in oilcloth. He remembered helping four quarrelsome young people to found Hogwarts more than a thousand years before. Long before that, he had been sent by the One beyond the golden gates to teach magic to the first frightened families after a great meltwater flood. Unseen, he watched Harry and Dracina duel. In Harry he saw the look of an old friend; in Dracina, the eyes of a prince of the forest folk. He sensed, too, a cold, whispering thing fastened over Dracina's heart, made in the same way as a gold ring he had once known. Peeves fled from him, and the Grey Lady recognised him from her mother's house. He waited all night in Dumbledore's office while Dumbledore was at the Ministry with Cornelius Fudge. The next morning the two old friends talked of the six summers Ambrose had spent teaching the young Albus staff magic, and of Greta Grindelwald, whom Dumbledore still loved. Ambrose handed over the package, a thing once used by Godric that had been broken and remade long ago. Dumbledore confessed his guilt over leaving Harry with the Dursleys. Ambrose insisted that the protection Harry's mother had given him must hold. He warned that Tom Riddle was only a leaf on a far older tree, planted by an ancient enemy. Then he vanished, leaving a smoke-ring ship sailing west. Dumbledore hid the package inside the Sorting Hat just as Justin's attack was discovered and Harry was brought upstairs.

Chapter 14A Yearning for Polyjuice

Left alone in Dumbledore's office, Harry noticed a Muggle portrait of a bald, blue-skinned man in golden armour. Then he put on the Sorting Hat. It told him that Salazar Slytherin had never been evil, and that Harry's mind reminded it most of Slytherin's. Fawkes burst into flame and was reborn. Hagrid stormed in to protest Harry's innocence. Dumbledore said he did not believe Harry guilty, though Harry kept back everything he knew. Panic sent most students home for Christmas. Fred and George mocked the idea of Harry as Heir. Dracina told the school, then Harry himself, that she knew he was the Heir and was on his side. Hermione grew pale and fixated. She muttered in her sleep. After a snowball fight on Christmas Eve, watched from a high window by a lonely fair-haired girl, Harry opened his presents, and Hermione declared the potion ready. That evening the boys drugged Crabbe and Goyle with cakes full of Sleeping Draught. Then Harry, as Goyle, and Ron, as Crabbe, followed Dracina into the Slytherin common room. Hermione had to stay behind, because the hair she had used turned out to be a cat's. Dracina, gravely ill, confided her lost hours, the red on her hands and the comfort of Tom in her diary. She told them of the Ministry raid on Malfoy Manor, and of her father's hints about the last opening of the Chamber, fifty years before. When Pansy mocked Harry, Dracina broke down sobbing, babbling of bars on a window and a house-elf who had misread her order to warn him. Harry took the abandoned diary. It was blank but for a faded name beginning with T and a date fifty years old. He resisted an urge to write in it, and locked it in his trunk.

Chapter 15What's Underneath

On Boxing Day 1992 Madam Pomfrey turned Harry and Ron away from the hospital wing, where Hermione was recovering from her cat-hair Polyjuice transformation. Harry, meanwhile, found himself constantly drawn to Tom Riddle's diary, which he had hidden in his trunk. Without the diary, Dracina Malfoy ransacked the Slytherin dungeon. Then she burst into the Great Hall barefoot, raving that a thief had taken her 'precious'. She scratched a Hufflepuff prefect and beat Harry with her fists. At last Dumbledore calmed her with a touch, and announced that she had Morrigan's Fever. Harry wrote in the diary. It answered him, knew his name and asked whether he had noticed 'what's underneath' Dracina's hostility. When Harry visited Dracina in the hospital wing, she taunted him that the Dursleys starved him. Ron found him afterwards on the Astronomy Tower, and promised that he would spend the summer at the Burrow. Hermione, recovering, admitted that the Polyjuice plan had become a personal crusade against Dracina. She resolved to be 'less a lot', and turned against Lockhart. Moaning Myrtle told them that a posh girl had searched her bathroom at night and whispered at the sinks. Ron caught Harry with the diary and recognised Riddle's name from a trophy. He urged Harry to give it to Dumbledore, which Harry silently decided not to do. After Hermione came back in February, spells failed to reveal what was in the diary, but the three of them found Riddle's name among the Head Boys. On Valentine's Day Lockhart's dwarfs sang Harry two Valentines on the stairs. Dracina briefly got hold of the fallen diary before Percy returned it to Harry. She then savaged Ginny for writing the second song. That night the diary drew Harry into Riddle's memory of 13 June 1943. In it the sixteen-year-old Riddle confronted the young Hagrid over a monster in a box. Harry concluded that Hagrid had opened the Chamber fifty years before.

Chapter 16Whoever Took It

Harry, Ron and Hermione argued over whether Hagrid could be the heir of Slytherin. Harry felt that only Tom Riddle could understand his life with the Dursleys, but he resisted the urge to confide in the diary. Months passed without an attack, while Dracina sickened, grey and silent. At Easter the second-years chose their subjects for the third year. On the eve of the Hufflepuff match Harry's dormitory was ransacked. The diary had been stolen, along with his match scarf. Neville behaved guiltily. Harry realised that his craving for the diary had not been wholly his own. The next morning Dracina appeared radiant and healthy. A pale, ink-stained Ginny tried to tell Harry that she had seen somebody the night before, until Percy interrupted. Harry heard the voice in the walls again, and Hermione ran off to the library. McGonagall then cancelled the match. Hermione and the Ravenclaw prefect Penelope Clearwater, she told them, had been Petrified near the library, with a mirror beside them. Dracina appeared at the door of the hospital wing to offer flat condolences. Harry, sure that she was guilty, punched a wall. Under the strict new rules, Harry and Ron went under the Invisibility Cloak to Hagrid's hut. There Cornelius Fudge took Hagrid off to Azkaban, and Lucius Malfoy delivered an Order of Suspension removing Dumbledore. Dumbledore declared that he would not truly be gone while anyone kept faith with him. Hagrid told the hidden boys to follow the spiders and to feed Fang. Harry's fury set off a burst of accidental magic, until Ron talked him down.

Chapter 17Total Spider Death

With Dumbledore and Hagrid gone, fear settled over Hogwarts. Dracina strutted about the castle, taunting Harry that being locked in and counted must feel like home. Ron reassured Harry that he belonged at the Burrow. Dracina pointedly thanked Neville for being 'such a help'. Percy caught Ginny alone on the second floor, where she claimed to have been 'following' something. In Potions, nearly a month after Dumbledore's suspension, Snape rebuked Dracina in front of the class, in a low, cold voice, for speaking of McGonagall without respect. Later in the lesson Dracina said it was a pity Hermione had not been killed, and Ron held Harry back. When she went on to mock Ginny, Ron had to be held back himself. In Herbology Ernie Macmillan apologised to Harry. Asked whether Dracina was the heir, Harry could only answer 'Maybe'. A line of spiders was seen heading for the Forbidden Forest. That night Harry and Ron took Fang into the Forest. There they met Mr Weasley's Ford Anglia, which had gone feral, before giant spiders carried them off to the hollow of the blind Aragog. Aragog told them that he had never been the monster of the Chamber, and that the girl killed fifty years earlier had been found in a bathroom. Spiders feared the creature too much to name it, he said. Then he gave the boys to his children for food. The car crashed into the hollow and rescued them. Back in bed, Harry realised that the dead girl might still be in her bathroom, as Moaning Myrtle.

Chapter 18Faith Managed

McGonagall announced that the exams would begin on 1 June 1993, with an allusion to friends of hers who had been eaten by Nephilim when she was young. Three days before the exams she announced that the Mandrakes were ready. Ginny again tried to confide in Harry and Ron, but Percy interrupted her. Caught slipping away towards Myrtle's bathroom, Harry disarmed McGonagall's anger with sarcasm. She let him visit Hermione. She also warned him never to go after the creature alone, citing her own encounters with Garou, Wraiths and William the Bloody. In Hermione's fist Harry found a page on the Basilisk with the word 'Pipes' written on it. From it he worked out how the monster moved about, and why its victims had survived. Hidden in a wardrobe in the staff room, he and Ron heard that Ginny had been taken into the Chamber. A Slytherin girl was missing too. The teachers sent Lockhart to face the monster. Finding Lockhart packing to run away, Harry disarmed him. Myrtle described her death, and Harry opened the entrance in the sink with Parseltongue. In the tunnel Lockhart's Memory Charm backfired through Ron's broken wand and brought down the roof. Harry went on alone. In the Chamber he found Dracina collapsing in his stolen scarf, Ginny bleeding, and Tom Riddle's memory taking solid form. Riddle explained Lucius Malfoy's plot, how he had possessed Dracina, and his own plans, then revealed himself as Lord Voldemort. Harry refused Riddle's offer of revenge on the Dursleys, and called him a fraud like Lockhart. The Basilisk was set on him, and its fang caught his arm. But a warm presence and a fatherly voice saved him. Fawkes brought the Sorting Hat, and from it Harry drew an ancient sword. Harry withstood the Basilisk's stare, beheaded it while he stood over Dracina, and destroyed the diary. Then the venom took hold again. He collapsed in Dracina's arms, while a man in white watched him with pride.

Chapter 19The Sign of the Cross

Harry woke unharmed, with his head in Dracina's lap. She healed Ginny's cut. Fawkes carried them up the pipe, with Ron and the memoryless Lockhart. The Weasleys were waiting in McGonagall's office, and so was Dumbledore, who had returned. Harry told the story but left out Dracina's part in it. Dumbledore and Ginny both shielded her. When Dracina broke down and confessed, Harry's hand on her shoulder silenced her. Dumbledore cleared both girls of blame. He awarded Harry and Ron Special Awards for Services to the School, with two hundred points each. He told Harry that his Parseltongue came from Voldemort, that choices define a person, and that the sword was an ancient blade once called the Sword of Gryffindor. Lucius Malfoy arrived with Dobby, and Dumbledore exposed his plot. Harry tricked Lucius into freeing Dobby with a sock. In a private exchange Lucius admitted that he had been 'instructed'. He laughed at Harry's mockery of Voldemort, and said that he was beginning to see what Dracina saw in Harry. In the hospital wing Harry and Dracina agreed to be friends. They found that both of them had seen the man in white; Harry wondered whether he might be Jesus Christ. Molly Weasley warned Dracina never to break Harry's heart. At the feast Hermione was revived. She privately resolved to be Harry's best friend until the time came to deal with Dracina. Hagrid came back, Gryffindor won the House Cup and the exams were cancelled. At the end of term Dumbledore told Harry that he must go back to Privet Drive. Lily Potter's protection, the magic of Elves and of Númenor, lived on in his aunt's blood. Dumbledore had also seen to it in person that the Dursleys would never harm Harry again. On the train Ginny revealed that Percy was secretly going out with Penelope Clearwater. At King's Cross Harry made the sign of the Cross for the first time.

How it differs from the original

  • Lucius always meant the diary for Ginny, but Dracina swept it into her own bag at Flourish and Blotts in a temper, and he did not know his daughter had it.
  • Dracina, not Ginny, is possessed by Riddle; she opens the Chamber, sets the Basilisk on Muggle-borns and writes on the walls without remembering.
  • Riddle petrifies Hermione deliberately as a gift to Dracina.
  • Both Dracina and Ginny are taken into the Chamber; Riddle drains Ginny instead of Dracina.
  • The diary passes from Dracina to Harry, who steals it while Polyjuiced as Goyle, and back to Dracina when Neville lets her into Gryffindor Tower.
  • Dracina is never punished; Dumbledore covers her breakdown as Morrigan's Fever, and Ginny covers for her.
  • Dracina sent Dobby to warn Harry, and Dobby told her about the bars, cupboard and bread.
  • Harry is rescued from Privet Drive in a far worse state, starved behind bars, and collapses at the Burrow; Molly takes him in and writes to Dumbledore condemning him.
  • The Burrow clock has one hand and no numbers, and the Weasleys keep a ghoul fed on gnomes.
  • Hermione is obsessed with vampire lore from Lockhart's books and catches him out over the Master.
  • Dracina sends Harry anonymous sugared violets in the hospital wing, and he assumes Ginny sent them.
  • Harry receives two singing Valentines, Dracina's and Ginny's, and Lockhart winks at Harry and Dracina.
  • Harry's detention is Lockhart's fan mail and Ron's the trophy room.
  • A wholly new Interlude has Ambrose Greyhame, implied to be Gandalf and Merlin, visit Dumbledore.
  • The sword from the Hat is not Gryffindor's by origin, but an older blade broken and reforged.
  • Harry is bitten, dies briefly, and is healed by a voice in the dark before Fawkes arrives; a man in white, Jesus Christ, watches by a pillar and Dracina sees him too.
  • Lucius ends the book half-liking Harry.
  • Dumbledore personally visits Privet Drive and threatens the Dursleys.
  • Hermione and Dracina each resolve to deal with the other, and Molly threatens to kill Dracina slowly if she hurts Harry.
  • Harry makes the sign of the Cross on the last page.
  • Harry baits the Dursleys on purpose, and calls them 'malignant'.
  • Harry keeps thinking about Dracina Malfoy, and the twinkle in her eyes.
  • Harry threatens to turn the hedge into an Ent, instead of setting it on fire.
  • Dobby says his Mistress wanted Harry to be warned.
  • Harry calls Dobby 'mate' and threatens him. He vows to kill Dobby.
  • Dracina appears in Harry's dream of the zoo.
  • Harry fights Vernon off in a rage, and hurls insults at him as they fly away.
  • Ron learns that Harry was starved, and Harry hints at the cupboard.
  • Percy's odd behaviour is tied to a statue Charlie gave him, which Molly confiscated.
  • The cursed tea set once belonged to a French nobleman who had himself been under a curse, and to his peasant wife.
  • A wholly new chapter, in which Harry tells Molly Weasley about his abuse and she comforts him.
  • Molly invites Harry to stay for as long as he wants.
  • Dracina and Lucius appear in Borgin and Burkes, not Draco. Lucius warns her about seeming obsessed with Harry, and mutters about 'Cissy'.
  • Ginny stands up to Dracina, and the two girls fight over the books.
  • Dracina, not Lucius, handles the books, and keeps a small black book for herself.
  • Hermione is jealous at the idea of Dracina talking about Harry.
  • Molly writes to Dumbledore to tell him, in terms that leave no room for argument, where Harry will live from now on. She also condemns his decision to leave Harry with the Dursleys.
  • Ginny has a diary of her own, which she leaves on her bed.
  • Ron now distrusts Dumbledore, while Harry reveres him.
  • The fight with the Whomping Willow is longer, and Ron saves Harry.
  • Hermione's book describes vampires and vampire hunters who never appear in the original.
  • McGonagall hints at past work alongside a Scottish Muggle agent.
  • Harry rescues Dracina from the pixies, and she writes in a small black book.
  • Dracina is the Slytherin Seeker, and the 'pretty thing' exchange is new.
  • Hermione and Dracina come to blows on the pitch.
  • Harry makes a speech about wizarding unity, and Hermione pledges herself to him.
  • Dracina shows signs of the black book's influence, and it is implied that she painted the message.
  • Harry openly tells Sir Patrick to leave, and defends Nick.
  • Hermione interviews ghosts such as Brother Aldric, and clings to Harry at the scene.
  • Dracina whispers, 'Mine.'
  • McGonagall openly catches Lockhart in one lie after another during the inquiry over Mrs Norris.
  • Harry, not Ron, makes the cutting remark about Filch's birth. He loses twenty points and apologises.
  • Dracina carries the black diary and writes in it. She waits on the stairs to make sure that Harry is unhurt.
  • Hermione writes Harry's essays for him, and pushes the Polyjuice plan out of personal animosity towards Dracina.
  • Hogwarts is dated to 990, and Hermione describes four rival magical cultures of early medieval Britain.
  • McGonagall bans Lockhart from bringing creatures into lessons after the business with the pixies.
  • Lockhart's anecdotes take in vampires, the Master, Angelus and the Slayer. Hermione exposes him in class.
  • McGonagall teaches Harry practical werewolf lore, and warns him about the Garou.
  • Dean Thomas leads football chants from the Gryffindor stand.
  • Dracina blocks the Bludger on purpose to protect Harry, and secretly leaves him sugared violets.
  • Dobby says that his mistress gave him an order, then punished him over the barrier.
  • Dracina, plainly under the diary's influence, holds the place that Ginny holds in the original.
  • Snape pairs Harry with Dracina. She casts Serpensortia after a far more violent duel.
  • Snape turns grey with recognition as he watches Dracina, and mutters about a foolish girl.
  • Dracina asks Ginny whether she loves him, without saying whom she means, and records it in the diary.
  • Harry hears a girl singing a lullaby just before he finds Justin and Nick.
  • A wholly original chapter, in which Gandalf visits Hogwarts as Ambrose Greyhame.
  • Gandalf is revealed as the guide who brought the four founders together. He also taught Dumbledore and Grindelwald staff magic.
  • Grindelwald is a woman, Greta, whom Dumbledore loved.
  • Gryffindor's sword is brought to Hogwarts from outside and hidden in the Sorting Hat.
  • A portrait, implied to be of Zordon, hangs in Dumbledore's office.
  • The Sorting Hat defends Salazar Slytherin at length.
  • Dracina believes Harry is the Heir. She is sick and losing time because of the diary.
  • Harry takes the diary from the Slytherin common room, instead of finding it in Myrtle's bathroom.
  • Dracina's order to Dobby was to warn Harry, and Dobby misread it.
  • Dracina Malfoy, not Ginny Weasley, has been writing in the diary. Her withdrawal from it brings on a public breakdown, which Dumbledore covers up as 'Morrigan's Fever'.
  • The diary talks to Harry about Dracina, and urges him to be kinder to her.
  • Hermione comes out of her Polyjuice mishap humbled, and resolves to change her ways.
  • The first singing Valentine is implied to be Dracina's. Percy, not Harry, gets the diary back from her.
  • The diary is stolen back by Dracina, with Neville's help, not by Ginny.
  • Ginny is shown trying to warn Harry about what she has seen, not confessing her own guilt.
  • Harry's rage in Hagrid's hut sets off accidental magic.
  • Snape publicly rebukes Dracina for disrespecting McGonagall.
  • Dracina thanks Neville, which hints at his part in the theft.
  • The narration states that God brightened the moon for Harry at the moment of his realisation.
  • Dracina, not Ginny, is the possessed girl lying in the Chamber; Ginny was taken after tracking her.
  • McGonagall reveals a past spent fighting Garou, Wraiths and William the Bloody.
  • Riddle speaks of a 'union' between the bloodlines of Potter and Malfoy. He speaks too of Lily Potter's ancient lineage.
  • The sword is neither jewelled nor named, and bursts into white fire. Harry is saved by a divine presence, not by phoenix tears.
  • A man in white, later suggested to be Jesus Christ, appears in the Chamber.
  • Dracina, not Ginny, is the one cleared and comforted. Harry and Dracina become friends.
  • Lucius Malfoy reveals that he was coerced, laughs at Harry, and leaves with grudging respect.
  • Dumbledore puts Lily Potter's protection down to the magic of Elves and Númenor. He has also confronted the Dursleys himself.
  • Harry is sent back to Privet Drive in spite of the Weasleys' offer, and the book ends with him making the sign of the Cross.

Characters introduced

  • Aragog
  • Colin Creevey
  • Cornelius Fudge
  • Dobby
  • Fawkes
  • Gandalf
  • Gilderoy Lockhart
  • God
  • Jesus Christ
  • Marjorie Dursley
  • Moaning Myrtle

pages.title: Harry Potter and the Imprisoned Girl
pages.html:
Front page · The Books

Harry Potter and the Imprisoned Girl

Book Three of the Malfoid Saga · 1993 to 1994 · Complete

Read Book ThreeFree at malfoid.lol

Chapters

InterludeThe Morgoth in the Details

On a rainy night in the summer of 1993, the night Harry Potter fled Privet Drive, John Constantine flagged down the Knight Bus in Liverpool. In a Tesco carrier bag he had a D'ni linking book marked Myst. The conductor, Stan Shunpike, kept stopping him from smoking. Constantine thought back to 1985, when he had stolen Dumbledore's Deluminator to defeat a demon that fed on light. Dumbledore was still livid about it. Now a letter had come from him in green ink, demanding that Constantine fetch the book from Ephraim Shacklewell in New Mexico. In memory he went back over his years at Hogwarts. They began in 1964, when he made friends with a stammering Lucius Malfoy before both of them were sorted into Slytherin. As a Muggle-born he was bullied relentlessly. He took clever revenges, he cheated, and he watched Lucius drift towards the future Death Eaters. It all ended in their seventh year, in a duel and then a fistfight over a Ravenclaw girl. He remembered burgling Shacklewell House without his wand. He had used salt, chalk, the seal of Andromalius, a backwards Lord's Prayer and a Hand of Glory. When the book fell open he had nearly been drawn into it. He had bluffed the sleepless Shacklewell with an enchanted library card, along with a receipt signed J. Lennon. On the bus he watched a boy get on at Magnolia Crescent who claimed to be Neville Longbottom. Constantine recognised the signs of abuse in him. He saw the Minister for Magic meet the boy at the Leaky Cauldron. There the boy, who was Harry Potter, called himself Barry Trotter. At a nearly empty Hogwarts Hagrid greeted Constantine joyfully, and the password Acid Pop let him into Dumbledore's office. Dumbledore had been expecting him. He lost his temper and began to echo Greta Grindelwald's words about the greater good. Then he stopped, horrified, and confessed his own regrets. He explained that the book belonged to a very old acquaintance, who had written it. A second small leather book led from that writer's island back to this world. As for the burglary, Dumbledore called it a kindness.

Chapter 1The Man Outside the Church

By late July 1993, five weeks into the summer after his second year, Harry Potter had noticed that the Dursleys had stopped hitting him. Every evening, after a strange twitch that seized both of them at once, they set a plate for him at dinner. It was the work of a visit Albus Dumbledore had paid to Privet Drive, though nobody had explained it to Harry. Harry brooded over the Chamber of Secrets. A voice there had told him that his work was not yet done, and he had seen a man in a white robe by a fallen pillar. Dracina Malfoy had seen the man too, and Harry was almost sure he had been Jesus Christ. Dumbledore had said that his mother's protection was the magic of Elves and of Númenor, so Harry was reading Dudley's unwanted copy of The Lord of the Rings. Ron had telephoned early in the holidays and been bellowed at by Uncle Vernon; nobody had written since. On his fourth visit to St Michael's Church in Magnolia Crescent, Harry met a very tall old man on the bench by the lych-gate, who had been counting his visits. The old man told him the door was open. When Harry looked back, he was gone. At midnight on 31 July Harry turned thirteen, and four owls arrived. Hedwig brought Hermione's present from Brittany, a Broomstick Servicing Kit. Errol brought Ron's Pocket Sneakoscope, with a cutting from the Daily Prophet about the Weasleys winning seven hundred Galleons and going to Egypt. A school owl brought Hagrid's present, a Monster Book of Monsters that bit, along with the Hogsmeade permission form. Last came Ganymede, Narcissa Malfoy's eagle owl, carrying a scented letter from Dracina tied with a green ribbon. The letter denied any affection whatever and promised Harry a present in person. It let slip that Lucius had forbidden her to have anything to do with him, and that Narcissa had helped her all the same. It also offered, should Uncle Vernon have been mistreating Harry, to try a few items from her father's cellar collection on him. Harry kept the ribbon in his pyjama pocket. For the first time in his life, he was glad it was his birthday.

Chapter 2Blood of Elves, Rage of Man

On the morning of 31 July 1993 the Dursleys' new kitchen television carried the news of Sirius Black's escape. It also reported that New Delhi had fallen to Khan Noonien Singh, the genetically engineered warlord. Neither the Avengers nor the Justice League would intervene without a mandate from the United Nations. Uncle Vernon announced that his sister Marge was coming to stay for a week, and that Harry was to pretend he attended St Brutus's Secure Centre for Incurably Criminal Boys. Then a British National Party membership card fell out of Uncle Vernon's wallet. Harry blackmailed him with it, threatening to reveal it unless Vernon agreed to sign his Hogsmeade form. Vernon agreed, visibly choking back his rage, and muttered about Dumbledore's threats. Harry sent Hedwig off to Egypt with Errol. Dudley, meanwhile, watched the Power Rangers fight a giant creature in Birmingham with rapt admiration. Aunt Marge arrived ranting about immigrants. Harry played the part of a dull-witted boy who said 'nuffink'. On the second night he overheard Vernon and Petunia whispering. Dumbledore, it seemed, had sat on their sofa and promised that he would know the moment they used a hand or a word against Harry. When Marge compared Lily to a defective bitch in dog breeding, Harry's anger made her wineglass explode. On the last evening she called James an unemployed drunk who had died in a car crash, and Harry's rage inflated her until she floated up against the ceiling. Harry grabbed his things. He held Uncle Vernon off at wandpoint, while Aunt Petunia begged her husband not to move. Then he walked out of the house, hating Muggles.

Chapter 3The Dog in the Dark

Harry dragged his trunk as far as Magnolia Crescent, furious with the Dursleys, with Marge, with Muggles and with himself. Then it came to him that the Ministry would snap his wand, and he panicked. He was searching for his Invisibility Cloak, meaning to fly to London, when he sensed that something was there. He lit his wand. An enormous black dog was standing in a gap between a garage and a fence. Harry fell backwards into the gutter, and the Knight Bus very nearly ran him over. He gave the conductor, Stan Shunpike, the name Neville Longbottom. All night he rode through the dark, past a dishevelled Liverpudlian in a raincoat who was guarding a glowing book in a carrier bag. In the Daily Prophet he read that twelve years earlier Sirius Black had killed thirteen people with a single curse. At the Leaky Cauldron Cornelius Fudge was waiting for him. Over tea and crumpets the Minister told him that Marge had been punctured. Her memory had been modified, and Harry, Fudge insisted, would not be punished. He gave Harry room eleven, on condition that he stayed in Diagon Alley and was back indoors before dark. Harry flattered him with a technique he had copied from Hermione, but it did him no good: Fudge refused to sign his Hogsmeade form. Harry realised afterwards that he had been expertly handled. Hedwig was waiting in his room. She had arrived only minutes after he had.

Chapter 4Two Parts of Himself

Harry spent the rest of August at the Leaky Cauldron, wrestling all the while with a growing anger at Muggles. In the end he decided that there were two of him: an angry boy from the cupboard and a boy from the Chamber who wanted to protect good things. Tom the landlord warned him that grudges weigh on the one who carries them. Florean Fortescue told him that most witch-burners had simply been frightened people. Harry admired the new Firebolt without buying it, and Madam Malkin measured him for robes. A black dog on the cover of a book of death omens chilled him. Near Knockturn Alley he met Lucius Malfoy, who complained that Dracina talked about Harry incessantly. When Lucius heard what Marge had said of Lily, his anger turned to cold menace. It turned out that he had never heard of Khan, Superman or Spider-Man. This convinced Harry that the wizarding world had no idea superhumans existed. Lucius urged him to stop living as though he were a Muggle, and Harry found himself nodding. Then he argued back that Muggle heroes saved people, just as he had gone down the pipe for Dracina. Lucius flared with anger. After that, fear crossed his face, followed by a sly grin. Harry had begun to doubt his vision of Christ. Then he found The Lord of the Rings lying in his trunk in a ray of sunlight, and began to read it properly. On 31 August he was reunited with Ron and Hermione. Hermione bought Crookshanks, and the Weasleys arrived. That night Harry overheard Arthur Weasley telling his wife that Sirius Black had escaped to kill him.

Chapter 5A Long, Slow Breath

On 1 September 1993 Ministry cars drove the Weasleys, Harry and Hermione to King's Cross. There Mr Weasley made Harry promise not to go looking for Sirius Black. Harry, Ron and Hermione shared a compartment with a sleeping Professor R. J. Lupin, whose presence unsettled Crookshanks. Dracina Malfoy turned up with Crabbe and Goyle behind her. She insulted Ron for form's sake, then signalled silently to Harry that it was all an act. In private she relished their secret and burned with jealousy of Hermione. She meant to arrange matters, one careful step at a time, until Harry looked up one day to find that what he wanted had been beside him all along. When a Dementor boarded the stopped train, Harry collapsed, hearing screams. Hermione held him. Lupin drove the creature off and handed round chocolate. At the carriages Dracina pressed a box into Harry's hands, and Lupin noticed her with interest. Professor McGonagall and Madam Pomfrey looked Harry over in an office that held a horrible stuffed creature. Hermione had a private word with McGonagall about her timetable. At the feast Dumbledore announced that Dementors were stationed at every entrance to the grounds. He also announced two appointments: Lupin to teach Defence Against the Dark Arts, and Hagrid to teach Care of Magical Creatures. Ron sat silently resenting Dumbledore for sending Harry back to the Dursleys. In bed Harry opened Dracina's box. Inside were a dozen chocolate violets, decorated by hand, with a card that read 'Not from Ginny'.

Chapter 6The Knight and the Hippogriff

At breakfast on 2 September 1993 Dracina mocked Harry's faint for the benefit of the Slytherins, but the joke went out of her the moment she saw him. Fred and George then told Harry that she had burst into their compartment during the Dementor attack, demanding that somebody fetch him. She went on to mimic Hermione, and implied that Hermione's people had stolen their magic. Sir Cadogan, after a comic exchange with Harry, guided the three of them to Professor Trelawney's tower. There Harry asked whether signs could be sent by somebody, and was mocked for his Muggle superstition. Hermione defended him. Then Trelawney saw the Grim in his teacup. McGonagall waved away Trelawney's annual death predictions. Ron and Hermione quarrelled over Grims, then over Arithmancy. In Care of Magical Creatures, Dracina's hair ribbons had mysteriously turned Gryffindor scarlet and gold. Harry bowed to the hippogriff Buckbeak and rode him over the lake. Buckbeak slashed Dracina's arm when she insulted him. Harry caught her. At her demand he nearly drew his wand on Buckbeak, until Hagrid stopped him. That evening Hermione explained why the wizarding world hated Christianity. The three of them found Hagrid drunk and despairing. Lupin watched them as they walked back up to the castle. Harry sneaked off to the hospital wing to rebuke Dracina for her cruelty. The rebuke provoked a furious, tearful outburst about Hermione and his indifference. Madam Pomfrey threw him out. Afterwards Dracina resolved to have her father ruin Hagrid and Buckbeak.

Chapter 7It Came Out of the Wardrobe

Dracina Malfoy spent a week in the hospital wing after Buckbeak's attack. Harry hovered outside the door, unable to decide how to apologise. She came back for double Potions on a Thursday, with her arm in a black silk sling, and sat down beside him. She had Harry prepare her Shrinking Solution, passing on potion tricks wrapped in insults, until he snapped that they could not be friends while she abused his friends. Their quarrel boiled both cauldrons over. Snape quelled them, docked both houses ten points and warned them that friendships had ended over a single word. Dracina apologised. She said she had decided not to send a four-page complaint to her father after all. When Seamus reported a Muggle sighting of Sirius Black, Dracina urged Harry to hunt Black down himself. After the lesson her heirloom serpent brooch went missing. For a short while nobody knew where Hermione was. When she reappeared she smelt of dittany. Then she dropped something silver and green. The brooch turned up on Peeves's bow tie, where it stayed until Lupin's Waddiwasi sent it flying into a fire bucket. In the staffroom Lupin introduced the class to a boggart. Neville dressed the boggart Snape in his grandmother's clothes. Dracina's boggart was her father, telling her that she was always second and not a real Malfoy. It made her weep, before she defied it and turned it into a drunken tramp. Lupin kept the boggart away from Harry. When it came back at Lupin himself, as a vast, blood-soaked werewolf that seemed to know him, he faced it and shrank its legs. Afterwards Hermione and Dracina each seized one of Harry's arms, growling at each other. Harry was left baffled. Ron resolved to keep an eye on both girls.

Chapter 8The Lady Who Wasn't There

Lupin's lessons on Red Caps, kappas and vampires quickly became the most popular in the school. The one on vampires covered the Masquerade, the Sabbat, the clans and the blood bond. It also covered the Camarilla's agreement with the Ministry and the world's other wizarding governments, made in 1900. Dracina began a campaign of public kindness. She helped Neville. She even greeted Ron and Hermione civilly, though Ron noticed that it only ever happened when Harry was looking. Hermione would have none of it. Oliver Wood held a desperate team meeting before his last season, and the first Hogsmeade visit was announced for Halloween. Crookshanks went for Ron's bag to get at Scabbers, which soured things between Ron and Hermione. Hermione also tactlessly questioned Lavender's belief that Professor Trelawney had foretold the death of her rabbit, Binky, on 16 October. In Transfiguration McGonagall described parasites that possess a host along the spine. She revealed that she had once killed one herself, with the help of a man she did not name. Then she refused Harry permission to go to Hogsmeade. On Halloween Dracina silenced Pansy and Daphne's taunts. She told Harry about a quill shop she had meant to show him. Over tea in his office, Lupin learnt that what Harry feared most was the Dementors, and drank a smoking potion that Snape brought him. At the feast Lupin flinched at a moon, nearly full, in the enchanted ceiling. Afterwards Hermione promised Harry that she would try to be nicer to Dracina. When the students got back to Gryffindor Tower, they found the Fat Lady's portrait slashed. Peeves told Dumbledore that Sirius Black had done it. Lupin, meanwhile, stood breathing in the air, as though he recognised a scent.

Chapter 9A Soft Answer

On Halloween night the whole school slept in the Great Hall. Dracina and Hermione bedded down on either side of Harry. Dracina told him that everybody in the castle slept better that night because Dumbledore was awake, while nobody had ever been awake for Harry. She admitted that her own childhood had been pampered. She had begun to confess something about the diary when Percy interrupted. Harry overheard Snape suggest to Dumbledore that Black had had help from inside the castle. Sir Cadogan took the Fat Lady's place. Percy and the staff shadowed Harry. Aunt Petunia wrote to him for the first time in his life, to forbid him to come home for Christmas. In a disused corridor on the fourth floor Harry met a painted man at a smouldering altar, who resented his brother's accepted offering. The painted man told Harry to mind the door-sill. McGonagall restricted Harry's movements but kept his Quidditch practices going under supervision. Hermione began a dogged campaign of courtesy towards Dracina, and Dracina stepped up her own in return. Slytherin pulled out of the opening match, citing Dracina's arm, so Gryffindor had to play Hufflepuff in a storm. On the path Dracina cowed her own team when they hissed at her for laughing with Harry. Hermione told Harry and Ron the history of the vampire Angelus. Snape, covering for Lupin, lectured the class on the Garou and humiliated Hermione. Harry would have had it out with him, but the Fat Friar's story of a shepherd turned aside from vengeance by a soft answer stopped him. At the match Harry glimpsed a huge black dog in the stands. Then more than a hundred Dementors flooded on to the pitch. Harry heard his mother pleading, and fell fifty feet. Dumbledore slowed his fall and drove the Dementors off. Cedric Diggory caught the Snitch. The Whomping Willow smashed Harry's Nimbus. After hours Dracina came to the ward. She had written to her father about the Dementors, she said, and nobody was permitted to kill Harry.

Chapter 10Rain Coming

Harry was kept in the hospital wing, where he refused to give up the splinters of his Nimbus. Hagrid, Ginny and the Quidditch team came to see him. Dracina paid a formal call with her entourage. Throughout it Pansy stared at the bedside table where Dracina's four-page letter had once lain, for it was Pansy herself who had taken the letter to the Owlery. That night Harry dreamt of revenge on the Dursleys. The painted man from the fourth-floor corridor watched him, until a beam of light burnt the watcher away. Back in lessons, Dracina, without her sling now, mimicked a Dementor and Harry's fall in Potions. Ron threw a crocodile heart into her face. Lupin returned. He cancelled Snape's essay, and agreed to teach Harry a defence against the Dementors after the holidays. When Harry described his dream, Lupin nearly lost control of himself. He told Harry to seek God, or at least a priest. Gryffindor's hopes revived when Ravenclaw beat Hufflepuff. Wood drove the team hard, telling Harry that he would be captain one day. Hermione and Dracina both took to watching practices, trading barbs. On the last Hogsmeade weekend before Christmas Fred and George gave Harry the Marauder's Map. He reached Honeydukes by the passage behind the one-eyed witch. In the Three Broomsticks Hermione told him she believed Dracina's attachment to him was possessive, and admitted her own jealousy. Then, hidden behind a Christmas tree, Harry heard McGonagall, Flitwick, Hagrid, Fudge and Madam Rosmerta talking. Sirius Black, they said, had been his father's best friend, his best man and Harry's own godfather. He had betrayed the Potters as their Secret-Keeper. He had handed Hagrid the motorbike that carried Harry away, then killed Peter Pettigrew in a street full of Muggles.

Chapter 11The Best Man

Harry went back to the castle in a daze. He found his parents' wedding photograph, and recognised Sirius Black as the laughing best man. In the dark he resolved to make Black pay. On the last morning of term Ron and Hermione begged him not to go after Black. Ron insisted that the Weasleys were his family, but Harry would not have it, because the blood protection tied him to Privet Drive. He shouted in Dumbledore's defence. Then he broke down, weeping about his childhood, while Hermione held him. When they went down to Hagrid's, they found him distraught over a letter from the Ministry. Lucius Malfoy's complaint had been upheld. Buckbeak was to face the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures on 20 April. Harry concluded that Dracina had lied about dropping her complaint. He threw himself into legal research for Buckbeak's defence. On Christmas morning he received a Weasley jumper and an anonymous Firebolt. Crookshanks went for Scabbers, which set off the Pocket Sneakoscope. At Christmas lunch Trelawney fretted about sitting down thirteen at table. Dumbledore said that Lupin was unwell, though he seemed worried by his absence. McGonagall told the story of a mission in Siberia in 1966, and of the rules taught her by her partner, whom she did not name. Above all, she said, the hard part was learning to put a weapon down. Afterwards Hermione reported the Firebolt to McGonagall, who confiscated it so that it could be tested for jinxes. Hermione told Ron that she believed Sirius Black had sent it.

Chapter 12A Single Happy Thing

Harry refused to speak to Hermione over the confiscated Firebolt. He apologised to Oliver Wood for losing it, and Wood told him that he did not have to carry the whole team on his back. When term began again in January 1994, Lupin started teaching Harry the Patronus Charm in the History of Magic classroom. He used a boggart that turned into a Dementor. The charm, Lupin explained, ran on light derived from God meeting a good soul. Harry privately doubted that he was good. He collapsed twice, hearing first his mother die and then, for the first time, his father. In the end he produced a large silver shield, though it had no shape. Lupin admitted that he had been James's friend and had known Sirius Black. He told Harry that Lily had believed in Christ with all her heart. Prompted by Mrs Weasley's letters, the Weasleys quietly organised themselves to keep watch over Harry. Slytherin beat Ravenclaw, with Dracina as Seeker. A Ministry letter had convinced Harry that she had lied about not sending a complaint about Buckbeak. Four times he tried to confront her, and four times he was stopped by something to do with faith, proof or forgiveness. A Hufflepuff fell through the ice on the lake. Two first-years tested a healed wound. Flitwick shamed Hobday over two Sickles, having secretly paid Hobday's own nine-Galleon debt. A Ravenclaw tested a fleece twice. Harry accepted Dracina's spare broom, a Nimbus Two Thousand and One. Lupin explained the Dementor's Kiss, which the Ministry had licensed for use on Black. Harry said Black deserved it. Lupin urged him to remember that nobody was beyond forgiveness. McGonagall gave back the Firebolt. Harry hugged her, then sent Dracina's broom back to her. He and Ron resolved to make peace with Hermione. Then Ron found that Scabbers had gone. There was blood on his bedsheet, with ginger hairs in it.

Chapter 13What the Hood Was Hiding

Ron and Hermione fell out bitterly over Scabbers. Isolated and overworked, Hermione began to frighten Harry with a cold, patient menace towards anyone who crossed her. At practice Madam Hooch admired the Firebolt. Wood warned them that Ravenclaw's Seeker was Cho Chang. Afterwards Ron had a go on the broom, and Harry mistook Crookshanks's eyes in a tree for the black dog. At breakfast Cedric Diggory apologised for his win in November. Percy let slip a ten-Galleon bet with Penelope Clearwater. Dracina taunted Harry in public, though Harry could see that she was privately frightened for him. In the match in early March Gryffindor were trailing 40 to 10 when Wood called a time-out. In the huddle Harry gave the tactical orders that turned the game round. When three hooded figures appeared below him, he cast a solid Patronus without a moment's hesitation, then caught the Snitch for a win of 230 to 70. The figures were Dracina, Crabbe, Goyle and Marcus Flint, in rigged robes. McGonagall gave them detention, taking fifty points from Slytherin besides. Harry felt betrayed. He turned his back on Dracina, who was plainly guilty. Lupin told him afterwards that his Patronus had been 'bright'. He also said that he recognised Harry's habit of hiding his feelings behind a blank face. At the victory party Harry told Hermione that she had been right about Dracina. Then a careless remark of Ron's sent her away in tears. That night Ron woke to find Sirius Black slashing his bed curtains with a knife, and punched him in the face. Sir Cadogan revealed that he had let Black in because Black had a written list of the week's passwords. Neville had lost it.

Chapter 14What She Deserved

After Black's escape the castle tightened its defences. Sir Cadogan was sacked. The Fat Lady, mended, came back under the guard of security trolls. Neville was banned from Hogsmeade for the rest of his schooling, and his grandmother sent him a Howler. A letter from Lucius Malfoy distressed Dracina. She spent the following week trying to make Harry listen to her, while he ignored her and burnt her notes unread. Hagrid revealed that Buckbeak's hearing had been brought forward at Lucius Malfoy's urging. He reproached Harry and Ron for neglecting Hermione. In his Thursday lesson Harry produced a Patronus that moved, and Lupin told him the teaching about forgiving seventy times seven. Afterwards Dracina ambushed Harry in a dark corridor, until Lupin interrupted. On the next Hogsmeade Saturday Harry went under the Invisibility Cloak. By the Shrieking Shack he pelted Dracina, Crabbe and Goyle with mud. Then the Cloak slipped, and he was seen. Frightened for his safety, Dracina ran to Snape. There she confessed everything. Her team had pressured her into the fake-Dementor stunt, and she had stood ready to catch Harry with Arresto Momentum. She had written the letter about Buckbeak but never sent it. She believed she deserved the mud. Snape told her that she still had a chance to do something, rather than merely say something. Then he interrogated Harry, mocking James Potter. He confiscated the Marauder's Map, which insulted him. Lupin, summoned by Floo, covered for Harry, though he was visibly fighting something bestial in himself. Afterwards he reproached Harry for gambling with his parents' sacrifice. Hermione met them with the news that Hagrid had lost. Buckbeak was to be executed.

Chapter 15Seventy Times Seven

Ron forgave Hermione first, and she apologised for Scabbers. It set Harry thinking about letting go of a grievance, even when he was in the right. After Care of Magical Creatures, Dracina accused Hermione of stealing her letter. When Dracina began a slur implying that Hermione was Jewish, Hermione punched her. The two of them fought on the castle steps until Harry and Ron pulled them apart. Dracina begged Harry to believe her. Remembering Lupin's teaching, Harry chose to embrace her and accept her account. She vowed to put everything right. Hermione denied any wrongdoing. She missed Charms for no reason anyone could see, and later walked out of Divination for good after Harry challenged Professor Trelawney's contempt for Christianity. On Hermione's advice Harry sought out the Fat Friar. The Friar told him that wizards and the Church had once lived in harmony. He told how the witch-hunts had grown, and spoke of an old man who had taught the early students of Hogwarts that magic was a gift from God. When Harry told him about seeing Jesus in the Chamber of Secrets, the Friar said that he believed him. Over the Easter holidays Dracina secretly borrowed books on hippogriffs, practised bowing to a suit of armour and gave Harry an Easter egg she had made by hand. Hermione grew more possessive of him. The night before the final Harry saw the black dog walking with Crookshanks. The final against Slytherin was vicious. Harry caught the Snitch, winning Gryffindor the Quidditch Cup. Only afterwards did he realise that Dracina had let him win on purpose, as an apology.

Chapter 16An Act of God

As the exams drew near, Ron told Harry about Percy's plans for a regulated 'fair and orderly society'. Harry remarked that a Minister was not what was needed to put things right. Many years later, when half the wizarding world had learnt to do as Harry told them, he would remember that conversation. Hermione's impossible timetable ended in a breakdown at two in the morning. Ron looked after her with evident, growing feeling. Twice Hermione was tempted to use the small golden object on her chain against Dracina. During a last flare-up of the house feud Harry hid the Invisibility Cloak down the one-eyed witch's chute. From then on Snape guarded the chute. Hagrid's appeal was fixed for the last day of the exams. Dracina avoided Harry, though she secretly helped him in the Potions exam. She also studied the ground between Hagrid's cabin and the Forest. In the Defence Against the Dark Arts exam Hermione's boggart was McGonagall, telling her she had failed. It led to a bitter exchange with Dracina, which Lupin broke up. On the front steps Harry flattered Cornelius Fudge. He also saw the executioner, Walden Macnair. At the sight of him Dracina fled. At the end of Harry's Divination exam Professor Trelawney fell into a trance. She prophesied that the Dark Lord's servant would break free that night. Hagrid lost the appeal. Hermione fetched the Cloak, and the three of them went down to see Hagrid. They found Scabbers alive in a milk jug, then left. At sunset the axe fell. But Buckbeak had broken loose, and he flew off into the Forest carrying a hooded rider, who waved to the castle. Hagrid cheered. Harry called it an act of God.

Chapter 17Wrath

After Buckbeak's escape Harry, Ron and Hermione stayed hidden under the Invisibility Cloak. They watched Walden Macnair rage in Hagrid's pumpkin patch, until Hagrid threw him into the pumpkins for insulting his giant mother. Hermione quietly remarked that Dracina Malfoy had not been at dinner. Scabbers broke free of Ron's pocket as Crookshanks stalked them. A huge black dog knocked Harry down, then dragged Ron by the arm under the Whomping Willow, snapping his leg on a root. Crookshanks froze the Willow by pressing a knot on its trunk. Harry and Hermione followed the tunnel to the Shrieking Shack, where old claw marks were gouged through the plaster to the brick. Upstairs Ron warned them that the dog was an Animagus. Then Sirius Black disarmed them. Harry went for Black with his bare hands, screaming about the cupboard under the stairs and about his parents. Black wore a crude wooden cross. He never struck back, only muttered that it was his fault. When Black's hand closed on Harry's throat, Hermione attacked him savagely. Harry got his wand back, but he could not bring himself to kill Black while Crookshanks lay across Black's chest. Remus Lupin burst in, disarmed them all and embraced Black. Then he admitted that he was a Garou, as Hermione had worked out from Snape's essay. He was also Moony, one of the makers of the Marauder's Map. The map, he said, had shown Peter Pettigrew with them. Black and Lupin declared that Scabbers was the Animagus Peter Pettigrew.

Chapter 18The Doorkeeper

Lupin and Black set out to prove that Scabbers was Pettigrew. All the while Lupin was fighting down his Garou war form, maddened by the Wyrm-reek of the rat, and Black steadied him by calling him Moony. Lupin told them how he had been bitten as a small boy. The Wolfsbane Potion now suppressed his compulsion to transform. Dumbledore had let him into Hogwarts, with the Whomping Willow planted and the Shrieking Shack built for his monthly transformations. James, Sirius and Peter had become illegal Animagi. They were known as Prongs, Padfoot and Wormtail. Snape had seen the Marauder's Map in Lupin's office, then followed them under Harry's Cloak. He bound Lupin, told Black 'You failed her!' and resolved to hand both men over to the Dementors. Harry blocked the door. He had been wrong about Dracina Malfoy, he said, which proved that things were complicated. He taunted Snape. Then Harry, Ron and Hermione disarmed Snape together, so forcefully that he was knocked out. Black explained that he had recognised Pettigrew in a photograph in the Daily Prophet, which Fudge had given him. Crookshanks had helped him. It was Black, too, who had persuaded the Potters to make Pettigrew their Secret-Keeper. Lupin and Black forced Pettigrew back into human form. Lupin nearly transformed. Black calmed him by quoting 'Be ye angry, and sin not', a verse Lily had kept on her wall. Black described how he had found true faith in Azkaban through Bible passages printed in The Quibbler. After that the Dementors had stopped coming to him. In the end he had escaped as a dog. Harry stopped Black and Lupin from killing Pettigrew, so that he could be handed over as evidence. Hermione listed four lethal curses with alarming relish. Then they set off. Pettigrew was shackled to Lupin by one wrist and to Ron by the other, while Snape floated along unconscious.

Chapter 19Fear No Evil

On the way out of the Shack Ron swore at the stairs and bantered with Black. Black said that Ron reminded him of himself, and that James would have liked him. Ron admitted he had been thinking about God ever since he saw Harry's Patronus. Once he had come to believe Sirius a murderer, Lupin said, he had spent years with a pack in the hills of mid-Wales. Most of the pack were of the Fianna tribe. He called himself a coward. He promised to tell Harry about James and the Black sisters. In the tunnel Black asked Harry to come and live with him. Harry joyfully agreed, before he remembered the blood ward that bound him to his aunt's house. Black revealed that he had watched Harry leave Magnolia Crescent the summer before. He asked whether all was well with the Dursleys, but Lupin interrupted before Harry could answer. On the lawn the two men said the evening collect together. Then the clouds parted to show the full moon. Lupin had missed his Wolfsbane Potion. He began the Lord's Prayer, and changed into a nine-foot Garou. His cross flew off, and Harry pocketed it. The creature called Harry 'Wyrm'. It hurled Black aside. Then it hunted Harry, clawing his arm and leg. It shrugged off every spell until a silver Sickle burnt its muzzle. Harry's Shield Charm held it for a moment. Black, praying Psalm 23, changed into the dog and fought it. Pettigrew seized Lupin's wand. He struck down Ron and Crookshanks, then escaped as a rat. The creature fled into the Forest as a giant wolf. By the lake about a hundred Dementors closed in on Sirius, Harry and Hermione. Harry's faith faltered, and his Patronus failed. A Dementor was about to give him the Kiss when a silver animal drove them back. Across the lake Harry glimpsed a figure he almost seemed to know.

Chapter 20The Ending Has Not Yet Been Written.

Harry woke in the hospital wing to hear Snape telling Fudge that the three of them had been Confunded. Black, he said, was locked in Professor Flitwick's office, awaiting the Dementor's Kiss. Harry flattered the Minister, then mocked him, until Madam Pomfrey silenced him with chocolate. Dumbledore heard Harry and Hermione out. He promised to believe them, then hinted that what they needed was more time. He named the thirteenth window from the right of the West Tower, and handed Harry a small leather book that was not to be opened. Hermione revealed her Time-Turner, a gift from McGonagall, and took them back three hours. Harry concluded that they must rescue Buckbeak. Before they could, a cloaked figure lured the hippogriff away with a dead ferret, then flew off on him as Macnair's axe fell. The figure was Dracina Malfoy. In the Forest Hermione accused Dracina of using Harry. She described Dracina's cruelty in the girls' toilets in their first year. When Harry brought up Dracina's missing brooch and ribbons, Hermione stormed off. The werewolf found Harry in the Forest. Dracina dived to his rescue on Buckbeak. Hermione whispered a confession, and her forgiveness, before she was hurled into a tree. Kneeling in a stream in front of Dracina, Harry cast a Shield Charm. It turned white as the moon came out, swept through the creature and restored Lupin to human form. Dracina sobbed her apologies. Harry carried her out of the stream and forgave her. At the lake he realised that the rescuer he had seen was himself. He cast a stag Patronus that scattered the Dementors, and an arrow of white light from the sky destroyed the last of them. Hermione and Dracina apologised to each other. Hermione admitted to the brooch and the ribbons, though not to the letter. The three of them flew Buckbeak to Flitwick's office. Sirius had vanished, leaving behind a book marked MYST with grey fingermarks on it. As Aurors opened the door, Hermione identified it as a D'ni linking book. All three of them linked to Myst Island.

Chapter 21Find The Red Pages

Harry, Hermione and Dracina Malfoy came through a D'ni linking book on to the rotting dock of a deserted island, in a grey, empty sea. Dracina mocked Hermione's explanation. Hermione accused her of never once having been kind, and very nearly said 'my Harry'. Dracina broke down. She told them about her lonely, gilded life at Malfoy Manor and her hopeless longing for her father's approval. In Harry's head the old voice of the cupboard silenced him, so that he heard none of what followed. Hermione hugged Dracina and confessed that she had been friendless as a child herself. She forgave Dracina properly, then offered her friendship. The two girls agreed to be friends and rivals for Harry. Hermione explained what was known of the D'ni, the Art, the linking books and Anna's journal. Then she realised that the small book Dumbledore had given Harry would take them home. They followed footprints to a ruined library, where they found Sirius Black. He had been keeping company with a woman who had since vanished. They linked back one at a time to Professor Flitwick's office. After they had gone, the woman reappeared. She took the little book her father had written and said 'Shorah'. Dracina whistled Buckbeak up to the window. Before Sirius flew away he told Harry that James was proud of him, and that Lily would want him to sort things out with Christ. Holding Dracina's hand at the window, Harry resolved that the wizarding world must be made to change. A brilliant white star shone out in the west. On the stairs they overheard Snape covering for Dumbledore with Fudge, and losing his Order of Merlin for it. They reached the hospital wing just as Dumbledore came to lock the door. He praised Dracina and sent her down to the dungeons. Then he walked away, thinking of Greta Grindelwald. Harry lay awake thinking about God, Númenor and the white arrow until Ron woke up.

Chapter 22The Greater Good

The next day Harry, Ron and Hermione found the castle almost empty, now that the Dementors had been driven off. On the front steps Pansy Parkinson confessed that it was she who had sent Dracina's letter about Buckbeak to Lucius Malfoy. Dracina flew at her, but Ron calmly talked her out of her rage. From then on Pansy looked at Ron with obvious interest. The Fat Friar told Harry that his Patronus had killed Dementors because he had touched God and stopped doubting, like Peter walking on the water. He asked Harry to go into the church near his home, just once. Lupin, exposed as a werewolf by Snape, resigned. He told Harry that Christianity was a gift given to everyone. He gave back the Invisibility Cloak and the Marauder's Map. Then he gave Harry his own little wooden cross. Dumbledore told Harry that saving Pettigrew had created a bond, and that his father lived on in him. Then he saw Greta Grindelwald's anger in Harry's eyes. The anger, he said, never completely went away. Harry resolved to use his for the greater good. Hermione and Dracina each wrote Molly Weasley a long letter about the Dursleys. They sent them together, by the same owl. Mrs Weasley read them and smiled. On the train Dracina secretly passed Harry a note about her owl, Juniper. Then a tiny owl brought a letter from Sirius, confessing that it was he who had sent the Firebolt. With it came a Hogsmeade permission form, and the owl itself was a gift for Ron. A week after he got back to Privet Drive, having finished The Lord of the Rings, Harry went into St Michael's for Evensong. The vicar turned out to be the old man from the bench by the lych-gate. He preached on holy anger.

How it differs from the original

  • The book opens with Harry visiting St Michael's church, where an old man on the lych-gate bench speaks to him.
  • The Dursleys no longer dare mistreat Harry after Dumbledore's visit, and Harry blackmails Vernon with a BNP membership card.
  • Muggle news reports Khan Noonien Singh's Augment War, the Avengers and Justice League, the Power Rangers in Birmingham, Superman's death and Spider-Man's retirement; wizards know nothing of them.
  • A dodgy Muggle-dressed man with a glowing book in a carrier bag rides the Knight Bus.
  • Lucius Malfoy meets Harry in Diagon Alley, defends Lily's standing as a witch against Marge, and shows fear of Harry.
  • Harry reads The Lord of the Rings, bookmarked with Dracina's green ribbon of favour.
  • Dracina sends Harry a birthday letter and hand-made chocolate violets, and conducts a secret friendship with him.
  • Buckbeak slashes Dracina's right arm; she writes a letter to Lucius but decides not to send it, and Pansy sends it.
  • Werewolves are the Garou, who change at will rather than by the moon; Lupin is heavily implied to be one, and his own boggart is a Garou war-form.
  • Lupin's lessons cover vampire clans, the Masquerade, the Camarilla and the Sabbat, and Snape lectures on the Garou.
  • Lupin is a Christian, tells Harry Lily believed in Christ, and teaches the Patronus as light from God.
  • Harry meets a painting of Cain and dreams of him; the Fat Friar turns Harry from attacking Snape with the story of David and Abigail.
  • McGonagall's previous career includes a 1966 Siberian mission and a kept parasite in her office.
  • Dracina's boggart is her disappointed father.
  • Harry breaks down before Ron and Hermione at the end of the autumn term.
  • Dracina lends Harry a Nimbus Two Thousand and One before McGonagall returns the Firebolt.
  • Harry casts his first corporeal Patronus at the Ravenclaw match, against Dracina and her teammates dressed as Dementors.
  • Ron strikes Sirius Black in the face during the dormitory break-in.
  • Buckbeak's hearing is brought forward from April to March on the strength of Dracina's letter.
  • Dracina reports Harry to Snape after the mud to make him come back to safety, and confides in Snape.
  • Dumbledore calls at Privet Drive in person and frightens the Dursleys out of ever striking or starving Harry again.
  • Harry believes he saw Jesus Christ in the Chamber of Secrets. He finds himself drawn to St Michael's Church, where a mysterious old man speaks to him.
  • Dumbledore has linked Lily's protection to the Elves and Númenor, so Harry reads The Lord of the Rings in search of his own ancestry.
  • Dracina Malfoy sends a birthday letter tied with a green ribbon, a token of her favour that Narcissa arranged.
  • Harry gets Uncle Vernon's promise to sign the form by blackmailing him over a British National Party membership card.
  • The television news covers Khan Noonien Singh's conquest in India, the Avengers, the Justice League and the Power Rangers in Birmingham.
  • Fear of Dumbledore visibly holds Vernon and Petunia back. As Marge inflates, Petunia watches Harry, not Marge.
  • Harry's rage is sharpened by what Dumbledore told him: that his mother was descended from Elves.
  • A man strongly hinted to be John Constantine rides the Knight Bus, with a glowing book in a Tesco carrier bag.
  • According to Ern, the cover story for Black's massacre was a mutant attack.
  • Harry jokingly introduces himself to Fudge as Barry Trotter, then manipulates him with flattery.
  • Fudge mentions the strange blood ward Dumbledore described to him, and admits that he saw the Dursleys himself.
  • Lucius Malfoy meets Harry in Diagon Alley, walks with him a while, and tries to win him over to blood purism.
  • Wizards turn out to know nothing at all of superhumans or of Muggle wars.
  • Harry reads The Lord of the Rings and is moved by the Elves of Rivendell.
  • Mr Weasley asks Harry privately whether the Dursleys hurt him, and puts him down on the Ministry car list under the name Weasley.
  • Fred and George tried to shut Percy in an Egyptian tomb, whose guardian questioned him about the weighing of his heart.
  • Lupin shows hints of animal senses: flaring nostrils, a dog-like growl and eyes that catch the light.
  • Dracina only pretends to bully Harry's friends, and secretly gives him chocolate violets she has made herself.
  • Hermione cradles Harry after his collapse and grows jealous of Dracina.
  • McGonagall's office contains a stuffed, eyeless creature with a four-way mouth.
  • Harry makes a friend of Sir Cadogan by joking with him on the way to Divination.
  • Harry asks Trelawney about signs from God and is mocked for it. Hermione defends him, then later explains why the wizarding world is hostile to Christianity.
  • Dracina's ribbons are turned to Gryffindor colours and her Potions essay is inked over; both are hinted to be Hermione's doing.
  • Harry catches the injured Dracina, and she begs him to kill Buckbeak.
  • Harry visits Dracina in the hospital wing, and she screams at him about Hermione.
  • Dracina, not Draco, faces the boggart. It becomes her disapproving father, Lucius, and she completes the Riddikulus herself.
  • Lupin faces the boggart himself. It becomes a nine-foot, blood-soaked werewolf that recognises him, not a full moon.
  • There is a new subplot about a brooch: Hermione is hinted to have taken Dracina's heirloom and left it for Peeves.
  • Snape gives Harry and Dracina private advice about friendships ending over a single word.
  • Dracina apologises and claims to have dropped her complaint about Buckbeak.
  • Vampires are taught in terms of the Masquerade, the Camarilla, the Sabbat and the clans, such as the Ventrue or the Malkavians.
  • McGonagall teaches about spinal parasites and keeps a dead one in her office.
  • Lupin's growling is shown openly, along with the way his body reacts to Snape or to the moon.
  • Dracina defends Harry from Pansy and Daphne on Halloween morning.
  • Harry tells Lupin that he would have turned a boggart Voldemort into a screaming baby.
  • Slytherin's excuse for pulling out is Dracina's arm, which turns out to be a prop she uses for theatre.
  • Snape's substitute lesson is on the Garou, with their five forms, moon signs and tribes, instead of textbook werewolves.
  • New scenes include the painting of two brothers at their altars, the Fat Friar's story and Hermione's account of Angelus.
  • Dean leads a football-style chant, which Hufflepuff answer.
  • Harry feels an unexplained stillness in the storm. In the hospital wing he makes the sign of the cross.
  • Pansy, not Dracina, sent the letter that led to Lucius Malfoy's complaint.
  • Harry's revenge dream ends with the watching figure burnt away by light, and Lupin advises him to seek God.
  • Hermione gives Harry a frank opinion of Dracina in the Three Broomsticks.
  • Flitwick privately recalls a long feud between the sisters Bellatrix and Narcissa in his Charms classes.
  • Fudge speaks of 'parasite creatures' and 'Nephilim'. McGonagall mentions her 'previous career'.
  • Harry's grief and rage are explored at length. Ron makes a speech about the Weasleys being Harry's family, and Harry breaks down.
  • The blood protection is the stated reason why Harry cannot live with the Weasleys.
  • Harry blames Dracina for the Buckbeak complaint, although it was Pansy who posted the letter.
  • At Christmas lunch McGonagall tells the story of a mission in Siberia.
  • Lupin's absence at Christmas is hinted to involve a pack and a fight against a corruption, not simple illness.
  • Lupin frames the Patronus as light derived from God and tells Harry that Lily was a devout Christian.
  • Dracina is the Slytherin Seeker who beats Ravenclaw. She lends Harry her spare Nimbus Two Thousand and One.
  • On Mrs Weasley's instructions, the Weasley family deliberately organise themselves to watch over Harry.
  • Four new scenes deal with trust and forgiveness. They show the boy on the lake ice, the Hufflepuff girls in the library, Flitwick with Hobday and the Ravenclaw with the fleece.
  • Harry's early Patronus has no shape at all, only a mass of silver light.
  • Harry takes command during a time-out and gives the team its tactics against Ravenclaw.
  • The fake Dementors are Dracina, Crabbe, Goyle and Marcus Flint, with Dracina on Goyle's shoulders.
  • Ron punches Sirius Black in the face during the break-in at the dormitory.
  • Lupin speaks to Harry about the trick of hiding his face, which he says he shares.
  • Dracina confesses privately to Snape, revealing that she was coerced into the fake-Dementor stunt and never sent the letter about Buckbeak.
  • Harry's mud lands on Dracina's carefully styled hair, and she refuses to have it mended because she thinks she deserved it.
  • In Snape's office Lupin shows signs of a struggle with something bestial. He smells Snape's left arm, and prays afterwards.
  • Lupin teaches Harry the saying about forgiving seventy times seven.
  • Hermione punches Dracina over a slur and the two girls fight on the steps, instead of Hermione slapping Draco.
  • Harry forgives Dracina and believes her account of the letter.
  • The Fat Friar gives Harry a long account of wizards, the medieval Church and the witch-hunts. He also believes Harry's account of seeing Jesus.
  • Dracina throws the final so that Gryffindor wins the Cup, and gives Harry an Easter egg she has made by hand.
  • Buckbeak escapes during the execution itself, flying off with a hooded rider who is hinted to be Dracina.
  • Hermione is tempted to use her Time-Turner against Dracina, and she grows possessive of Harry.
  • Dracina secretly coaches Harry through the Potions exam.
  • A look ahead shows Harry's future rule over much of the wizarding world.
  • The Fat Lady flirts with the security trolls.
  • Lupin is a Garou rather than a classic werewolf. He struggles to hold back a war form, and he smells dark magic as the reek of the Wyrm.
  • Sirius wears a home-made wooden cross from Azkaban and keeps saying 'my fault'.
  • Harry physically beats Sirius at length, and Hermione attacks him even more savagely.
  • Hermione learnt Lupin's secret from Snape's essay, and she calls him a Garou.
