  • Sirius's faith, with Psalm 84 at its heart, runs right through the scene in the Shack. So does Lupin's struggle with a war form that hates the Wyrm.
  • Lupin can smell dark magic on Pettigrew and on Snape's left arm.
  • Harry taunts Snape about having no friends, and mentions Dracina Malfoy as a lesson learnt.
  • Hermione describes several killing curses in gruesome detail.
  • Lupin changes into a Garou war form, described in great physical detail, and it calls Harry 'Wyrm'.
  • Harry burns the creature with a silver Sickle and holds it off with a Shield Charm.
  • Sirius and Lupin pray together. Harry's failure with the Patronus is tied to a crisis of faith.
  • Sirius offers Harry a home, but it is Harry himself who remembers the blood ward.
  • Dracina Malfoy, not Harry and Hermione, rescues Buckbeak. She later joins the time-travelling rescue.
  • Harry's Shield Charm turns white and forces Lupin back into human form.
  • An arrow of white light falls from the sky to destroy the last Dementor.
  • Sirius escapes, apparently by a D'ni linking book. Instead of freeing him on Buckbeak, Harry, Hermione and Dracina link to Myst Island.
  • Hermione confesses to persecuting Dracina all year.
  • John Constantine is a Muggle-born Slytherin who was at Hogwarts with Lucius Malfoy, and he rides the Knight Bus with Harry.
  • Grindelwald is a woman, Greta Grindelwald. Dumbledore owns a Deluminator that Constantine once stole.
  • The D'ni of Myst really existed, in a cavern under New Mexico, and their linking books circulate in the wizarding world.
  • The Headmaster's password is Acid Pop.
  • Sirius escapes from Flitwick's office to Myst Island through a D'ni linking book, rather than being freed directly on Buckbeak.
  • Dracina Malfoy is with Harry and Hermione throughout the rescue.
  • Dracina and Hermione are reconciled. They become friends and rivals for Harry.
  • Snape covers for Dumbledore in front of Fudge, and Fudge withdraws the Order of Merlin in person.
  • Sirius is a Christian, and he urges Harry to see the Fat Friar.
  • Harry makes up his mind that the wizarding world must change.
  • Pansy Parkinson, not Hermione, turns out to have sent the Buckbeak letter, and Ron makes peace on the castle steps.
  • Harry goes to the Fat Friar about God and his Patronus.
  • Lupin gives Harry his wooden cross and urges him to go to church.
  • Dumbledore admits that the anger never completely stops, and Harry takes up the phrase 'the greater good'.
  • Hermione and Dracina write to Molly Weasley about the Dursleys.
  • The last chapter ends with Harry at Evensong in St Michael's.

Characters introduced

  • Buckbeak
  • Cain
  • Crookshanks
  • Ephraim Shacklewell
  • John Constantine
  • Peter Pettigrew
  • Remus Lupin
  • Sirius Black
  • Stan Shunpike
  • Sybill Trelawney
  • Walden Macnair

pages.title: Harry Potter and the Girl of Fire
pages.html:
Front page · The Books

Harry Potter and the Girl of Fire

Book Four of the Malfoid Saga · 1994 to 1995 · In progress

Read Book FourFree at malfoid.lol

Chapters

Chapter 1The House on the Hill

Harry dreamt that he was walking down a Privet Drive that lay sunk at the bottom of a valley. He passed number four, which was an orphanage kept by Aunt Petunia, where his mother had died after giving birth to him. He passed Mrs Figg at her knitting, then went through a leafless wood to a shack with a dead boa constrictor nailed to its door. Inside he found a filthy Uncle Vernon. The two of them spoke to each other in hisses. Harry put Vernon to sleep and took his wand, along with a gold ring set with a black stone. He climbed on past the Leaky Cauldron, and past a small boy weeding by moonlight, to the big house on the hill. There his father, James, sat at dinner with Harry's grandparents, Fleamont and Euphemia. Aunt Marge was serving them. James claimed that Lily had tricked him, and that he had abandoned her when the spell wore off. Harry tortured all three of them with the Cruciatus Curse until they apologised. Then he killed them with the Killing Curse, and felt wonderful. Dracina appeared in a scaled blue dress and embraced him. Then she slipped away through the curtains into a rainy circus. There she turned into a long blue snake, and slid off into the dark. Harry screamed that he loved her, begging her not to forget him. A flash of green light woke him. He was in his bedroom at Privet Drive, clutching Lupin's cross, with his scar burning.

Chapter 2The Scar

Harry woke at Privet Drive on a Saturday morning in August 1994 with his scar burning. He tried to make sense of his dream. In it he had murdered his own father and grandparents, then lost Dracina to a snake. Thinking of Dracina, he admitted to himself that he was in love with her. He read her birthday letter again. It offered help against his relatives, and reported that her father kept asking after Harry. Her mother, it said, was helpfully covering for her. It also described Pansy's sudden passion for the Chudley Cannons. The last line, 'Don't forget me', made his scar sear. He wondered whom he could tell. He remembered St Michael's, where he had been to Evensong every Sunday since July, and the elderly vicar, who took an odd interest in his soul. Then he read Hermione's letter again. A Muggle computer game called Myst, she wrote, showed their island exactly. She told the story of Atrus and his sons. There were Muggles online, she reported, who felt called towards New Mexico. Harry thought back over his summer of hard study. There had been a night when moonlight lit his book, and two cheerful letters from Sirius, brought by tropical birds. There had also been a prank in which the Dursleys' fridge was filled with bleeding rats. He wrote to Sirius about his scar, leaving out the dream. Then he heard a scream from downstairs.

Chapter 3Fear and Anger

Harry ran downstairs to find the Dursleys' kitchen coated in pond mud, which had erupted from the plughole. Uncle Vernon realised who was behind it. He thrust at Harry a letter from Mrs Weasley, so heavily stamped that there was hardly room for the address, inviting Harry to the final of the Quidditch World Cup. It ended 'P.S. Actions have consequences.' Dudley was on a strict diet. He had lately become devoted to the Green Ranger, and to karate. He made room for Harry on the sofa, and they watched the news together. The bulletin described the Augment War. Khan Noonien Singh's forces were near Belgrade, and a commander called Joaquin was overrunning the Balkans. Then it showed Superman, alive again, asking the Security Council of the United Nations to let the Justice League and the Avengers intervene. It showed angry protests against superhumans outside the United Nations. Among the protesters were grieving victims of the Hulk, of Coast City, of the Sub-Mariner and of a mutant's blackout. There was a report, too, of a proposal to revive the Sentinel robots. The last item was the death of the Egyptologist Daniel Jackson in a shaft collapse at Giza, with a tribute from Dr Richard Watson in New Mexico. Harry realised how small the wizarding world was beside the Muggle one, and how ignorant. He felt ashamed of his plans to remake it. Upstairs Ron's tiny owl, Pig, brought word that Mr Weasley had got the tickets. They would come and fetch Harry at five on Sunday. Harry sent Hedwig off to Sirius. Then he fished a large slab of birthday cake out from under the loose floorboard and ate it, perfectly content.

How it differs from the original

  • In the original, the first chapter follows Frank Bryce at the Riddle House. Here it is Harry's dream instead, in which he murders his own father and grandparents in a house on a hill.
  • Harry admits to himself that he is in love with Dracina Malfoy.
  • Letters from Dracina and Hermione replace the letters in the original chapter. Hermione's is about the Myst game and the D'ni.
  • Harry goes to Evensong every week and is reading a Bible from the vicar.
  • The prank with the bleeding rats in the Dursleys' fridge is new.
  • Mrs Weasley's invitation comes by Muggle post, covered in stamps, as in the original, but here it arrives with a magical mud attack on the kitchen and a threatening postscript.
  • Dudley is a Power Rangers fan who is learning karate, and he shows signs of a gentler nature.
  • The Muggle news of the Augment War, Superman, the Justice League, the Avengers, the Sentinels and Daniel Jackson's death is entirely new.
  • Ron's letter comes by the tiny owl Pig, as in the original, but here it adds Mrs Weasley's warning that the Dursleys had better say yes, for their own sake.

Events in these years

  1. August 1994
    Parallax is stopped at the beginning of time
    Hal Jordan, the lost Green Lantern, now calling himself Parallax, was revealed as the power behind Zero Hour, trying to remake history so that Coast City had never fallen. The heroes stopped him, and Connor Hawke, son of the first Green Arrow, shot him through the heart; he survived and vanished again.
  2. August 1994
    Time begins again
    Early in August 1994 the young hero Damage released the energy of a new beginning at the dawn of all things, and time was started again from it. History came back very nearly as it had been, and most people remember the weeks of Zero Hour only as a strange dream.
  3. August 1994
    The Justice Society disbands
    After Zero Hour the surviving members of the Justice Society, old now in body as well as in years, agreed that the Society's day was done, and disbanded it.
  4. August 1994
    Daniel Jackson declared deadB4 Ch3
    The Egyptologist Daniel Jackson, twenty-nine, was declared dead after a shaft collapsed beneath the Giza plateau.
  5. August 1994
    Senate hearing on the Sentinel programmeB4 Ch3
    The Senate Armed Services Committee was to hear evidence on reviving the Sentinels against Khan.
  6. c. 1994
    Death of Manfred WörnerB4 Ch3
    Nato's Secretary-General Manfred Wörner died the weekend before 20 August 1994, and an acting Secretary-General took over.
  7. 18 August 1994
    Bleeding rats in the Dursleys' fridgeB4 Ch2
    On Thursday morning Aunt Petunia found the fridge crammed with bleeding rats; Harry suspected Sirius.
  8. 18 August 1994
    The Prime Minister returns from holidayB4 Ch3
    The British Prime Minister returned early from his holiday because of the Augment War.
  9. 19 August 1994
    Superman addresses the Security CouncilB4 Ch3
    Superman asked the UN Security Council to let the Justice League and the Avengers act against the Augments; the Council adjourned without a vote.
  10. 20 August 1994
    Harry's dream of the house on the hillB4 Ch1
    Harry dreamt of murdering his father and grandparents in a house on a hill and of Dracina turning into a snake, and woke with his scar burning.
  11. 20 August 1994
    Harry writes to Sirius about his scarB4 Ch2
    At dawn Harry wrote to Sirius that his scar had hurt, leaving out the dream.
  12. 20 August 1994
    Protest outside the United NationsB4 Ch3
    More than twenty thousand people protested against superhumans outside the United Nations overnight, chanting 'No more capes!'
  13. 20 August 1994
    Mud from the Dursleys' plugholeB4 Ch3
    Pond mud erupted from the Dursleys' kitchen plughole, and Vernon gave Harry Molly Weasley's letter inviting him to the World Cup final.
  14. 20 August 1994
    Augment forces near BelgradeB4 Ch3
    The news reported Augment forces within forty miles of Belgrade after the collapse of the rump Yugoslav army.
  15. 20 August 1994
    Pig brings Ron's letterB4 Ch3
    Pig brought Ron's letter about the World Cup tickets; Harry replied and sent Hedwig to Sirius.
  16. 21 August 1994
    The Weasleys to collect HarryB4 Ch3
    The Weasleys planned to fetch Harry from Privet Drive at five o'clock on Sunday.
  17. 22 August 1994
    Quidditch World Cup finalB4 Ch3
    The 1994 Quidditch World Cup final, Ireland against Bulgaria, was set for Monday night.
  18. 23 August 1994
    Security Council to meet againB4 Ch3
    The UN Security Council was due to meet again on Tuesday, and the protest was to continue until then.
  19. 1995
    The fall of Outer Heaven
    Learning that Outer Heaven, Big Boss's fortified mercenary state in southern Africa, had built the walking nuclear weapon Metal Gear, FOXHOUND sent in Gray Fox, who was captured, and then the rookie Solid Snake alone, who destroyed Metal Gear and brought down Venom Snake at its head.
  20. 1995
    Apocalypse returns
    Apocalypse came back from the Moon, where he had been left for dead.

pages.title: Book 5
pages.html:
Front page · The Books

Book 5

Book Five of the Malfoid Saga · 1995 to 1996 · Untitled

This book has not been written yet and has no title. Events already fixed for its years are listed below and on the timeline.

Events in these years

  1. 1996
    John Mason helps retake Alcatraz
    John Mason was brought out of Wolfburg to guide a naval team into Alcatraz, which renegade Marines had seized with rockets of poison gas aimed at San Francisco.
  2. 1996
    Buffy Summers is called as the Slayer
    Buffy Summers, a fifteen-year-old Los Angeles schoolgirl, was called as the Slayer and trained by the Watcher Merrick. After he was killed and she burned down her school gymnasium full of vampires, her parents' marriage broke up.
  3. 1996
    Whistler shows Angel the Slayer
    A demon named Whistler found Angel starving in the streets of New York and showed him the newly called Slayer, Buffy Summers.
  4. c. 1996
    A Prague mob nearly destroys Drusilla
    Shortly before 1997 a mob in Prague nearly destroyed Drusilla, leaving her weakened.
  5. 1996
    Elias Zandi dies
    Elias Zandi died of a massive heart attack, leaving his fortune to the restoration of D'ni with Richard Watson as sole chairman, and his land round the Cleft to his estranged son, Jeff.
  6. 1996
    Bond retakes Alcatraz
    When renegade Marines under General Francis Hummel seized Alcatraz and threatened San Francisco with rockets of VX gas, James Bond was brought out of Wolfburg as the only man who had ever escaped the island, to take a team back in.

pages.title: Book 6
pages.html:
Front page · The Books

Book 6

Book Six of the Malfoid Saga · 1996 to 1997 · Untitled

This book has not been written yet and has no title. Events already fixed for its years are listed below and on the timeline.

Events in these years

  1. 1997
    Riven released
    The game Riven was released.
  2. 1997
    Buffy Summers moves to Sunnydale
    Buffy and her mother moved to Sunnydale, California, a town built over a Hellmouth, where her new Watcher, Rupert Giles, worked as the school librarian.
  3. 1997
    Angel goes to Sunnydale
    Angel went to Sunnydale to help Buffy, and fought beside her against the Master's followers and his own former companions.
  4. 1997
    Jenny Calendar watches Angel for the Kalderash
    Janna of the Kalderash, living as the computer teacher Jenny Calendar, was in Sunnydale on her clan's orders to watch Angel, and her uncle Enyos came to hold her to the task.
  5. 1997
    Spike brings Drusilla to Sunnydale
    William the Bloody brought the weakened Drusilla to Sunnydale, where he met Angel again.
  6. 1997
    The D'ni Restoration Council is founded
    Richard Watson founded the D'ni Restoration Council with Dr Ikuro Kodama, Victor Laxman and Dr Marie Sutherland to survey the city, make it safe, restore its machinery and record what it found.
  7. 1997
    The Goa'uld return through the Stargate
    Apophis, who had been taking over Ra's domains since Ra's death and had heard that Thor was busy elsewhere, broke Ra's ban on Earth and came through the Stargate. His Jaffa killed the soldiers guarding it and carried one off. On Abydos he took Sha'uri and Skaara as hosts. The programme was reopened with teams sent out to other worlds; Jack O'Neill was recalled to command SG-1, and Daniel Jackson returned to Earth.
  8. 1997
    Zanzibar Land declares independence
    Zanzibar Land in Central Asia rose against the Commonwealth of Independent States, beat back its armies with mercenaries gathered from all over the world and declared itself an independent military state with Big Boss behind it.
  9. 1997
    Teal'c turns against Apophis
    Teal'c, Bra'tac's best pupil and his successor as First Prime of Apophis, turned against his master and joined SG-1, and Bra'tac became one of Earth's closest allies and a leader of the free Jaffa.
  10. 1997
    Darla is destroyed in Sunnydale
    Serving the imprisoned Master in Sunnydale, Darla was staked by Angel as she tried to kill the Slayer Buffy Summers.
  11. 1997
    Thor's Hammer destroyed
    On Cimmeria the device called Thor's Hammer seized the Jaffa Teal'c for the larva he carried, and SG-1 destroyed it to free him.
  12. 1997
    Nirrti wipes out Hanka
    To hide her breeding of a perfect host, Nirrti killed the people of Hanka with a plague. Only Cassandra survived.
  13. 1997
    The Supreme Intelligence returns
    The Supreme Intelligence, believed dead since the Avengers executed it in 1992, was found to have survived.
  14. Spring 1997
    Buffy Summers destroys the Master
    In the spring the Master fed on Buffy and left her to drown, and her brief death freed him; revived the same night, she destroyed him, and later ground his bones to powder when his followers tried to raise him.

pages.html:
Front page · The Books

Book 7

Book Seven of the Malfoid Saga · 1997 to 1998 · Untitled

This book has not been written yet and has no title. Events already fixed for its years are listed below and on the timeline.

Events in these years

  1. Autumn 1997
    Drusilla is restored with her sire's blood
    Late in the year Drusilla was restored to strength in Sunnydale with the blood of her own sire, Angel.
  2. 1998
    Angelus kills Jenny Calendar and Enyos
    After the curse broke, Angelus killed Janna, the Kalderash woman known as Jenny Calendar, and her uncle Enyos; her translation of the ritual survived her.
  3. 1998
    Buffy sends Angel into a hell dimension
    Buffy Summers was forced to send Angel into a hell dimension.
  4. 1998
    Apophis's motherships destroyed above Earth
    Apophis and Klorel brought two motherships against Earth. SG-1 and Bra'tac destroyed both. Apophis and Klorel escaped through the Stargate on board.
  5. 1998
    Heru'ur driven from Cimmeria again
    Heru'ur invaded Cimmeria after Thor's Hammer fell. Asgard answered, and he escaped through the gate, leaving his army behind.
  6. 19 January 1998
    Angel's curse breaks
    On Buffy's seventeenth birthday Angel knew a moment of true happiness with her, the Kalderash curse broke, and Angelus returned and turned on everyone who had trusted Angel.
  7. Spring 1998
    Willow Rosenberg restores Angel's soul
    In the spring the witch Willow Rosenberg used Jenny Calendar's translation to restore the Kalderash curse.

pages.title: Timeline
pages.html:
Front page

Timeline of the Malfoid Saga

From the Elder Days to the years still to come. 1528 entries.

Before the Sun: the Music, the Lamps and the Trees

  1. c. 250,000 BC
    Bertron makes Doomsday on Krypton
    The alien scientist Bertron bred Doomsday on prehistoric Krypton by cloning a creature again and again from its own remains.
  2. c. 100,000 BC
    The Clone Wars begin on Krypton
    Nyra's clone bride for her son Kan-Z set off a thousand-year war, which ended when Black Zero's Destroyer wiped out Kandor.
  3. c. 80,000 BC
    Ilúvatar makes the Ainur
    Before the world was made, God, whom the Elves would call Eru Ilúvatar, the One, made the Ainur, the Holy Ones, the offspring of His thought, and they sang before Him in the Timeless Halls.
  4. c. 79,990 BC
    The Music of the Ainur
    Ilúvatar set a mighty theme before the Ainur, and out of it they made the Ainulindalë, the Great Music, from which the shape of the world would come.
  5. c. 79,985 BC
    Melkor sings out of tune
    Melkor, mightiest of the Ainur, the being whom Scripture calls Lucifer, the light-bearer, and Satan, and whom the Garou call the Wyrm, wove thoughts of his own into the Music in his pride, and the discord spread about him. It was the first rebellion against God and the first of all falls, and dark magic began with it.
  6. c. 79,980 BC
    Eä is given Being
    Ilúvatar showed the Ainur a Vision of the world their Music had foretold, then sent the Flame Imperishable into the Void and said 'Eä! Let these things Be', and the world was made.
  7. c. 79,000 BC
    The Valar enter the world
    Those of the Ainur who loved the Vision went down into Eä to labour on Arda; the mightiest were the Valar, among them Manwë, Varda, Ulmo, Aulë and Yavanna, and with them came the lesser spirits called the Maiar. Melkor came down too, claiming the world for his own.
  8. c. 78,000 BC
    The First War
    Melkor made war on the Valar for the mastery of Arda and marred whatever they made, raising mountains where they dug valleys, and he poured his own malice and power into the very substance of the world, so that nothing in it was afterwards wholly untouched by him.
  9. c. 77,000 BC
    Tulkas drives Melkor out
    Tulkas the Strong came laughing into Arda to aid the Valar, and Melkor fled before his wrath out of the world into the outer darkness, where he brooded for a long age.
  10. c. 76,000 BC
    Olórin among the Maiar
    Olórin, wisest of the Maiar, dwelt in the gardens of Lórien in the Undying Lands and went often to the house of Nienna, from whom he learned pity and patience; in a far later age Men would call him Gandalf.
  11. c. 70,000 BC
    Melkor seduces Sauron and the Balrogs
    Melkor drew many of the Maiar into his service, among them the spirits of fire later called Balrogs and Mairon of the people of Aulë the Smith, who became Sauron, his chief servant and lieutenant.
  12. c. 60,000 BC
    The Two Lamps are raised
    Aulë wrought two vast lamps, Illuin in the north and Ormal in the south, and Varda filled them with light; under them came the Spring of Arda, and the Valar dwelt on the isle of Almaren in the Great Lake.
  13. c. 58,000 BC
    Melkor delves Utumno
    Melkor returned in secret with his servants and delved the fortress of Utumno beneath the mountains of the north, with the outpost of Angband to the west of it, and his blight crept over the Spring of Arda.
  14. c. 55,000 BC
    Melkor throws down the Lamps
    Melkor came out of the north and threw down the pillars of the Lamps; their flames poured over the earth, Almaren was destroyed, and the lands and seas were broken and marred.
  15. c. 54,500 BC
    The Valar remove to Valinor
    The Valar left Middle-earth to the dark and went into Aman in the uttermost West, where they raised the mountain wall of the Pelóri and founded the guarded realm of Valinor and the city of Valmar.
  16. c. 52,020 BC
    The Two Trees of Valinor
    On the green mound of Ezellohar Yavanna sang into being the Two Trees, silver Telperion and golden Laurelin, whose waxing and waning light measured the Years of the Trees in Valinor while Middle-earth lay under the stars.
  17. c. 41,540 BC
    Varda kindles the stars
    Foreseeing the coming of the Elves, Varda made new and brighter stars from the silver dews of Telperion and set the Seven Stars of the Sickle of the Valar in the northern sky as a sign of doom to Melkor.
  18. c. 41,530 BC
    The Elves awaken at Cuiviénen
    In the year 1050 of the Trees the Elves, the Firstborn of Ilúvatar, awoke by the starlit water of Cuiviénen in the far east of Middle-earth, and the first things they saw were the stars.
  19. c. 41,450 BC
    Melkor breeds the Orcs
    Melkor's servants took Elves from the shores of Cuiviénen and carried them to Utumno, where by slow arts of cruelty he bred from them the race of Orcs in mockery of the Firstborn.
  20. c. 41,180 BC
    Oromë finds the Elves
    In the year 1085 of the Trees Oromë, the huntsman of the Valar, came upon the Elves while riding in Middle-earth and named them Eldar, the people of the stars.
  21. c. 41,030 BC
    Melkor is chained with Angainor
    In the Battle of the Powers, fought for the Elves' sake from the year 1090 of the Trees, the Valar broke Utumno; Tulkas wrestled Melkor down, and in 1100 he was bound with the chain Angainor and shut in the Halls of Mandos for three ages. Sauron was never found.
  22. c. 40,980 BC
    The Great Journey begins
    In the year 1105 of the Trees the Eldar set out westward from Cuiviénen at the summons of the Valar, the Vanyar, the Noldor and the Teleri, while those who refused remained in the east as the Avari.
  23. c. 40,730 BC
    Thingol meets Melian
    On the long march Elwë of the Teleri wandered into the wood of Nan Elmoth, met Melian the Maia among the nightingales and stood entranced for many years; he became Thingol, King of the Sindar of Beleriand, and she his queen.
  24. c. 40,710 BC
    The Eldar come to Aman
    In the year 1132 of the Trees the Vanyar and the Noldor were ferried over the Great Sea to Aman, and built the white city of Tirion upon the hill of Túna in the light of the Trees.
  25. c. 40,340 BC
    Fëanor is born
    In the year 1169 of the Trees Fëanor was born in Tirion to Finwë, King of the Noldor, and his mother Míriel spent so much of her spirit in bearing him that she laid down her life and went to the Halls of Mandos.
  26. c. 38,030 BC
    Melkor is released
    In the year 1400 of the Trees, his three ages of captivity over, Melkor was released by Manwë after feigning repentance, and went among the Noldor offering counsel and sowing lies.
  27. c. 37,530 BC
    Fëanor makes the Silmarils
    About the year 1450 of the Trees Fëanor wrought the three Silmarils, jewels that held the blended light of the Two Trees, and Varda hallowed them so that no evil hand could touch them unburnt; Melkor lusted for them from that day.
  28. c. 37,130 BC
    Fëanor is banished to Formenos
    In the year 1490 of the Trees, inflamed by Melkor's lies, Fëanor drew his sword on his half-brother Fingolfin in Tirion and was banished for twelve years to his northern stronghold of Formenos, where Finwë followed him with the Silmarils.
  29. c. 37,080 BC
    The Darkening of Valinor
    In the year 1495 of the Trees, during a festival in Valmar, Melkor came with Ungoliant, the great spider of darkness; he smote the Two Trees with his black spear and she drank their light, and Valinor was plunged into darkness.
  30. c. 37,080 BC
    Finwë slain and the Silmarils stolen
    Melkor went on to Formenos, slew Finwë, King of the Noldor, before his doors and carried off the Silmarils, the first blood shed in the Blessed Realm; Fëanor cursed him and named him Morgoth, the Black Foe of the World.
  31. c. 37,080 BC
    The Oath of Fëanor
    In Tirion by torchlight Fëanor and his seven sons swore a dreadful oath to pursue with vengeance and hatred anyone who withheld a Silmaril from them, and the greater part of the Noldor followed him into exile.
  32. c. 37,078 BC
    Morgoth crowns himself with the Silmarils
    Rescued from Ungoliant in Lammoth by his Balrogs, Morgoth returned to Angband, raised the reeking towers of Thangorodrim above it, and set the Silmarils in an iron crown which he wore on his throne.
  33. c. 37,075 BC
    The Kinslaying at Alqualondë
    When the Teleri refused them their ships, the Noldor of Fëanor fell upon them at the Swan Haven of Alqualondë and took the white ships by force, the first slaying of Elves by Elves.
  34. c. 37,070 BC
    The Doom of Mandos
    In the year 1496 of the Trees, as the Noldor marched north along the coast of Aman, Mandos pronounced their Doom: tears unnumbered, and the betrayal of kin by kin, would follow their oath.
  35. c. 37,060 BC
    The ships are burned at Losgar
    In the year 1497 of the Trees Fëanor crossed to Middle-earth with his own host and burned the ships at Losgar, abandoning Fingolfin and his people, who crossed the grinding ice of the Helcaraxë on foot at the cost of many lives.
  36. c. 37,060 BC
    The Battle under Stars
    Fëanor routed the hosts of Morgoth in Dagor-nuin-Giliath in Mithrim, but pursued too far towards Angband and was mortally wounded by Gothmog, Lord of Balrogs, and his body fell to ash; soon after, his eldest son Maedhros was taken by treachery at a parley and hung by his right wrist from a cliff of Thangorodrim.
  37. c. 37,030 BC
    The Moon rises and Fingolfin arrives
    From the last silver flower of Telperion the Valar made the Moon, and at its first rising Fingolfin's host came at last over the ice into Middle-earth and marched to Mithrim with trumpets blowing.

The First Age: Beleriand, Eden and the curse of Cain

  1. c. 37,029 BC
    The Sun rises for the first time
    From the last golden fruit of Laurelin the Valar made the Sun, and at its first rising the Years of the Sun began; the First Age of the Sun is reckoned from that dawn.
  2. c. 37,028 BC
    God forms Adam
    In the first years of the Sun, when Men awoke in the far east of the world, God formed Adam, the first man, of the dust of the ground, breathed into his nostrils the breath of life and set him in the garden of Eden, eastward, to tend it.
  3. c. 37,027 BC
    Eve is made
    God cast Adam into a deep sleep and made Eve from his rib to be his wife, and they lived in Eden together, naked and unashamed.
  4. c. 37,026 BC
    The serpent in Eden
    Morgoth came to Eve in the garden as the serpent and beguiled her into eating the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, which God had forbidden; she gave the fruit to Adam, and he ate.
  5. c. 37,025 BC
    Adam and Eve driven from Eden
    God drove Adam and Eve out of Eden and set cherubim and a flaming sword at its east gate to keep the way of the tree of life, and Men went out into the world with a darkness behind them.
  6. c. 37,024 BC
    Cain and Abel are born
    Eve bore Adam two sons: Cain, the elder, who became a tiller of the ground, and Abel, who became a keeper of sheep.
  7. c. 37,013 BC
    The offerings of Cain and Abel
    Cain brought an offering of the fruit of the ground and Abel the firstlings of his flock; God had respect to Abel's offering and not to Cain's, and warned the angry Cain that sin lay at his door, that its desire was for him, and that he must rule over it.
  8. c. 37,012 BC
    Cain murders Abel
    Cain talked with his brother in the field, rose up against him and killed him, the first murder among Men, and Abel's blood cried out to God from the ground.
  9. c. 37,012 BC
    God curses Cain and sets the mark
    God cursed Cain from the ground that had drunk Abel's blood: he would be immortal, repelled and burned by the sun, and a wanderer without rest or home for ever, and beneath those three the sentence was soullessness. When Cain cried that whoever found him would slay him, God set a mark upon him so that none who met him would kill him.
  10. c. 37,011 BC
    Cain goes out into Nod
    Cain went out from the presence of the Lord and dwelt in the land of Nod, east of Eden, and from there began his wandering through the world, a cursed, deathless, sun-shy man with no soul and no powers, not yet a vampire.
  11. c. 37,011 BC
    Maedhros is rescued
    In the first years of the Sun Fingon the Valiant climbed Thangorodrim alone and, with the help of Thorondor, King of Eagles, freed Maedhros by cutting off his hand; Maedhros waived his claim, and Fingolfin became High King of the Noldor.
  12. c. 37,010 BC
    The Feast of Reuniting
    In the year 20 of the First Age Fingolfin held the Mereth Aderthad at the pools of Ivrin, where the Noldor and the Sindar of Beleriand feasted together in friendship.
  13. c. 36,978 BC
    Nargothrond and Gondolin begun
    After Ulmo sent them dreams by the river Sirion in the year 50, Finrod began in 52 to delve Nargothrond by the river Narog, and was named Felagund, Hewer of Caves, while Turgon began in secret to build Gondolin, the Hidden City, in the vale of Tumladen.
  14. c. 36,970 BC
    The Glorious Battle
    In the year 60 the Noldor destroyed an army of Morgoth in Dagor Aglareb, the Glorious Battle, and laid the Siege of Angband, which held for almost four hundred years.
  15. c. 36,914 BC
    Turgon's people enter Gondolin
    In the year 116 Gondolin was complete, and Turgon led his people secretly out of Nevrast into the Hidden City, which no enemy found for nearly four hundred years.
  16. c. 36,899 BC
    Seth is born
    When Adam was a hundred and thirty years old, far away in the east, Eve bore him Seth in place of Abel; from the line of Seth, long ages afterwards, Noah would come.
  17. c. 36,800 BC
    Telchar forges Narsil
    In the First Age Telchar, the Dwarf smith of Nogrod in the Blue Mountains, forged the sword Narsil, whose name joined the words for fire and white light; it would come down to Elendil.
  18. c. 36,770 BC
    Glaurung comes forth
    In the year 260 Glaurung, first of the fire-drakes of Morgoth, issued young from Angband and burned the plain of Ard-galen, but Fingon's mounted archers drove him back.
  19. c. 36,720 BC
    Finrod finds the first Men
    In the year 310 Finrod Felagund came upon Bëor and his people in the hills of Ossiriand, the first Men to come into Beleriand; they spoke little of their past, saying only that a darkness lay behind them in the east, and that they had turned their backs on it.
  20. c. 36,600 BC
    Cain wanders through the First Age
    Through the wars of the First Age Cain wandered the wild places of the east, deathless, soulless and shunning the sun, unknown to the Elves and to the chroniclers of Beleriand.
  21. c. 36,575 BC
    The Battle of Sudden Flame
    In the midwinter of the year 455 Morgoth broke the Siege of Angband in Dagor Bragollach, sending rivers of flame over Ard-galen, with Glaurung grown to his full might and Balrogs before his hosts.
  22. c. 36,574 BC
    Fingolfin duels Morgoth
    In the year 456 Fingolfin rode alone to the gates of Angband and challenged Morgoth to single combat; he wounded him seven times and was slain, Thorondor marred Morgoth's face, and Morgoth went halt for ever after.
  23. c. 36,573 BC
    Sauron takes Tol Sirion
    In the year 457 Sauron, Morgoth's lieutenant and master of werewolves, took the tower of Minas Tirith on the isle of Tol Sirion and filled it with wolves, and it was called Tol-in-Gaurhoth, the Isle of Werewolves.
  24. c. 36,566 BC
    Beren sees Lúthien
    In the year 464, after the betrayal and death of his father Barahir, Beren came over the Mountains of Terror into Doriath and saw Lúthien, daughter of Thingol and Melian, dancing in the woods of Neldoreth, and loved her; Thingol set the price of her hand at a Silmaril from Morgoth's crown.
  25. c. 36,566 BC
    Túrin is born
    In the winter of the year 464 Túrin was born in Dor-lómin to Húrin of the House of Hador and his wife Morwen.
  26. c. 36,565 BC
    Finrod dies in Sauron's dungeons
    In the year 465 Finrod Felagund went with Beren on his quest, was taken by Sauron and cast into the pits of Tol-in-Gaurhoth, and died there wrestling the werewolf that came for Beren.
  27. c. 36,565 BC
    Lúthien overthrows Sauron
    Lúthien came to Tol-in-Gaurhoth with Huan, the hound of Valinor, who throttled Sauron until he yielded the isle and fled in the shape of a vampire; she threw down his tower and freed Beren.
  28. c. 36,564 BC
    A Silmaril out of the Iron Crown
    In the year 466 Beren and Lúthien entered Angband in disguise; she sang Morgoth and all his court to sleep, and Beren cut a Silmaril from the iron crown, though the great wolf Carcharoth bit off his hand with the jewel in it.
  29. c. 36,564 BC
    The Hunting of the Wolf
    Carcharoth, maddened by the Silmaril, broke into Doriath; in the hunt Beren was mortally wounded and Huan slew the wolf and died, and the jewel was cut from its belly and given to Thingol.
  30. c. 36,561 BC
    Beren and Lúthien return
    Lúthien's spirit followed Beren to the Halls of Mandos and sang her grief before him, and she was granted to return with him to life as a mortal woman; they dwelt on the isle of Tol Galen in Ossiriand.
  31. c. 36,558 BC
    The Battle of Unnumbered Tears
    In the year 472 the Union of Maedhros marched on Angband in the Nirnaeth Arnoediad and was destroyed through the treachery of the Easterling Men; Fingon was slain by Gothmog, and the Noldor never recovered their strength.
  32. c. 36,558 BC
    Húrin's last stand
    Húrin and his brother Huor held the fens of Serech so that Turgon could escape to Gondolin; Huor fell, and Húrin slew seventy Trolls crying 'Aurë entuluva! Day shall come again!' until he was taken alive.
  33. c. 36,557 BC
    Morgoth curses Húrin's kin
    Morgoth set Húrin in a chair upon Thangorodrim and cursed him and all his kin, compelling him to see through Morgoth's eyes everything that befell them for twenty-eight years.
  34. c. 36,535 BC
    The fall of Nargothrond
    In the year 495 Morgoth's host and Glaurung defeated the Elves at Tumhalad and sacked Nargothrond, where Túrin had counselled open war; the dragon laid a spell of forgetting on Túrin and couched upon the treasure.
  35. c. 36,534 BC
    Tuor comes to Gondolin
    In the year 496 Tuor son of Huor, guided by Ulmo, found the hidden way to Gondolin and brought Turgon the warning of the Vala, which Turgon did not heed.
  36. c. 36,529 BC
    Túrin slays Glaurung
    In the year 501 Túrin stabbed Glaurung from beneath at the ravine of Cabed-en-Aras; dying, the dragon revealed that Túrin's wife Níniel was his sister Nienor, who cast herself into the torrent, and Túrin fell upon his sword.
  37. c. 36,528 BC
    Thingol slain over the Nauglamír
    In the year 502, after the freed Húrin brought him treasure out of Nargothrond, Thingol had the Dwarves of Nogrod set the Silmaril in the necklace Nauglamír, and they slew him in Menegroth for it; Melian left Middle-earth and her Girdle about Doriath failed.
  38. c. 36,527 BC
    Eärendil is born
    In the year 503 Tuor wedded Idril, daughter of Turgon, in Gondolin, the second union of Elves and Men, and their son Eärendil was born there.
  39. c. 36,525 BC
    The second death of Beren and Lúthien
    Beren took back the Nauglamír from the Dwarves at the ford of Sarn Athrad, and Lúthien wore the Silmaril on Tol Galen until the two of them died the death of mortals together; the jewel was brought by night to their son Dior in Doriath.
  40. c. 36,524 BC
    The Ruin of Doriath
    In the year 506 the sons of Fëanor, bound by their oath, attacked Doriath to claim the Silmaril in the Second Kinslaying; Dior and his queen were slain, and his daughter Elwing escaped with the jewel to the Mouths of Sirion.
  41. c. 36,520 BC
    The Fall of Gondolin
    In the year 510, betrayed by Turgon's nephew Maeglin, Gondolin was stormed by Balrogs, dragons and Orcs; Ecthelion and Gothmog slew one another, Glorfindel fell with a Balrog at Cirith Thoronath, Turgon perished, and Tuor and Idril escaped with Eärendil.
  42. c. 36,498 BC
    Elrond and Elros are born
    In the year 532 Elwing bore twin sons to Eärendil at the Havens of Sirion: Elrond and Elros, the Half-elven.
  43. c. 36,492 BC
    The Third Kinslaying
    In the year 538, while Eärendil was at sea, the sons of Fëanor fell upon the Havens of Sirion; Elwing cast herself into the sea with the Silmaril and Ulmo bore her up in the shape of a white bird, and Maglor took Elrond and Elros.
  44. c. 36,488 BC
    Eärendil reaches Valinor
    In the year 542 Eärendil came with Elwing and the Silmaril on his ship Vingilot to Valinor, the first of mortal kin to set foot there, and pleaded before the Valar for Elves and Men; they set him to sail the heavens with the Silmaril on his brow, and he rose in the west as the Evening Star.
  45. c. 36,485 BC
    The War of Wrath begins
    In the year 545 the host of the Valar under Eönwë landed in Beleriand, and the War of Wrath began, the Great Battle that would break the north of the world.
  46. c. 36,443 BC
    Ancalagon falls and Morgoth is taken
    In the year 587 Morgoth loosed his winged dragons, but Eärendil and the Eagles fought them all day in the sky, and Eärendil slew Ancalagon the Black, who fell upon Thangorodrim and broke its towers. Morgoth fled into his deepest pits and sued for peace, but was taken and bound again with Angainor, and his iron crown was beaten into a collar for his neck.
  47. c. 36,442 BC
    The fate of the Silmarils
    Maedhros and Maglor stole the last two Silmarils from the camp of Eönwë, but the jewels burned their hands; Maedhros cast himself into a fiery chasm and Maglor flung his into the sea, so that one jewel came to rest in the sky, one in the fire and one in the water.

The Second Age: Númenor and the Rings

  1. c. 36,441 BC
    Morgoth thrust into the Void
    At the end of the First Age the Valar thrust Morgoth out of the world through the Door of Night into the Timeless Void, and the lands of Beleriand, broken in the war, went under the sea; but the malice he had poured into the world remained, and the lies he had sown went on bearing fruit.
  2. c. 36,441 BC
    Elros and Elrond choose
    The Valar gave the Half-elven sons of Eärendil the choice of their kindred: Elros chose to be counted among Men and Elrond among the Elves, so that Aragorn would one day come of Elros's line and Arwen of Elrond's.
  3. c. 36,441 BC
    Sauron hides in Middle-earth
    Sauron put on a fair form and repented before Eönwë, but would not go to Valinor for judgement, and fled and hid himself in Middle-earth.
  4. c. 36,440 BC
    The Grey Havens founded
    In the first year of the Second Age Círdan the Shipwright founded the Grey Havens of Mithlond, and Gil-galad dwelt in Lindon as High King of the Noldor in Middle-earth.
  5. c. 36,409 BC
    Númenor is founded
    In the year 32 of the Second Age the Edain sailed, following the star of Eärendil, to the star-shaped isle of Elenna, which the Valar had raised from the sea as their reward, and Elros became the first King of Númenor as Tar-Minyatur.
  6. c. 35,999 BC
    Elros dies
    In the year 442 Elros Tar-Minyatur died after five hundred years of life; the Númenóreans, granted lives three times as long as other Men, grew wise and mighty and became the greatest mariners in the world.
  7. c. 35,691 BC
    Eregion founded
    In the year 750 Noldor under Celebrimbor, grandson of Fëanor, founded Eregion near the west gate of Khazad-dûm, and its smiths were the greatest in Middle-earth.
  8. c. 35,441 BC
    Sauron fortifies Mordor
    About the year 1000 Sauron chose the land of Mordor for his stronghold and began to build the Dark Tower of Barad-dûr near the fire-mountain Orodruin.
  9. c. 35,241 BC
    Annatar, the Lord of Gifts
    About the year 1200 Sauron came among the Elves in fair form as Annatar, the Lord of Gifts; Gil-galad and Elrond refused him, but the smiths of Eregion took him in.
  10. c. 34,941 BC
    The Rings of Power are made
    About the year 1500 the Elven smiths of Eregion, instructed by Sauron, reached the height of their skill and began to forge the Rings of Power, and from them Sauron learned the craft of rings.
  11. c. 34,851 BC
    The Three Rings
    About the year 1590 Celebrimbor finished alone the Three Rings of the Elves, Narya, Nenya and Vilya, which Sauron never touched.
  12. c. 34,841 BC
    Sauron forges the One Ring
    About the year 1600 Sauron forged the One Ring in secret in the fire of Orodruin to rule the other Rings, and poured the greater part of himself into it so that he could not be ended while it endured. It was the first Horcrux, and it could be made only with the elven craft he had learned in Eregion.
  13. c. 34,744 BC
    Eregion laid waste
    Sauron made war on the Elves in the year 1693 to seize the Rings, and the Three were hidden; in 1697 Eregion was laid waste and Celebrimbor slain, and Elrond led the survivors north and founded the refuge of Imladris, called Rivendell.
  14. c. 34,641 BC
    The Shadow falls on Númenor
    About the year 1800 the Númenóreans began to establish dominions on the coasts of Middle-earth, and the Shadow fell upon Númenor as its people began to envy the Elves their deathlessness.
  15. c. 34,190 BC
    The Nazgûl first appear
    In the year 2251 Tar-Atanamir took the sceptre and Númenor was divided; about this time the Nazgûl, the Ringwraiths, slaves of the Nine Rings that Sauron had given to great kings of Men, first appeared.
  16. c. 33,542 BC
    Ar-Adûnakhôr takes the sceptre
    In the year 2899 Ar-Adûnakhôr took the sceptre, the first king to take his royal name in the Adûnaic tongue, and the Faithful who kept the friendship of the Elves were persecuted.
  17. c. 33,500 BC
    Cain walks through the Second Age
    While Númenor rose and darkened and the Rings were made, Cain went on wandering the earth by night, older than the Rings and older than any king of Men, still without powers of any kind.
  18. c. 33,186 BC
    Ar-Pharazôn seizes the sceptre
    In the year 3255 Ar-Pharazôn the Golden took Tar-Palantír's daughter Míriel to wife against her will and seized the sceptre, the last and mightiest King of Númenor.
  19. c. 33,179 BC
    Sauron brought captive to Númenor
    Ar-Pharazôn landed at Umbar with a vast host in the year 3261, and in 3262 Sauron humbled himself before him and was taken as a hostage to Númenor.
  20. c. 33,165 BC
    Sauron seduces the King
    Within a few years Sauron had become the King's chief counsellor, and persuaded him that Morgoth, the Lord of the Darkness, was the true god, who could give him life without end.
  21. c. 33,150 BC
    Isildur saves the White Tree's fruit
    When Sauron urged Ar-Pharazôn to cut down Nimloth, the White Tree of Númenor, Isildur son of Elendil went in disguise into the King's courts by night and took a fruit from it, and was sorely wounded escaping.
  22. c. 33,148 BC
    The Temple of Morgoth
    Nimloth was cut down and burned, and on the hill of Armenelos Sauron raised a great domed temple to Morgoth, where Men of the Faithful were burned in sacrifice.
  23. c. 33,131 BC
    The Great Armament
    In the year 3310 Ar-Pharazôn, fearing death in his old age, began to build the Great Armament to wrest everlasting life from the Valar.
  24. c. 33,122 BC
    Ar-Pharazôn assails Valinor
    In the year 3319 Ar-Pharazôn broke the Ban of the Valar, sailed into the West and set foot on the shores of Aman; the Valar laid down their government of the world and called upon Ilúvatar.
  25. c. 33,122 BC
    The Downfall of Númenor
    Ilúvatar changed the fashion of the world: a chasm opened in the sea and swallowed the fleet, Ar-Pharazôn and his warriors were buried under falling hills, and Númenor went down beneath the waves. The Exiles called it the Akallabêth, Atalantë, the Downfallen.
  26. c. 33,122 BC
    The world is made round
    In the Downfall Aman was taken away out of the circles of the world, and the world was made round, so that only the Elves could find the Straight Road into the West.
  27. c. 33,122 BC
    Elendil escapes with nine ships
    Elendil the Faithful and his sons Isildur and Anárion escaped the Downfall with nine ships, bearing the Seeing-stones and a seedling of the White Tree, and were cast up on the shores of Middle-earth.
  28. c. 33,121 BC
    The Realms in Exile founded
    In the year 3320 Elendil founded Arnor in the north and his sons founded Gondor in the south, with Minas Ithil, Minas Anor and Osgiliath; Sauron, whose fair body had perished in the Downfall, returned to Mordor as a spirit.
  29. c. 33,012 BC
    Sauron attacks Gondor
    In the year 3429 Sauron attacked Gondor, took Minas Ithil and burned the White Tree; Isildur escaped with a seedling, and Anárion held Osgiliath.
  30. c. 33,007 BC
    The Last Alliance at Dagorlad
    Gil-galad and Elendil formed the Last Alliance of Elves and Men in the year 3430, and in 3434 their host defeated Sauron on the plain of Dagorlad before the Black Gate and laid siege to Barad-dûr for seven years.

The Third Age: the War of the Ring

  1. c. 33,000 BC
    Sauron overthrown
    In the year 3441 Sauron came out to fight on the slopes of Orodruin and slew Gil-galad and Elendil, and Narsil broke beneath Elendil as he fell; Isildur took up the hilt-shard and cut the One Ring from Sauron's hand, and Sauron was overthrown.
  2. c. 33,000 BC
    Isildur keeps the Ring
    Though Elrond and Círdan counselled him to cast it into the fire, Isildur kept the One Ring as weregild for his father and his brother, and so the Second Age ended.
  3. c. 32,998 BC
    The Gladden Fields
    In the year 2 of the Third Age Isildur and his three elder sons were waylaid by Orcs at the Gladden Fields; he put on the Ring and fled into the Anduin, but it slipped from his finger and he was slain, and the Ring lay lost in the river for two and a half thousand years.
  4. c. 32,998 BC
    Narsil kept at Rivendell
    The shards of Narsil were carried to Rivendell, where Isildur's youngest son Valandil was being fostered, and they were kept for three thousand years as the heirloom of Isildur's heirs.
  5. c. 32,759 BC
    Arwen is born
    In the year 241 Arwen Undómiel, the Evenstar, was born to Elrond and Celebrían, daughter of Galadriel; she was said to bear the likeness of Lúthien.
  6. c. 32,001 BC
    The Valar choose the Istari
    The Valar met in council to send messengers to Middle-earth against Sauron; Olórin said that he feared Sauron and was too weak, and Manwë answered that this was the more reason why he should go.
  7. c. 32,000 BC
    The Istari come over the Sea
    About the year 1000 of the Third Age five Istari, Maiar sent on commission in the likeness of old men, landed at the Grey Havens to unite all who would resist Sauron; Saruman the White came first, and they were forbidden to match his power with power or to dominate the minds of those they came to help.
  8. c. 32,000 BC
    Círdan gives Narya to Gandalf
    Gandalf came last of the five, seeming the least of them, and Círdan at the Grey Havens gave him Narya, the Ring of Fire, set with a red stone; Radagast the Brown went to the borders of the Greenwood.
  9. c. 31,998 BC
    The Blue Wizards go east
    The two Blue Wizards, the Ithryn Luin, went into the far East with Saruman and never returned, and the record of them goes vague, never settling what became of them.
  10. c. 31,995 BC
    Zordon is sent to Eltar
    One of the two Blue Wizards went further than anyone was keeping records of, off the world altogether to Eltar; he became Zordon of Eltar, Gandalf's equal and colleague of the same commission, while Gandalf's charge was the Earth.
  11. c. 31,900 BC
    The Necromancer of Dol Guldur
    About the year 1100 the Wise discovered that an evil power had made a stronghold at Dol Guldur in southern Mirkwood; they thought it one of the Nazgûl, but it was Sauron taking shape again.
  12. c. 31,700 BC
    The Witch-king rises in Angmar
    About the year 1300 the Nazgûl stirred again, and their chief came north and founded the realm of Angmar, where he was called the Witch-king, and made war on the divided kingdoms of Arnor.
  13. c. 31,563 BC
    The Kin-strife
    In the year 1437, in the Kin-strife of Gondor, Castamir the Usurper drove out King Eldacar, Osgiliath was burned and its Seeing-stone lost in the river; Eldacar returned in 1447 and slew Castamir.
  14. c. 31,399 BC
    The Shire founded
    In the year 1601 the hobbit brothers Marcho and Blanco crossed the Brandywine with leave of the King at Fornost, and the Shire was founded.
  15. c. 31,025 BC
    The end of the North-kingdom
    In the year 1974 the Witch-king took Fornost, and in 1975 King Arvedui was drowned in the Ice Bay of Forochel and the kingdom of Arnor came to an end; the heirs of Isildur became the hidden Rangers of the North.
  16. c. 31,025 BC
    The Battle of Fornost
    In the year 1975 Eärnur of Gondor and Glorfindel of Rivendell overthrew the Witch-king at the Battle of Fornost, and Glorfindel foretold that he would not fall by the hand of man.
  17. c. 31,020 BC
    Durin's Bane wakes in Moria
    In the year 1980 the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm delved too deep and woke a Balrog, which slew King Durin VI, and Moria was soon abandoned; the same year the Witch-king came to Mordor and gathered the Nazgûl.
  18. c. 30,950 BC
    Eärnur rides to Minas Morgul
    In the year 2050 Eärnur, last King of Gondor, accepted the Witch-king's challenge, rode to Minas Morgul, the Tower of Sorcery that had once been Minas Ithil, and was never seen again; Mardil began the rule of the Stewards.
  19. c. 30,937 BC
    The Watchful Peace
    In the year 2063 Gandalf went to Dol Guldur and Sauron withdrew into the East, and the Watchful Peace began; it ended in 2460, when Sauron returned to Dol Guldur.
  20. c. 30,537 BC
    Sméagol murders Déagol
    About the year 2463, the year the White Council was formed, the river-hobbit Déagol found the One Ring in the Anduin near the Gladden Fields, and his friend Sméagol strangled him for it on his birthday; Sméagol became Gollum and hid under the Misty Mountains with the Ring, which lengthened his life and wore it thin.
  21. c. 30,490 BC
    Eorl and the founding of Rohan
    In the year 2510 Eorl the Young rode from the north to the Field of Celebrant and saved Gondor, and Cirion the Steward gave his people Calenardhon, which became Rohan; the same year Celebrían, wounded by Orcs, passed over the Sea.
  22. c. 30,230 BC
    Smaug takes Erebor
    In the year 2770 the dragon Smaug descended on the Lonely Mountain, drove out the Dwarves of Erebor and destroyed the town of Dale.
  23. c. 30,150 BC
    Gandalf in Dol Guldur
    In the year 2850 Gandalf entered Dol Guldur in secret and discovered that its master was Sauron, gathering the Rings and seeking news of the One; he found Thráin dying in the dungeons and received from him a map and a key.
  24. c. 30,069 BC
    Aragorn is born
    On 1 March in the year 2931 Aragorn son of Arathorn, the heir of Isildur, was born, the last of the line whose ancestors had come out of drowned Númenor.
  25. c. 30,067 BC
    Aragorn raised as Estel
    In the year 2933 Arathorn was slain, and his widow Gilraen took the boy to Rivendell, where Elrond fostered him under the name Estel, Hope.
  26. c. 30,059 BC
    Gandalf sends Bilbo to Erebor
    In April of the year 2941 Gandalf sent Bilbo Baggins out of the Shire as burglar to Thorin Oakenshield and twelve Dwarves, to win back the Lonely Mountain from Smaug.
  27. c. 30,059 BC
    Bilbo finds the Ring
    In July of the year 2941 Bilbo, lost in the goblin tunnels under the Misty Mountains, found a ring on the floor and won his way out of Gollum's cave in a contest of riddles; the Ring had wanted to be found.
  28. c. 30,059 BC
    The Battle of Five Armies
    In the autumn of 2941 Bard the Bowman shot down Smaug over Lake-town, and Elves, Men, Dwarves and Eagles defeated the Goblins and Wargs before the Lonely Mountain; Thorin died of his wounds.
  29. c. 30,058 BC
    Bilbo comes home with the Ring
    In the year 2942 Bilbo returned to Bag End with the Ring, and Sauron secretly returned to Mordor.
  30. c. 30,049 BC
    Aragorn learns his lineage and meets Arwen
    In the year 2951 Elrond told Estel his true name and ancestry and gave him the shards of Narsil, and the next day, in the woods of Rivendell, Aragorn met Arwen and loved her.
  31. c. 30,047 BC
    Saruman takes Isengard
    In the year 2953 the White Council met for the last time, and Saruman withdrew to Isengard, coveting the One Ring for himself.
  32. c. 30,044 BC
    Aragorn meets Gandalf
    In the year 2956 Aragorn met Gandalf, and their long friendship began.
  33. c. 30,043 BC
    Aragorn's errantries
    From the year 2957 Aragorn went on great journeys, serving in disguise as Thorongil under Thengel of Rohan and Ecthelion of Gondor, and as a Ranger of the North he guarded Eriador unthanked; to the folk of Bree he was Strider.
  34. c. 30,020 BC
    Troth plighted on Cerin Amroth
    In the year 2980 Aragorn met Arwen again in Lothlórien and gave her the ring of Barahir, and they plighted their troth on the hill of Cerin Amroth; Elrond would not let them wed until Aragorn was king of both Gondor and Arnor.
  35. c. 29,999 BC
    Bilbo's farewell party
    In the year 3001 Bilbo held his farewell party, left the Shire and gave the Ring to Frodo Baggins, and Gandalf first suspected that it was the One.
  36. c. 29,982 BC
    The fire at Bag End
    In April of the year 3018, in a little round room with a fire in the grate at Bag End, Gandalf threw Frodo's ring on the fire and read the letters of fire that rose on it, one Ring to rule them all, and knew it for the One.
  37. c. 29,982 BC
    Gandalf imprisoned in Orthanc
    In July 3018 Saruman revealed his treachery and imprisoned Gandalf on the pinnacle of Orthanc, whence Gwaihir the eagle bore him away in September.
  38. c. 29,982 BC
    Strider at the Prancing Pony
    On 29 September 3018 Frodo, fleeing the Black Riders, came to the Prancing Pony at Bree, where a weather-stained ranger called Strider sat hooded in a dark corner; it was Aragorn, who guided the hobbits towards Rivendell.
  39. c. 29,982 BC
    Frodo wounded on Weathertop
    On 6 October 3018 the Witch-king and four other Ringwraiths attacked on Weathertop and wounded Frodo with a Morgul knife, and on 20 October Frodo escaped them over the Ford of Bruinen.
  40. c. 29,982 BC
    The Council of Elrond
    On 25 October 3018 the Council of Elrond at Rivendell resolved to destroy the Ring in the fire where it was made, and Frodo took the task upon himself.
  41. c. 29,982 BC
    Narsil reforged as Andúril
    Before the Fellowship set out, the Elven smiths of Rivendell reforged the shards of Narsil for Aragorn, and he named it Andúril, Flame of the West; its blade was traced with seven stars between a crescent moon and a rayed sun.
  42. c. 29,982 BC
    The Fellowship sets out
    On 25 December 3018 the Fellowship of the Ring set out from Rivendell: Frodo, Sam, Merry, Pippin, Gandalf, Aragorn, Boromir, Legolas and Gimli.
  43. c. 29,981 BC
    Gandalf falls in Moria
    On 15 January 3019 Gandalf held the Bridge of Khazad-dûm against Durin's Bane, the Balrog of Moria, and fell with it into the abyss.
  44. c. 29,981 BC
    Gandalf the White
    Gandalf pursued the Balrog to the peak of Zirakzigil and threw it down on 25 January 3019, and died; he was sent back on 14 February as Gandalf the White.
  45. c. 29,981 BC
    The Breaking of the Fellowship
    On 26 February 3019 the Fellowship was broken at Parth Galen: Boromir fell defending Merry and Pippin, and Frodo and Sam went on alone towards Mordor.
  46. c. 29,981 BC
    Helm's Deep
    On 3 March 3019 the Rohirrim under Théoden, with Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli, held the Hornburg at Helm's Deep against the host of Saruman, and at dawn the host was destroyed.
  47. c. 29,981 BC
    Saruman's staff broken
    On 5 March 3019 Gandalf cast Saruman out of the order of the Istari and broke his staff on the stair of Orthanc.
  48. c. 29,981 BC
    Aragorn wrestles Sauron in the palantír
    On 6 March 3019 Aragorn looked into the palantír of Orthanc and wrestled with Sauron himself through it, showing him the reforged sword, and from then on he stopped doubting that he would be king.
  49. c. 29,981 BC
    The Paths of the Dead
    On 8 March 3019 Aragorn took the Paths of the Dead under the White Mountains, which everybody told him led only to death, came out at the other end, and summoned the Oathbreakers to the Stone of Erech.
  50. c. 29,981 BC
    The Battle of the Pelennor Fields
    On 15 March 3019 the Witch-king was slain by Éowyn and Merry on the Pelennor Fields before Minas Tirith, and Aragorn came up the Anduin on the black ships with a star on his brow, Arwen's standard unfurled and Andúril drawn, and turned the battle.
  51. c. 29,981 BC
    The hands of the king
    That night in the Houses of Healing Aragorn laid his hands on Faramir, Éowyn and Merry and they woke, and the old woman Ioreth said that the hands of the king are the hands of a healer.
  52. c. 29,981 BC
    The One Ring destroyed
    On 25 March 3019 the One Ring, the first Horcrux, was destroyed in the fire of Orodruin where it was made, when Gollum seized it from Frodo and fell; Barad-dûr fell and Sauron's power ended for ever.
  53. c. 29,981 BC
    Aragorn crowned
    On 1 May 3019 Gandalf set the crown on Aragorn's head before the gates of Minas Tirith, and he became King Elessar of Gondor and Arnor.
  54. c. 29,981 BC
    Aragorn weds Arwen
    At Midsummer of the year 3019 Aragorn wedded Arwen in Minas Tirith; she chose the mortality of Men, and from their line, which carried the Elves and Númenor together, would come Godric Gryffindor, the Pevensies and Harry Potter.
  55. c. 29,981 BC
    The Battle of Bywater
    On 3 November 3019 the hobbits drove Saruman's ruffians out of the Shire at the Battle of Bywater, and Saruman was killed by Gríma Wormtongue at Bag End.

The Fourth Age and the forgotten ages

  1. c. 29,979 BC
    The Ring-bearers sail West
    On 29 September 3021 Frodo and Bilbo sailed from the Grey Havens into the West with Elrond, Galadriel and Gandalf, who bore Narya openly at last; it was the end of the Third Age.
  2. c. 29,919 BC
    Samwise sails
    In the year 61 of the Fourth Age, after the death of his wife Rose, Samwise Gamgee rode to the Grey Havens and sailed into the West, the last of the Ring-bearers.
  3. c. 29,860 BC
    King Elessar dies
    On 1 March in the year 120 of the Fourth Age King Elessar laid down his life at the age of two hundred and ten, after a reign of a hundred and twenty years, and his son Eldarion took the throne.
  4. c. 29,860 BC
    Andúril passes to Eldarion
    Andúril passed to Eldarion and went on down the line of Aragorn and Arwen, carried by a series of brave men through the ages.
  5. c. 29,860 BC
    Legolas and Gimli sail
    After Elessar's death Legolas built a grey ship in Ithilien and sailed down the Anduin and over the Sea, taking Gimli the Dwarf with him, and the last of the Fellowship passed out of Middle-earth.
  6. c. 29,859 BC
    Arwen dies on Cerin Amroth
    Arwen went alone to Lórien, empty by then, and in the year 121 of the Fourth Age, when the mallorn leaves were falling, she laid herself to rest on the hill of Cerin Amroth.
  7. c. 29,000 BC
    The Elves pass out of the world
    Through the Fourth Age, the Dominion of Men, the last of the Elves took ship into the West or faded, and elven craftsmanship went with them, so that a thing like the One Ring could never be made again: the missing part was not knowledge but a people.
  8. c. 28,000 BC
    Cain walks through the Middle-earth ages
    Through the Third and Fourth Ages and the forgotten ages after them Cain still wandered, older than the Istari and the Rings, unseen by the Wise, a cursed man who could not die and had no powers.
  9. c. 27,000 BC
    The heirs of Elessar endure
    In the lost ages after the Fourth Age the line of Aragorn and Arwen went on unrecognised among Men, carrying the blood of the Elves and of Númenor.

The Thurian Age

  1. c. 24,000 BC
    The serpent men rule Valusia
    In the lost ages after the Fourth Age the serpent men, an ancient race who served the Old Serpent and practised his sorcery, ruled the land of Valusia on the Thurian continent.
  2. c. 22,000 BC
    Men cast down the serpent men
    Kings of men overthrew the serpent men and took Valusia for their own, but the serpent men lingered in hiding, able by their sorcery to wear the faces of men.
  3. c. 21,000 BC
    The Seven Empires of the Thurian Age
    Valusia, eldest and greatest of the Seven Empires, flourished with Kamelia, Verulia, Grondar, Thule and Commoria on the Thurian continent, while barbarian Atlantis lay in the ocean to the west, the Pictish Isles beyond it, and the isles of Lemuria in the east.
  4. c. 20,000 BC
    Atlanteans and Picts at war
    The barbarian Atlanteans and the Picts of the western isles waged long wars on one another, and Valusia kept the Picts as allies.
  5. c. 18,620 BC
    Kull is born in Atlantis
    Kull was born in Atlantis, a foundling who grew up wild in the Tiger Valley until the Sea-mountain tribe took him in.
  6. c. 18,602 BC
    Kull exiled from Atlantis
    As a youth Kull broke the law of his tribe by killing a girl condemned to the stake so that she would not suffer the fire, and fled Atlantis an exile.
  7. c. 18,595 BC
    Kull's wandering years
    Kull was in turn a pirate, a galley slave of the Lemurians, an outlaw, a gladiator and a soldier of the Valusian armies, in which he rose to high command.
  8. c. 18,580 BC
    Kull takes the throne of Valusia
    Kull slew the tyrant Borna and took the throne of Valusia, an Atlantean barbarian on the seat of the oldest kingdom of men.
  9. c. 18,578 BC
    The Shadow Kingdom
    Warned by Ka-nu, the Pictish ambassador, Kull and the Pict Brule the Spear-slayer uncovered serpent men wearing the faces of his own court, exposed them with the ancient words 'Ka nama kaa lajerama' and slew them.
  10. c. 18,575 BC
    The Mirrors of Tuzun Thune
    The wizard Tuzun Thune lured Kull into gazing into his enchanted mirrors until he nearly passed into them, and Brule saved the king by running the wizard through.
  11. c. 18,570 BC
    By this axe I rule
    When Ardyon and a band of conspirators fell on him in his chamber, Kull fought them off, then broke with his axe the ancient tablet of law so that the girl Lala-ah could marry Seno val Dor, the man she loved, crying 'By this axe I rule!'
  12. c. 18,565 BC
    Kull and Thulsa Doom
    Kull thwarted the plotting of the skull-faced necromancer Thulsa Doom, a sorcerer of the old dark craft who fled from him rather than be destroyed.

The Hyborian Age

  1. c. 18,000 BC
    The Cataclysm
    The Thurian Age ended in the Cataclysm: Atlantis and Lemuria sank beneath the sea, the Pictish Isles were heaved up to become the peaks of a new continent, and Valusia and the Seven Empires were broken by earthquake, fire and flood.
  2. c. 17,800 BC
    The survivors of the Cataclysm
    The Atlanteans of a colony on the mainland survived the Cataclysm and fell back into ape-like savagery, the Picts sank to the Stone Age, and a remnant of the Thurian folk, the Zhemri, endured in the eastern hills.
  3. c. 17,000 BC
    The Lemurians enslaved
    Survivors of Lemuria who reached the eastern shores were enslaved by an ancient race that dwelt there.
  4. c. 16,500 BC
    The Hyborians appear in the north
    In the north a tribe descended from Thurian survivors grew into a nation of hunters named after their chief Bori, who was later worshipped as a god; these were the Hyborians.
  5. c. 16,000 BC
    The founding of Stygia
    The Lemurians rose and threw off their masters, and the ancient race, driven westward, conquered the land south of the river Styx and founded Stygia, the serpent kingdom.
  6. c. 15,500 BC
    Hyperborea founded
    The Hyborians drifted south and built their first kingdom, Hyperborea, with fortresses of uncut stone.
  7. c. 15,000 BC
    Set worshipped in Stygia
    The Stygians worshipped Set, the Old Serpent, who was the being once called Morgoth, in black temples where a great serpent was kept and fed, and their sorcerers learned their art from the thing in those temples and paid dearly for it.
  8. c. 14,800 BC
    Stygia becomes the library of dark magic
    Stygia did not invent dark magic, but there Morgoth's craft was kept, collected, systematised and practised at scale, and most dark spells still in use derive at least in part from what Stygia held.
  9. c. 14,500 BC
    Acheron rises
    Acheron, an empire of sorcerers whose capital was purple-towered Python, rose in the lands that would later be Aquilonia, Nemedia and Argos.
  10. c. 14,000 BC
    The Cimmerians emerge
    Over long ages the descendants of the Atlanteans climbed back out of savagery and became the Cimmerians, a grim people of the dark northern hills.
  11. c. 13,050 BC
    Xaltotun of Python
    Xaltotun of Python, a priest of Set and the greatest sorcerer of Acheron, wielded the Heart of Ahriman, a jewel that burned like living fire.
  12. c. 13,040 BC
    The fall of Acheron
    The barbarian Hyborians overthrew Acheron three thousand years before Conan's reign; Xaltotun's body was hidden away and the Heart of Ahriman taken from him, and Acheron's surviving sorcerers fled into Stygia with their craft.
  13. c. 12,500 BC
    The Hyborian kingdoms
    In the centuries after Acheron's fall the Hyborians founded Nemedia, Koth, Ophir, Argos, Corinthia and the Border Kingdom, and in the west Aquilonia, which became the mightiest of them.
  14. c. 12,000 BC
    Cain wanders the Hyborian world
    Through the Hyborian Age Cain walked unnoticed among its kingdoms and sorcerers, older than Stygia and still no vampire, only a cursed man who could not die.
  15. c. 11,550 BC
    Epemitreus the Sage
    Epemitreus the Sage, who had fought Set and his servants all his life, died and was laid in a crypt beneath Mount Golamira in Aquilonia, fifteen hundred years before Conan's reign.
  16. c. 11,000 BC
    Turan founded
    The Hyrkanians, descendants of the Lemurians, came out of the east round the inland Vilayet Sea and founded the kingdom of Turan on its western shore.
  17. c. 10,400 BC
    The Nephilim are born
    In the days before the Flood the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men, and their children were the Nephilim, giants in the earth, mighty men of old, men of renown; the Book of Enoch tells that their fathers were the Watchers, angels who had left their place.
  18. c. 10,350 BC
    Noah is born
    Noah was born to Lamech, a descendant of Seth son of Adam, who named him saying that this son would comfort them concerning their work and the toil of their hands on the ground which the Lord had cursed.
  19. c. 10,200 BC
    The giants devour men
    The Nephilim consumed all that men could grow and then turned to devouring men themselves, and the earth was filled with violence.
  20. c. 10,090 BC
    Conan is born in Cimmeria
    Conan was born in Cimmeria, among the dark hills of the north, of a ritual in which a circle of the elder world's sorcerers gave their lives so that their power would be reborn together in a single child.
  21. c. 10,075 BC
    The sack of Venarium
    At fifteen Conan was among the Cimmerian warriors who stormed and burned Venarium, the Aquilonian fort on their southern border.
  22. c. 10,073 BC
    The Frost-Giant's Daughter
    Fighting beside the Æsir against the Vanir in the snows of Nordheim, Conan pursued Atali, daughter of Ymir the frost-giant, across the ice.
  23. c. 10,070 BC
    Thoth-Amon of the Black Ring
    In Stygia Thoth-Amon, mightiest sorcerer of the Black Ring, drew his power from the Serpent Ring of Set and kept the dark craft of the serpent kingdom.
  24. c. 10,070 BC
    The Tower of the Elephant
    As a young thief in Zamora Conan climbed the Tower of the Elephant to steal its jewel and found Yag-Kosha, a blinded being from the stars, enslaved by the sorcerer Yara; at his bidding Conan used the Heart of the Elephant to destroy Yara and his tower.
  25. c. 10,069 BC
    The God in the Bowl
    In the temple of Kallian Publico in Numalia in Nemedia, Conan, accused of murder, faced a serpent thing out of Stygia that had been sent there sealed in a bowl.
  26. c. 10,065 BC
    Conan and Bêlit
    Conan joined Bêlit, the pirate queen of the Black Coast, on her ship the Tigress, and her black corsairs called him Amra, the Lion.
  27. c. 10,063 BC
    The death of Bêlit
    In a ruined city on the river Zarkheba Bêlit was killed by a winged demon like an ape; Conan laid her on the Tigress and sent her burning out to sea.
  28. c. 10,062 BC
    Black Colossus
    Made general of Khoraja's armies by Princess Yasmela, Conan destroyed Natohk the Veiled One, the sorcerer Thugra Khotan, who had woken from three thousand years' sleep in ruined Kuthchemes.
  29. c. 10,061 BC
    A Witch Shall Be Born
    In Khauran the witch Salome usurped the throne of her twin sister Queen Taramis and had Conan, captain of the guard, crucified in the desert; he survived and returned to overthrow her.
  30. c. 10,060 BC
    The People of the Black Circle
    As chief of the Afghuli hillmen of the Himelian Mountains, Conan carried off Yasmina, the Devi of Vendhya, and with her broke the Black Seers of Mount Yimsha.
  31. c. 10,058 BC
    Red Nails
    With Valeria of the Red Brotherhood, Conan came upon the walled city of Xuchotl in the southern jungles and ended both its long feud between the Tecuhltli and the Xotalanc and the witch Tascela.
  32. c. 10,056 BC
    Beyond the Black River
    Serving as a scout at Fort Tuscelan on the Pictish frontier of Aquilonia, Conan fought the Pictish wizard Zogar Sag, whose swamp devils and painted warriors destroyed the fort.
  33. c. 10,053 BC
    Thoth-Amon loses the Serpent Ring
    Thoth-Amon lost the Serpent Ring of Set to a thief, fled Stygia, and fell into slavery to the outlaw Ascalante.
  34. c. 10,050 BC
    Conan seizes Aquilonia's throne
    As general of Aquilonia's armies on the western frontier, Conan led a rebellion against the mad king Numedides and strangled him on his own throne, taking the crown of Aquilonia with his own hand at about forty years of age.
  35. c. 10,049 BC
    The Phoenix on the Sword
    Ascalante and his Rebel Four plotted to murder King Conan; the shade of Epemitreus marked Conan's sword with a phoenix in a dream, and Thoth-Amon, his ring regained, sent a demon out of Set's darkness that slew Ascalante and was slain by Conan with the marked sword.
  36. c. 10,048 BC
    The Scarlet Citadel
    Betrayed by Strabonus of Koth and Amalrus of Ophir, Conan was cast into the dungeons beneath the Scarlet Citadel of Khorshemish by the wizard Tsotha-lanti, freed the imprisoned sorcerer Pelias, and returned to save his throne.
  37. c. 10,045 BC
    The Hour of the Dragon
    The priest Orastes raised Xaltotun from his three-thousand-year sleep with the Heart of Ahriman; by his sorcery Tarascus of Nemedia and the pretender Valerius overthrew Conan at Valkia, and Conan escaped the pits of Belverus with the help of the girl Zenobia.
  38. c. 10,044 BC
    Conan in Khemi
    Pursuing the stolen Heart of Ahriman, Conan went into Stygia, to the black city of Khemi and the dark places of Set, and won the jewel back.
  39. c. 10,044 BC
    Conan regains his throne
    With the Heart of Ahriman Conan destroyed Xaltotun and won back the throne of Aquilonia, and made Zenobia his queen.
  40. c. 10,025 BC
    Conan lays down his crown
    Conan gave the crown of Aquilonia to his son Conn and sailed west into the unknown lands beyond the ocean. In the years that followed he understood that he was not growing old, and could not die.
  41. c. 9980 BC
    The Hyrkanians press west
    In the generations after Conan the Hyrkanians pressed in from the east and the Hyborian kingdoms began to fall apart in war.
  42. c. 9960 BC
    The ice begins to come down
    The ice began to come down out of the north, until it lay a mile thick on the mountains, and drove the Nordic peoples, the Æsir and the Vanir, south against the failing Hyborian kingdoms.
  43. c. 9950 BC
    Arus and Gorm
    A Nemedian priest named Arus went among the Picts to teach them the gentle worship of Mitra, but their chief Gorm learned from him and his kind the arts of war and iron, and united the Pictish clans.
  44. c. 9930 BC
    The Picts overrun Aquilonia
    Under Gorm the Picts broke over the Black River and overran Aquilonia, and the Hyborian kingdoms fell to Picts, Hyrkanians and Nordic invaders.
  45. c. 9900 BC
    The second great cataclysm
    A second great cataclysm shook the west of the world: lands sank and seas broke in, the dominion of the Picts was thrown down, and the wrecks of the Hyborian kingdoms were scattered under the ice, though Stygia's black towers still stood by the warm seas.
  46. c. 9850 BC
    Shem, Ham and Japheth are born
    When Noah was five hundred years old he begat Shem, Ham and Japheth.

Noah's Flood and the end of the Ice Age

  1. c. 9820 BC
    God's warning to Noah
    God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth and resolved to destroy all flesh; but Noah found grace in His eyes, and God told him that the end of all flesh was come and commanded him to build an ark.
  2. c. 9800 BC
    Noah builds the ark
    At God's command Noah built an ark of gopher wood, three hundred cubits long, fifty broad and thirty high, pitched within and without, with rooms, a window and a door in its side; Noah did all that God commanded him.
  3. c. 9750 BC
    Noah enters the ark
    When Noah was six hundred years old he went into the ark with his wife, his sons Shem, Ham and Japheth and their wives, and the beasts of the earth went in with him two by two, and the Lord shut him in.
  4. c. 9750 BC
    Noah's Flood ends the Ice Age
    The ice that had lain a mile thick on the mountains of the north went back at last, groaning and cracking, and its meltwater came down over the old world. That was the Flood of Genesis, the forty days of rain and the waters that rose above the mountains, God's judgement on the old world. Noah, who had built the ark at God's command, was saved in it with his family and the animals while everything else drowned.
  5. c. 9750 BC
    The rains and the rising waters
    The fountains of the great deep were broken up and the windows of heaven were opened, and it rained forty days and forty nights; the waters increased and bore up the ark, and it went upon the face of the waters.
  6. c. 9740 BC
    The waters at their height
    The waters prevailed exceedingly upon the earth, fifteen cubits above the highest mountains, and every living thing outside the ark perished; the Nephilim, who were under no sentence of immortality, drowned with the rest.
  7. c. 9740 BC
    Stygia and the Hyborian world drowned
    The Flood drowned whole countries: the black towers of Stygia by the warm seas, the temples where men had worshipped a great serpent and fed it, and the sorcerers who had learned their craft from the thing in those temples.
  8. c. 9740 BC
    Knowledge of the elder ages drowned
    Nearly all knowledge of the ages of Middle-earth and of the Hyborian Age went under the water, so that they would reach later times only as story, and a wizard digging for the origins of his craft would find Egypt, then Stygia, then nothing.
  9. c. 9740 BC
    Cain survives the Flood
    Cain came through the Flood because he could not die: God had already sentenced him to live, and God does not revoke His own sentences, so he went into the water a cursed man and came out of it a cursed man, still no vampire.
  10. c. 9740 BC
    The line of Aragorn survives the Flood
    The line of Aragorn and Arwen survived the Flood and the forgetting of the old ages, carrying the magic of Elves and of Númenor in its blood towards Godric Gryffindor, the Pevensies and Harry Potter.
  11. c. 9740 BC
    Morgoth's craft scattered, not drowned
    The dark craft that Stygia had kept was scattered rather than drowned: one Stygian sorcerer lived through the water carrying its broken remnants, the man history would later miscall Herpo the Foul.
  12. c. 9720 BC
    The ark rests on Ararat
