    In the seventh month, on the seventeenth day of the month, as the waters went down, the ark came to rest upon the mountains of Ararat.
  13. c. 9715 BC
    The raven and the dove
    Noah sent out a raven, and then a dove, which came back the second time with an olive leaf plucked off in her mouth, and the third time did not return.
  14. c. 9705 BC
    Noah leaves the ark
    When the face of the ground was dry, Noah came out of the ark with his household and the beasts, built an altar to the Lord and offered burnt offerings on it.
  15. c. 9700 BC
    The covenant of the rainbow
    God blessed Noah and his sons and made His covenant with them and with every living creature, that the waters would never again become a flood to destroy all flesh, and He set His bow in the cloud as its token.

After the Flood: Cain, the First City and the first vampires

  1. c. 9600 BC
    God sends Gandalf to teach light magic
    After the Flood that ended the Ice Age, God sent the Maia Gandalf to the few frightened families of men left on the cold new shores, to teach them light magic as a counterweight to Morgoth. By their fires he taught them how to call a flame, ask the rain to wait, heal a cut and know that a voice from the dark offering power is never a friend's.
  2. c. 9598 BC
    Gandalf teaches the first Patronus Charm
    Among the first spells Gandalf gave the earliest wizards of men after the ice went back was the Patronus Charm, a defence against Morgoth's works and the only spell that has no dark version. The hands that passed it down were afterwards forgotten.
  3. c. 9595 BC
    Noah plants a vineyard
    In the years after the Flood Noah became a husbandman and planted a vineyard. Every man living after the Flood descends from him and his three sons.
  4. c. 9590 BC
    Cain meets Lilith
    Shortly after the Flood the cursed, deathless wanderer Cain met Lilith, a powerful immortal servant of Morgoth, who lied to him that she was Adam's first wife, the woman made before Eve who would not bow. He believed her.
  5. c. 9585 BC
    Cain learns blood magic and becomes the first vampire
    Lilith showed Cain the power in his own cursed blood and taught him blood magic, and he drank and became a vampire as the Kindred know them, with the Beast, the thirst and the Disciplines: the First Generation. He thought he was being given relief from his sentence; the bargain put him and every vampire after him under Morgoth's will.
  6. c. 9550 BC
    A Stygian survivor invents the modern Horcrux
    A Stygian sorcerer who lived on after the Flood, the man history calls Herpo the Foul and wrongly makes a Greek, gathered the broken remnants of Morgoth's craft and filled the gaps by guesswork. The result was the modern Horcrux, the One Ring reverse-engineered at the price of the maker's torn soul.
  7. c. 9500 BC
    Cain Embraces Enoch, Irad and Zillah
    After a time alone with his blood in the land of Nod, Cain Embraced three childer, Enoch, Irad and Zillah, who became the Second Generation of vampires.
  8. c. 9450 BC
    Enoch, the First City, is built
    With his three childer and the mortals who gathered to them, Cain built a city and named it Enoch after his eldest childe. It was the First City, and its vampires ruled it openly as gods.
  9. c. 9400 BC
    The Garou begin the Impergium
    In the age after the ice, fearing mankind's numbers and its growing works, the Garou began to hold humanity down by culling it. They call this age, which lasted some three thousand years, the Impergium, and many hold that the Delirium is its memory.
  10. c. 9400 BC
    Noah dies
    Noah died three hundred and fifty years after the Flood, at the age of nine hundred and fifty.
  11. c. 9300 BC
    The Antediluvians are Embraced; Cain forbids more
    The Second Generation Embraced thirteen childer of their own, the Third Generation or Antediluvians, founders of the thirteen clans: Brujah, Ennoia of the Gangrel, Malkav, Absimiliard of the Nosferatu, Arikel of the Toreador, the Ventrue founder, Lasombra, the Eldest of the Tzimisce, Haqim of the Assamites, Set, Ravnos, Saulot of the Salubri and Cappadocius. Seeing what the blood was becoming, Cain forbade any more Embraces.
  12. c. 9200 BC
    The Garou divide into tribes
    The Garou, once a single people, grew apart into tribes in the ages after the ice, each following its own totem spirit and its own Kinfolk across the world. The Silver Fangs led the Garou Nation from those ages onwards.
  13. c. 9000 BC
    The First City falls
    In time Enoch, the First City of Cain and his childer, fell.
  14. c. 9000 BC
    The first Slayer is made
    In the ages after the Flood, as the childer of Cain spread across the world, the men the Watchers remember as the Shadow Men worked a ritual that drew on the dwindling power of the Solar Exalted and bound it into a girl, the first Slayer, a guardian of the people where she lived.
  15. c. 8990 BC
    The Third Generation slays the Second
    The thirteen Antediluvians of the Third Generation rose against their sires and slew Enoch, Irad and Zillah of the Second.
  16. c. 8980 BC
    Cain curses the clans and departs into Nod
    Cain cursed the clans for the slaying, laying on each its own weakness, so that Absimiliard, once the most beautiful of the Third Generation, and all his Nosferatu line were made to wear their cruelty on their faces. Then Cain departed into the wilderness of Nod and has not ruled his get since.
  17. c. 8500 BC
    The Garou wage the War of Rage
    In the same ages as the Impergium the Garou made war on the other shapeshifting peoples, among them the bear-folk, cat-folk and raven-folk, and destroyed several of them outright. They count the War of Rage among their great shames.
  18. c. 8000 BC
    The D'ni come to the cavern under New Mexico
    Ri'neref led the D'ni, descendants of the Ronay of the Age of Garternay, through a linking book into an enormous cavern deep beneath what is now the New Mexico desert. They gave the cavern, the city they raised round its underground lake and themselves the one name, D'ni.
  19. c. 8000 BC
    Zordon's war with Rita Repulsa
    Some ten thousand years ago the sorceress Rita Repulsa made war on Zordon on Earth and on Eltar; her curse put him in a tube outside time with no body to return to, and he sealed her and her servants in a space dumpster that came to rest on the Moon.
  20. c. 7990 BC
    The D'ni enslave the Bahro
    The D'ni took the cavern from its original inhabitants, the Bahro, and enslaved them, binding them by a stone Tablet whose holder could command them; there are signs the Bahro were once hunted for sport.
  21. c. 7500 BC
    The Warders of Men watch over the first towns
    In the earliest towns the Garou who lived among humans and watched over them were called the Warders of Men, the forerunners of the Glass Walkers, while the Bone Gnawers followed people into the towns and scavenged at their edges.
  22. c. 7000 BC
    The Kree experiment on Earth
    In the thousands of years after the Flood the Kree took a tribe of hunters and altered them, hoping to make soldiers, then lost interest and left. Their descendants are the Inhumans.
  23. c. 6400 BC
    The Concord ends the Impergium
    The Impergium ended at a great gathering of the Garou tribes called the Concord, where the Children of Gaia were foremost in calling for its end. The Garou agreed to hide among men rather than rule them by fear, and took the Litany as their common law.
  24. c. 5000 BC
    Attilan is built
    The Inhumans built Attilan on an island far out in the North Atlantic.
  25. c. 3100 BC
    Egypt inherits Stygia's dark craft
    Ancient Egypt rose as Stygia's descendant and heir, and everything the European wizarding tradition calls ancient and dark came through Egypt first.

Antiquity and the first ages of magic

  1. c. 3000 BC
    Set is worshipped as a god in Egypt
    The Antediluvian Set was worshipped as a god in ancient Egypt, where he murdered Osiris and fought Horus. His childer, the Followers of Set, revere him as a god who sleeps and will rise to rule.
  2. c. 3000 BC
    Egypt rises against Ra
    Thousands of years ago the people of Egypt rose against Ra, the Goa'uld who ruled them as sun god and carried Egyptians through the Stargate as slaves to Abydos. Thor, the son of Odin, came down in a storm to fight beside them. Ra fled, and they buried his gate at Giza under cover stones declaring it sealed for all time.
  3. c. 3000 BC
    Ra forbids the Goa'uld to speak of Earth
    After the rising in Egypt, in which Thor fought beside the rebels, Ra forbade any Goa'uld to speak of Earth again. The other System Lords kept the ban, and most of them avoided Earth from then on.
  4. c. 3000 BC
    En Sabah Nur is born at Akkaba
    Abandoned for his grey skin, the first of the mutants was raised by Baal of the Sandstormers in the years after the rising against Ra.
  5. c. 2900 BC
    Set drives the Silent Striders from Egypt
    Set laid a great curse on the Silent Striders, the Garou tribe of the Nile who had fought him, which drove them out of Egypt, scattered them across the earth and cut them off from the spirits of their ancestors.
  6. c. 2070 BC
    Yu rules China
    The Goa'uld Yu, defying Ra's ban, ruled China as Yu the Great and founded its first dynasty.
  7. c. 1440 BC
    Moses's spies see the sons of Anak
    The spies Moses sent into Canaan reported seeing the sons of Anak, who came of the giants, beside whom they were as grasshoppers.
  8. c. 1000 BC
    Ba'al raids the North
    About three thousand years ago Ba'al, defying Ra's ban, sent ships to the coasts of the North to take slaves and hosts. Thor killed every Jaffa on the shore, brought one ship down into the sea and followed the rest to Ba'al's palace, which he broke open. Ba'al escaped.
  9. c. 600 BC
    The dark inheritance passes to Greece
    The dark craft descended from Stygia passed from Egypt into Greece, where the wizarding record later picked up the Stygian it remembers as Herpo the Foul.
  10. c. 450 BC
    The Toreador flourish in Athens
    The Toreador, the clan of artists and lovers of beauty, flourished in Athens and afterwards in Rome.
  11. 146 BC
    Rome destroys Brujah Carthage
    Rome, guided by the Ventrue, destroyed Carthage, where the Brujah ruled and Kindred and mortals were said to have lived openly together. The Brujah have never forgiven the Ventrue for it.
  12. c. 4 BC
    Jesus Christ is born in Bethlehem
    Jesus Christ, the Son of God, was born in Bethlehem of the Virgin Mary in the reign of the emperor Augustus, and grew up in Nazareth.
  13. c. 27
    Christ is baptised and tempted in the wilderness
    Jesus was baptised by John in the Jordan, and was tempted by Satan for forty days in the wilderness and refused him.
  14. c. 28
    Christ calls Simon Peter
    Simon, son of Jonah, was fishing on the lake of Galilee with his brother Andrew when Jesus called them to follow him and become fishers of men, and gave Simon the name Peter, the rock.
  15. c. 29
    Peter walks on the water
    One night in a storm Christ came to his disciples walking on the lake of Galilee, and Peter climbed out of the boat and walked towards him until he looked at the wind and the waves and began to sink. Christ caught him by the hand: 'O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?'
  16. c. 29
    Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ
    Peter was the first to confess Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God, and when he asked how often he must forgive his brother, Christ answered, until seventy times seven.
  17. c. 30
    Christ drives the money changers from the Temple
    In Jerusalem Christ found the Temple turned into a market, made a whip of cords and drove out the money changers, overturning their tables.
  18. c. 30
    Peter denies Christ three times
    On the night Christ was betrayed, Peter denied him three times before the cock crowed, and wept bitterly.
  19. c. 30
    Christ is crucified under Pontius Pilate
    Jesus was betrayed, condemned under Pontius Pilate and crucified at Jerusalem.
  20. c. 30
    Christ rises from the dead
    Christ rose from the dead on the third day and showed his wounds to his disciples, and Thomas believed. He asked Peter three times whether he loved him, and told him to feed his sheep.
  21. c. 30
    Peter leads the apostles after Pentecost
    After Pentecost Peter led the apostles in spreading the faith of Christ.
  22. c. 43
    The dark inheritance reaches Britain through Rome
    From Greece the dark craft passed to Rome, and with Rome it came to England and the rest of Europe, where Celtic, Norse and Druidic blood rites carried downstream fragments of the same source.
  23. c. 64
    Saint Peter is crucified at Rome
    By tradition Peter was crucified at Rome under the emperor Nero, head downwards at his own request.
  24. c. 95
    The Revelation warns of the Mark of the Beast
    In the Revelation given to John, a beast rising out of the earth causes all to receive a mark on the right hand or the forehead, the number six hundred threescore and six, without which none may buy or sell; the power behind the beasts is the dragon, Satan.
  25. c. 300
    The Peverell brothers meet Death
    Antioch, Cadmus and Ignotus Peverell made a bridge by magic over a dangerous river at twilight and met Death on it, who gave them the Elder Wand, the Resurrection Stone and his own Cloak of Invisibility: the Deathly Hallows.
  26. c. 301
    Antioch Peverell is murdered for the Elder Wand
    The eldest brother, Antioch, boasted of his unbeatable wand and was murdered in his sleep for it; the wand passed on by murder and conquest through a long line of owners.
  27. c. 302
    Cadmus Peverell takes his own life
    The second brother, Cadmus, called back the girl he had hoped to marry with the Resurrection Stone, found her cold and sorrowful, and killed himself to join her. The stone came down his line to the Gaunts.
  28. c. 360
    Ignotus Peverell greets Death as an old friend
    The youngest brother, Ignotus, lived to a great age, gave the Cloak of Invisibility to his son and greeted Death as an old friend. From his line came the Pendragons.
  29. c. 400
    The White Howlers dance the Black Spiral
    In the days when the Picts held the north, the White Howlers, the Garou of Scotland, went down into the caverns beneath their land to carry the war to the Wyrm and danced the Black Spiral. It turned their minds inside out, and they came back up as the Black Spiral Dancers, the fourteenth tribe, which serves the Wyrm.
  30. c. 480
    Arthur Pendragon is conceived at Tintagel
    Arthur, son of Uther Pendragon, King of the Britons, and Igraine of Cornwall, was conceived at Tintagel through Merlin's art and raised in secret away from the court. Merlin was Gandalf, who advised him through the whole long, strange stretch of his years.
  31. c. 495
    Arthur draws the sword from the stone
    Arthur proved his right to the throne of the Britons by drawing a sword from a stone.
  32. c. 496
    The Lady of the Lake gives Arthur Excalibur
    From the Lady of the Lake, an Elf, Arthur received Excalibur, which the Elves of the Grey Havens had forged for him. Its scabbard kept its bearer from bleeding.
  33. c. 500
    Arthur founds the Round Table and marries Guinevere
    At Camelot Arthur gathered the knights of the Round Table, at which no seat stood higher than another, and married Guinevere.
  34. c. 500
    Wizards and the Church begin their long conflictB3 Ch6
    About fifteen hundred years before 1993, Christian missionaries reached Britain; early monks were often wizards, but the Church later turned against magic.
  35. c. 510
    Arthur defeats the Saxons
    King Arthur and his knights defeated the Saxons.
  36. c. 520
    Arthur's knights seek the Holy Grail
    Arthur sent the knights of the Round Table on the quest for the Holy Grail.
  37. c. 525
    Morgana steals the scabbard of Excalibur
    Morgana, Arthur's half-sister, a dark sorceress learned in healing and the dark arts, stole the scabbard of Excalibur and threw it into a lake, and sent enchantments to Camelot to expose Queen Guinevere.
  38. c. 537
    Arthur falls at Camlann and is borne to Avalon
    Arthur's reign was broken by Lancelot's love for Guinevere and Mordred's treachery. At Camlann he killed Mordred but was mortally wounded. He was carried in a barge to Avalon, which was the Grey Havens of the Elves.
  39. c. 600
    Arthur's heirs take the name Potter
    Attacked by Arthur's ancient enemies, dark wizards aligned with Morgana among them, his descendants the Pendragons changed their name to Potter as camouflage, long before the Norman Conquest. It worked so well that the wizarding world forgot what the name hid. The Peverell Cloak came down the line intact.
  40. c. 600
    Wizard monks bring Christianity into British magic
    When the missionaries came to Britain many of the early monks were wizards; half the healing charms still in use came from monasteries, and some monasteries were all but magical schools. For a long while wizards and the Church lived in harmony there.
  41. 664
    Synod of WhitbyB3 Ch15
    The Synod of Whitby was held; Hermione Granger later questioned the Fat Friar about it.
  42. c. 795
    Viking raids begin the Fenris and Fianna feud
    The Get of Fenris came raiding with the Norse across the North Sea into Britain and Ireland, and the Viking raids began the long feud between them and the Fianna, still sung on both sides.
  43. c. 870
    Thor frees the Northmen on Cimmeria
    The Goa'uld Heru'ur, son of Ra, carried off the people of several Norse settlements to a cold world far from Earth. Thor followed, destroyed his army in a storm that lasted three days and left the Northmen on Cimmeria under his protection, with the device called Thor's Hammer to guard its gate.
  44. c. 950
    The beard-gold feud beginsB3 Ch4
    In the 900s a ritual failed to turn the dwarfs' beards to gold, starting a feud with a party of warlocks.
  45. 954
    Anglo-Saxons take Jorvik
    The wizarding war between the Norse völvas of Jorvik and the last Hellenic sorcerers out of London ended with the Anglo-Saxons taking Jorvik.
  46. c. 979
    Gandalf gathers the four founders on the crag
    Gandalf rounded up the four most quarrelsome young wizards of the isle, Rowena Ravenclaw, Godric Gryffindor, Helga Hufflepuff and Salazar Slytherin, and stood them in the mud on a crag above a Highland lake. It took him eleven years and two broken staffs to get them to sit at one table.
  47. c. 980
    Gandalf wins an argument with Rowena Ravenclaw
    When her daughter Helena was very small, Gandalf came to Rowena Ravenclaw's house and argued with her by the fire all night, and in the morning she said he was the only man who had ever won an argument with her.
  48. 980s
    Gandalf gives Andúril to Godric Gryffindor
    When he gathered the four founders of Hogwarts, Gandalf placed Andúril in the hands of Godric Gryffindor, Aragorn's heir. Millennia had worn the blade down, and Godric took it to the goblin smith Ragnuk the First to be repaired, the work on which the goblins later built their claim to have forged it.
  49. 990
    Hogwarts is founded
    Hogwarts was founded by Ravenclaw, Gryffindor, Hufflepuff and Slytherin, whom Gandalf had brought together after eleven years of argument. Gandalf had placed in Godric Gryffindor's hands Andúril, which was his by blood as an heir of Aragorn.
  50. 990
    Founding of HogwartsB2 Ch10
    Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry was founded by Godric Gryffindor, Helga Hufflepuff, Rowena Ravenclaw and Salazar Slytherin, the first place where Britain's rival magical communities were made to sit together.
  51. 990
    Hogwarts foundedB2 Ch10
    Hogwarts was founded, after Ambrose Greyhame spent eleven years getting the four founders round one table.
  52. c. 990
    Ambrose Greyhame unites the foundersB2 Ch13
    Over eleven years Ambrose Greyhame brought the four quarrelling founders to the same table and made them build a hall of grey stone on a crag above a lake, breaking two staffs on the table along the way.
  53. c. 991
    Gandalf speaks to the first Hogwarts pupils
    When the hall at Hogwarts had half a roof, Gandalf came up out of the valley in the snow and told the muddy first-years by the kitchen fire, the boy who became the Fat Friar among them, that magic was a gift from Somebody who had never given up on them. The young school used the Patronus Charm against all sorts of nasty things.
  54. c. 993
    Hogwarts shuts out the old roadsB3 Interlude
    About a thousand years before 1993, the Hogwarts castle saw to it that none of the old crossroads routes ran within twenty miles of it.
  55. 990s
    Helga Hufflepuff teaches the first pupils
    Helga Hufflepuff taught at Hogwarts in its first years, brought house-elves into the castle kitchens where they could work in safety, and boxed the ears of the boy who became the Fat Friar for turning the porridge into frogspawn.
  56. 990s
    The founders enchant the Sorting Hat
    The four founders of Hogwarts put something of their own minds into a hat that had belonged to Godric Gryffindor, so that it could go on choosing their students after them; it still speaks of Godric, Helga and Salazar by their first names.
  57. 990s
    Thor destroys the fleets of the System Lords
    Apophis, Heru'ur and Ba'al joined their fleets to strike at Asgard. Thor, given command of Asgard's ships by Odin, destroyed two of the three above a dead world the Jaffa will not name; Apophis saved his own by running.

The Middle Ages to the sixteen hundreds

  1. c. 1000
    Hogwarts closes the midnight roads
    About a thousand years before 1994 the castle of Hogwarts saw to it that none of the old midnight roads, which run from crossroads to crossroads across the world, came within twenty miles of it.
  2. c. 1000
    The Protected Planets Treaty is signed
    Soon after their defeat by Thor the Goa'uld System Lords asked Asgard for terms, and the Protected Planets Treaty closed a list of worlds to them, Cimmeria among them. Earth, which the Goa'uld were forbidden to name, was left off it.
  3. 1000s
    Slytherin leaves Hogwarts
    After a bitter quarrel with Godric Gryffindor over admitting children of non-magical parents, Salazar Slytherin left Hogwarts, breaking Helga Hufflepuff's heart, and before he went built the Chamber of Secrets deep beneath the castle, sealed so that only his true heir could loose its Basilisk.
  4. 1000s
    Death of Helena Ravenclaw
    Helena Ravenclaw stole her mother Rowena's diadem and fled to Albania; the dying Rowena sent the Baron to bring her home, and when she refused him he stabbed her to death in an Albanian forest and killed himself, returning with her to Hogwarts as the Bloody Baron and the Grey Lady, while the diadem lay hidden in a hollow tree.
  5. 1000s
    Quidditch first played at Queerditch Marsh
    Quidditch was first played at Queerditch Marsh in the eleventh century and took its name from the place.
  6. 1000s
    The Tzimisce fight the Tremere
    From the eleventh century the Tzimisce voivodes of Transylvania fought the Tremere, newly become vampires, for the Carpathians.
  7. c. 1020
    Death of the Fat Friar
    The Fat Friar, a pupil of Helga Hufflepuff who became a Benedictine monk at a priory on the Wash that was in effect a school of magic, died about two centuries before the first friars reached England, and haunted his priory for a few hundred years.
  8. 1022
    The Tremere become vampires
    House Tremere, a house of wizards of the Order of Hermes, sought immortality as their magic waned, and Tremere's pupil Goratrix found it in the blood of captured vampires. Tremere and his inner council drank it and became vampires, and turned their magic into Thaumaturgy.
  9. c. 1030
    Gandalf takes back Gryffindor's sword from the goblins
    After Godric Gryffindor died, the goblins named his sword the Sword of Gryffindor and claimed to have forged it, meaning to take it for themselves. Gandalf stole it back first and kept it hidden for a later heir of Aragorn, and the histories record only that the sword vanished.
  10. c. 1050
    Gandalf hides the sword of Gryffindor
    After Godric Gryffindor's death the goblins put about the name 'the Sword of Gryffindor' for Andúril and claimed to have forged it, as grounds for taking it; before they could, Gandalf stole the sword back and hid it for the day another of Aragorn's heirs would need it.
  11. 1066
    Norman Conquest
    Norman wizarding families won the Conquest for William the Conqueror mostly with dark magic; Armand Malfoy received land in Wiltshire.
  12. 1066
    Armand Malfoy is granted land in Wiltshire
    The Malfoys came over from Normandy with William the Conqueror, who granted Armand Malfoy the land in Wiltshire where Malfoy Manor stands and the family has lived ever since.
  13. 1066
    Malfoys arrive in EnglandB2 Ch3
    The Malfoy family came to England at the Norman conquest and, according to Fred Weasley, have been Dark wizards ever since.
  14. 1093
    Elisabetha Cronqvist dies
    While the knight and strategist Mathias Cronqvist was away on campaign in the Church's wars, his wife Elisabetha fell ill and died. Mathias took it as a betrayal by God, withdrew from the Church's service and resolved to live for ever to curse Heaven.
  15. 1094
    Leon Belmont and the Vampire Killer
    Leon Belmont stormed the castle of the vampire Walter Bernhard to rescue his betrothed, Sara, and the whip made there with her sacrifice became the Vampire Killer, the Belmonts' weapon against the undead ever since.
  16. 1094
    Walter Bernhard carries off Sara Trantoul
    The Tzimisce vampire Walter Bernhard, lord of a castle in a forest of eternal night kept dark by the Ebony Stone, carried off Sara Trantoul, betrothed of the knight Leon Belmont. Leon, refused leave by the Church, gave up his title and went after her alone.
  17. 1094
    The Vampire Killer is made
    The alchemist Rinaldo Gandolfi gave Leon Belmont a whip of alchemy, and when Leon found Sara already bitten and turning, she gave her soul to the whip, which became the Vampire Killer.
  18. 1094
    Leon Belmont destroys Walter Bernhard
    With the newly made Vampire Killer Leon Belmont destroyed Walter Bernhard in his castle, the whip's first victim.
  19. 1094
    Mathias Cronqvist rises as a vampire
    At the moment of Walter's destruction Mathias Cronqvist, who had set the whole affair in motion, took Walter's blood and soul into the Crimson Stone and rose as a vampire. The Stone broke the rules of diablerie, setting him at the fourth generation and in Walter's clan, the Tzimisce.
  20. 1094
    Leon Belmont swears the Belmont oath
    Leon refused Mathias's offer of eternity at his side and fought Death, who had begun to serve Mathias, while Mathias withdrew. Leon then swore that his descendants would hunt the night for ever, and the war between the Belmonts and the vampire who became Dracula began.
  21. 1094
    Dracula becomes a Tzimisce
    Mathias Cronqvist, later Dracula, became a Tzimisce of the fourth generation when through the Crimson Stone he took the blood and soul of Walter Bernhard.
  22. c. 1099
    The Assamites fight the Crusaders
    From their mountain fortress of Alamut in Persia, the Assamites fought the Crusaders and the Kindred who came east with them.
  23. 1133
    Tremere usurps the blood of Saulot
    Tremere drank the blood and soul of Saulot, the Antediluvian of the Salubri, and took his place among the Third Generation; the Tremere then hunted the Salubri almost to nothing and are called the Usurpers.
  24. 1140s
    The fall of Vyšehrad buries Christof
    Mortal forces stormed the Tzimisce castle of Vyšehrad above Prague and brought it down, burying Christof Romuald in torpor; the Tzimisce elders bound the Methuselah Vukodlak in a sleep of their own.
  25. 1141
    Christof Romuald is Embraced in Prague
    After killing a Tzimisce monster in a silver mine near Prague, the French crusader Christof Romuald was Embraced into Clan Brujah by Ecaterina the Wise.
  26. c. 1150
    The Tremere and Tzimisce war over Transylvania
    For generations the Tremere fought the Tzimisce for the mountains of Transylvania from their first fortress, Ceoris, and made gargoyles from captured Tzimisce, Gangrel and Nosferatu to fight for them.
  27. c. 1170
    The Toreador preside over the Courts of Love
    In the Middle Ages the Toreador presided over the Courts of Love of France and the courts of Spain and Italy, while the Ventrue ruled Europe's Kindred as feudal princes.
  28. c. 1190
    The four peoples of Hogwarts intermarry
    About two hundred years after Hogwarts was founded, the four magical peoples of Britain at last began to marry one another.
  29. c. 1220
    Leopold of Murnau leaves his testament
    Leopold of Murnau, a leading inquisitor of the early thirteenth century, left a testament that became the rule of the Society of Leopold, the secret Catholic order that carried the Inquisition's war on vampires into the modern age.
  30. 1289
    International Warlock Convention of 1289B2 Ch10
    The International Warlock Convention met, with a sub-committee of Sardinian sorcerers sitting that September.
  31. 1296
    Manticore clearedB3 Ch11
    A manticore was cleared of savaging a woodcutter, only because the Committee could find nobody willing to fetch it in.
  32. c. 1300
    Medieval witch-burningsB3 Ch1
    Thousands were burned between 1300 and 1400.
  33. 1346
    Welsh knight killed at CrécyB2 Ch9
    A Welsh knight was killed by a crossbow bolt through his visor at the Battle of Crécy and became a ghost.
  34. c. 1350
    The Ravnos come west with the Romani
    The Ravnos, a clan of tricksters out of India, came west into Europe with the Romani caravans, from whom they Embraced many of their childer.
  35. c. 1350
    Fourteenth-century witch burningsB3 Ch1
    Between 1300 and 1400 many thousands were burned, nearly all without magic; Wendelin the Weird was burned forty-seven times.
  36. 1392
    The Wailing Widow drownsB2 Ch9
    A woman of Kent drowned herself in a well when her husband did not return from the Crusades; he returned a week later, and she became the Wailing Widow.
  37. c. 1400
    The Anarch Revolt breaks out
    As the Inquisition burned vampires across Europe and the elders saved themselves by giving their young to the fires, the young Kindred rose against their sires, learned to break the blood bond and hired Assamite assassins. The Brujah Tyler was among the revolt's leaders.
  38. 1400s
    The first Quidditch World Cup
    The Quidditch World Cup began to be played in the fifteenth century.
  39. 1400s
    Lugoj claims the Eldest's blood
    In the Anarch Revolt of the early fifteenth century the anarch Lugoj Blood-Cursed claimed to have drunk the blood and soul of the Eldest, the Antediluvian founder of Clan Tzimisce, though many Tzimisce doubt it.
  40. c. 1405
    Gratiano storms the Castle of Shadows
    Lasombra anarchs led by Gratiano, the Antediluvian's youngest childe, stormed the Castle of Shadows on Sicily with Assamite allies, and Gratiano claimed to have drunk the blood and soul of Lasombra himself. No witness has ever confirmed it.
  41. c. 1413
    Lugoj claims to destroy the Tzimisce founder
    In the Anarch Revolt Lugoj Blood-Cursed claimed to have destroyed the Eldest, the Antediluvian founder of the Tzimisce.
  42. c. 1430
    Alucard is born to Dracula and Lisa
    Dracula's son Adrian, the dhampir later called Alucard, was born to the vampire's second wife, Lisa, a mortal woman; from his father he took long life and strength, and from his mother a conscience.
  43. 1430s
    Nider's book about antsB3 Ch15
    The Dominican Johannes Nider wrote a long book about ants in which he described witches as an organised army with the Devil for its bishop.
  44. 1435
    The vampire Masquerade begins
    The Masquerade, the vampires' own law of secrecy, came into force for vampires.
  45. 1435
    The elders found the Camarilla
    With the Inquisition burning and the Anarch Revolt raging, the Ventrue Hardestadt called a convocation of elders of several clans, among them the Toreador Rafael de Corazón, from which the Camarilla grew.
  46. 1435
    The Masquerade is proclaimed
    The convocation of elders agreed that the Kindred must vanish from mortal sight and become a legend, and the Masquerade became the first of the Camarilla's Six Traditions. After it vampires grew harder to find, and the Society of Leopold dwindled for long periods.
  47. c. 1437
    Johannes Nider calls witches a secret church
    The Dominican Johannes Nider wrote in a book about ants that witches were an army, a secret church with the Devil for its bishop.
  48. 1444
    Augustus Giovanni usurps the blood of Cappadocius
    Augustus Giovanni, a Venetian merchant prince Embraced into the line of Cappadocius, drank the blood and soul of Cappadocius himself and took his place in the Third Generation. The Giovanni then hunted down the rest of the Cappadocians.
  49. 1450
    Sonia Belmont faces Dracula
    Sonia Belmont, the first of her family to fight the vampire under the name Dracula, faced him with Alucard's help.
  50. c. 1450
    A blood-boiling curse kills a Muggle-baiterB3 Ch18
    A fifteenth-century curse that boils the blood from the feet up, recorded in a footnote in Moste Potente Potions, took nine hours to kill a Muggle-baiter in Shropshire.
  51. c. 1470
    The Wallachians drive out the Belmonts
    The people of Wallachia, afraid of the Belmont family's powers, drove them out of the land.
  52. 1473
    Every Quidditch foul in one match
    All seven hundred recognised ways of committing a Quidditch foul were committed in a single World Cup match.
  53. c. 1474
    Hector leaves Dracula's service
    Hector, a Devil Forgemaster who forged demonic Innocent Devils for Dracula's armies, turned against his master, gave up his powers and lived quietly among mortals.
  54. c. 1475
    Lisa is put to death as a witch
    Dracula's wife Lisa was put to death as a witch; her last wish to their son was that he should not hate mankind for it. Dracula answered her death with war on the human race, and Alucard took the opposite side.
  55. 1476
    Trevor Belmont destroys Dracula
    When Dracula loosed armies of the dead on Wallachia, the Church called back Trevor Belmont, who freed the petrified sorceress Sypha Belnades and the pirate Grant DaNasty, was tested and then joined by Alucard, and with them destroyed Dracula in his castle. The reported death of the Wallachian prince Vlad Tepes, which was Dracula, fell at the end of the same year.
  56. c. 1477
    Trevor Belmont marries Sypha Belnades
    After the war Trevor Belmont married Sypha Belnades, joining the Belnades gift for magic to the Belmont line.
  57. c. 1477
    Alucard seals himself in sleep
    After his father's defeat Alucard chose to sleep, sealing himself away so that the blood of Dracula in him could do the world no harm.
  58. c. 1478
    Hector's beloved Rosaly is burned as a witch
    As Dracula's lingering curse spread plague, war and fear across Europe, Hector's beloved Rosaly was burned as a witch through the scheming of Isaac, a fellow Forgemaster still loyal to Dracula.
  59. 1479
    Hector defeats Isaac
    Hector, a Devil Forgemaster who had deserted Dracula, defeated his rival Isaac and thwarted an attempt to bring Dracula back through him.
  60. 1479
    Hector breaks Dracula's curse
    Death, in the guise of a man called Zead, killed Isaac and called Dracula into his body; Hector destroyed what rose and, with a last forging, destroyed the essence of the curse. Trevor Belmont crossed his path that year and tested him.
  61. 1486
    The Malleus Maleficarum is published
    Two Dominicans published the Malleus Maleficarum, after which witchcraft on the Continent was an organised heresy and a pact with the Devil, and inquisitors and witch-finders followed.
  62. 1490s
    Honeydukes founded (approx.)B3 Ch8
    Honeydukes had stood in Hogsmeade for about five hundred years by 1993, according to Ron.
  63. 1490s
    Death of Nearly Headless NickB1 Ch3
    Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington died in a botched beheading almost five hundred years before 1991.
  64. 31 October 1492
    Death of Nearly Headless Nick
    Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington, a wizard courtier of King Henry VII condemned after a spell to straighten the Lady Grieve's teeth left her with a tusk, was struck forty-five times on the neck with a blunt axe, leaving his head held on by an inch of skin, and remained as the ghost of Gryffindor Tower.
  65. 1493
    The Convention of Thorns ends the Anarch Revolt
    In England the Camarilla, the anarchs and the Assamites made peace at the Convention of Thorns; the anarchs who accepted were pardoned, and the Brujah, Gangrel, Malkavians, Nosferatu, Toreador, Tremere and Ventrue stood as the Camarilla's seven founding clans.
  66. 1493
    The Tremere lay the blood curse on the Assamites
    Under the terms of the Convention of Thorns the Assamites accepted a curse laid by the Tremere, under which any Assamite who drinks another vampire's blood is burnt by it.
  67. 1493
    The Sabbat is formed
    The anarchs who refused the Convention of Thorns, most of them Lasombra and Tzimisce, withdrew to Spain and the east and became the Sabbat, the Sword of Caine; the Tremere Goratrix, who had gone over to the anarchs, took his followers into it.
  68. 1493
    The Convention of Thorns and the Sabbat
    When the Convention of Thorns made peace at the end of the Anarch Revolt, the Tzimisce anarchs refused it and founded the Sabbat with the Lasombra.
  69. 1528
    The Giovanni make the Promise
    The Giovanni made the Promise with the Camarilla: they would keep out of Kindred politics, and the Camarilla would leave them alone.
  70. 1530s
    Destruction of the Fat Friar's prioryB3 Ch15
    King Henry pulled down the priory on the Wash that the Fat Friar haunted, to sell the lead off its roof, and the Friar returned to Hogwarts.
  71. c. 1538
    The Fat Friar comes home to Hogwarts
    When King Henry VIII pulled down the Fat Friar's priory on the Wash to sell the lead off the roof, the ghost came home to Hogwarts, where he haunts a window at the end of the kitchen corridor.
  72. c. 1539
    Brother Aldric hides the Glastonbury booksB2 Ch9
    Under Henry the Eighth, Brother Aldric hid Glastonbury Abbey's books from the King's commissioners in a cave on the Tor before being hanged, drawn and quartered, about 450 years before 1992.
  73. 1540
    Coronado marches north into New Mexico
    The Spanish explorer Francisco Vásquez de Coronado led an army north into New Mexico in search of the golden Seven Cities of Cíbola, which did not exist; a few wizards marched with him unrecognised.
  74. 1541
    Spanish wizards stumble into D'ni
    Experimenting with long-distance Apparition across the desert, a few Spanish wizards from Coronado's army arrived by accident in the cavern of D'ni. The D'ni talked with them for a few hours through an interpreter, then sent them back up firmly and rather rudely; the Spaniards wrote it down and thought the D'ni not magical at all.
  75. 1576
    Christopher Belmont faces Dracula
    Christopher Belmont went into Dracula's castle and defeated him, though the vampire escaped destruction and returned.
  76. 1576
    Christopher Belmont destroys Dracula
    Christopher Belmont destroyed Dracula, but the vampire survived as mist.
  77. 1588
    The ArmadaB3 Ch15
    Around the time of the Armada the Fat Friar gave up correcting people who called him a friar rather than a monk.
  78. 1591
    Dracula possesses Soleiyu Belmont
    Dracula possessed Christopher Belmont's son Soleiyu, and Christopher defeated him again.
  79. c. 1592
    Belmonts begin hunting DraculaB2 Ch7
    The Belmont family began hunting Dracula about four hundred years before 1992.
  80. c. 1600
    European Garou come to the Americas
    When Europeans crossed the Atlantic their Garou came with them, seized caerns and made war on the native tribes, the Uktena and the Wendigo, who call them Wyrmcomers and have never forgiven them.
  81. 1609
    The Master sires Darla
    In the Virginia colony the Master, the fourth-generation Ventrue who founded the Aurelian line and its priesthood, the Order of Aurelius, sired his favourite childe, Darla.
  82. 1612
    The goblin rebellion of 1612
    One of the inns of Hogsmeade, the only all-wizard village in Britain, served as the headquarters of the goblin rebellion.
  83. 1612
    A killing curse is bannedB3 Ch18
    A fourth lethal curse known to Hermione Granger was banned in 1612, so that hardly anybody now knows its countercurse.
  84. 1637
    Werewolf Code of Conduct
    The Werewolf Code of Conduct was established.
  85. 1689
    The Statute of Secrecy is signed
    The International Confederation of Wizards signed the International Statute of Wizarding Secrecy, by which the witches and wizards of the world would hide from Muggles; it came into force in 1692.
  86. 1691
    Simon Belmont destroys Dracula
    When Dracula's castle rose again, Simon Belmont went in alone with the Vampire Killer, met Death in its halls and destroyed Dracula at the top of the castle, but took from him a curse, a wound that would not heal.
  87. 1692
    The Statute of Secrecy hides wizards from the Church
    When the International Statute of Wizarding Secrecy came in, the wizarding world hid from the Church in particular and threw out God and angels as it went, so that most wizards have scorned Christianity since. Some wizards say the Statute was inspired by the vampires' Masquerade.
  88. 1698
    Simon's Quest
    Simon Belmont faced Dracula again.
  89. 1698
    Simon Belmont breaks Dracula's curse
    Seven years on, Simon Belmont gathered Dracula's rib, heart, eye, nail and ring from mansions across Transylvania, burned them in the ruins of the castle, destroyed the Dracula who rose from the fire and was freed of the curse.

The seventeen hundreds and eighteen hundreds

  1. c. 1700
    Angelus rampages across EuropeB2 Ch7
    In the eighteenth century the vampire Angelus cut a path across Europe, including Romania and London.
  2. c. 1700
    Wand magic takes its modern formB2 Ch10
    Wand magic took its modern form in the eighteenth century, many thousands of years after Gandalf first taught light magic.
  3. c. 1700
    Anna finds the D'ni cavernB3 Ch21
    In the 1700s Anna, a Muggle, found a way into the D'ni cavern and was taken prisoner.
  4. 1709
    Warlocks' Convention bans dragon breedingB1 Ch10
    The Warlocks' Convention of 1709 outlawed dragon breeding.
  5. 1722
    Hippogriff case lostB3 Ch11
    A hippogriff tried before the wizarding authorities lost its case and was treated barbarically afterwards.
  6. 1727
    Liam is born in Galway
    Liam, later the vampire Angelus, was born in Galway, the son of a linen merchant.
  7. 1748
    Juste Belmont destroys Dracula's remains
    Juste Belmont, grandson of Simon, went into a castle conjured from Dracula's remains to rescue his friend Lydie Erlanger, and destroyed what was left of Dracula there.
  8. 1748
    Juste Belmont fights Dracula's revenant
    Juste Belmont fought a revenant raised from Dracula's relics.
  9. c. 1750
    Azkaban becomes the Ministry's prison
    In the eighteenth century the Ministry of Magic made Azkaban, a fortress in the North Sea that the dementors already haunted, its prison, and has used the dementors as its guards ever since.
  10. 1753
    Darla sires Angelus
    In Galway Darla beckoned a handsome, drunken linen merchant's son from outside a tavern into an alley and sired him as the vampire Angelus, and the two cut a path across Europe for decades.
  11. 1753
    Darla sires Liam
    On the night his father finally turned him out of the house, Liam was beckoned into an alley by a pale lady from the colonies, Darla, who sired him.
  12. 1753
    Angelus slaughters his family in Galway
    Liam's first act as a vampire was to go home: his little sister Kathy, thinking he had come back as an angel, let him in, and he killed the whole household, servants and all, saving his father for last. From her mistake he took the name Angelus.
  13. 1753
    Angelus turned in GalwayB3 Ch9
    A linen merchant's idle son in Galway was turned by a pale lady from the colonies and became Angelus, who began by killing his whole household.
  14. c. 1755
    Angelus and Darla begin their reign of terror
    For decades Angelus and Darla roamed Europe in open defiance of the Masquerade, Angelus cutting a cross into the cheeks of his victims; it was in all the broadsheets. The Camarilla secretly backed mortal hunters against him, the Society of Leopold among them.
  15. 1764
    Daniel Holtz begins his hunt for Angelus
    Holtz, a hunter of the Society of Leopold, pursued Angelus and Darla across Europe for nine years without catching them, never knowing that some of the money behind the hunt came from the Camarilla.
  16. May 1764
    Angelus and Darla destroy Daniel Holtz's family
    At York Angelus and Darla killed the vampire hunter Daniel Holtz's wife Caroline and their infant son and turned his daughter Sarah, whom Holtz had to destroy by putting her out into the sunlight.
  17. 1773
    Holtz accepts Sahjhan's bargain
    A demon named Sahjhan offered Daniel Holtz a way to outlive Angelus and Darla, and Holtz accepted and slept, untouched by the years.
  18. c. 1782
    Anna finds the cavern of D'ni
    Anna, a Muggle woman of the New Mexico wilds who had learnt the rocks from her father, found a way down through the caves into the cavern of D'ni. The D'ni took her prisoner and questioned her, and she learnt their language in captivity.
  19. c. 1784
    Anna marries Aitrus and takes the name Ti'ana
    Given into the keeping of Lord Kahlis, Anna married his son Aitrus and took the name Ti'ana; Aitrus taught her the Art against D'ni custom, and she recorded everything she saw.
  20. c. 1785
    Gehn is born in D'ni
    Anna bore Aitrus a son, Gehn, a sickly child whom the healers did not expect to live.
  21. c. 1786
    Anna pleads for Lord Veovis's life
    When Lord Veovis was condemned for conspiring with the renegade A'Gaeris, an outcast of the Guild of Writers, Anna argued for exile instead of death and the council spared him; A'Gaeris then freed him.
  22. c. 1788
    The plague of A'Gaeris destroys D'ni
    A'Gaeris and Veovis loosed a plague that ran through the cavern of D'ni and out into its Ages and killed nearly every D'ni, ending ten thousand years of their city. The Art was lost with them, more or less, and the cavern stood empty for two centuries.
  23. c. 1788
    A'Gaeris murders Veovis
    When Veovis refused to write an Age in which the two of them would be worshipped as gods, A'Gaeris murdered him.
  24. c. 1788
    Aitrus dies trapping A'Gaeris
    Aitrus lured A'Gaeris into an unstable Age, where both of them died.
  25. c. 1788
    Anna escapes D'ni with Gehn
    Anna led her young son Gehn up through the caves by her husband's maps to the surface, near where she had first gone down, and made her home in the Cleft, a fissure beside an old volcano above the cavern.
  26. c. 1789
    Gehn returns to the dead city of D'ni
    Gehn, who never forgave his mother for sparing Veovis, left her, went back down into the dead city and taught himself the Art from the books there, writing flawed Ages of his own; on his Fifth Age, Riven, the people worshipped him as a god.
  27. c. 1790
    The Fall of D'ni
    A plague, the plague of A'Gaeris, killed nearly all the D'ni a few years after Anna came to live among them, about two hundred years before the 1990s.
  28. c. 1790
    Atrus is born in the Cleft
    Gehn brought his wife Keta, a woman of the surface gravely ill with child, to his mother in the Cleft; Keta died giving birth, Gehn went away without naming the baby, and Anna named him Atrus after his grandfather and raised him.
  29. 1792
    Rondo of Blood
    Richter Belmont faced Dracula.
  30. 1792
    Richter Belmont destroys Dracula
    A cult led by the priest Shaft raised Dracula, whose servants took young women from the villages near the castle, among them Annette and the twelve-year-old Maria Renard. Richter Belmont, aged nineteen, rescued the captives, destroyed Dracula and afterwards married Annette.
  31. c. 1793
    The Prague Hand of Glory is made
    About two hundred years before 1993 a hand was cut from a man hanged on the gallows of Prague and made into a Hand of Glory, each of its fingers a candle. John Constantine later bought it from a dealer in Prague's Old Town and swore never to use it.
  32. 1796
    Richter Belmont disappears
    Richter Belmont vanished.
  33. 1797
    Alucard puts his father to rest
    When Dracula's castle rose again, Alucard, Dracula's son by a mortal woman, went into it, freed Richter Belmont from a dark priest's spell and defeated his father.
  34. 1797
    Alucard destroys Dracula
    When Dracula's castle rose again with the missing Richter as its puppet lord under Shaft, Alucard woke from his long sleep, freed Richter with Maria Renard's help, destroyed Shaft and destroyed his father, telling him that Lisa had loved and forgiven him.
  35. c. 1798
    Gehn teaches Atrus the Art
    Gehn came back to the Cleft for his son, took Atrus down into the ruined city and taught him the Art, and destroyed Atrus's first Age because it did not suit him. Atrus was awed, then horrified by his father's belief that a Writer owns the worlds he writes.
  36. c. 1799
    Atrus meets Catherine on Riven
    When Atrus tried to escape, Gehn shut him in a chamber whose only way out led to Riven, and there Atrus met and fell in love with Catherine, called Katran, a woman of that Age whom Gehn meant to make one of his wives.
  37. c. 1799
    Anna writes the Age of Myst
    Anna wrote the Age of Myst, a small island of grey rock and dark pines, as a refuge for her family.
  38. c. 1800
    Atrus and Catherine strand Gehn on Riven
    With Anna's help Atrus and Catherine destroyed every linking book out of Riven and left Gehn stranded there. Atrus leapt into the Star Fissure and linked to Myst Island as he fell, and his Myst linking book went on falling, out of Riven and down to Earth.
  39. c. 1801
    Atrus and Catherine marry on Myst Island
    Atrus and Catherine married and made their home on Myst Island, where they raised two sons, Sirrus and Achenar, and from its library Atrus wrote and visited Age after Age.
  40. c. 1804
    Sirrus and Achenar plunder their father's Ages
    Growing up, Sirrus and Achenar stripped their father's Ages of riches and power and ruined the peoples of some of them, Sirrus hoarding fine things and Achenar weapons, poisons and instruments of torture.
  41. c. 1805
    Sirrus and Achenar betray their parents
    The brothers took their mother to Riven, where Gehn made her his prisoner and she became leader of the Moiety rebels, and stranded Atrus in D'ni by tearing a page out of his book home. Many of Myst's books were burnt.
  42. 1806
    Gehn is imprisoned on Riven
    Atrus sent the Stranger to Riven with a prison book disguised as a linking book; the Stranger freed Catherine and tricked Gehn into the book, and Atrus came for his wife as Riven began to break apart and the Rivenese were taken to safety. The Stranger went home through the Star Fissure and kept the little book, which his family handed down until it came to Albus Dumbledore.
  43. c. 1806
    The Stranger frees Atrus from his sons' trap
    A traveller from the surface, remembered only as the Stranger, found Atrus's lost Myst book and came to the island, refused both brothers trapped in the red and blue books and brought Atrus his missing page. Atrus came home, imprisoned his sons in separate Ages, Sirrus on Spire and Achenar on Haven, and wrote the Stranger a small leather linking book home.
  44. c. 1807
    Atrus and Catherine settle on Tomahna
    After Catherine's rescue Atrus and Catherine made a new home on the Age of Tomahna, where she wrote Ages of her own guided by her dreams, among them Serenia.
  45. c. 1810
    Atrus writes Releeshahn for the D'ni survivors
    Atrus gathered the few D'ni who had survived the plague scattered across their Ages and wrote the Age of Releeshahn as a new home for them.
  46. 1812
    Yorkshire lady found in chimneyB2 Ch9
    The body of a Yorkshire lady bricked up in a chimney by her steward was found when the chimney was swept.
  47. 1815
    Yeesha is born on Tomahna
    Yeesha, daughter of Atrus and Catherine, was born on Tomahna; being of D'ni descent, she has lived far beyond any ordinary human span.
  48. 1816
    Saavedro steals the book of Releeshahn
    Saavedro, a man of an Age that Sirrus and Achenar had ruined, broke into Tomahna and stole the Releeshahn book in revenge, and the Stranger came back and recovered it.
  49. c. 1826
    Sirrus and Achenar die over Yeesha
    Released after twenty years in their prison Ages, Sirrus kidnapped his young sister Yeesha; Achenar, who had come to regret what he had been, died saving her, and Sirrus died too. The Stranger helped save her.
  50. 1830
    Circle of the Moon
    Nathan Graves faced Dracula.
  51. c. 1830
    The Glass Walkers become the Iron Riders
    In the age of steam and railways the Garou tribe of the cities, once the Warders of Men, were known as the Iron Riders.
  52. 1830
    Nathan Graves destroys Dracula
    Dracula's servant Camilla raised him while the Belmonts were missing, and Nathan Graves destroyed him.
  53. c. 1835
    Shanoa of the Order of Ecclesia destroys Dracula
    In the nineteenth century the Order of Ecclesia tried to master Dracula's power, and Shanoa of that Order destroyed him while the Belmonts were missing.
  54. 1844
    Cornell rescues his sister
    The werewolf Cornell went into Dracula's castle to rescue his adopted sister Ada, who had been taken to help bring Dracula back.
  55. 1844
    Cornell fights Dracula's forces
    Cornell fought Dracula's forces.
  56. 1852
    Dracula is destroyed in the body of Malus
    Reinhardt Schneider and Carrie Fernandez, of Sypha's Belnades blood, destroyed Dracula in the body of a boy, Malus, into which he had been reborn.
  57. 1859
    Apocalypse makes Nathaniel Essex Mister Sinister
    In London Apocalypse remade the geneticist Nathaniel Essex into the long-lived Mister Sinister.
  58. 1860
    Angelus turns Drusilla in a London convent
    Angelus found Drusilla, a devout, gentle London witch with a little of the Sight, killed her family one by one and let her find them, and when she fled to a convent he came through the chapel on the day she took her holy orders and turned her, so that she would be mad for ever.
  59. 1860
    Drusilla joins Angelus and Darla
    Angelus's childe Drusilla joined him and Darla on their path across Europe.
  60. 1860s
    Birth of Bra'tac
    Bra'tac, later First Prime of the Goa'uld Apophis and master of the Jaffa of Chulak, was born; kept strong by his larva, he had lived some hundred and thirty years by the 1990s.
  61. 1875
    Underage Sorcery decreeB2 Ch2
    The Decree for the Reasonable Restriction of Underage Sorcery was enacted.
  62. 1877
    The duel over Quaffle weight
    The Grail and Valmond duel over the weight of the Quaffle left two hundred dead and a three-page casualty list.
  63. 1877
    The Grail and Valmond duel
    A dispute over the proper weight of a Quaffle between the England manager Francis Grail and the French manager Juste Valmond ended in a duel that killed two hundred witches and wizards in the crossfire.
  64. 1880
    Drusilla sires William the Bloody
    In London William, a young gentleman whose sentimental verse earned him the name William the Bloody, was scorned at a party and met Drusilla in the street, who sired him. As Spike he travelled with Drusilla, Angelus and Darla, the most feared company of vampires in Europe.
  65. 1880
    William the Bloody joins Angelus
    Drusilla's childe William the Bloody joined Angelus, Darla and Drusilla.
  66. 1881
    Birth of Albus Dumbledore
    Albus Percival Wulfric Brian Dumbledore was born in the West Country, the eldest child of Percival and Kendra Dumbledore, elder brother of Aberforth and Ariana.
  67. 1883
    Birth of Greta Grindelwald
    Greta Grindelwald, later the most dangerous Dark witch of the age before Voldemort, was born.
  68. 1890s
    Birth of James Howlett
    James Howlett, later Logan and Wolverine, was born to a wealthy family in Alberta, Canada, late in the nineteenth century. His mutant powers first showed when he saw his father murdered, and he fled and took the name Logan.
  69. c. 1892
    Dumbledore starts at Hogwarts
    Albus Dumbledore was sorted into Gryffindor and became one of the most brilliant pupils Hogwarts had known, a prefect and Head Boy.
  70. Summer 1892
    Gandalf begins teaching Albus Dumbledore staff magic
    In the summer Albus Dumbledore was eleven, Gandalf found him skimming stones in the river at the bottom of the lane, sent out for setting fire to the curtains, and asked what he could do with a good stick. He spent the next six summers teaching him staff magic.
  71. 1897
    Quincy Morris destroys Dracula
    Quincy Morris, a Texan of distant Belmont blood who carried the Vampire Killer, destroyed Dracula and died of his wounds.
  72. 1898
    The Kalderash curse Angelus with a soul
    In Romania Angelus killed the favourite daughter of the Kalderash, an old Romani clan of the Carpathians, and their elders sat round a fire and cursed him with a new soul, by a binding the Ministry of Magic has never reconstructed. One moment of true happiness would undo it, and the Scourge of Europe vanished overnight.
  73. 1898
    Darla casts out the ensouled Angel
    When Darla learned what Angelus had become she cast him out, and for most of the twentieth century Angel lived alone and out of sight, unwilling to feed on people.
  74. c. 1899
    Greta Grindelwald expelled from Durmstrang
    As a teenager Greta Grindelwald was expelled from the Durmstrang Institute for twisted experiments.
  75. Summer 1899
    Gandalf teaches Greta Grindelwald staff magic
    In the last of his six summers teaching Albus Dumbledore, which had begun in 1892, Gandalf also taught Greta Grindelwald, who took to staff magic faster than Albus.
  76. Summer 1899
    Greta Grindelwald comes to Godric's Hollow
    One summer nearly a hundred years before 1994, Greta Grindelwald came to Godric's Hollow to stay with her great-aunt Bathilda Bagshot and met the young Albus Dumbledore; Ambrose Greyhame taught her staff magic alongside him, and she once turned a whole river to light.
  77. Summer 1899
    Death of Ariana Dumbledore
    The summer at Godric's Hollow ended in a three-cornered duel between Albus Dumbledore, his brother Aberforth and Greta Grindelwald in which their sister Ariana was killed, and Greta fled.

1900 to 1945

  1. 1900
    Aslan sings Narnia into being
    Aslan, who is Christ, sang the world of Narnia into being before two children from London, Digory Kirke and Polly Plummer, and the witch Jadis whom they had brought with them by accident.
  2. 1900
    William the Bloody kills a Slayer in Beijing
    During the Boxer Rising in Beijing, William the Bloody killed the Slayer of the day, the first of two Slayers he would kill.
  3. c. 1900
    The Glass Walkers take their name
    As the modern cities rose, the Iron Riders took the name Glass Walkers.
  4. c. 1900
    The wizarding world and the Camarilla come to terms
    Through the International Confederation of Wizards, the wizarding governments of the world, the British Ministry of Magic among them, agreed to lend the Camarilla their wards and Muggle-Repelling Charms to help keep the Masquerade; in return no vampire answering to the Camarilla would ever hunt, harm or feed on a witch or wizard.
  5. 1901
    The Austrian rules are adopted
    Every national Quidditch team agreed to play by the Austrian rules, ending more than a thousand years of argument between the English and the French.
  6. 1912
    New Mexico becomes a state
    New Mexico, beneath whose desert lies the cavern of D'ni, became a state of the Union.
  7. 1914
    First World War beginsB1 Ch7
    The First World War began, about thirteen years after the Austrian rules were adopted; Harry did not know whether wizards noticed.
  8. 1916
    Roderick Burgess captures Dream
    The English occultist Roderick Burgess, trying to capture Death of the Endless and win immortality, caught her brother Dream instead and shut him in a glass prison. With sleep's keeper gone, a sleeping sickness spread across the world.
  9. 1917
    John Morris and Eric Lecarde destroy Dracula
    Dracula's niece Elizabeth Bartley worked to raise him through the slaughter of the Great War, and Quincy Morris's son John and Eric Lecarde destroyed him; the strain of wielding the Vampire Killer without Belmont blood shortened John's life.
  10. 1917
    The Russian Revolution breaks the Silver Fangs
    The Russian Revolution was a catastrophe for the Silver Fangs, the royal tribe of the Garou, whose noble Kinfolk were killed or scattered, and their power in the East never recovered.
  11. c. 1918
    Birth of Catherine Langford
    Catherine Langford, daughter of Professor Paul Langford, was born; she was a girl of about ten when her father's workmen uncovered the Stargate at Giza.
  12. 1920
    Birth of Namor
    Namor, the Sub-Mariner, was born the son of the American sea captain Leonard McKenzie and Fen, a princess of the Atlanteans, whose kingdom lies under the Antarctic sea. He was a hybrid of the two races and a mutant besides.
  13. c. 1920
    Birth of Nick Fury
    Nicholas Joseph Fury was born in New York City around the end of the First World War, the eldest of the three children of Jack Fury, and grew up there with his brother Jake and his sister Dawn.
  14. 1920
    Kent Nelson opens the tomb of Nabu
    Exploring the Valley of Ur in Mesopotamia with his father, the archaeologist Sven Nelson, the twelve-year-old Kent Nelson opened the tomb of the Babylonian sorcerer Nabu, a Lord of Order. The gas from the tomb killed his father, and Nabu raised the orphan in the arts of order.
  15. 1920s
    Greta Grindelwald talks Fascism with Mussolini
    Through the 1920s and after, Greta Grindelwald sought out Benito Mussolini and talked Fascism with him many times; she admired him and believed in Fascism completely, as the model for a world empire ruled by wizards.
  16. 4 July 1920
    Birth of Steve Rogers
    Steven Grant Rogers, later Captain America, was born on the Lower East Side of Manhattan to poor Irish immigrant parents, and grew up thin, sickly and determined.
  17. c. 1926
    Tom Riddle abandons Merope Gaunt
    Merope Gaunt, of the decayed Gaunt family descended from Salazar Slytherin, bewitched the Muggle Tom Riddle of the house on the hill above Little Hangleton; when the enchantment wore off he left her, expecting a child.
  18. c. 1926
    Birth of Tom RiddleB2 Ch15
    Tom Marvolo Riddle was born to a Muggle father and a witch mother who died almost at once; he was sixteen in June 1943.
  19. December 1926
    Greta Grindelwald unmasked in New York
    Disguised as Percival Graves, Director of Magical Security at MACUSA, Greta Grindelwald was exposed in New York by Newt Scamander and imprisoned by MACUSA.
  20. 31 December 1926
    Birth of Tom Marvolo Riddle
    Merope Gaunt gave birth to Tom Marvolo Riddle in a Muggle orphanage in London on the last night of 1926, and died having lived just long enough to name him.
  21. 1927
    Peter Pevensie is born
    Peter Pevensie, eldest of the four Pevensie children and like them a descendant of Aragorn and Arwen, was born.
  22. 1927
    Greta Grindelwald escapes and rallies Paris
    Greta Grindelwald escaped while being moved to Europe and, at a rally in the Lestrange mausoleum in Paris, showed her followers a vision of the coming war and won many to her side, Queenie Goldstein among them.
  23. 1928
    The Stargate is dug up at Giza
    An expedition under Professor Paul Langford uncovered the Stargate beneath the Giza plateau with two cover stones declaring it Ra's, sealed and buried for all time, and a gold amulet bearing the Eye of Ra, which his young daughter Catherine kept.
  24. 1928
    Susan Pevensie is born
    Susan Pevensie, later Queen Susan the Gentle of Narnia and Harry Potter's grandmother, was born.
  25. 6 December 1928
    Birth of Rubeus Hagrid
    Rubeus Hagrid was born, the son of a wizard and the giantess Fridwulfa, and was raised by his father.
  26. 1930
    Edmund Pevensie is born
    Edmund Pevensie, the third of the Pevensies, was born.
  27. 1930s
    Dumbledore begins teaching at Hogwarts
    Albus Dumbledore began teaching Transfiguration at Hogwarts under Headmaster Armando Dippet; his pupils included Tom Riddle, Minerva McGonagall and later John Constantine.
  28. 1930s
    The pantomime fire at Hogwarts
    When Albus Dumbledore was a young member of staff, Silvanus Kettleburn supplied an Ashwinder swollen by an Engorgement Charm as the Worm for a Christmas pantomime of the Fountain of Fair Fortune; it exploded and set the Great Hall alight, Kettleburn was put on probation and pantomimes were never staged at the school again.
  29. 1931
    Richard Watson is born
    Richard Allan Watson, later a professor of philosophy, cave explorer and one of the excavators of D'ni, was born.
  30. 1932
    Lucy Pevensie is born
    Lucy Pevensie, the youngest of the four Pevensies, was born.
  31. 1932
    Greta Grindelwald fails to take the Confederation
    Greta Grindelwald tried to make herself leader of the International Confederation of Wizards by trickery and failed in public; the blood pact she and Albus Dumbledore had sworn in 1899 was broken.
  32. c. 1932
    Riddle first locked in the coal cellarB2 Ch18
    At about five, Tom Riddle was first locked in the orphanage coal cellar by the woman who ran it.
  33. c. 1935
    Birth of Big Boss
    The soldier later called Big Boss, known to his friends as Jack, was born in America in the mid-1930s; he was trained for ten years by The Boss, with whom he developed close-quarters combat.
  34. 4 October 1935
    Birth of Minerva McGonagall
    Minerva McGonagall was born in Caithness in the north of Scotland, the daughter of Robert McGonagall, a Presbyterian minister, and Isobel Ross, a witch.
  35. c. 1936
    Siberian village begins its crimesB3 Ch11
    Men in a hidden Siberian village began nearly thirty years of doing something to the people in the valley below.
  36. 1937
    The Master is sealed beneath Sunnydale
    The Master tried to open the Hellmouth from a church in Sunnydale, California; an earthquake swallowed the church, the ritual failed, and he was trapped beneath the town in a mystical prison where his followers attended him for sixty years.
  37. c. 1938
    Dumbledore tells Riddle he is a wizard
    Albus Dumbledore came to the London orphanage to tell Tom Riddle that he was a wizard.
  38. 1938
    Superman's first appearanceB4 Ch3
    Superman was first photographed lifting a car above his head.
  39. September 1938
    Tom Riddle starts at Hogwarts
    Tom Riddle entered Hogwarts and was sorted into Slytherin, where he became a prefect and a Parselmouth who discovered that he was Slytherin's heir.
  40. 1939
    Batman first appears in Gotham
    Bruce Wayne, heir to the Wayne fortune, who had seen his parents shot dead in an alley as a boy, came to public notice in Gotham as Batman, a masked vigilante in grey and black who hunted criminals by night.
  41. 1939
    Dan Garret becomes the Blue Beetle
    The archaeologist Dan Garret, given strength and endurance by an ancient scarab he had found in an Egyptian tomb, began fighting crime in a blue costume as the Blue Beetle.
  42. 1939
    The Sub-Mariner comes to public notice
    Namor, prince of Atlantis, raised among his mother's people to see the surface world as the enemy that was poisoning and plundering the sea, first came to public notice.
  43. 1939
    Jay Garrick becomes the Flash
    At the end of 1939 Jay Garrick, a Midwestern University student who had gained superhuman speed from the fumes of an experiment with hard water, came to public notice in Keystone City as the Flash, in a red shirt and his father's winged steel helmet.
  44. 1939
    The Stargate is shipped to America
    The Stargate and its cover stones were shipped from Egypt to the United States, out of reach of Germany.
  45. 1939
    Death of Ba'al
    Ba'al, come back from 2008 to stop the gate reaching America, was shot by Cameron Mitchell aboard the Achilles.
  46. 1940
    The Pevensies are sent to Professor Kirke's house
    Sent out of London during the war, the four Pevensie children came to the country house of Professor Digory Kirke.
  47. 1940
    Lucy Pevensie finds Narnia
    Playing hide-and-seek, Lucy Pevensie stepped into a wardrobe and came out in a snowy wood by a lamp-post in Narnia, where the White Witch had held the land in winter for a hundred years, and met the faun Mr Tumnus. Nobody believed her until the others followed.
  48. 1940
    Edmund Pevensie betrays his siblings to the White Witch
    Fed enchanted Turkish Delight and promised a prince's place, Edmund went to the White Witch and betrayed his brother and sisters, so that by the Deep Magic his life was forfeit to her.
  49. 1940
    Aslan dies on the Stone Table and rises
    Aslan gave himself up to die on the Stone Table in Edmund's place, watched by Susan and Lucy, and rose again by a deeper magic from before the dawn of time, breaking the Witch's power.
  50. 1940
    Peter Pevensie is knighted Wolf's-Bane
    Peter killed the wolf captain of the White Witch's secret police with his sword Rhindon, and Aslan knighted him Sir Peter Wolf's-Bane.
  51. 1940
    The Battle of Beruna
    Peter led Aslan's army at the Battle of Beruna until Aslan came with the freed creatures; Edmund smashed the Witch's wand and was badly wounded, and Lucy healed him with her cordial.
  52. 1940
    The Pevensies are crowned at Cair Paravel
    Aslan crowned the four Pevensies at Cair Paravel, Peter as High King, and they reigned through the Golden Age of Narnia until, grown, they followed the White Stag back through the wardrobe and became children again at the moment they had left.
  53. 1940
    Weapon I produces Captain America
    Turned down by the army as unfit, Steve Rogers was picked for Project Rebirth, the first project of the Weapon programme, and made a super-soldier by Dr Abraham Erskine's serum and Vita-Rays. Minutes later a Nazi agent shot Erskine dead, and most of the formula died with him.
  54. 1940
    Lex Luthor becomes Superman's enemy
    The scientist Lex Luthor came to public notice in Metropolis, already grown to manhood, and set his intellect against Superman, the one thing that could stop him having the world.
  55. 1940
    Robin joins Batman
    Bruce Wayne took in Dick Grayson, an orphan of the Flying Graysons trapeze act whose parents had fallen to their deaths when a gangster sabotaged their rigging. Trained by Wayne, the boy appeared beside Batman as Robin, the first of the costumed partners.
  56. 1940
    The Joker first appears
    The clown-faced murderer called the Joker first appeared in Gotham, and became the worst of the city's costumed criminals and Batman's most famous enemy.
  57. 1940
    Alan Scott makes his ring
    The young railway engineer Alan Scott survived a bridge disaster by the light of a mysterious green lantern and made a magic ring from its metal, becoming the first Green Lantern. His ring had nothing to do with the Green Lantern Corps and could not affect wood.
  58. 1940
    Jim Corrigan returns as the Spectre
    The police detective Jim Corrigan was murdered by gangsters and sent back as the Spectre, a spirit of vengeance.
  59. 1940
    Doctor Fate comes to public notice
    Kent Nelson, raised by Nabu and given a golden helmet, an amulet and a cloak, came to public notice as the sorcerer Doctor Fate.
  60. 1940
    The Justice Society is founded
    Late in 1940, at President Roosevelt's request, eight heroes founded the Justice Society: the Atom, Doctor Fate, the Flash, Green Lantern, Hawkman, Hourman, the Sandman and the Spectre. Superman and Batman were honorary members, and the Flash, Jay Garrick, was its first chairman.
  61. 1940s
    Max Eisenhardt survives Auschwitz
    As a boy Max Eisenhardt, later Magneto, was sent with his Jewish family to the Warsaw Ghetto and then to Auschwitz, where his parents and sister died and he survived.
  62. 1940
    The Sub-Mariner comes out of the seaB4 Ch3
    The Sub-Mariner tore up a street in New York and threw a fire engine through a pharmacy.
  63. 1940s
    Greta Grindelwald fights the heroes of the war
    In the Second World War Greta Grindelwald fought Captain America and the Invaders in occupied Europe, and the Justice Society where her war spilt beyond the Axis lands.
  64. c. 1940
    Hagrid starts at Hogwarts
    Rubeus Hagrid entered Hogwarts and was sorted into Gryffindor.
  65. Autumn 1940
    Mystery men break a Nazi invasion scheme
    In the autumn of 1940 several American mystery men, working separately, broke a Nazi scheme to prepare an invasion of Britain.
  66. December 1940
    Captain America debuts
    Captain America came to public notice in wartime, the success of Weapon I.
  67. 1941
    Prince Caspian calls the Pevensies back to Narnia
    Prince Caspian blew Susan's horn in his need and called the four back to Narnia, then ruled by the Telmarines; Peter fought King Miraz in single combat, and Aslan told Peter and Susan afterwards that they were too old to return.
  68. 1941
    Hawkman becomes the Society's chairman
    Hawkman, the archaeologist Carter Hall, succeeded the Flash as chairman of the Justice Society and chaired it for most of the decade, while the Flash and Green Lantern stepped back to honorary membership.
  69. 1941
    Shiera Sanders becomes Hawkgirl
    Shiera Sanders began fighting beside Carter Hall as Hawkgirl.
  70. 1941
    Aquaman comes out of the sea
    Arthur Curry, the son of a lighthouse keeper and a woman of Atlantis, came out of the sea as Aquaman.
  71. 1941
    Green Arrow begins fighting crime
    The archer Oliver Queen began fighting crime as Green Arrow.
  72. 1941
    Logan meets Captain America
    The long-lived Canadian mutant Logan, who fought in both world wars, met Captain America.
  73. 1941
    Steve Trevor crashes on Themyscira
    The American intelligence officer Steve Trevor crashed on Themyscira, the hidden island of the Amazons. Queen Hippolyta decreed a contest to choose the Amazon who would take him home, and her daughter Diana, forbidden to enter, entered in disguise and won.
  74. 1941
    Wonder Woman comes to America
    Late in 1941, on the eve of America's entry into the war, Diana of Themyscira came to public notice in America as Wonder Woman, in red and gold with a gold tiara, a golden lasso that compels the truth and silver bracelets that turn aside bullets.
  75. 1941
    The Sub-Mariner returns with the waterB4 Ch3
    The Sub-Mariner came back with the water and flooded New York; the protester's father drowned.
  76. Summer 1941
    Johnny Thunder joins the Justice Society
    In the summer of 1941 Johnny Thunder, a hapless young man who could summon a genie-like Thunderbolt with a word, joined the Justice Society.
  77. December 1941
    The All-Star Squadron is formed
    After the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, President Roosevelt called every mystery man in America into a single wartime body, the All-Star Squadron, based in the Perisphere left from the 1939 World's Fair at Flushing Meadows. The Justice Society's members served in it under their own name.
  78. c. 1941
    The Spear of Destiny holds back the heroes
    Because Hitler held the Spear of Destiny, and Japan the Holy Grail, any hero of great power who entered Axis lands, above all those touched by magic, could be bent to their will. The Justice Society's strongest members fought the war at home and at the edges of occupied territory, and the war abroad was fought by ordinary soldiers.
  79. 1942
    Edmund and Lucy sail on the Dawn Treader
    Edmund and Lucy sailed east with their cousin Eustace on the Dawn Treader to the edge of Aslan's country, and Aslan told them that in their own world he had another name.
  80. c. 1942
    Doctor Mid-Nite and Starman join the Society
    At the turn of 1942 Hourman stepped back from the Justice Society and two new men came in: Doctor Mid-Nite, the blinded physician Charles McNider, who could see in the dark, and Starman, the astronomer Ted Knight, with his gravity rod.
  81. 1942
    Wonder Woman becomes the Society's secretary
    Wonder Woman became secretary of the Justice Society, and soon afterwards a full member; being an Amazon, she did not age.
  82. 1942
    The Society serves as the Justice Battalion
    For a few months the Justice Society served as the Justice Battalion, an extension of the American armed forces.
  83. 1942
    The Howling Commandos are formed
    Captain Samuel Sawyer gave Sergeant Nick Fury command of the First Attack Squad, Army Rangers based in England, and after its first missions Winston Churchill granted it the honorary title of commandos. As the Howling Commandos it fought across occupied Europe and North Africa until the end of the war, more than once beside Captain America and Bucky.
  84. c. 1942
    Junior Juniper is killed in action
    Junior Juniper, the youngest of the Howling Commandos, was killed early in the squad's career, and the Englishman Percy Pinkerton took his place.
  85. c. 1942
    The Invaders are formed
    Once America was at war, Captain America, Bucky, the Sub-Mariner, the android Human Torch and his partner Toro saved Winston Churchill from the Nazi superman Master Man, and Churchill suggested they become a team. As the Invaders they fought the rest of the war in occupied Europe against the Red Skull, Baron Heinrich Zemo and the Axis armies.
  86. c. 1942
    Hagrid raises Aragog
    A traveller gave the schoolboy Rubeus Hagrid an egg from a distant land, and he raised the spider that hatched from it, Aragog, in a castle cupboard on table scraps.
  87. c. 1942
    Previous opening of the Chamber of SecretsB2 Ch14
    About fifty years before 1992 the Chamber of Secrets was opened; a Muggle-born student died, the culprit was expelled, and the affair was kept quiet.
  88. c. 1942
    The black diary datedB2 Ch14
    The diary later carried by Dracina Malfoy bore a printed date almost exactly fifty years before Christmas 1992.
  89. c. 1942
    The Chamber opened by Tom RiddleB2 Ch14
    Fifty years before 1993 the Chamber was opened, a Muggle-born girl (Myrtle) died, and Riddle framed Hagrid.
  90. February 1942
    The All-Star Squadron goes to Detroit
    The Squadron was sent to Detroit to head off violence at the opening of the Sojourner Truth Homes, built for Black war workers, where an agitator calling himself the Real American was stirring up a white mob. Afterwards the Black athlete Will Everett, Amazing-Man, joined the Squadron.
